docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text: The search returned 26 screened trial rows (CBX-250 added on re-run), 17 clinical-evidence rows (14 included), and 16 preclinical mechanism rows across six feature axes: HLA-restricted minor-antigen and WT1 TCR-T, the CG1/HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager, CD33- and CD123-directed agents, TP53 Y220C reactivation, and the second-transplant platform. Board agreement ran from unanimous (score 1.0) on the confirmatory workup and on second allo-HCT, through 0.8 on Iomab-B conditioning, down to -0.2 on rezatapopt. The one veto in the file is conservative's threshold-conditional CRS veto against ranking CBX-250 front-line; it is liftable to a dissent on a documented cytoreduction-first mitigation plan, and it is overridden here by ranking CBX-250 mid-list rather than over the cytoreduction backbone. The disagreement was mostly about order, not membership: all five personas endorsed a curative-intent arc of cytoreduce, carry into a second transplant, then consolidate on the HLA-restricted axis. The split was sharpest over the newly added CBX-250, which the risktaker and advocate ranked first on off-the-shelf speed, concensusite fourth as an enrollment target, and the critic left unranked as the least clinically-evidenced option.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
Three pending diagnostics gate the options this case was submitted for, and none of them is resolved. The HLA-restricted immunotherapy the patient came here for is doubly gated: HLA-A02:01 is only a chart placeholder, and HA-directed TCR-T additionally needs a recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch that has not been genotyped in either the patient or the sibling donor. RNA or qualitative typing does not substitute for allele-level HLA plus a paired mHAg genotype. The newly added CBX-250 rides the same HLA-A02:01 switch, so that one records pull now gates three HLA-restricted levers, not two. The TP53 handle is separately double-gated: the 2019-pathogenic-versus-2026-negative discrepancy sits on a 2% LOD, CNV-blind panel, and even a confirmed aberration only opens rezatapopt if the specific variant is Y220C.

  • The ranking is scoped to the patient's stated targetable features. It carries the confirmatory workup (rank 1), the curative transplant/cytoreduction backbone that targets the allograft platform and the confirmed CD33/CD123 antigens (ranks 2-6, 8-9), and the biomarker-conditional cell therapies and rezatapopt (ranks 7, 10, 11, 12). Standard salvage chemotherapy that does not act on one of these handles is out of scope and is a separate conversation with the treating team.
  • What each negative result forecloses: if HLA-A02:01 is negative, HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T (rank 7), the A02:01 WT1 TCR-T (rank 10), and CBX-250 (rank 11) are all foreclosed, and the only remaining HLA-restricted lever is the A24:02 WT1-siTCR, which has no reachable US site. If A02:01 is positive but the HA-1/HA-2 pair does not mismatch, rank 7 is foreclosed and CBX-250 plus WT1 become the surviving immunotherapy options on the A*02:01 axis. If TP53 is not Y220C, or a true reversion to wild-type is confirmed, rezatapopt (rank 12) is foreclosed. The curative transplant arc (ranks 2-6, 8) stays within scope regardless of how the immunotherapy and TP53 gates resolve, because it targets the allograft platform and the confirmed CD33/CD123 antigens rather than the pending markers.
  • Workup logistics: retrieving the 2020 HLA typing is same-day; repeat high-resolution typing is 3-7 days. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping runs 1-2 weeks and usually goes through the trial sponsor's central lab rather than a catalog test, and it needs a paired sibling-donor sample. STR chimerism on FACS-sorted CD34+ blasts (1-2 weeks) confirms recipient-origin relapse, which a bulk-marrow result cannot do; cell sorting is the load-bearing step because a donor-derived leukemia would redirect the whole plan.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• HLA-restricted minor-antigen TCR-T (HA-1/HA-2): NCT05473910, NCT06704152, PMID 38683966.
  • HLA-restricted WT1 TCR-T (A02:01 and A24:02 siTCR fallback): PMID 31235963, NCT07645469, PMID 28860210.
  • CG1/HLA-A*02:01 TCR-mimetic T-cell engager (off-the-shelf): CBX-250 NCT06994676, ASH 2024 abstract, doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699.
  • Targeted / sequential transplant conditioning: Iomab-B PMID 39298738, NCT07157514; FLAMSA-RIC PMID 16110027.
  • Second allo-HCT and sibling DLI platform: PMID 23918951, PMID 17909197.
  • CD33-directed ADC: gemtuzumab ozogamicin PMID 11432892.
  • CD123-directed: pivekimab sunirine PMID 38423051, NCT06561152; dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T NCT04156256, PMID 29515236.
  • TP53 Y220C reactivation: rezatapopt PMID 40608889, PMID 41740031, NCT06616636.

docs.title: Rank 1. Confirmatory diagnostic gate (HLA typing + HA-1/HA-2 genotyping + relapse TP53/Y220C NGS + sorted-CD34 STR chimerism)
docs.text: What it resolves: whether the HLA-restricted immunotherapy the case was built around is reachable at all, whether the TP53 handle is Y220C-actionable, and whether the relapse is recipient-derived and therefore targetable by minor-antigen TCR-T.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is not a therapeutic; it is the set of tests every downstream option depends on. The HA-directed TCR-T programs (NCT05473910, and the Bleakley precedent PMID 38683966) require HLA-A02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch; the off-the-shelf CBX-250 engager (NCT06994676) requires documented HLA-A02:01 alone; the myeloid rezatapopt trial (NCT06616636) requires a confirmed TP53 Y220C. The relapse NGS row that anchors the TP53 gate (PMID 39811143) is a variant-level, low-VAF, copy-number-capable panel, which is exactly what the 2026 assay lacked. Read the NGS alongside p53 IHC, 17p FISH, and the retrieved 2019 variant identity; do not adjudicate the discrepancy from any one of them alone.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Diagnostic certainty rather than a response probability. Each result independently opens or closes a door: HLA-A*02:01 for the whole restricted axis (HA-1/HA-2, WT1, and CBX-250), the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch for donor TCR-T, the Y220C call for rezatapopt, and sorted-CD34 STR chimerism for recipient-origin relapse. The tests are cheap and fast relative to what they decide, which is why all five personas placed their entire ranking behind them.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text: • None beyond a records request plus assays on blood, marrow, and a paired sibling-donor sample. No procedure-level risk beyond a marrow aspirate the patient is already having for disease assessment.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was unanimous. There is nothing to dissent from: a non-toxic test that gates everything is the one thing every persona agreed on without qualification.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Retrieve the 2020 allele-level HLA typing from the transplant / donor-registry chart first, since that is same-day; repeat typing is 3-7 days if the record cannot be found. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is not a routine catalog test and is most reliably run through the ALLOHA sponsor central lab or an academic immunogenetics lab, and it needs the sibling donor sampled too. Confirm recipient-origin relapse by STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts (the sex-matched sibling donor rules out XY-FISH). While typing is pending, the transplant team can hold parallel screening conversations with the enrolling programs.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Confirmatory test What it decides Turnaround Reference High-resolution HLA-A typing (A02:01, A24:02) Master switch for the HLA-restricted axis (HA-1/HA-2, WT1, CBX-250) Same-day retrieval; 3-7 days repeat NCT05473910, NCT06994676 HA-1 / HA-2 genotyping, patient + sibling donor TSC-100 (HA-1) / TSC-101 (HA-2) eligibility 1-2 weeks PMID 38683966 Relapse myeloid NGS, variant-level + CNV TP53-aberrant call and Y220C status 1-3 weeks PMID 39811143, NCT06616636 STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts Recipient- vs donor-origin relapse 1-2 weeks NCT05473910

docs.title: Rank 2. Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2)
docs.text: The curative backbone, deliverable only after the marrow is cytoreduced.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The Christopeit EBMT registry of 179 second transplants (PMID 23918951) puts 2-year OS at ~37% in the matched-related-donor subgroup that fits her, against ~25% pooled. Remission duration after the first transplant and disease stage at the second were the dominant survival drivers, and her ~6-year first remission sits on the favorable side. The FLAMSA-RIC (PMID 16110027) and DLI (PMID 17909197) series fill in how the platform is delivered and consolidated. All three are retrospective or single-arm (ROBINS-I Serious), and the 37% is a fitness-selected subgroup number, not a whole-cohort estimate.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate for her specific profile. The long first remission pushes the odds up; 85% marrow blasts and complex TP53-aberrant cytogenetics pull hard the other way, and the same registry names active high-burden disease at transplant as the single biggest adverse driver. This is why HCT2 earns rank 2 only on the condition that cytoreduction brings the marrow close to a transplantable state first.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Substantial non-relapse mortality and acute/chronic GVHD in a second allograft, not broken out in the abstract-level registry.
  • Infection and conditioning organ toxicity, which cannot be safely bounded without the missing cardiac and organ-function workup.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented; the critic and concensusite qualified the number (subgroup, retrospective, 2A-by-absence-of-anything-better) but agreed on the rank. The mechanism-level worry is real though: this disease already slipped graft-versus-leukemia once, and a TP53-aberrant complex karyotype is exactly the biology that escapes a second graft too. A durable HCT2 is not assured even with a good first remission.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCCN AML v3.2026 keeps second transplant a category 2A option for fit patients, and ELN 2022 places it at the center of curative-intent management once the marrow is back in remission. Settle donor strategy (same sibling versus an alternative) using the HA-1/HA-2 genotyping already underway, and get a cardiac / organ-function assessment on record before choosing conditioning intensity. The extramedullary thigh sarcoma may need directed radiotherapy separate from the transplant plan.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Second allo-HCT, matched-related subgroup 2-yr OS ~37% (related-donor) NRM/GVHD substantial PMID 23918951 FLAMSA-RIC sequencing into HCT2 88% CR, 2-yr OS 42% GVHD dominant PMID 16110027 Sibling DLI adjunct 2-yr OS 21% vs 9% GVHD PMID 17909197

docs.title: Rank 3. Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) conditioning into HCT2
docs.text: The RCT-grade way to carry an active, high-blast marrow into the transplant.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: SIERRA (PMID 39298738, NCT02665065) is the only randomized phase 3 in the whole dossier. CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning produced durable CR (>=180 days) of 17.1% versus 0% (p<0.0001) and EFS HR 0.23. The number the board weighted most was grade >=3 treatment-related AE parity, 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care, meaning the targeted conditioning did not stack toxicity on top of what these patients already face. Three honest limits: ITT OS was flat (HR 0.99, p=0.96), which the authors attribute to 52% crossover rather than a true failure; SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so the durable-CR endpoint is a surrogate read against a population that was not heading to a second transplant; and in August 2024 the FDA judged the SIERRA package insufficient for a BLA and asked Actinium for a fresh non-crossover study, so the drug is neither approved nor guideline-adopted, and its regulatory path is unsettled.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, and the best-evidenced route to the one thing that makes every downstream cellular play possible: getting an 85%-blast marrow into an allograft. The efficacy caveat is that dCR is a durable-remission surrogate and the survival signal did not separate. It competes with FLAMSA-RIC (rank 8) for the same conditioning job.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs ~60%: cytopenias, febrile neutropenia, infection, mucositis, as expected for myeloablative conditioning.
  • Marrow-directed conditioning may not reach the extramedullary thigh sarcoma, which needs separate directed-RT planning.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Four personas endorsed the evidence; concensusite left it off their ranked list because NCCN and ELN have not adopted CD45 RIT, and in round 2 both concensusite and the critic sharpened that the FDA declined the SIERRA package as a BLA basis in August 2024 and asked for a fresh non-crossover study, so its guideline standing is trial-route rather than consensus. The risktaker and advocate pushed back that demoting the single highest-tier randomized readout on adoption status optimizes for the wrong variable in a patient who explicitly accepts trials. The critic conceded it is the one tier-1b anchor in the file, with a surrogate/crossover caveat. Conservative endorsed the tolerability parity but held the go/no-go contingent on a fitness assessment.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational and not approved; SIERRA is closed and the go-forward non-crossover study (NCT07157514) is not yet recruiting. The load-bearing eligibility question is prior transplant: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so confirm the new protocol accepts a prior allo-HCT before banking on it. Have the transplant team weigh Iomab-B against FLAMSA-RIC, since both target the same high-burden-disease problem.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Iomab-B conditioning + allo-HCT (SIERRA) Durable CR 17.1% vs 0%; EFS HR 0.23; OS HR 0.99 G3+ TRAE 59.7% (parity with control) PMID 39298738 131I-apamistamab go-forward conditioning Not yet reported Myeloablative conditioning profile NCT07157514

docs.title: Rank 4. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (CD33 ADC)
docs.text: The one agent a treating team can simply write; a modest on-label CD33 debulk.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The Sievers pooled phase 2 (PMID 11432892, n=142) reported ~30% overall remission (CR+CRp) in CD33-positive AML in first relapse, with grade >=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23% and transaminase elevation 17%. It is on-label and on-mechanism for her confirmed CD33-positive blasts, but the registration population was less pretreated than she is: no antecedent MDS, no prior FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure, no extramedullary disease. It is a CD33-directed bridge toward HCT2, not definitive therapy.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-moderate, and probably toward the low end here given how far past first relapse she is. Benefit tracks CD33 antigen density, and only qualitative positivity is on file, so the quantitative flow readout should anchor the go/no-go rather than the density being assumed.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade >=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23%, transaminitis 17%, infection 28%.
  • Veno-occlusive disease is the characteristic calicheamicin class risk and stacks peri-transplant, which argues for an adequate interval and fractionated dosing before HCT2.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent stood; concensusite actively defended it against the critic's evidence-quality downgrade, noting that a category 2A rating is the panel's own calibration of exactly that single-arm data plus twenty-plus years of VOD-monitoring experience. The mechanism-level catch is timing rather than direction: the hepatotoxicity that makes it a bridge could compromise the transplant it is bridging to if the interval is too short.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: FDA-approved on-label for CD33-positive relapsed AML; NCCN AML v3.2026 carries single-agent gemtuzumab at category 2A. Available by routine prescription, no trial or expanded-access mechanism needed. Request quantitative CD33 antigen density first, and factor VOD timing into the HCT2 plan.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy ~30% CR+CRp (first relapse) G3+ hyperbilirubinemia 23%; VOD class risk PMID 11432892

docs.title: Rank 5. Donor lymphocyte infusion (sibling DLI)
docs.text: A readily available transplant adjunct whose honest expectation is modest in florid disease.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The Schmid EBMT registry (PMID 17909197, n=399) found 21% versus 9% 2-year OS with versus without DLI (adjusted P=0.04). That is the one comparative signal in the transplant set, and it is confounding-by-indication wearing a p-value: benefit concentrated in the remission or favorable-karyotype group (~56%), while the active-disease or aplasia stratum came in around 15%. Her late relapse (~6 years) predicts DLI benefit, but 85% blasts and adverse cytogenetics put her in the worse stratum.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low for the stratum she falls in. The registry reads as an argument for cytoreduction before any DLI, not for DLI into a florid marrow, and every persona who touched it read it that way.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Acute and chronic GVHD is the characteristic toxicity and would complicate a subsequent HCT2.
  • Marrow aplasia when given into active high-burden disease.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent stood; the critic and concensusite ranked it as an adjunct with the active-disease caveat baked in. The mechanism-level risk is that DLI into 85% blasts drives GVHD without meaningful graft-versus-leukemia, which is why it belongs after cytoreduction and alongside the transplant rather than as standalone salvage.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: ASTCT/EBMT-recognized for AML relapse after allo-HCT. Confirm the sibling donor is available and willing to donate lymphocytes again, and pair DLI with the transplant plan (including the FLAMSA-RIC prophylactic-DLI schedule) rather than using it alone. Watch for GVHD if combined with HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Sibling DLI for post-HCT relapse 2-yr OS 21% vs 9%; ~15% in active disease GVHD; marrow aplasia PMID 17909197

docs.title: Rank 6. Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC)
docs.text: A CD123 debulk that avoids the failed backbone, though its VOD signal works against the transplant it bridges to.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Pivekimab (PMID 38423051) is a CD123 antibody-drug conjugate with single-agent activity in R/R AML: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the recommended phase 2 dose, matching her confirmed CD123 positivity without re-running the FLAG-IDA scaffold the disease already failed. Preclinically (PMID 29661755) it kills AML at low picomolar potency and reaches the leukemic stem-cell compartment while sparing normal progenitors. There is a recruiting Stanford trial pairing it with low-intensity chemotherapy (NCT06561152).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low as a single agent, and density-directed selection is still advisory since quantitative CD123 flow is pending. The 21% ORR comes off a 29-patient RP2D expansion, so the interval around it is wide. It is a cytoreductive bridge, not a curative move by itself, so it earns its rank only as a debulk toward the transplant and cellular options.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Reversible veno-occlusive disease surfaced as a dose-limiting toxicity (2/68) and carries a boxed warning, the wrong hepatic risk to stack into a planned HCT2.
  • Febrile neutropenia 10% at the RP2D, and one treatment-related death (1%) against a modest 21% ORR.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The risktaker and advocate ranked pivekimab as a CD123 bridge that debulks without re-using a failed backbone; no persona issued a formal dissent against it this round. The round-2 critiques on it were sequencing caveats: conservative flagged the peri-transplant VOD and would run on-label gemtuzumab first until organ-function data land, and the critic held the 21%-from-29-patients interval honestly. The mechanism-level catch is direct: the VOD that could compromise the very transplant it is bridging to, which is why gemtuzumab, with its mature VOD-monitoring playbook, sits ahead of it for the same debulk.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: FDA-approved for BPDCN (Decnupaz, May 2026), so a clinician can prescribe off-label for CD123-positive AML, though reimbursement will be a fight this soon after approval, and both AML-relevant trials are closed to new enrollment. Request quantitative CD123 density, weigh the boxed VOD warning with the transplant team, and confirm off-label supply and prior authorization now that it is marketed. Tagraxofusp is the CD123 alternative but adds capillary-leak risk that argues even harder for fitness data first.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Pivekimab sunirine monotherapy ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40); composite CR 17% Reversible VOD (DLT); febrile neutropenia 10%; 1 TRD PMID 38423051 Pivekimab + low-intensity chemo Not yet reported CD123-ADC profile NCT06561152

docs.title: Rank 7. HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after HCT2
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201_ha:positive. Foreclosed if either the HLA-A02:01 type or the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch is negative.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is the handle the case was submitted for and the highest-ceiling cure swing. Bleakley's phase 1 (PMID 38683966, n=9) got 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients into or holding CR, one remission past two years, no dose-limiting toxicity. The mechanism aims donor T cells at recipient HA-1/HA-2, minor antigens presented mainly on blood-lineage cells, so graft-versus-leukemia reaches the leukemia while largely sparing the tissues that drive GVHD. TSC-100/TSC-101 (NCT05473910) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152) run the same mechanism on the back of a fresh matched transplant. This is feasibility-grade evidence: n=9, single-arm, and the per-term grade-level AE table could not be retrieved from the Blood 2024 full text, so "no DLTs" is the only safety datum on file.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Signal-level in the positive branch. A 4/9 uncontrolled CR fraction with durable responders is a live cure signal, not proof; the trial exists precisely to test whether that ceiling is real. And it only exists for this patient if the typing breaks the right way. A negative HLA-A*02:01 or a non-mismatched HA-1/HA-2 pair forecloses it entirely.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No dose-limiting toxicities across the n=9 cohort; the characteristic setting risks are lymphodepletion cytopenias and GVHD.
  • The per-grade AE table is not retrievable from the full text, which is itself the reason two personas held it back in a fitness-unknown patient.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: This is the preference-conflict row. The advocate ranked it near the top as the axis the run was built around; the risktaker and concensusite endorse it (concensusite through the guideline's enroll-in-a-trial language). Two personas hold back, and their objections are not biomarker-contingent, so they persist in the positive branch: the critic dissents on evidence maturity (n=9 feasibility, not efficacy, above options with a phase 3 or on-label read), and the conservative parks it on the same evidence-maturity grounds plus the undocumented fitness. Because advocate flagged it preference-aligned while two personas dissented, status is considered_with_caveats and the tension is left visible rather than smoothed over. The load-bearing uncertainty is not the HLA type (a records pull) but the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch, a biological coin-flip that genotyping the pair simply closes.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational, no consensus category of its own; NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022 both make trial enrollment the preferred R/R route, which makes this a guideline-consistent enrollment target. Three US programs are recruiting (TScan ALLOHA at 15 sites, Fred Hutch NCT03326921, BlueSphere BSB-1001 at 6 sites), all delivered on the back of a fresh allo-HCT. It is post-HCT2 consolidation by design and does nothing for the current marrow, so it sequences after the transplant, not instead of it.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference HA-1 TCR-T (Bleakley) 4/9 CR; 1 remission >2 yr 0 DLTs (n=9) PMID 38683966 TSC-100 / TSC-101 (ALLOHA) Not yet reported Safety endpoint NCT05473910 BSB-1001 (HA-1 TCR-T) Not yet reported Safety/dose endpoint NCT06704152

docs.title: Rank 8. FLAMSA-RIC sequential conditioning + reduced-intensity allo-HCT + prophylactic DLI
docs.text: The chemo-based conditioning alternative to Iomab-B for the same transplant.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Schmid's prospective cohort (PMID 16110027, n=75) took refractory AML with adverse cytogenetics straight into a reduced-intensity allograft: 88% CR, 2-year OS 42%, and the refractory / complex-karyotype subgroup did as well as lower-risk patients. Thirty-one of 75 used HLA-identical sibling donors, matching her situation, and the DLI series (PMID 17909197) covers the prophylactic-DLI component from day +120.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, and the same order of magnitude as the transplant registry, in a design built for exactly the hard subgroup she is in. It is a delivery route to HCT2 rather than an independent modality, so its likelihood is really the transplant's likelihood by a chemotherapy-conditioning path.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• GVHD, including prophylactic-DLI-associated GVHD, is the dominant risk; per-term toxicity is not tabulated in the source abstract.
  • An older regimen whose conditioning intensity depends on the undocumented cardiac / organ-function fitness.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented. Advocate carried FLAMSA-RIC as the chemotherapy-based sequencing alternative inside the transplant discussion, and it overlaps with the transplant platform by design rather than competing with it. It sits behind Iomab-B only because Iomab-B carries the randomized evidence, and that gap narrows now that Iomab-B is unapproved with an unsettled regulatory path, which arguably strengthens the case for a generic-agent conditioning route the transplant center can actually run today. The mechanism-level caution is the standard one for prophylactic DLI: GVHD without proportional graft-versus-leukemia if disease burden is not reduced first.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Established regimen, more common in European practice, with no distinct NCCN/ELN category. Ask the transplant center whether it runs FLAMSA-RIC sequencing and how it compares, for this patient, with Iomab-B conditioning; fold the prophylactic-DLI component into the post-transplant plan alongside any TCR-T consolidation.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference FLAMSA-RIC + prophylactic DLI 88% CR; 2-yr OS 42% GVHD dominant PMID 16110027

docs.title: Rank 9. Dual CD33/CD123 compound CAR-T
docs.text: The antigen-escape hedge for a clonally evolving relapse, held back by xenograft-only evidence.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The relapse already shows clonal evolution between 2019 and 2026, so betting on a single antigen invites escape. The compound CAR-T co-targets both CD33 and CD123, and the dual construct beat single-antigen targeting for survival across four AML xenograft models (PMID 29515236). Both antigens are confirmed on her blasts. The honest problem is that the entire case is xenograft-based with no post-allo-HCT human data, and the recruiting sites (NCT04156256) are in mainland China.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Speculative. There is no clinical efficacy read at all, so the ceiling is theoretical and the human toxicity is uncharacterized. This is where a longshot earns or loses the argument, and both the risktaker and advocate ranked it last on their own slates for that reason.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• CRS plus on-target myeloablation of normal CD33- and CD123-positive progenitors, with no clinical toxicity table to plan against.
  • Post-allo-HCT CAR-T eligibility and manufacturing feasibility are unaddressed.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Conservative dissented on safety: a dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T stacks cytokine toxicity with marrow-aplasia risk in a re-transplant candidate, and xenograft survival curves do not tell a clinician how to manage the patient. That is a mechanism-grounds objection, so counter-productive-MoA severity is moderate. Status is considered_with_caveats because the evidence is entirely preclinical and the access route is out of the country.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational, no approval anywhere. The practical route is uncertain: confirm whether either China-based sponsor will accept an overseas patient before counting on it, and weigh CRS and post-transplant CAR-T risk with the transplant team. If no slot materializes, on-label gemtuzumab (rank 4) is the immediately available CD33 alternative.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference CD123-CD33 compound CAR-T Xenograft survival benefit only CRS; progenitor myeloablation (no human data) PMID 29515236, NCT04156256

docs.title: Rank 10. WT1 HLA-A02:01 TCR-T (with A24:02 siTCR fallback)
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201:positive. Foreclosed if neither A02:01 nor A24:02 is present.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: WT1 keeps the HLA-restricted axis alive if the HA-1/HA-2 pair does not mismatch but the patient is A02:01-positive. The Chapuis WT1-TCRc4 work (PMID 31235963, n=12) held high-risk AML patients relapse-free post-transplant, reporting 100% RFS at median 44 months versus 54% in a concurrent cohort. The live product is FH-WT1-E50 plus azacitidine (NCT07645469), written for MRD-positive disease. If A02:01 is negative, A*24:02 opens the WT1-siTCR lever (PMID 28860210), which is why both alleles should be typed in parallel.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Setting-mismatched in the positive branch. The 100% RFS figure comes from a prophylaxis product given against relapse, not salvage of a florid 85%-blast marrow, and the 54% comparator is a concurrent non-randomized cohort, so the survival contrast is confounded. Best positioned as post-cytoreduction or post-HCT2 consolidation, and foreclosed entirely if neither allele is present.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Engineered into EBV-specific donor cells to minimize GVHD; no per-term AE breakdown in the abstract.
  • On-target hematopoietic risk is theoretical, since WT1 is a shared self-antigen, though the preclinical work showed normal-progenitor sparing.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The critic dissented because prophylaxis/MRD data cannot rank a lever for florid relapse on a confounded comparator, and concensusite likewise flagged the setting mismatch; both objections are about the evidence and the disease state rather than the biomarker, so they persist in the positive branch. Advocate carried it explicitly so an A02:01-positive but HA-non-mismatched result does not foreclose the immunotherapy axis the patient prioritized. It sits just below CBX-250's score on the same A02:01 axis, but its evidence is prophylaxis in a setting she is not in.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational, no consensus category; trial enrollment is the guideline-preferred R/R route. The live FH-WT1-E50 product is not yet recruiting and is written for MRD-positive disease, so treat it as a consolidation concept after disease control. The A*24:02 siTCR fallback (TBI-1301) has no reachable US site, so it is more concept than route.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference WT1-TCRc4 post-HCT prophylaxis 100% RFS at 44 mo vs 54% (confounded) GVHD-minimized; no per-term data PMID 31235963 FH-WT1-E50 + azacitidine Not yet reported (MRD-positive) WT1-directed profile NCT07645469 WT1-siTCR (A*24:02 fallback) 2/8 transient blast reduction No normal-tissue AEs (n=8) PMID 28860210

docs.title: Rank 11. CBX-250 (CG1/HLA-A*02:01 TCR-mimetic T-cell engager)
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201:positive. Foreclosed if the HLA-A02:01 type is negative. Ranked here rather than front-line: the conservative CRS veto is overridden by not placing it over cytoreduction, and it is gated on a documented CRS-mitigation plan.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: CBX-250 was added to the dossier on this re-run after the initial screen missed it, because CG1/Cathepsin-G was not a nominated feature. It is a TCR-mimetic bispecific that binds the CG1 nonamer presented on HLA-A*02:01 and cross-links CD3 to redirect polyclonal T cells against blasts, so it works off-the-shelf with no donor or autologous manufacturing. The evidence is preclinical and conference-abstract-level (ASH 2024, doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699): sub-nanomolar T-cell-mediated killing across a range of antigen density, no activity against healthy-donor neutrophils, CD34+ cells, or PBMCs, and tumor control plus a survival benefit in a primary-AML PDX at doses as low as 0.005 mg/kg. CROSSCHECK-001 (NCT06994676) is a recruiting first-in-human phase 1 at 11 US sites with no efficacy or safety readout yet. There is no PMID for the abstract, and the DOI is carried as-in-dossier rather than asserted beyond it.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Preclinical only, even in the positive branch. The mechanism data are genuinely strong for a phase-1 asset, but potency in a PDX is not a response in a patient, and CROSSCHECK-001 has yet to treat and report a single participant. Frame the likelihood as unproven and foreclosed entirely if HLA-A*02:01 comes back negative.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• First-in-human with no established MTD/RP2D and no characterized AE profile in a single treated patient. As a CD3 engager the anticipated class toxicity is cytokine release syndrome, and CRS severity scales with tumor burden, so an 85%-blast marrow is the highest-risk setting to debut an uncharacterized engager.
  • The conservative persona issued a threshold-conditional toxicity veto against ranking it front-line. The veto is liftable to a dissent only on a documented CRS-mitigation plan: cytoreduce the 85%-blast burden below threshold first, use step-up dosing, and keep tocilizumab on hand. None of that is on file yet.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: This is the row the re-deliberation turned on. The risktaker and advocate ranked it first on off-the-shelf speed for a marrow climbing 58% to 82% peripheral blasts in a month; concensusite ranked it fourth as an enrollment-preferred target that carries no consensus category of its own; the critic left it unranked because everything under it is preclinical and ranking it over options with human data inverts the evidence hierarchy; and the conservative issued the threshold-conditional CRS veto against the two rank-1 placements. Handled per the veto rules, the row is retained rather than dropped and is not ranked over the cytoreduction backbone. The veto is overridden by that placement plus the explicit cytoreduction-first / CRS-mitigation gate, and it is left visible in the persona pills and this narrative. The critic's evidence-maturity dissent is not biomarker-contingent, so it persists in the positive branch. Counter-productive-MoA severity is high because the standing veto rests on a mechanism concern: an uncharacterized CRS that scales with the very blast burden the drug is meant to reduce.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational, first-in-human, no approval or compassionate-use route; the only access is CROSSCHECK-001 (NCT06994676), recruiting at 11 US sites (City of Hope, Stanford, Moffitt, Northwestern, Dana-Farber, Washington University, MSK, Thomas Jefferson, Sarah Cannon, Vanderbilt, MD Anderson). Enrollment hinges on documented HLA-A02:01, the same pending typing that gates the rest of the axis; prior allo-HCT is permitted once 60 days have elapsed, and at least 4 weeks from any non-conditioned DLI, so the ~2020 transplant is not a barrier. Its honest edge over the TCR-T handles is that it needs neither the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch nor an HCT2 platform under it, so it could move fastest once A02:01 confirms. That speed is exactly why the safety gate matters: pair any move with the transplant team's CRS-mitigation plan and current organ-function assessment.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference CBX-250 preclinical (PDX + cell lines) Sub-nM killing; PDX survival benefit at 0.005 mg/kg No normal-tissue activity; CRS untested doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699 CBX-250 (CROSSCHECK-001, first-in-human) Not yet reported No MTD/AE profile established NCT06994676

docs.title: Rank 12. Rezatapopt (Y220C-selective p53 reactivator) + azacitidine
docs.text: Conditional on tp53_y220c:positive. Foreclosed if TP53 is not Y220C or a true reversion is confirmed.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Rezatapopt binds the surface pocket created by the Y220C substitution and refolds mutant p53 toward a wild-type shape. In Y220C AML models (PMID 40608889) it reactivates the p53 program but drives little apoptosis on its own; adding venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 inhibition restores real killing. The solid-tumor PYNNACLE data (PMID 41740031) show ORR 20%, and 30% in the KRAS-wild-type subset. Every clinical response so far is in solid tumors; the myeloid trial (NCT06616636, rezatapopt + azacitidine at MD Anderson) has posted nothing.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Cross-tumor only, even in the positive branch, and doubly contingent: confirm a TP53 aberration at all off the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy, then confirm it is specifically Y220C. A low-positive or unconfirmed biomarker is a weaker predictor of benefit than a tier-matched confirmed one, and the mechanism needs a venetoclax partner she is already refractory to. Treat the likelihood as speculative until both contingencies land.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade >=3 anaemia 16%; predominant low-grade nausea (58%) and vomiting (44%), less frequent when taken with food.
  • Oral, continuous dosing; the toxicity burden is genuinely lower than the transplant and cytoreduction options, which is the one thing it has going for it.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Two dissents that persist through biomarker confirmation because they are about the evidence, not the marker. The critic marks it down for solid-tumor-only data plus the venetoclax dependency in a venetoclax-refractory patient, and in this round also caught a citation drift in the risktaker's rationale, correcting the quoted 30% ORR down to PYNNACLE's actual 20% (the 30% is the KRAS-wild-type subset). Concensusite marks it off-consensus, since no AML guideline lists a p53 reactivator and the myeloid trial has no results. Only the risktaker ranked it, as a mechanistic longshot. The counter-productive-MoA is that reactivated p53 barely triggers apoptosis alone and needs a partner drug she has already failed.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Investigational, absent from NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022, and off the HLA-restricted axis that is the stated reason for the run, so the advocate deliberately kept it off the preference-carrying slate. Worth resolving in parallel with the HLA workup, not foregrounding. A non-Y220C aberration or a true reversion closes it; eprenetapopt is the low-yield pan-reactivator alternative and is functionally unavailable in myeloid disease.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Rezatapopt monotherapy (PYNNACLE, solid tumors) ORR 20% (30% KRAS-WT) G3+ anaemia 16%; low-grade GI PMID 41740031 Rezatapopt + azacitidine (myeloid) Not yet reported Needs venetoclax/MDM2 partner preclinically PMID 40608889, NCT06616636

docs.title: Workup considerations
docs.text:
Beyond the four gating tests in rank 1, several high-priority but non-gating confirmatory steps sit adjacent to the profile and should run off the same specimens:

  • Quantitative CD33 and CD123 antigen-density flow (antibodies-bound-per-cell), batched on one fresh draw, to convert the qualitative-positive calls into the metric that actually predicts ADC benefit for gemtuzumab and pivekimab.
  • p53 protein IHC (clone DO-7) and TP53 (17p13) FISH on the marrow biopsy, plus retrieval of the 2019 diagnostic report, to reconcile the TP53 discrepancy at the protein and copy-number level without down-calling on the CNV-blind panel.
  • A full metaphase karyotype at relapse to characterize the adverse MECOM rearrangement and KMT2A amplification for risk stratification and trial eligibility.
  • Right-thigh contrast MRI plus whole-body FDG-PET/CT to map the extramedullary myeloid sarcoma and decide whether directed radiotherapy is warranted before or bridging to HCT2.

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• Tagraxofusp (CD123 immunotoxin): targets the confirmed CD123 handle, but no persona ranked it; pivekimab was preferred as the CD123 lever, and tagraxofusp adds capillary-leak risk that argues for fitness data first. Carried as the CD123 alternative in rank 6.
  • CD123xCD3 bispecifics (flotetuzumab, vibecotamab): on-mechanism for CD123 with real salvage signal for flotetuzumab in chemo-refractory AML, but both programs are discontinued or terminated, so neither is an open route.
  • PRAME-directed TCR-T (BPX-701): the third A*02:01-restricted handle named in the profile, but the only clinical program is terminated with no successor, so there is no way to reach a PRAME-directed TCR-T today.
  • Eprenetapopt (pan-p53 reactivator): targets the TP53 handle, but it is not Y220C-selective, its phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint, and myeloid development sits under a clinical hold, so it is the low-yield and functionally unavailable p53 option behind rezatapopt.

docs.title: Ranked prioritization
docs.text:
Confirmatory workup (gates the biomarker-conditional ranks below):

Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 1 Confirmatory diagnostic gate (HLA typing + HA-1/HA-2 genotyping + relapse TP53/Y220C NGS + sorted-CD34 STR chimerism)endorse: risktaker conservative critic concensusite advocate Diagnostic certainty - independently resolves HLA-A*02:01, the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch, TP53/Y220C status, and recipient-clonal origin Low (none - records + assays on blood, marrow, paired donor sample) N/A (diagnostic, not therapeutic) The non-toxic gate the whole plan waits on; genotyping the sibling pair turns the stated-reason immunotherapy axis from undetermined into eligible.

Ranked options:

Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 2 Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2)endorse: risktaker conservative critic concensusite advocate Moderate in this subset - ~37% 2-year OS in matched-related-donor HCT2 (Christopeit 2013), lifted by her ~6-year first remission but pulled down by 85% blasts High (non-relapse mortality, acute/chronic GVHD, infection, conditioning organ toxicity) Moderate (disease already escaped GVL once; marrow aplasia in active disease) Low (DLI into 85% blasts drives GVHD without meaningful GVL; needs cytoreduction first) A readily available sibling-donor adjunct; belongs after cytoreduction, alongside the transplant, not as standalone salvage. 6 Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC)endorse: risktaker advocate Low - single-agent ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40), composite CR 17% at RP2D (Daver 2024); CRS; no post-HCT data) The dual-antigen escape hedge for a clonally evolving relapse, held back by xenograft-only evidence and China-only trial access. 10 WT1 A02:01 TCR-T (A24:02 siTCR fallback) (conditional on hla_a0201 positive)endorse: advocatedissent: critic Setting-mismatched, positive branch - 100% RFS at 44 months as post-HCT prophylaxis (Chapuis 2019, n=12, confounded comparator); unproven for florid relapse Low (engineered to minimize GVHD; no per-term AE breakdown; on-target hematopoietic risk theoretical) Moderate (validated as prophylaxis, not salvage; unproven against florid marrow; WT1 is a shared self-antigen) The second HLA-restricted lever that keeps the axis open if HA-1/HA-2 does not mismatch, but its evidence is prophylaxis in MRD, not salvage. 11 CBX-250 (CG1/HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager) (conditional on hla_a0201 positive)endorse: risktaker advocate concensusitedissent: criticveto: conservative (threshold-conditional, overridden) Preclinical only, positive branch - sub-nanomolar killing and PDX survival benefit (ASH 2024 abstract); zero human efficacy readout; foreclosed if A*02:01 negative Unknown - first-in-human, no characterized AE profile (expected CD3-engager CRS scaling with the 85%-blast burden) High (uncharacterized CRS scaling with 85%-blast burden could harm before it debulks; the standing conditional veto rests on this) The only off-the-shelf option on the exact A*02:01 axis - fastest to move once typing confirms, but first-in-human with no efficacy and gated behind a cytoreduction-first CRS-mitigation plan. 12 Rezatapopt + azacitidine (conditional on tp53_y220c positive)endorse: risktakerdissent: critic concensusite Cross-tumor only, positive branch - solid-tumor ORR 20% (30% KRAS-WT, PYNNACLE); no myeloid clinical data; preclinically needs a venetoclax partner Low (grade >=3 anaemia 16%; predominant low-grade nausea 58%, vomiting 44%) Moderate (reactivated p53 barely triggers apoptosis alone; needs a venetoclax/MDM2 partner she is already refractory to) A mechanistically elegant Y220C longshot off the stated axis, double-gated on confirming TP53 then Y220C, with no myeloid data.

How to read the last two columns

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity (tiered Low / Moderate / High from the grade >=3 rates in the cited evidence). Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that the intervention could blunt its own therapeutic goal, such as graft-versus-leukemia escape, on-target progenitor myeloablation, cytokine release scaling with tumor burden, or a p53 reactivator that needs a partner drug the patient has already failed. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page. The veto pill on CBX-250 is the conservative persona's threshold-conditional CRS stop against ranking it front-line; it is overridden here by ranking it mid-list rather than over cytoreduction, and it lifts to a dissent once a documented CRS-mitigation plan exists.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. The strongest row (Iomab-B / SIERRA) is a randomized phase 3 but open-label with a durable-CR surrogate endpoint and a null ITT OS confounded by 52% crossover, and the FDA declined it as a BLA basis in August 2024, so it is unapproved with an unsettled regulatory path. Everything else is retrospective registry (HCT2, DLI), single-arm phase 1/2 (HA-1 TCR-T n=9, WT1 n=12, pivekimab), cross-tumor only (rezatapopt), xenograft-only (dual CAR-T), or, for CBX-250, a single first-in-human trial-in-progress with no readout backed only by an ASH 2024 conference abstract (no PMID). For the HA-1 TCR-T precedent, the per-grade AE table could not be retrieved from the full text, so its safety profile rests on "no DLTs" across nine patients.
  • Biomarker dependencies. Ranks 7, 10, and 11 assume HLA-A*02:01 confirmation; rank 7 additionally assumes a recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch; rank 12 assumes TP53 confirmed aberrant and specifically Y220C. Without those, the respective ranks are foreclosed. The transplant backbone (ranks 2-6, 8) does not depend on the pending markers and stays in scope regardless.
  • What would change the ranking. A retrievable HLA-A02:01-positive type plus a confirmed HA-1/HA-2 mismatch would move rank 7 from a conditional longshot toward the top of the therapeutic list, since it is the stated-reason option with the highest ceiling. An HLA-A02:01-positive type alone would activate CBX-250 (rank 11), and a documented CRS-mitigation plan (cytoreduction first, step-up dosing, tocilizumab on hand) would lift the conservative CRS veto to a dissent and could move it up on speed grounds. Documented organ-function and cardiac fitness would firm up the conditioning and transplant ranks and could raise the efficacy weight the file asks to revisit. A confirmed TP53 Y220C would lift rank 12 out of double contingency; a confirmed reversion to wild-type would foreclose it. A donor-derived leukemia on sorted-CD34 STR chimerism would redirect the entire plan away from minor-antigen TCR-T.
  • Re-scoping caveat. If fitness comes back poor, or goals of care shift away from curative intent, the whole arc changes: the transplant backbone and its conditioning would move toward palliative CD33/CD123 cytoreduction, and the efficacy-leaning 0.75 weight would need to be re-set.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text: Re-authored 2026-07-09 by the PI agent after the board was re-deliberated on the newly added CBX-250 (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676), an off-the-shelf CG1/HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager. Synthesized from the full dossier: profile, preferences, 11 target-validation rows, 26 trials, 17 clinical-evidence rows, 16 preclinical rows, accessibility, and the board's five re-run positions plus 39 critiques. Twelve recommendation rows: a unanimous rank-1 shared confirmatory workup, a biomarker-independent transplant/cytoreduction backbone (ranks 2-6, 8-9), and four biomarker-conditional rows (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T on hla_a0201_ha:positive, WT1 TCR-T and CBX-250 on hla_a0201:positive, rezatapopt on tp53_y220c:positive). CBX-250 landed at rank 11, considered_with_caveats: the risktaker and advocate ranked it first on off-the-shelf speed, but the conservative issued a threshold-conditional CRS veto against that front-line placement, and per the veto-handling rules the row was retained and ranked mid-list rather than over cytoreduction, with the conditional veto and the cytoreduction-first / CRS-mitigation gate documented on the row and the page. The TP53 discrepancy was held as aberrant-pending-confirmation and not collapsed. Two board-surfaced corrections were applied: the risktaker's rezatapopt rationale had cited a 30% ORR, which was corrected to PYNNACLE's actual 20% (30% is the KRAS-wild-type subset); and the August 2024 FDA determination that the SIERRA/Iomab-B package was insufficient for a BLA was folded into Iomab-B's guideline status, which keeps it the RCT-grade conditioning enabler but unapproved with an unsettled path. Menin inhibitors (revumenib, ziftomenib) remain out-of-feature-scope and are not surfaced. Fitness and organ-function data are the main inferred gap; the efficacy weight of 0.75 is flagged for revisiting once they exist.

docs.title: 1. Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT HCT2, second allo-HCT, HSCT2
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-07-06

A second allo-HCT is the curative-intent platform this whole plan sits on, and it is standard of care rather than anything experimental. It is also the hardest to earn: registry data put 2-year survival around 37% in matched-sibling second transplants, better with the patient's long ~6-year first remission but worse with 85% marrow blasts and adverse cytogenetics going in. The gate is disease control and fitness, not access.

Regulatoryestablished transplant procedure; no drug approval involved GuidelinesRecognized option for relapse after a first allo-HCT (ASTCT/EBMT/NCCN transplant guidance) Geographic scopeAny allo-HCT transplant center.

Next steps

  1. Get a second-transplant consult at the patient's allo-HCT center to confirm candidacy (organ function, cardiac, goals of care).
  2. Settle donor strategy: same HLA-identical sibling versus an alternative donor, informed by the HA-1/HA-2 genotyping already underway.
  3. Sequence cytoreduction to get the marrow as close to remission as possible before HCT2, since disease burden at transplant is the dominant survival driver.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

NotesProcedure delivered at an allo-HCT transplant center; no manufacturer.

Payer / coverage notes. Covered as a standard transplant procedure when a patient meets center and insurer criteria (disease control, organ function, donor availability). A second transplant draws closer payer scrutiny than the first, so pre-authorization and a center consult come early.

docs.title: 2. Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning) Iomab-B, 131I-apamistamab, iodine-131 apamistamab, BC8, anti-CD45 RIT
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: radioimmunotherapy   Verified: 2026-07-06

Iomab-B is the targeted-conditioning platform that could carry an 85%-blast marrow into a second transplant, and it is trial-only. The pivotal SIERRA trial is closed, so the route is the go-forward study NCT07157514, which is not yet recruiting. The eligibility axis to nail down is prior transplant: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, and this case needs a second, so confirm the new protocol accepts a prior allo-HCT.

Next steps

  1. Email mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com (347-814-2268) to ask when NCT07157514 opens and, critically, whether a prior allo-HCT is allowed.
  2. Have the transplant team weigh Iomab-B conditioning against FLAMSA-RIC for the second transplant, since both aim at the same high-burden-disease problem.
  3. Confirm second-transplant candidacy (organ function, donor availability) in parallel, since the conditioning only matters if HCT2 is on.

docs.title: 3. Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the sibling donor DLI, donor lymphocyte infusion
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-07-06

Sibling DLI is standard of care and readily available given the matched-sibling donor, but the honest expectation is modest. Registry data favor DLI when relapse comes late (this patient at ~6 years qualifies) and when it is given in remission, yet with 85% marrow blasts and adverse cytogenetics the active-disease subgroup sees roughly 15% 2-year survival. That argues for cytoreduction before DLI rather than DLI into florid disease.

Regulatoryestablished post-transplant procedure; no drug approval involved GuidelinesRecognized for AML relapse after allo-HCT (ASTCT/EBMT practice) Geographic scopeThe patient's allo-HCT center, using the original sibling donor.

Next steps

  1. Confirm the sibling donor is available and willing to donate lymphocytes again.
  2. Cytoreduce toward remission before DLI rather than infusing into high-burden disease, and pair DLI with the second-transplant plan rather than using it as a standalone salvage.
  3. Watch for GVHD, the characteristic DLI toxicity, especially if combined with HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

NotesCells collected from the original sibling donor at the transplant center; no manufacturer.

Payer / coverage notes. Covered as a standard post-transplant procedure. Access hinges on the sibling donor being available and willing to donate lymphocytes again.

docs.title: 4. FLAMSA-RIC sequential chemotherapy + reduced-intensity allo-HCT (+ prophylactic DLI) FLAMSA-RIC, sequential FLAMSA conditioning
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-07-06

FLAMSA-RIC is a way to take refractory AML with adverse cytogenetics straight into a reduced-intensity transplant, and it is standard of care where centers offer it. It is the sequencing this patient's plan is built on, and it competes with Iomab-B conditioning for the same job. Access comes down to picking a transplant center that does it.

Regulatoryestablished conditioning regimen; no drug approval involved GuidelinesUsed for high-risk/refractory AML at transplant centers, mainly European practice Geographic scopeTransplant centers offering the regimen (more common in Europe).

Next steps

  1. Ask the transplant center whether it runs FLAMSA-RIC sequencing and how it compares, for this patient, with targeted Iomab-B conditioning.
  2. Fold the prophylactic-DLI component into the post-transplant plan alongside any HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

NotesConditioning regimen assembled from generic agents (fludarabine, cytarabine, amsacrine, TBI, ATG, cyclophosphamide); no single manufacturer.

Payer / coverage notes. Delivered as part of an allo-HCT admission and covered on that basis. The component chemotherapy drugs are generic and non-limiting; the constraint is finding a center that runs the FLAMSA-RIC sequence.

docs.title: 5. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC) gemtuzumab ozogamicin, Mylotarg, GO, CMA-676
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-07-06

Gemtuzumab is FDA-approved for CD33-positive AML including relapse, and the patient's blasts are CD33-positive, so it is available through routine prescription. The caveats are clinical rather than access: single-agent depth in relapse is modest (about 30% in less pretreated patients), and the hepatic/veno-occlusive-disease signal matters with a second transplant on the plan.

  2. Factor the veno-occlusive-disease risk into the timing relative to any planned second allo-HCT.

Three HA-directed TCR-T programs are recruiting in the US (TScan ALLOHA, Bleakley at Fred Hutch, BlueSphere BSB-1001), all delivered on the back of a fresh allo-HCT.
