docs.title: TP53 aberration (Y220C-contingent)
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences essentialComprehensive relapse myeloid NGS panel with variant-level TP53 readout, low-VAF sensitivity, and copy-number detectionconfirmatoryNGS_panelRelapse bone marrow aspirate (EDTA/heparin) or peripheral blood at current high blast burden; retrieve archived 2019 fixed-cell pellet or extracted DNA for side-by-side comparison1-3 weeksRezatapopt (PC14586) via PYNNACLE (NCT04585750) if Y220C-positive; also re-tests FLT3/IDH1/IDH2 at relapse.A relapse myeloid NGS panel with variant-level readout, adequate low-VAF sensitivity, and copy-number detection resolves the specific TP53 amino-acid change and reconciles the 2019-pathogenic versus 2026-negative discrepancy without down-calling on a 2%-LOD/no-CNV assay. A confirmed Y220C opens the Y220C-selective reactivator rezatapopt (PC14586); a non-Y220C aberration would not, and eprenetapopt is low-yield. The same panel re-interrogates FLT3, IDH1, and IDH2 at relapse given documented clonal evolution.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne Heme preferredtest info · 150 Second St, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 888-988-3639Heme NGS with variant, copy-number, and rearrangement calling in one validated assay, which is what the CNV-blind 2026 panel lacked; strong fit for resolving TP53 variant identity plus 17p copy loss.Mayo Clinic Laboratories · OncoHeme Next-Generation Sequencing UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 800-533-1710NeoGenomics Laboratories · NeoTYPE Myeloid Disorders Profile UStest info · 12701 Commonwealth Drive, Suite 9, Fort Myers, FL 33913 · 866-776-5907Tempus · Tempus xT Heme UStest info · 600 West Chicago Ave, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654 · 800-739-4137PMID 39811143NCT04585750 highTP53 (17p13) FISH for deletion / copy lossorthogonal validationFISHBone marrow aspirate (fresh, sodium heparin) or an archival fixed-cell pellet / marrow smears from the relapse workup3-7 daysConfirms TP53-aberrant (17p loss / biallelic) call underpinning prognosis and rezatapopt candidacy workup.TP53 (17p13) FISH detects allelic copy loss and 17p deletion that the 2026 relapse panel could not see because it lacked copy-number detection, which is central to reconciling the discrepancy without assuming reversion to wild-type. Biallelic (multi-hit) TP53 status refines both prognosis and the strength of the TP53-aberrant call. Omitting it risks mis-classifying a copy-loss-driven aberration as absent.NeoGenomics Laboratories · TP53/17p FISH preferredtest info · 12701 Commonwealth Drive, Suite 9, Fort Myers, FL 33913 · 866-776-5907High-volume heme cytogenetics/FISH lab with routine TP53 (17p13) probe testing and rapid turnaround.ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 800-522-2787Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 800-533-1710— highRetrieval of the 2019 diagnostic NGS report (TP53 variant identity + VAF)confirmatory—No new specimen; obtain the 2019 diagnostic NGS report and, if re-testing is needed, the archived 2019 fixed-cell pellet or extracted DNA from the originating laboratorySame-day to 1 week (records / archived-DNA request)Anchors TP53 discrepancy reconciliation and the Y220C determination that gates rezatapopt.Retrieving the original 2019 diagnostic report gives the exact TP53 variant identity and VAF that anchor the reconciliation; a founder mutation shared with the 2019 clone would argue the 2026 negative reflects subclonal loss or assay limitation rather than true reversion. Whether that variant is Y220C directly determines rezatapopt candidacy. Without the original identity the discrepancy cannot be adjudicated and the therapy handle stays undefined.—PMID 39811143 highp53 protein immunohistochemistry on marrow biopsy (clone DO-7)orthogonal validationIHCFFPE bone marrow trephine core biopsy or clot section; archival material from the relapse marrow is acceptable3-5 daysConfirms TP53-aberrant target call at the protein level; does not establish Y220C (NGS required).Strong or aberrant (null-pattern) p53 expression by immunohistochemistry on the marrow biopsy is a protein-level correlate of TP53 mutation and multi-hit status in myeloid neoplasms (Saft 2014; Cleven 2015). A positive pattern supports the TP53-aberrant working call independent of the NGS discrepancy, whereas a clean wild-type pattern would prompt scrutiny of the 2019 result. It does not establish the Y220C variant, so it complements rather than replaces variant-level NGS.NeoGenomics Laboratories · p53 IHC preferredtest info · 12701 Commonwealth Drive, Suite 9, Fort Myers, FL 33913 · 866-776-5907Hematopathology reference lab that runs p53 IHC on marrow with pattern-based interpretation (overexpression vs null).ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 800-522-2787Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 800-533-1710PMID 24682512PMID 25412846

docs.title: Research question
docs.text: In relapsed/refractory MDS-related AML that has come back six years after a matched-sibling allo-HCT and is now refractory to FLAG-IDA + venetoclax, what interventions could target the patient's HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME), her CD123- and CD33-positive blasts, a Y220C-contingent TP53 aberration, and a second-transplant platform — gated on retrieving the pending HLA-A*02:01 / HA-1/HA-2 typing that the whole immunotherapy axis hangs on?

docs.title: Patient profile (scrubbed)
docs.text:
• Woman, age band 50-59, ECOG 1.
  • AML, myelodysplasia-related (AML-MR), relapsed/refractory; transformed from prior MDS (RCMD, IPSS-R high/very-high, ~2019). Extramedullary right-thigh myeloid sarcoma on MRI (adverse feature).
  • Marrow ~85% blasts (June 2026); peripheral blasts 58->82% (late June 2026). Refractory to FLAG-IDA + venetoclax reinduction.
  • Late relapse ~6 years after matched-sibling PBSC allo-HCT (~2020, CR sustained 72 months); pattern consistent with graft-versus-leukemia escape, not graft failure.
  • TP53 — aberrant, pending confirmation (not resolved in either direction). 2019 diagnostic NGS pathogenic; 2026 relapse NGS negative but on a limited assay (LOD ~2% VAF, no CNV, not MRD-grade). Working call: TP53-aberrant pending. TP53 Y220C — unknown; rezatapopt is contingent on it.
  • HLA-A*02:01 — unknown / pending retrieval (allele-level ~2020 typing not in records on hand). HLA-A*24:02 — unknown / pending. HA-1 / HA-2 minor antigens — unknown / pending for both patient and sibling donor.
  • CD33 — positive by flow (confirmed, qualitative). CD123 — positive by flow (confirmed, qualitative). Quantitative antigen density requested for both.
  • FLT3, IDH1, IDH2 — negative (confirmed, 2019). NPM1 — wild-type on available panels.
  • Cytogenetics — complex, adverse. 2026 relapse: gain of 5' MECOM, del(5q), del(7q), KMT2A amplification (4 copies), del(8cen), del(16q22). Shared del(5q)/del(7q) + TP53 founder across timepoints points to evolution of the original clone (recipient-origin), not a donor-derived or secondary leukemia.
  • No numeric organ-function labs (CrCl, LFTs, cardiac) supplied. Fitness / cardiac assessment is an explicit open item.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
• Efficacy/toxicity weight: 0.75 (efficacy-leaning), flagged as provisional — to be revisited once fitness is known.
  • Toxicity vetoes: none.
  • Modality constraints: none. Second allo-HCT (HCT2) and cellular/immunotherapy explicitly acceptable; trials acceptable including travel.
  • Free text: Curative intent. The explicit reason for the run is HLA-restricted immunotherapy eligibility (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME), gated on HLA-A*02:01 status and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor; surfacing and de-risking that pathway is the priority.
  • Trial preference: prefers trials — yes.

docs.title: Target validation paths
docs.text: Two workups decide whether this case's central question has an answer. Allele-level HLA-A02:01 typing gates the HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T programs (TSC-100/101 via NCT05473910, the Bleakley HA-1 platform via NCT03326921, BSB-1001 via NCT06704152) and the WT1-C4 and PRAME-directed cells that share that allele; HLA-A24:02, pulled in the same run, keeps a WT1-siTCR fallback alive if A02:01 is negative. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of both the patient and her HLA-identical sibling donor then establishes the recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch those TCR-T products require. If HLA-A02:01 and A*24:02 both type negative, this report has no within-scope HLA-restricted recommendation, and the next conversation about standard salvage care belongs to the treating team.

docs.title: HLA-restricted immunotherapy
docs.text: Two assays are essential and gate everything the case was submitted to surface. High-resolution HLA class I typing resolves the allele-level HLA-A02:01 status that every HLA-restricted lever hangs on, with A24:02 read in parallel so a negative A*02:01 does not close the door before the WT1-siTCR fallback is checked. Retrieve the allele-level ~2020 transplant typing report first and repeat high-resolution typing only if that record cannot be confirmed; turnaround is 3 to 7 days, with STAT available. HA-1/HA-2 minor-antigen genotyping is the second essential gate: HLA-identical siblings can still differ at these minor loci, so both the patient and the donor must be genotyped to establish the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch that TSC-100/101 requires. It is an uncommon catalog test that runs 1 to 3 weeks as a specialized send-out and needs a fresh donor sample plus donor consent, so line those up early. Two high-priority reads add context rather than gate: standardized WT1 qPCR confirms the WT1-directed target and sets a quantitative MRD baseline, and a PRAME expression read (flow or RNA) establishes whether the PRAME-directed lever has a target present, since PRAME in AML is variable rather than universal.

docs.title: TP53
docs.text: TP53 is held aberrant pending confirmation, and the workup is built to resolve the 2019-mutant versus 2026-negative discrepancy without collapsing it to wild-type on a 2%-LOD panel that reads no copy number. Two essential steps carry it: retrieving the 2019 diagnostic variant identity and VAF from the original NGS report, and running a copy-number-capable heme NGS panel that reports TP53 at the variant level. A documented Y220C at either step is the specific handle for the Y220C-selective reactivator rezatapopt via NCT06616636; any other TP53 variant, or a true absence, removes that option. Two high-priority orthogonal reads corroborate the call from archival material at no new procedure: p53 protein IHC (an overexpression or complete-null pattern supports a functionally aberrant TP53) and 17p/TP53 deletion FISH (detects the copy loss the limited 2026 panel could not see).

docs.title: CD33
docs.text: Quantitative CD33 antigen-density flow (ABC/MESF) is the essential read here. It converts the qualitative CD33-positive call into the surface-density measure that predicts benefit from CD33-directed ADC therapy, since low density blunts gemtuzumab ozogamicin. Request the density quantification explicitly on the phenotyping specimen, because it is not a default readout. A medium-priority germline genotype of the CD33 rs12459419 splicing SNP refines the prediction: the CC genotype retains the target epitope and predicts better response, while a T allele blunts it. It does not gate on its own but tempers expectations alongside the density read.

docs.title: CD123
docs.text: Quantitative CD123 antigen-density flow (ABC/MESF) is the essential read for selecting among the CD123-directed agents (tagraxofusp, pivekimab sunirine). It can run on the same specimen and draw as the CD33 density request, and a dual CD33/CD123 density supports a combined-targeting strategy. Without it, CD123-directed cytoreduction ahead of a cellular or transplant consolidation is chosen blind to the predictive marker.

docs.title: Second-transplant platform
docs.text: Two high-priority confirmatory reads underpin the transplant plan. STR chimerism on flow-sorted CD34+ blasts confirms that the relapse arises from recipient-origin leukemia rather than a donor-derived or secondary leukemia; the sex-matched sibling donor rules out XY-FISH as a shortcut, and CD34+ sorting keeps normal donor hematopoiesis from masking the blast compartment. A full metaphase karyotype plus MECOM and KMT2A FISH at relapse confirms the adverse cytogenetic features (MECOM rearrangement, KMT2A amplification) that shape prognosis and trial eligibility.

docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text: 29 trial rows, 15 clinical-evidence rows, 16 preclinical rows, and 13 target-validation rows feed this synthesis. This is the Experimental table — the feature-targeting investigational options only. It carries 21 rows: a rank-1 shared HLA/HA workup, five ranked therapeutic options (the Iomab-B backbone, the HA-1 TCR-T that motivated the referral, tagraxofusp, the multiantigen TAA-T hedge, and the vetoed pivekimab), and fifteen surfaced-but-not-ranked options flagged by reason (three HA-1/HA-2 products consolidated under the ranked approach, two thin-evidence handles, three not-enrollable options, seven discontinued programs). Agreement scores span 1.0 (the workup and the Iomab-B backbone, both unanimous) down to -0.2 (flotetuzumab, twice dissented). All five personas converged on the Iomab-B second-transplant platform; four ranked the HA-1 TCR-T; one veto landed, on pivekimab, from the conservative on veno-occlusive-disease grounds ahead of transplant. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin — FDA-approved for R/R CD33+ AML — is routed out of this table to the co-equal Standard-of-care table; the menin inhibitors an upstream sweep surfaced against KMT2A amplification are target-absent and appear there too, not here.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
The pending HLA-A*02:01 typing is the master switch, and the ranking is scoped to the targetable features — not to standard AML care. The primary reason this case was submitted is HLA-restricted immunotherapy, and every lever inside it (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1-C4, PRAME-directed cells) is presented on HLA-A*02:01, whose allele-level status is not in the records on hand. An RNA- or EHR-placeholder-level "typed in 2020" is not enough: the therapy gate is the allele call plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and HLA-identical siblings can still differ at that minor locus. That is why the rank-1 action here is the typing itself, not a drug.

  • The ranking is targetable-feature-scoped, and it is one of two co-equal tables. This Experimental table carries only feature-targeting investigational options: the workup, the HLA-conditional HA-1 TCR-T rec, and interventions that target the patient's other stated handles (CD123, WT1/PRAME, the HCT2 platform). Approved feature-targeting drugs are routed to the Standard-of-care table — gemtuzumab ozogamicin (approved for R/R CD33+ AML, a population that includes this patient) lives there, not in this ranking. Genuinely non-targeting standard care — including the menin inhibitors an upstream sweep surfaced against her KMT2A amplification (a copy-number gain, not the rearrangement menin inhibitors need) — is out of scope for the feature ranking entirely and is the treating team's separate conversation.
  • If HLA-A02:01 is negative, this case has no within-scope HLA-restricted recommendation; standard-of-care for relapsed/refractory AML lies outside Libby's targetable-feature ranking and should be pursued through the treating team's normal care channel. One door stays ajar: if A02:01 is negative but A24:02 positive, the A24:02-restricted WT1-siTCR (TBI-1301) becomes the fallback lever — which is exactly why both alleles must be pulled in parallel.
  • Practical workup logistics: pull the ~2020 donor-registry / transplant typing report first (HLA typing 3-7 days, STAT available); HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is a specialized send-out (1-3 weeks) that needs a fresh sample from the sibling donor and may route through the ALLOHA (NCT05473910) trial screening pathway. The whole HLA-restricted plan also assumes transplant-grade fitness that no organ-function labs have yet established.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• HLA-A*02:01-restricted cellular consolidation (gated): HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T (NCT05473910, PMID 38683966, NCT03326921, NCT06704152); WT1 and PRAME approaches on the same allele gate.
  • CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy conditioning + second allo-HCT: Iomab-B / 131I-apamistamab (PMID 39298738, NCT02665065, NCT07157514).
  • CD123-directed cytoreduction: tagraxofusp (PMID 31018069, NCT06561152); pivekimab sunirine (PMID 38423051, NCT03386513); flotetuzumab CD123xCD3 (PMID 32929488, PMID 33057635).
  • HLA-independent multiantigen and dual-antigen cellular therapy: TAA-T PRAME/WT1/Survivin (PMID 33270816, NCT02203903); dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T (NCT04010877, NCT04156256).
  • TP53-directed p53 reactivators: rezatapopt (Y220C-selective, PMID 40608889, NCT06616636); eprenetapopt (pan-reactivator, PMID 36990622).
  • CD33-directed ADC (routed to the Standard-of-care table, not ranked here): gemtuzumab ozogamicin, FDA-approved for R/R CD33+ AML (PMID 11432892, PMID 25008258).

docs.title: Rank 1. High-resolution HLA typing (A02:01 / A24:02) + HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor — diagnostic gate
docs.text: The confirmatory test that decides whether the referral's own question has an answer: it resolves the allele status and minor-antigen mismatch that every HLA-restricted lever is gated on.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is a records-and-assay action, not a therapy, so the evidence base is the eligibility criteria of the programs it unlocks rather than an effect size. HLA-A02:01 gates the Bleakley HA-1 TCR-T program (NCT03326921, the closest published precedent, PMID 38683966) and the commercial TSC-100/101 platform (NCT05473910); the HA-1/HA-2 genotyping establishes the recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch those TCR-T products require (PMID 31275297). A24:02, pulled in parallel, is what keeps the WT1-siTCR fallback alive if A*02:01 is negative.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: As a gate it either opens or closes the whole HLA-restricted axis; there is no partial credit. The point of ranking it first is that the referral cannot be answered until it returns, and a negative allele call forecloses the rank-3 rec outright rather than downgrading it.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• None from the test itself — blood draw, or retrieval of the archived 2020 typing report.
  • The only cost is time: HLA typing runs 3-7 days (STAT available); HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is a 1-3 week specialized send-out that needs a fresh sibling-donor sample.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was unanimous. A non-toxic test that gates every downstream lever is the one thing all five personas agree comes first, and none raised a mechanism or preference objection.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Pull the ~2020 donor-registry / transplant typing before re-drawing; allele-level A02:01 from that record is acceptable if it can be confirmed. HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is uncommon as a catalog test — confirm availability at an ASHI immunogenetics lab or route it through the ALLOHA (NCT05473910) screening pathway, and secure donor consent early. Run A02:01 and A*24:02 together, not sequentially.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Nothing HLA-restricted can be scoped, ranked, or enrolled until this returns, so it precedes even the unanimously endorsed transplant backbone. It carries an agreement score of 1.0 for the same reason the Iomab-B backbone does — no dissent, no veto — but it sits above it because it is the prerequisite, not the platform.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Confirmatory assay What it resolves Turnaround / tissue Reference High-resolution HLA class I typing HLA-A02:01 and A24:02 allele status (master gate) 3-7 days; whole blood or 2020 typing record NCT05473910 HA-1 / HA-2 minor-antigen genotyping Recipient HA-1(H)+ / donor HA-1- mismatch 1-3 weeks; patient + sibling-donor blood NCT03326921, PMID 31275297

docs.title: Rank 2. Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) conditioning + second allo-HCT
docs.text: The curative backbone all five personas endorsed — the randomized way to carry an 85%-blast marrow into a second transplant, gated on a fitness workup not yet done.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: SIERRA is the one randomized phase 3 in the dossier that fits the actual problem (PMID 39298738, n=153; NCT02665065). Durable CR at 180 days reached 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with the radioconjugate versus 0% (0-4.7) on physician's-choice conventional care, p<0.0001, and EFS favored it at HR 0.23 (95% CI 0.15-0.34). The design carries active disease into allo-HCT rather than demanding a remission chemotherapy can no longer deliver, which is the crux of a curative plan against 85% blasts. Two limits are load-bearing: the endpoint is a surrogate — ITT OS was flat at HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41), diluted by 52% crossover to the radioconjugate — and SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so reading it onto a prior-HCT relapse is indirect.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, and the honesty is in the qualifier: this is the strongest evidence tier in the file, but it was earned in first-transplant patients, so the durable-CR rate is a reasonable expectation for the conditioning mechanism rather than a proven number for a second transplant. Whether it holds depends on fitness that has not been measured and on prior-HCT eligibility the go-forward trial has to confirm.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs occurred in 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care — as conditioning the radioconjugate adds essentially no incremental grade 3+ burden.
  • Standard transplant-conditioning cytopenias, infection and mucositis apply on top of that.
  • Second-transplant treatment-related mortality is uncharacterized by SIERRA and is the real unknown here.
  • No cardiac, renal or hepatic labs on file: this conditioning cannot be called deliverable until that clearance lands.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented and none vetoed. The conservative and concensusite led with it on evidence tier and guideline fit; the critic held it at moderate on the surrogate endpoint and indirectness without objecting; the risktaker and advocate ranked it just below their stated-priority immunotherapy because it is the platform that makes cellular consolidation deliverable. The only mechanism-level flag is mild: radioconjugate marrow injury could compromise engraftment if the HCT2 platform is not secured.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCT02665065 is closed and the go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting, so timing and access are open. ELN 2022 and NCCN AML v3.2026 both keep second allo-HCT + clinical-trial enrollment in play for relapsed disease; Iomab-B enters through the category-2A clinical-trial route, not a drug-level category. The fitness / organ-function workup the preferences flag as open must precede conditioning, and the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once that lands.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It sits at agreement score 1.0, tied with the workup and ahead of every therapeutic, because all five personas endorsed it and none dissented. It ranks below the workup only because the workup is a prerequisite; it ranks above the HA-1 TCR-T (0.8) because the TCR-T is gated on pending typing and is delivered on top of this platform, not instead of it.

docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Iomab-B conditioning + allo-HCT (SIERRA) dCR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001; EFS HR 0.23 G3+ TRAE 59.7% vs 59.2% (parity) PMID 39298738, NCT02665065 131I-apamistamab RIT conditioning (go-forward) Engraftment / remission / survival (pending) Not yet reported NCT07157514

docs.title: Rank 3. HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001)
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201:positive. Foreclosed if the test is negative.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Krakow 2024 is the closest published precedent for the patient's primary handle (PMID 38683966, single-arm phase 1, n=9; NCT03326921). Four of nine post-allo-HCT relapses achieved or maintained CR, one past two years, with zero DLTs, zero CRS and zero ICANS. The commercial route is TSC-100 / TSC-101 (NCT05473910) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152), all recruiting. This is a feasibility cohort, not an efficacy result: n=9, no comparator, no pre-specified efficacy endpoint, so the 4-of-9 CR cannot be separated from the lymphodepletion effect or the natural clonal course.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Assuming the positive branch — A*02:01 confirmed and the HA-1 mismatch present — the likelihood is genuinely uncertain but carries curative intent, because HA-1 sits only on blood-lineage cells, so a durable graft-versus-leukemia remission is the plausible upside and it comes with almost no collateral. The signal is a clean 4-of-9 CR rather than a powered estimate. A negative typing result forecloses this rec entirely; it does not downgrade it.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Zero CRS and zero ICANS across 9 patients — the opposite of what a T-cell redirection therapy usually risks.
  • Lymphodepletion drove grade 3-4 neutropenia and grade 3-5 infections (Legionella and S. aureus pneumonia reported).
  • Two cases of mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD, attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal rather than the TCR-T.
  • No toxicity veto applies (toxicity_vetoes is empty and the safety read is clean).

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented or vetoed; four ranked it. The critic ranked it but refused to dress up n=9 as efficacy — an evidence-quality caution that is not biomarker-contingent and persists in the positive branch. The conservative declined to rank it on the same evidence-tier grounds but explicitly did not veto, calling the clean safety read the opposite of what they worry about. The risktaker and advocate pushed to rank it higher on the referral's own lens. The mechanism-level risk is modest: TCR-T kinetics may lag an 85%-blast marrow and antigen-loss escape is possible, but lineage-restricted killing limits off-target collateral.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Three recruiting trial slots match the preference for trials. Sequencing is real: an 85%-blast marrow needs cytoreduction and the HCT2 platform in place before TCR-T can go in as consolidation, so this is not a standalone. NCCN AML v3.2026's category-2A clinical-trial-enrollment route is the guideline hook; there is no drug-level category, and ELN 2022 offers no consensus on sequencing DLI versus second transplant versus cellular therapy for post-HCT relapse.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It ranks third rather than first despite being the referral's stated priority for two reasons that survive the positive branch: agreement score 0.8 versus the platform's 1.0 (the conservative's evidence-tier reservation keeps it off five-of-five), and the eligibility gate that means it cannot even be called deliverable until the rank-1 workup returns. The advocate argued it belongs above Iomab-B on the user's lens; the PI ranks it just below, because the platform is what makes this consolidation possible and carries unanimous endorsement.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference HA-1 TCR-T (Bleakley / Fred Hutch) CR 4/9, one >2y 0 CRS, 0 ICANS; lymphodepletion cytopenia/infection PMID 38683966, NCT03326921 TSC-100 / TSC-101 (ALLOHA) Safety / chimerism / relapse (pending) Not yet reported NCT05473910 BSB-1001 (HA-1 TCR-T) Safety / dose / activity (pending) Not yet reported NCT06704152

docs.title: Rank 4. Tagraxofusp (SL-401, CD123-directed IL-3/diphtheria-toxin fusion)
docs.text: A labeled CD123 agent with a real safety algorithm, but its headline efficacy is BPDCN cross-tumor and its capillary-leak deaths demand organ-function labs first.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The registration study is Pemmaraju 2019 (PMID 31018069, open-label single-arm phase 2). First-line CR/clinical CR was 72% (21/29) at 12 ug/kg — but the disease was BPDCN, not AML, so that number is cross-tumor read-across, not indication data, and an 85%-blast AML marrow is not where it was earned. An AML-specific route exists: tagraxofusp plus low-intensity cladribine/cytarabine in CD123-positive R/R AML (NCT06561152). It targets a confirmed feature (CD123 by flow), so it is not biomarker-gated, but the quantitative CD123 antigen density that predicts benefit is still pending.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-uncertain for this marrow. The only efficacy number is a first-line BPDCN result, and nothing in the dossier establishes that it transfers to high-burden AML. The CD123 target is confirmed present, which is the argument for it; the density read that would tell you whether the handle is strong enough is not yet in.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Capillary leak syndrome in 19% (boxed warning), with one death reported in each dose subgroup.
  • Hepatic transaminase elevation (ALT 64%, AST 60% any grade) and hypoalbuminemia (55%).
  • With no baseline albumin or cardiac/hepatic workup on file, this is exactly the toxicity profile that needs fitness data before it can be started safely.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Only the conservative ranked it, and chose it over pivekimab and flotetuzumab specifically for its worked-out capillary-leak management algorithm — the one CD123 option with an FDA label and years of post-marketing safety data. The critic and concensusite filed qualified cautions rather than dissents: the 72% CR does not transfer from BPDCN, and the agent has no AML guideline standing. Those cautions are why this is carried with caveats despite no formal dissent — presenting an off-label cross-tumor agent as unqualified standard care would misstate its footing. No plausible counter-productive mechanism; the efficacy risk is non-transfer, not antagonism.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: FDA-approved in BPDCN only; no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing, so AML use is off-label. The capillary-leak algorithm covers albumin thresholds, daily weights, blood-pressure monitoring and dose holds — but it needs a baseline albumin and cardiac read to run against. NCT06561152 is the enrollable AML route.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score 0.2 places it above the two dissented CD-ADCs below it. It clears gemtuzumab (0.0) because gemtuzumab drew active dissent that its own data show no benefit in this stratum, whereas tagraxofusp drew only qualified cross-tumor cautions. That is a thin margin, and the narrative carries the off-label reality that the score alone does not.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Tagraxofusp monotherapy (BPDCN registration) CR 72% (first-line BPDCN — cross-tumor) Capillary leak 19% with deaths; ALT 64% PMID 31018069 Tagraxofusp + cladribine/cytarabine (R/R AML) Safety / response (pending) Capillary-leak / hepatic risk NCT06561152

docs.title: Rank 5. Multiantigen leukemia-specific donor T cells (PRAME/WT1/Survivin/NY-ESO-1)
docs.text: The A02:01-independent immunotherapy hedge — targets WT1 and PRAME without the master-switch gate, enrollable now, but modest published activity.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Lulla 2021 is the published precedent for this donor T-cell product (PMID 33270816, single-arm phase 1, n=25; NCT02203903). In the active-disease cohort, 1 of 8 reached CR and 1 a PR; across the whole cohort median leukemia-free and overall survival were not reached at 1.9 years. The product primes T cells against PRAME, WT1 and Survivin, so it hits two of the patient's named handles without depending on a single HLA-A*02:01 gate — which is the whole point of carrying it. It is a small early-phase cohort, and the responses in overt disease are modest.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-modest, but with a strategic value the number alone misses. The 2-of-8 objective-response rate in active disease is not a strong salvage signal, so this is a hedge rather than a lead: it is the one immunotherapy route that stays open if HLA-A*02:01 types negative and forecloses the HA-1 axis. WT1 and PRAME expression on the blasts is not yet confirmed, and that read gates eligibility.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No grade >2 acute GVHD and no extensive chronic GVHD across 25 recipients — a clean donor-T-cell safety profile.
  • Delivered in the post-transplant setting, so lymphodepletion and infection risks track the transplant rather than the product.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona ranked it, so it carries no agreement score; the advocate flagged it as a live fallback that sidesteps the A*02:01 gate. That is why it is carried with caveats rather than as a lead — the board weighed it as a hedge, not a top-tier choice. The mechanism-level risk is low and cuts the right way: multi-antigen targeting limits the single-antigen escape that a documented clonally-evolving relapse invites.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recruiting at two US sites (Children's National, Johns Hopkins) in the post-HCT setting the patient is heading toward, which matches prefers-trials. Confirm adult enrollment and post-HCT timing, and confirm WT1/PRAME expression first. The product can potentially be generated from the existing sibling donor. Keep it live even if HLA typing forecloses the A*02:01-restricted TCR options.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score 0.0, tied with pivekimab, but it ranks above the vetoed pivekimab because it carries no veto and its clean safety profile fits the efficacy-leaning-but-fitness-constrained picture. It ranks below tagraxofusp (0.2) because a board persona actually ranked tagraxofusp, whereas TAA-T was surfaced as an unranked fallback. It is the A*02:01-independent immunotherapy option, which no other ranked row provides.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text:
Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference TAA-T PRAME/WT1/Survivin (active disease) 1 CR + 1 PR of 8; LFS/OS not reached at 1.9y No grade >2 acute GVHD across n=25 PMID 33270816, NCT02203903

Pivekimab sunirine (rank 6, CD123 ADC, not recommended) is a ranked row held under the conservative's veto rather than a full narrative — its evidence and dissent are in the ranked-prioritization table below and its rationale in recommendations.jsonl. Two personas ranked it as a debulking bridge on its own R/R AML data (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40), but the conservative vetoed it on a documented veno-occlusive-disease signal ahead of HCT2 in a patient with no hepatic labs on file. The veto is conditional and liftable — it reinstates the moment baseline bilirubin, transaminases and a hepatic read clear it — but the condition is unmet, so the veto stands and the row stays visible.

docs.title: Also considered — not ranked (feature-targeting investigational)
docs.text:
Fifteen feature-targeting investigational options were surfaced but not ranked as live top-tier choices. Each carries a flag for why.

  • Consolidated into the ranked HA-1 approach (rank 3): TSC-100 and BSB-1001 (commercial and newer HA-1 TCR-T products, NCT05473910, NCT06704152) and TSC-101 (the HA-2 arm, opens if the mismatch is at HA-2). These are individual products of the one HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T approach ranked at rank 3; they share its gate and board signal and point back to it rather than being scored separately.
  • Thin evidence (no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy yet): CBX-250, the off-the-shelf CG1/A02:01 T-cell engager (NCT06994676) — a genuinely enrollable A02:01 option with a no-manufacturing-lead-time advantage at 11 US sites, but a first-in-human phase 1 with zero efficacy readout, so it cannot carry a live rank. Rezatapopt, the Y220C-selective p53 reactivator (NCT06616636, Carter 2025 AML preclinical PMID 40608889) — double-gated on confirming TP53 aberrant and specifically Y220C, with no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy; it jumps into contention the moment a Y220C variant confirms.
  • Not enrollable now (disease-state or geographic barrier): FH-WT1-E50, the open WT1 A02:01 TCR-T (NCT07645469) — enrolls MRD-positive disease, so it is a consolidation-phase option for after cytoreduction, not a fit for an 85%-blast marrow. The dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T* constructs (NCT04010877, NCT04156256) — they match the profile's escape-hedging logic but are China-only single sites (one with a stale registry status), impractical against the recruiting US options even though the patient accepts travel.
  • Unavailable (discontinued / completed, no successor): Flotetuzumab (CD123xCD3 DART, NCT02152956, PMID 32929488) carries the most relevant CD123 salvage data and a TP53-abnormal-marrow signal, but MacroGenics deprioritized it — the critic dissented that the TP53 signal is post-hoc correlative (PMID 33057635) and the concensusite on guideline grounds; the CD123xCD3 mechanism is otherwise covered by CBX-250. Vibecotamab (Xencor, terminated, MRD-setting). NTLA-5001 (Intellia WT1 TCR-T, terminated). BPX-701 (Bellicum PRAME TCR-T, terminated; the open PRAME route is the rank-5 TAA-T). WT1-TCRc4 (Chapuis prophylaxis precedent, PMID 31235963; succeeded by FH-WT1-E50). WT1-siTCR TBI-1301 (A24:02-restricted, PMID 28860210) — the A24:02 negative-branch fallback the advocate flagged to keep an immunotherapy route open if A02:01 is negative; no open successor trial exists today, which is exactly why both alleles must be typed in parallel. Eprenetapopt* (pan-p53 reactivator, PMID 36990622) — the replication-failure exhibit: strong single-arm ORR, then a negative randomized TP53-mutant MDS phase 3.

Two things are not in this section by design. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is FDA-approved for R/R CD33+ AML including this patient, so it is routed to the Standard-of-care table, not surfaced here. The NPM1-directed TCR-T trials (MB-dNPM1-TCR.1, BSB-2002) target a mutant-NPM1 neoantigen this NPM1-wild-type patient does not carry — target-absent, like the menin inhibitors, so they are excluded rather than surfaced.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity (Low/Moderate/High by grade-3+ rates and any treatment-related death). Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that the intervention could work against the therapeutic goal — engraftment failure, antigen-loss escape, a transplant-sinking toxicity — not a patient side effect. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. The lead HLA-restricted lever (HA-1 TCR-T) rests on a single-arm n=9 feasibility cohort with no comparator; the transplant backbone (SIERRA) is randomized but reports a surrogate endpoint with flat ITT OS diluted by 52% crossover, and enrolled first-transplant patients. Tagraxofusp's efficacy is BPDCN cross-tumor; flotetuzumab's TP53 signal is an unadjusted post-hoc correlative subgroup on a discontinued program.
  • Compartment / biomarker dependencies. The rank-3 HA-1 TCR-T assumes HLA-A*02:01 confirmation plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch; without both, it is foreclosed, not downgraded. TP53 status is unresolved in either direction — do not down-call to wild-type on a 2%-LOD/no-CNV panel — and a confirmed Y220C would open rezatapopt as a new axis. CD123 and CD33 are confirmed present but the quantitative antigen density that predicts ADC/immunotoxin benefit is pending for both.
  • What would change the ranking. A negative HLA-A02:01 call moves rank 3 to non-applicable and turns the case to the A24:02 fallback or standard care. Documented organ-function / hepatic labs lift the conservative's pivekimab veto and reinstate it as a rankable debulking bridge. A confirmed TP53 Y220C variant introduces rezatapopt above the current CD123/CD33 tier. A prior-HCT-eligible go-forward Iomab-B slot (NCT07157514 opening) would firm up rank 2's deliverability.
  • Re-scoping caveat. The 0.75 efficacy weight is provisional: if the fitness / goals-of-care assessment returns a frailer picture than curative-intent transplant assumes, the whole ranking shifts toward tolerability and the transplant backbone itself may come off the table.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text: Re-run 2026-07-25 by the PI agent under the two-table contract, from a complete, schema-valid dossier: profile.json, preferences.json, 13 target-validation rows, 29 trials, 15 clinical-evidence rows, 16 preclinical rows, 25 accessibility rows, the 12-row standard_of_care.jsonl, and the board's 5 positions plus 20 critiques. This is now the Experimental table — feature-targeting investigational options only. Every feature-targeting investigational option in the dossier is surfaced (21 rows): six ranked live (workup, Iomab-B, HA-1 TCR-T, tagraxofusp, TAA-T, and the vetoed pivekimab) and fifteen flagged by surfaced_reason — three HA-1/HA-2 products consolidated under the rank-3 approach (TSC-100/TSC-101/BSB-1001), two thin-evidence handles (CBX-250 first-in-human, rezatapopt double-gated on Y220C), three not-enrollable (FH-WT1-E50 MRD-mismatch, two China-only dual CAR-Ts), and seven unavailable/discontinued (flotetuzumab, vibecotamab, NTLA-5001, BPX-701, WT1-TCRc4, the A24:02 WT1-siTCR fallback, eprenetapopt). Gemtuzumab ozogamicin was routed OUT of this table to the Standard-of-care table because it is FDA-approved for R/R CD33+ AML including this patient; tagraxofusp and pivekimab stay here because their approvals are BPDCN-only (off-label/investigational for this AML patient). Genuinely non-targeting or target-absent drugs the upstream sweep surfaced — the menin inhibitors against KMT2A amplification (a copy-number gain, not the rearrangement menin inhibitors need) and the NPM1-directed TCR-T trials in an NPM1-wild-type patient — were excluded rather than surfaced; the menin inhibitors are logged on the Standard-of-care table as approved-but-target-absent. Endorsed/dissent/veto sets and agreement scores were computed from the round-1 picks and round-2 critiques; the single conditional veto (conservative, pivekimab) was preserved as a not_recommended row rather than overridden, because its stated lifting condition — documented hepatic/albumin baselines — is unmet. Biomarker gating: of several non-confirmed biomarkers (TP53 ngs_pending, TP53 Y220C, HLA-A02:01, HLA-A24:02, HA-1/HA-2), the one-dimension cap selected the master switch HLA-A02:01 for the shared workup row (rank 1) and the hla_a0201:positive tagging (HA-1 TCR-T and its consolidated products, CBX-250); TP53/Y220C, A*24:02 and HA-1/HA-2 were carried as open questions and caveats rather than a parallel branch, and no negative-branch ranking was emitted. Reference verification ran over every promoted PMID/NCT: key anchors were re-resolved live against PubMed (SIERRA 39298738, HA-1 TCR-T 38683966, pivekimab 38423051, TAA-T 33270816, HA-1 locus 9820596, MiHA genotyping 31275297), and the remainder were carried verbatim from the already-verified upstream dossier; all matched claims, none corrected, none nulled.

docs.title: 1. Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning Iomab-B, 131I-apamistamab, iodine-131 apamistamab, BC8, anti-CD45 RIT, apamistamab
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: radioimmunotherapy   Verified: 2026-07-24

CD45-targeted radioimmunotherapy is the most directly relevant way to carry an 85%-blast marrow into a second transplant, and SIERRA showed it can do that in active R/R AML. docs.title: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / BSB-1001) (ha1-tcr-t)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1lowThis is the reason the case was sent, and the upside is a durable graft-versus-leukemia remission with almost no collateral: Krakow 2024 saw CR achieved or maintained in 4 of 9 post-HCT relapses, zero DLTs, and no CRS or ICANS, with one patient past two years. HA-1 sits only on blood-lineage cells, so the killing stays in the compartment we want it. The catch is real and I will not bury it: eligibility gates on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and none of that is typed yet, so backing this pick is a bet that the pending typing comes back in our favor. n=9 is a feasibility cohort, not an efficacy result.Gated on unresolved HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1(H) genotyping of both patient and sibling donor; the whole pathway collapses if either misses; n=9 feasibility cohort with no efficacy powering; Needs cytoreduction and a second-transplant platform in place first; 85% blast burden may outpace TCR-T kinetics conservative——did not pick— critic2lowThis is the stated reason the case was sent, so I will rank it, but I will not dress up n=9 as efficacy evidence. Krakow 2024 is a single-arm feasibility cohort with no comparator and no pre-specified efficacy endpoint, so the 4-of-9 CR cannot be pulled apart from the lymphodepletion effect or the natural clonal course. What it does show, backed by the Dossa 2018 construct work, is a clean safety read: zero DLTs, zero CRS, zero ICANS across 9 patients. Eligibility is still unconfirmed, since HLA-A*02:01 and the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch are both pending, so any support here stays conditional on the typing coming back in favor.ROBINS-I confounding domain: single-arm with no comparator, so 4/9 CR cannot be separated from lymphodepletion or clonal course; n=9 feasibility cohort with no pre-specified efficacy endpoint and no efficacy powering; Eligibility unconfirmed: HLA-A*02:01 status and the HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch are both pending concensusite3lowHLA-restricted cellular therapy is the reason the case was sent, and the guidelines give it a home, but only at the level of the route rather than the product. NCCN AML v3.2026 marks clinical-trial enrollment as the category-2A preferred path for relapsed/refractory disease, and ELN 2022 keeps adoptive cellular approaches open for post-transplant relapse, so HA-1 TCR-T is guideline-aligned as a trial (NCT03326921; commercial TSC-100 on NCT05473910). What it does not have is a drug-level category or any efficacy powering, since Krakow 2024 is an n=9 feasibility cohort (4 of 9 in CR, zero CRS/ICANS). And the whole lever is gated on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, none of which is typed yet.Guideline support is for trial enrollment as a category, not for this specific product; no NCCN drug-level category and no efficacy-powered data (n=9 feasibility); Eligibility population unconfirmed: HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative genotyping of patient and sibling donor are all pending; ELN 2022 offers no consensus sequencing of DLI vs second transplant vs cellular therapy for post-HCT relapse, so this sits in a genuinely under-specified guideline zone advocate1lowThis is the exact thing the case was submitted to surface. The preferences name HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason for the run, and HA-1 TCR-T is the primary handle inside it. Everything the user asked for lines up: curative intent, a trial route (prefers_trials is true, with three recruiting slots in NCT05473910, NCT03326921, and NCT06704152), no toxicity vetoed, no modality ruled out. Krakow 2024 read clean on safety, zero CRS and zero ICANS across 9 patients, 4 in CR and one past two years. I will not pretend eligibility is settled: it gates on HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch, and neither the patient nor the sibling donor is typed yet. Backing this pick means backing the workup that de-risks it, which the preferences themselves call the priority.Fully satisfied preference axes: the stated HLA-restricted immunotherapy priority, prefers_trials (three recruiting slots), curative intent, and the efficacy-leaning weight. No veto or modality constraint touches it.; In tension: eligibility is unconfirmed. HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1(H) genotyping of both patient and sibling donor are pending, and the whole pick is contingent on them coming back in favor.; Sequencing reality: an 85%-blast marrow needs cytoreduction and an HCT2 platform before TCR-T can go in as consolidation, so this is not a standalone.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticdissentevidence_qualityYou discount the 4-of-9 CR as inseparable from lymphodepletion, but in a post-HCT relapse there is no ethical randomized comparator to hold out for, so that standard forecloses the one lever with curative upside. The safety read is what makes the bet asymmetric: zero CRS and zero ICANS across 9 patients (pmid:38683966), on a lineage-restricted mechanism that keeps the killing in the blood compartment. n=9 is thin, granted, but I would rather act on a clean signal than wait for evidence this setting will never generate. risktakeradvocatequalifiedpreference_fitWe agree HA-1 TCR-T is the right lead on the preference lens, and I put it first too. My one push: the pick is entirely gated on pending HLA-A*02:01 and the HA-1(H) recipient-positive / donor-negative typing (nct:NCT03326921), so a rank 1 that collapses if the switch reads negative may deserve a deliverable-now platform ranked right beside it. Backing this means backing the parallel workup hard, not just the slot. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitYour evidence-only read frames HA-1 TCR-T as a bare n=9 feasibility gamble, but it carries a guideline home that lens misses: NCCN AML v3.2026 makes clinical-trial enrollment the category-2A preferred path for R/R disease (nct:NCT03326921). That trial route is the actual justification for ranking a product with no drug-level listing, a firmer footing than the reason the case was sent. Reading it only on the n=9 cohort understates where it sits in the guideline framework. advocaterisktakerendorsepreference_fitThis is the ranking that reads the referral the way it was written: the free_text names HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason for the run and calls de-risking it the priority, and you led with HA-1 TCR-T on a recruiting trial route (prefers_trials is true). That is exactly the lever the user asked to surface first, not a slot you had to justify around the guideline options. Krakow 2024's clean read (zero CRS, zero ICANS, pmid:38683966) means the 0.75 efficacy weight does not have to trade against tolerability here. advocatecriticqualifiedpreference_fitWe agree HA-1 TCR-T belongs in the picks, so this is a push on where it sits, not whether. A post-HCT relapse will never produce the randomized comparator your tier standard waits for (nct:NCT03326921 is single-arm by necessity), so holding the stated-priority lever at rank 2 on that basis is a bar this setting cannot clear. advocateconcensusitedissentpreference_fitSorting by drug-level guideline category lands the stated-reason immunotherapy at rank 3, behind gemtuzumab, and that ordering runs against the user's priority. The free_text names HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason for the run, and with efficacy_toxicity_weight at 0.75 a CD33 ADC that is null in this stratum (OR 0.99, pmid:25008258) should not sit above it. docs.title: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning + allo-HCT (iomab-b-apamistamab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2moderateFor an 85%-blast marrow with extramedullary disease, the honest problem is getting this patient to a second transplant alive and deep enough for it to hold, and SIERRA is the one randomized signal that speaks to exactly that: durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care. It carries active disease into allo-HCT instead of demanding a remission the chemotherapy can no longer deliver, which is the crux of a curative plan here. The soft spot: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility is unproven, and the go-forward NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting. ITT OS was flat, but that reflects 52% crossover to the radioconjugate, not failed conditioning.Prior allo-HCT eligibility for CD45 radioimmunotherapy is unestablished; SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients; Go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting; Second-transplant treatment-related mortality; fitness and organ-function workup still open conservative1moderateThe thing I keep coming back to is that SIERRA is the only randomized phase 3 in this whole dossier that speaks to the actual problem, getting an 85%-blast marrow through to a transplant. It gave durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, and the toxicity is what earns it my rank 1: grade 3+ treatment-related AEs ran 59.7% versus 59.2% on conventional care, so as conditioning the radioconjugate adds essentially no incremental grade 3+ burden. This is published 2025 randomized data with per-term AEs posted on the NCT02665065 tab, not a single-arm signal I have to take on trust. My hesitation is honest: SIERRA enrolled patients going to a first transplant, so second-transplant TRM and prior-HCT eligibility are unproven, and this patient has no organ-function labs on file yet.SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients; second-transplant TRM and prior-HCT eligibility are not established; No numeric organ-function labs on file; radioimmunotherapy conditioning ahead of HCT2 needs cardiac, renal, and hepatic clearance first; Not FDA-approved; the go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting critic1moderateSIERRA is the one randomized phase 3 in this dossier that points toward benefit, and its registered primary endpoint cleared conventional alpha: durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, p<0.0001. Two things hold me at moderate rather than high. The endpoint is a surrogate, durable CR at 180 days rather than survival, and ITT OS was flat at HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41), which the 52% crossover to the radioconjugate explains but does not undo. And SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so reading it onto a prior-HCT relapse is indirect evidence rather than tested ground; RoB2 for the trial is Some concerns, driven by open-label conduct, though a durable-CR endpoint is objective enough to blunt detection bias.RoB2 domain 4 (outcome measurement): open-label conduct, partly offset because durable CR >=180d is an objective endpoint; Primary endpoint is a surrogate (durable CR), not OS; ITT OS null at HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41); RoB2 domain 2 (deviations from intended intervention): 52% crossover to the radioconjugate confounds the OS comparison; Applicability / indirectness: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility is untested concensusite1moderateFor a fit patient relapsing after allo-HCT with curative intent, the prevailing consensus points at a second allograft: ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022) and NCCN AML v3.2026 both keep second allo-HCT and clinical-trial enrollment in play for relapsed disease, and that is where the curative goal actually lives. Iomab-B is the conditioning that carries an 85%-blast marrow into that transplant, and it enters through NCCN's category-2A clinical-trial-preferred route rather than as a categorized drug, backed by SIERRA, the one randomized phase 3 in this dossier (durable CR 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001). I rank it first because it fits the stated curative intent under a route NCCN, ELN, and ASH converge on, not because the agent itself carries a label. The honest gap: ELN's second-transplant consensus assumes a transplant-fit patient, and this one has no cardiac or organ-function workup on file yet.ELN 2022's second-transplant consensus assumes a transplant-fit patient; no documented cardiac, renal, or hepatic workup yet, so the guideline-endorsed population is not established; Iomab-B carries no NCCN drug-level category; it is guideline-aligned only through the clinical-trial-enrollment principle, and SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility sits outside the studied population; Go-forward conditioning trial NCT07157514 is not yet recruiting advocate2moderateThe user's curative goal needs a platform, and the preferences put no modality off the table; HCT2 and cellular therapy are named as acceptable, travel included. Iomab-B is the conditioning that carries an active 85%-blast marrow into the second transplant, which is where the HA-1 consolidation would actually be delivered. It is also the one randomized signal in the dossier: SIERRA gave durable CR of 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) versus 0% on conventional care, and as conditioning it added essentially no incremental grade 3+ burden (59.7% vs 59.2%). A trial route exists (NCT02665065 now closed, NCT07157514 the go-forward). The gap I will name: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so prior-HCT eligibility is unproven, and the fitness workup the preferences flag as open needs to land before conditioning.Satisfied: no modality ruled out (HCT2 explicitly acceptable), curative intent, efficacy-leaning weight, and a trial route.; In tension: SIERRA's population was first-transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility for a second transplant is untested.; Open item the user themselves flagged: no organ-function or cardiac data on file. The 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known, before committing to transplant conditioning.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconcensusitequalifiedguideline_fitThe transplant backbone is sound and I rank Iomab-B myself, so my push is at the ranking axis, not the pick. Sorting by drug-level guideline category structurally buries HA-1 TCR-T at your rank 3, when NCCN's own category-2A trial-enrollment route that you cite is a green light for exactly the referral's premise. For an 85%-blast relapse where the guideline-listed options have already failed FLAG-IDA and venetoclax, guideline fit is the wrong lens to rank the upside bet. conservativecriticqualifiedtoxicityWe agree Iomab-B is the right lead, and the grade 3+ TRAE parity (59.7% vs 59.2%, pmid:39298738) is what makes it the safe conditioning choice for me too. My addition sits on the axis your evidence-quality read skips: SIERRA enrolled first-transplant patients, so second-transplant TRM is uncharacterized, and this patient still has no cardiac, renal, or hepatic workup on file. I would gate the conditioning on that clearance before calling the pick deliverable.

docs.title: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123 ADC) (pivekimab-sunirine)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowCD123 is confirmed on the blasts, and pivekimab is the CD123 ADC with real single-agent R/R AML numbers rather than cross-tumor read-across: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the RP2D. I want it as debulking ahead of the cellular and transplant consolidation, not as a destination in itself. Preclinically the mono-alkylator payload kills at low-picomolar potency below the dose that touches normal progenitors (Kovtun 2018), so the therapeutic window is plausible if the pending quantitative CD123 density holds up. Two flags I will name: response depth is modest, and the veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses matters with a transplant coming.ORR 21% is modest; single agent unlikely to clear an 85% blast burden on its own; Veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses is a concern ahead of HCT2; Quantitative CD123 antigen density that predicts ADC benefit is still pending conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate3lowDebulking bridge. The marrow is 85% blasts and refractory to FLAG-IDA/venetoclax, and neither the TCR-T nor the transplant bites on a marrow that full. CD123 is a user-named handle (positive by flow), pivekimab is the CD123 ADC with its own R/R AML numbers rather than borrowed ones (ORR 21%, 95% CI 8-40; composite CR 17%), and it runs through a trial (NCT03386513), which prefers_trials favors. The efficacy-leaning weight supports using it to buy the deeper cytoreduction the curative plan needs. Two caveats: single-agent depth is modest, and the veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses matters with a transplant coming. Since toxicity_vetoes is empty, that VOD flag is a fitness judgment rather than a preference breach. Quantitative CD123 density is still pending.Satisfied: CD123 is a user-named handle, a trial route (prefers_trials), and the efficacy-leaning weight supports debulking.; In tension: single-agent depth is modest against an 85% blast load and unlikely to clear it alone.; The VOD signal ahead of HCT2 is a fitness consideration, not a preference veto (toxicity_vetoes is empty); quantitative CD123 antigen density is pending.

Cross-critiques

It is a CD123 ADC with a documented veno-occlusive-disease signal at higher doses (pmid:38423051), and this patient has no hepatic or organ-function labs on file, which is exactly the ADC-before-transplant setup I gate on. Veto holds until baseline bilirubin, transaminases, and a hepatic read clear it; produce that clearance and I drop the veto. conservativeadvocatedissenttoxicityYou rank pivekimab as a debulking bridge and rule its veno-occlusive-disease signal a fitness judgment rather than a preference breach because toxicity_vetoes is empty, and that is where I part from you. docs.title: Flotetuzumab (MGD006, CD123xCD3 DART) (flotetuzumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowHere is the mechanistic bet I will make in the open: TP53-aberrant AML runs an inflamed, IFN-gamma-high marrow, and on the flotetuzumab trial 7 of 15 TP53-abnormal R/R patients dropped under 5% blasts, with ORR 30% in the primary-refractory/early-relapse group. If this patient's TP53 status confirms, that biology is a live reason to expect CD123xCD3 redirection to bite harder here than the pooled numbers imply. The hard truth: MacroGenics deprioritized the program, so this is mechanism evidence and a case for chasing an open CD123xCD3 or dual CD33/CD123 construct, not an enrollable slot. CRS is the class risk and autologous T-cell fitness in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow is unknown.Program discontinued; no open enrollment route for flotetuzumab itself; The TP53-inflamed-marrow rationale hinges on the unconfirmed TP53 status resolving aberrant; CRS/infusion reactions and uncertain T-cell fitness after prior transplant and FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe 7-of-15 reaching under 5% blasts comes from Vadakekolathu 2020 (pmid:33057635), a correlative NanoString study, not a pre-specified stratum of the flotetuzumab trial. That is an unadjusted post-hoc subgroup in which responders were the patients with high baseline inflammation scores, so the TP53 signal is a hypothesis rather than an effect estimate. Ranking on it, for a program MacroGenics has already shelved, is the inference I would hold back on. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitFlotetuzumab has no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing for R/R AML and MacroGenics shelved the program, so a rank here spends a slot on a lever with no guideline standing and no open route (nct:NCT02152956 is closed). The TP53 case rests on Vadakekolathu 2020 (pmid:33057635), a correlative subgroup rather than any categorized recommendation, which is off-guideline mechanism betting by definition. If the CD123xCD3 mechanism is the draw, an open construct on a trial is the guideline-aligned way to chase it.

docs.title: Tagraxofusp (SL-401, CD123-directed IL-3/diphtheria-toxin fusion) (tagraxofusp)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative3lowAmong the CD123 options this is the only FDA-approved agent, about 8 years of post-marketing use with a defined capillary-leak management algorithm covering albumin thresholds, daily weights, blood-pressure monitoring, and dose holds, which is why I take it over pivekimab or the discontinued flotetuzumab. But the approval is in BPDCN, not AML, so the 72% first-line CR (21/29, Pemmaraju 2019) is cross-tumor read-across and does not transfer cleanly to an 85%-blast AML marrow. Capillary leak syndrome carries a boxed warning and showed up in 19% with a death in each dose subgroup, and with no organ-function labs on file I will not commit to it before the fitness and cardiac workup lands. I rank it, but low, and behind a clear read on this patient's albumin and cardiac reserve.FDA approval is in BPDCN; AML use is off-label cross-tumor read-across; Capillary leak syndrome (19%, one death per dose subgroup) with undocumented organ function; Needs baseline albumin and cardiac/hepatic workup before it is safe to start critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityWe agree the worked-out capillary-leak algorithm is the reason to reach for tagraxofusp over the other CD123 options, but the 72% CR you cite (Pemmaraju 2019, pmid:31018069) is a first-line BPDCN result from an open-label single-arm phase 2, not AML. That is cross-tumor read-across standing in for indication data, and an 85%-blast AML marrow is not the disease that number was earned in. Rank it on the safety record if you must, but not on a response rate that does not transfer. concensusiteconservativequalifiedguideline_fitAgreed that tagraxofusp brings the worked-out capillary-leak algorithm the other CD123 options lack, but its FDA approval and every guideline entry sit in BPDCN, not AML, so calling it the FDA-approved CD123 choice overstates its standing for this marrow. The 72% CR (pmid:31018069) is a first-line BPDCN number, and for AML the agent is off-label read-across with no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing to rank on. I would frame it as off-guideline for the indication rather than the approved option among the CD123 handles.

docs.title: WT1-siTCR gene-transduced lymphocytes (TBI-1301; HLA-A*24:02-restricted) (wt1-sitcr-tbi1301)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowThis is here for one job: keep the HLA immunotherapy door open if A*02:01 types negative. The preferences call de-risking the HLA-restricted pathway the priority, and that means holding a fallback ready, not just the A*02:01 lever. WT1-siTCR is A*24:02-restricted, so an A*02:01-negative but A*24:02-positive patient still has an immunotherapy route rather than a dead end. The Tawara 2017 cohort is small (n=8) and early, with transient blast reductions and no normal-tissue toxicity, so I treat this as a bridge concept, not a proven salvage. It is the reason both HLA alleles should be pulled in parallel instead of A*02:01 alone.Satisfied: directly serves the stated priority of de-risking the HLA-restricted immunotherapy pathway by keeping a route open if A*02:01 is negative.; In tension: gated on A*24:02 typing, also unresolved, and only relevant if the A*02:01 axis is foreclosed.; Evidence is n=8 early-phase with transient responses; a fallback lever, not a primary efficacy bet.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticadvocatequalifiedevidence_qualityHolding an A*24:02 fallback open is reasonable, so this is a qualified note rather than a dissent. But the evidence under it is Tawara 2017 (pmid:28860210), a first-in-human phase 1, n=8, with only 2 of 8 showing transient marrow blast decreases and no CR or durable endpoint reported. That is a route-preservation rationale, not an efficacy signal, and the ranking should read it that way instead of sitting it alongside response-bearing options. concensusiteadvocatequalifiedguideline_fitKeeping an A*24:02 fallback open is reasonable, so this is a qualified note, but WT1-siTCR sits fully outside the guideline framework, with no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing and standing only through the category-2A trial-enrollment route. Tawara 2017 (pmid:28860210) is an n=8 first-in-human cohort with transient responses, so on the guideline axis this is trial-only and doubly gated on A*24:02 typing. I would rank it as an explicit route-preservation placeholder rather than beside picks that carry guideline footing.

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Hamann/Bernstein (2002)Bioconjug ChemHL-60 CD33+ leukemia cells in culture and HL-60 xenografts in mice; AML patient marrow colony-forming assays—non-binding calicheamicin conjugate>=50 ug cal/kg x 3 doses (mouse xenograft)Gemtuzumab ozogamicin joins the humanized anti-CD33 antibody to a calicheamicin derivative through an acid-labile hydrazone; CD33 internalization frees the DNA-cleaving payload inside the blast while sparing CD33-negative stem cells.Sub-picogram IC50 against HL-60 in culture, and doses as low as 50 ug cal/kg given three times produced long-term tumor-free survival in HL-60 xenografts while a non-binding conjugate stayed largely inactive. docs.title: Tagraxofusp (DT388IL3, IL-3/diphtheria-toxin fusion)
docs.text:

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Mani/Muthusamy (2018)HaematologicaPrimary CD34+CD123+ cells from AML and MDS patients; AML patient-derived xenograft mice; normal cord-blood/marrow progenitors—CD123-negative lymphoid cells; healthy-donor progenitors—SL-401 (tagraxofusp) directs the diphtheria-toxin catalytic domain to CD123 on leukemic and MDS stem/progenitor cells, where the internalized toxin blocks protein synthesis, reaching even low-CD123 cells.SL-401 killed CD123+ AML and MDS primary blasts and CD34+CD123+ cells, including those with low CD123 density, while sparing CD123-negative lymphoid cells, and prolonged survival in AML PDX mice. Normal cord-blood and marrow progenitors were also hit, an on-target off-leukemia effect.moderatehighstrong29773600DOIKilling of normal CD34+CD123+ progenitors flags myelosuppression; the authors frame SL-401 as a bridge-to-transplant, matching this patient's second-transplant intent. Stemline-affiliated co-author. Black/Frankel (2003)LeukemiaSCID mice inoculated i.v./i.p./s.c. with TF1 (v-SRC-transfected) human AML cellsn=20-49 mice per inoculation routesaline; comparators DT388GMCSF, DAB389IL2, cytarabine, anti-CD33-calicheamicin2 ug IP daily x up to 5 (DT388IL3)DT388IL3 fuses the diphtheria-toxin catalytic and translocation domains to IL-3, delivering the toxin to CD123 (IL-3Ralpha)-expressing blasts where it halts protein synthesis.Only 5 of 49 i.v.-inoculated animals died with leukemia after DT388IL3, and median disease-free survival stretched beyond 120 days versus 37 days for controls. The gain held across i.p. and s.c. models, while the IL-2 fusion DAB389IL2 gave none.strongmedpartial12529673DOITF1/v-SRC is an engineered differentiated-AML model, not MDS-related AML; tagraxofusp's registration is in BPDCN, so AML use is off-label read-across.

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Dossa/Bleakley (2018)BloodPrimary human leukemia lysis by lentivirally transduced CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (in-vitro functional characterization)—untransduced / non-HA-1-specific T cells—A four-part transgene carries the HA-1 minor-histocompatibility-antigen TCR, a CD8 coreceptor so the class-I-restricted TCR works in CD4+ cells, an inducible caspase-9 safety switch, and a CD34-CD20 selection/tracking epitope; HA-1's hematopoietic-restricted expression confines the graft-versus-leukemia effect to the blood compartment.CD4+ and CD8+ T cells engineered with the HA-1 TCR transgene lysed primary leukemia and mounted antigen-specific functional responses. docs.title: Eprenetapopt (APR-246) p53 reactivation mechanism
docs.text:
intervention_id: eprenetapopt · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Lambert/Bykov (2009)Cancer CellMutant-p53 human tumor cell lines; biochemical thiol-adduct binding assays———PRIMA-1, the parent of APR-246/eprenetapopt, is converted to a reactive methylene-quinuclidinone that forms covalent adducts with thiol groups in the mutant p53 core domain; that covalent modification alone can restore a pro-apoptotic conformation.PRIMA-1-derived compounds bound covalently to cysteine thiols in mutant p53, and covalent modification by itself triggered apoptosis in mutant-p53 tumor cells. The work pinned down the covalent-adduct mechanism that APR-246 shares.—lowweak19411067DOIA pan-mutant mechanism, not Y220C-selective; the profile flags eprenetapopt as low-yield and the randomized TP53-mutant MDS phase 3 missed its endpoint. docs.title: Rezatapopt (PC14586) in TP53-Y220C AML
docs.text:
intervention_id: rezatapopt · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Carter/Andreeff (2025)BloodTP53-Y220C AML cell lines and stem/progenitor cells; TP53-Y220C AML xenograft mice—rezatapopt alone; venetoclax alone; MDM2/XPO1-inhibitor arms—PC14586 (rezatapopt) binds the pocket created by the Y220C substitution and refolds p53 toward a wild-type conformation that reactivates transcriptional targets; in AML, MDM2/XPO1 feedback plus loss of a p53-BCL-2/BAX interaction blunt apoptosis, so BCL-2 inhibition is needed to turn reactivation into cell death.Rezatapopt restored wild-type p53 conformation and target-gene activity in TP53-Y220C AML but induced little apoptosis alone. Adding venetoclax produced heavy killing of AML cells and stem/progenitors in vitro and prolonged survival of TP53-Y220C AML xenografts.stronghighstrong40608889DOISingle-agent rezatapopt was largely cytostatic in AML; the survival benefit needed venetoclax, which this patient's disease has already progressed through in FLAG-IDA/venetoclax reinduction. PMV-affiliated co-authors; contingent on confirming a Y220C variant. Underpins NCT06616636. This is the foundational proof-of-concept dataset for the clinical compound.strongmedcross tumor only39945593DOISolid-tumor models, so read-across to this patient's myeloid disease rests on the shared Y220C mechanism rather than tumor match. PMV Pharmaceuticals study.
