docs.title: Rank 3. Second allogeneic HCT from the HLA-identical sibling, on a cytoreduce-first or sequential-conditioning platform
docs.text: The only option in this dossier with a documented cure fraction, and the one whose favourable numbers all require a marrow she does not currently have.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Four independent registries say the same thing about relapse after allo-HCT, which is as close to replication as this question gets. Ruutu 2015 covers 2,632 second transplants with 5-year relapse-free survival of 15% (PMID 26367221). Christopeit 2013 (n=179) puts her stratum, a related-donor first graft, at 2-year OS 37% +/- 6% against 16% +/- 4% after an unrelated first graft (PMID 23918951). Schmid 2012 (n=263) supplies the prognostic score, where marrow blasts below 27% carry HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40-0.72, p<0.001) for survival and the worst band sits at 4% +/- 2% at two years (PMID 22167752). All of it is retrospective, none of it adjusts for the obvious confounder that selection into a second graft is itself a fitness judgement made by the treating centre, and none of the four tabulates non-relapse mortality, so the harm side of every quoted curve is missing.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate if she is cytoreduced, low as she stands. She is on the favourable side of nearly every factor those registries measure: a sibling donor already collected once, a six-year first remission far past the five-month cut that drives the EBMT score, a related-donor first graft. The single exception is the one that decides it, and it is not marginal. At roughly 85% blasts she sits in Schmid's worst prognostic band today, so quoting 37% +/- 6% for her as she is would be an indirectness error rather than a rounding error. About half of those who do reach CR relapse again.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Non-relapse mortality after a second graft, which no registry row tabulates. The tolerability case rests on survival curves rather than a per-organ risk table.
  • Acute and chronic GVHD, prolonged cytopenias, infection.
  • Conditioning intensity is unresolved, and there is no cardiac or renal baseline from which to choose it. That decision should not rest on an ECOG score alone.
  • The US sequential protocol asks her to repeat a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through, which is a clinical objection for the investigator rather than an access one.
  • Marrow-directed conditioning does not treat the thigh sarcoma, which needs its own local plan.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent and no veto; all five personas ranked it top-four and critic ranked it first. Concensusite established the guideline gap and it should be read as uncovered rather than contraindicated: NCCN AML v3.2026 tells you to start the donor search at first relapse and ELN 2022 recommends allogeneic HCT once cytoreduction is achieved, but neither body writes a graded recommendation for a second allograft after post-transplant relapse, because the pathway assumes a first transplant. Critic's reconciliation is the formulation to carry forward. A missing category is not missing evidence, and evidence quality is not the same axis as clinical value; what backs HCT2 is four registries replicating a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, with selection unadjusted in every one. The mechanism-level worry conservative raised is separate and unanswered: a second graft from the same sibling does nothing about whatever let this leukaemia escape graft-versus-leukaemia the first time, which is why HLA loss and class I surface expression on sorted blasts belong in the workup.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Gate it on a documented remission, or at minimum blasts under 27%, plus a measured ejection fraction and a creatinine clearance. NCT06928662 is the American sequential-conditioning route, cytoreducing into a reduced-intensity graft without waiting for remission, and prior FLAG-Ida triggers a case-by-case review where the patient was sensitive to it. Payer authorisation is likelier to turn on documented cytoreduction than on anything biological, which is another reason rank 2 precedes this. The germline question is open and it bears on donor choice: a predisposition variant shared with the sibling would redirect the plan, and the hereditary panel needs cultured fibroblasts rather than blood while blasts are circulating.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Tied at 1.0 with the cytoreduction above it and ranked second on sequencing alone. Concensusite put it plainly: read against the guideline text, HCT2 is the consolidation step and not the next thing to do. The gap to the HA-1 TCR-T below (0.8) is the critic's evidence-tier dissent, which does not attach here.

docs.title: Rank 4. HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform)
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201:positive. Foreclosed if the typing is negative.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Krakow 2024 is the entire clinical evidence base and it is nine patients (PMID 38683966, NCT03326921). Four of nine achieved or maintained CR after lymphodepletion and infusion, one MRD-negative past 27 months, with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS. The registered primary endpoint is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so 44.4% is a descriptive secondary readout and not a pre-specified efficacy result, and the denominator mixes patients whose remission was induced with patients whose remission was maintained. What separates this from the rest of the HLA-restricted field is that the preclinical work is on the actual clinical construct (PMID 29051183), with independent replication of the target across a 13-TCR panel and 15 HA-1-positive patient samples (PMID 36900382). There is no published HA-1 TCR-T data at anything like 85% marrow blasts, and none in extramedullary disease.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Assuming the positive branch, meaning A*02:01 confirmed and the HA-1 mismatch running the right way, the likelihood is genuinely uncertain but the intent is curative: HA-1 sits only on blood-lineage cells, so a durable graft-versus-leukaemia remission is the plausible upside and it arrives with very little collateral. The counterweight the board took seriously is burden. The same class did nothing against active disease in the WT1 TCR-T cohort, where median OS was 242 days across 15 patients with only 2 carrying overt disease (PMID 40473616), and Medigene read tumour burden as the limiting factor in their own PRAME phase 1 (PMID 41008812). A negative typing result forecloses this rec outright rather than downgrading it.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS across nine infused patients. That is the opposite of what a T-cell redirection product usually risks, and conservative called it the best-tolerated product in the dossier.
  • One grade 4 infusion reaction in nine.
  • Grade 3-5 infections after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion, including Legionella and S. aureus pneumonia. Lymphodepletion in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow is not a low-toxicity step just because the cells are.
  • Two mild grade 1-2 acute GVHD cases, attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal before infusion rather than to the TCR-T.
  • No patient in the series was infused after a second allograft, so the interaction with HCT2 immunosuppression and engraftment is unmeasured rather than reassuring.
  • No user toxicity veto applies; the list is empty.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: All five personas ranked this and three dissented from putting it first, which is the disagreement that most needed resolving. Advocate ranked it first as the reason the case exists, then conceded the ordering in round 2, and conceded to one argument specifically, risktaker's tumour-burden case, not to the endpoint or guideline objections. That concession is about therapy order, not action order, and the surviving half of advocate's position is load-bearing: the HLA record pull and the HA-1 genotyping of both parties belong in the rank-1 workup running now, during induction, because a fresh donor collection cannot start until the sibling genotype returns and nothing else on this page carries that lead time. The dissents from risktaker and conservative were explicitly conditioned on a rank-1 placement and are satisfied by this one, which is where both of them put it in their own orderings; conservative additionally declined to veto. Critic's dissent persists at any rank and is not contingent on anything: n=9 on a feasibility-and-DLT primary endpoint limits what may be claimed, and nobody should quote 44.4% as an expected response rate. The mechanism-level risk is that antigen-presentation escape is unmeasured, and a six-year escape from an HLA-identical sibling graft is exactly the history that predicts it.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Of every HA-directed programme in the dossier, this is the only one that requires the prior allograft rather than excluding it, with relapse at 5% or more marrow blasts qualifying at any time post-transplant, no blast ceiling and no performance-status floor. That is why TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 are shut to her and this is not. It is a single site in Seattle; travel is acceptable under her preferences with geography_band null, but travel plus lymphodepletion plus cytopenias needs a local backup plan written before she goes. The product is made from donor cells, so the sibling has to agree to a fresh collection before anything gets manufactured, and that consent conversation is on the critical path and has not started. No guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T, but NCCN's R/R pathway names clinical trial as strongly preferred and NCCN's own AML workup already orders the high-resolution typing this rec waits on, so pursuing it is guideline-concordant care rather than a research errand.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It ranks fourth rather than first for a reason every persona including its own advocate ended up accepting: a T-cell product that cannot work at 85% blasts serves the stated request while failing the stated goal, which is cure. The agreement score of 0.8 sits below the two 1.0 rows above it on critic's surviving evidence-tier dissent alone. It ranks above sibling DLI despite a lower score, and that inversion is deliberate: DLI's three endorsements each arrive attached to the finding that DLI at this burden is off-guideline with a 15% +/- 3% two-year survival band and a shut trial route, whereas the objections here were about placement and are answered by the placement.

docs.title: Rank 5. Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after cytoreduction
docs.text: Curative intent without committing her to a second conditioning regimen, and off-guideline at the blast burden she currently has.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Schmid 2007 is the only row in this dossier's post-transplant relapse literature carrying a concurrent untreated comparator: 171 patients given DLI against 228 not, 2-year OS 21% +/- 3% versus 9% +/- 2%, p=0.04, n=399 (PMID 17909197). Confounding by indication is the central problem and the design cannot fix it, because the patients who received DLI are the ones their centres judged well enough to receive it. Within the DLI group the split is stark: 56% +/- 10% given in remission or with a favourable karyotype, against 15% +/- 3% given in aplasia or with active disease. Orti 2018 compared DLI with a second graft in 46 patients after debulking and found the univariate survival advantage of HCT2 (p=0.021) did not hold on multivariate analysis (PMID 29526774); that is the only head-to-head in the set and it is too small to support an equivalence claim.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low as she stands, moderate after cytoreduction. Her late relapse beyond five months post-HCT puts her on the favourable side of the strongest variable in Schmid's model (p<0.0001). Roughly 85% blasts and an adverse karyotype put her in the 15% +/- 3% band rather than the 56% +/- 10% one, and that is an argument for cytoreducing before the infusion rather than against the infusion. Before committing to anything that depends on donor T cells recognising these blasts, measure HLA class I and II on them.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• GVHD is the toxicity and the mechanism at the same time. Grade III-IV GVHD would close the door on HCT2 and on any post-transplant cellular consolidation.
  • Not one registry row grades adverse events, so the harm cannot be quantified for her from this evidence at all. Schmid 2007 discusses GVHD narratively with no per-term table.
  • Marrow aplasia after infusion into a graft that has been in place six years.
  • Cell dose and escalation schedule are centre-specific, so whoever gives it owns the toxicity, which argues for doing it where her transplant records live.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Three personas ranked it and none dissented, which is why the score is 0.6. Every one of those endorsements carries the same caveat inside it. Concensusite noted that the EBMT best-practice recommendations set therapeutic sibling DLI at a starting dose of 1x10^7 CD3/kg but are written for low-burden or post-cytoreduction disease, and that NCCN AML v3.2026 carries no DLI recommendation at all, which is worth saying out loud rather than letting the silence read as endorsement. The mechanism worry is the one concensusite named: a relapse six years out looks like graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft loss, so re-infusing the same donor repertoire that already stopped holding this disease is a bet no guideline addresses. Advocate's round-2 objection was aimed at the ordering rather than the option, arguing that guideline silence was doing too much work when DLI was ranked above the product this run was submitted to find.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The therapy is available; the trial route is not, at least at present burden. NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% by morphology or flow and allows a single prior post-transplant salvage line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent, so cytoreducing her under the ceiling would itself consume the eligibility. Her donor is an HLA-identical sibling who has already donated, so the logistics are the easy part, and the same collection conversation is on the HA-1 critical path at rank 4. If the fitness workup comes back badly, this is what keeps curative intent on the table without a second conditioning regimen.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Its 0.6 sits below the HA-1 product's 0.8, and it sits below on substance too. Three personas endorsed it and each attached the finding that it is off-guideline at this burden and shut out of its own trial, whereas the objections at rank 4 were about placement and resolve at the placement given. It ranks above the CG1 engager (0.4) because it has published comparative evidence and a donor already collected once, where the engager has neither.

docs.title: Rank 6. CBX-250, CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific engager
docs.text: Conditional on hla_a0201:positive. Foreclosed if the typing is negative.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is no human efficacy readout, and both personas who ranked it said so in their own rows. The case rests on preclinical work: the engager killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo (PMID 39939820), and the CAR version of the same cathepsin-G leader-sequence target left normal marrow haematopoiesis intact (PMID 40437170). NCT06994676 is a first-in-human phase 1 dose escalation across eleven US sites, recruiting.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown, and it should be framed that way rather than dressed up. In a first-in-human escalation she could sit at a dose level chosen to be safe rather than active. Assuming A*02:01 confirms, what this row actually offers is reachability: eleven sites against one, a published compassionate-use address for a patient who cannot get a slot, and no dependence on the sibling genotype or on a fresh donor collection. A negative allele call forecloses it exactly as it forecloses rank 4.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No published grade-level toxicity of any kind.
  • Peptide-HLA engagers have no characterised CRS profile in humans yet, and this would be given into a post-transplant marrow carrying a heavy blast burden.
  • No user toxicity veto applies, so cytokine release is a conversation to have with her rather than a reason to strike this off her list.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented and none vetoed; advocate ranked it second and risktaker fourth. The status here is considered_with_caveats rather than the recommended a mechanical read of the endorsement counts would produce, because a first-in-human escalation with no efficacy readout should not carry the same label as an option with published activity. Two mechanism-level cautions carry over. It rides HLA-A*02:01 alone, so HLA loss on the relapsed blasts silences it as surely as it silences the HA-1 product. And CG1 appears nowhere on her nominated feature list: this rides an HLA restriction rather than a validated target in her disease, and nobody has measured whether her blasts express it.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The protocol names recurrence after HSCT as eligible more than 60 days out, ECOG 0-1 matches, and the extramedullary exclusion applies only to isolated lesions, which her marrow involvement takes her out of. Enrolment wants white cells under 25,000 against peripheral blasts that ran 58% to 82%, so this becomes real only after the rank-2 cytoreduction is working. Crossbow publishes a compassionate-use route, which almost nothing else in this dossier offers and which is worth using if slots are full. Ask the sponsor whether CG1 expression is measured on study or whether A*02:01 alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete before anyone books a flight.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score 0.4 against 0.6 for DLI above it, and the substantive gap is the same: DLI has published comparative evidence and an available donor. It ranks above everything below it because it is the second HLA-A*02:01 lever in a case submitted about HLA-restricted immunotherapy, and it is the one that asks nothing of the sibling, the hedge if the HA-1 mismatch runs the wrong way.

docs.title: Rank 7. BMS-986497 (ORM-6151), CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader, monotherapy arm
docs.text: The trial fallback that does not depend on the pending allele, listed on eligibility and reachability rather than on evidence.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is none published, and that is the honest summary. NCT06419634 is a recruiting first-in-human phase 1 of a CD33-directed conjugate delivering a GSPT1 degrader, with monotherapy, doublet and triplet arms. What the row offers is the eligibility profile, which is unusual across the 47 trials screened here: MDS-related secondary AML is named in the inclusion criteria, CD33 needs only to be detectable rather than above a threshold, ECOG 2 is permitted, and no blast cap or prior-allograft bar appears in the posted criteria.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown. Nobody knows what this does in humans, and she should hear it framed exactly that way. It is on the list because it is open, reachable, compatible with her trial preference, and independent of the HLA answer, which matters because ranks 4 and 6 both close on the same afternoon if the 2020 report comes back A*02:01-negative.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No published clinical safety of any kind.
  • Class expectations rather than data: CD33-ADC myelosuppression, hepatic risk from a conjugate payload, and the broad cytotoxicity of GSPT1 degradation.
  • On-target CD33 killing hits normal myeloid progenitors in a marrow that has to support a graft afterwards.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Advocate ranked it fifth and no persona dissented or vetoed. The absent exclusions in the posted criteria are unusual enough that advocate flagged confirming them with the site rather than assuming, which is the right instinct. Trial-arm assignment is the practical risk: if the site will only take her onto the azacitidine-venetoclax triplet, the venetoclax objection stands, since she progressed through venetoclax and re-exposing her would spend a trial slot on a drug that has already failed. No mechanism objection was raised.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Push for the monotherapy arm. Confirm with the site that the blast cap and the prior-allograft silence in the posted criteria are real. Enrolling consumes weeks an 85% marrow may not have, so this competes with rank 2 on time rather than complementing it, which is the argument for treating it as a fallback rather than a parallel track. Quantitative CD33 density is not required by this protocol but is being measured anyway inside the rank-1 workup.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score 0.2, one endorsement and no dissent, which places it above the two 0.0 CD123 rows below. It ranks below the CG1 engager (0.4) despite both having zero published efficacy, because two personas ranked the engager and one ranked this, and because the engager answers the question the case was submitted about.

docs.title: Rank 8. Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed ADC) at the 0.045 mg/kg RP2D
docs.text: The only CD123 agent with data in her own disease and line, carrying a hepatic condition that has to be checked rather than assumed.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Daver 2024 is peer-reviewed, in the right disease and the right line, and reports its own uncertainty honestly: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% (6-36) in 29 patients at the recommended phase 2 dose (PMID 38423051). Response was a secondary endpoint of a dose-finding study whose primary was MTD and RP2D selection, the study was single-arm, open-label and sponsor-analysed, and there is no OS readout in the R/R AML cohort. An interval running from 8% to 40% on n=29 carries almost no information on its own. The combination arms that would matter most here, pivekimab with azacitidine and venetoclax in R/R disease, are closed to accrual (NCT04086264). The 75% frontline composite CR figure belongs to BPDCN and must not be carried across (PMID 41671533).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate as debulking and no better than that. It is the only CD123 agent in this dossier with an efficacy estimate generated in relapsed/refractory AML rather than borrowed from BPDCN, which is why critic ranked it, and the point estimate is too soft to displace the rank-2 cytoreduction. Read it as the fallback if quantitative CD33 density comes back low and the CD33 route weakens.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Hepatic veno-occlusive disease. Two dose-limiting events occurred in 68 patients, and this is the number the board argued about. Both events were at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg, four to ten times the 0.045 mg/kg RP2D, and both were reversible.
  • The US label (DECNUPAZ, approved 27 May 2026 for BPDCN) carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including hepatic veno-occlusive disease.
  • At the RP2D: grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion-related reactions 7%, anaemia 7%.
  • No baseline bilirubin, transaminases or albumin on file, and a second conditioning regimen is planned.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: This is the disagreement the board could not resolve internally, because the personas ran concurrently. Conservative dissented on toxicity grounds, arguing that two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the wrong hepatic exposure in the weeks before a conditioning regimen, and noting for consistency that they ranked another calicheamicin conjugate second on the strength of a pre-transplant hepatic series pivekimab does not have. Risktaker corrected the read: the events sat 4 to 10 times above the RP2D and both reversed, so it is a dose-level finding rather than a property of the drug, and striking CD123 out of the pre-conditioning window on that basis is an over-read. Conservative never saw the correction. Adjudicating it, the correction holds and the dissent is sustained in narrowed form rather than as a bar. What survives is specific and checkable: no pre-transplant hepatic series exists for pivekimab comparable to the 57 fractionated-gemtuzumab patients of whom seven were transplanted afterwards, and the label carries a VOD boxed warning, so baseline bilirubin and transaminases with weekly monitoring are the condition, not exclusion. No veto was issued anywhere in this round.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The AML cohorts are closed to accrual, so this would be off-label use of a BPDCN-approved drug rather than trial enrolment, which cuts against her trial preference. There is no NCCN AML or ELN listing. Quantitative CD123 antigen density is unmeasured and spans roughly 200 to 10,000 molecules per cell across AML, so agent selection is currently blind to the predictive marker. If HCT2 comes off the table for fitness reasons, the hepatic condition loses most of its force and this row strengthens.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score 0.0: one endorsement from critic, one dissent from conservative. It ranks above tagraxofusp, which shares the 0.0, because it is the only CD123 agent with own-disease and own-line data, where tagraxofusp's headline number is cross-tumour. It ranks below the CD33 degrader (0.2) on board signal rather than on evidence, and that inversion is worth noticing: the row with the better published data sits below the row with none, because a persona dissented on this one and nobody dissented on that one.

docs.title: Rank 9. Tagraxofusp (SL-401, CD123-directed IL-3 / diphtheria-toxin fusion)
docs.text: The only labelled CD123 agent with a worked-out toxicity algorithm, and a headline number earned in a different disease.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The registration study is BPDCN, not AML: first-line CR or clinical CR 72% (21/29) at 12 mcg/kg (PMID 31018069). That is cross-tumour read-across and it says nothing about an 85%-blast AML marrow. The nearest AML data are 69% overall response with azacitidine with or without venetoclax in 26 patients with untreated AML, a different line from hers (PMID 38052038). NCT03113643 has an open R/R AML cohort where CD123 expression is the only biomarker gate and it is already documented, and transplant more than 60 days ago is fine at six years out.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low to uncertain in AML. The board's own read, from risktaker who passed it over explicitly, is that it is weaker cytoreduction than CLAG-GO for someone who needs the marrow emptied fast. The CD123 target is confirmed present, which is the argument for keeping it on the page; the density read that would tell you whether the handle is strong enough is not yet in.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Capillary leak syndrome in 19% (boxed warning), with one fatal case reported in each dose subgroup.
  • Transaminase elevation, ALT 64% and AST 60% any grade, and hypoalbuminaemia 55%.
  • The NCT03113643 cohort requires albumin above 3.2 g/dL, which nobody has measured.
  • With no baseline albumin, cardiac or hepatic workup on file, this is exactly the profile that needs fitness data before it can be started safely.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona ranked it in round 1 and none dissented, so the score is 0.0 by default rather than by contest. Risktaker's pass-over is the only direct board comment and it is about potency rather than mechanism. There is no plausible mechanistic antagonism here; the efficacy risk is cross-tumour non-transfer, and the mechanism-adjacent cost is on-target killing of normal CD34+CD123+ progenitors adding myelosuppression ahead of a graft.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: FDA- and EMA-approved in BPDCN only, with no NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022 listing, so AML use is off-label and investigational for her rather than standard care. Presenting the 72% as an expectation would misstate its footing. The capillary-leak management algorithm covers albumin thresholds, daily weights, blood-pressure monitoring and dose holds, and it needs a baseline albumin and cardiac read to run against. Prior venetoclax excludes from NCT03113643 unless the last dose was more than two months ago, which her FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax exposure may or may not satisfy. NCT06498973 is the one CD123 trial that names a second allogeneic HCT in its inclusion criteria, which makes it the natural consolidation partner for whatever gets her to HCT2.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Tied at 0.0 with pivekimab and ranked below it, because pivekimab has an efficacy estimate in her own disease and line and this does not. It ranks above the radioimmunotherapy conditioning row below (-0.2) because that row drew two dissents and this drew none.

docs.title: Rank 10. 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning before allogeneic HCT
docs.text: The one targeted-conditioning protocol that admits her prior graft, carrying a principle proved in a population that excluded her.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The borrowed evidence is SIERRA, and it is the only phase 3 in this file that hit its registered primary endpoint: durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with 131I-apamistamab conditioning against 0% (0-4.7) on physician's-choice conventional care, p<0.0001, n=153, in patients who had active disease at randomisation (PMID 39298738). Overall survival did not move at all, HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), the FDA determined the analyses did not support a filing and required a randomised OS study, and prior allo-HCT was an exclusion. The astatine conjugate then inherits the principle with no human efficacy behind it: what exists is a syngeneic mouse transplant using a murine anti-CD45, with median survival 123, 101, 61 and 37 days at 24, 20, 12 and 0 microCi (PMID 23471305). NCT03670966 is recruiting.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown for this construct, and the SIERRA number cannot be quoted for her at any rank. What makes the row worth a phone call rather than a footnote is the eligibility: patients with a previous non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity allograft are eligible provided there is no ongoing GVHD and six weeks off immunosuppression, and primary refractory disease qualifies. That combination appears nowhere else in the conditioning literature here.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Alpha-emitter dosimetry plus a second graft in a heavily pretreated marrow: an unquantified cytopenia and non-relapse-mortality risk with no human adverse-event table for this construct.
  • Circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3, which at 82% peripheral blasts means hydroxyurea has to work first.
  • For context from the borrowed trial, grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events ran 59.7% with the radioconjugate against 59.2% on conventional care, so the conditioning added essentially no incremental grade 3+ burden there.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Two dissents and one endorsement, which is why the score is -0.2, and both dissents landed on transportability rather than on the principle. Conservative withdrew a pre-registered veto cleanly: it was conditioned on a rank-1 pick taking her to conditioning at 85% blasts on the strength of Iomab-B, and at rank 5 with human efficacy stated as nil, the condition was not met. What conservative kept is a dissent, because SIERRA excluded prior allo-HCT and the successor protocol excludes it again while capping blasts at 20%. Critic dissented on the same axis and added the flat OS and the FDA refusal, plus the observation that the preclinical support models neither allogeneic immunology nor the human antibody. Risktaker's own position conceded most of this and ranked it anyway, on the argument that a targeted conditioning route is the only answer for a patient nobody can get into remission.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Two hard gates decide whether this is real. The protocol wants a haploidentical relative rather than the HLA-identical sibling who gave the 2020 graft, so if no such relative exists the row evaporates; that is a phone call worth making now rather than a discovery in three months. And myeloablative conditioning in 2020 would exclude her, while the profile does not record what she was given. Retrieving the 2020 conditioning regimen belongs alongside the HLA report in the same records request.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Agreement score -0.2, the lowest of any row still carried with caveats, and it sits here rather than lower because the eligibility fit is genuinely rare and the alternative conditioning routes are closed outright. It ranks below tagraxofusp (0.0) on the two dissents alone.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text:
Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference 211At-BC8-B10 + haploidentical allo-HCT Recruiting; no human efficacy published Not yet reported NCT03670966 131I-apamistamab conditioning (SIERRA, borrowed principle) dCR 17.1% (9.4-27.5) vs 0%, p<0.0001; OS flat, HR 0.99 (0.70-1.41) G3+ TRAE 59.7% vs 59.2% conventional care PMID 39298738, NCT02665065 211At anti-CD45 conditioning (preclinical) Median survival 123/101/61/37 days at 24/20/12/0 microCi (syngeneic mouse) Not applicable PMID 23471305

Rezatapopt (rank 11, TP53 Y220C-selective p53 reactivator, not recommended) is carried as a visible row rather than a narrative, because it was considered and declined rather than overlooked. Concensusite ranked it fifth in round 1 as the trial-shaped answer NCCN points at for TP53-aberrant poor-risk AML, framed from the outset as contingent on a Y220C call that does not exist in either direction, then withdrew the pick outright in round 2 and said why: the assay-decides-eligibility problem was decisive. Risktaker and conservative had dissented on converging grounds. Carter 2025 restored wild-type p53 conformation in Y220C AML and got limited or absent apoptosis unless venetoclax or an MDM2/XPO1 partner was added (PMID 40608889), and venetoclax is the drug she just progressed through, so even a positive Y220C call leaves the pick without a partner. NCT06616636 screens on a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, which sits at the detection limit of the same class of panel that returned her 2026 TP53-negative result, so the assay could decide eligibility before the biology does. No peer-reviewed clinical effect size exists for the agent in myeloid disease, and the parent solid-tumour study requires RECIST-measurable disease a marrow-based leukaemia cannot provide. Declining it does not collapse the TP53 branch in either direction: the rank-1 workup still retrieves the 2019 variant identity and VAF, adds p53 IHC, 17p FISH and a copy-number-capable panel, and a confirmed Y220C would reopen this row with an MDM2 or XPO1 partner rather than azacitidine.

docs.title: Also considered — not ranked (feature-targeting investigational)
docs.text:
Seventeen feature-targeting investigational options were surfaced without a live rank. Each carries a flag for why.

  • Not enrollable because prior allo-HCT is an exclusion: TSC-100 and TSC-101 (NCT05473910) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152) are the HA-directed products that get the attention, and both exclude a prior allogeneic transplant; BSB-1001 additionally caps myeloblasts at 25%. MDG1021 (NCT04464889) was the one HA-1 protocol written specifically for sibling-donor recipients at least 100 days post-transplant, and it was withdrawn without enrolling a patient. Critic's methodological note belongs on the record: the HA-2 arm rests on a 2003 in vitro paper describing a different TCR from the one in the clinical product, so HA-1 and HA-2 are not equivalently evidenced.
  • Not enrollable on disease state: WT1 A*02:01 TCR-T: the open successor requires morphologic remission with under 5% blasts and detectable MRD (NCT07645469), and the two published cohorts are the exhibit for the tumour-burden argument, since 100% relapse-free survival at a median 44 months was prophylaxis into remission (PMID 31235963) while the active-disease cohort gave median OS 242 days (PMID 40473616). Multi-antigen donor T cells: every open protocol excludes her, on post-transplant relapse and a planned second HCT (NCT02203903), on an age-65 floor and a 10% blast cap (NCT06552416), or on being active but not recruiting (NCT02494167, the one written for post-transplant relapse that counts extramedullary sites as qualifying disease, and worth re-checking if cytoreduction succeeds). GTB-3650 (NCT06594445) excludes transplant candidates by protocol, which rules out a case organised around getting to a second graft.
  • Not enrollable geographically: WT1-siTCR TBI-1301 (PMID 28860210) is the A24:02 fallback the profile insists on checking, with Japan-only development and no route a US patient can enter; advocate declined to rank it rather than tell her a door was open when the sponsor is not opening it. Dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T* (NCT04010877) hits both antigen handles at once with no blast cap and no prior-transplant bar, at a single non-US site.
  • Thin evidence, no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy: Switchable CD123 CAR-T (NCT05949125) is recruiting with a soluble target module that can be withdrawn to switch the CAR off, a real safety design at high blast burden and no published activity. CD33 CAR-T (NCT05672147) permits a prior allograft more than six months out and names AML evolving from MDS, resting on one published patient who progressed at nine weeks (PMID 25174587).
  • Unavailable, discontinued or supply-suspended: Flotetuzumab (PMID 32929488) produced CR/CRh in 26.7% of 30 patients in exactly her chemorefractory population and MacroGenics stopped it for business reasons; the 47% figure in TP53-abnormal disease is a post-hoc correlative read on 15 patients with no confidence interval (PMID 33057635) and should travel no further. Vibecotamab (PMID 37647601), terminated for under-accrual, ORR 9.0% on n=120 with 26.7% grade 3+ cytokine release. VIP943 (NCT06034275) has the friendliest posted criteria of any CD123 protocol here and a sponsor that began wind-down in 2025. PRAME TCR-T: both programmes dead (NCT03503968, NCT02743611), and the sponsor's own reading of the phase 1 was that tumour burden limited activity (PMID 41008812). GLIDE (NCT03091933), the only minor-antigen approach here that accepts nineteen class I alleles rather than bottlenecking on A02:01, with an unknown registry status. Lintuzumab-Ac225 after CLAG-M (PMID 39955432) is where the 56.6% composite CR that keeps being attached to CLAG-GO actually comes from, and its trials are suspended for drug supply. Iomab-B (PMID 39298738) is the highest design tier in the dossier and closed to her on both protocols. Eprenetapopt* (PMID 36990622) is the replication-failure exhibit and explicitly not the fallback if the Y220C call fails.
  • Consolidated into the ranked transplant approach: FLAMSA-RIC sequential conditioning (PMID 16110027) is the sequential form of rank 3 rather than a separate option. Amsacrine is not marketed in the US, FLAMSAClax (NCT05807932) excludes her twice over on prior therapy and a 30% blast cap, and the reachable version is NCT06928662 or an institutional regimen.

Two categories are absent by design. Single-agent gemtuzumab ozogamicin is FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML including this patient, so it is routed to the Standard-of-care table rather than surfaced here. The NPM1-directed TCR-T trials (NCT06424340, NCT07566585) ride her nominated HLA-A02:01 restriction but target a mutant-NPM1 neoantigen no panel has reported in her, and menin inhibition targets a KMT2A translocation* she does not have; both are target-absent and excluded rather than surfaced.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity, tiered Low/Moderate/High by grade-3+ rates and any treatment-related death. Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that an intervention could work against the therapeutic goal, such as antigen-loss escape, graft-versus-leukaemia failure repeating itself, or a hepatic toxicity that sinks the transplant the debulking was meant to enable. Those are not patient side effects. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. Nothing this patient is actually eligible for gets above evidence tier 2b, and the board said so rather than letting rank order imply otherwise. The lead HLA-restricted lever rests on a single-arm n=9 feasibility cohort whose registered primary endpoint is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity. The transplant platform rests on four retrospective registries that replicate a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, none of which adjusts for selection into a second graft or tabulates non-relapse mortality. The rank-2 regimen has no posted results and imports its estimates from trials that excluded her disease type. Two ranked rows, the CG1 engager and the CD33 degrader, have no published human efficacy at all. Tagraxofusp's headline number is cross-tumour, and flotetuzumab's TP53 signal is a post-hoc correlative read on 15 patients with no confidence interval, on a discontinued programme.
  • Compartment and biomarker dependencies. Ranks 4 and 6 assume allele-level HLA-A02:01 confirmation, and rank 4 additionally assumes a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch in a sibling nobody has genotyped. Without those, both are foreclosed rather than downgraded. TP53 is unresolved in either direction and must not be down-called to wild-type on a 2%-LOD panel that reads no copy number. CD33 and CD123 are confirmed present qualitatively, and the quantitative density that predicts ADC and immunotoxin benefit is pending for both; the rank-2 trial gates on CD33 at 20% of blasts, which the current result does not establish. HLA loss on the relapsed blasts is unmeasured and would silence every A02:01-restricted option at once.
  • What would change the ranking. A negative HLA-A*02:01 call moves ranks 4 and 6 to non-applicable and leaves nothing HLA-restricted within scope. A successful cytoreduction to under 27% blasts moves rank 3 from a gated destination to an actionable step and reopens the DLI trial route, the MRD-setting WT1 TCR-T, and the multi-antigen products; under 10% it reopens MT-401-OTS on disease state, though the age-65 floor still bars her. Documented hepatic and albumin baselines resolve the narrowed condition on rank 8 either way. A confirmed TP53 Y220C reopens rank 11, but with an MDM2 or XPO1 partner rather than the azacitidine backbone the trial specifies, since venetoclax is spent. Confirming that a haploidentical relative exists would make rank 10 a real option rather than a phone call.
  • Re-scoping caveat. The 0.75 efficacy weight was set before anyone documented organ function, and her own free text asks for it to be revisited once fitness is known. If the cardiac or hepatic assessment comes back poor, ranks 2, 3 and 10 are the ones that move, and a second conditioning regimen may come off the table entirely, which would promote sibling DLI and the lower-intensity CD123 options relative to everything above them.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text: Authored 2026-08-07 by the PI agent under the two-table contract, from a complete dossier: profile.json, preferences.json, 20 biomarker-survey rows, 16 target-validation rows, 47 trials, 36 clinical-evidence rows, 33 preclinical rows, 32 accessibility rows, and the board's 5 positions plus 20 critiques. This is the Experimental table, feature-targeting investigational options only; the standard-of-care track is a separate parallel surface owned by the standard_of_care_screener and nothing here was narrowed to make room for it. All 28 rows validate against recommendations.schema.json. Endorsement, dissent and agreement scores were computed from round-1 picks and round-2 critiques, with two documented departures from the mechanical rule. First, the advocate's round-2 "dissent" against concensusite on ha1-tcr-t argues for the intervention (it objects to concensusite's demotion of it), so it was not counted as a dissent on that row. Second, the risktaker's and conservative's dissents on ha1-tcr-t were explicitly conditioned on a rank-1 placement and are satisfied by the rank-4 placement both of them argued for, so only the critic's evidence-tier dissent, which is not contingent on anything, was carried; that is recorded in the row's rationale rather than hidden. Zero vetoes were issued: the conservative's pre-registered veto against radioimmunotherapy conditioning was withdrawn in round 2 when its condition went unmet, and the pivekimab hepatic objection was filed as a dissent rather than a veto and is adjudicated in narrowed form on that row. Biomarker gating: of five non-confirmed biomarkers (TP53, TP53 Y220C, HLA-A02:01, HLA-A24:02, HA-1/HA-2), the one-dimension cap selected HLA-A02:01 for the shared workup row at rank 1 and the hla_a0201:positive tagging on the HA-1 TCR-T and the CG1 engager; TP53/Y220C, A24:02 and the HA-1 direction are carried as open questions and caveats rather than a parallel branch, and no negative-branch ranking was emitted. Routing: single-agent gemtuzumab ozogamicin is FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML including this patient and was routed OUT to the Standard-of-care table, while the CLAG-GO regimen stays here because the combination is trial-only or off-label with no published efficacy in refractory AML; second allo-HCT and sibling DLI are carried here because they are user-stated targetable features and neither NCCN nor ELN attaches a category to either after post-transplant relapse, and the standard-of-care screener may reasonably carry them too, since the tables are additive. Menin inhibitors (KMT2A amplification is not the translocation they need) and the two NPM1-directed TCR-T trials (no NPM1 mutation on either panel) are target-absent and were excluded rather than surfaced. The accessibility row pending-diagnostics-workup has a matching intervention_id here so it does not render under the unmatched-interventions sentinel. Reference verification ran over every identifier promoted into recommendations.jsonl and this page: 39 PMIDs re-resolved live against PubMed for title, journal, year and claim fit, and 37 NCT identifiers re-resolved against ClinicalTrials.gov for title and recruitment status. One correction was made before writing: the pivekimab anchor was moved from NCT03386513 to NCT04086264, because the registry brief title for NCT03386513 has drifted to BPDCN-only and no longer supports the R/R AML claim attached to it. Nothing was nulled and no fabricated identifier was found.

docs.title: 1. CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin) CLAG-GO, CLAG-M + GO, cladribine/cytarabine/G-CSF plus gemtuzumab ozogamicin
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

This is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier and it takes post-allograft relapse by name. If the Maryland slot does not materialise, the regimen can be reproduced at the home centre from marketed drugs, which is the practical fallback that most other options in this case do not have. The gating items are the 60-day and GVHD conditions, both comfortably met six years out.

RegulatoryRegimen of individually approved agents. Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is FDA-approved for relapsed/refractory CD33-positive AML; cladribine, cytarabine and filgrastim are approved products used off-label in this combination. Geographic scopeUnited States; single trial site in Baltimore, Maryland, with the regimen reproducible at any centre from marketed drugs.

Next steps

  1. Call the University of Maryland study contacts (410-328-9416 / veronica.kflu@umm.edu) this week and ask about slot availability and screening turnaround for NCT04050280
  2. Send the marrow report, current blast trajectory and CD33 flow with the first contact so screening is not delayed
  3. Confirm the patient is off all immunosuppression and has no more than grade 1 GVHD, and get that documented
  4. Ask the home centre in parallel whether it will deliver CLAG plus fractionated gemtuzumab off-trial if the Baltimore slot slips
  5. Plan the cellular or transplant consolidation before starting, since CLAG-GO is a cytoreduction step in a curative-intent sequence rather than an endpoint

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT040502802Relapsed/refractory AMLrecruitingeligible: likelyVeronica Kfluveronica.kflu@umm.edu410-328-9416trial sitesRegistry record updated 2026-07-01, estimated completion 2028-02. Post-allograft relapse is explicitly eligible at >=60 days from infusion with no more than grade 1 GVHD and off immunosuppression. Excludes APL and CML blast phase. PI: Vu H. Duong, MD, MS.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyUniversity of Maryland, Baltimore (sponsor); Pfizer supplies gemtuzumab ozogamicin commercially CountryUnited States Medical info phone1-800-438-1985 Product informationhttps://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04050280 NotesInvestigator-initiated regimen, so there is no single company to call. The only branded component with a medical-information desk is gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Pfizer).

Payer / coverage notes. Inside the trial, protocol-specified drug and monitoring are covered by the study. Off-trial, every component is a marketed product and gemtuzumab is on-label here, so the regimen can usually be assembled without a novel coverage fight, though the cladribine-based backbone itself is off-label combination use.

docs.title: 2. BMS-986497 (ORM-6151, CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader) ORM-6151, BMS-986497
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-08-07

This is the broadest CD33-directed study open to her on paper: relapsed or refractory AML, any detectable CD33, ECOG up to 2, with prior allograft not named as an exclusion. Sixteen sites makes it geographically the easiest to reach of the CD33 options. The two things to confirm with a site are the post-transplant question and whether the current dose-escalation cohort is open.

Regulatoryinvestigational; IND-stage, no filing Geographic scopeUnited States; 16 listed sites, two withdrawn.

Next steps

  1. Email Clinical.Trials@bms.com with NCT06419634 in the first line, or call 855-907-3286, and ask which sites have open slots and whether prior allogeneic HCT is permitted
  2. Ask for the full protocol exclusion list, since the public registry summary ends with 'other protocol-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria apply'
  3. Send documented CD33 expression with the enquiry and add quantitative density when it returns
  4. Check whether the marrow blast burden and any leukocytosis limits apply, as they are not in the public record

docs.title: 3. CD33-directed CAR T cells CART-33, anti-CD33 CAR-T, CD33 CAR T

The City of Hope study is the realistic CD33 CAR-T route and it is written for a post-allograft patient with a donor still identifiable, which describes this case. On-target marrow aplasia means the protocol assumes a subsequent transplant, so it only makes sense as part of a transplant-consolidation plan. The Shenzhen study is open but mainland-China-only.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no approved CD33 CAR-T product Geographic scopeUnited States (City of Hope, Duarte CA) and mainland China (Shenzhen) only.

  2. Confirm the sibling donor's availability and willingness for a further collection, because the protocol requires the original donor as the stem-cell source
  3. Order quantitative CD33 antigen density alongside the trial enquiry
  4. Ask the study team how they sequence CD33 CAR-T against a planned second allograft, since the aplasia risk drives the timeline
  5. Only revisit NCT04010877 if the US route closes, and then ask explicitly about non-resident enrollment and follow-up obligations in Shenzhen

Since she has already had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax since relapsing, the study team has to rule on it rather than the file. Peripheral blasts also need to be under 20,000 at treatment start.

  2. Ask whether hydroxyurea-controlled blasts under 20,000 is acceptable given a peripheral blast fraction that reached 82%

docs.title: 5. Dual CD33/CD123-directed CAR T cells (Loop33 x 123 and related constructs) Loop33x123, CD33/CD123 dual CAR, CLL-1/CD33/CD123 CAR-T
docs.text:

Dual CD33/CD123 targeting exists in the clinic only through a single mainland-China study, so this is a geography problem before it is a biology problem. The dual-antigen rationale is strong for a patient whose blasts carry both antigens, but no US or EU site is running it.   2. If the family wants the Chinese option explored anyway, have the treating haematologist write to c@szgimi.org about non-resident enrollment, manufacturing timelines and follow-up obligations, and get the cost structure in writing
  3. In the meantime pursue CD33 and CD123 sequentially through reachable agents rather than waiting on a dual construct

docs.title: 7. Second allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant (HCT2) HCT2, second allograft, salvage allo-HCT
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

A second allograft is the platform the rest of the curative-intent plan sits on, and unlike most rows here it needs no trial and no manufacturer. What gates it is disease control and a donor decision, not availability. Two Fred Hutch protocols wrap the transplant in a specific conditioning strategy, and both hinge on what the 2020 conditioning regimen was.

RegulatoryEstablished procedure rather than a regulated product; conditioning agents are individually approved, and treosulfan was FDA-approved in the US in 2025 for use in allogeneic transplant conditioning. Geographic scopeUnited States; the transplant itself is available at any allogeneic transplant centre, while the two conditioning protocols are Seattle-only.

Next steps

  1. Get a transplant-programme consultation booked now rather than after salvage, since donor work-up and authorisation run on a longer clock than chemotherapy
  2. Retrieve the 2020 conditioning regimen and the high-resolution HLA typing for the patient and the sibling, which every transplant protocol here asks for
  3. Ask the transplant team to decide between the original HLA-identical sibling and a haploidentical family donor, since some protocols require the latter and graft-versus-leukaemia escape argues for a different donor
  4. Contact the Fred Hutch DEC-FLAG-Ida study (nali2@fredhutch.org, 206-667-5854, NCT06928662) if a conditioning trial is wanted, and raise the prior FLAG-Ida failure with them directly
  5. Begin payer pre-authorisation early and document the cytoreduction plan, because disease burden is what payers will question

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT069286621/2Primary refractory or relapsed AMLrecruitingeligible: unconfirmedNaveed Ali, MDnali2@fredhutch.org206-667-5854trial sitesFred Hutch, single site, registry updated 2026-05-15. Prior TBI-containing allogeneic HCT is permissible up to 3 Gy if more than 6 months after the transplant, so the 2020 regimen again decides eligibility. Sibling donors must be genotypically or phenotypically HLA-identical confirmed by high-resolution typing, which is another reason the pending HLA retrieval is load-bearing. Matched-unrelated, mismatched-unrelated and haploidentical donors are all accommodated. Note the regimen repeats a FLAG-Ida backbone that this patient has already progressed through, which is a clinical rather than an access objection. NCT036709661/2Relapsed/refractory acute leukaemiarecruitingeligible: unconfirmedPhuong Voptvo@fredhutch.org206-667-2749trial sitesThe radioimmunotherapy-conditioning route to a second transplant; requires a haploidentical related donor and excludes prior myeloablative conditioning.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyNot applicable; delivered by transplant centres. Donor search and unrelated-donor logistics run through NMDP. CountryUnited States NotesAccess runs through a transplant programme's evaluation, not a manufacturer. The relevant contacts are the treating centre's transplant coordinator and the original donor's centre.

Payer / coverage notes. A second allogeneic transplant is covered by Medicare and most commercial plans as established care for relapsed AML, but it is prior-authorised individually and payers look closely at disease control before conditioning. Refractory disease at roughly 85% marrow blasts is the most likely reason for an authorisation fight, which is an argument for documented cytoreduction first.

docs.title: 8. Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the HLA-identical sibling donor DLI, donor leukocyte infusion, prophylactic DLI
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

DLI is one of the few options in this dossier the patient's own team can arrange without a sponsor, a trial slot or an off-label appeal, since the sibling donor is identified and the relapse pattern points to graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft failure. Its weakness is disease burden, because DLI works poorly against bulky disease and is usually given after cytoreduction. The interferon-gamma combination study would add to it but caps blasts at 30%.

RegulatoryEstablished post-transplant practice; cells are collected and infused under the transplant programme's own authorisations rather than as a licensed product. Geographic scopeUnited States; DLI itself is available at any transplant centre, the combination study at three sites (St Louis, Pittsburgh, Seattle).

Next steps

  1. Ask the original transplant centre what donor cells are still available and whether the sibling would consent to a fresh collection, since that answer takes time to obtain
  2. Sequence DLI after cytoreduction rather than against 85% marrow blasts, which is both the clinical and the trial-eligibility position
  3. If salvage brings blasts under 30%, contact the UPMC study team (eliaslj@upmc.edu, 412-623-6037, NCT06529731) about the interferon gamma-1b plus DLI protocol
  4. Discuss GVHD risk explicitly with the patient, since a six-year disease-free interval suggests a tolerated graft that DLI would deliberately provoke
  5. Ask the transplant team about class II HLA downregulation on the relapsed blasts, which is the mechanism most likely to blunt a DLI response after an HLA-identical sibling graft

Trial pathways

Sponsor of record is Sawa Ito, MD at UPMC Hillman. Blast criteria close it at present disease burden: at least 5% myeloblasts by morphology but not exceeding 30%, and abnormal cells with a leukaemia-associated immunophenotype not exceeding 30% of nucleated cells. It becomes reachable if salvage brings blasts down. Second registry contact: Amy Rodger, RN, 412-623-4036, rodgax@upmc.edu. Registry updated 2026-07-30.

Payer / coverage notes. DLI after allogeneic transplant is routinely covered as established care for post-transplant relapse. Costs are the collection, the infusion and the management of any resulting GVHD, all billed through the transplant programme.

docs.title: 9. 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) conditioning before allogeneic HCT 211At-BC8-B10, astatine-211 anti-CD45, At-211 BC8
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: radioimmunotherapy   Verified: 2026-08-07

This is a live, recruiting radioimmunotherapy-conditioning route at Fred Hutch, and it is the practical replacement for Iomab-B. Two facts about this patient decide it: whether the 2020 transplant used myeloablative conditioning, which would exclude her, and whether a haploidentical family donor exists, since the protocol wants a one-haplotype-mismatched related donor rather than the HLA-identical sibling. Both are answerable from the chart and a family history.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no filing Geographic scopeUnited States; single site in Seattle, Washington.

Next steps

  1. Pull the 2020 conditioning regimen from the transplant record and establish whether it was myeloablative, since that single fact opens or closes this option
  2. Map the family for a haploidentical donor (children, parents, other siblings), because the HLA-identical sibling does not meet this protocol's donor requirement
  3. Email Phuong Vo's team (ptvo@fredhutch.org, 206-667-2749, NCT03670966) with the conditioning history and donor picture rather than a general enquiry
  4. Confirm CD45 expression on blasts is documented, and get circulating blasts under 10,000/mm3 with hydroxyurea before screening
  5. Coordinate with the NCT03326921 intake at the same institution, since both routes run through Fred Hutch and could be sequenced

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT036709661/2Relapsed/refractory acute leukaemia, MDSrecruitingeligible: unconfirmedPhuong Voptvo@fredhutch.org206-667-2749trial sitesSingle site, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center; registry updated 2026-06-22, completion estimated 2029-10-20. Three things to check against this case. Prior myeloablative allogeneic HCT is an exclusion, while prior non-myeloablative or reduced-intensity allo-HCT is allowed if there is no ongoing GVHD and the patient has been off all immunosuppression for at least 6 weeks, so the 2020 conditioning regimen decides eligibility. The protocol requires a related donor identical for one HLA haplotype and mismatched at the unshared haplotype, which an HLA-identical sibling is not, so a different family member would have to be the donor. Circulating blasts should be under 10,000/mm3, hydroxyurea allowed. Blasts must express CD45 in patients not in remission.

docs.text:
Access status: Unavailable Modality: radioimmunotherapy   Verified: 2026-08-07

Iomab-B has no approval anywhere and the FDA rejected the SIERRA package, asking for a new randomised trial. That trial is not yet recruiting, has no listed sites, excludes anyone with a prior allograft and caps marrow blasts at 20%, so it fails this patient on two independent criteria.   2. If confirmation is wanted, email mvusirikala@actiniumpharma.com asking whether any prior-transplant cohort is planned for the new study

docs.title: 11. FLAMSA-RIC (sequential fludarabine/cytarabine/amsacrine with reduced-intensity conditioning and prophylactic DLI) FLAMSA, FLAMSA-RIC, sequential conditioning
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

FLAMSA-RIC in its original form is hard to reproduce in the United States because amsacrine is not marketed here, and the one recruiting FLAMSA study is in Germany with a venetoclax-containing arm that sits awkwardly against documented venetoclax refractoriness. The transferable idea, cytoreduction running straight into reduced-intensity conditioning, is available in the US through the Fred Hutch DEC-FLAG-Ida protocol or as an institutional sequential regimen. Discuss it as a conditioning strategy with the transplant team rather than as a drug to obtain.

RegulatorySequential-conditioning strategy assembled from individually approved agents. Amsacrine is not FDA-approved in the United States, which is why US centres substitute other sequential regimens. Geographic scopeGermany for the FLAMSA study; the sequential-conditioning strategy is deliverable at US transplant centres in modified form.

Next steps

  1. Raise sequential conditioning with the transplant programme as a strategy question and ask what their institutional sequential regimen is, given amsacrine is not available in the US
  2. If the German study is of interest, email Guido Kobbe (kobbe@med.uni-duesseldorf.de, NCT05807932) and ask about non-resident enrollment and about the venetoclax arm in a venetoclax-refractory patient
  3. Consider NCT06928662 at Fred Hutch as the US-reachable equivalent, subject to the prior-TBI and 6-month conditions
  4. Fold prophylactic post-transplant DLI planning into the conditioning discussion, since it is part of what makes the sequential approach work

Trial pathways

The registry lists extension 826 for the contact phone. Venetoclax-containing conditioning against documented venetoclax refractoriness is a clinical objection worth putting to the investigator. docs.title: 12. HA-1 TCR-T (donor-derived CD8+/CD4+ memory T cells, Bleakley/HighPassBio platform) HA-1 TCR T, HA-1 T TCR T cells, FH HA-1 TCR-T, Bleakley HA-1 TCR-T, HPB-101

The Fred Hutch phase 1 is the one HA-1-directed program written for a patient like this one: prior allo-HCT is required, not excluded, and 85% marrow blasts does not disqualify. Everything now turns on genotyping, since the recipient must be HLA-A02:01 positive and HA-1(H) positive while the sibling donor must be HA-1(H)-negative or A02:01-negative. There is no off-trial route to this product.

Regulatoryinvestigational; IND-stage, no FDA or EMA filing Geographic scopeUnited States; single open site (Seattle, WA). Unrelated donors residing outside the US are handled through NMDP-affiliated centres, which does not apply to an HLA-identical sibling.

Next steps

  1. Call or email the Fred Hutch immunotherapy intake line (206-606-4668 / immunotherapy@fredhutch.org, NCT03326921) and ask what they need to open a screening file, including whether they will run the HA-1 rs1801284 genotyping in-house for both the patient and the sibling donor
  2. Retrieve the 2020 high-resolution HLA typing for the patient and the sibling from the first-transplant / donor-registry chart before the call, since A*02:01 status decides whether the referral is worth making
  3. Confirm with the sibling donor that a repeat apheresis collection is acceptable to her, because the product is donor-derived
  4. Ask the study team about current slot availability and expected screening-to-infusion interval, and whether bridging cytoreduction on another protocol is permitted in the interval
  5. Have the referring centre start out-of-network / travel authorisation in parallel rather than after eligibility is confirmed

docs.title: 13. CBX-250 (CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager) CBX-250, CG1/HLA-A2 TCR-mimetic, CROSSCHECK-001
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Compassionate use Modality: bispecific_other   Verified: 2026-08-07

Of the HLA-A02:01-restricted options, this is the one with the widest geographic footprint and the most permissive post-transplant language, and it also has a published compassionate-use address if a slot is not available. The single decisive gate is HLA-A02:01 status, the same value that governs the HA-1 pathway. White cells need to be under 25,000 at enrollment, which cytoreduction can address.

  1. Retrieve HLA-A*02:01 status first; without it neither this nor the HA-1 route can be screened
  2. Email Rachel Ghiraldi (rachel.ghiraldi@crossbowtx.com, 857-301-6432, NCT06994676) to ask which of the eleven sites has open slots and what cytoreduction they accept to reach a white count under 25,000
  3. Ask whether CG1 (cathepsin G) expression is measured on study or whether HLA-A*02:01 positivity alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete
  4. If no slot is available, have the treating physician request the compassionate-use form at clinical@crossbowtx.com and submit it alongside the trial enquiry rather than after it
  5. Note the ECOG 0-1 requirement and keep performance status documented, since it can drift quickly at this disease burden

docs.title: 30. Pending diagnostics that gate the ranked options (HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, quantitative CD33 and CD123, TP53 variant-level NGS with CNV, HLA-LOH on blasts) high-resolution HLA typing, HA-1 rs1801284 genotyping, HA-2 genotyping, quantitative antigen density flow, QuantiBRITE ABC, TP53 NGS with copy-number calling, p53 IHC, 17p FISH, HLA loss of heterozygosity
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

This is the cheapest and highest-yield item in the whole dossier, and most of it can be ordered today. The 2020 high-resolution HLA typing for both the patient and the sibling almost certainly exists in the first-transplant or donor-registry chart and needs retrieving rather than repeating, and A*02:01 status alone decides whether the HA-1 and CBX-250 routes are open at all. The exceptions are HA-1/HA-2 genotyping, which is not a routine US clinical send-out and is best obtained through the Fred Hutch screening pathway, and quantitative antigen density, which the flow laboratory has to be asked for by name.

RegulatoryLaboratory testing rather than a regulated therapeutic. High-resolution HLA typing runs in ASHI-accredited histocompatibility laboratories; TP53 sequencing, p53 immunohistochemistry, 17p FISH and quantitative flow run in CLIA-certified clinical laboratories. Geographic scopeAvailable at the treating centre and its reference laboratories, with HA-1/HA-2 genotyping most reliably obtained through the Fred Hutch protocol in Seattle.

Next steps

  1. Request the 2020 high-resolution HLA typing reports for the patient and the sibling donor from the transplant centre or donor registry before ordering any new test; retrieval is faster than repeat typing and A*02:01 gates two of the best options
  2. Ask the Fred Hutch intake line (206-606-4668 / immunotherapy@fredhutch.org) whether HA-1 rs1801284 and HA-2 genotyping for both the patient and the sibling can be run through NCT03326921 screening, since routine clinical laboratories generally do not offer it
  3. Order quantitative CD33 and CD123 antigen density by name (antibodies bound per cell against calibrated beads, not mean fluorescence intensity), because qualitative positivity does not support ADC or engager selection
  4. Order TP53 sequencing that reports the specific amino-acid change with variant allele frequency and includes copy-number calling, and add p53 immunohistochemistry and 17p FISH; retrieve the 2019 variant identity and allele frequency at the same time so the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy is resolved on data
  5. Discuss HLA-LOH testing with the transplant team before ordering it: genomic HLA haplotype loss requires a mismatched haplotype, so after an HLA-identical sibling graft the more informative question is HLA class I and class II downregulation on the blasts, which a flow or expression assay answers

Ask the intake team whether they perform it in-house during screening. docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-08-07

The BPDCN approval in May 2026 turned pivekimab from a trial-only agent into a drug a treating team can write off-label for CD123-positive AML. Both adult AML studies that took relapsed/refractory patients are closed to new enrollment, and the one recruiting adult study is front-line, so the trial door is effectively shut. docs.text:

Tagraxofusp is an approved drug, so a treating team can prescribe it off-label for CD123-positive AML without waiting for a trial slot, but reimbursement is the obstacle rather than supply. Access status: Unavailable Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-07

The registrational trial in TP53-mutant MDS failed its primary endpoint and Aprea moved on, so there is no sponsor, no open study and no compassionate route. The upstream read that eprenetapopt is low-yield here matches the access picture. If the TP53 question resolves to Y220C, rezatapopt is the live molecule, not this one.

Regulatoryinvestigational; development discontinued after the phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint Geographic scopeNo open access path in any geography.

Next steps

  1. Record eprenetapopt as closed and do not hold it as a TP53 fallback
  2. Direct any confirmed TP53 Y220C result to rezatapopt (NCT06616636) instead

docs.title: 25. WT1-siTCR gene-transduced lymphocytes (HLA-A*24:02-restricted; logged upstream as TBI-1301) WT1-siTCR, TBI-1301 (as logged upstream), TBI-1201, Mie University WT1 siTCR
docs.text:
Access status: Not yet accessible Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

The WT1-siTCR platform sits with Japanese investigators and has no open study a US patient could enter, so this is a geography-and-sponsor problem rather than a biology one. It only becomes a question at all if the patient turns out to be HLA-A02:01-negative and A24:02-positive. Even then the route would be an investigator-initiated Japanese protocol.

Regulatoryinvestigational; Japanese academic/industry development, no US or EU filing for the WT1 product Geographic scopeJapan; no US, EU or AU site for the WT1 product.

Next steps

  1. Resolve HLA-A24:02 alongside A02:01 in the same typing pull, so this branch is either opened or closed on data
  2. If A02:01-negative and A24:02-positive, ask the treating haematologist to write to the Mie University group about any enrolling WT1-siTCR study before assuming there is one
  3. Confirm the product designation before any outreach: upstream files carry this as TBI-1301, which is Takara's NY-ESO-1 siTCR product, so the WT1 program identifier should be checked against the sponsor's own materials

docs.title: 26. Donor-derived multi-leukemia-antigen-specific T cells (mLSTs targeting PRAME, WT1, survivin, NY-ESO-1) multiTAA-specific T cells, mLSTs, TAA-T, ADSPAM, MT-401-OTS
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

Multi-antigen T-cell products are all gated on low disease burden, and at 85% marrow blasts none of the three studies will take her now. MT-401-OTS is the one worth tracking, because it becomes reachable if a salvage regimen drops marrow blasts to 10% or less. The other two are either closed to enrollment or written for patients who have not relapsed.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no FDA or EMA filing Geographic scopeUnited States; MT-401-OTS at City of Hope, Moffitt and KU Cancer Center.

Next steps

  1. Email Marker Therapeutics (pallison@markertherapeutics.com, NCT06552416) now to ask how quickly they can screen a patient who reaches <=10% marrow blasts on salvage, so the window is not missed later
  2. Sequence this behind whatever cytoreductive option the board picks; it is a consolidation-slot candidate, not an induction one
  3. Ask whether the off-the-shelf product requires any HLA restriction the patient must be typed for, and fold that into the same typing request
  4. Re-check NCT02494167 status in three months in case Baylor reopens accrual

docs.title: 28. Extramedullary myeloid sarcoma (right thigh) — assessment and local control myeloid sarcoma, chloroma, extramedullary AML
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-07

This row is biology rather than a drug, and it earns a place because the thigh lesion changes what the other options can achieve. A sanctuary site can carry a different clone from the marrow, so a biopsy of the lesion is the only way to know whether CD33 and CD123 are expressed there at the density the marrow shows. Every trial screening in this dossier will also ask for current extramedullary disease measurements.

RegulatoryNot a drug. Biopsy, cross-sectional imaging and local radiotherapy are established clinical services rather than regulated products. Geographic scopeAvailable at the treating centre; no geographic constraint.

Next steps

  1. Ask whether the thigh lesion can be biopsied for site-specific immunophenotype and genotype rather than assuming the marrow result applies to it
  2. Include the lesion in baseline imaging so response can be assessed separately from the marrow, since trials will ask for it
  3. Raise local radiotherapy with radiation oncology for symptom control or consolidation, particularly if a systemic response leaves the thigh lesion behind
  4. Flag the extramedullary site to any cell-therapy or engager investigator, since trafficking to soft-tissue disease is a known weak point of those modalities

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyNot applicable Country— NotesNo manufacturer. Access runs through the treating centre's interventional radiology, pathology and radiation oncology services.

Payer / coverage notes. Biopsy, MRI and palliative or consolidative radiotherapy to a symptomatic myeloid sarcoma are routinely covered. The item most likely to need justification is repeat cross-sectional imaging for response assessment at a site outside the marrow.

docs.title: 29. Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (CD33-directed antibody-drug conjugate) MYLOTARG, CMA-676, gemtuzumab ozogamicin, GO
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-08-07

Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is on-label for exactly this patient's situation, relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in an adult, so her own team can prescribe it without a trial slot or an off-label appeal. The open question is antigen density rather than access, since qualitative CD33 positivity does not predict benefit the way antibodies-bound-per-cell does. The CLAG-GO study at Maryland offers the same drug inside a salvage backbone and is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (MYLOTARG). The label carries two indications: newly-diagnosed CD33-positive AML in adults and paediatric patients 1 month and older, and relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML in adults and paediatric patients 2 years and older. EMA-approved for newly-diagnosed CD33-positive AML. Geographic scopeUnited States and EU for the marketed product; the CLAG-GO study is single-site in Baltimore, Maryland.

Next steps

  1. Order quantitative CD33 antigen-density flow before committing, since it is the variable that separates a reasonable ADC bet from a futile one
  2. Contact the University of Maryland study team (veronica.kflu@umm.edu / 410-328-9416, NCT04050280) about a screening slot, and ask how they handle a rapidly rising peripheral blast count given the G-CSF priming
  3. If the trial route is slow, have the treating haematologist write fractionated single-agent gemtuzumab on-label as a bridge and confirm the Part B billing pathway locally
  4. Document hepatic function and any veno-occlusive-disease risk factors ahead of a possible second transplant, because sinusoidal obstruction syndrome is the sequencing risk
  5. Ask Pfizer medical information (1-800-438-1985) for the fractionated MyloFrance-style dosing dossier if the local team wants it

Trial pathways

Requires relapse after or refractoriness to at least one intensive regimen, which FLAG-IDA satisfies. Symptomatic leukostasis excludes, and G-CSF is part of the regimen, so a rising peripheral blast count needs discussing before screening. Single site, University of Maryland, Baltimore. Second registry contact: Oyinkansola Arasanmi, 410-328-6635, Oyinkansola.Arasanmi@umm.edu.
