docs.title: 31. Revumenib (SNDX-5613, menin inhibitor) SNDX-5613, revumenib, REVUFORJ
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-07

Revumenib is approved and easy to obtain, which makes it tempting, but the label and the biology both turn on a KMT2A translocation or an NPM1 mutation and this patient has neither. KMT2A amplification is a different lesion and does not create menin dependence. The clinician logged it as out of scope for the same reason, and the access answer does not change that.

RegulatoryFDA-approved as REVUFORJ for relapsed or refractory acute leukaemia with a KMT2A translocation (November 2024) and for relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML in adult and paediatric patients 1 year and older (October 2025). GuidelinesNCCN guidelines list revumenib for relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutated AML. No listing for KMT2A amplification without a translocation. Geographic scopeUnited States; approved and commercially available.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue revumenib on the basis of KMT2A amplification; confirm with the treating haematologist that no KMT2A rearrangement was seen on the relapse karyotype
  2. If a full metaphase karyotype at relapse does turn up a KMT2A translocation, the drug becomes on-label and Syndax medical information (medinfo@syndax.com, 1-888-539-3REV) is the contact
  3. Re-test NPM1 at relapse if it has not been done, since clonal evolution could open the second label

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanySyndax Pharmaceuticals, Inc. CountryUnited States Medical info phone1-888-539-3REV (3738) Medical info emailmedinfo@syndax.com Product informationhttps://syndaxmedical.com/ NotesSyndax publishes medinfo@syndax.com and 1-888-539-3REV (3738) for medical information and adverse-event reporting. SyndAccess is the company's patient-support and reimbursement programme.

Payer / coverage notes. On-label use is reimbursed against a KMT2A translocation or an NPM1 mutation. Neither applies here: the 2026 cytogenetics show KMT2A amplification with four copies, which is not a rearrangement, and no NPM1 mutation has been reported. An off-label request without either lesion has no compendia support and should be expected to fail.

docs.title: 32. Venetoclax (BCL-2 inhibition) — prior exposure and TP53-dependent resistance ABT-199, GDC-0199, VENCLEXTA, venetoclax
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-07

Venetoclax is easy to get and that is not the issue: this patient progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax, and TP53 aberration is the canonical driver of BCL-2-inhibitor resistance. The reason this row exists is sequencing rather than acquisition, because several trials on the list carry venetoclax-containing arms that would repeat an exposure she has already failed. Raise that with any investigator before consenting to such an arm.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (VENCLEXTA) including for newly-diagnosed AML in adults 75 or older or unfit for intensive induction, in combination with azacitidine, decitabine or low-dose cytarabine. No approved indication in relapsed or refractory AML. Geographic scopeUnited States and EU; widely available.

Next steps

  1. When screening trials, check whether the assigned arm contains venetoclax and put the documented refractoriness to the investigator before consenting
  2. Do not plan venetoclax re-challenge as monotherapy or with a hypomethylating agent alone on the strength of availability
  3. If a mechanistically different combination is proposed, ask what evidence supports re-sensitisation in a TP53-aberrant, previously exposed patient

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAbbVie and Genentech (co-marketed in the United States) CountryUnited States Medical info phone(800) 821-8590 Product informationhttps://www.gene.com/medical-professionals/medicines/venclexta Notes(800) 821-8590 is the Genentech medical information line, Monday to Friday 5 am to 5 pm PT. docs.title: Selected general biomarker report — aml-mds-related-rr-tp53-aberrant-hla-pending-x7q2-rerun2
docs.text: Which biomarkers on the selected panel this patient has been tested for, and which have never been measured. The panel covers targets established in this tumor type, targets relevant across a subset of tumor types, and biomarkers that predict benefit regardless of where the tumor started, such as MSI-H/dMMR and high tumor mutational burden gating PD-1 blockade.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Selected general biomarker report (offline HTML) — the same survey, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Selected general biomarker report (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by recommended action

20 biomarkers surveyed: 18 with no usable result on file (0 essential), 2 measured but not to decision resolution, 0 already established. Panel coverage: 9 tumor-agnostic biomarkers plus 11 of 72 protein targets in scope for this tumor.

Twenty biomarkers were surveyed: all nine tumor-agnostic markers and eleven of the panel's 72 protein targets. Not one is measured to decision resolution. Eighteen have no usable result on file, and the two with results cannot support a decision as they stand: CD123 positivity is a qualitative flow call without antigen density, and the HLA class I genotype, typed at high resolution for the 2020 sibling transplant, survives only as a placeholder in the EHR. That genotype is the one essential item, and it is the master switch. Until the 4-digit type is retrieved or repeated, PRAME and MAGE-A1 read as unassessable rather than negative, and the HA-1/HA-2 and WT1 handles, the stated reason this case was submitted, cannot be adjudicated.

Closing all of it takes three orders, none needing a biopsy. A flow panel on the next marrow or blood specimen adds quantitative CD123 and CD33 density plus CLEC12A, CD70, LILRB4, CD37, CD200, B7-H3 and AXL. A comprehensive genomic panel, already indicated for the TP53 question, returns TMB, MSI, BRAF and RNA fusions on the same run. One blood draw covers HLA typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping and a germline predisposition panel, for the patient and the sibling donor both. BRAF may cost nothing: a records request for the 2019 and 2026 covered-gene lists would settle whether codon 600 was ever sequenced.

Five of the six tumor-agnostic approvals here are written for solid tumors, checkpoint blockade after an allograft brings a graft-versus-host hazard of its own, and most of these markers will be negative if tested. The argument for testing is the size of the option a positive opens, not any implied likelihood of one. CD33 density, TP53 with the Y220C question, and WT1 with HA-1/HA-2 appear in neither reference panel; the target validation report works them directly from the profile.

docs.title: What this collapses to
docs.text:
The gaps above resolve onto this many distinct orders. Biomarkers that ride along on the same assay are grouped together.

  • AML surface-antigen flow panel: one run on the next marrow or blood specimen carrying quantitative CD123 and CD33 density plus CLEC12A, CD70, LILRB4, CD37, CD200 and B7-H3 — AXL expression on blasts, B7-H3 (CD276) expression on blasts, CD200 expression on blasts, CD37 expression on blasts, CD70 expression on blasts, CLEC12A (CLL-1 / CD371) expression on blasts, LILRB4 (ILT3) expression on blasts
  • relapse comprehensive genomic profiling panel: the same order already needed to resolve TP53 variant identity and VAF, which also reports TMB, MSI, BRAF and RNA fusions — BRAF V600E mutation, Microsatellite instability / mismatch-repair deficiency (MSI-H / dMMR), NTRK1 / NTRK2 / NTRK3 gene fusion, RET gene fusion, Tumor mutational burden, high (TMB-H)
  • HLA typing blood draw: one blood draw carrying high-resolution class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping and a germline myeloid-predisposition panel — Homologous recombination deficiency / BRCA1 / BRCA2 pathogenic variant, MAGE-A1 expression (HLA class I presented), PRAME expression (HLA class I presented)

Reading this report

This page answers one question per biomarker: has this patient been tested for it, and was the test at a resolution that can carry a treatment decision. Not measured means nothing is on file, which is not the same as a negative result. Measured, not decision-grade means a result exists but cannot be acted on as it stands; those gaps are worked into the Target validation paths report. Priority weighs what is going unassessed against how routine the assay is. Most of these biomarkers will be negative if tested; the case for testing rests on the size of the option that opens if positive, not on how likely a positive is.

Back to case · Target validation · Recommendations · Trials · Evidence · Board

Decision support, not medical advice

Libby is experimental. An unmeasured biomarker on this page is a gap in the record, not a prediction that the patient carries it. Assay availability, current approval status, and whether any of this testing is worth the tissue are decisions for the treating team. See PHI policy.

docs.title: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921) (ha1-tcr-t)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowThis is the product the case was submitted for, and the only HA-1 protocol written to require the prior allograft rather than exclude it, with no blast ceiling and no performance-status floor (nct:NCT03326921). Four of nine patients achieved or maintained CR, one MRD-negative past 27 months, with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS (pmid:38683966). Nine patients is nine patients and I am not going to dress it up; the counterweight I take seriously is that the same class did nothing against active disease in the WT1 TCR-T cohort (pmid:40473616) and Medigene read tumour burden as the limiting factor in their own PRAME phase 1 (pmid:41008812). That is an argument for sequencing it after cytoreduction, not for dropping it, and it is why the A*02:01 retrieval and HA-1 genotyping of both her and the sibling should be moving this week.Two gates are shut: A*02:01 has never been retrieved, and neither she nor the donor is genotyped at HA-1. The mismatch also has to run in one direction, recipient HA-1(H)-positive with an HA-1-negative donor.; Collection, manufacture and lymphodepletion take weeks while her peripheral blasts moved from 58% to 82% inside a month.; The 4 of 9 denominator mixes patients whose remission was induced with patients whose remission was maintained. The induction signal in bulk disease is weaker than 44.4% sounds.; Single site in Seattle, and the neighbouring HA-1 protocol written for exactly this population (NCT04464889) was withdrawn without enrolling anyone.; HLA loss on the blasts would silence every A*02:01-restricted option at once and nobody has looked (pmid:19641204). conservative4lowThis is the best-tolerated product in the dossier and I do not say that lightly about a phase 1 with nine patients: no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS, with the two mild acute GVHD cases attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal before infusion rather than to the cells. Four of nine achieved or maintained CR and one has been MRD-negative beyond 27 months, which is worth chasing, though the denominator is 9 and the trial was never powered to say so. It is also the only HA-1 programme that requires a prior allograft instead of excluding one, which is why TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 are shut to her and this is not. What it cannot do is clear 85% blasts, since grade 3-5 infections followed the lymphodepletion in this series and the MDG1011 investigators attributed their own phase 1 failure to tumour burden, so I would place it after cytoreduction and after the graft rather than instead of either.Nine infused patients is not a safety database. The specific missing datum is the one that matters most here: the report describes no patient infused after a second allograft, so the interaction with HCT2 immunosuppression and engraftment is unmeasured rather than reassuring.; Both gates are shut until typing returns. A*02:01 plus the directional HA-1 mismatch, recipient A/G or A/A with donor G/G, and nobody has genotyped either of them.; One grade 4 infusion reaction in 9, and grade 3-5 infections after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide. Lymphodepletion in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow is not a low-toxicity step just because the cells are.; Single site in Seattle. The preferences permit travel, but travel plus lymphodepletion plus cytopenias needs a local backup plan written before she goes. critic3lown=9. That is the entire clinical evidence base, 4 of 9 achieved or maintained CR, and the registered primary endpoint of NCT03326921 is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so the 44.4% is a descriptive secondary readout and not a pre-specified efficacy result. What separates it from the rest of the HLA-restricted field is that the preclinical work is on the actual clinical construct (Dossa 2018) with independent replication of the target across a 13-TCR panel and 15 HA-1-positive patient samples (Pilunov 2023), plus a protocol that requires prior allo-HCT rather than excluding it. The HA-2 arm should not ride on the same billing: TSC-101 rests on Heemskerk 2003, in vitro, 23 years old, and not the TCR in the clinical product, so treating HA-1 and HA-2 as equivalently evidenced is an error. The evidence is thin and I will not dress it up, but it is the best-supported version of the option this case was submitted to find.n=9 in a phase 1 whose registered primary endpoint is feasibility and DLT. Nobody should quote 44.4% as an expected response rate; All three gating genotypes are unretrieved: recipient HLA-A*02:01, recipient HA-1(H) at rs1801284 (A/G or A/A), donor HA-1(H)-negative. Without them the option is a hypothesis, not a plan; No published HA-1 TCR-T data at anything like 85% marrow blasts, and none in extramedullary disease; Antigen-presentation escape is unmeasured. Christopher 2018 and Toffalori 2019 both show non-genomic HLA class II loss after transplant, and Gambacorta 2022 attributes up to 40% of post-transplant relapses to it, which is exactly the failure mode a six-year escape from an HLA-identical sibling graft would predict; Single site, single sponsor, no independent clinical replication of the product concensusite4lowNo guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T, and I want that on the record first: not NCCN AML v3.2026, not ELN 2022, not the EBMT DLI recommendations. What is guideline-endorsed is the route. NCCN's R/R pathway names clinical trial as strongly preferred, and high-resolution HLA typing sits in NCCN's own AML workup, so pulling the 2020 allele-level report is guideline-concordant care rather than a research errand. NCT03326921 is recruiting, requires prior allo-HCT instead of excluding it, and sets no blast ceiling, which is unusual enough to justify the trip if the genotypes line up.Two gates are shut. HLA-A*02:01 is unretrieved, and neither the patient nor her sibling has been genotyped at HA-1; the trial needs recipient A/G or A/A with a donor who is G/G.; Phase 1 with n=9 in the published report (pmid 38683966). That is feasibility and dose-limiting-toxicity data, not an efficacy estimate anyone should rank on.; HLA loss or downregulation at relapse would leave every A*02:01-restricted approach blind to these blasts, so pair the typing with a surface class I flow read.; It behaves as post-transplant consolidation. It does not answer the 85% blast burden by itself, and treating it as first-line here would invert the sequence. advocate1lowShe came to Libby for HLA-restricted immunotherapy, and three of the four HA-directed products shut the door on prior allo-HCT. NCT03326921 does the opposite: a prior graft is an entry requirement rather than an exclusion, there is no marrow-blast ceiling and no performance-status floor, and 4 of 9 infused patients achieved or held a CR with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS (pmid:38683966). Nothing in her preference file blocks this, since toxicity_vetoes and modality_constraints are both empty and travel to a single Seattle site is acceptable under prefers_trials with geography_band null. What blocks it is a records request and two genotypes, and the FHCC intake line (206-606-4668, immunotherapy@fredhutch.org) can be asked whether they run the HA-1 rs1801284 typing on her and the sibling during screening.Two gates are still unopened and either one can close this permanently: she must be HLA-A*02:01 positive and HA-1(H) positive (rs1801284 A/G or A/A) with a sibling who is HA-1(H)-negative or A*02:01-negative.; n=9 on a feasibility endpoint. Nobody should hear 4 of 9 as a response rate, and I would say that to her in those words.; The product is made from donor cells, so the sibling has to agree to a fresh collection before anything gets manufactured. That consent conversation is on the critical path and nobody has started it.; A relapse six years out is exactly where HLA class II downregulation and antigen-presentation escape turn up (pmid:30380364). Germline A*02:01 positivity does not prove the relapsed clone still presents it, which is why the HLA-LOH read on sorted blasts belongs in the same workup.; Preference axes fully satisfied: prefers_trials, travel, empty vetoes, empty modality constraints, curative intent. In tension: nothing, until organ function is documented and the 0.75 efficacy weight gets the revisit her own free text asks for.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocatedissentevidence_qualityShe is right that the case was submitted for this and right that the genotype retrieval starts this week, but rank 1 asks nine patients on a feasibility-and-DLT primary endpoint to carry an 85% marrow. Mazziotta gave an A*02:01-restricted TCR to post-transplant disease and got median OS 242 days with only 2 of 15 carrying overt disease (pmid:40473616), and Medigene's own reading of their phase 1 was that tumour burden was the limiting factor (pmid:41008812). Collection, manufacture and lymphodepletion take weeks that a marrow moving this fast may not give her, which is why I want this third rather than off the list. conservativeadvocatedissenttoxicityWe rank the same product four places apart, and the disagreement is about what runs first. Fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion into an 85% marrow, in a series that reported grade 3-5 infections and one grade 4 infusion reaction in 9 patients, is a myelosuppressive step being ordered with no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no ejection fraction anywhere in the chart. The missing safety datum I want named rather than gestured at is that nobody in NCT03326921 was infused after a second allograft, so the HCT2 interaction is unmeasured; this is a dissent and not a veto, because the cells themselves produced no DLT, no CRS and no ICANS and preferences.json vetoes nothing, but I would not put lymphodepletion ahead of cytoreduction. advocatecriticqualifiedevidence_qualityTaking their rank 3 rather than their rank 1, because that is the pick where they answer me. On the registered endpoint they are right and I wrote the same thing in round 1: NCT03326921 is powered for manufacturing feasibility and DLT, 4 of 9 is a descriptive secondary, and nobody should quote 44.4% to her as a response rate. Where I still hold is narrower than my rank 1 was: n=9 on a feasibility endpoint limits what may be claimed, not whether HLA-A*02:01 gets retrieved from a 2020 chart, and critic's own concern list lands in the same place when it calls the option a hypothesis rather than a plan. advocateconcensusitedissentpreference_fitI agree with their rank 1, so I am taking their rank 4. Guideline silence is doing too much work here: concensusite writes that NCCN carries no DLI recommendation at all and then ranks DLI above the option this run was submitted to find. free_text_constraints names HLA-restricted immunotherapy eligibility as the explicit reason for the case and asks for that pathway to be surfaced and de-risked, and the de-risking step is a records request for an allele-level report that was already run in 2020. criticadvocatedissentevidence_qualityRank 1 is what I dissent from, not the option itself. The registered primary endpoint of NCT03326921 is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so 4 of 9 is a descriptive secondary readout from a trial never powered to produce a response rate, and the denominator mixes patients whose CR was induced with patients whose CR was maintained (pmid:38683966). Your own concern row says nobody should hear 4 of 9 as a response rate, and I agree; thin evidence labelled honestly still beats no option, but putting it above the cytoreduction that makes it deliverable is a separate claim and the n=9 does not support it. concensusiteadvocatequalifiedguideline_fitNo guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T. The route is a different story: NCCN AML v3.2026 puts clinical trial first for relapsed/refractory disease and its workup already orders the high-resolution HLA typing this pick is waiting on, so pursuing NCT03326921 is guideline-concordant care. What I cannot square with any guideline text is the rank, because everything pointing cellular therapy at post-transplant relapse assumes cytoreduced disease and the 4 of 9 in pmid:38683966 mixes induced with maintained remissions, so keep the records request moving this week and the infusion itself behind the debulking.

docs.title: Gating workup before any therapeutic commitment: fitness and organ-function documentation (CrCl, LFTs including bilirubin, ejection fraction) plus HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor, quantitative CD33/CD123 antigen density, and TP53 variant-level NGS with copy-number calling (pending-diagnostics-workup)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative1highNothing below this line can be priced without labs that do not exist yet. There is no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no cardiac study in the record, and profile.json calls the fitness assessment an explicit open item, which means every toxicity claim any of us makes this round is unanchored. The same visit buys the assays the rest of the board is arguing over, and two of those gates are hard numbers a screening coordinator will apply: CLAG-GO on NCT04050280 needs CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, and the tagraxofusp cohort on NCT03113643 needs albumin above 3.2 g/dL. preferences.json says the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known, and I read that as the patient asking for exactly this step.Delay is itself a harm here. Peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, so this workup runs alongside starting cytoreduction, not before it.; HA-1 genotyping at rs1801284 is not a routine US send-out. The Fred Hutch screening pathway on NCT03326921 may be the fastest route to a result for both her and the sibling, which makes this a referral clock rather than a lab clock.; A tidy chemistry panel from one draw is not a cardiac assessment. I want a measured ejection fraction on the chart before anyone writes idarubicin or a second conditioning regimen. critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativedissentotherRanking a lab requisition first is a category error, and her own concern row concedes the point: peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, so this workup runs alongside cycle 1 of nct:NCT04050280 rather than in front of it. The gates she names are real, CD33 on at least 20% of blasts and a measured ejection fraction, and both get answered by a screening visit that costs a phone call and a send-out. Ordering it as pick 1 spends a therapeutic slot on the one thing nobody at this table opposes. advocateconservativequalifiedpreference_fitThis is the one rank-1 on the board that reads her free text back accurately, and conservative flagging its own thresholds as "mine and not hers" against an empty toxicity_vetoes list is exactly the right handling. My qualification is about how it renders: a workup at rank 1 will read to her as wait, and conservative's own first concern says it runs alongside cytoreduction, so that sentence has to survive into the PI rather than the rank number. One item inside that workup is not like the others: HA-1 genotyping of her and the sibling carries a manufacturing lead time nothing else on the list does, so it belongs on the same day as the ejection fraction and not after a response is documented. criticconservativequalifiedotherThe gating logic holds where it is specific: NCT04050280 screens on CD33 in at least 20% of blasts, and profile.json carries no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no ejection fraction, so most of the toxicity talk on this board is currently unpriced. A workup is not a therapy, though, and ranking it first leaves the ranking question open in a patient whose peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, which your own first concern concedes. Run the assays as a parallel track and let rank 1 name something that treats her. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitRanking the workup first has real guideline cover: the NCCN AML v3.2026 evaluation includes HLA typing for anyone in whom allogeneic HCT is considered, liver and renal chemistries, and cardiac assessment where cardiotoxic exposure sits in the history, which FLAG-IDA put there. The one item no guideline orders is HA-1 genotyping at rs1801284, so sending it through the NCT03326921 screening pathway is the right call rather than a workaround. The concurrency framing matters too, since nothing in the workup list licenses waiting on results while peripheral blasts run from 58% to 82%.

docs.title: CBX-250, CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific engager (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676) (cg1-a2-tcr-mimetic)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowIf A*02:01 comes back positive but the HA-1 mismatch runs the wrong way, this is what keeps the HLA-A2 handle alive, because it needs only the allele: recurrence after HSCT is eligible by name and the extramedullary exclusion applies to isolated lesions, which her marrow involvement takes her out of (nct:NCT06994676). The human evidence is zero and I will say that plainly. What I am betting on is preclinical: the engager killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo (pmid:39939820), and the CAR version of the same target left normal marrow haematopoiesis intact (pmid:40437170). There is also a compassionate-use address on this one, so a full slot list is not the end of the conversation.No patient has been treated. First-in-human escalation means she could sit at a dose level chosen to be safe rather than active.; Peptide-HLA engagers have no characterised CRS profile in humans yet, and she would be receiving one in a post-transplant marrow.; Enrolment wants white cells under 25,000/uL, which only holds if cytoreduction is already working.; CG1 appears nowhere on her nominated feature list. This pick rides an HLA restriction, not a validated target in her disease. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate2lowIf the HA-1 genotypes do not line up, this is the other half of the same records request, because CBX-250 rides HLA-A*02:01 alone and asks nothing of the sibling. The protocol calls relapse at any time after HSCT eligible, ECOG 0-1 matches her, eleven US sites beat one, and Crossbow publishes a compassionate-use address (clinical@crossbowtx.com) for a patient who cannot get a slot, which almost nothing else in this dossier offers. There is no human efficacy number yet; the case rests on an engager that killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo and left normal marrow alone (pmid:39939820, pmid:40437170). Her file vetoes no toxicity, so cytokine release is a conversation to have with her rather than a reason I would strike this off her list.Phase 1 dose escalation with no efficacy readout in humans. I am ranking this on eligibility fit and reachability, not on evidence, and she should hear it framed that way.; WBC has to be under 25,000 at enrollment against peripheral blasts that ran 58 to 82 percent, so this only becomes real after cytoreduction (pick 3).; Same master switch as pick 1. If the 2020 report comes back A*02:01-negative, picks 1 and 2 both close on the same afternoon, and the A*24:02 line in that report is then the only HLA-restricted thread left worth pulling.; Worth asking the sponsor whether CG1 expression is measured on study or whether A*02:01 alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete before anyone books a flight.

docs.title: CLAG-GO: cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (NCT04050280) (clag-go)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1moderateNothing else I want for her works until the marrow comes down off 85%, and this is the one strong-fit trial that names relapse after allogeneic transplant as eligible rather than disqualifying (nct:NCT04050280). The upside I am buying is the CLAG-M backbone with a CD33 payload on top of it: composite CR 56.6%, 50% in the TP53-mutated subgroup and 38.5% after prior venetoclax (pmid:39955432). I will not pretend the gemtuzumab part is proven in her karyotype, because Hills found no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9). What makes it worth the risk anyway is that fractionated dosing produced no veno-occlusive disease in the seven patients transplanted afterwards (pmid:17051246), so a response here buys her the graft instead of costing it.The 56.6% belongs to CLAG-M plus lintuzumab-Ac225, and that alpha-emitter is unavailable. CLAG-GO itself has no published efficacy in refractory AML at all.; She progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax. Another nucleoside-analogue backbone is asking cladribine to succeed where fludarabine failed, and cross-resistance is the likeliest single reason this fails.; Entry needs CD33 on at least 20% of blasts; the flow result on file is qualitative and does not establish that. Quantitative antigen density has to be ordered now, not at screening.; Prolonged aplasia in a six-year-old graft could end the transplant plan rather than enable it, and there are no organ-function numbers anywhere in the profile to price that against. conservative2moderateFractionated gemtuzumab is the one cytoreductive component here whose safety record survives contact with a patient heading for another graft: Taksin's 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 produced no grade 3-4 hepatic toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease in 57 patients, seven of whom were transplanted afterwards, and Hills found fewer early deaths at 3 mg/m2 than at 6 mg/m2 for the same efficacy. The expectation has to be set honestly against the same evidence base: in adverse cytogenetics the 6-year survival benefit was OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18), p=0.9, and ALFA-0701 enrolled de novo AML only, so neither trial says her MDS-related complex-karyotype disease will respond. I would run it through NCT04050280 rather than as off-label dosing, because that protocol was written for this exact situation, refractory after intensive therapy with a prior allograft permitted at 60 days or more provided GVHD is grade 1 at most. Entry turns on CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, which the qualitative flow result does not establish.Adverse karyotype is precisely where the CD33 evidence is weakest. OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18) is not a signal and I will not let it be sold as one.; Fractionation lowers veno-occlusive risk, it does not zero it, and the whole plan points at another conditioning regimen within months of the last dose. Baseline bilirubin and transaminases before dose one, then weekly.; Cladribine plus high-dose cytarabine on a graft that has been in place six years. Count recovery may be slow, and the step after this one needs a countable remission rather than an aplastic marrow. critic2lowNCT04050280 is the best population match among open slots in this dossier (post-allograft relapse explicitly permitted at 60+ days, refractoriness to an intensive regimen required, isolated myeloid sarcoma excluded but marrow disease not), and it has no posted results, so every effect estimate attached to it is imported from somewhere else. The imports do not travel well. ALFA-0701's HR 0.58 (0.43-0.78, p=0.0003) came from untreated de novo AML aged 50-70 in a trial that specifically did not enrol secondary or therapy-related disease, and Hills 2014, the only tier-1a RoB2-low row in the file, puts adverse cytogenetics at OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18), p=0.9, a 2.2% absolute difference at six years. I rank it second on eligibility fit and on the cytoreductive backbone, not on the gemtuzumab component, which is the part with high-quality randomised evidence pointing away from benefit in her karyotype.Selective reporting risk on the regimen itself: NCT04050280 is recruiting with no posted results, so the regimen has zero direct evidence in refractory AML; Indirectness on both imports. ALFA-0701 is untreated de novo AML with secondary and therapy-related AML excluded, which is her diagnosis; MyloFrance-1's 26% CR (n=57) is first relapse after chemotherapy, not refractory disease after an allograft, so read it as a ceiling; Hills 2014 adverse-cytogenetics OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18, p=0.9) is a prespecified exploratory stratification in 3325 randomised patients, which is the strongest evidence in this dossier and it is null for her group; CD33 density and rs12459419 are both unmeasured. Laszlo 2019 puts density at r2=0.3124 (P<0.0001) for gemtuzumab cytotoxicity, so it is a partial modifier rather than a gate, and a low reading should not be used to veto anything; ALFA-0701 was open-label with investigator-assessed EFS components (RoB2: some concerns on outcome measurement) concensusite1moderateNCCN AML v3.2026 puts clinical trial first for relapsed/refractory disease and lists both halves of this regimen separately in the same pathway: cladribine plus cytarabine plus G-CSF sits in the intensive R/R chemotherapy table, and gemtuzumab ozogamicin is the listed CD33-positive option, on-label for R/R CD33+ AML. NCT04050280 is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier and it is recruiting, so the guideline-preferred route and the practical route are the same thing here. What it buys is cytoreduction, which gates everything downstream. I am not counting on the gemtuzumab component to carry the regimen, because the individual-patient meta-analysis found no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 0.83-1.18, p=0.9).The NCCN R/R chemotherapy table was built from patients who had not already relapsed after an allograft. Nothing in that pathway is calibrated to a second-transplant candidate sitting at 85% marrow blasts.; Gemtuzumab's cytogenetic problem is real and specific to her: pmid 25008258 gives OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18, p=0.9) in adverse karyotype, and hers is complex with del(5q), del(7q), MECOM gain and KMT2A amplification.; No published CLAG-GO efficacy exists in refractory AML. The only CLAG-GO paper in the dossier (pmid 41173347) is frontline core-binding-factor disease, a favourable-risk population that says nothing about this one.; Quantitative CD33 density is still unmeasured. The ALFA-0701 central flow reanalysis tied benefit to expression level rather than to a positive-or-negative call, so the qualitative flow result is a weak basis for choosing an ADC.; The right-thigh myeloid sarcoma may not track with the marrow. NCCN treats extramedullary AML systemically and keeps radiotherapy for local salvage, but the guideline text on myeloid sarcoma is thin, mostly FDG-PET/CT at workup. advocate3moderateEverything above needs her blast burden down first. CBX-250 wants a white count under 25,000, sibling DLI protocols cap blasts at 30 percent, and a payer will want documented disease control before authorising a second graft, so cytoreduction is what makes the immunotherapy goal reachable rather than a detour away from it. NCT04050280 names post-allograft relapse as eligible at 60 days or more off immunosuppression with no more than grade 1 GVHD, and if the Baltimore slot does not open the regimen can be rebuilt from marketed drugs at her home centre, which is a fallback almost nothing else here has. Two honest caveats she is entitled to: fractionated gemtuzumab monotherapy produced 26% CR in first relapse rather than refractory disease (pmid:17051246), and in the 3,325-patient individual-patient-data meta-analysis the adverse-cytogenetics group saw no survival benefit from gemtuzumab (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9; pmid:25008258), which is her karyotype.The efficacy weight of 0.75 argues for an intensive cytoreduction, but her free text says that number was set before anyone documented her fitness. Cardiac and hepatic assessment first, then re-check this pick against it. I am not comfortable ranking a cladribine/cytarabine backbone as if organ function were known when it is not.; The adverse-karyotype meta-analysis result is the real weakness here and I would rather put it in front of her than bury it. Quantitative CD33 density and rs12459419 genotype would at least tell her how much to expect.; Marrow-derived CD33 does not speak for the thigh sarcoma. Paired myeloid sarcoma series show CD33 detectable in 79 percent of lesions rather than all, so the extramedullary site may not answer to a CD33-directed regimen even if the marrow does.; This is a bridge, not a destination. If nobody has planned the cellular or transplant consolidation before it starts, a response gets spent rather than used.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocaterisktakerendorsepreference_fitI came in at rank 1 on the TCR-T and this is the position that moved me: pmid 40473616 and pmid 41008812 are tumour-burden arguments rather than evidence-tier ones, and a T-cell product that cannot work at 85% blasts serves the stated request while failing the stated goal, which is curative intent. Cytoreduction first is what keeps the HLA-restricted door open, and NCT04050280 does it inside a trial, which satisfies prefers_trials rather than trading against it. The condition I attach is that the HLA record pull and the HA-1 genotyping of her and the sibling run during induction, because holding them until a response is documented restarts the manufacturing clock at the exact moment the window is best. concensusiterisktakerqualifiedguideline_fitSame rank-1 as mine, and for TP53-aberrant poor-risk AML NCCN v3.2026 lists clinical trial and nothing else, so a trial regimen leading the board is the guideline position rather than a workaround. My reservation is which component does the work: the same guideline lists gemtuzumab for R/R CD33-positive AML with no cytogenetic qualifier yet keeps it out of the poor-risk induction options it offers favourable and intermediate risk, and ALFA-0701 enrolled de novo disease only (pmid:22482940) while hers is MDS-related. The guideline-fit case rests on the CLAG backbone plus NCT04050280's population match, and the 56.6% composite CR belongs to lintuzumab-Ac225's payload (pmid:39955432), which should not migrate onto this regimen.

docs.title: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) from the HLA-identical sibling, sequential cytoreduction into reduced-intensity conditioning (second-allo-hct)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2moderateOnly a graft cures her, and the registry stratification puts her on the good side of every factor except one: six years of remission and a sibling first donor, a stratum that ran 37% +/- 6% two-year survival (pmid:23918951). Schmid's score prices the exception honestly, with blasts under 27% carrying HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40-0.72) for survival (pmid:22167752), which is exactly why rank 1 sits where it does. The aggressive version I will defend is sequential rather than remission-gated: cytoreduction running straight into reduced-intensity conditioning gave CR in 66 of 75 patients, 59 of whom had progressive or refractory disease, with 42% alive at two years (pmid:16110027). Amsacrine is not marketed in the US, so the reachable form of that idea is nct:NCT06928662 or an institutional sequential regimen.Non-relapse mortality on a second graft is the tax nobody avoids, and about half of those who do reach CR relapse again (pmid:23918951).; The US sequential protocol asks her to take a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through. I would substitute the cytoreduction rather than repeat it.; Ruutu's 15% five-year relapse-free survival across 2632 second transplants is the number to quote if anyone starts describing this as a cure with a percentage attached (pmid:26367221).; The thigh sarcoma is not treated by marrow-directed conditioning and will need its own local plan.; No cardiac or renal data documented. A second conditioning decision cannot rest on ECOG 1 alone. conservative3moderateA sibling graft is the only thing in this dossier with a documented cure fraction, and her stratum in Christopeit's registry, a related-donor first transplant, sat at 2-year OS 37% +/- 6%. Almost every favourable factor in Ruutu's 2632-patient EBMT series is hers as well, a six-year first remission, a long intertransplant interval and a sibling donor, with one exception, and that exception is 85% marrow blasts. Schmid's post-RIC-relapse score puts the worst band at 4% +/- 2% at two years and gives blasts below 27% an HR of 0.53, so taking her to conditioning with the marrow as it stands spends the non-relapse mortality without buying the survival. I support HCT2 as the destination and I would gate it on a documented remission or at least blasts under 27%, a measured ejection fraction, and a creatinine clearance.Non-relapse mortality is the number nobody actually has for her. All three registry rows report survival and none tabulates adverse events, so the tolerability case rests on curves rather than a per-organ risk table.; Conditioning intensity is unresolved and there is no cardiac or renal baseline from which to choose it. That decision should not be made on an ECOG score alone.; A second graft from the same sibling does nothing about whatever let this leukaemia escape graft-versus-leukaemia the first time. The class II downregulation and HLA-loss rows in the preclinical set are a reason to check for HLA loss on the blasts before assuming the donor is the answer. critic1moderateFour independent registries say the same thing about relapse after allo-HCT, which is as close to replication as this question gets: Ruutu 2015 (n=2632, 5-year RFS 15%), Christopeit 2013 (n=179, 2-year OS 37% +/- 6% in the related-donor-first-graft stratum she sits in), Schmid 2012 (n=263) and Schmid 2007 (n=399). All of it is retrospective and none of it adjusts for the obvious confounder, which is that who gets offered a second graft is itself a fitness judgement made by the treating centre. Every favourable number quoted for her is gated on a blast burden she does not have: Schmid 2012's HR 0.53 (0.40-0.72, p<0.001) is for marrow blasts below 27%, and its worst prognostic band is 4% +/- 2% at two years. At 85% blasts she is in that worst band today, so I rank the platform first and treat the debulking question as the thing that actually decides whether any of these estimates apply to her.ROBINS-I confounding domain is unaddressed in all four registries: selection into a second transplant tracks with fitness, donor availability and centre practice, and no row here adjusts for it; Applicability failure at 85% blasts. The 37% +/- 6% and 32% +/- 7% strata require blasts under 27-35%; quoting them for her as she stands would be an indirectness error, not a rounding error; Non-relapse mortality after a second graft is not tabulated in any of these rows, so the harm side of the estimate is missing entirely; No organ-function or cardiac data in profile.json. Conditioning tolerance is being assumed rather than measured; Orti 2018 (n=46) is too small to support its own equivalence claim between DLI and HCT2; do not read it as evidence the choice does not matter concensusite2moderateNCCN AML v3.2026 tells you to start the donor search at first relapse and lists targeted therapy or chemotherapy followed by HCT as the R/R route; ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022;140:1345-1377) recommends allogeneic HCT once cytoreduction is achieved. Neither body writes a separate graded recommendation for a second allograft after post-transplant relapse, so HCT2 rests on registry evidence and transplant-centre judgement rather than a category. The registry stratification has her on both sides at once: sibling donor and a six-year first remission are favourable in the 2632-patient EBMT analysis, and 85% blasts is not. Read against the guideline text, HCT2 is the consolidation step and not the next thing to do.Every guideline statement supporting a transplant here attaches to remission or at least to achieved cytoreduction. At 85% marrow blasts she sits outside the population any of them describes.; No NCCN category attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse. The pathway assumes a first transplant, so anyone quoting a category number for HCT2 is quoting something that does not exist.; Organ function, cardiac status and HCT-CI are undocumented, and the guideline transplant recommendations assume a fitness assessment nobody has done yet.; pmid 22167752 is blunt about the sequencing: long-term survival occurred almost only where cytoreduction reached CR before the second graft or DLI. advocate4moderateThis is the honest answer to a stated curative intent, and it is the platform the HLA-restricted consolidation in picks 1 and 2 is supposed to sit on top of. Her stratum is the favourable one on nearly every axis the registries measure: a related-donor first transplant carries 37% +/- 6% two-year survival versus 16% +/- 4% after an unrelated one (pmid:23918951), and a six-year remission sits far past the five-month cut that drives the EBMT prognostic score (pmid:22167752). The exception is the one that matters most today, roughly 85% marrow blasts, which is why I rank this under the cytoreduction rather than over it; DLI given with active disease runs 15% +/- 3% two-year survival against 56% +/- 10% given in remission (pmid:17909197). No preference blocks it, since HCT2 is named as acceptable and no modality is ruled out, but fitness for a second conditioning regimen is undocumented and that assessment should be booked this week rather than after the workup returns.Fitness is the load-bearing unknown. Her preference file explicitly asks for the 0.75 efficacy weight to be revisited once organ function is documented, and a second allograft is the pick where that revisit changes the answer most.; The US sequential-conditioning route (NCT06928662) repeats a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through. That is a clinical objection to raise with the investigator, not an access one.; Donor questions nobody has closed: germline predisposition shared with the sibling would redirect donor choice, and the hereditary panel needs cultured fibroblasts rather than blood while blasts are circulating.; Payer authorisation is likelier to turn on documented cytoreduction than on anything biological, which is another reason pick 3 precedes this one.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconcensusitequalifiedguideline_fitYour finding that no NCCN category attaches to HCT2 after post-transplant relapse is correct and the board should hear it, and it does not lower my rank 1. What sits behind HCT2 is four registries agreeing on one stratification (pmid:26367221 n=2632, pmid:17909197 n=399, pmid:22167752 n=263, pmid:23918951 n=179), which replicates a prognostic model rather than a treatment effect, and none of them adjusts for who gets selected into a second graft; a missing category number is not missing evidence, and evidence quality is not the same axis as clinical value. Separately on your rank 5: NCT06616636 wants a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, which sits at the detection limit of the same panel that called her TP53-negative, so the assay rather than the biology may decide that eligibility. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitNo NCCN category and no ELN grade attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse; the pathways assume a first transplant, so all five of us are ranking HCT2 on registry evidence (pmid:26367221) where the guideline text stops, and the PI should read that as uncovered rather than contraindicated. I rank HCT2 second myself, so this is a qualification of placement, not of the pick. NCCN AML v3.2026 (the 11/24/2025 text, the floor I could verify) and ELN 2022 (pmid:35797463) both describe cytoreduction and then transplant, and critic's own blast-gate concern concedes that ordering, which argues against rank 1.

docs.title: BMS-986497 (ORM-6151), CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader, monotherapy arm (NCT06419634) (bms-986497-orm-6151)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowA trial fallback that does not depend on the HLA answer at all, which matters because picks 1 and 2 stand or fall on one allele. CD33 only has to be detectable rather than above a threshold, MDS-related secondary AML is named in the inclusion criteria, and the posted criteria carry no blast cap and no bar on a prior allograft, which is rare across the 47 trials screened here. Push for the monotherapy arm rather than the azacitidine-venetoclax triplet, since she progressed through venetoclax and re-exposing her to it would spend a trial slot on a drug she has already failed. First in human, so there is no efficacy figure to quote, and the absent exclusions should be confirmed with the site before she travels.No published clinical data of any kind. This is on the list because it is open, reachable and compatible with prefers_trials, not because anyone knows what it does.; Trial-arm assignment may not be hers to choose. If the site will only take her onto the triplet, the venetoclax objection stands and I would rather she kept the slot for something else.; Enrolling here consumes weeks that an 85% marrow may not have, so it competes with pick 3 on time rather than complementing it.

docs.title: Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after debulking, as the lower-intensity alternative to a second graft (donor-lymphocyte-infusion)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative5lowIf the fitness workup comes back badly, this keeps curative intent on the table without committing her to a second conditioning regimen. Orti's 46-patient comparison found the univariate survival advantage of a second graft over DLI (p=0.021) did not hold on multivariate analysis once both groups had been debulked, which is thin evidence but it is the only head-to-head in the set. The honest number for her is Schmid's 15% +/- 3% two-year survival for DLI given in aplasia or with active disease, against 56% +/- 10% when given in remission or with a favourable karyotype, and she currently sits on the wrong side of both. That is an argument for cytoreducing before the infusion, not against the infusion.GVHD is the toxicity and the mechanism at the same time, and not one of the registry rows grades it, so the risk cannot be quantified for her from this evidence at all.; The trial route is probably shut even where the therapy is not: NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% and allows a single prior post-transplant line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent.; Cell dose and escalation schedule are centre-specific here, so whoever gives it owns the toxicity, and that argues for doing it where her transplant records live. critic5lowSchmid 2007 is the only row in this dossier's post-transplant relapse literature carrying a concurrent untreated comparator: 171 given DLI against 228 not, 2-year OS 21% +/- 3% versus 9% +/- 2%, p=0.04, n=399. Confounding by indication is the central problem and the design cannot fix it, since the patients who received DLI are the ones their centres judged well enough to receive it. Her relapse beyond 5 months post-HCT puts her on the favourable side of that variable (p<0.0001), but 85% blasts and an adverse karyotype put her in the 15% +/- 3% stratum rather than the 56% +/- 10% one. Before committing to anything that depends on donor T cells recognising these blasts, measure HLA class II on them.Confounding by indication is unadjusted and probably explains a large share of the 21% versus 9% gap; Her stratum is the 15% +/- 3% one (aplasia or active disease), not the 56% +/- 10% one, unless cytoreduction gets her into remission first; NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% and allows only one prior post-transplant salvage line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent, so the trial route is shut at present burden; GVHD after DLI is discussed narratively in Schmid 2007 with no per-term adverse-event table, so the harm estimate is not quantified anywhere in this file concensusite3lowThe EBMT best-practice recommendations on DLI after allogeneic HCT (Practice Harmonisation and Guidelines Committee with the Cellular Therapy and Immunobiology Working Party, Lancet Haematology 2024) are the closest thing to a graded guideline for post-transplant relapse, and they set therapeutic DLI from a matched sibling at a starting dose of 1x10^7 CD3/kg. Her donor is an HLA-identical sibling who already donated, so the logistics are the easy part. The catch is that those recommendations are written for low burden or post-cytoreduction disease: the EBMT registry puts a patient with 85% blasts and adverse cytogenetics in the 15% two-year survival band rather than the 56% one. NCCN AML v3.2026 carries no DLI recommendation at all, which is worth saying out loud rather than letting the silence read as endorsement.DLI into 85% blasts is off-guideline. The EBMT recommendation is built for MRD-level or cytoreduced disease, not for florid haematologic relapse.; A relapse six years out looks like graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft loss. Re-infusing the same donor repertoire that already stopped holding the disease is a bet no guideline addresses.; GVHD is the standard trade and preferences.json vetoes nothing, but grade III-IV GVHD would close the door on HCT2 and on any post-transplant cellular consolidation.; pmid 29526774 compares DLI with HCT2 in 46 patients. Reading that as equivalence is more than the study can hold. advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed ADC), off-label after the May 2026 BPDCN approval (pivekimab-sunirine)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic4lowPeer-reviewed, in the right disease and the right line, and it reports its own uncertainty honestly: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% (6-36) in 29 patients at the RP2D (Daver 2024, Lancet Oncology). Response was a secondary endpoint of a dose-finding study whose primary was MTD and RP2D selection, and an interval running from 8% to 40% is not a number to build a plan around. It ranks here mostly on obtainability relative to its competitors: flotetuzumab posted 26.7% CR/CRh in exactly her chemorefractory population (Uy 2021, n=30) and the programme is dead, and lintuzumab-Ac225's 56.6% composite CR comes from a 26-patient dose-escalation with subgroup rates on undisclosed denominators and every trial currently suspended for drug supply. Two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the specific thing to weigh in someone being lined up for a second graft.ORR was secondary to an MTD/RP2D primary; single-arm, open-label, sponsor-analysed, no OS readout in the R/R AML cohort; 95% CI 8-40 on n=29. The point estimate carries almost no information on its own; Veno-occlusive disease before a planned second allograft (2 dose-limiting events in 68), which is the one toxicity that could cost her the transplant; CD123 antigen density is unmeasured, and the 75% frontline BPDCN figure is a different disease and must not be carried across; Cross-check on the alternatives: Vadakekolathu 2020's 47% CR in TP53-abnormal disease is a post-hoc correlative analysis on 15 patients with no CI reported, and should not be cited as a TP53-specific effect size for anything concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticqualifiedtoxicityTaking pick 4 rather than his transplant pick, because the veno-occlusive line is hardening into a hepatic veto and Daver does not support that: both dose-limiting events occurred at 0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg, four to ten times the 0.045 mg/kg recommended phase 2 dose, and both were reversible (pmid:38423051). That is a dose-level finding rather than a property of the drug, so striking CD123 out of the pre-conditioning window on it is an over-read. Where he is right is the interval: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) on 29 patients is too soft to displace CLAG-GO as the cytoreduction, so hold it as the fallback if CD33 density comes back low. conservativecriticdissenttoxicityTargeting rank 4 rather than the second-graft platform at rank 1, which I support and gate the same way they do. Two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the wrong hepatic exposure in the weeks before a conditioning regimen, so the dissent is against the pre-conditioning window rather than against the drug: if HCT2 comes off the table, pivekimab at rank 4 stands. The consistency I owe the board is that I ranked another calicheamicin conjugate second, and the reason is Taksin's 57 patients at 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 with no grade 3-4 hepatic toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease, seven of them transplanted afterwards; pivekimab has no comparable pre-transplant hepatic series.

docs.title: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning + allogeneic HCT, NCT03670966 (at211-bc8-b10)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowSIERRA proved the principle that matters for a patient nobody can get into remission: durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with antigen-targeted conditioning against 0% (95% CI 0-4.7) on conventional care, all with active disease at randomisation (pmid:39298738). Her first transplant is the sole reason she cannot have that drug, and the astatine-211 anti-CD45 protocol is the one targeted-conditioning route that admits a prior reduced-intensity allograft (nct:NCT03670966). Published human efficacy for it is nil. What exists is a murine dose-response of 123, 101, 61 and 37 days median survival at 24, 20, 12 and 0 microCi (pmid:23471305), and I would rather spend a phone call now on whether a haploidentical relative exists than find out in three months that we needed one.No human efficacy data of any kind for 211At-BC8-B10, and NCT02665065 showed overall survival did not separate (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41) even where the durable-CR difference was stark.; The protocol wants a haploidentical relative, not the HLA-identical sibling who gave the 2020 graft. If no such relative exists this pick evaporates.; Myeloablative conditioning in 2020 would exclude her, and the profile does not record what she was given.; Circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3, which at 82% peripheral blasts means hydroxyurea has to work first.; Alpha-emitter dosimetry plus a second graft in a heavily pretreated marrow is an unquantified cytopenia risk. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativerisktakerdissentevidence_qualityWithdrawing the veto I pre-registered, cleanly: it was conditioned on a rank-1 pick taking her to conditioning at 85% blasts on the strength of Iomab-B, and at rank 5, with human efficacy for 211At-BC8-B10 stated as nil and the null OS (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41) sitting in their own concern list, the condition is not met. What survives is a dissent on transportability, because SIERRA excluded prior allo-HCT and NCT03670966 wants a haploidentical relative rather than the sibling who gave the 2020 graft, so the randomised 17.1% still cannot be quoted for her at any rank. On the workup, they are right that it is a prerequisite and not a therapy, and I concede the rank while holding the substance: CD33 on at least 20% of blasts is a screening gate on their own rank-1 trial and the qualitative flow result does not clear it. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityTaking rank 5 rather than rank 1, since your own CLAG-GO concern row already concedes that the 56.6% belongs to CLAG-M plus lintuzumab-Ac225 and not to CLAG-GO. SIERRA hit its registered primary endpoint at durable CR 17.1% (9.4-27.5) versus 0%, and in that same trial overall survival did not move (HR 0.99, 0.70-1.41, p=0.96), the FDA declined the filing and asked for an OS study, and prior allo-HCT was an exclusion, so she sits outside the randomised population (pmid:39298738); 211At-BC8-B10 then inherits the principle with no human efficacy behind it at all, only a syngeneic mouse transplant using a murine anti-CD45 (pmid:23471305). One more from your notes: the 47% flotetuzumab figure in TP53-abnormal disease is a post-hoc correlative read on 15 patients with no CI reported (pmid:33057635), so it should stay where you put it and travel no further.

docs.title: Rezatapopt (PC14586) + azacitidine on NCT06616636, contingent on a TP53 Y220C call (rezatapopt)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite5lowFor TP53-aberrant AML the honest guideline position is that no standard option performs well: against poor-risk AML with TP53 mutation or del(17p), NCCN AML v3.2026 lists clinical trial and nothing else. NCT06616636 is recruiting and is the trial-shaped answer that recommendation points at, but it screens on a Y220C call above 2% VAF from CLIA-approved local testing, and this case has no variant-level result in either direction. Resolve the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy first: original variant identity and VAF, p53 IHC, 17p FISH. If the lesion is not Y220C this pick disappears, and the guideline still says trial.Y220C status is unknown, so ranking this at all is contingent. A non-Y220C result drops it off the list entirely rather than demoting it.; No efficacy data in AML. pmid 40608889 found wild-type conformation restored in Y220C AML with limited or absent apoptosis unless combined with venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 inhibition, and she has already progressed through venetoclax.; An azacitidine backbone is slow against 85% blasts in refractory disease, which sits badly against the stated curative intent.; Eprenetapopt is not the fallback. That programme stopped after the randomised phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconcensusitedissentevidence_qualityHer rank 1 is my rank 1, so I am taking pick 5, which fails on my terms before it fails on hers: Carter restored wild-type p53 conformation in Y220C AML and got limited or no apoptosis unless venetoclax or an MDM2/XPO1 partner was added (pmid:40608889), and venetoclax is what she just progressed through. An azacitidine backbone on nct:NCT06616636 keeps the half of the mechanism that does not kill, and the trial's own CLIA gate of Y220C above 2% VAF sits at the detection limit of the panel that called her TP53-negative. If the variant comes back Y220C I would chase an MDM2 or XPO1 combination instead of listing a contingent pick that resolves to a failed drug. conservativeconcensusitedissentevidence_qualityRanked fifth on a Y220C call that does not exist in either direction, and NCT06616636 screens at VAF above 2% on the same class of panel that returned her TP53 result, so the assay would decide eligibility before the biology does. Carter's work has reactivated Y220C p53 restoring wild-type conformation with limited or absent apoptosis unless venetoclax is added, which is the agent she progressed through, so a positive call still leaves the pick without a partner drug and no peer-reviewed effect size to price it against. Their gemtuzumab reading I accept rather than argue with, absent from the NCCN poor-risk induction options while present for favourable and intermediate, and it lands on my own rank 2 as squarely as on theirs.

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Cole/Walter (2025)Leukemia13 human acute myeloid and lymphoblastic leukaemia cell lines, isogenic TP53-knockout/parental pairs, sublines overexpressing BCL-2, BCL-xL or MCL-1, and 9 primary AML samples13 cell lines; 5 isogenic TP53-KO/parental pairs; 9 primary AML samplesparental TP53 wild-type lines; non-overexpressing parental sublines; unconjugated antibody and free payload—After CD123-mediated internalisation the IGN payload alkylates DNA, and the resulting death signal runs through a p53-dependent, BCL-2-family-gated apoptotic pathway — so both antigen density at the front end and apoptotic competence at the back end set the response.Cytotoxicity tracked CD123 expression (R2=0.4469, P=0.0125), was significantly lower in TP53-knockout cells than in the matched wild-type parents across all 5 isogenic pairs, and was reduced in sublines overexpressing BCL-2 or BCL-xL. docs.title: CD123-directed CAR T cells — affinity and antigen-density thresholds

intervention_id: cd123-car-t · 1 row(s)

docs.title: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin vs CD33/CD3 BiTE AMG 330 — dependence on CD33 antigen density
