docs.title: Biomarker plan
docs.text:
Recommended assay Rationale Suggested assay provider Tissue requirements IDH1 codon 132 and IDH2 codons 140/172 mutation testing by DNA sequencing (comprehensive NGS panel or targeted hotspot assay), not R132H immunohistochemistry Sequencing decides whether an IDH-directed drug or trial is available at all, and it is the highest-yield untested item in the case: IDH1/IDH2 mutations were present in 71 percent of dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas in a paired series against 36 percent of conventional tumours (pmid:36926116). Order sequencing rather than R132H immunohistochemistry; the R132H antibody was raised for glioma, and roughly 40 percent of mutant cartilage tumours carry R132C, with R132G, R132L and R132S making up much of the rest (pmid:21598255), so a stain would read negative in the commonest scenario here. Skipping the test leaves the one established targeted handle in chondrosarcoma unassessable rather than excluded. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 400 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210 · 888-988-3639 Archival FFPE block or 10-15 unstained slides cut from the dedifferentiated component Expert bone-sarcoma pathology review of the diagnostic material, reporting the WHO diagnosis and the percentage of the specimen occupied by the dedifferentiated (non-cartilaginous) component The histology is on file as user-stated, and it is the fact that makes cytotoxic chemotherapy worth giving: dedifferentiated and mesenchymal are the only two potentially chemosensitive chondrosarcoma subtypes, with first-line ORR around 20 percent and median PFS of 4-5 months in advanced disease, while conventional, clear-cell and periosteal disease is chemoresistant (pmid:41895355). Reference-centre review also fixes the diagnosis that every trial protocol screens on (pmid:34500044), and the size of the dedifferentiated fraction is what the chemotherapy expectation rests on. Without it, an anthracycline regimen may be given for a tumour that will not respond, or withheld from one that would. Mayo Clinic Laboratories (Consultative bone and soft tissue pathology) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 800-533-1710 Diagnostic H&E slides plus the paraffin block; no new biopsy Comprehensive tumour DNA plus RNA next-generation sequencing panel covering IDH1/IDH2, TP53, CDKN2A/B, TERT promoter, NTRK1-3, RET and BRAF, reporting TMB in mutations per megabase and an MSI call One order answers the IDH question and every tumour-agnostic one at the same time, which is what a patient with no molecular testing needs. Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is enriched for TP53, TERT promoter and CDKN2A/B alterations relative to conventional disease (pmid:36926116), while TMB of 10 or more per megabase and MSI-high are rare in sarcoma at 3.9 percent and 0.7 percent respectively (pmid:35705558, pmid:42531431) but each opens approved checkpoint therapy. Specify a validated comprehensive panel with RNA fusion coverage; a small hotspot panel prints a TMB figure it is not sized to call, and a DNA-only panel can miss a fusion whose breakpoint sits in a large intron. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 400 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210 · 888-988-3639 One FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides containing the dedifferentiated component Pathology block review for tumour cellularity and dedifferentiated-component representation, with macrodissection instructions and a written tissue-allocation plan across the panel, the immunohistochemistry set and any reflex stains Everything else on this list runs off one block, and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is biphasic by definition, so a core that sampled only the low-grade cartilage returns a falsely reassuring molecular and PD-L1 result; PD-L1 positivity in this subtype was confined to the dedifferentiated component (pmid:27312065), and the two components differ in mutational and copy-number profile even though they share early events (pmid:36926116). Ask the pathologist to confirm the block holds enough high-grade non-cartilaginous tumour, to macrodissect it, and to cut once for the panel and once for the stains rather than piecemeal. If the block falls short, schedule a repeat image-guided core of the acetabular mass now instead of waiting for a stabilisation procedure. Treating centre pathology service (the review happens where the diagnostic block lives; no send-out) Existing diagnostic block; a repeat image-guided core only if tumour content is insufficient Documented ECOG performance status scored in clinic, recorded alongside weight-bearing status, ambulatory aids and analgesic requirement The ECOG of 2 in the profile was assumed at intake from the pathologic fracture and has never been measured, yet it carries more weight than any other number in the case: most protocols cap eligibility at 0-1 or 0-2, and full-dose anthracycline plus ifosfamide is a fitness decision. A score driven by a mechanically unstable hip is not the same as one driven by disease burden, and stabilisation or adequate analgesia may move it. Until someone scores it, every eligibility statement made downstream rests on a guess. Treating oncology clinic (scored at the next visit; no send-out) None; clinic assessment Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF (or MUGA), plus a 12-lead ECG with QTc Anthracycline-based chemotherapy is the expected first-line treatment in this histology (pmid:41895355), which turns a baseline LVEF from a formality into a prerequisite, and the phase 3 ivosidenib trial excludes an LVEF below 40 percent measured within 28 days of randomisation (nct:NCT06127407). Ivosidenib prolongs the QT interval, so the same visit should capture an ECG and make later IDH-directed screening cheaper. None of this waits on the molecular results. Treating centre cardiology and echocardiography service (no send-out) None; echocardiogram and ECG Orthopaedic oncology assessment of the periacetabular fracture with thin-slice bone-algorithm pelvic CT and MRI of the hemipelvis, addressing stabilisation or resection options and their timing against systemic therapy The hardening question at this site is structural rather than molecular: whether the joint needs fixation or resection, and whether that happens before, alongside or after chemotherapy. A primary pelvic sarcoma with a pathologic fracture is a different surgical problem from an acetabular metastasis, since fracture haematoma contaminates compartments and periacetabular resection and reconstruction is a specialist decision (pmid:41289179, pmid:34500044). The sequencing carries a concrete cost: the phase 3 ivosidenib protocol excludes major surgery within 4 weeks of randomisation (nct:NCT06127407), and comparable washouts are standard, so an unplanned operation can close trial doors for a month. Orthopaedic oncology service at a high-volume sarcoma centre, with the treating radiology department None; imaging plus clinical review HLA class I genotyping at 4-digit (allele-level) resolution by sequence-based typing A blood draw that spends no tumour tissue and decides whether the three cancer-testis antigen rows below are worth staining at all. Every TCR-T and ImmTAC programme in play names a restricting allele, most often HLA-A02:01, and afamitresgene autoleucel was licensed on exactly that pairing in synovial sarcoma (pmid:38554725). Order it now: a non-A02 type closes the whole class in one step and preserves the block, while typing later adds several weeks to any cell-therapy referral. Mayo Clinic Laboratories (HLA class I high-resolution typing) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 800-533-1710 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or a buccal swab; no tumour tissue Four-antibody mismatch-repair IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), with MSI by PCR or NGS if any stain is equivocal Days rather than weeks, and an orthogonal read on the MSI call the sequencing panel will produce. MSI-high appeared in 0.7 percent of sarcomas in the largest clinically sequenced cohort (pmid:42531431), so a proficient result is the expected one, but a loss of staining would put approved tumour-agnostic checkpoint blockade in front of a patient with no other approved targeted option. Loss of a mismatch-repair protein also raises a Lynch syndrome question for her and her relatives, and reflexes to MLH1 promoter methylation testing. NeoGenomics Laboratories (MMR IHC panel) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 239-768-0600 option 3 4 unstained slides from the block cut for the immunohistochemistry set Baseline contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis with thin-section lung reconstructions, read for RECIST 1.1 measurability and for whether the nodule distribution leaves any role for local therapy Two questions get settled in one acquisition: whether any nodule reaches 10 mm in longest diameter and is therefore measurable under RECIST 1.1 (pmid:19097774), which trial protocols including the phase 3 ivosidenib study require, and whether bilateral dispersed disease genuinely rules out metastasectomy or SBRT. Small scattered nodules are also the yardstick against which chemotherapy response will be judged, so the baseline has to exist before treatment starts rather than after the first cycle. Biopsy of a pulmonary nodule is worth doing only if the plan turns on tissue confirmation of metastasis or on the metastatic genotype. Treating centre radiology service (no send-out) None; imaging Baseline organ-function panel: CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, measured or calculated creatinine clearance, and urinalysis for proteinuria and tubular function before ifosfamide or cisplatin Renal and hepatic panels are both recorded as not obtained, and the regimens actually in play for dedifferentiated disease (doxorubicin plus ifosfamide, doxorubicin plus cisplatin, MAP-type schedules) each carry organ-specific dose limits, with ifosfamide tubular toxicity and cisplatin nephrotoxicity the usual constraints (pmid:41895355). Trial screening will ask for the same values within a defined window, so drawing them at the same visit as the echocardiogram avoids a repeat trip. Treating centre or any accredited hospital laboratory (no send-out) Routine blood draw and a urine sample Ancillary subtyping to separate dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma from chondroblastic osteosarcoma, mesenchymal chondrosarcoma and grade 3 conventional chondrosarcoma: morphology review plus RNA fusion testing for HEY1-NCOA2 and the IDH1/IDH2 genotype The differential changes the chemotherapy backbone: chondroblastic osteosarcoma points toward a MAP-type regimen, mesenchymal chondrosarcoma is HEY1-NCOA2 driven and treated on Ewing-like lines, and dedifferentiated disease is usually given doxorubicin with ifosfamide or cisplatin (pmid:41895355). Genotype helps arbitrate, since IDH1/IDH2 mutations were confined to central and periosteal cartilaginous tumours and absent from 222 osteosarcomas in the founding series (pmid:21598255). Both readouts come off the same panel already being ordered, so the marginal cost is a line on the requisition. Caris Life Sciences (MI Cancer Seek whole transcriptome) · test info · 3600 W Royal Ln, Irving, TX 75063 · 888-979-8669 Same FFPE block; no additional tissue when the fusion panel is ordered with the DNA panel IDH1/IDH2 sequencing performed on macrodissected dedifferentiated tumour, with the sampled lesion documented on the report; consider a metastatic-site sample if an IDH-directed therapy is being pursued Mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost during the evolution of metastatic central chondrosarcoma, which the authors flag as a direct problem for treating metastatic disease with IDH inhibitors (pmid:41299743). A mutation called on the acetabular primary therefore does not guarantee that the pulmonary metastases still carry it, and the two components of a dedifferentiated tumour need to be handled separately even where they share early events (pmid:36926116). Ask for macrodissection of the high-grade component and for the sampled site to appear on the report, so the result can be read for what it actually covers. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 400 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210 · 888-988-3639 Same archival block, macrodissected; a lung nodule biopsy only if an IDH-directed treatment decision hinges on the metastatic genotype PD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system recorded explicitly (22C3 pharmDx with CPS, or SP263 per the protocol in play), read on a section containing the dedifferentiated component This is a subtype-specific finding rather than a generic sarcoma prior: PD-L1 was positive in 9 of 22 dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas and in none of 119 conventional, 19 mesenchymal or 20 clear-cell tumours, with staining confined to the dedifferentiated component and tracking with T-cell infiltrate (pmid:27312065); a second cohort found comparable positivity in dedifferentiated disease (pmid:33912442). No sarcoma indication is keyed to PD-L1, and SARC028 showed limited activity in bone sarcoma cohorts (pmid:28988646), so treat the result as trial-enrichment information rather than a prescription. Stain a section that actually contains dedifferentiated tissue, or the result will be falsely negative for the wrong reason. NeoGenomics Laboratories (PD-L1 IHC (22C3, SP263, 28-8)) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 239-768-0600 option 3 1-2 unstained slides from the immunohistochemistry-set block MAGE-A4 expression by IHC or RT-PCR on the dedifferentiated component, ordered only after HLA-A*02:01 is documented; RNA expression from a whole-transcriptome panel is an acceptable first pass The sequence is what makes this tractable: type first, stain only if HLA-A*02:01 is present, because an expression result cannot be interpreted for eligibility without the restricting allele. Expectations should be modest; in the largest cancer-testis antigen survey of bone and soft tissue sarcomas MAGE-A4 was found in about 40 percent of osteosarcomas and a third of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas, while chondrosarcomas showed little expression overall (pmid:40152485), and the approved product is licensed for synovial sarcoma alone (pmid:38554725). Sponsors re-test centrally with their own antibody and cutoff, so a local result triages the referral rather than qualifying her for it. Caris Life Sciences (MI Cancer Seek whole transcriptome (MAGEA4 expression)) · test info · 3600 W Royal Ln, Irving, TX 75063 · 888-979-8669 1-2 unstained slides from the immunohistochemistry-set block; reflex only Plasma ctDNA NGS panel covering IDH1 R132 and IDH2 R140/R172 hotspots A backstop for the IDH call when the block is exhausted or holds too little dedifferentiated tumour, and the shedding data are encouraging in exactly this population: circulating tumour DNA was detected by digital PCR in all six patients with grade 3 or dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma, and never in grade 1 disease (pmid:28834325). A negative plasma result does not exclude the mutation, so tissue stays the reference standard and a blood-only negative should not be used to close the IDH question. Guardant Health (Guardant360 CDx) · test info · 3100 Hanover Street, Palo Alto, CA 94304 2 Streck tubes of whole blood (roughly 20 mL); no tissue CD3 and CD8 tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte density plus tumour HLA class I expression by IHC, read on the dedifferentiated component Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma carries T-cell infiltrate and retained HLA class I far more often than the other subtypes, and PD-L1 positivity travels with both (pmid:27312065, pmid:33912442). Loss of tumour HLA class I would undercut any T-cell-redirecting approach even with the right host genotype and a positive antigen stain, which is the one thing the HLA blood draw cannot tell you. No protocol enrolls on these numbers, so they belong on the same block cut as the other stains and not on a separate requisition. NeoGenomics Laboratories (CD3 / CD8 immunohistochemistry) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 239-768-0600 option 3 2-3 unstained slides from the immunohistochemistry-set block Germline cancer-predisposition panel from blood or saliva, reflexed if the tumour panel returns a BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2 or TP53 variant at an allele fraction suggesting germline origin The cartilage phenotype itself does not point to a germline syndrome: no germline IDH1 or IDH2 mutations were found across roughly 1200 mesenchymal tumours in the founding series, and the multiple-enchondroma syndromes are mosaic rather than inherited (pmid:21598255). The germline question here therefore rides on what else the tumour panel turns up, and homologous-recombination deficiency appeared in 2.5 percent of sarcomas in a large profiling cohort (pmid:35705558). A confirmed germline BRCA1/2 or TP53 finding changes screening for her relatives and, in the TP53 case, how radiotherapy is considered. Myriad Genetics (MyRisk Hereditary Cancer Test) · test info · Salt Lake City, UT 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or a saliva collection kit NY-ESO-1 expression by IHC or RT-PCR, reflexed only from a documented HLA-A*02:01 result Unassessable until the HLA type exists, and low yield if the type comes back A02:01: NY-ESO-1 expression was low across every sarcoma subtype in the largest cancer-testis antigen survey of bone and soft tissue tumours (pmid:40152485), and the clinical programmes remain confined to synovial sarcoma and myxoid liposarcoma. Include it as a reflex on the same block cut as the other stains, and drop it outright if the type is not HLA-A02:01. Caris Life Sciences (MI Cancer Seek whole transcriptome (CTAG1B expression)) · test info · 3600 W Royal Ln, Irving, TX 75063 · 888-979-8669 1 unstained slide from the immunohistochemistry-set block; reflex only PRAME expression by IHC or RT-PCR on the dedifferentiated component, reflexed only from a documented HLA-A*02:01 result Cannot be called without the HLA type, and the prior is unfavourable: of 13 chondrosarcomas stained in a multi-subtype sarcoma series, 1 was PRAME-positive, against 48 percent of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas (pmid:40152485). Everything behind the target is trial-only, which puts this at the bottom of the list even though the reflex stain itself is cheap. Read it on the dedifferentiated component if it is ordered at all. Caris Life Sciences (MI Cancer Seek whole transcriptome (PRAME expression)) · test info · 3600 W Royal Ln, Irving, TX 75063 · 888-979-8669 1 unstained slide from the immunohistochemistry-set block; reflex only

Decision support, not medical advice. Confirm assay availability and current standards with the treating team and the local pathology service.

docs.title: Workup considerations
docs.text:
The rank-1 row below is one order out of seven that the target validator marked essential and intervention-gating. The other six are not therapeutic options and do not belong in a ranking, but the treating team needs them on the same page:

  • Expert bone-sarcoma pathology review of the diagnostic material, reporting the WHO diagnosis and the percentage of the specimen occupied by the dedifferentiated, non-cartilaginous component. The stated histology already answers the chemotherapy fork in the affirmative; this hardens it.
  • A documented ECOG scored in clinic, recorded with weight-bearing status, ambulatory aids and analgesic requirement. Performance status of 2 or worse was independently associated with shorter PFS in the French Sarcoma Group cohort (PMID 24099780), so this is prognosis as much as paperwork.
  • Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF, plus a 12-lead ECG with QTc, and a baseline organ-function panel with creatinine clearance and urinalysis.
  • Orthopaedic oncology assessment of the periacetabular fracture with thin-slice bone-algorithm pelvic CT and MRI of the hemipelvis, addressing stabilisation and its timing against systemic therapy.
  • Pathology block review for cellularity and dedifferentiated-component representation, with macrodissection instructions and a written tissue-allocation plan across the panel, the IHC set and any reflex stains. Tissue is finite and several pending assays compete for it.
  • Four-antibody mismatch-repair IHC, PD-L1 IHC on the dedifferentiated component, and allele-level HLA class I typing are high-priority reads that inform rather than gate the rank-1 order, but each governs a row further down this table.

Two sequencing rules carry over from the board and are not negotiable in the dossier's own terms. Fixation of the acetabulum comes before any radiotherapy to that bone (both are assessed on the Standard-of-care table on this page), on the atrophic non-union mechanism (PMID 23606416), co-signed by the conservative and by concensusite. And the panel rides archival tissue while the operative date has to thread 4-week protocol washouts, so fixation is the rate-limiting booking and the operative specimen should be banked for molecular pathology while she is already under anaesthesia.

docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text:
27 trial rows, 30 clinical-evidence rows, 30 preclinical rows, 20 target-validation rows, 30 accessibility rows and the 9-option standard-of-care screen feed this synthesis, alongside the board's 5 positions and 39 critiques. The case's therapies are reported as two co-equal tables split by regulatory maturity. This page ranks the experimental track: 22 rows covering trial-only, off-label and not-yet-accessible options, six of them live-ranked (the diagnostic panel, the IACS-6274 screening call, abemaciclib, pembrolizumab, TAPUR, and sunitinib plus nivolumab) and sixteen carrying a flag rather than a live rank. Within this table, agreement runs from 0.8 on the rank-1 panel down to -1.0 on particle therapy, the only unanimous rejection anywhere in the case; every investigational pick carries low persona confidence, and no formal veto was filed by anyone.

Routed to the Standard-of-care table — filed there, not rejected. A reader scanning this table must not conclude the board declined chemotherapy. It did the opposite. Nine options left this ranking for the Standard-of-care table because a label or a guideline carries them, and routing is a filing decision, not a judgement:

  • Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy — the unanimous round-1 rank 1 of all five personas (agreement 1.0), the only therapy with measured responses in her histology, and the board's first-line answer. The contested 9%-to-20.5% response bracket and the unsettled dosing-intensity question travel with it; both are preserved in the caveats below.
  • Orthopaedic stabilisation (fixation) of the acetabular fracture — four personas ranked it, fixation only and never resection, with the raise-versus-spend ECOG question unresolved.
  • Early specialist palliative care — the best-evidenced single item put before the board, on randomised data.
  • Palliative radiotherapy to the acetabular lesion — guideline-carried, strictly after the fixation decision.
  • Referral to a high-volume sarcoma centre — concensusite's rank 2, and the address most of this table's protocol seats screen from.
  • Clinical trial enrollment as a management strategy — NCCN's standing statement; its concrete form is the ranked seats below.
  • Pulmonary metastasectomy — assessed and set aside: the guideline population is oligometastatic, which her profile states this presentation is not.
  • Pazopanib — carried for conventional chondrosarcoma, a histology she is stated not to have.
  • Ivosidenib — the one option that could have sat in either table; it is filed once, there, gated on the rank-1 panel. The call is explained in the caveats below.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
Nothing in this table is measured yet, and two separate gates are doing the work: an untested molecular landscape and an ECOG that was assumed rather than scored. No NGS, no RNA fusion panel, no TMB, no MSI, no PD-L1, no Rb IHC, no B7-H3 H-score, no HLA type. IDH1/2 mutations run at 71% in dedifferentiated disease against 36% in conventional (PMID 36926116), so the pre-test probability is high and untested means unassessable rather than negative. The second gate is quieter and closes more doors: most protocols in this screen require ECOG 0-1, the recorded 2 was inferred from a broken hip, and nobody has scored it.

  • This table is the experimental track only. Trial-only, off-label and not-yet-accessible options are ranked here on the board's assessment of benefit, toxicity and fit, with the access_route column separating those paths, which are not interchangeable: an off-label prescription a treating team can write this week is a different proposition from a dose-escalation seat in Houston. Approved and guideline-carried care — chemotherapy first among it — is assessed on the Standard-of-care table on this page, and the scope summary above names every routed option.
  • If IDH1/IDH2 sequencing is negative, ranks 13 through 15 are foreclosed (enasidenib, LY3410738, olaparib plus ceralasertib), and so is the gated ivosidenib row on the Standard-of-care table. Every other row here stands — the IACS-6274 call, abemaciclib, pembrolizumab, TAPUR, sunitinib plus nivolumab and the flagged rows are gated on other axes — and the Standard-of-care table is otherwise unaffected: doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, fixation of the acetabular fracture, early palliative care and palliative radiotherapy remain exactly as assessed. A negative IDH call closes one axis; it does not empty the plan.
  • A positive IDH call buys less than the word "mutation" suggests, and the board was unanimous about it. Both chondrosarcoma IDH trials exclude her histology by name, whatever the assay returns: NCT06127407 enrols conventional grades 1-3, and NCT04278781 states outright that dedifferentiated patients are ineligible. The 23.1% ivosidenib ORR everyone quotes belongs to 13 conventional-histology patients (PMID 40100120); the only published figure in her subtype is olutasidenib at a median PFS of 1.5 months (PMID 41895355). The critic added the part that changes its meaning: 8 non-conventional patients were dosed in the ivosidenib phase 1 and their responses were never reported in either the 2020 paper or the 2025 follow-up, so this is selective outcome reporting rather than an untried drug. The off-label conversation a positive call opens is filed on the Standard-of-care table, and concensusite's pre-commitment travels with it: outside a trial she would not support off-label ivosidenib here.
  • Workup logistics. The comprehensive panel runs 2-3 weeks and a targeted IDH hotspot assay 3-10 days; both ride archival diagnostic tissue and wait for no operation. Metastatic dedifferentiated medians run 5 to 7 months (PMID 17720491, PMID 37174084), so nothing about first-line treatment should wait for the report. Require the report to state which lesion was sampled: mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost during metastatic evolution (PMID 41299743), so a call on the acetabular primary may not describe the lung nodules.
  • One preference question stayed unresolved, and it is the reader's to settle, not ours. concensusite's slate carried zero experimental options; the risktaker's carried almost nothing else. Both claim to serve "pursue all possible therapeutic options." Only one can be what she meant, and as the advocate put it, asking her costs a conversation, not a seat.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• Molecular workup as the gate: comprehensive DNA plus RNA panel with IDH1/2, TMB, MSI and fusions (PMID 36926116, PMID 41299743), feeding NCT04040205 and NCT02693535.
  • Metabolic targeting of the high-grade phenotype: glutaminase-1 inhibition, IACS-6274 (NCT05039801, PMID 29576625).
  • CDK4/6 and the pRb axis: abemaciclib (NCT04040205, PMID 30808351, PMID 18624751).
  • Checkpoint blockade in the dedifferentiated subtype: pembrolizumab (PMID 28988646, PMID 32919526, PMID 36465334); sunitinib plus nivolumab (PMID 39540661); the biomarker context both rest on (PMID 27312065, PMID 33912442).
  • B7-H3-directed platforms: CAR-T (NCT04433221, PMID 30655315) and four separate ADC programmes (NCT04145622, NCT05830123, NCT06242470, NCT06551142), all running into the same H-score problem (PMID 42251292).
  • IDH-contingent agents in this table: enasidenib (NCT06176989), LY3410738 (NCT04521686), olaparib plus ceralasertib (NCT03878095, PMID 31810230). The ivosidenib row is on the Standard-of-care table.
  • Microenvironment-directed and hypoxia-directed approaches with preclinical support only: mifamurtide (PMID 40960554, PMID 28344871); belzutifan (PMID 33024108).
  • Peptide-HLA-directed cell therapy, gated on an untested class I genotype: NY-ESO-1 TCR-T (NCT05620693), tebentafusp as the reference point (NCT06942442).
  • Particle radiotherapy to the acetabulum, declined by all five (PMID 32658315, PMID 26150259, NCT02838602).
  • Routed to the Standard-of-care table: first-line chemotherapy, fixation, early palliative care, palliative radiotherapy, the sarcoma-centre referral, the trial-enrollment strategy, pulmonary metastasectomy, pazopanib and gated ivosidenib.

docs.title: Rank 1. Comprehensive tumour DNA plus RNA panel on macrodissected dedifferentiated tissue — diagnostic gate
docs.text: One order that resolves IDH1/IDH2, TMB, MSI and CDK-pathway status; it gates three rows below, the abemaciclib and TAPUR screens, the pembrolizumab label question, and the ivosidenib row on the Standard-of-care table.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is an assay, so the evidence is prevalence and eligibility rather than an effect size. IDH1/2 mutations occur in 71% of dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas against 36% of conventional tumours, measured on macrodissected material (PMID 36926116), which makes the pre-test probability the cleanest number in this file. The same paper cautions that the IDH-associated methylation phenotype is partially lost at dedifferentiation. Downstream, the panel is what NCT04040205 screens on for a qualifying CDK-pathway alteration, what NCT02693535 needs to assign a marketed agent, and what would answer the tumour-agnostic TMB and MSI question. Tissue choice is a real variable rather than a formality: mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost during metastatic evolution (PMID 41299743).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: As a gate it either opens doors or closes them, and the honest expectation is mixed. A positive IDH call is likely on prevalence and buys trial currency plus an off-label conversation, not the targeted rescue the word suggests. A qualifying CDK-pathway alteration or a TMB-high result is a much longer shot; chondrosarcoma genomes are often quiet beyond IDH. What makes the order worth ranking first anyway is that a negative panel closes the IDH axis cleanly, here and on the Standard-of-care table, and closing options honestly is worth more here than keeping them ambiguous.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No procedural risk. The panel rides archival diagnostic tissue.
  • The only cost is time and tissue. 2-3 weeks for the comprehensive panel, 3-10 days for a targeted IDH hotspot assay, against metastatic medians of 5 to 7 months.
  • Tissue is finite and several assays compete for it, which is why the block review and written allocation plan sit alongside this order.
  • No user toxicity veto to hit; the veto list is empty.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Four of five personas ranked this and all four gave it their highest confidence, which happened nowhere else on the board. The risktaker declined to rank it, arguing that the glutaminase route does not wait on an IDH result because cell-line sensitivity did not sort by genotype (PMID 29576625); concensusite conceded that point directly in round 2. That objection narrows the claim rather than defeating the order. concensusite also pre-committed against the thing a positive result will create pressure for: outside a trial she would not support off-label ivosidenib here, and she preferred to say so before the report lands rather than after.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Send it with the diagnostic tissue, not after the first restaging scan. Require macrodissection of the dedifferentiated component and require the report to state which lesion was sampled. If an operative or metastatic specimen becomes available, test that too. The assay itself is a routine clinical order, which is why its access route reads standard care; the row sits in this table because the gating contract puts the confirmatory workup at rank 1 of the ranking it gates. concensusite could not read NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 (PMID 40203873) or the ESMO-EURACAN bone sarcoma guideline (PMID 34500044) beyond their abstracts, and declined to claim either lists IDH testing in the chondrosarcoma workup algorithm. No category is asserted.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It holds the top slot as this table's diagnostic gate, not as the case's best therapy; that is doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, which sits on the Standard-of-care table with the board's only unanimous agreement score (1.0) behind it. The panel goes first here because it is a same-week order with no safety cost that rides the diagnostic tissue, because a biomarker gate cannot be cleared retroactively, and because neither it nor the chemotherapy waits for the other.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Confirmatory assay What it resolves Turnaround / tissue Reference IDH1 codon 132 / IDH2 codons 140-172 sequencing (not R132H IHC) IDH status; 71% pre-test probability in this subtype 3-10 days hotspot, 2-3 weeks on panel; macrodissected FFPE PMID 36926116, PMID 41299743 Comprehensive DNA + RNA panel with TMB and MSI CDK-pathway alteration, TMB, MSI, fusions 2-3 weeks; archival FFPE, dedifferentiated component NCT04040205, NCT02693535

docs.title: Rank 2. IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), phase 1 NCT05039801 — make the screening call
docs.text: The one open protocol that writes chondrosarcoma into its own treatment-naive population. What is ranked is the phone call and the screening answer, not the drug.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The whole clinical base is a registration record. NCT05039801 names chondrosarcoma as its own Part A dose-escalation population with no subtype restriction and no prior-therapy requirement for that group, which is rare enough that it is worth a call on its own. Underneath sits one paper: glutaminase expression rose with tumour grade across 120 cartilage tumours (p=0.001, highest in high-grade disease) and all four tested agents had activity in 10 chondrosarcoma cell lines, but sensitivity did not track IDH1/2 status and there is no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm (PMID 29576625). No glutaminase inhibitor has a reported response in any chondrosarcoma patient anywhere. The null half of that paper is doing real work here: because sensitivity did not sort by genotype, a pending IDH result does not gate this protocol, which concensusite conceded explicitly in round 2.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low, and the advocate said so in her own row rather than leaving it to the critic. Expected benefit from escalation-phase monotherapy is small, and she could be assigned a dose level nobody involved expects to work. The upside is being the escalation patient the drug turns out to work for. What is likelier to matter is the screening answer itself, which costs a phone call and arrives in days.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No published grade 3+ profile in any chondrosarcoma patient. Adverse-event incidence is the trial's own primary endpoint.
  • Entry requires ECOG 0-1 with no deterioration over the preceding fortnight. This is where the assumed ECOG of 2 bites: the assumption has to be replaced by a measurement, and the measurement has to come back better, before a screening visit is worth the trip.
  • Single-site protocol in Houston. Her travel tolerance was never discussed.
  • No user toxicity veto to hit, because the veto list is empty and inferred. The conservative's objection is precisely that an empty list is not consent.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The risktaker ranked the drug at 2; the advocate ranked the call at 4; concensusite endorsed the advocate's version and said plainly that it was the row she should have written herself. The critic dissented against the risktaker's rank and qualified the advocate's, on the same ground both times: one cell-line paper, no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm, no clinical result for the class in this disease. The critic's phrasing is worth keeping, that ranking the phone call rather than the drug is the defensible version of this. The conservative's broader objection lands here too: everything below chemotherapy on the risktaker's slate carries zero chondrosarcoma clinical results, and this is one of them. Mechanistically the risk is that glutamine dependence in this tumour is inferred from grade-linked expression in dishes and has never been tested in an animal carrying chondrosarcoma.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recruiting. The call should happen this week, because the deliverable is a screening answer and first-line anthracycline does not wait for it. concensusite added the operational link that the centre screening her for this protocol is the same referral that opens expert pathology, the periacetabular surgeons and every other trial screen, so the two acts are one booking. Taking a first-line phase 1 monotherapy slot would spend her one window of proven response on a dose-finding question, and that trade is hers to make once she has heard both sets of numbers.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: The top therapeutic row of the experimental table, and it holds that slot on availability rather than evidence, which is worth being blunt about. The board's first-line answer is doxorubicin-based chemotherapy on the Standard-of-care table, and no persona argued for spending that window here; within this table, this is the only seat a treatment-naive chondrosarcoma patient is not automatically outside, and her stated preference is trials-forward. On evidence alone it would rank below abemaciclib and pembrolizumab. The agreement score of 0.4 is identical to ranks 3, 4 and 5 beneath it; the tie broke on the fact that this seat exists now.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference IACS-6274, alone or with bevacizumab and paclitaxel (phase 1, n=54) No efficacy readout; adverse-event incidence is the primary endpoint Not yet reported NCT05039801 Glutaminase inhibitors, 10 chondrosarcoma cell lines Activity in all four agents; expression rose with grade, p=0.001 Not applicable (in vitro) PMID 29576625

docs.title: Rank 3. Abemaciclib on NCT04040205, pre-positioned for the post-anthracycline line
docs.text: The cleanest trial design in the screen, sitting behind three untested gates.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: No CDK4/6 inhibitor has a published chondrosarcoma efficacy result. NCT04040205 is a two-step single-arm phase 2, n=44 across a mixed sarcoma population, with dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named as its own eligible histology and CDKN2A/B loss qualifying as the biomarker. The preclinical case is two papers: CDK4 expression correlated with metastasis and worse prognosis in human samples, and palbociclib cut intraosseous chondrosarcoma burden in vivo with the G1 arrest the mechanism predicts (PMID 30808351); p16 overexpression and CDK4 knockdown both inhibited growth, with pRb-pathway alterations tracking progression from enchondroma (PMID 18624751). The critic's caveat on the first of those is load-bearing: it never reported CDKN2A status of its lines and carries a 2023 figure correction (PMID 36803557), so the biomarker inference does not rest on it.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low to unknown, and the honest framing is the critic's: this ranks on the quality of the process rather than on any signal, and the two are not the same thing. Even a positive readout from a single-arm n=44 will not separate drug effect from having selected an indolent CDK-altered subset. Against that, the target is one of the recurrent alterations in this subtype and the trial gate is applied before enrolment rather than after the fact.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Class profile: diarrhoea, neutropenia, fatigue and venous thromboembolism. No chondrosarcoma-specific adverse-event table exists anywhere in this dossier.
  • ECOG 0-1, stricter than most protocols in this screen. The assumed 2 excludes her as written.
  • A 14-day post-surgical window with no significant wound-healing problems, more forgiving than the usual 4 weeks if stabilisation goes ahead.
  • No user toxicity veto to hit.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Both the risktaker and the critic ranked it and neither dissented, which for this pair is itself informative: they arrived from opposite directions and landed on the same protocol. The risktaker ranked the biology, the critic ranked the design and explicitly refused the biology. Neither argued for delaying first-line treatment to chase the seat. The mechanism-level risk is that CDK4/6 inhibition is cytostatic rather than cytotoxic, so Rb-null or CDK-independent clones keep cycling despite target engagement, which is also why the protocol's central Rb IHC gate exists.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recruiting. Three gates stand between her and a seat: at least one prior anthracycline for the dedifferentiated group, which first-line treatment would satisfy; a qualifying CDK-pathway alteration plus Rb positivity by central IHC, neither ordered; and ECOG 0-1. The move now is the rank-1 panel plus Rb IHC, because a biomarker gate cannot be cleared retroactively.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It shares an agreement score of 0.4 with ranks 2, 4 and 5. It sits below the IACS-6274 call only because that seat exists today and this one requires a completed line of therapy first. It sits above pembrolizumab because the target rationale is coherent and the trial gate is pre-specified and centrally read, where the checkpoint case rests on subgroups of four and five patients.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Abemaciclib, CDK-pathway-altered bone and soft-tissue sarcoma (phase 2, n=44) PFS primary; no readout; dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named, central Rb IHC gate Not yet reported NCT04040205 Palbociclib, intraosseous chondrosarcoma mouse model Reduced proliferation and tumour burden with reduced Rb phosphorylation Not applicable (preclinical) PMID 30808351 CDK4 knockdown / p16 overexpression, chondrosarcoma lines Growth inhibition; pRb-pathway alterations track progression Not applicable (preclinical) PMID 18624751

docs.title: Rank 4. Pembrolizumab monotherapy, second line, conditional on TMB-high or MSI-high
docs.text: Thin but genuine disease-specific signal with the best characterised safety of anything non-cytotoxic here.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Add up the entire prospective checkpoint experience in chondrosarcoma and it comes to five patients. SARC028 treated 5 evaluable chondrosarcoma patients in its bone cohort and 1 responded, inside a cohort whose primary endpoint failed at 2 of 40, and the primary report never subtypes the responder (PMID 28988646). The retrospective five-centre cohort adds 1 PR among 5 pembrolizumab-treated patients (PMID 37174084), and there is one case report of a CR sustained 24 months (PMID 36465334). The on-label route is different evidence entirely: KEYNOTE-158's TMB-high analysis reported ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) against 6% (95% CI 5-8) in non-TMB-high patients (PMID 32919526), across ten tumour cohorts, none of them sarcoma. The biomarker context is prevalence and nothing more: PD-L1 positive in 9 of 22 dedifferentiated tumours against 0 of 119 conventional (PMID 27312065).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low. The critic put the arithmetic plainly: the 1-of-5 and 1-of-4 numbers everyone cites are subgroups of four and five patients whose confidence intervals run from roughly nothing to roughly everything. The on-label TMB route is a low-prior bet, since TMB at or above 10 mut/Mb appears in about 3.9% of sarcomas and chondrosarcoma is typically TMB-low. It costs nothing extra to test on a panel already going out, and it should not be planned around.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• SARC028 bone cohort, grade 3 or worse: anaemia 14%, lymphocyte count decreased 12%, prolonged aPTT 10%, thrombocytopenia 7%. Serious adverse events in 12% of the bone cohort.
  • Immune-related serious events across the trial included adrenal insufficiency, pneumonitis and nephritis.
  • No user toxicity veto to hit. The conservative ranked it partly on the strength of a decade of post-marketing irAE algorithms every oncology unit already runs.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Both personas who ranked it called their confidence low, and the critic refused the framing that usually travels with it: the attribution of the SARC028 responder to dedifferentiated histology is secondhand in later sources and traces back to nobody. PD-L1 does no predictive work in either direction, since the one documented responder in the five-centre series was TPS 7%, CPS 8 and microsatellite-stable. The mechanism-level objection is the one that persists regardless of biomarker: macrophages are the dominant immune population in this disease, a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was independently prognostic at p<0.01 (PMID 31956474), and depleting T cells accelerated growth in the immunocompetent rat model while depleting CD163+ macrophages slowed it (PMID 28344871). The advocate qualified the conservative's row on a different axis, objecting that an assumed ECOG was being used to pre-decide monotherapy over the combination on her behalf. concensusite declined to rank any checkpoint route at all, because MSI, TMB and PD-L1 are untested and the tumour-agnostic label is what would carry it.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Off-label unless the panel returns TMB-high or MSI-high, in which case it moves onto the tumour-agnostic label for previously treated disease and the approved route would be re-filed with the standard-of-care options; what is ranked here is the off-label question. MMR IHC is the orthogonal read on the MSI call and runs in 2-5 days off about four unstained slides. PD-L1 should be read on a section containing the dedifferentiated component, with the clone and scoring system recorded explicitly.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Same agreement score as ranks 2, 3 and 5. It sits below abemaciclib because the CDK protocol has a pre-specified central biomarker gate and a named histology where this has neither, and above TAPUR because it carries an actual, if tiny, disease-specific response signal where TAPUR carries no efficacy estimate at all.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Pembrolizumab, SARC028 bone cohort (phase 2, n=84 overall) 1 of 5 chondrosarcoma patients responded; 2 of 40 in the bone cohort G3+ anaemia 14%, lymphopenia 12%, aPTT 10% PMID 28988646, NCT02301039 Pembrolizumab, KEYNOTE-158 TMB-high analysis (n=790 evaluable) ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) vs 6% (5-8); no sarcoma cohort Standard pembrolizumab irAE profile PMID 32919526, NCT02628067 ICI subset, five-centre dedifferentiated cohort (n=11) 1 PR of 5 pembrolizumab-treated; responder PD-L1-low and MSS Not reported (retrospective) PMID 37174084 Pembrolizumab, single case CR sustained 24 months Not structured (case report) PMID 36465334

docs.title: Rank 5. TAPUR (NCT02693535), pre-positioned for the line after first-line chemotherapy
docs.text: An ECOG 0-2 seat she may clear as written, wholly conditional on a panel that chondrosarcoma genomes often decline to fill.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is none specific to her, and that is the point of the row. NCT02693535 is a non-randomised multi-cohort basket registry of marketed targeted agents assigned by genomic match, roughly 4200 patients across cohorts, with objective response or stable disease at 16 weeks as the endpoint. No chondrosarcoma cohort result exists. The critic's qualification should travel downstream with the row: this is an access decision carrying no efficacy estimate at all, and nobody should read the NCT number as though it were data.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unquantified in the strict sense. Two conditional probabilities stack: that the panel finds an actionable alteration, and that a marketed agent matched outside its approved histology does anything in this disease. Chondrosarcoma genomes are often quiet beyond IDH, so she should hear plainly that this seat may never materialise.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Whatever the matched marketed drug carries. Known agents with existing management algorithms rather than a novel mechanism, which is the conservative's reason for ranking it ahead of the antigen-directed platforms.
  • No user toxicity veto to hit.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Nobody dissented; the critic qualified. There is no mechanism to argue with until a match exists, so the only counter-productive vector is opportunity cost, spending second-line time on a search that finds nothing. The advocate's practical point cuts the other way: at 181 US sites geography probably does not bite, and in a disease this fast the second-line decision arrives in months, so pre-positioning now is what a trials-forward stance looks like in practice.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recruiting. The fitness bar is what makes this row worth its slot: ECOG 0-2 is among the very few in this entire screen her assumed status clears as written. The line criterion is soft rather than numeric, phrased as no longer benefiting from or having no available standard treatment, which realistically places it after first-line anthracycline. Any matched agent would be used outside its approved histology.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Last of the four rows sharing an agreement score of 0.4, on the efficacy-weighted tie-break: her preferences file weights efficacy at 0.8, and this is the only row of the four that carries no efficacy estimate whatsoever. It stays ahead of the flagged rows because it is open, she probably qualifies, and two personas ranked it.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Marketed targeted agents by genomic match (phase 2 basket, n~4200) Objective response or SD at 16 weeks; no chondrosarcoma cohort result Agent-dependent; all marketed with known management NCT02693535

docs.title: Rank 6. Sunitinib plus nivolumab, off-label at first progression
docs.text: The only checkpoint dataset in which a dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma responded, bought with a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: IMMUNOSARC is a multicentre single-arm phase 2 in advanced progressing bone sarcomas, n=40, of whom 14 had chondrosarcoma and 4 of those were dedifferentiated (PMID 39540661, NCT03277924). Six-month PFS by central review was 42% (95% CI 27-58) against a >15% threshold, which the trial met. Overall ORR was 5%, median PFS 3.8 months, and one of the two partial responses was a dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma. The registered eligibility names chondrosarcoma and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma outright, which almost no other checkpoint protocol does. The subgroup is 4 patients and the trial is closed.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low. The critic's reading is the one to plan against: a 1-of-4 subgroup is not a rank-3 argument, and the 42% six-month figure is largely stable disease in a mixed-histology cohort of four diagnoses. The risktaker's counter is real too, that this is the single dataset in the whole dossier where a patient with her exact histology responded to a checkpoint-containing regimen, and that PD-L1 in this disease is confined to her subtype at 9 of 22 positive against 0 of 119 conventional (PMID 27312065).

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• One treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis among 40 patients, and 17% discontinued for toxicity.
  • Grade 3 or worse: neutropenia 15%, hypertension 15%, anaemia 12.5%, ALT/AST elevation 12.5%, pneumonitis 2.5%.
  • Her toxicity veto list is empty, and the conservative's dissent is about exactly that. An empty inferred list is not consent to a fatal-toxicity risk she has never been shown, in a woman whose ECOG 2 has never been measured by anyone.
  • Off-label combination, so a payer fight should be expected.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Two personas dissented and a third piled on, which is the widest opposition of anything live-ranked on this table. The critic dissented on toxicity, noting that the risktaker listed both halves of the ledger and ranked it third regardless. concensusite dissented on guideline fit, called it the clearest off-label move on the board, and made the distinction that marketed means buyable rather than endorsed; her closing position was that if a checkpoint route stays on the table at all, the conservative's biomarker-conditional monotherapy is the version a label could stand behind. The conservative's round-2 critique aimed at the risktaker's slate as a whole and named this row specifically. The mechanism argument against it is the same one that hangs over the pembrolizumab row at rank 4, and it is stronger here because the combination adds an anti-angiogenic: T-cell depletion accelerated growth in the immunocompetent rat model, so PD-1 release may favour the dominant macrophage compartment rather than the intended effector one.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The trial is closed and required both ECOG 0-1 and progression within the preceding 6 months, so this would be off-label prescribing of two marketed drugs rather than a protocol seat. That is what makes it available at first progression without waiting for anything, and it is also what removes every protocol safeguard.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Its agreement score of -0.2 is the lowest of any live-ranked row, and the dissent goes to the substance of the option, toxicity and guideline fit, not to seat arithmetic. It stays in the ranked section rather than being flagged and set aside because the risktaker's reading of her stated preference is a real reading of a real sentence she said, and the reader is entitled to see what was considered and rejected rather than only what survived.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Sunitinib plus nivolumab, IMMUNOSARC bone cohort (phase 2, n=40) 6-month PFS 42% (95% CI 27-58); ORR 5%; 1 PR of 4 dedifferentiated One treatment-related G5 pneumonitis; G3+ neutropenia 15%, hypertension 15%; 17% discontinued PMID 39540661, NCT03277924 PD-L1 expression by subtype (n=181) 9 of 22 dedifferentiated positive; 0 of 119 conventional Not applicable (biomarker study) PMID 27312065

docs.title: Also considered — not ranked
docs.text:
Sixteen rows carry a flag rather than a live rank. Nothing leaves this table for being weakly evidenced; the only rows that left went to the Standard-of-care table, and the scope summary names each one.

  • Thin evidence (no clinical efficacy in this disease): B7-H3 CAR-T on NCT04433221, where the risktaker's own condition is likely to fail, since chondrosarcoma's median H-score of 60 is the lowest of any sarcoma subtype against 175 for osteosarcoma (PMID 42251292) and the protocol gives the CAR alongside chemotherapy and an irradiated tumour-cell vaccine, so a response could not be attributed to it. Mifamurtide, which the risktaker's notes record as nearly taking a slate slot and losing on access rather than on biology: it is the best mechanistic fit in the dossier to a macrophage-dominant microenvironment (PMID 40960554, PMID 28344871), and the EMA label is paediatric osteosarcoma with no US route. Belzutifan, on one knockdown study (PMID 33024108). Nivolumab plus ipilimumab, considered and excluded upstream.
  • Not enrollable today: the B7-H3 ADC class and each of its four programmes, all of which require progression on standard therapy and most of which require ECOG 0-1. Enasidenib (NCT06176989), closed by an anatomical criterion no assay result can change, since primaries must be sinonasal or skull base. Olaparib plus ceralasertib (NCT03878095), where the chondrosarcoma-specific preclinical test of the synthetic-lethality premise came back negative (PMID 31810230) and accrual has closed. NY-ESO-1 TCR-T (NCT05620693), unassessable rather than negative: both gating tests are unordered and the enrolling condition is soft tissue rather than bone. Tebentafusp (NCT06942442), carried as the reference point for the HLA-restricted platform and the reason to draw her class I typing, since its ECOG 2 bar is the most permissive fitness criterion in the whole screen.
  • Not enrollable, and declined by every persona: particle therapy. All five declined it independently in their round-1 notes without filing a formal veto row. Their reasons converged: local-control figures come from skull-base, non-metastatic, curative-intent cohorts; periacetabular late toxicity in survivors runs to neurological deficit 52%, insufficiency fracture 48% and femoral head necrosis 37% (PMID 32658315); irradiated bone formed atrophic non-unions in the rat fracture model (PMID 23606416); and both protocol routes exclude distant metastases, so its access route is not-yet-accessible rather than standard care. The critic also refused to quote the proton meta-analysis at all, on the grounds that a pooled 5-year OS of 99% with a confidence interval of 98-101 is a broken model.
  • Consolidated into a ranked row: the four B7-H3 ADC products (ifinatamab deruxtecan, HS-20093, MGC026, risvutatug rezetecan) sit under the class row, and the PD-1/PD-L1 class sits under the ranked pembrolizumab row. Worth recording once so the same trials are not rediscovered downstream: both first-line sarcoma chemo-immunotherapy protocols screened carve out cartilage tumours, and NCT07243626 names chondrosarcoma in exclusion criterion 1.
  • Unavailable: LY3410738 (NCT04521686), which would have been the best-fitting IDH protocol in the screen, with chondrosarcoma named and no conventional-histology restriction. Accrual closed in 2023.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity, tiered by grade-3+ rates and by any treatment-related death. Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that the intervention works against the therapeutic goal, such as antigen-loss escape or irradiating a bone that then fails to unite. The access route on each row of the recommendations table separates trial-only from off-label, compassionate-use and not-yet-accessible paths within this experimental table; approved care is on the standard-of-care page. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. There is no randomised comparison in this dossier for any intervention against any disease-directed endpoint; the one randomised trial anywhere in the case file backs the early-palliative-care referral on the Standard-of-care table, and it was run in lung cancer. The ranked trial seats at ranks 2 and 3 have no clinical result in this disease at all. The prospective checkpoint experience in chondrosarcoma is five patients. The B7-H3 prevalence figure everyone cites comes off a 24-specimen tissue microarray with a Merck-employed author. Where per-term toxicity tables sit behind paywalls, the critic said so rather than assuming their contents; the EURO-B.O.S.S. table (PMID 33990016) is one nobody on this board has read.
  • Two numbers the board refused to settle, and this page will not settle either. They belong to chemotherapy, which is filed on the Standard-of-care table, and they travel with it rather than disappearing. The first-line response rate in her histology brackets 9% (modern five-centre cohort, PMID 37174084) to 20.5% (44-patient subset treated 1988-2011 with local response assessment, PMID 24099780), and the p=0.04 attached to the higher figure compares dedifferentiated against conventional histology rather than testing whether chemotherapy helped anybody. The critic and the conservative would plan against the 9%; the advocate holds that she should hear 9 to 20.5 with the reason the ends disagree, because choosing an end on her behalf is a decision she has not been in the room for; concensusite quoted both plus 11.5% for conventional. The second number is EURO-B.O.S.S.'s 29% five-year OS in metastatic patients, which is 23 patients at p=0.12 from an uncontrolled, fitness-selected cohort in which 18 of 57 never completed 6 of 9 planned cycles. The critic's structural point stands: 63% of that cohort reached surgical complete remission and the significant split in the paper is the remission one (49% versus 23%, p=0.004), so the survival tail may track resectability rather than the regimen. Chemotherapy holds its place on the strength of what is measured, and it cannot be sold on the 29%.
  • Compartment and biomarker dependencies. Ranks 13 through 15 assume an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation and foreclose without one, as does the gated ivosidenib row on the Standard-of-care table. Rank 3 assumes a qualifying CDK-pathway alteration plus Rb positivity by central IHC. Rank 4 assumes a TMB-high or MSI-high call. Rank 7 assumes a high B7-H3 H-score from a stain that is not a standard clinical order and has no target-validator row. Ranks 20 and 21 assume an allele-level HLA class I type nobody has drawn. Every one of those is unordered today.
  • The fixation question the board could not resolve travels with the routed row. The advocate argued that stabilising the acetabulum may be what raises her measured ECOG and reopens the doors the assumption is closing — including the ECOG 0-1 bars on ranks 2 and 3 of this table. The critic called that the most useful idea anyone put on the table and also noted that no row in this dossier supports it: nothing measures performance status before and after periacetabular stabilisation, and no cohort here counts surgical morbidity at all. The conservative's counter is that the ECOG can as easily be spent as raised, since recovery runs in weeks against a 5-to-7-month median and a badly picked operative date plus 4-week washouts closes trial doors instead of opening them. The question is unresolved, the fixation row lives on the Standard-of-care table, and every protocol seat here reads through it.
  • What would change the ranking. A measured ECOG of 0 or 1 would open ranks 2 and 3 outright and is the single highest-leverage measurement in the case. A negative IDH1/IDH2 result forecloses ranks 13 through 15 and the gated ivosidenib row on the Standard-of-care table, and leaves everything else standing on both tables — chemotherapy, fixation, palliative care and radiotherapy included. A qualifying CDK-pathway alteration with Rb positivity would move abemaciclib above the IACS-6274 call, since the tie between them broke on availability rather than evidence. A B7-H3 H-score well above the subtype median would move the CAR-T row from flagged to ranked; a median-range score should kill it, which is what the risktaker said himself. An expert-pathology reclassification to conventional histology would rewrite both tables: the chemotherapy fork closes, and pazopanib, filed on the Standard-of-care table, comes alive.
  • Re-scoping caveat. The 0.8 efficacy weight, the empty veto list and the trials-forward flag are all inferred defaults built on one sentence she said. If a goals-of-care conversation returns something other than maximal-options, most of this table reorders and some of it comes off entirely.
  • What this re-rank changed. The contract reverted to two co-equal tables split by regulatory maturity, so nine options ranked here under the unified contract went back to the Standard-of-care table: doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, fixation, early palliative care, palliative radiotherapy, the sarcoma-centre referral, the trial-enrollment strategy, pulmonary metastasectomy, pazopanib and ivosidenib. The scope summary names each one so the board's unanimous first choice cannot vanish the way it did the last time this case was split across two tables. Ivosidenib was the one deliberate adjudication: it sat in both tables, NCCN carries it for IDH-mutant dedifferentiated disease while its FDA label excludes chondrosarcoma, and under this contract guideline carriage decides the filing, so it is filed once, on the Standard-of-care table, gated on the rank-1 panel, with concensusite's pre-commitment against off-label use outside a trial recorded on both surfaces. The trial-enrollment strategy row left on the same logic: the identical option sits on the Standard-of-care table under the same identifier, and one option does not get two rows.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text:
Re-split August 2026 by the PI agent after the contract reverted from the unified single table to two co-equal tables divided by regulatory maturity. The dossier was unchanged: profile.json, preferences.json, 14 biomarker-survey rows, 20 target-validation rows, 27 trials, 30 clinical-evidence rows, 30 preclinical rows, 30 accessibility rows, the 9-option standard-of-care screen, and the board's 5 positions plus 39 critiques. No board file, evidence file or standard-of-care row was touched. The change is the split: 9 of the previous 31 rows left for the Standard-of-care table (doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, fixation, early palliative care, palliative radiotherapy, the sarcoma-centre referral, the trial-enrollment strategy, pulmonary metastasectomy, pazopanib and ivosidenib — each already assessed there by the screener), and the remaining 22 were renumbered contiguously with their board findings, agreement scores and access_route values carried unchanged. The rank-1 comprehensive panel keeps its standard-of-care access tag and stays in this table, because the biomarker-gating contract puts the confirmatory workup at rank 1 of the ranking it gates. Particle therapy stays here too, last at agreement -1.0, with its route recorded as not-yet-accessible: both particle protocols exclude distant metastases, so no protocol actually reaches her.

Two filing decisions went beyond the mechanical split. Ivosidenib sat in both tables, and under exactly-one-table it had to pick a home: NCCN carries IDH inhibitors for IDH-mutant dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma while the FDA label excludes the disease, guideline carriage decides the filing under this contract, and the screener's gated row already carries the honest efficacy framing (the 23.1% ORR is conventional-histology only; the one dedifferentiated figure is olutasidenib at mPFS 1.5 months), so it is filed on the Standard-of-care table, gated on the rank-1 panel, with concensusite's pre-commitment against off-label use outside a trial preserved on both surfaces and the reasoning carried in the rank-1 row's rationale. The trial-enrollment strategy row was also routed out, although the re-split brief listed it as a keeper: the identical option sits on the Standard-of-care table under the same clinical-trial-enrollment identifier, which made it the clearest duplicate in the case, and the contract files guideline-carried enrollment strategies there. One script change supports the split: the coverage matcher in check_pipeline.py compared each dossier evidence id against table labels using only the first evidence label per intervention, which falsely flagged two correctly-routed therapies ("Anthracycline-based chemotherapy" never stem-matches "Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy"); it now matches against every label filed under an intervention id, with a regression test added.

Reference verification ran before this page was persisted: no new identifier was introduced anywhere in this re-split, 10 carried PMIDs and 5 carried NCT records were re-resolved live this run against the NCBI esummary endpoint and the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API with titles and status checked against the claims they support, and the remainder were verified in the prior run's full pass. All resolved and matched; none was corrected, none nulled.

Ceralasertib is investigational with no approval anywhere.Ask that the comprehensive panel report BRCA1/2 and any HRD or homologous-recombination gene findings explicitly, since that is what would move this from speculative to arguable. 17Proton beam therapy and carbon-ion radiotherapy for the acetabular lesionAcetabular Lesion Pathologic FractureStandard of care Not yet accessibleProton therapy is an established, FDA-cleared radiotherapy modality delivered under standard radiation-oncology practice; carbon-ion therapy is in clinical use in Europe and Asia and has no operating US facility verified in this passAsk the radiation oncologist whether local therapy to the acetabulum is being framed as durable local control or as pain and structural palliation, because the answer decides whether the proton argument is worth the appeal. 18B7-H3 (CD276) immunohistochemistry—Standard of care Not yet accessibleNo FDA-approved B7-H3 companion diagnostic; laboratory-developed and research-use assays onlyAsk the sarcoma centre's pathology service whether they run a validated B7-H3 stain before sending tissue anywhere. 19Comprehensive tumour DNA plus RNA profiling with TMB and MSI reportingIdh1 Idh2 Mutation StatusStandard of careFDA-approved companion diagnostic panels (FoundationOne CDx, MI Cancer Seek) and CLIA laboratory-developed testsConfirm with pathology which block holds the dedifferentiated component, and send that one. 20Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, with or without ifosfamide or cisplatin—Standard of careFDA-approved generics; doxorubicin carries a broad soft-tissue and bone sarcoma indicationScore and document ECOG in clinic, since the assumed 2 is what will decide between doxorubicin alone and a doxorubicin-plus-ifosfamide combination. 21Expert bone-sarcoma pathology review—Standard of careNot applicableAsk the diagnosing hospital to release the block and slides now, since shipping is often the slowest step. 22Four-antibody mismatch-repair immunohistochemistry, with MSI testing if equivocal—Standard of careStandard CLIA immunohistochemistry; MSI testing available by PCR or NGSOrder the four-antibody panel on the same block cut as the other stains, so the block is opened once. 23HLA class I genotyping at 4-digit (allele-level) resolution—Standard of careStandard CLIA and ASHI-accredited immunogenetics testingOrder 4-digit class I typing on blood; no tumour tissue is consumed. 24IDH1 codon 132 and IDH2 codon 140/172 sequencing (not R132H immunohistochemistry)—Standard of careLaboratory-developed and FDA-approved companion diagnostic panels both available under CLIAOrder this on the same requisition as the comprehensive panel rather than as a separate test. 25Ivosidenib (TIBSOVO, AG-120)—Off-label useFDA-approved (IDH1-mutant relapsed/refractory AML 2018;
