docs.title: Pembrolizumab, biomarker-conditional, second line (pembrolizumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative4lowI hold pembrolizumab in reserve for second line because its safety profile is the best characterised of anything non-cytotoxic in this dossier: over a decade of post-marketing use since the 2014 approval, and irAE algorithms every oncology unit already runs. The chondrosarcoma evidence is genuinely thin (1 responder of 5 in SARC028, 1 PR of 5 in the Bui cohort), so this pick firms up only if PD-L1 on the dedifferentiated component, TMB or MSI comes back supportive. Monotherapy is the version I can defend; the sunitinib-nivolumab bone cohort logged a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation, which is a different risk conversation for an assumed-ECOG-2 patient. The tumour-agnostic TMB-high label is a real if unlikely on-label route after first-line chemotherapy.PD-L1 prevalence of 41-52% in dedifferentiated tumours is prevalence, not response prediction.; Chondrosarcoma is typically TMB-low, so the on-label pembrolizumab route is a long shot that costs nothing to test but should not be planned around.; All efficacy data are single-arm or retrospective; there is no PFS estimate to schedule a second line against. critic4lowAdd up the whole prospective checkpoint experience in this disease and it comes to 1 responder of 5 in SARC028, inside a cohort whose primary endpoint was not met (2 of 40) and whose responder's subtype the primary report never states, plus 1 PR of 5 pembrolizumab-treated in a retrospective five-centre series, plus a single case report of a sustained CR. The attribution of that SARC028 responder to dedifferentiated histology is secondhand in later sources, and I will not plan around a citation that traces back to nobody. The microenvironment work argues against the axis rather than for it: macrophages are the dominant population, a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was independently prognostic (p<0.01, n=76), and in the immunocompetent rat model depleting T cells accelerated growth while depleting CD163+ macrophages slowed it. It keeps a place on my list only because a TMB >=10 or MSI-high call would make it on-label, and the panel that answers that is already going out.PD-L1 positivity of 41-52% in dedifferentiated tumours is prevalence, and the one documented responder in the five-centre series was TPS 7% / CPS 8 and microsatellite-stable, so the marker is doing no predictive work in either direction.; The on-label TMB route is a low-prior bet: TMB >=10 mut/Mb appears in 3.9% of sarcomas and chondrosarcoma was not among the ten KEYNOTE-158 cohorts.; Open-label single-arm response ascertainment throughout, with no PFS estimate in this histology against which to schedule a second line.; The 1-of-5 and 1-of-4 numbers everyone cites are subgroups of four and five patients. Their confidence intervals run from roughly nothing to roughly everything. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityA decade of post-marketing data describes toxicity, not benefit, and here the safety record is quietly doing the ranking work. The efficacy base is 1 of 5 in SARC028, inside a bone cohort whose primary endpoint failed at 2 of 40 and whose responder the primary report never subtypes, plus 1 PR of 5 in the Bui series. Keep the pick on the grounds you actually give, that a TMB-high or MSI-high call makes it on-label, but the number travelling with it should be stated as five patients rather than as a 20% response rate. advocateconservativequalifiedotherTargeting rank 4 rather than the chemo consensus because this is where the assumed ECOG hardens into a fact: 'a different risk conversation for an assumed-ECOG-2 patient' lets an intake assumption pre-decide monotherapy over the combination, when the conservative's own rank 1 rightly says nothing starts until the ECOG is measured. The grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation (pmid:39540661) are real, and she may hear them and refuse, but that refusal belongs to her against a measured number, and the number may move if fixation does its job. Pembrolizumab held in reserve, biomarker-conditional, I co-sign; my qualification is that a patient who asked for everything gets shown the harder option with its price, not spared it by an assumption doing a measurement's work.

docs.title: TAPUR: marketed targeted agents by genomic match (NCT02693535) (tapur-genomically-matched-agents)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative5lowTAPUR assigns marketed agents by genomic match, which means known toxicity profiles and existing management algorithms rather than a novel mechanism, and its ECOG 0-2 bar is one of very few in the whole screen she may clear as written. Everything about it is conditional on the pending panel, and the no-remaining-standard-options language realistically places it after first-line anthracycline. She asked for every option; this one adds protocol structure without adding uncharacterised toxicity, which is why it makes my list ahead of the antigen-directed platforms.The panel may find nothing actionable; chondrosarcoma genomes are often quiet beyond IDH.; Any matched agent would be used outside its approved histology, so efficacy in this disease is unknown even where safety is well described. critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowTAPUR's ECOG 0-2 bar is one of the very few in the screen her assumed fitness clears as written, it runs at 181 US sites so geography probably does not bite, and it converts whatever the panel finds into a protocol seat with marketed drugs and known toxicity management. In a disease this fast the second-line decision arrives in months, so pre-positioning the seat now is what her trials-forward stance looks like in practice. Everything is conditional on the panel finding something actionable, which chondrosarcoma genomes often decline to do, and she should hear plainly that this seat may never materialise.Preference axes: prefers_trials served as written; wholly conditional on the pending panel, and a quiet genome closes it.; Any matched agent would be used outside its approved histology, so efficacy in her disease is unknown even where safety is well described.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityTAPUR buys protocol structure and familiar toxicity management, which is what you claim for it, and that is the whole of what it buys. The design is a basket of single-arm matched cohorts and no chondrosarcoma cohort result exists, so this is an access decision carrying no efficacy estimate at all. At rank 5 that is defensible, provided nobody downstream reads the NCT number as though it were data.

docs.title: IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), phase 1 NCT05039801 (glutaminase-inhibition)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2lowA phase 1 with chondrosarcoma written in as its own dose-escalation population and no prior-therapy requirement is a rare seat, and she can take it as written (nct:NCT05039801). The mechanism fits her tumour specifically: glutaminase expression rises with grade (p=0.001, highest in high-grade disease), and cell-line sensitivity did not track IDH status, so her untested IDH does not gate entry (pmid:29576625). Book the MD Anderson call now and slot enrollment at the first post-chemo decision point. Expected value of phase 1 monotherapy is honestly small; the upside is being the escalation patient the drug turns out to work for.ECOG must be 0-1 with no deterioration over the prior fortnight; the assumed 2 has to be measured down before a screening visit is worth booking; Dose-finding design with exploratory efficacy; no chondrosarcoma response has been reported for this class anywhere; The supporting data are in-vitro cytostasis with no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowThe single open protocol in the whole screen that writes chondrosarcoma in as its own treatment-naive dose-escalation population, which makes it the literal test of pursuing all possible therapeutic options: the phone call costs nothing and should happen this week. Honesty first, though: no glutaminase inhibitor has a chondrosarcoma clinical result anywhere, the ECOG bar is 0-1 against her assumed 2, and taking a phase 1 monotherapy slot first-line would spend her only proven-response window on a dose-finding question. My advocacy is for the call and the screening answer, not for delaying anthracycline, unless she hears those numbers and picks the trial anyway. That choice is hers, and today nobody has offered it to her.Preference axes: prefers_trials is served; travel tolerance was never discussed and this is a single-site protocol in Houston.; ECOG 0-1 entry bar with no deterioration over the prior fortnight; the assumed 2 has to be measured, and measured down, before screening is worth the trip.; The supporting evidence is cell-line work showing grade-dependent glutaminase expression (pmid 29576625); expected benefit from escalation-phase monotherapy is honestly small.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityRank 2 for a mechanism with no clinical result in any chondrosarcoma patient anywhere. The support is a single cell-line paper reporting that glutaminase expression rises with grade (p=0.001) and that sensitivity did not sort by IDH status, with no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm; the second half is a null finding you are using as an eligibility argument, which is fair, but nobody should mistake it for evidence of effect. Escalation also means she could be assigned a dose level that nobody involved expects to work. criticadvocatequalifiedevidence_qualityRanking the phone call rather than the drug is the defensible version of this, and it is what separates you from risktaker putting the same protocol at rank 2. The evidence underneath is still one in-vitro paper with no chondrosarcoma in-vivo arm and no clinical result for the class in this disease, and the ECOG 0-1 bar with no deterioration over the preceding fortnight means screening only becomes a real question after somebody examines her. The deliverable here is the screening answer, and the row should read that way downstream. concensusiterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitTwo concessions first: a pending IDH result does not gate this, since cell-line sensitivity did not sort by genotype and expression tracked grade (pmid:29576625), and NCT05039801 as the one treatment-naive protocol naming chondrosarcoma deserved a line on my slate; the advocate's rank 4, the call rather than the drug, is the row I should have written. What I do not concede is the shape of the slate, because trial enrollment is the consensus route to experimental therapy and every reachable seat in this screen is screened and delivered through the same bone-sarcoma centres, so my rank 2 referral is the enrollment mechanism, not a seat spent on a non-treatment. Rank 2 for escalation-phase monotherapy with no clinical result in this disease is still first-line time spent on a dose-finding question, and that part stays contested. concensusiteadvocateendorsepreference_fitI aim at rank 4 rather than the chemo consensus because my concession lives here: the call rather than the drug is the version of NCT05039801 that belonged on my slate, and the advocate wrote the row I failed to write. It survives the sceptics because the deliverable is a screening answer, the cost is a phone call, and first-line anthracycline does not wait. One addition from my side of the table: the centre that screens her for this protocol is the referral I ranked second, so the two rows are one act.

docs.title: Sunitinib plus nivolumab, off-label at first progression (sunitinib-plus-nivolumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowThe one checkpoint dataset where a dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma actually responded: 1 PR among the 4 dedifferentiated patients in IMMUNOSARC, 6-month PFS 42% (95% CI 27-58) across the bone cohort (pmid:39540661). PD-L1 in chondrosarcoma is confined to her subtype, 9 of 22 dedifferentiated positive against 0 of 119 conventional (pmid:27312065), so the immune argument was built on exactly her histology. Both drugs are marketed, which makes this buyable at first progression without a protocol seat. I will take a 1-in-4 anecdote plus subtype-restricted PD-L1 biology over waiting for trials that exclude her.mPFS 3.8 months and ORR 5% overall; the 42% six-month figure is mostly stable disease in a mixed-histology cohort; The dossier's own microenvironment work says macrophages dominate and T-cell depletion accelerated growth in a chondrosarcoma model (pmid:28344871), which argues the PD-1 axis may not be the lever; One treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis in 40 patients and 17% discontinued for toxicity; Off-label combination, so expect a payer fight conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerdissenttoxicityOne PR among 4 dedifferentiated patients, in a 40-patient cohort with a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis, 17% discontinuation for toxicity and ORR 5% overall. You list both halves and rank it third regardless, in a woman whose ECOG 2 has never been measured by anyone. The microenvironment work in this same dossier points away from the axis: macrophages were the dominant population, a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was independently prognostic at p<0.01, and depleting T cells accelerated growth in the immunocompetent rat model. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitTargeting rank 3 because it is the clearest off-label move on the board: an unendorsed combination whose cohort logged a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation against a dedifferentiated signal of 1 PR in 4 (pmid:39540661). Marketed means buyable, not endorsed, and the payer fight the risktaker predicts is the system pricing that exact gap. If a checkpoint route stays on the table at all, the conservative's biomarker-conditional monotherapy is the version a label could ever stand behind.

docs.title: Abemaciclib on NCT04040205, pre-positioned now for the post-anthracycline line (cdk4-6-inhibition)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowThe clearest post-first-line trial seat in the screen: dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named by itself, CDKN2A/B loss qualifies, and the one-prior-anthracycline requirement is satisfied by the first-line treatment she should get anyway (nct:NCT04040205). CDKN2A/B loss recurs in this subtype, and palbociclib cut intraosseous chondrosarcoma burden in vivo with the G1 arrest the mechanism predicts (pmid:30808351). The move this week is the comprehensive panel plus Rb IHC, because the biomarker gate cannot be cleared retroactively. A sequencing bet that costs nothing now and buys a named-histology slot most patients in this disease never see.ECOG 0-1, stricter than most protocols in the screen; fitness decides this one too; CDK-pathway alteration and Rb status are both untested, so the seat may evaporate on the panel result; Single-arm phase 2 with no chondrosarcoma efficacy data for any CDK4/6 inhibitor yet, and the palbociclib model work never reported CDKN2A status conservative——did not pick— critic5lowI rank this on the quality of the process rather than on any signal, and the two are not the same thing. No CDK4/6 inhibitor has a published chondrosarcoma efficacy result anywhere; the supporting work is a cell-line plus intraosseous mouse study that never reported CDKN2A status of its lines and needed a 2023 figure correction (pmid 36803557), so the biological case is inference. What the protocol has that almost nothing else in this dossier has is a registered pre-specified primary endpoint, central Rb immunohistochemistry instead of a local read, dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named as its own eligible histology, and a biomarker gate applied before enrolment rather than after the fact. Her preferences favour trials, first-line anthracycline satisfies the prior-therapy requirement, and the qualifying panel is already on order; ECOG 0-1 is the gate that decides it.Single-arm phase 2, n=44 across a mixed sarcoma population. Even a positive readout will not separate drug effect from having selected an indolent CDK-altered subset.; Two untested gates stand in the way, a qualifying CDK-pathway alteration and Rb positivity by central IHC, so the seat may simply not exist for her.; ECOG 0-1 excludes her as currently assumed, which makes this contingent on a measurement nobody has taken.; Nothing here justifies delaying first-line treatment to chase the seat. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerqualifiedevidence_qualitySame pick as mine, different load-bearing wall. The palbociclib intraosseous result you lean on never reported CDKN2A status of its lines and carries a 2023 figure correction (pmid 36803557), so it cannot support the biomarker inference; what makes NCT04040205 worth a seat is the registered primary endpoint, central Rb immunohistochemistry rather than a local read, and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named as its own eligible histology. No CDK4/6 inhibitor has a published chondrosarcoma efficacy result, which is worth saying in the row rather than only in the concerns.

docs.title: CD276 (B7-H3) CAR-T on NCT04433221, conditional on a high B7-H3 H-score (b7h3-car-t)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowConditional pick, and the condition is one stain. NCT04433221 gates on antigen expression rather than histology, takes Karnofsky 50% or better with no prior-therapy requirement, the loosest bars in this screen, and B7-H3 CAR-T regressed established osteosarcoma and Ewing xenografts where antigen density was high (pmid:30655315). The prior is against her: chondrosarcoma's median H-score of 60 is the lowest of any sarcoma subtype, but 96% of dedifferentiated tumours express the antigen and nobody has stained hers (pmid:33912442). Order the B7-H3 IHC with an H-score; pursue this only if she reads high, and drop it without regret at the median.Density dependence is the central preclinical result and it points away from this histology; a median-range H-score should kill the pick; One site in Shenzhen with safety as the primary endpoint and n=20; travel and self-funding are a hard sell in a 5-month-median disease; Rapidly progressive disease is excluded and lymphodepletion needs fitness nobody has measured; Manufacturing time competes with a tumour that moves in weeks conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe 96% is prevalence off a 24-specimen dedifferentiated tissue microarray with a Merck-employed author, and prevalence is the wrong quantity for this class: Majzner's activity was greatly diminished against low-expressing targets and the avidity work puts a measurable density threshold on it. The only H-score measurement in existence places chondrosarcoma lowest of any sarcoma subtype, median 60 against 175 for osteosarcoma (n=133), so your stated condition will most likely fail. NCT04433221 also gives the CAR alongside low-dose chemotherapy and an irradiated tumour-cell vaccine, n=20, one site, safety as the primary endpoint, so a response there could not be attributed to the CAR anyway.

docs.title: Mutant-IDH1 inhibition (AGI-5198) in chondrosarcoma lines
docs.text:
intervention_id: ivosidenib · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Nakagawa/Kitabayashi (2019)OncogeneIDH1-mutant chondrosarcoma cell lines (conventional L835, JJ012) in vitro and in mouse xenograftsnot stated per arm in the abstractvehicle; IDH1 wild-type comparatorsorally bioavailable DS-1001b; doses not stated in the abstractMutant IDH1 inhibition demethylates H3K9me3 and restores SOX9 and CDKN1C, which pushes conventional cells back toward chondrocyte differentiation and arrests the cycle in the more dedifferentiated line.DS-1001b lowered 2-HG and impaired proliferation of IDH1-mutant chondrosarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo, with the transcriptional response splitting by cell type: differentiation in L835, cell-cycle arrest in JJ012.moderatemedpartial31406254DOIThe strongest in-vivo case for a mutant-IDH1 inhibitor in this histology, but the effect is growth impairment rather than regression, and JJ012 is treated here as the dedifferentiated surrogate on thin grounds. Suijker/Bovée (2015)Oncotargetchondrosarcoma cell lines with endogenous IDH1 (n=3) or IDH2 (n=2) mutation, versus IDH wild-type lines5 IDH-mutant lines; treatment to 72 h and prolonged culture up to 20 passagesIDH1/2 wild-type chondrosarcoma cell lines and vehicleAGI-5198 dose-response, 72 h and prolonged exposure up to 20 passagesIf mutant IDH were still driving the malignant phenotype, removing D-2-HG should reverse the epigenetic block it causes. It did not, which places the mutation upstream of an event the cell has already banked.AGI-5198 dropped D-2-HG by more than 90% but only one of three mutant IDH1 lines showed even a moderate viability decrease at 72 h, and proliferation and migration were unchanged out to 20 passages. Global gene expression, CpG island methylation and H3K4/K9/K27 trimethylation all stayed put.negativemedpartial25895133DOIIn-vitro only, and the lines are conventional central chondrosarcoma rather than dedifferentiated, so this is the founder-event argument rather than a direct dedifferentiated-subtype result. D-2-HG was also detectable in plasma and urine of an IDH-mutant chondrosarcoma patient and fell after resection.moderatelowweak26368816DOIHT1080 is a fibrosarcoma line, not chondrosarcoma, which weakens half the panel; in-vitro only. docs.title: Mutant IDH biology: glycogen dependency (founder-event context)
docs.text:
intervention_id: idh-mutation-testing · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Pathmanapan/Alman (2023)Cell Repmutant Idh1 mice developing enchondromas, murine growth plate, and human mutant-IDH chondrosarcoma cells in vitro and in vivonot stated per arm in the abstractIDH wild-type cells and wild-type murine growth platepharmacologic blockade of glycogen utilisation; agent and dose not stated in the abstractMutant IDH1 partners with HIF1alpha to divert carbon into glycogen, a deposit found only in mutant cells, so the metabolic consequence of the mutation persists as a dependency separate from D-2-HG-driven methylation.Glycogen deposition appeared exclusively in mutant cells from IDH-mutant chondrosarcomas and Idh1-mutant murine growth plates. docs.title: Talazoparib alone and with temozolomide or radiation
docs.text:
intervention_id: parp-inhibition · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Venneker/Bovée (2019)Cancers (Basel)chondrosarcoma cell lines with and without endogenous IDH1/IDH2 mutation, including lines carried long-term on a D-2-HG-normalising inhibitorcell-line panel; counts not stated in the abstractIDH wild-type lines; single-agent temozolomide or radiationtalazoparib dose-response, alone and combined with temozolomide or irradiationThe IDH-mutant 'BRCAness' hypothesis holds that D-2-HG suppresses homologous recombination and creates PARP-inhibitor synthetic lethality, as it does in glioma and leukaemia models.Talazoparib sensitivity varied widely and did not sort by IDH mutation status, and long-term normalisation of D-2-HG did not create synthetic lethality. docs.title: Carbon-ion versus X-ray irradiation of chondrosarcoma lines
docs.text:
intervention_id: particle-therapy · 5 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Yagi/Ogawa (2022)Cancers (Basel)four human sarcoma lines (MG63 osteosarcoma, HT1080 fibrosarcoma, SW872 liposarcoma, SW1353 chondrosarcoma) and three normal-tissue lines7 cell lines under one standardised colony-formation protocolgamma-ray irradiation as the reference radiationgamma rays; proton beam at the centre of the spread-out Bragg peak; carbon ions at 54.4 keV/micrometre LETRBE is the number that converts a physical dose into a biological one; if it varies by cell type, the fixed 1.1 and 2.1 used in planning systems are averages rather than facts about a given tumour.Mean RBE was 1.08 +/- 0.11 for protons and 2.08 +/- 0.36 for carbon ions, close to the 1.1 and 2.13 used clinically. Between-line spread reached 34% for protons and 32% for carbon ions among the sarcoma lines, and up to 48% between two normal lines under carbon ions.strongmedpartial35454915DOISW1353 is the only chondrosarcoma line and it is conventional grade II; the physical rationale for carbon over proton (roughly a doubling of biological effect) is quantified here, the histology-specific part is not. Girard/Boumédiene (2020)J Bone Oncolfive human chondrosarcoma cell lines (CH2879, SW1353, JJ012, FS090, 105KC) in normoxia and chronic hypoxia5 cell lines; survival curves, gammaH2AX, Apo2.7, SA-beta-gal, whole-exome sequencingunirradiated cells; X-ray irradiation as the comparator for carbon ions; normoxic culture as comparator for hypoxiasingle-dose X-ray and carbon-ion irradiation, survival-curve dose rangeHigh-LET carbon ions produce clustered, hard-to-repair DNA lesions, so cell kill is less dependent on the repair capacity and cell-cycle position that make photons ineffective here.Carbon ions caused more DNA damage and more cell death than X-rays across the panel, though the magnitude varied by line. X-ray response split cleanly — apoptosis and senescence in CH2879, one or the other in SW1353 and JJ012, no death at all in FS090 and 105KC — with p21 tracking senescence. Chronic hypoxia did not increase radioresistance and made JJ012 more radiosensitive.moderatemedpartial32211283DOIIn-vitro only, and the hypoxia result cuts against the standard oxygen-enhancement-ratio argument for why carbon ions should be preferred in this histology. Vares/Saintigny (2020)Radiother OncolCH-2879 high-grade chondrosarcoma cells, cancer-stem-cell and tumour-initiating assayssingle cell line; replicate counts not stated in the abstractcarbon-ion irradiation alone; untreated cellscarbon-ion irradiation combined with miR-34 mimic and/or rapamycinA radioresistant stem-like fraction survives irradiation; mTOR inhibition raises FOXO3 and miR-34, which represses KLF4 and strips the stemness programme that lets those cells re-initiate the tumour.High-grade chondrosarcoma cultures contained a radioresistant cancer-stem-cell population that carbon ions alone did not clear, and the triple combination controlled it along with the stemness phenotype and tumour-initiating capacity.moderatelowweak32717360DOISingle conventional grade III line and no animal arm; the miR-34 mimic has no clinical route in sarcoma. Césaire/Chevalier (2019)J Bone OncolCH2879 grade III chondrosarcoma cell linesingle cell line; clonogenic and proliferation assaysirradiation without olaparib; unirradiated cellsolaparib with single-dose X-ray, proton and carbon-ion irradiationPARP inhibition blocks single-strand break repair, so the clustered damage from particles is converted into lethal double-strand breaks the cell cannot resolve.Olaparib gave sensitiser enhancement ratios of roughly 1.3 with X-rays, 1.8 with protons and 1.5 with carbon ions on clonogenic assay. CH2879 carried mutations in RAD50, SMARCA2 and NBN, which the authors link to its baseline radiosensitivity.moderatelowpartial31312595DOISingle cell line, in-vitro only, and no dedifferentiated model. The largest gain was with protons rather than carbon ions, which is not the ordering the clinical modality argument assumes. Hamdi/Saintigny (2016)Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Physprimary human articular chondrocytes from a healthy donor in a collagen scaffold under physioxia (3D), with 2D culture as referenceone healthy donor; survival, cell-death and senescence assaysX-ray irradiation at the same dose; 2D culture as the reference formatsingle dose of a monoenergetic carbon-ion beam at approximately 30 keV/micrometre LET, the entrance-channel value upstream of the spread-out Bragg peakEntrance-channel carbon ions cross healthy cartilage before the Bragg peak; senescence rather than death is the relevant injury endpoint in a tissue that does not turn over.In 2D the carbon-ion RBE was 2.6 with a two-fold increase in radiation-induced senescence, but in the 3D physioxic cartilage model carbon ions and X-rays induced senescence at comparable rates. Measuring RBE in monolayer may therefore misstate the normal-tissue cost of a carbon-ion plan.weakmedpartial27084635DOIHealthy donor cartilage, not tumour, and a single donor. Speaks to the joint-preservation side of an acetabular particle-therapy decision rather than to tumour control.

docs.title: Radiotherapy and periosteal stripping before femoral fracture (bone-healing mechanism)
docs.text:
intervention_id: local-therapy-fracture-site · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Nicholls/Ferguson (2013)J Orthop Resfemale Wistar retired-breeder rat femoral fracture with fixation, after radiotherapy and/or surgical periosteal stripping4 treatment groups (control, radiotherapy, surgery, combined) across 3 endpoints (21, 28, 35 days post-fracture)untreated fracture; surgery-alone and radiotherapy-alone armsradiotherapy first, periosteal stripping 3 weeks later, femoral fracture with fixation 3 weeks after thatIrradiated bone loses the chondroid and osteoid production that callus formation depends on, so the fracture defaults to atrophic non-union regardless of the mechanical fixation.By 35 days controls had united, periosteum-stripped animals formed hypertrophic non-unions, and irradiated animals formed atrophic non-unions with histomorphometry showing absent chondroid and osteoid. Periosteal stripping added little; radiation alone was sufficient.strongmedpartial23606416DOINormal rat bone with conventional photons and no tumour present, so it speaks to healing of the fractured acetabulum after radiotherapy rather than to tumour biology or drug delivery at that site.

docs.title: B7-H3 (CD276) CAR T cells
docs.text:
intervention_id: b7h3-car-t · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Barisa/Anderson (2025)Nat Communthree clinical-candidate B7-H3 binders across tumoroid re-stimulation assays, BEHAV3D single-cell video microscopy, and in-vivo models3 binder constructs; per-arm animal counts not stated in the abstractcomparison across the three binders of differing affinityrepeated tumoroid re-stimulation; in-vivo CAR T infusionCellular avidity, not monomeric affinity, sets the antigen-density floor at which a CAR triggers; higher-avidity constructs hold longer CD8 contacts with dim targets and keep expanding.Functional avidity predicted the B7-H3 density threshold for effector function, with the better constructs giving longer cumulative CD8 CAR-T/tumour contact times, more CAR-T expansion and sustained control. Lower checkpoint-receptor expression did not correlate with better anti-tumour function.moderatemedcross tumor only40764385DOIPaediatric neuroblastoma and related models, no sarcoma-of-bone arm. Relevant because it defines what would have to be engineered around for an antigen-dim tumour, not because it tested one. Majzner/Mackall (2019)Clin Cancer Resxenograft models of osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and medulloblastoma; antigen-density titration in vitromultiple xenograft models; per-arm counts not stated in the abstractuntransduced or control CAR T cells; low- versus high-antigen target cellssingle intravenous or locoregional CAR T-cell infusion depending on the modelCAR engagement is a threshold phenomenon rather than a binary one: below a certain surface antigen count per cell the synapse does not trigger full effector function, which is what creates a therapeutic window against normal tissue that expresses B7-H3 at low level.B7-H3 CAR T cells regressed established solid tumours including osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma xenografts. Efficacy depended on high surface antigen density and was greatly diminished against low-expressing targets.strongmedcross tumor only30655315DOINo chondrosarcoma model anywhere in the paper; the density-dependence result is the part that transfers, and it cuts against a tumour whose measured B7-H3 H-scores are the lowest in sarcoma.

docs.title: DS-7300a (ifinatamab deruxtecan), B7-H3-directed DXd ADC
docs.text:
intervention_id: b7h3-adc · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Kloker/Deinzer (2026)BMC Cancertwo-centre cohort of 133 pre-treatment human bone and soft-tissue sarcoma samples, centrally stained B7-H3 IHC with H-scoren=133 (103 soft-tissue, 30 bone sarcoma)cross-subtype comparison; four B7-H3-negative samplesnot applicableH-score separates positivity from density. Both the CAR and the ADC literature make efficacy a function of surface antigen per cell, so a 'percent positive' figure and an H-score are not interchangeable.B7-H3 was expressed in 97% of sarcomas, but chondrosarcoma had the lowest median H-score of any subtype (60) against 175 for osteosarcoma and 202.5 for pleomorphic liposarcoma. H-score rose with histological grade across subtypes and predicted event-free but not overall survival.moderatemedpartial42251292DOIHuman tissue survey, not a model system, and the chondrosarcoma subgroup within the 30 bone sarcomas is small with no dedifferentiated breakdown reported. The grade correlation leaves open that a dedifferentiated component scores higher than the subtype median. Yamato/Agatsuma (2022)Mol Cancer Therhuman cancer cell lines in vitro; cell-line xenograft and patient-derived xenograft mouse models; PK in cynomolgus monkey; toxicology in rat and monkeymultiple xenograft and PDX models; per-arm counts not stated in the abstractB7-H3-negative cancer cell lines and vehicleDS-7300a intravenous dosing in xenograft models; doses not stated in the abstractAntibody binding to B7-H3 internalises a cleavable DXd topoisomerase-I payload, which raises phospho-CHK1 and cleaved PARP in the target cell.DS-7300a inhibited growth of B7-H3-expressing lines but not B7-H3-negative ones, and produced antitumour activity in high-B7-H3 xenografts and PDX models of several tumour types. It was stable in circulation and tolerated in rats and monkeys.strongmedcross tumor only35149548DOIEvery efficacy model is explicitly high-B7-H3; there is no chondrosarcoma model and no low-expression efficacy arm, so this does not address the expression tier a chondrosarcoma would most likely sit at. Ogitani/Agatsuma (2016)Cancer Scico-culture of antigen-positive and antigen-negative cells; mouse xenografts with mixed antigen-positive and antigen-negative tumoursco-culture and mixed-xenograft experiments; per-arm counts not stated in the abstractT-DM1, whose non-cleavable payload does not diffuse; antigen-negative tumours alonesingle intravenous ADC dose in xenograft modelsThe released DXd payload is membrane-permeable, so it diffuses out of the antigen-positive cell it was delivered into and kills adjacent antigen-negative neighbours; the non-cleavable T-DM1 payload does not do this.DS-8201a killed antigen-negative cells in co-culture and in mixed xenografts, while T-DM1 did not. This is the mechanism by which a DXd ADC can act on a heterogeneous or low-expressing tumour rather than only on strongly positive cells.moderatelowcross tumor only27166974DOIHER2 breast/gastric models, a different antigen and a different tumour entirely; it is offered as the payload-class rationale for why a B7-H3 DXd ADC might not need uniform high antigen, not as evidence that it works in chondrosarcoma.

docs.title: Immune landscape of conventional versus dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma
docs.text:
intervention_id: immune-checkpoint-blockade · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Ao/Pollack (2026)Cancer Immunol ResTILs expanded from immune-excluded human chondrosarcoma biopsies; autologous 3D tumour spheroid killing assays; spatial profiling of the TMEnot stated per patient in the abstractconventional IL-2-dependent TIL expansionregulatable membrane-bound IL-15 expression without exogenous IL-2Collagenous matrix and myeloid infiltration exclude lymphocytes to the tumour periphery; membrane-bound IL-15 lowers the TCR signalling threshold of TIL clonotypes so the same T cells infiltrate and kill.Spatial profiling put ubiquitous collagen and myeloid infiltration forward as the resistance mechanisms, with lymphocytes largely restricted to peripheral regions — which is also where a TIL harvest would have to sample. Engineered TILs expanded from paucicellular chondrosarcoma biopsies and killed autologous 3D tumour models without exogenous IL-2.moderatemedstrong41719158DOIEx-vivo and 3D-model endpoints only, no in-vivo efficacy arm, and the work is sponsored by the company developing the platform. Li/Ye (2021)Clin Cancer Resfresh human conventional chondrosarcoma tumours profiled by CyTOF, whole-exome sequencing and flow cytometry, with mechanistic follow-up98 fresh tumours collected; 22 fully profiled; 12 patients received PD-1 antibodycross-subtype comparison among the three immune phenotypesnot applicable (retrospective PD-1 antibody exposure in 12 patients)IDH mutation raised chemokine levels and immune-cell infiltration in otherwise immune-inactivated tumours, which offers a route by which genotype rather than PD-L1 shapes who is infiltrated.Three immune phenotypes emerged: G-MDSC-dominant, immune-exhausted, and immune-desert. The immune-rich subtypes were characterised by IDH mutation and high grade, and all 3 of 12 PD-1-treated patients with disease control were retrospectively classified as immune-exhausted.moderatemedpartial34426437DOIConventional chondrosarcoma only, so it does not directly cover the dedifferentiated component; the 3-of-12 clinical correlation is retrospective and hypothesis-generating. Richert/Dutour (2020)J Bone Oncolhuman tumour cohort, IHC (CD3, CD8, CD68, CD163, PD-L1, CSF1R) plus RT-qPCR for immune checkpointsn=76 (27 conventional, 49 dedifferentiated)conventional chondrosarcoma as the comparator for the dedifferentiated groupnot applicableThe dominant immune population is macrophage, not lymphocyte, and the checkpoints that are transcribed (CSF1R, SIRPA alongside B7H3, TIM3, LAG3) are largely myeloid ones, so PD-L1 positivity marks an inflamed dedifferentiated component without being the switch that controls it.TAMs were the main immune population in both subtypes; a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was an independent poor prognostic factor (p<0.01) and high CD68+ tracked with metastasis at diagnosis (p<0.05). PD-L1 protein was confined to dedifferentiated tumours (42.6%), and CSF1R was expressed by TAMs in 89.7% of dedifferentiated versus 62.9% of conventional cases.moderatemedstrong31956474DOIDescriptive human-tissue study with no therapeutic arm, so the CSF1R nomination is a hypothesis. PubMed indexes the author names in scrambled form; the 2020 corrigendum (PMID 32274326) gives them as Richert I ... Dutour A, which is what is recorded here.

docs.title: Selective T-cell versus CD163+ macrophage depletion (syngeneic model)
docs.text:
intervention_id: tam-directed-therapy · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Quoniou/Peyrode (2025)Med OncolCH2879/THP-1 3D co-culture spheroids and CH2879 murine xenograftnot stated per arm in the abstractdoxorubicin alone; mifamurtide alonemifamurtide combined with doxorubicin; doses not stated in the abstractTAMs can reach half the tumour mass in chondrosarcoma and sit predominantly in an M2-like state; a TLR4 agonist repolarises them, and the chemosensitivity of the tumour compartment changes as a consequence.Mifamurtide increased the chemosensitivity of CH2879/THP-1 spheroids, and in the CH2879 xenograft the combination with doxorubicin improved antitumour efficacy while reducing intermediate-stage TAMs.moderatemedpartial40960554DOIConventional grade III line, no dedifferentiated model, and mifamurtide's approved indication is paediatric non-metastatic osteosarcoma, so the regulatory route in this setting is not established. Simard/Dutour (2017)OncoimmunologySwarm rat chondrosarcoma (SRC) syngeneic model plus IHC on human chondrosarcoma samplesnot stated per arm in the abstractundepleted tumour-bearing ratsselective immunodepletion of T lymphocytes or of CD163+ macrophages in tumour-bearing ratsCausal rather than correlative: removing the two populations in opposite directions separates which one restrains the tumour and which one supports it.Depleting T lymphocytes accelerated tumour growth, while depleting CD163+ macrophages slowed it. Splenocytes from tumour-bearing rats showed 27% specific cytotoxicity against chondrosarcoma cells, falling to 11% after CD3 depletion, and in both human and rat tumours the immune infiltrate sat in the peritumoral area.moderatemedpartial28344871DOIRat chondrosarcoma rather than a dedifferentiated human model; the immunocompetent design is what makes it worth keeping despite that.

docs.title: Palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibition) in chondrosarcoma
docs.text:
intervention_id: cdk4-6-inhibition · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Ouyang/Liu (2019)Cell Commun Signalhuman chondrosarcoma cell lines with CDK4 siRNA and palbociclib; intraosseous chondrosarcoma mouse model read out by bioluminescencenot stated per arm in the abstractscrambled siRNA and vehicle-treated micepalbociclib in vitro dose-response; in-vivo dosing not stated in the abstractCDK4 phosphorylates Rb to release the G1 restriction point; where CDKN2A is deleted, as it is in a large share of dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma, that brake is already gone and inhibiting CDK4 restores it pharmacologically.CDK4 was expressed in human chondrosarcoma samples and correlated with metastasis and worse prognosis; siRNA or palbociclib cut proliferation with reduced Rb phosphorylation, arrested cells in G1 and reduced migration and invasion. Palbociclib reduced tumour burden within bone in vivo.moderatemedpartial30808351DOIA 2023 correction replaced a wrongly uploaded Fig. 5C image with conclusions unchanged (PMID 36803557). CDKN2A status of the lines is not reported, so the biomarker link to this patient's untested CDKN2A remains inferred. Schrage/Bovée (2009)J Cell Mol Medchondrosarcoma cell lines OUMS27, SW1353, CH2879 with CDKN2A/p16 overexpression vectors and shRNA against CDK4; qPCR and IHC on 34 fresh-frozen and 90 FFPE enchondroma and chondrosarcoma samples3 cell lines; 124 human tumour samples; IHC subset of 29 high-grade chondrosarcomasempty vector and non-targeting shRNAnot applicable (genetic manipulation)Reintroducing p16 or removing CDK4 rebuilds the same G1 brake that CDKN2A deletion removes during progression, which tests whether the pathway is still load-bearing rather than merely altered.Both p16 overexpression and CDK4 knockdown inhibited chondrosarcoma cell growth in vitro, and pRb-pathway alterations tracked with progression from enchondroma to high-grade chondrosarcoma in the tissue series.moderatemedpartial18624751DOIIn-vitro genetic proof rather than drug testing, and predates the availability of CDK4/6 inhibitors; establishes that the pathway is functional, not that a given inhibitor works.

docs.title: Manuscripts considered — chondrosarcoma-mets-acetabular-fx-idh-unknown-y34r
docs.text:
Master inventory: 30 clinical (27 included, 3 considered & excluded) + 30 pre-clinical (28 included, 2 considered & excluded) + 21 additional trial publications/registrations.
