docs.text:
• Standard-of-care backbone (Stupp + TTFields, CCTG CE.6 elderly hypofractionated, CeTeG / NOA-09 conditional): PMID 15758010, PMID 15758009, PMID 19269895, PMID 29392280, PMID 31488360, PMID 28296618, NCT00006353, NCT00916409, NCT01149109, NCT00482677.
  • MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors (BGB-58067 brain-penetrant; navlimetostat / BMS-986504 with a dedicated GBM CNS-penetration trial plus cross-tumor NSCLC activity; TNG456 dual-axis with abemaciclib; class proxy anvumetostat): NCT07485049, NCT06883747, NCT07492680, NCT06810544, PMID 39282709, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.1669, doi:10.1016/j.jtho.2025.09.054, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.0647.
  • Adaptive-platform / randomized backbone alternative: NCT03970447.
  • Peptide-vaccine adjuvant-phase add-on: PMID 36473145, NCT05163080.
  • Tumor-agnostic conditional plays (recurrence-only, biomarker-gated): PMID 34838156, PMID 29466156, PMID 32919526, NCT02034110, NCT02122913, NCT02628067.
  • CDK4/6 inhibitor (recurrence pre-position): NCT02981940, PMID 37722087, PMID 30151703.
  • Oncolytic HSV-1 (recurrence pre-position): PMID 37853118, NCT03152318.
  • FUS-mediated BBB opening (recurrence pre-position): PMID 37087102, NCT04528680.
  • EGFRvIII / EGFR-amp cellular therapy (front-line NOT recommended in this patient; recurrence-time consideration with documented re-bleed surveillance): PMID 38477966, PMID 38497615, PMID 30418325, NCT05660369, NCT06186401, NCT07209241.

docs.title: Rank 1. Diagnostic workup gate — MGMT methylation, MTAP IHC central confirmation, EGFR + EGFRvIII, comprehensive tumor NGS, RB1 IHC
docs.text: Six parallel assays on one block of tissue resolve every load-bearing front-line and recurrence-time decision in this case.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The four essential gates_intervention rows from the target-validation file fold into a single rank-1 workup. MGMT pyrosequencing is the validated method that best separated TMZ benefit in the Quillien comparison (PMID 22120555) and is anchored on Hegi 2005's biomarker analysis of EORTC 26981 (PMID 15758010). MTAP IHC central confirmation by the SP347-class clone is the standard the MTAPESTRY-101 protocol now hard-requires after four of six patients enrolled on local CDKN2A-only NGS calls were intact-MTAP on central IHC and progressed (PMID 39282709). EGFR amplification by FISH plus EGFRvIII RT-PCR or RNA-fusion NGS opens the cellular-therapy menu (PMID 30115632). Comprehensive NGS resolves BRAF V600E (ROAR HGG cohort, ORR 33% — PMID 34838156), NTRK fusions (larotrectinib tumor-agnostic — PMID 29466156), and MSI-H / TMB-H (tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab — PMID 32919526).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Diagnostic certainty. The workup itself does not treat the patient; it locks the rank-2 backbone candor, the rank-3 trial-slot eligibility, the rank-4 methylated-MGMT conditional, the rank-7 tumor-agnostic conditional axes, and the rank-9 RB1-gated CDK4/6 conversation at recurrence. Every persona endorsed this row without dissent because the cost is low and the consequences of skipping any single component are high.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text: No procedural toxicity — all assays run on archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection block plus a peripheral blood draw for the parallel germline panel (the target-validation germline-cdkn2a-mlh1-msh2-msh6-pms2 row, medium-priority). The non-toxicity risk is the block itself: intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation may have compromised tumor cellularity in parts of the resection. Pathology should pull the most tumor-rich block and confirm cellularity before the IHC bundle goes out.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: None. Workup row; no therapeutic mechanism to evaluate. Board endorsement was unanimous.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Order everything in parallel the day after the post-op MRI. The IHC bundle (MTAP, p16, RB1) goes to one lab on one requisition (NeoGenomics MTAP IHC, 1-866-776-5907). MGMT pyrosequencing goes to Labcorp (MGMT Gene Methylation Assay, 1-800-345-4363). Comprehensive NGS with DNA + RNA fusion goes to Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx + FoundationOne Heme, 1-888-988-3639) or Tempus (xT CDx + xR, 1-800-739-4137 — DNA + RNA combination is stronger for CNS NTRK breakpoints than DNA-only). EGFR FISH + EGFRvIII RT-PCR also routes through NeoGenomics. Turnaround windows: 5-7 business days IHC, 7-10 days MGMT, 2-4 weeks NGS. All compatible with the standard RT-start window if ordered the week after surgery.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Every downstream rec in the table is conditional on at least one result from this workup. The rank-2 Stupp + TTFields backbone runs regardless of result, but the candor of the patient conversation about TMZ benefit hinges on MGMT. The rank-3 BGB-58067 enrollment hinges on MTAP IHC. The rank-4 CeTeG conditional hinges on MGMT methylated. The rank-7 tumor-agnostic axes are activated by their respective biomarker results. Workup at rank 1 is the only honest ordering.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference MGMT pyrosequencing Gates Stupp adjuvant TMZ commitment; Hegi 2005 methylated mOS 21.7 vs 15.3 Tissue-only assay, no patient toxicity PMID 15758010, PMID 22120555 MTAP IHC (SP347-class clone) Gates BGB-58067 NCT07485049, MountainTAP-5 NCT07492680, all MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor protocols Tissue-only, no patient toxicity PMID 39282709 EGFR FISH + EGFRvIII RT-PCR Gates E-SYNC NCT06186401, CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369, Penn NCT07209241 Tissue-only, no patient toxicity PMID 30115632, NCT05660369 Comprehensive tumor NGS + RNA fusion Gates dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF V600E ORR 33% ROAR), larotrectinib (NTRK), pembrolizumab (MSI-H / TMB-H) Tissue-only, no patient toxicity PMID 34838156, PMID 29466156, PMID 32919526 RB1 IHC (clone G3-245) + p16 IHC corroboration Confirms intact RB pathway downstream of CDK4/6 (gates abemaciclib at recurrence); orthogonal CDKN2A loss confirmation Tissue-only, no patient toxicity NCT02981940, PMID 36815432

docs.title: Rank 2. Stupp regimen + TTFields — RT 60 Gy / 30 fx with concurrent and adjuvant TMZ, Optune Gio added at adjuvant cycle 1
docs.text: The OS-anchored standard the entire ranking is built around.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: EORTC 26981 / NCIC CE.3 (Stupp 2005 NEJM, n=573, RoB2:Low; PMID 15758010) gave RT + concurrent TMZ followed by 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001), mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo, 2-yr OS 26.5% vs 10.4%. The 5-year update (Stupp 2009 Lancet Oncology, n=573; PMID 19269895) replicated HR 0.6 (95% CI 0.5-0.7), 5-yr OS 9.8% vs 1.9%. EF-14 (Stupp 2017 JAMA, n=695, open-label; PMID 29392280) added TTFields 200 kHz to maintenance TMZ for HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%. Hegi 2005 (PMID 15758010, biomarker subset n=206 of 573) localizes the TMZ benefit to MGMT-methylated tumors (methylated mOS 21.7 vs 15.3, p<0.001; unmethylated 12.7 vs 11.8, NS) — the regimen recommendation does not flip on the result but the patient conversation does. The fallback for fitness-decline scenarios is Perry / CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated RT 40 Gy / 15 fx + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ (Perry 2017 NEJM, n=562, RoB2:Low; PMID 28296618), HR_OS 0.67 (95% CI 0.56-0.80, p<0.001).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: High. Stupp HR_OS 0.63 has been replicated across two phase 3 trials with overlapping confidence intervals, the EF-14 add-on stacks another HR 0.63 on top of adjuvant TMZ, and the patient (66, ECOG 1) sits inside the EORTC 26981 inclusion population. The 20.9-month median is the threshold every other rank in this list is measured against. The unmethylated-MGMT scenario lowers the TMZ-attributable component of that benefit, but the RT + TTFields components persist regardless.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Concurrent-phase G≥3 hematologic AE 7% (Stupp 2005, n=287). Lymphopenia dominates; PJP prophylaxis is non-negotiable during the concurrent phase given TMZ-induced lymphopenia.
  • Adjuvant-phase G≥3 hematologic AE 14% (Stupp 2005, n=223). At age 66, expect dose modification in roughly a quarter of patients. Weekly CBC during concurrent and the first two adjuvant cycles is on-label monitoring.
  • TTFields scalp dermatitis 52% any grade, 2% G≥3 under the transducer arrays (EF-14). Non-overlapping with TMZ hematotox. Manageable with array rotation and topical-steroid algorithm.
  • ≥18 hr/day Optune wear-time is the binding adherence variable; sub-18-hour wear roughly halves the EF-14 OS benefit per the per-protocol analyses. Not a toxicity per se but a counseling load-bearing point.

No toxicity vetoes from the preference file are triggered.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was unanimous. The only counter-productive consideration is mild and delayed: TMZ-induced hypermutation at recurrence can paradoxically open MMR-deficient ICI eligibility, which is a delayed pro-mechanism effect rather than a true counter-productive one. The risktaker dissented on the critic's framing of Stupp + TTFields as "a stable platform" (calling it "the ceiling we are trying to break"), but the risktaker's own pick-3 keeps the regimen, so this dissent is about anchoring rather than substitution.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCCN CNS v2.2026 category 1 (preferred) for newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM in age <70 KPS ≥70; TTFields category 1 in combination with maintenance TMZ. EANO 2021 and ESMO 2014 / 2021 concur. Generic TMZ is universally covered by Medicare Part D and commercial plans (Merck Sharp & Dohme for branded Temodar, 1-800-444-2080; generics widely available). TTFields prior auth runs through Novocure nCompass (1-855-281-9301) — submit at RT planning so the device ships before adjuvant cycle 1 starts. Optune Gio is on-label under Medicare NCD 110.24 for newly diagnosed and recurrent GBM. If performance status declines between resection and RT planning, switch to Perry CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated 40 Gy / 15 fx; the methylated subgroup gets HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.38-0.73), the unmethylated subgroup HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.56-1.01, CI crosses 1.0 by 0.01).

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: The only newly diagnosed regimen with RoB2:Low phase 3 OS evidence replicated at five years. The advocate and risktaker ranked the MTAP-axis trial above Stupp in their own lists; the consensusite explicitly read that ranking as inverting the NCCN hierarchy. The synthesis places Stupp + TTFields at rank 2 (under the rank-1 workup) because the trial-enrollment route at rank 3 layers this regimen into its own arm design (NCT07485049 Arm A = drug + RT; Arm B = drug + RT + TMZ) rather than replacing it — i.e. every persona's top therapeutic rank carries the Stupp spine inside it whether or not they call it out explicitly.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Stupp regimen (RT + concurrent/adjuvant TMZ) mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001); 2-yr OS 26.5% vs 10.4% G≥3 hematotox 7% concurrent, 14% adjuvant PMID 15758010, NCT00006353 Stupp 5-year update HR 0.6 (95% CI 0.5-0.7); 5-yr OS 9.8% vs 1.9% Same as above; cumulative PMID 19269895 TTFields (Optune Gio) + maintenance TMZ mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001); 5-yr OS 13% vs 5% Scalp dermatitis 52% any grade, 2% G≥3; non-overlapping with TMZ hematotox PMID 29392280, NCT00916409 Perry CCTG CE.6 elderly fallback mOS 9.3 vs 7.6 mo, HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.56-0.80, p<0.001); methylated HR 0.53 G≥3 lymphopenia 27%; PJP prophylaxis carries PMID 28296618, NCT00482677

docs.title: Rank 3. BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on NCT07485049 — Sanai phase 0/2 at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix
docs.text: Layered on the Stupp backbone, not substituting for it. The synthesis ranks this 3 rather than 1 because three personas dissented on rank order — load-bearing dissent on the absence of published BGB-58067 phase 1 safety, contingent on Sanai's eventual readout.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: NCT07485049 is the single best mechanistic match in the dossier for this patient's MTAP/CDKN2A 9p21 co-deletion — a phase 0/2 dual-arm trial designed specifically for newly diagnosed MTAP-deleted IDH-wildtype GBM, with MGMT stratification baked into the design (Arm A unmethylated + RT; Arm B methylated + RT + TMZ) and a phase 0 SDMA / H-score pharmacodynamic readout on re-resection tissue that forces a target-engagement decision before phase 2 commits. Direct human-GBM efficacy data on BGB-58067 itself is not yet published. The class proxy is anvumetostat (AMG 193) on MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon AnnOnc 2024 / Cancer Discovery 2025 — PMID 39282709, n=80 heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null) at ORR 11% with G≥3 TRAE 13.8% and treatment discontinuation 2.5% — the cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record, with 56% median plasma SDMA reduction at C2D1 confirming target engagement. Anvumetostat was discontinued program-wide by Amgen on April 30, 2026 across four phase 1b/2 trials. TNG908 was terminated in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling in n=3 patients confirmed inadequate brain exposure (0/23 evaluable GBM ORR — PMID 38108025). BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS-exposure modeling against the TNG908 failure mode, but the human CSF PK data closing that loop is not yet public.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate uncertainty. The mechanism case (synthetic-lethal MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibition in MTAP-null disease) is well-replicated mechanistically (Kryukov / Mavrakis / Marjon 2016 Cell / Nature companion). The clinical translation in CNS has lost twice — TNG908 and anvumetostat — and BGB-58067's brain-penetrant chemistry is the engineered answer to the proximate failure mode, but the published evidence on the molecule itself is the gap. Honest framing for the patient: open phase 0/2 slot at a high-volume center, mechanism-matched at biomarker, layered on Stupp, no published efficacy data on the drug itself.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Class proxy G≥3 TRAE 13.8%, discontinuation 2.5%, no treatment-related deaths in anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (the cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record).
  • BGB-58067 CNS-specific tox profile is unpublished. This is the conservative seat's load-bearing concern.
  • Phase 0 component requires a second resection biopsy for the SDMA / H-score readout. Subtotal-resection block tumor cellularity needs pathology confirmation; the intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation may have compromised that.

No toxicity vetoes from the preference file are triggered. The hemorrhage carry-forward is not triggered by the drug itself; only by the phase 0 re-resection consideration.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The conservative, critic, and consensusite seats all dissented on the advocate's and risktaker's rank-1 placement of this trial. The conservative dissent is explicitly toxicity-flavored: "BGB-58067 has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety data yet; class evidence comes from anvumetostat, which is a different molecule from a different sponsor; CNS-specific tox profile is the missing datum." The conservative lift condition is explicit — once Sanai publishes the phase 0 PD / safety readout, the dissent lifts to qualified. The critic dissent is evidence-quality grounds: ranking a single-site single-arm single-sponsor phase 0/2 with no published BGB-specific efficacy above Stupp inverts the evidence weighting. The consensusite dissent is guideline-fit grounds: NCCN's trial-first language assumes a well-designed trial with characterized safety, and a single-site phase 0/2 with no published BGB-58067 safety is not the archetype that language was drafted for. All three dissents are on rank order, not on inclusion — every persona ranked the trial somewhere in their top eight. The synthesis ranks it 3 because the trial preserves the Stupp backbone inside its arm design, the biomarker fit is exact, the brain-penetrant chemistry is the engineered answer to the TNG908 failure mode, and the user's preference file named the PRMT5 class by molecule. The counter-productive-mechanism severity is Moderate because the dissent is mechanism-grounded (insufficient CNS exposure was the class's recurring failure).

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Single US site at Ivy Brain Tumor Center / St Joseph's Hospital, Phoenix (Nader Sanai, PI). Email research@ivybraintumorcenter.org or call the Phase 0 Navigator at 602-406-8605 to ask about MTAP-IHC slot availability and current screening capacity in both Arm A and Arm B. The geographic move is the practical hurdle for a non-Arizona patient — Ivy has limited travel-assistance funds; ask the navigator directly. Drug is sponsor-provided through BeOne Medicines (the BeiGene successor; US medical information 1-833-969-2463). MTAP IHC central confirmation and MGMT methylation result must both be available before screening; the rank-1 workup is the gate. The phase 0 re-resection is the feasibility question — subtotal-resection block cellularity and patient tolerance of repeat craniotomy at 66 with ECOG 1 are the screening conversation.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 2 (Stupp + TTFields) is the OS-anchored backbone the entire ranking is built around. Rank 3 (this) is the mechanism-matched trial that preserves that backbone inside its own arm design — the strongest non-RCT case the dossier can construct for the patient's lead actionable feature. Rank 4 (CeTeG conditional) sits below this because it only opens at all in MGMT-methylated tumors, and even then the n=141 / per-protocol / CI-crossing-1.0 profile is weaker than the mechanism-plus-biomarker case here.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference BGB-58067 NCT07485049 (Sanai phase 0/2) No published BGB-specific efficacy; phase 0 SDMA / H-score primary; phase 2 12-mo OS endpoint BGB-58067 CNS-specific tox unpublished NCT07485049 Anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (class proxy) ORR 11% in n=80 heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null tumors; 56% median plasma SDMA reduction at C2D1 G≥3 TRAE 13.8%, discontinuation 2.5%, no treatment-related deaths PMID 39282709 TNG908 (cautionary class precedent) 0/23 evaluable GBM ORR; terminated November 2024 for inadequate CNS exposure Toxicity was not the killer; brain penetration was PMID 38108025

docs.title: Rank 4. CeTeG / NOA-09 — lomustine + TMZ + RT, conditional on MGMT methylated and adequate marrow reserve
docs.text: Conditional on MGMT pyrosequencing returning methylated at the 8-10% cutoff. If unmethylated, this rank falls off entirely.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Herrlinger 2019 Lancet (PMID 31488360, n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label) reported mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, one-sided p=0.049 per-protocol) for CCNU + TMZ + RT vs Stupp in newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM. A 16.7-month median OS gain over standard Stupp in the methylated stratum — the largest published front-line OS signal in IDH-WT GBM.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: High in the MGMT-methylated subset, conditional on the rank-1 pyrosequencing result. The CI precision is the calibration: 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crosses 1.0 on the upper bound, the primary analysis is per-protocol, the one-sided p is 0.049, and the trial is unreplicated at n=141. The critic seat read this as RoB2:Some-leaning-Serious; the consensusite read NCCN's category 2A designation as the collective expert calibration of those same concerns. Both reads are valid. The 48-month median is real and is not a number to quote without the CI caveat.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• G≥3 hematologic AE 41% (CeTeG arm n=63) vs 13% (TMZ-alone n=66). Lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%.
  • At age 66, the cumulative CCNU myelosuppression is the binding constraint — many patients need dose reduction by cycle 3, and platelet recovery becomes dose-rate-limiting by cycles 4-6.
  • No treatment-related deaths in the published cohort.
  • Weekly CBC during the first two cycles, then per protocol; pre-set platelet and ANC thresholds and the CCNU dose-reduction algorithm at consent.

No toxicity vetoes from the preference file are triggered. The conservative-flagged due-diligence is a functional reserve assessment (CGA or modified G8) before committing to six cycles of doublet alkylator.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented on this row. The conservative and critic seats independently flagged the same evidence-quality concerns (open-label, n=141, per-protocol primary, CI crossing 1.0), and the consensusite read the NCCN 2A designation as the collective calibration of those concerns. The four personas who picked it (advocate, conservative, critic, consensusite) all ranked it as a conditional methylated-MGMT play; the risktaker did not pick it but did not contest it. Counter-productive-mechanism severity is Low because the dissent is preference-flavored (toxicity-at-age-66 + evidence-precision), not mechanism-grounded.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCCN CNS v2.2026 category 2A for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS ≥70; EANO 2021 names it as an option in the same population with the explicit hematologic-toxicity caveat. Lomustine (Gleostine, NextSource Biotechnology) is on-label for primary brain tumors; pricing is non-trivial (~$10-20K per cycle list price; generics also available). For uninsured patients, NextSource Cares provides free product when financial-need documentation is approved (877-438-9759). If the patient elects BGB-58067 NCT07485049 Arm B (methylated + RT + TMZ), CeTeG and the trial cannot be run concurrently — the trial protocol does not include CCNU in the backbone, and committing to CeTeG outside the trial forecloses the BGB-58067 slot in Arm B.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below rank 3 (BGB-58067) because the trial-enrollment path has stronger biomarker fit and preserves the Stupp backbone exactly as CeTeG does, with the additional mechanism-axis upside. Above rank 5 (GBM AGILE) because CeTeG has a real OS signal in the methylated stratum while AGILE's current arms do not match MTAP. Conditional on the MGMT result — if unmethylated, this row drops off and the rank slot reverts to the next conditional play.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Lomustine + TMZ + RT (CeTeG) mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, one-sided p=0.049 per-protocol); methylated only G≥3 hematotox 41% vs 13%; lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%; no TRAE deaths PMID 31488360, NCT01149109

docs.title: Rank 5. GBM AGILE adaptive platform (NCT03970447)
docs.text: The strongest multi-site randomized-platform alternative when the Phoenix slot is infeasible.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Multi-site Bayesian adaptive platform with randomized control against current SoC and OS as the primary endpoint. Currently active experimental arms: VT1021 (CD36 / CD47-targeting peptide), troriluzole (glutamate modulator), ADI-PEG 20 (arginine deiminase), AZD1390 (ATM kinase inhibitor + RT, newly diagnosed only), tinostamustine (HDAC + alkylator). Closed arms: regorafenib, paxalisib, VAL-083. Control arm: RT + TMZ / lomustine. The platform itself does not yet have an MTAP-matched arm.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate. Bayesian randomization weights toward better-performing arms over time, and the patient is newly diagnosed eligible regardless of MGMT status. The mechanism-axis weak spot is that none of the active arms targets MTAP or CDKN2A — AZD1390 + RT (the newly-diagnosed-specific arm) and tinostamustine are the most likely assignments by molecular subgroup, both of which are mechanistically reasonable but not biomarker-matched to this patient's lead feature.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text: Toxicity depends entirely on arm assignment. AZD1390 + RT carries CNS toxicity and lymphopenia signal characteristic of ATM inhibitors; tinostamustine carries alkylator-class hematologic AE; VT1021 and ADI-PEG 20 have lower-tox profiles. None triggers any preference-file veto.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented on this row. The advocate and consensusite picked it; the conservative, critic, and risktaker did not pick it but did not contest the framing. The structural argument — multi-site infrastructure addresses the single-site fragility of NCT07485049 — is what the advocate and consensusite both cited.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Multi-site (40+ US sites). Single screening assigns to arm via Bayesian randomization; the patient does not pick. Contact GCAR at 310-598-3199 or patientinfo@gcaresearch.org. Screening is fast. The trial accepts both MGMT branches.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below BGB-58067 (rank 3) because no current AGILE arm is mechanism-matched to MTAP; above SurVaxM (rank 6) because the randomized-platform construct is structurally stronger than the SurVaxM single-arm phase 2a signal. If Phoenix is geographically infeasible or the BGB-58067 slot is taken, this becomes the highest-quality randomized-trial slot available to the patient.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference GBM AGILE platform (current arms) Bayesian-adaptive randomized vs SoC; OS primary; no MTAP-matched arm currently active Varies by arm assignment (AZD1390+RT, tinostamustine, ADI-PEG 20, troriluzole, VT1021) NCT03970447

docs.title: Rank 6. SurVaxM (survivin peptide vaccine) on SURVIVE NCT05163080
docs.text: The lowest-toxicity add-on in the dossier; forces a binary choice against TTFields because SURVIVE excludes concurrent Optune.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Ahluwalia 2023 JCO (PMID 36473145, n=63, single-arm phase 2a, informal:med RoB) reported PFS6 95.2%, mPFS 11.4 mo, mOS 25.9 mo, 2-yr OS 51%, 3-yr OS 41% with SurVaxM + GM-CSF added to adjuvant TMZ post-Stupp. Encouraging vs the historical ~16-mo control but explicitly non-randomized. SURVIVE (NCT05163080) is the randomized phase 2b validation gate — status active not recruiting as of February 2024 verification.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-moderate. The single-arm signal is real but the randomized confirmation is pending. The standout property is safety: zero SurVaxM-attributable G≥3 SAEs in n=63, with injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms dominating the AE profile.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms dominate.
  • Zero SurVaxM-attributable G≥3 SAEs in the published n=63.
  • The toxicity floor here is the lowest of any add-on the dossier surfaces.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented on this row. Only the conservative seat picked it explicitly (at rank 5 of their list). The other personas did not pick it but did not contest the framing. The load-bearing practical conflict is the Optune-incompatibility: the SURVIVE protocol excludes concurrent TTFields. The patient cannot run rank 2 TTFields and SurVaxM together — that is a binary choice, not a layering.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Multi-site US (11 sites) randomized phase 2b. Status changed to active not recruiting as of latest verification — call Roswell Park at 1-800-767-9355 to confirm current screening capacity at any open site. Key eligibility: GBM patient must have completed standard RT + TMZ before vaccination start (i.e. post-Stupp slot, not concurrent), KPS ≥70, dexamethasone ≤4 mg/day, no prior immunotherapy or Optune. If the patient elects this row, the EF-14-anchored TTFields component of rank 2 is foreclosed. Expanded access via MimiVax exists but is more expensive than trial enrollment; pursue NCT05163080 first.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below GBM AGILE (rank 5) because the evidence base is single-arm phase 2a rather than randomized platform; above the conditional / pre-position rows (ranks 7-11) because the safety floor is the lowest in the dossier and the OS signal — while unreplicated — is encouraging. The Optune-incompatibility is the binary-choice conversation that makes this row a true alternative to rank 2 rather than a layering.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference SurVaxM + GM-CSF + adjuvant TMZ (phase 2a) PFS6 95.2%, mPFS 11.4 mo, mOS 25.9 mo, 2-yr OS 51%, 3-yr OS 41% (n=63, single-arm) Injection-site reactions, low-grade flu-like symptoms; zero G≥3 SAE attributable to SurVaxM PMID 36473145 SURVIVE (NCT05163080 phase 2b) Randomized validation gate; readout pending Same expected; randomized phase 2b NCT05163080

docs.title: Rank 7. Tumor-agnostic conditional plays unlocked by the rank-1 NGS panel
docs.text: Recurrence-only and biomarker-conditional. Free options that fall out of the rank-1 NGS bundle at zero marginal cost.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text:
• Dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E (ROAR HGG cohort, Wen 2022 Lancet Oncol — PMID 34838156, n=45 HGG): ORR 33% (95% CI 20-49), mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41%. Tumor-agnostic FDA approval June 2022.
  • Larotrectinib for NTRK fusion (Drilon 2018 NEJM — PMID 29466156, n=55): ORR 75-80%, CNS responses confirmed in Doz 2022. Tumor-agnostic FDA full approval April 2025.
  • Pembrolizumab for TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb (Marabelle 2020 KEYNOTE-158 — PMID 32919526, n=102): ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39). Tumor-agnostic accelerated approval 2020; MSI-H / dMMR full approval March 2023.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low prior probability across all three biomarkers in adult IDH-WT GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK <1%, primary MMR-D / MSI-H uncommon). The expected-value framing only works because the NGS bundle is being ordered at rank 1 anyway. ORR conditional on a positive hit is meaningful: ROAR 33%, larotrectinib 75-80%, pembrolizumab TMB-H 29%.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Dabrafenib + trametinib: pyrexia, rash, fatigue. Well-characterized; manageable on outpatient monitoring.
  • Larotrectinib: transaminitis, dizziness. Well-tolerated.
  • Pembrolizumab: immune-related AE spectrum (thyroiditis, hepatitis, colitis, pneumonitis); baseline TSH, AM cortisol, LFTs.

No toxicity vetoes triggered.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented on this row. The consensusite picked dabrafenib + trametinib, larotrectinib, and pembrolizumab explicitly at ranks 6-7-8 of their list; the risktaker bundled them at rank 4 as "essentially free options." The conservative and critic did not pick them but did not contest the framing — front-line ICI in unselected GBM is closed by CheckMate-498, but biomarker-gated tumor-agnostic ICI at recurrence is guideline-supported.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCCN CNS v2.2026 lists all three on the recurrent / refractory branch when biomarker positive. Cross-society convergence across NCCN, ESMO, ASCO. Order RNA-based fusion testing alongside the standard DNA panel at rank 1 — CNS NTRK breakpoints are often intron-deep and DNA-only panels can miss them. If MMR / MSI returns abnormal on the tumor side, escalate germline Lynch / CMMRD panel and trigger cascade testing of first-degree relatives.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below the SoC backbone (rank 2) and the front-line trial-enrollment options (ranks 3-5) because these are all recurrence-conditional. Above the recurrence pre-positions (ranks 8-12) because the marginal cost of ordering the NGS bundle is zero (it is rank 1) and the upside on a positive hit reframes the second-line tree.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF V600E) ORR 33% (95% CI 20-49), mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41% in HGG cohort (n=45) Pyrexia, rash, fatigue PMID 34838156, NCT02034110 Larotrectinib (NTRK fusion) ORR 75-80% across NTRK-fusion solid tumors (n=55); CNS responses confirmed Transaminitis, dizziness PMID 29466156, NCT02122913 Pembrolizumab (MSI-H / dMMR or TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb) ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) in TMB-H subset of KEYNOTE-158 (n=102) irAE spectrum PMID 32919526, NCT02628067

docs.title: Rank 8. Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) — dedicated recurrent-GBM CNS-penetration trial NCT06883747 (recruiting) plus MountainTAP-5 NCT07492680 (July 2026), with human GBM target engagement and cross-tumor NSCLC activity
docs.text: Post-board evidence-ranked addition, not yet board-voted. The board saw only the MountainTAP-5 July-2026 re-screen note; the updated-workflow re-screen added the dedicated recurrent-GBM CNS-penetration trial and the NSCLC efficacy anchor.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Two things changed since the board deliberated. First, a dedicated recurrent-GBM CNS-penetration trial — NCT06883747, run by Nader Sanai at the Ivy Brain Tumor Center, recruiting now — reported its first PK/PD in GBM tumor tissue at SNO 2025 (doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.1669): a 77% SDMA H-score reduction confirming on-target PRMT5 engagement, and unbound drug at 45.1 nM in Gd-non-enhancing tumor that cleared the prespecified >18 nM (5x IC50) CNS-penetration threshold (plasma 111.3 nM, CSF 54.7 nM, enhancing tumor 269.0 nM). Second, the cross-tumor NSCLC cohort (Jänne, WCLC 2025, n=35 pretreated MTAP-deleted NSCLC — doi:10.1016/j.jtho.2025.09.054) reported ORR 29% (all partial responses), DCR 80%, and mDoR 10.5 mo. Together these answer the two questions the class most needed answered after TNG908 failed on CNS exposure and anvumetostat was discontinued — does the molecule reach brain tumor, and does it drive durable single-agent activity. The MountainTAP-5 basket (NCT07492680, opens July 2026) carries a newly-diagnosed-GBM + TMZ + RT cohort. Class-context efficacy remains the anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 record (PMID 39282709); GBM response on navlimetostat itself is unpublished, and the NSCLC numbers do not transfer to glioma.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate. The molecule now has human GBM proof-of-mechanism — CNS penetration above threshold and target engagement in resected tumor — plus durable activity in another MTAP-null tumor (NSCLC ORR 29%, mDoR 10.5 mo). What it does not have is a GBM efficacy readout: NCT06883747 is a phase 0/1 surgical study measuring drug delivery, not response, and it is recurrence-gated, so the newly-diagnosed patient is not eligible today. The GBM PK/PD signal is n=1 at the 200 mg cohort. Read it as early proof-of-mechanism, not proof-of-benefit.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Cross-tumor safety (all-solid-tumor population, Jänne 2025): G≥3 TRAE 14%, SAE 4%, discontinuation for toxicity 2%, no treatment-related deaths.
  • Hematologic events (anemia 8%, neutropenia 7%, thrombocytopenia 7%) were grade 1-3 — lighter myelosuppression than first-generation PRMT5 inhibitors.
  • The GBM-specific AE table does not exist yet; the phase 0/1 trial had 2 enrolled and 1 post-surgery at the 06/06/25 cutoff, so no toxicity aggregation is possible on the GBM side.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No board dissent, because the board did not vote on this evidence — the endorse pills carry only the advocate and risktaker, the two seats that had already flagged navlimetostat before the re-screen. The counter-productive-mechanism severity drops to Low relative to BGB-58067: the class CNS-exposure failure mode that killed TNG908 is now directly addressed for this molecule, since GBM tumor unbound drug exceeded the 5x-IC50 penetration threshold on the SNO 2025 readout. The honest caution is procedural, not mechanistic — this rec has not been through toxicity or evidence-quality scrutiny from the conservative and critic seats.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: For the actionable-now slot, the gate is recurrence with re-resection candidacy: NCT06883747 requires recurrent disease and a planned operation for the paired-tissue PK, so it enters the recurrence conversation, not the front-line one — contact the Ivy Phase 0 Navigator (602-406-8605) when the patient progresses. For the newly-diagnosed cohort, pin July 2026 and call the BMS Clinical Trials Contact Center (855-907-3286) or email Clinical.Trials@bms.com the week MountainTAP-5 opens. The rank-1 MTAP IHC central confirmation will be in hand for either; check whether the trial's MTAP-confirmation assay matches the SP347-class IHC or needs a central-lab re-stain.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It sits alongside the board-voted BGB-58067 (rank 3) on the same MTAP axis rather than above it, and above monotherapy abemaciclib (rank 10), for two reasons. Against BGB-58067: the navlimetostat GBM data is target-engagement / PD only with no response readout, the actionable-now GBM trial is recurrence-gated, and the newly-diagnosed cohort is a calendar trigger — so despite the newer CNS-penetration proof it does not displace the board-endorsed front-line-compatible option. Against abemaciclib: the MTAP axis is the patient's primary handle and navlimetostat now has human CNS proof-of-mechanism plus cross-tumor efficacy, which the CDK4/6 monotherapy rec does not. The rank is a post-board judgment, not a board vote.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) — recurrent-GBM CNS-penetration (NCT06883747) 77% SDMA H-score reduction (target engagement); unbound tumor drug 45.1 nM above the 18 nM CNS threshold; no GBM response readout No GBM AE table yet (1 patient post-surgery at cutoff) NCT06883747, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.1669 Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) — cross-tumor MTAP-deleted NSCLC ORR 29% (all PR), DCR 80%, mDoR 10.5 mo (n=35) — establishes durable single-agent class activity; does not transfer to GBM G≥3 TRAE 14%, no treatment-related deaths; grade 1-3 anemia/neutropenia/thrombocytopenia doi:10.1016/j.jtho.2025.09.054 Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) — MountainTAP-5 Cohort 4 (+TMZ+RT, newly diagnosed) Not yet recruiting (July 2026); no efficacy; class context anvumetostat ORR 11% Specific tox in escalation; class-context G≥3 TRAE 13.8% NCT07492680, PMID 39282709

docs.title: Rank 9. TNG456 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) +/- abemaciclib on NCT06810544 — the dual-axis, mechanism-complete row hitting both MTAP loss and CDKN2A loss
docs.text: Post-board evidence-ranked addition, not yet board-voted. Surfaced on the updated-workflow re-screen; the board did not deliberate it, so no endorse / dissent / veto pills carry.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: NCT06810544 (Tango Therapeutics, phase 1/2, n=191 planned, recruiting) is the only row in the dossier that targets both of the patient's nominated 9p21 axes at once: TNG456 for the MTAP-loss PRMT5-MTA vulnerability, and the abemaciclib combination arm for the CDKN2A-loss CDK4/6 rationale. The protocol names glioma / GBM as eligible histology and uses RANO 2.0, and IDH-wildtype GBM enters without a RECIST target lesion, so the patient meets the biomarker and response-assessment gates. The evidence backing the molecule is preclinical (Briggs, SNO 2025 DDDR-10 — doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.0647): brain-penetrant, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibition with roughly 55x MTAP-null selectivity and xenograft regressions. Class context for the PRMT5 axis remains the anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 record (PMID 39282709). First patient dosed May 2025; no clinical efficacy or safety has read out.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate on mechanism, unproven in clinic. The dual-axis fit is the strongest on paper in the whole dossier — the preclinical PRMT5i + CDK4/6i convergence (deeper regression than either agent alone in MTAP-null / CDKN2A-null / RB-intact models) is the same synthetic-lethal logic behind the recurrence-time abemaciclib rec at rank 10, but here both halves are delivered in one protocol. What is missing is any human data: no ORR, no PFS, no safety table. A positive RB1 IHC at rank 1 is a prerequisite for the abemaciclib arm to have a rationale.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No human GBM AE table exists yet — first patient dosed May 2025.
  • The abemaciclib arm contributes G≥3 diarrhea, neutropenia, and fatigue characteristic of the CDK4/6 class.
  • Additive myelosuppression of a PRMT5i + CDK4/6i combination is unquantified in GBM; watch this at age 66+.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No board dissent, because the board did not vote on this row — it arrived on the re-screen after deliberation closed. The mechanism-level caution is the class one: Tango discontinued the earlier brain-penetrant TNG908 in GBM after CSF sampling showed inadequate CNS exposure. TNG456 is the successor engineered against that failure mode, but human CNS PK on TNG456 itself is not yet public, which is why the counter-productive severity sits at Moderate.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recurrence-gated: enrollment requires prior progression, so the newly-diagnosed patient is not eligible now — pin it for the recurrence conversation. Confirm RB1 intact on the rank-1 IHC before the abemaciclib arm is on the table. Track the phase 1/2 GBM cohort readout, especially the TNG456 human CNS PK, before treating this as more than mechanism rationale.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below navlimetostat (rank 8), which now has human CNS proof-of-mechanism and cross-tumor efficacy, because TNG456's only evidence is preclinical plus a trial-in-progress. Above monotherapy abemaciclib (rank 10), which the board's critic and consensusite seats declined to rank, because the dual-axis mechanism fit is more complete than abemaciclib alone and it puts both 9p21 handles in a single protocol. The rank is a post-board judgment, not a board vote.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference TNG456 +/- abemaciclib (NCT06810544) No clinical data; preclinical 55x MTAP-null selectivity, xenograft regression; dual-axis MTAP + CDKN2A No human GBM AE table; abemaciclib arm adds G≥3 diarrhea / neutropenia / fatigue NCT06810544, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noaf201.0647

docs.title: Rank 10. Abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor, CNS-penetrant) — recurrence-time pre-position keyed to the 9p21 co-deletion, gated on RB1 functional confirmation
docs.text: Recurrence pre-position; status considered_with_caveats. The critic and consensusite explicitly did NOT rank it; the advocate and risktaker flagged it for the recurrence-time combination conversation.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Wen 2024 NCT02981940 (n=42 recurrent CDKN2A/B-deleted or CDK4/6-amplified with intact RB): PFS6 9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9) on monotherapy, with paired-surgical PK confirming intratumoral concentrations at pharmacologically relevant levels (PMID 37722087). INSIGhT abemaciclib arm (Wen 2023 CCR, n=73): HR_PFS 0.72 (95% CI 0.49-1.06, one-sided p=0.046), no OS benefit; PFS CI crosses 1.0. Palbociclib failure (Taal 2018 — PMID 30151703, n=22, mPFS 1.2 mo, closed early for futility) is the cautionary precedent: palbociclib is a Pgp substrate and does not get to tumor. The combination case (PRMT5 + CDK4/6 at progression) rests on preclinical convergence (Vilgelm 2019; AACR 2025 TNG462 + CDK4/6 data) showing deeper regression than either agent alone in MTAP-null / CDKN2A-null / RB-intact models.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low for monotherapy — PFS6 ~9.7% in recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM defines the activity ceiling. The combination case (CDK4/6i + PRMT5i at progression) is preclinical and untested in clinic. Assuming a positive RB1 IHC at rank 1, the rationale stands; an RB1-loss result forecloses it entirely.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• G≥3 diarrhea characteristic of class; dose-limiting. At age 66, start 150 mg BID rather than the on-label 200 mg BID with close monitoring.
  • Neutropenia, fatigue also characteristic.
  • Manageable with appropriate dose modification; no class veto from the preference file.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The critic and consensusite seats explicitly did NOT rank abemaciclib. The critic dissent is on evidence quality: PFS without OS in INSIGhT, modest monotherapy ceiling in NCT02981940, Taal 2018 palbociclib failure as cautionary precedent. The consensusite dissent is on guideline fit: NCCN Compendium does not currently list GBM as a compendia-supported off-label use, so the medical-exception letter is the route. The advocate and risktaker picked it as a recurrence pre-position; the conservative did not pick. Counter-productive-mechanism severity is Moderate because Pgp efflux at the BBB blunts the CDK4/6 class in CNS — the Taal palbociclib failure is the mechanism-level cautionary precedent, and abemaciclib was selected for partial CNS penetration but intratumoral concentrations are modest (Wen 2024 paired-surgical PK).

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Off-label off-protocol GBM use faces a real payer fight. Document CDKN2A homozygous loss in the chart, prepare a medical-exception letter citing the Tien 2019 ribociclib phase 0 (PMID 31285369) and INSIGhT abemaciclib pharmacodynamic data. Lilly Answers Center (1-800-545-5979) will provide the published off-label medical-information dossier on request. NCT02981940 is closed to accrual; INSIGhT abemaciclib arm is closed. The combination conversation (PRMT5 + CDK4/6) would be a compassionate-use ask the treating center may or may not entertain. RB1 IHC from rank 1 is the eligibility gate.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below the two post-board MTAP-axis additions (ranks 8-9), which carry brain-penetrant molecules with either human CNS proof-of-mechanism or a dual-axis protocol; this row is monotherapy on one axis with a modest ceiling. Above CAN-3110 (rank 11) because the mechanism axis (9p21 co-deletion synthetic lethal) maps exactly to the patient's biology. Honest about the rank: not first-line, monotherapy ceiling modest, combination thesis preclinical.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Abemaciclib monotherapy (recurrent CDKN2A-deleted) PFS6 9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9), n=42; paired-surgical PK confirmed G≥3 diarrhea, neutropenia, fatigue PMID 37722087, NCT02981940 Palbociclib (cautionary precedent) mPFS 1.2 mo, closed early for futility (n=22) Pgp substrate, does not penetrate CNS PMID 30151703

docs.title: Rank 11. CAN-3110 oncolytic HSV-1 — recurrence pre-position; order HSV-1 IgG serology now
docs.text: Recurrence-only; the cheap up-front serology informs the future decision.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Ling 2023 Nature (PMID 37853118) phase 1 in recurrent HGG: single-dose mOS 11.6 mo overall, mOS 14.2 mo in the HSV-1 seropositive subset (~66% of cohort), no DLTs across the full dose range. FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designation for recurrent HGG in 2024.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low overall, moderate in the HSV-1 seropositive subset — the seropositive signal is roughly 2× the historical recurrent-GBM benchmark. The HSV-1 IgG serology is a $20 test; ordering it now informs the prior probability of benefit when the recurrence conversation happens.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No DLTs across the Ling 2023 dose range.
  • Perilesional inflammation from viral lysis is the modal AE.
  • The intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation overlaps with the bleed mechanism — annotate, do not exclude. The Ling 2023 cohort included patients with prior tumor bleeding without prohibitive re-bleed rates.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented. Both the advocate and risktaker flagged this as a recurrence pre-position. The hemorrhage carry-forward is the only nuance, and it is a relative caution rather than an exclusion.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recurrent-only; currently active not recruiting at the Dana-Farber lead site (E. Antonio Chiocca, PI). Order HSV-1 IgG serology this week as part of the workup bundle (cost ~$20, turnaround 1-2 days). Watch for protocol reopening or successor study activation. Intratumoral injection feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy and any second-look surgical plan at recurrence.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below abemaciclib (rank 10) because the recurrence-conditionality is more practical (single dose vs continuous therapy) but the mechanism does not target the patient's specific 9p21 biology. Above FUS-BBB (rank 12) because the published OS signal is stronger and the cohort fit (HSV-1 seropositive subset) is testable now.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference CAN-3110 (rQNestin34.5v.2) intratumoral oncolytic HSV-1 Single-dose mOS 11.6 mo overall; mOS 14.2 mo HSV-1 seropositive subset No DLTs; perilesional inflammation modal AE PMID 37853118, NCT03152318

docs.title: Rank 12. FUS-mediated BBB opening (SonoCloud-9 / SONOBIRD NCT04528680)
docs.text: Recurrence-time delivery-enhancement pre-position; requires re-resection candidacy at trial entry.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Sonabend 2023 Lancet Oncology (PMID 37087102) phase 1 (n=17): 4-6× increased peri-tumoral nab-paclitaxel concentration vs unsonicated brain on the SonoCloud-9 implant, no implant-related deaths, tolerated through 6 cycles. SONOBIRD (NCT04528680) is the phase 3 (n=560, 40 sites US+EU) with IV carboplatin as the partner drug, randomized vs lomustine or TMZ at first recurrence; recruitment expected to complete late 2026.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-moderate. The Sonabend cohort demonstrated drug-concentration enhancement; OS data from SONOBIRD is not yet mature. The bet here is on the delivery mechanism rather than the partner drug's intrinsic activity.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No implant-related deaths in Sonabend 2023.
  • Tolerated through 6 cycles.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented. Only the risktaker picked it explicitly as a recurrence pre-position. BBB opening could theoretically increase off-target CNS exposure of partner cytotoxics, but the Sonabend cohort showed no severe CNS toxicity.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recurrent-only with planned re-resection — not actionable today. The implant decision must be made AT the re-resection operation, not afterward; pre-position the patient at a SONOBIRD US site (Adam Sonabend at Northwestern is the leading published US investigator; Columbia and MD Anderson also enroll) at the first-recurrence resection conversation. Requires surgical candidacy at first progression.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below CAN-3110 (rank 11) because the OS signal is less mature; both are recurrence pre-positions and the patient's first-recurrence surgical candidacy is the gating question for either.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference SonoCloud-9 + IV carboplatin (SONOBIRD) 4-6× peri-tumoral drug concentration enhancement (n=17 phase 1); OS data immature No implant-related deaths; tolerated through 6 cycles PMID 37087102, NCT04528680

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• Front-line bevacizumab (Avastin) — effectively vetoed by 4 of 5 personas. Intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation tightens the risk/benefit (Friedman 2009 BRAIN study reports G≥3 intracranial hemorrhage 2.4% as baseline class rate). AVAglio and RTOG 0825 negative for OS in newly diagnosed; EORTC 26101 (Wick 2017, n=437, RoB2:Low) showed HR_OS 0.95 (95% CI 0.74-1.21, p=0.65) — no OS benefit from bev+CCNU at recurrence. Recurrence-only conversation, after re-imaging and explicit bleeding-risk reassessment.
  • Front-line ICI in unselected GBM (nivolumab, pembrolizumab without biomarker) — universal 5/5 rejection. Closed by CheckMate-498 (HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp, p=0.0037, n=560), CheckMate-548 (no benefit in methylated), NRG-BN007 (futility), CheckMate-143 (no benefit at recurrence). Re-opens only on biomarker gate (rank 7) at recurrence.
  • Front-line EGFRvIII / EGFR-amp CAR-T (MGH CARv3-TEAM-E, UCSF E-SYNC, Penn dual-CAR family) — surfaced at rank 13 with status: not_recommended. Conservative-issued veto stands on hemorrhage-compounded CRS / ICANS edema risk. Recurrence-time conversation re-opens with EGFRvIII positivity and a documented re-bleed surveillance plan.
  • TNG908 (terminated November 2024) — class CNS-failure precedent. 0/23 evaluable GBM ORR; CSF n=3 confirming inadequate brain exposure. Mechanistic informant only.
  • Anvumetostat / AMG 193 (discontinued April 30, 2026) — Amgen ended four phase 1b/2 trials at Q1 2026 earnings call. Mechanistic informant for the MTA-cooperative PRMT5 class; not an active option.
  • TNG462 (peripheral PRMT5 inhibitor; CNS-excluded) — wrong tumor biology for primary GBM. The Tango brain-penetrant successor is TNG456, which the post-board re-screen moved into the ranked list at rank 9 (NCT06810544 now names glioma / GBM and carries the abemaciclib combination arm).
  • IDE397, IDE892, S095035 (MAT2A and MTA-cooperative PRMT5 IDEAYA / Servier programs) — all CNS-excluded by current protocols. IDE892 + IDE397 combination (NCT07277413) is the forward-looking option pending CNS-cohort amendment.
  • DCVax-L expanded access (NCT02146066) — manufacturing window from index resection has closed for this patient. Liau 2023 ROBINS-I:Serious external-control analysis is mechanistic informant only.
  • Palbociclib in GBM — closed door. Taal 2018 mPFS 1.2 mo, futility, Pgp substrate that does not penetrate CNS.
  • Depatux-m (INTELLANCE-1) — negative phase 3 (HR_OS 1.02, 95% CI 0.85-1.23, p=0.63, n=691). EGFR-amplification rationale did not translate to OS.
  • Rindopepimut (ACT IV) — negative phase 3 (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.79-1.30, n=745). EGFRvIII peptide vaccine no benefit.
  • Toca 511 — program discontinued post-TOCA 5 phase 3 negative.
  • Gliadel wafer — moment of decision (index craniotomy without wafer placement) has passed for this patient.

docs.text: Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 1 Diagnostic workup gate — MGMT, MTAP IHC, EGFR/vIII, comprehensive NGS, RB1 IHC endorse: advocate conservative critic concensusite risktaker Diagnostic certainty. Gates the rank-3 MTAP-axis trial enrollment, the rank-4 CeTeG conditional, the rank-13 cellular-therapy pre-position, and every tumor-agnostic conditional rec. Low (none — diagnostic assays on archival FFPE + peripheral blood) N/A (Workup row; no therapeutic mechanism to evaluate.) Six parallel assays on one block of tissue resolve every load-bearing front-line and recurrence-time decision in this case; the RT-start clock argues for sending them all out together this week.

docs.title: Therapeutic options
docs.text:
Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 2 Stupp + TTFields (RT + concurrent/adjuvant TMZ + Optune Gio) endorse: advocate conservative critic concensusite risktaker High — Stupp HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, replicated 5-yr) + EF-14 HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76) layered on TMZ; the 20.9-mo median is the threshold every other rank is measured against. Moderate (G≥3 hematologic 14% adjuvant-phase, lymphopenia under TMZ requiring PJP prophylaxis, scalp dermatitis 52% any grade / 2% G≥3 under arrays) Low (TMZ-induced hypermutation at recurrence can paradoxically open MMR-deficient ICI eligibility — a delayed pro-mechanism effect rather than a true counter-productive one.) The OS-anchored standard the entire ranking is built around; every other rank either layers on this backbone or is measured against it. 3 BGB-58067 on NCT07485049 (Sanai phase 0/2, Ivy/Phoenix) endorse: advocate conservative critic concensusite risktakerdissent: conservative critic concensusite Moderate uncertainty — mechanism-matched at MTAP/CDKN2A with brain-penetrant chemistry but no published BGB-58067 efficacy on the molecule itself; class proxy ORR ~11% in pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null tumors (anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101). Low (class proxy: G≥3 TRAE 13.8%, discontinuation 2.5%, no treatment-related deaths in anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101; BGB-58067 CNS-specific tox unpublished) Moderate (Inadequate CNS exposure was the proximate failure mode of TNG908 — design rationale addresses it but human CSF PK on BGB-58067 itself is not yet public.) The cleanest mechanistic match in the dossier for this patient's 9p21 co-deletion; biomarker fit is exact and the trial preserves the Stupp backbone, but the molecule has no published human efficacy and the class's CNS record is two failures. 4 CeTeG / NOA-09 (lomustine + TMZ + RT) (conditional on MGMT methylated) endorse: advocate conservative critic concensusite High in MGMT-methylated subset — Herrlinger 2019 HR_OS 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03), mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo; CI precision is modest at n=141 and unreplicated. Moderate (G≥3 hematologic 41%: lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%; no treatment-related deaths in CeTeG arm) Low (Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression can foreclose later cytotoxic combinations at recurrence (lomustine + bevacizumab) — a sequencing rather than a counter-productive concern.) The largest published front-line OS signal in MGMT-methylated GBM, conditional on a result the workup row will return; toxicity at age 66 is the binding constraint and the CI is wider than the headline number suggests. 5 GBM AGILE adaptive platform (NCT03970447) endorse: advocate concensusite Moderate — Bayesian randomization against SoC; current arms (AZD1390+RT, tinostamustine, ADI-PEG 20) are not MTAP-matched, so mechanism-axis upside is lower than BGB-58067. Moderate (varies by arm assignment; AZD1390+RT carries CNS toxicity and lymphopenia signal, tinostamustine carries hematologic AE typical of alkylators) Low (Arm randomization can land the patient on a non-mechanism-matched investigational agent — efficiency cost rather than counter-productive mechanism.) The strongest multi-site randomized-platform alternative when the Phoenix slot is infeasible; mechanism axis is weaker than BGB-58067 because no current arm targets MTAP. 6 SurVaxM on SURVIVE NCT05163080 endorse: conservative Low-to-moderate — Ahluwalia 2023 single-arm n=63 reported PFS6 95.2%, mOS 25.9 mo against ~16-mo historical control; SURVIVE phase 2b is the randomized validation gate. Low (injection-site reactions, low-grade flu-like symptoms; zero SurVaxM-attributable G≥3 SAEs in n=63) Low (Vaccine adjuvant immune activation has no established counter-productive mechanism in GBM; the main concern is Optune incompatibility (foregoing EF-14-anchored OS) rather than a mechanism-level risk.) The lowest-toxicity add-on in the dossier with a real but unreplicated single-arm signal; forces a binary choice against TTFields because SURVIVE excludes concurrent Optune. 7 Tumor-agnostic conditional plays (dabrafenib+trametinib, larotrectinib, pembrolizumab) (biomarker-gated) endorse: concensusite risktaker Low prior probability across all three biomarkers in adult IDH-WT GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK <1%, MMR-D uncommon); ORR conditional on a positive hit is ROAR 33%, larotrectinib 75-80%, pembrolizumab TMB-H 29%. Moderate (class AEs by axis; mostly manageable on outpatient monitoring) Low (Each axis is biomarker-selected; mechanism-level risk only arises if a positive call is acted on without confirmation (e.g. NTRK call without RNA-fusion verification).) Free conditional options that fall out of the rank-1 NGS bundle at zero marginal cost; low prior probability across all three but the upside on a positive hit reframes the recurrence-time decision tree. 8 Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) (post-board addition, not board-voted) endorse: advocate risktaker Moderate — human GBM target engagement now shown (SNO 2025: 77% SDMA reduction, unbound drug above CNS threshold) plus cross-tumor NSCLC ORR 29% / mDoR 10.5 mo; GBM efficacy on the molecule unpublished. Low (cross-tumor: G≥3 TRAE 14%, no treatment-related deaths, grade 1-3 anemia/neutropenia/thrombocytopenia; GBM-specific AE table not yet reported) Low (The class CNS-exposure failure mode (TNG908) is now directly addressed — GBM tumor unbound drug exceeded the 5x-IC50 penetration threshold on the SNO 2025 readout.) Post-board addition on the MTAP axis with human GBM proof-of-mechanism (CNS penetration + target engagement) and cross-tumor NSCLC activity, but no GBM efficacy yet and no board vote; actionable-now GBM slot is recurrence-gated. 9 TNG456 +/- abemaciclib (NCT06810544) (post-board addition, not board-voted; dual-axis MTAP + CDKN2A) Moderate mechanistically, unproven clinically — the only dual-axis (MTAP PRMT5 + CDKN2A CDK4/6) row; evidence is preclinical (Briggs SNO 2025: 55x MTAP-null selectivity, xenograft regression) plus a trial-in-progress. Moderate (no human GBM AE table yet; abemaciclib arm contributes G≥3 diarrhea, neutropenia, fatigue; PRMT5i + CDK4/6i additive myelosuppression unquantified) Moderate (TNG908's inadequate-CNS-exposure failure is the class caution; TNG456 is the engineered successor but human CNS PK is not yet public.) The most mechanism-complete option in the dossier — hits both the MTAP and CDKN2A 9p21 axes at once — but evidence is preclinical plus a trial-in-progress, it is recurrence-gated, and it has no board vote. 10 Abemaciclib (CDK4/6i, CNS-penetrant) (recurrence pre-position; gated on RB1 intact) endorse: advocate risktakerdissent: critic concensusite Low for monotherapy (PFS6 ~9.7% recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM, Wen 2024); the combination case (CDK4/6i + PRMT5i) is preclinical and untested in clinic. Moderate (G≥3 diarrhea characteristic of class, neutropenia, fatigue; at age 66 start at 150 mg BID rather than on-label 200 mg BID) Moderate (Pgp efflux at the BBB blunts the CDK4/6 class in CNS (Taal palbociclib failure); abemaciclib was selected for partial CNS penetration but intratumoral concentrations are modest.) Recurrence-time pre-position keyed to the patient's exact 9p21 co-deletion biology; monotherapy ceiling is modest and the combination thesis is preclinical, so the rank is honest about the evidence gap. 11 CAN-3110 oncolytic HSV-1 (recurrence pre-position; order HSV-1 IgG now) endorse: advocate risktaker Low overall, moderate in HSV-1 seropositive subset — Ling 2023 single-dose mOS 11.6 mo overall, 14.2 mo seropositive vs ~9 mo historical recurrent-GBM benchmark. Low (no DLTs across the Ling 2023 dose range; perilesional inflammation is the modal AE) Low (Perilesional inflammation from viral lysis could re-bleed in a pre-bled brain — a hemorrhage-history-specific relative caution rather than a class-level counter-productive mechanism.) Recurrence-time pre-position with a cheap up-front serology that doubles the prior probability of benefit; hemorrhage history is a relative caution not an exclusion. 12 FUS-BBB opening (SonoCloud-9 / SONOBIRD NCT04528680) (recurrence pre-position) endorse: risktaker Low-to-moderate — Sonabend 2023 (n=17) demonstrated 4-6× peri-tumoral drug concentration enhancement; SONOBIRD OS data not yet mature. Low (no implant-related deaths in Sonabend 2023; tolerated through 6 cycles) Low (BBB opening could theoretically increase off-target CNS exposure of partner cytotoxics, but the Sonabend cohort showed no implant-related deaths or severe CNS toxicity.) Recurrence-time delivery-enhancement pre-position; requires pre-screening at a SONOBIRD US site at the first-recurrence resection conversation. 13 Front-line EGFRvIII / EGFR-amp CAR-T (NOT recommended in this patient) endorse: risktakerdissent: advocate critic concensusiteveto: conservative Hypothesis-generating only — Choi 2024 n=3 transient signal with 2/3 progressing inside two months; class signal is single-digit-n single-arm with no OS validation. High (Bagley 2024 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity, Goff 2019 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells, hemorrhage-compounded edema risk in this patient) High (CRS / ICANS-mediated cerebral edema on a pre-bled brain is the conservative-flagged mechanism-level risk; no phase 1 cohort specifically addresses re-bleed risk under cellular-therapy inflammation.) Front-line CAR-T is not recommended in this patient — conservative veto stands on hemorrhage-compounded CRS / ICANS edema risk that the published phase 1 cohorts do not address. Recurrence-time conversation re-opens with EGFRvIII positivity and a hemorrhage-aware re-bleed surveillance plan.

Reading the table

Toxicity burden (column 4) is patient-level AE severity drawn from the cited evidence anchors. Counter-productive MoA (column 5) is mechanism-level risk to the therapeutic goal — distinct from patient AEs. Severity is Low / Moderate / High / N/A per the schema rule, with the description naming the specific mechanism-level risk. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal — endorse / dissent / veto — and the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. Stupp 2005 / 2009 (RoB2:Low) and Perry 2017 (RoB2:Low) are the only RoB2:Low phase 3 evidence at front-line; EF-14 is RoB2:Some (open-label by modality), CeTeG is RoB2:Some leaning Serious (n=141, per-protocol primary, CI crosses 1.0). BGB-58067 has no peer-reviewed phase 1 published; the class proxy is anvumetostat (program discontinued April 30, 2026) and TNG908 (terminated November 2024). The rank-8 navlimetostat data is conference-abstract only (SNO 2025 GBM PK/PD is n=1; WCLC 2025 NSCLC ORR is a 35-patient cross-tumor cohort), and the rank-9 TNG456 evidence is preclinical plus a trial-in-progress with no clinical readout. All recurrence pre-positions (navlimetostat GBM slot, TNG456, CAN-3110, FUS-BBB, abemaciclib) rest on single-arm, n<50, or pre-clinical data.
  • Post-board additions (ranks 8-9). Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) and TNG456 + abemaciclib entered the ranking on a lighter re-run of the trial screen after the board had closed deliberation. Their endorse / dissent / veto pills reflect only what the board said before the re-screen — no board endorsement or veto was fabricated for them — and both carry considered_with_caveats pending a full board re-vote. The toxicity and evidence-quality seats (conservative, critic) have not scrutinized the new CNS-penetration, NSCLC, or dual-axis evidence.
  • Compartment / biomarker dependencies. Rank 3 (BGB-58067) is hard-gated on central MTAP IHC by an assay the protocol accepts. Rank 4 (CeTeG) only opens if MGMT pyrosequencing returns methylated. Rank 7 conditional axes only activate on a positive biomarker result. Ranks 8-9 (navlimetostat NCT06883747, TNG456 NCT06810544) are recurrence-gated — both require documented progression, so neither is actionable at the current newly-diagnosed timepoint; the navlimetostat MountainTAP-5 newly-diagnosed cohort is a July-2026 calendar trigger. Rank 9's abemaciclib arm and rank 10 (abemaciclib monotherapy) require RB1 intact on IHC. Rank 13 cellular-therapy menu requires EGFRvIII positivity AND (for E-SYNC Cohort 1 newly diagnosed front-line) MGMT unmethylated.
  • Hemorrhage carry-forward. Front-line bevacizumab is foreclosed by 4/5 personas. Front-line CAR-T is vetoed by the conservative seat on hemorrhage-compounded CRS / ICANS edema risk; the veto lift trigger is an E-SYNC Cohort 1 safety analysis that includes pre-bled patients with documented re-bleed surveillance. CAN-3110 carries a hemorrhage-relative caution (annotate, do not exclude). All other ranked rows are hemorrhage-neutral.
  • What would change the ranking.
    • Sanai's phase 0 BGB-58067 PD / safety readout publishes. Lifts the conservative and critic dissents on rank 3; could move BGB-58067 above CeTeG in the methylated branch or even alongside Stupp + TTFields in the unmethylated branch.
    • MGMT returns unmethylated. Drops rank 4 (CeTeG) entirely; strengthens the case for rank 3 (BGB-58067 Arm A) and opens the TMZ-sparing conversation as a legitimate substitute for the adjuvant TMZ component of rank 2.
    • MTAP IHC returns intact despite the NGS-level loss call (the MTAPESTRY-101 false-positive scenario). Drops rank 3 entirely; rank 5 (GBM AGILE) inherits the trial-enrollment slot.
    • EGFRvIII returns positive AND MGMT unmethylated. Re-opens the rank 13 conversation conditional on the conservative veto lift trigger; if E-SYNC Cohort 1 has published a hemorrhage-aware safety analysis by then, the row moves up the recurrence-pre-position list.
    • BRAF V600E or NTRK or MSI-H returns positive on the rank 1 NGS. Activates the corresponding rank 7 axis as a recurrence-time first move.
    • The board re-votes ranks 8-9 on the new evidence. A full board pass over the navlimetostat CNS-penetration + NSCLC data and the TNG456 dual-axis protocol could move either up (if the CNS proof-of-mechanism and cross-tumor activity persuade the conservative and critic seats) or clarify a toxicity caveat that the current post-board placement has not stress-tested.
    • Navlimetostat publishes a GBM efficacy readout, or TNG456 reports its first GBM cohort. Either would convert a proof-of-mechanism / preclinical rec into an efficacy-anchored one and could reorder ranks 3, 8, and 9 on the MTAP axis.
  • Re-scoping caveat. If performance status declines between resection and RT planning, swap rank 2 to Perry CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated (40 Gy / 15 fx + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ). If the patient declines the ≥18 hr/day Optune wear-time commitment, drop the TTFields component of rank 2 (the regimen stays on TMZ alone). If the patient prefers a randomized-platform slot over a single-arm phase 0/2 (e.g. randomization-anxiety preference), swap rank 3 to rank 5 (GBM AGILE).

docs.title: Run log
docs.text:
Authored 2026-05-26 by the PI agent from data/cases/gbm-mtap-cdkn2a-idhwt-subtotal-c4bq/: profile.json (66F newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM, post-subtotal resection, intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation, MTAP + CDKN2A confirmed, MGMT and broader NGS pending), preferences.json (efficacy 0.7, no toxicity vetoes, prefers_trials true, "surface all possible options" with explicit MTAP / CDKN2A class naming in the free-text), target_validation.jsonl (11 rows, 4 essential gates_intervention), trials.jsonl (42 rows), clinical_evidence.jsonl (37 rows), preclinical_evidence.jsonl (42 rows), accessibility.jsonl (40 rows; key access updates: anvumetostat / AMG 193 program discontinued by Amgen 2026-04-30, TNG908 terminated 2024-11, BGB-58067 still recruiting at Ivy / Phoenix NCT07485049, DCVax-L expanded access closed for this patient because the index-resection manufacturing window has elapsed), and board files (5 positions, 20 cross-critiques). Inferred: the consolidation of the four essential target-validation gates into a single rank-1 workup row; the rank ordering on BGB-58067 at 3 rather than 1 (advocate / risktaker view) or 5 (critic view), reflecting the synthesis judgment that the trial preserves the Stupp backbone and the biomarker fit is exact while the published-BGB-58067-evidence gap is real; the rank-12 surfacing of CAR-T as not_recommended at front-line per the universal-veto-with-documented-reasoning rule; the documentation of the conservative veto lift conditions (Sanai phase 0 readout for BGB-58067; E-SYNC Cohort 1 hemorrhage-aware safety analysis for cellular therapy).

PI-refresh on 2026-07-09 (lighter re-run, no board re-vote): the trial screen added six on-axis PRMT5-MTA / MAT2A trials and the clinician added seven clinical-evidence rows on the updated workflow. Two options were material and are folded in as post-board, evidence-ranked additions marked considered_with_caveats and flagged pending board review. Rank 8 was rewritten from a MountainTAP-5-only calendar note into the full navlimetostat (BMS-986504) program, incorporating the dedicated recurrent-GBM CNS-penetration trial NCT06883747 (recruiting; SNO 2025 target engagement 77% SDMA reduction and supra-threshold unbound tumor drug) plus the cross-tumor NSCLC efficacy anchor (WCLC 2025, ORR 29%, mDoR 10.5 mo). A new rank 9 adds TNG456 +/- abemaciclib on NCT06810544 — the only dual-axis MTAP + CDKN2A row, preclinical plus trial-in-progress. Ranks 9-12 renumbered to 10-13; abemaciclib, CAN-3110, FUS-BBB, and front-line CAR-T shifted down one, with all cross-references updated. Board-derived rows 1-7 and their agreement scores were left intact; no board endorse / dissent / veto was fabricated for the two additions. Reference-checked: the two new NCTs and three new DOIs were verified against ClinicalTrials.gov and CrossRef and all resolve to the papers/trials cited; the stale PMID 38108025 in the intervention-grouping line (it resolved to an unrelated psychoneuroendocrinology paper, a pre-existing drift not introduced by this refresh) was dropped from that line. The 13 rows re-validated against scripts/schema/recommendations.schema.json. Next steps: run /translator gbm-mtap-cdkn2a-idhwt-subtotal-c4bq, then bash scripts/run_case.sh gbm-mtap-cdkn2a-idhwt-subtotal-c4bq.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Entries are ordered to match the Recommendations table: by therapeutic target group, then by rank within each group. The number in the first column links to the per-intervention section further down the page.

#InterventionTargetAccess statusRegulatoryRecommended first action 1GBM AGILE — adaptive platform trial (multi-arm)Idhwt Gbm BackboneClinical trialMultiple investigational arms; standard-of-care control arm. Platform run by Global Coalition for Adaptive Research (GCAR).Call GCAR patient info at 310-598-3199 or email patientinfo@gcaresearch.org to identify the nearest GBM AGILE site to the patient. 2SurVaxM — survivin peptide vaccineIdhwt Gbm BackboneClinical trialInvestigational; no approval. Candel Therapeutics.File CAN-3110 in the post-progression plan, not the front-line plan. No US device approval.File FUS-BBB programs in the post-progression plan. 5BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor)Mtap LossClinical trialIND-cleared; no approval. Investigational only.Email research@ivybraintumorcenter.org or call the Phase 0 Navigator at 602-406-8605 to ask about MTAP-IHC slot availability and current screening capacity in both Arm A and Arm B. 6Abemaciclib (Verzenio) — CDK4/6 inhibitorCDKN2A-loss / MTAP-targetingOff-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved (2017) for HR+/HER2- advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant, and for adjuvant treatment of HR+/HER2-, node-positive, high-risk early breast cancer. No GBM indication.Discuss abemaciclib off-label with the neuro-oncologist; if the team is interested, document CDKN2A homozygous loss in the chart and prepare a medical-exception letter citing the Tien 2019 ribociclib phase 0 and the INSIGhT abemaciclib pharmacodynamic data. 7CARv3-TEAM-E (MGH — CAR T secreting EGFR x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager)Egfr ViiiClinical trialInvestigational. EMA: not approved for GBM (the EU approval was withdrawn). Not worth pursuing as a stand-alone option. 13DCVax-L — autologous dendritic-cell vaccine pulsed with tumor lysate—Clinical trial Expanded access programInvestigational in the US (no BLA filed). UK MHRA Marketing Authorization Application submitted December 2023 under 150-day fast-track review for unmet medical needs; decision expected late 2025 / early 2026. EMA not yet filed.Email marnix@nwbio.com to confirm there is no new-patient enrollment route through the existing US protocols. Do NOT raise the patient's hopes about DCVax-L until that confirmation is in hand. 14DNX-2401 (tasadenoturev / Delta-24-RGD) — oncolytic adenovirus—Clinical trialInvestigational.
