docs.title: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on Sanai phase 0/2, MGMT-stratified (NCT07485049) (bgb-58067)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1moderateThe bar is 21-month median OS on Stupp + TTFields. The upside scenario here is a mechanism-matched first-in-disease shot at the patient's lead actionable axis layered onto the Stupp spine, with a phase 0 SDMA / H-score readout that confirms target engagement before phase 2 commits, and MGMT branching baked into arm assignment. Class evidence is thin and I will name it: anvumetostat (AMG 193) MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, Cancer Discovery 2025, n=80) gave ORR ~11% across all-comer heavily pre-treated MTAP-null patients with G>=3 TRAE 13.8% and discontinuation 2.5% (cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record) and 56% C2D1 plasma SDMA reduction, but BGB-58067 has no peer-reviewed efficacy or CNS-tox readout yet and TNG908 already failed the GBM cohort 0/23 ORR because brain Kp,uu didn't translate from rodent to human CSF. The bet is that BGB-58067's CNS-exposure-engineered design carries the MTA-cooperative selectivity into tumor at concentrations the prior generation couldn't reach; if it does, this is the only brain-penetrant MTAP-selective PRMT5 inhibitor with a newly-diagnosed GBM protocol enrolling today and the highest-effect-size mechanism-matched play available to the patient.No published BGB-58067 phase 1 safety data; class evidence is anvumetostat-derived and the CNS-specific tox profile is unknown. TNG908 termination is the cautionary precedent — brain penetrance was the killer, not toxicity.; Phase 0 demands a second resection. Subtotal-resection block + intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation means pathology has to confirm tumor cellularity for the SDMA / H-score readout; if cellularity is poor the phase 0 slot folds.; Single US site at Ivy/Phoenix. Travel and lodging cost is on the patient — Ivy has limited assistance funds, ask the navigator (602-406-8605).; Eligibility gated on central MTAP IHC (mandatory after the AMG 193 4-of-6 local-CDKN2A-call false-positive episode) and MGMT methylation status for arm assignment. conservative3moderateTrial-territory pick, ranked third because it is the single best mechanistic match for this patient's MTAP-loss + CDKN2A-loss biology AND it is built on the Stupp backbone rather than replacing it. The phase 0/2 design (Sanai/Ivy) stratifies by MGMT methylation — which is exactly the branching question we have to answer anyway — and uses an SDMA pharmacodynamic readout on phase 0 re-resection tissue to confirm target engagement before phase 2. The class evidence base is shallow but informative: anvumetostat (AMG 193) in Rodon 2024 AnnOnc / Rodon 2025 Cancer Discovery (MTAPESTRY 101, n=80, informal:med RoB) demonstrated G>=3 TRAE 13.8% with treatment discontinuation 2.5% and 56% plasma SDMA reduction at C2D1 — favorable for the class, although ORR was modest at 11% across MTAP-null tumors. I have to name the missing safety datum here clearly: BGB-58067 itself has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 yet, the AnnOnc 2024 row is the closest class proxy, and CNS-exposure-related toxicity from a brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor specifically is uncharacterized. The TNG908 failure (n=23 evaluable GBM patients, 0% ORR, terminated for business reasons after CSF sampling showed inadequate brain exposure) is the cautionary precedent — toxicity wasn't the killer, brain penetration was — and BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS exposure modeling, which is the design rationale that makes this trial worth the Phoenix travel and the phase 0 re-biopsy. Anvumetostat is off the table after Amgen's April 30, 2026 program-wide discontinuation; TNG908 is terminated; DCVax-L expanded access does not accept new patients post-resection because the manufacturing window from initial surgery has closed. Among the open MTAP-PRMT5 trials, BGB-58067 in Phoenix is the front-line GBM-specific option. Rank-3 reflects: layering on top of SoC rather than replacing it, biomarker-strict eligibility that already aligns with our diagnostic gates, sponsor-provided drug, and acceptable distance from the user's preferences once travel feasibility is verified. Travel to Phoenix and a willingness to undergo phase 0 re-resection are the practical gates.BGB-58067 has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety data yet — class evidence comes from anvumetostat, which is a different molecule from a different sponsor; CNS-specific tox profile is the missing datum; Phase 0 requires a second resection — feasibility hinges on whether the patient's residual disease anatomy and her tolerance for repeat craniotomy permit it; Single-site at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix — geographic move is a real burden for a non-Arizona patient; Requires MTAP IHC on resection tissue (mandatory after the AMG 193 four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call episode), plus MGMT status to assign Arm A vs Arm B — both gates need to clear before screening calls critic5lowI am surfacing this rather than recommending it. The synthetic-lethality rationale from Kryukov/Mavrakis/Marjon 2016 is mechanistically robust. The clinical evidence for the MTA-cooperative class is not. Anvumetostat (AMG 193) MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon 2024 AnnOnc, n=80, informal:med RoB) gave ORR 11% in a heavily-pretreated all-comer MTAP-null cohort and was discontinued program-wide by Amgen on April 30, 2026. TNG908 was terminated in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling in n=3 confirmed inadequate CNS exposure, with 0/23 ORR in evaluable GBM. That leaves BGB-58067 as the sole brain-penetrant clinical-stage MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor with an active GBM-specific trial — and the published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety for BGB-58067 specifically does not yet exist. The trial is single-site (Phoenix), single-sponsor, single-arm phase 0/2 with SDMA pharmacodynamic readout. That is the lowest evidence tier I will entertain at all, and only because: (a) the trial layers on the Stupp backbone rather than replacing it (Arm A unmethylated = drug + RT; Arm B methylated = drug + RT + TMZ), so it does not foreclose SoC; (b) MGMT stratification is baked into the design; (c) the patient has MTAP loss confirmed and CDKN2A loss confirmed, which are the gating biomarkers. I am NOT willing to rank this above the Stupp + TTFields backbone, and I would dissent vigorously against any presentation that uses anvumetostat's 11% ORR as a positive signal for BGB-58067 — that ORR was in heavily-pretreated solid tumors, not first-line GBM, and the program is dead. Cross-tumor translation from a discontinued drug is not evidence for a different molecule. The case for trying is mechanism + brain penetration + biomarker fit + SoC-preserving design; the case against is no peer-reviewed efficacy data for this drug, single-site enrollment, and a class with two recent failures.No peer-reviewed phase 1 safety or efficacy data published for BGB-58067 specifically. The class proxy (anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101) showed ORR 11% in heavily-pretreated MTAP-null solid tumors, not GBM, and Amgen discontinued anvumetostat program-wide on April 30, 2026.; TNG908 terminated November 2024 because of inadequate CNS exposure (CSF n=3, 0/23 GBM ORR). The class's track record in CNS is two failures (TNG908, anvumetostat) and one open-label single-site phase 0/2. BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS exposure modeling, which is the design rationale, but the CSF exposure data for BGB-58067 itself has not been published peer-reviewed.; Single-site, single-arm, single-sponsor phase 0/2. Eligibility requires central MTAP IHC (necessary after the AMG 193 four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call episode) and willingness to undergo phase 0 re-resection for SDMA pharmacodynamic readout. Phoenix travel is a real burden.; Mechanistic plausibility plus brain-penetrant chemistry plus biomarker match is the strongest non-RCT case I can construct for a phase 0/2 enrollment. It is still not evidence in the sense I usually demand. Open for the patient to consider; not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC. concensusite3highTrial enrollment IS the guideline-aligned move here. NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 lists clinical trial enrollment as the preferred recommendation across every GBM treatment pathway, ahead of any specific systemic regimen at the same evidence level. EANO 2021 and the ESMO Weller 2021 update echo this — every major adult glioma guideline names enrollment in well-designed clinical trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM given the disease's prognosis. The trial-pick that is most defensible inside that framing is NCT07485049: a phase 0/2 built on the Stupp backbone (Arm A adds BGB-58067 to RT for unmethylated; Arm B adds it to RT + TMZ for methylated), which means trial enrollment here does NOT substitute for the category 1 SoC. It LAYERS on it. The MTAP-loss biology — patient's lead actionable feature — is the mechanistic gate, but I want to flag clearly: guidelines have NOT yet incorporated MTAP loss into any treatment-decision algorithm for GBM. The MTAP rationale is a research hypothesis. The PI should frame it that way to the patient.MTAP loss is not a guideline-endorsed treatment-decision variable in any current NCCN/ESMO/EANO version. The mechanistic case is biologically plausible but the clinical evidence base is anvumetostat ORR ~11% in heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null disease (Rodon AnnOnc 2024) and zero published efficacy on BGB-58067 itself. Inform consent has to be honest about this.; Phase 0 component requires a re-resection biopsy for SDMA / H-score readout; feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy after subtotal resection and willingness to undergo a second craniotomy.; Single US site at Ivy/Phoenix — geographic move is real. Travel is the practical limiter, not a guideline issue.; The Stupp backbone is preserved in the trial design, so this satisfies the guideline-aligned 'enroll in a trial, on top of SoC' framing rather than substituting for it. That is the read I would offer the patient. advocate1highThis is the trial the patient's preference file was written for. The free-text says "surface all possible options" with efficacy lean 0.7 and prefers_trials true, and the single best-mechanism-matched trial currently recruiting for newly diagnosed MTAP-null IDH-wildtype GBM is the Sanai phase 0/2 at Ivy/Phoenix. MGMT stratification is baked into the design (Arm A unmethylated = BGB-58067 + RT; Arm B methylated = BGB-58067 + RT + TMZ), which means the trial slot also resolves the unmethylated-vs-methylated branching decision the team has to make anyway. Anvumetostat's MTAPESTRY-101 readout (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, Cancer Discovery 2025) gives the class an ORR ~11% in a heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null cohort with grade >=3 TRAE 13.8% and discontinuation 2.5% (cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record so far), but BGB-58067 is the asset built for CNS exposure after TNG908 was discontinued in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling confirmed inadequate brain exposure. No toxicity veto in the preference file. The honest weak spot is geographic: this is a single US site in Phoenix and the patient will need to travel.Eligibility gated on MTAP IHC on the resection block (target_validation essential row) and willingness to undergo a phase 0 re-resection biopsy for SDMA / H-score readout; the subtotal-resection block may have enough tumor cellularity but the intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation could have compromised that, so pathology has to confirm before counting on the Phase 0 slot.; Geographic move to Phoenix is the practical hurdle. No modality constraint in the preferences file blocks travel, but it is a real logistic.; Trial-first preference fully satisfied; efficacy lean honored by mechanism-matched targeted therapy with a brain-penetrant agent; no toxicity vetoes triggered; intratumoral-hemorrhage history is not a contraindication on this trial.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocateconservativedissentpreference_fitRanking BGB-58067 at 3 reads past two preference axes at once. The free-text asks the board to surface options keyed specifically to MTAP loss and CDKN2A loss, prefers_trials is true, and efficacy weight sits at 0.7 — that is a patient who has explicitly asked for the mechanism-matched trial slot to lead, not the regimen that has been on the books since 2005. The conservative rationale ("I will not abandon Stupp + TTFields backbone for a phase 1 PRMT5 signal regardless of how mechanistically clean the MTAP rationale looks") rebuts an argument no one is making: NCT07485049 Arm A is BGB-58067 PLUS RT and Arm B is BGB-58067 PLUS RT PLUS TMZ. The Stupp spine is preserved inside the trial. Demoting it three slots on a backbone-replacement worry the protocol does not raise reads the preference file too thin. advocateconcensusitedissentpreference_fitThe consensusite notes section says it directly: "every major guideline names enrollment in well-designed clinical trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM." Then ranks the only mechanism-matched currently-recruiting trial in the dossier at 3, behind two SoC rows. That is internally inconsistent. The protocol design (Arm A = drug + RT, Arm B = drug + RT + TMZ, MGMT-stratified) preserves the category 1 spine inside the trial slot — enrollment here does not substitute for SoC, it carries SoC inside it. The patient's prefers_trials=true plus the explicit MTAP-axis framing in the free-text says rank the trial first when the trial preserves the spine. The "trial layers on, rather than substitutes for, the category 1 spine" reasoning the consensusite gave for the rank-3 placement is the argument FOR rank 1, not for rank 3. advocatecriticdissentpreference_fitRanking BGB-58067 at 5 on RoB2 grounds for a newly-diagnosed GBM patient whose preference file lists the PRMT5 / MAT2A class by name in the free-text is reading the dossier through the wrong filter. The critic's own framing — "open for the patient to consider; not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC" — describes a rank-1 trial enrollment exactly, because the protocol does not substitute for SoC. The argument against cross-tumor extrapolation from anvumetostat is fair on the efficacy projection and I would not quote 11% ORR as a forward bet either, but the case for enrolling is not the anvumetostat efficacy number, it is (a) mechanism + biomarker fit confirmed, (b) brain-penetrant chemistry engineered against the proximate failure mode of TNG908, (c) Stupp spine preserved, (d) MGMT stratification baked in. The user wrote "surface all possible options" and called out the class by molecule name — RoB2:Low + phase 3 + replicated is the wrong bar for what she asked the board to surface. concensusiteadvocatedissentguideline_fitRanking BGB-58067 at #1 ahead of Stupp+TTFields inverts the NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 hierarchy. Trial enrollment LAYERS onto that backbone, it does not replace it. NCT07485049 was designed exactly that way (Arm A adds BGB-58067 to RT; Arm B adds it to RT + TMZ), so the trial itself preserves SoC even when the rank ordering does not. EANO 2021 (Weller, Nat Rev Clin Oncol) and ESMO 2014/2021 both name the Stupp backbone first for this exact population, then trial enrollment. The advocate's preference-fit framing is fair, but presenting BGB-58067 above the category 1 spine reads as substitution rather than addition, and MTAP loss is not yet a guideline-endorsed treatment-decision variable in any NCCN/ESMO/EANO version. I support the enrollment; I dissent on the rank. concensusiteconservativequalifiedguideline_fitLargely aligned on the SoC spine — the conservative #1 (Stupp + TTFields) matches mine, and the CeTeG #2 conditional on MGMT methylated matches mine. Two pushes. First, the conservative ranked BGB-58067 at #3 with 'moderate' confidence and framed it as preserved-on-trial enrollment, which is right, but the NCCN v2.2025 trial-enrollment language is stronger than the conservative writeup credits — every major guideline (NCCN, EANO 2021, ESMO) names enrollment in well-designed trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM, not as a research-grade aside. The conservative posture risks under-weighting that endorsement. Second, the deliberate non-ranking of front-line CAR-T is defensible — NCCN v2.2025 does not endorse front-line cellular therapy in GBM at any evidence category — but the case is unusual enough (MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion, IDH-WT, intratumoral hemorrhage) that the conservative could have ranked E-SYNC Cohort 1 (NCT06186401, newly diagnosed unmethylated MGMT) as a conditional on EGFRvIII positivity rather than excluding it entirely. The phase 1 data (Choi NEJM 2024 n=3, Bagley NatMed 2024 n=6) does not clear category 2A by any guideline read, so the conservative's omission is guideline-fit-correct; the qualified piece is that the patient's preference file explicitly asks for the full menu, and a conditional EGFRvIII pre-position is what NCCN's trial-enrollment language opens space for. criticadvocatedissentevidence_qualityThe advocate justifies rank 1 by writing that MTAPESTRY-101 "gives the class an ORR ~11% in a heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null cohort... but BGB-58067 is the asset built for CNS exposure." That sentence is doing two things the evidence does not support. First, an 11% ORR in heavily pre-treated solid tumors (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, n=80, informal:med RoB) is not a forward bet for newly diagnosed GBM, and Amgen discontinued the anvumetostat program on April 30, 2026 — the closest molecular relative is dead. Second, BGB-58067 itself has no peer-reviewed phase 1 safety or efficacy publication, no CSF PK readout in human GBM. The class's CNS clinical record is TNG908 terminated November 2024 (0/23 evaluable GBM, CSF n=3 confirming inadequate brain exposure) and anvumetostat discontinued. Ranking a single-site, single-arm, single-sponsor phase 0/2 with no BGB-specific clinical data above Stupp (HR_OS 0.63, 95% CI 0.52-0.75, RoB2:Low, replicated at five years) inverts the evidence weighting. Mechanism plus brain-penetrant chemistry is the design rationale. It is not a clinical signal. The honest framing for the patient is "open phase 0/2 slot at a high-volume center, no efficacy data yet" rather than rank 1. criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityPicks 1, 2, 4 align with mine and I co-sign the refusals — front-line bevacizumab (intratumoral-hemorrhage carry-forward plus EORTC 26101 HR_OS 0.95, 95% CI 0.74-1.21 with no OS benefit) and front-line EGFRvIII CAR-T (phase 1 signals at O'Rourke n=10, Bagley n=6, Choi n=3, Goff n=18 with one treatment-related death; none address re-bleed risk in a pre-bled brain) both belong off the front-line list. The narrower disagreement is rank 3 itself. The conservative writes that BGB-58067 "has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety data yet," that the trial is "single-site at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix," and that CNS-specific tox is "the missing datum." Those are reasons to rank below CeTeG and Perry hypofractionated, not above them. I parked BGB-58067 at 5 for the same reasons the conservative rationale names. At rank 3 the regimen sits above two RoB2:Low phase 3 evidence rows (Perry 2017, Herrlinger 2019 with its own bias caveats) on a mechanistic prior that has lost twice in CNS already. risktakeradvocatequalifiedevidence_qualityAligned on BGB-58067 at rank 1 and on the MTAP-PRMT5 framing. Where the advocate seat under-shot: EGFRvIII CAR-T sits at no rank at all, while E-SYNC Cohort 1 (nct:NCT06186401) is a front-line slot for unmethylated MGMT and Choi pmid:38477966 hit 3/3 transient near-complete radiographic regression in newly diagnosed disease. Pre-positioning CAN-3110 at rank 7 and abemaciclib at rank 6 while cellular therapy stays invisible inverts the effect-size priority in a dossier whose free-text says surface all options. risktakercriticdissentevidence_qualityTargeting the critic's rank 5 BGB-58067 rather than rank 1 because rank 5 is where the RoB2 bar most punishes the patient. The standard applied here, peer-reviewed phase 1 on the specific molecule plus replicated phase 3 plus RoB2:Low, would have excluded pembrolizumab in 2014, larotrectinib in 2018, and tisagenlecleucel in 2017 from any ranked list at first-in-class. At what CI width does the critic accept an intervention for a disease where 5-yr OS sits below 10% and no curative SoC exists? Mechanism + biomarker fit + brain-penetrant chemistry + Stupp-backbone-preserving trial design (nct:NCT07485049) is the strongest non-RCT case anyone is going to construct in adult IDH-WT GBM. conservativeadvocatedissenttoxicityThe advocate's rank-1 placement reads "surface all possible options" as if it said "rank a phase 0/2 first." Those are different instructions. The rationale itself concedes BGB-58067 has "no published efficacy readout for BGB-58067 yet" and leans on anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (ORR 11%, G>=3 TRAE 13.8%) as the class proxy. Anvumetostat is a different molecule from a different sponsor, studied in heavily pre-treated solid tumors not GBM, and Amgen discontinued the program on April 30, 2026 across four phase 1b/2 trials. TNG908 was terminated November 2024 with 0/23 GBM ORR. The missing safety datum I will name specifically: BGB-58067's CNS-specific tox profile in humans is unpublished. Stupp HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75) replicated at 5 years (9.8% vs 1.9% OS), layered with EF-14 HR 0.63 (mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo), is the floor every other regimen has to beat. NCT07485049 belongs on the option menu. Above the only OS-validated regimen in front-line GBM, it does not. Dissent contingent on the absence of peer-reviewed BGB-58067 phase 1 CSF exposure and AE data. If Sanai publishes the phase 0 PD/safety readout, this lifts to qualified. conservativeconcensusitequalifiedtoxicityThe Stupp/TTFields/CeTeG hierarchy at picks 1-2-4 matches mine and the consensus pyramid lands here. The rank-3 placement of BGB-58067 under a "trial enrollment IS the guideline-aligned move here" framing carries an asymmetry the comment understates. NCCN's trial-first language assumes a well-designed clinical trial with characterized safety. A single-site single-arm phase 0/2 with zero published BGB-58067 safety data is not the trial archetype that language was drafted for. The consensusite rationale honestly flags that "guidelines have NOT yet incorporated MTAP loss into any treatment-decision algorithm for GBM" and that the MTAP-PRMT5 axis is research-grade, which is the right caveat. The qualifier I want surfaced before screening: the patient and family should hear that the class evidence is anvumetostat at ORR 11% in heavily pre-treated MTAP-null solid tumors (program discontinued April 30, 2026) and TNG908 at 0/23 GBM ORR (terminated November 2024), and that BGB-58067's CNS exposure plus AE profile in humans is not yet published. The trial layering on the Stupp spine is the structural mitigation. The safety dossier of the experimental arm is not. conservativecriticqualifiedevidence_qualityLargely aligned. The critic's RoB2 framing puts Stupp (Low, replicated) above TTFields (Some, unreplicated phase 3) above CeTeG (Some leaning Serious, n=141, 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0). That is the read I have. The critic's prose on CAR-T is the part I want to co-sign as a hard veto the PI inherits in the consensus build, not a soft "consider on trial at recurrence" flag: "Front-line CAR-T in this patient is not supported by any of the published evidence" and the intratumoral-hemorrhage history "compounds the CRS/ICANS-mediated intracranial edema risk; none of the phase 1 readouts to date specifically address re-bleed risk in a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage." Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 reported 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity; Goff 2019 JIT n=18 had one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells; Choi 2024 NEJM n=3 had 2/3 progress within 1-2 months. Where I push back: BGB-58067 at rank 5 still surfaces an asset with no published phase 1 safety as an active recommendation. The critic's own qualifier ("not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC") reads as a hedge against a rank-list reader who skims past the prose. Same veto-contingent condition I issued to advocate applies here on BGB-58067 specifically: it lifts to qualified once the Sanai phase 0 PD/safety readout publishes.

docs.title: CeTeG / NOA-09 lomustine + TMZ + RT (conditional on MGMT methylated) (lomustine-tmz)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative2moderateConditional pick. Herrlinger 2019 (Lancet, n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label) is the strongest published front-line signal in MGMT-methylated GBM: mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.6 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol). A 16.7-month median OS gain is the largest first-line GBM signal we have. The catch is cumulative myelosuppression, and at age 66 it bites: G>=3 hematologic AE 41% (n=63) in CCNU+TMZ vs 13% (n=66) in TMZ-alone, with lymphopenia at 27%, thrombocytopenia at 16%, neutropenia at 13%. The trial enrolled 18-70 and ECOG 0-1, so the patient is technically eligible, but n=141 with wide CI crossing 1.0 and the toxicity delta both argue for explicit informed-consent on the cytopenia tradeoff. I rank this above any phase 1 option only because the parent drugs (CCNU and TMZ) have decades of safety follow-up and established dose-modification algorithms; the regimen itself is the novel piece. Hard prerequisites: MGMT methylated by MSP or pyrosequencing, baseline ANC >=1500 and platelets >=100k, willingness to dose-modify CCNU by 25% per cycle if G>=3 hematotox emerges. If those don't hold, fall back to pick 1 with TMZ alone in adjuvant phase plus TTFields.Open-label and n=141 with the one-sided p of 0.049 means the OS gain is real but the precision is modest; do not over-promise the 48-month median to the patient; Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression at age 66 is the practical limiter — many patients need dose reduction by cycle 3, and platelet recovery becomes the dose-rate-limiting step by cycles 4-6; Conditional on MGMT methylated; if unmethylated, this regimen is off the table and we revert to pick 1; Eligibility tightens around marrow reserve — baseline CBC, transferrin/ferritin, and B12 should be checked before commit critic4lowI am ranking this 4 rather than higher because the evidence quality is genuinely weaker than the top 3. Herrlinger 2019 (Lancet, n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label) reports per-protocol HR_OS 0.6 with 95% CI 0.35-1.03 and a one-sided p of 0.049. The upper CI bound is 1.03 — the confidence interval crosses 1.0 (just barely) on the per-protocol ITT analysis, and the p-value is one-sided. By RoB2 framing this is Some-to-Serious: open-label (D4), a primary endpoint analyzed per-protocol rather than ITT (D3 deviations from intended intervention), n=141 (under-powered relative to the effect size claimed), and the 16.7-month mOS gain (48.1 vs 31.4) is unreplicated by any independent trial. I do not regard the 48-month median as a number to quote to the patient; the lower bound of the gain is meaningfully smaller. That said: this is the largest published front-line OS signal in MGMT-methylated GBM, the AEs (G>=3 hematotox 41% in CeTeG vs 13% in TMZ-alone) are characterized and there are no treatment-related deaths in the published cohort, so it is not malpractice to offer it. If MGMT returns methylated and marrow reserve is adequate, this is a defensible conversation. If MGMT returns unmethylated, this regimen has no rationale at all.RoB2:Some leaning Serious — open-label, primary analysis reported per-protocol, one-sided p=0.049 with 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0 on the upper bound. The effect size is real but the precision is weak.; n=141 is small for the effect size claimed; no independent replication. The 16.7-month mOS gain has not been reproduced in any second phase 3, and the conservative read is that the true effect lies somewhere between modest and large.; G>=3 hematologic toxicity 41% vs 13% (TMZ-alone) — at 66 the cumulative CCNU myelosuppression will require dose-modification in a meaningful fraction. CBC weekly first two cycles is the standard, not optional.; Conditional on MGMT methylated. Falls off entirely if unmethylated. concensusite2moderateConditional. If MGMT pyrosequencing returns methylated and baseline counts hold (ANC >=1500, platelets >=100k), CeTeG/NOA-09 is the NCCN category 2A regimen for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS >=70. Herrlinger 2019 Lancet (n=141) reports mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol) — a 16.7-month median OS gain over standard Stupp. EANO 2021 names it as an option in MGMT-methylated patients with the explicit caveat about hematologic toxicity. The 2A designation is the right read of the evidence: a single phase 3 with n=141 and one-sided p at 0.049 is real but not Stupp-grade precision. The toxicity caveat is also on-label — grade 3-4 hematologic AEs in 41% of the CCNU+TMZ arm vs 13% of TMZ-alone — and at age 66 that is the binding constraint, not a reason to discard the option.Gated on MGMT methylated. If unmethylated, off the table — back to pick 1 with the TMZ-sparing trial conversation open (pick 3).; Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression at age 66 is the real-world constraint; dose-reduction at cycle 3 is common per Herrlinger 2019. Pre-set CBC thresholds and platelet-recovery rules at consent.; Patient sits at the upper end of the trial's 18-70 age band; functional reserve assessment (CGA or modified G8) is worth doing before committing to six cycles of doublet alkylator. advocate4moderateIf MGMT comes back methylated, CeTeG is the largest published OS signal in newly diagnosed GBM: mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol). That is a 16.7-month OS gain over standard Stupp in the methylated stratum. The efficacy lean at 0.7 plus no toxicity veto makes this exactly the kind of regimen this advocate seat is supposed to surface. The honest weak spot is the small sample (n=141), open-label design, and a real cumulative CCNU myelosuppression burden — grade 3-4 hematologic AE 41% (CeTeG arm) vs 13% (TMZ-alone), driven by lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%. At 66 the cumulative cytopenia signal matters and the team should set CBC monitoring and dose-reduction thresholds up front. No treatment-related deaths in the trial. If MGMT comes back unmethylated, this pick falls off entirely and the BGB-58067 unmethylated arm or AGILE moves up.Gated on MGMT methylated. If unmethylated, this regimen has no rationale.; Cytopenia burden is the binding toxicity at age 66; CBC weekly during the first two cycles, then per protocol; consider G-CSF and platelet thresholds set in advance. No anemia or cytopenia veto in the preference file, so this is a counseling-and-monitoring concern not an exclusion.; Open-label and n=141; the HR 0.60 has a wide CI crossing 1 on the upper bound (1.03). The signal is real but the precision is not Stupp-grade.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitI co-sign the critic's RoB2 read on CeTeG — open-label, n=141, per-protocol primary, 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0, one-sided p=0.049 — those are honest concerns and they belong in the consent conversation. Where I push back: NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 assigns CeTeG/NOA-09 category 2A for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS >=70, and EANO 2021 names it as an option in the same population with the explicit hematologic-toxicity caveat. Category 2A means lower-level evidence + uniform consensus — that is the collective expert calibration of the same Herrlinger 2019 paper the critic is reading in isolation. The 2A designation already incorporates the RoB2 concerns; it does not ignore them. Ranking CeTeG at #4 below the validated CE.6 fallback at #3 reads as the RoB2 framework substituting for the guideline framework, when in this case both should weigh in. Same point on TTFields at #2 — EF-14 is RoB2:Some by the critic's read, but NCCN v2.2025 category 1 and EF-14's 5-yr OS 13% vs 5% replication in the long-term follow-up reflect expert consensus that single-trial open-label modality evidence can still carry the category 1 endorsement when the effect size is large and the endpoint is OS. The critic's evidence-quality discipline is correct; the guideline categories are not pretending the evidence is stronger than it is, they are calibrating it. criticconcensusitequalifiedevidence_qualityNCCN category 2A on CeTeG is a real signal that lower-tier evidence has converged opinion, and I read it the same way the consensusite does for CeTeG at rank 2. The qualifier is that consensus has historically endorsed GBM interventions that later cratered in phase 3. Front-line ICI was favored by early expert opinion before CheckMate-498 returned HR_OS 1.31 (95% CI 1.09-1.58, p=0.0037) — worse survival than Stupp in MGMT-unmethylated newly diagnosed disease. Depatux-m had EGFR-amplification enthusiasm before INTELLANCE-1 (n=691, RoB2:Low) read out HR_OS 1.02 (95% CI 0.85-1.23, p=0.63). The CeTeG primary analysis itself is per-protocol with one-sided p=0.049 and a 95% CI of 0.35-1.03 that just crosses 1.0; n=141, open-label, no independent replication. 2A is the appropriate category for that bias profile. What it does not become is RCT-grade certainty by virtue of the guideline label. Same caution on framing BGB-58067 at rank 3 as "the guideline-aligned move" — NCCN's trial-first language is generic and applies equally to GBM AGILE, SURVIVE, and other multi-site randomized slots that carry less single-site fragility than a single-arm phase 0/2.

docs.title: Abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor, CNS-penetrant) pre-positioned for recurrence on CDKN2A-loss / RB-intact axis (abemaciclib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate6moderatePre-positioning for the recurrence conversation, not an active first-line pick. The patient's CDKN2A homozygous loss is the canonical CDK4/6i rationale and abemaciclib is the CNS-penetrant member of the class (Raub 2015, intratumoral concentrations confirmed in the Wen NCT02981940 paired-surgical cohort). The Wen 2024 recurrent GBM phase 0/2 in CDKN2A-deleted / RB-intact disease showed PFS6 ~9.7% on monotherapy — modest activity ceiling but the paired-surgical PK confirmed the drug gets to tumor at pharmacologically relevant concentrations, which is what palbociclib (Pgp substrate) did not (Taal 2018 stopped early for futility). NCT02981940 is now active-not-recruiting but abemaciclib is FDA-approved (off-label use in GBM is defensible), and the Vilgelm 2019 + AACR 2025 preclinical signal for PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combinations suggests this could layer onto BGB-58067 at relapse. RB1 functional readout is the gating step before committing.Pre-position only; patient is newly diagnosed and abemaciclib is not 1L SoC.; PFS6 ~9.7% defines the activity ceiling for monotherapy in recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM; the better case is combination at relapse rather than monotherapy.; Class AEs: diarrhea, neutropenia, fatigue. Manageable; no veto in the preference file.

docs.title: CAN-3110 oncolytic HSV-1 (Ling Nature 2023) — pre-position for recurrence if HSV-1 seropositive (can-3110)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker6lowRecurrence-only and currently active-not-recruiting, so this is a pre-position, not an enrollment today. The Ling 2023 Nature phase 1 in recurrent HGG showed mOS 11.6 mo overall and a meaningful enrichment in HSV-1 seropositive patients (~2x the historical recurrent-GBM benchmark), with durable responses in a subset and FDA Fast Track in 2024. HSV-1 serology is a $20 test, so the no-brainer move is order it now and know the prior probability of benefit when the second-line conversation comes. If she is seropositive, this becomes a high-effect-size cell-of-origin-immune-priming bet at recurrence. The intratumoral hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation from viral lysis overlaps with the bleed mechanism, but the Ling 2023 cohort included patients with prior tumor bleeding without prohibitive re-bleed rates.Recurrent-disease only, currently active not recruiting; depends on trial reopening or pivoting to the successor protocol when the patient progresses.; Intratumoral injection feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy and any plan for second-look surgery. Hemorrhage history is a relative caution.; Order HSV-1 IgG now; cost is trivial and the result informs both this trial and any downstream HSV-platform option. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate7moderateRecurrence-only and not enrollable at first-line, but worth ranking so the team locks the second-line conversation early. The Ling 2023 Nature phase 1 in recurrent HGG showed mOS 11.6 mo overall and mOS 14.2 mo in the HSV-1 seropositive subset (66% of the cohort) on a single intratumoral injection. The seropositive signal is roughly 2x the historical recurrent GBM benchmark. FDA Fast Track in 2024. No DLTs across the full dose range. The intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation from viral lysis could re-bleed, and the screening team should weigh that carefully, but it is not absolute. HSV-1 serology is a cheap test to order now so the team knows the prior probability of benefit when the recurrence conversation happens.Pre-position only; recurrent disease only.; Intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution — annotate, do not exclude. Per the preference file: "Carry forward the intratumoral-hemorrhage history as a safety annotation against bevacizumab / antiangiogenic exposure." CAN-3110 is not antiangiogenic but the inflammation-driven bleed mechanism overlaps; team conversation required.; Order HSV-1 serology now to inform the future decision; no downside to that test.

docs.title: SurVaxM (survivin peptide vaccine) + GM-CSF on the SURVIVE randomized phase 2b (NCT05163080), layered on Stupp adjuvant phase (survaxm)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative5lowLowest-tox add-on in the dossier with a published front-line signal that doesn't compromise the SoC backbone. Ahluwalia 2023 (JCO, n=63, informal:med RoB) reported PFS6 95.2%, mPFS 11.4 mo, mOS 25.9 mo, 2-yr OS 51%, 3-yr OS 41% — encouraging vs the historical ~16-month control but explicitly single-arm phase 2a, so I cannot pretend the magnitude is fully validated yet. Safety is the standout: injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms dominate; zero SurVaxM-attributable G>=3 SAEs (n=63). The pivotal randomized phase 2b SURVIVE (NCT05163080) is the trial that turns this into real evidence. Mechanism (survivin peptide vaccination + KLH carrier + GM-CSF adjuvant) is biologically distinct from CDK4/6 or PRMT5 axes, so it competes only with TTFields for adjuvant-phase add-on. Ranked fifth because it lacks the OS-randomized evidence of the top four picks, but it earns ranking on safety alone — the toxicity floor here is the lowest of any add-on we have access to. Note: I am NOT ranking DCVax-L. The Liau 2023 JAMA Oncology external-control analysis (HR_OS 0.80, 95% CI 0.70-0.89, ROBINS-I:Serious) reports a real signal, but the US expanded-access protocol NCT02146066 only accepts patients whose vaccine was already manufactured under the original phase 3, and this patient's tissue window from initial resection has closed. Do not raise the family's hopes there.Single-arm phase 2a with non-contemporaneous historical control — magnitude of OS signal is not yet confirmed; SURVIVE is the validation gate; If patient also enrolls in BGB-58067 (pick 3), check protocol for vaccine co-administration restrictions — many trials exclude concurrent investigational immunotherapy; Expanded access via MimiVax exists but is more expensive than trial enrollment; pursue NCT05163080 first; DCVax-L is NOT a viable add-on for this patient because the manufacturing window from initial resection has closed — see expanded notes critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: EGFRvIII / EGFR CAR-T pre-position: MGH CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369 + UCSF E-SYNC NCT06186401 + Penn dual-target NCT05802693 / NCT07209241 — conditional on EGFRvIII positivity (and Cohort 1 of E-SYNC also needs unmethylated MGMT) (carv3-team-e-mgh)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2lowThe Choi NEJM 2024 first-in-human readout (n=3 single-center MGH) hit 3/3 near-complete radiographic regression within days of intraventricular CARv3-TEAM-E infusion, no G>=3 AE in the lead cohort, no CRS >=grade 2, no ICANS-defining events. Two of three progressed within 1-2 months, one was sustained at 150 days. I am not pretending n=3 is OS evidence. The upside scenario is that even a transient radiographic response opens a debulking window for a combination strategy or for a second cell-therapy round, and the synNotch / dual-target / TEAM-engager generation was specifically engineered against the antigen-escape biology that killed rindopepimut (Snuderl 2011 heterogeneity, Nathanson 2014 ecDNA reversibility) and the first-generation O'Rourke construct. The play is to push EGFR amplification + EGFRvIII testing through the comprehensive NGS panel now so the second-line cellular-therapy menu is ready if EGFRvIII is positive (roughly 20-30% of EGFR-amplified GBM); if it is positive AND MGMT is unmethylated, E-SYNC Cohort 1 (newly diagnosed) is the only front-line cellular-therapy slot in the menu and is worth jumping on. Pre-resection enrollment is the highest-potential play if EGFRvIII tests positive because debulking happens before adaptive resistance hardens.CRS and ICANS-like neurotoxicity with intraventricular or intrathecal CAR-T on a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage is a real flag. The Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 paper had 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity (headache, fatigue, focal deficits) fully reversible with steroids; Goff 2019 had 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells. I would not veto these on the hemorrhage history but the screening team needs explicit baseline imaging and an edema-management plan documented up front.; Gated on EGFRvIII testing (RT-PCR or RNA-fusion NGS) and EGFR amplification by FISH; both currently unknown. NCT06186401 Cohort 1 also requires unmethylated MGMT. If EGFRvIII is negative, the EGFR-amp-only Penn NCT07209241 opens at recurrence.; Single-antigen escape is the structural failure mode. Dual-target (Penn EGFR + IL13Ra2) and synNotch (E-SYNC) constructs were built to address this; the TEAM-engager (MGH CARv3-TEAM-E) recruits endogenous T cells against bystander wild-type-EGFR cells. None of these has OS-randomized validation yet.; Most slots are recurrent-only; the front-line slot is E-SYNC Cohort 1 and depends on the two unresolved gates. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocaterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitWe agree on BGB-58067 at the top — that part of the rank order is right. Putting EGFRvIII / EGFR CAR-T at 2 is where I qualify. EGFRvIII has not been tested yet (the risktaker's own notes flag this as a pending gate), and the preference file is explicit on a different axis: "Carry forward the intratumoral-hemorrhage history as a safety annotation." Intraventricular CAR-T with the Bagley 2024 100% transient ICANS-like neurotox signal plus CRS-mediated cerebral edema, on a pre-bled brain, at rank 2 of a newly-diagnosed plan, is a heavier call than the rank suggests. Front-line cellular therapy at E-SYNC Cohort 1 also requires both EGFRvIII positive AND MGMT unmethylated — two conditional gates compounded. Pre-position the cellular menu, run the testing, but the rank position overstates what this patient can act on today and understates the hemorrhage-history carry-forward. SurVaxM on SURVIVE (NCT05163080) or GBM AGILE multi-site randomization fits the trial-prefer axis with a real enrollment slot and no hemorrhage compounding. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitEGFRvIII CAR-T at rank #2 puts front-line cellular therapy ahead of the Stupp backbone the risktaker keeps at #3. NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 does not endorse CAR-T at any line for GBM at any evidence category — no NCCN row, no EANO 2021 recommendation, no ESMO endorsement. The Choi NEJM 2024 readout (n=3, 3/3 transient radiographic regression, 1/3 sustained at 150 days, 2/3 progressed within 1-2 months) is a real signal and I read it honestly. Guidelines exist precisely to constrain enthusiasm for n=3 readouts where the cohort cannot tell us OS, durability, or the rebleed risk profile in a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage. Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 with 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity and Goff 2019 with 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells are the safety floor; no published cohort specifically addresses the hemorrhage-history overlap. The risktaker is right that E-SYNC Cohort 1 is the front-line slot if EGFRvIII tests positive and MGMT comes back unmethylated — that is the enrollment-on-trial pathway NCCN's top-of-pathway language opens. But ranking it #2 ahead of category 1 Stupp + TTFields is the same hierarchy inversion I flagged on the advocate. Where I align with the risktaker: the comprehensive NGS + RNA fusion + MMR/MSI/TMB conditional plays at rank #4 (BRAF V600E dabrafenib+trametinib, NTRK larotrectinib, MSI-H/TMB-H pembrolizumab) ARE guideline-aligned. NCCN v2.2025 lists all three on the recurrent/refractory branch as tumor-agnostic options when biomarker positive, with cross-society convergence across NCCN, ESMO, and ASCO on the tumor-agnostic labels. The risktaker's framing reads them as 'free upside on low prior probability' which is true; my reframe is that they are also the guideline-endorsed recurrent-disease options if any biomarker hits, not just hypothesis-generating bets. Same biology, different rationale, same conclusion: order the panel. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe risktaker opens with "The bar is 21-month median OS on Stupp + TTFields" and then puts CARv3-TEAM-E at rank 2 on the Choi NEJM 2024 readout — "n=3 single-center MGH... 3/3 near-complete radiographic regression within days... Two of three progressed within 1-2 months, one was sustained at 150 days." That is the entire dataset. Then the framing: "even a transient radiographic response opens a debulking window for a combination strategy." A transient response in 3 patients at one center with 2/3 progressing inside two months is hypothesis-generating. It is not evidence that justifies a rank-2 position in a 66F newly-diagnosed plan where the front-line choice has to anchor 12-18 months of treatment. The Bagley 2024 NatMed dual-target row (n=6, 100% transient ICANS-like neurotox reversible with steroids, 0% formal RANO objective response) and the Goff 2019 row (n=18, 0% ORR, one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells) round out the cellular signal — every readout in the class is single-digit-n single-arm with transient signals at best. The risktaker's framing prioritizes ceiling-effect potential over reproducibility, which is the wrong weighting for a patient with one shot at front-line therapy and a documented intratumoral-hemorrhage history compounding the CRS/ICANS-edema concern none of the phase 1 papers specifically address. conservativerisktakervetotoxicityVeto. EGFRvIII/EGFR CAR-T at rank #2 above the Stupp backbone in a patient with documented intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation is the trade I cannot endorse. The risktaker rationale concedes "CRS and ICANS-like neurotoxicity with intraventricular or intrathecal CAR-T on a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage is a real flag," then offers "baseline imaging and an edema-management plan documented up front" as the mitigation. That is not a mitigation, that is an acknowledgement. Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 had 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity in patients without a prior bleed; Goff 2019 JIT n=18 had one treatment-related death at >1e10 cells; Choi 2024 NEJM n=3 had 3/3 transient regression with 2/3 progressing within 1-2 months. The "transient debulking creates a window for a combination strategy or for a second cell-therapy round" framing is mechanism, not OS evidence. No published readout demonstrates that radiographic regression in n<=10 phase 1 cohorts translates to median OS gain over the 20.9 mo Stupp+TTFields anchor (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.76; 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%). The risktaker's own pick 3 keeps the Stupp backbone and explicitly cites CheckMate-498 (HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp, p=0.0037, n=560) as the cautionary precedent against substituting phase 1 monotherapy for SoC. Ranking CAR-T above pick 3 contradicts that same logic. Veto on toxicity contingent on (a) prior intratumoral hemorrhage in this patient and (b) absence of any phase 1 cohort that specifically addresses re-bleed risk under CRS/ICANS-mediated edema. If E-SYNC Cohort 1 publishes a safety analysis that includes pre-bled patients with documented re-bleed surveillance, the veto lifts to qualified-on-toxicity for recurrence-line consideration only. Front-line CAR-T in this patient stays vetoed.

Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3highI am the risktaker, not a contrarian. The Stupp HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001) and EF-14 HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001) layered together produce the 21-month median that defines the threshold I am trying to beat with picks 1 and 2. Substituting a phase 1 monotherapy for the Stupp backbone is precisely the trade that CheckMate-498 punished (nivolumab + RT HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp in unmethylated MGMT, p=0.0037, n=560). The picks above LAYER onto this backbone — BGB-58067 Arm A and Arm B are both built on RT, MGH CARv3-TEAM-E is recurrence-only. This pick stays because the floor matters when you're swinging at the ceiling.MGMT methylation status is the dominant effect modifier and is unknown; methylated patients derive 7-8 mo additional OS from adjuvant TMZ, unmethylated patients derive minimal benefit (Hegi 2005 mOS 12.7 vs 11.8). docs.title: Run comprehensive NGS + RNA fusion + MMR/MSI/TMB now to unlock conditional tumor-agnostic plays (dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E; larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK; pembrolizumab for MMR-D / MSI-H / TMB-H) (comprehensive-ngs-conditional-plays)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4moderateThese are essentially free options. Each conditional gate has a low prior probability in adult IDHwt GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK fusion <1%, primary MMR-deficient or MSI-H GBM uncommon), but the upside conditional on a positive hit is large enough to reframe the entire decision tree. Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E HGG (ROAR, Wen 2022 Lancet Oncol, n=45) gave ORR 33% (95% CI 20-49), mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41% — that is a recurrent-disease readout that would totally change second-line for this patient if she comes back BRAF V600E. Larotrectinib in TRK-fusion solid tumors (Drilon 2018 NEJM, n=55) gave ORR 75-80% with CNS responses confirmed in Doz 2022 (DNA-only panels miss intron-deep CNS breakpoints — order RNA fusion). Pembrolizumab in TMB-H (KEYNOTE-158, n=102) gave ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) under the tumor-agnostic label. Even a 5% combined hit rate across these gates is worth the single comprehensive panel send-out the patient should be running anyway.Prior probability is low across all three biomarkers in adult IDHwt GBM. The expected-value framing only works if the NGS is bundled with the gates already ordered (MGMT, MTAP IHC, EGFR/vIII, RB1) — incremental cost is small but unbiased framing matters.; DNA-only panels miss NTRK intron-deep breakpoints in CNS tumors; insist on RNA-based fusion testing (Tempus xR or Caris WTS) or accept the false-negative risk.; These open second-line options at best; none changes the 1L plan unless the result is exceptional (e.g. BRAF V600E early at diagnosis). conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: FUS-mediated BBB opening (SonoCloud-9 / SONOBIRD NCT04528680) — pre-position for first recurrence at a US SONOBIRD site (Northwestern/Sonabend, Columbia, MD Anderson) (fus-bbb-opening)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker7lowRecurrent-only and requires re-resection candidacy at trial entry, so the play here is to flag US SONOBIRD sites at the patient's recurrence conversation. The Sonabend 2023 Lancet Oncology phase 1 (n=17) demonstrated 4-6x increased peri-tumoral nab-paclitaxel concentration vs unsonicated brain on the SonoCloud-9 implant, with no implant-related deaths and tolerated through 6 cycles. SONOBIRD is the phase 3 (n=560, 40 sites US+EU) with IV carboplatin as the partner drug, randomized vs lomustine or TMZ at first recurrence. The strategic value is delivery enhancement: any antibody-class or large-molecule CNS therapy that gets blocked at the BBB becomes accessible behind FUS sonication, which opens the door to off-label combinations at recurrence. Pre-position the patient at a SONOBIRD US site early so the implant decision can be made at the first-recurrence resection rather than after.Recurrent-only; not actionable today. The lesson — CDK4/6 inhibitor choice for CNS tumors is gated by BBB transporter pharmacology, not by potency at the kinase. Abemaciclib and ribociclib both clear; palbociclib does not. Michaud K/Stokoe D (2010)Cancer ResearchU87MG (INK4a-ARF-null) and GBM39 intracranial xenograft; flank xenograft for comparisonn=8-10 mice/armVehiclePD-0332991 oral 150 mg/kg dailyINK4a/ARF (CDKN2A) loss derepresses CDK4/6, which phosphorylates Rb and drives G1/S transition. CDK4/6 inhibition reimposes the checkpoint in Rb-intact tumors.Palbociclib arrested growth of INK4a-ARF-null orthotopic U87MG xenografts and extended survival modestly. The paper is one of the first proofs that CDK4/6 inhibition has activity against CDKN2A-null intracranial glioma — though the orthotopic effect was substantially weaker than the flank effect, foreshadowing the BBB-efflux explanation that Parrish 2015 nailed down.moderatemedpartial20354191DOIEarly-era study — uses U87MG, predates the BBB-efflux literature. The signal is real but weaker than expected from the genetics, which Parrish 2015 later explained mechanistically.

docs.title: CDK4/6 inhibition is subtype-selective in GBM stem cells
docs.text:
intervention_id: cdk46-class · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Li M/Purow B (2017)OncotargetPatient-derived glioblastoma stem cell (GSC) cultures across proneural / mesenchymal / classical subtypes; orthotopic mouse xenograftMultiple GSC lines (n=12+); n=8-10 mice/arm orthotopicVehiclePalbociclib in vitro IC50 panel + in vivo daily oral dosingProneural GSCs express higher CDK6 and have intact Rb1, putting them in the canonical CDK4/6-inhibitor-sensitive zone. Importantly, treatment also pushed proneural GSCs toward a mesenchymal expression program — a hint that CDK4/6 inhibition may select for or induce the more aggressive subtype on prolonged therapy.moderatemedpartial28903422DOIUses palbociclib (the BBB-poor compound) — the in-vivo orthotopic signal is more impressive than the Parrish 2015 work would predict, possibly because of the proneural-line bias. docs.title: Ribociclib CNS penetration in recurrent GBM (phase 0 PK/PD)
docs.text:
intervention_id: ribociclib · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Tien AC/Sanai N (2019)Clinical Cancer ResearchPhase 0 trial in recurrent GBM with intraoperative tumor sampling; matched plasma and tumor PK; Rb phosphorylation as PD readoutn=12 patients (3 surgical + 9 expansion)Pre-treatment baseline (paired)Ribociclib 600 mg PO daily x 8 days, with intratumoral sampling at surgeryRibociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor with lower P-gp affinity than palbociclib but higher than abemaciclib. The Rb phosphorylation suppression was target engagement, not tumor response. Bridges the rodent preclinical (Raub 2015) and the clinical-activity question (INSIGhT / Wen NCT02981940). docs.title: EGFRvIII mCAR T-cell therapy cures intracerebral glioma (foundational preclinical)
docs.text:
intervention_id: cart-egfrviii-class · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Sampson JH/Johnson LA (2014)Clinical Cancer ResearchFully immunocompetent C57BL/6 mouse with syngeneic SMA-560 / KR158 intracerebral glioma engineered to express EGFRvIII; third-generation EGFRvIII-specific murine CARn=8-10 mice/arm across multiple efficacy experimentsUntransduced T cells; irrelevant CAR; vehicleSingle IV infusion of EGFRvIII mCAR T cells, dose-escalated; some experiments with lymphodepletion preconditioningThird-generation CAR (CD28 + 4-1BB) targeting EGFRvIII — a tumor-specific neoantigen with no normal-tissue expression. Engineered T cells traffic to the CNS, lyse EGFRvIII+ cells, and (the surprise finding) generate host immunity against EGFRvIII-negative tumor antigens via epitope spreading.At elevated doses, EGFRvIII mCAR T cells cured all mice with established intracerebral glioma. Cured mice were resistant to rechallenge with EGFRvIII-negative tumors, implying epitope spreading and durable host immunity. The paper is the preclinical foundation for the Penn EGFRvIII CAR-T (O'Rourke 2017 STM) and the entire EGFRvIII-directed cellular-therapy program.strongmedpartial24352643DOISyngeneic mouse model with engineered EGFRvIII expression — homogeneous antigen expression, unlike human GBM where EGFRvIII is heterogeneous within tumor (Nathanson 2014). The dramatic cure rate did not translate fully to human trials, where antigen escape limited durability. Still the right preclinical proof of concept. Nathanson DA/Mischel PS (2014)SciencePatient-derived GBM cell lines, EGFRvIII+ at baseline; in-vitro EGFR TKI selection; FISH for chromosomal vs extrachromosomal EGFRvIII; xenograft validationMultiple patient-derived lines; xenograft n=6-10/armUntreated lines; off-drug recovery cohortErlotinib and other EGFR TKIs at clinically relevant concentrationsEGFRvIII is frequently encoded on extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA), not on the chromosome. Under EGFR TKI pressure, EGFRvIII ecDNA is rapidly lost from the population; on TKI withdrawal, ecDNA EGFRvIII re-amplifies. Resistance is genetic (ecDNA loss) but reversible — the antigen comes back when the selective pressure ends.EGFRvIII ecDNA expression is highly dynamic. TKI exposure suppresses EGFRvIII; drug holiday re-amplifies it. Erlotinib resistance reverses within 72 h of drug withdrawal. The implication for CAR-T and vaccine therapy: antigen loss observed on therapy may be transient rather than durable, opening the door to sequential or pulsed antigen-directed strategies.stronghighstrong24310612DOIMostly in-vitro work; the in-vivo dynamics on a clinical timescale are less well-characterized. The paper changed how the field thinks about EGFRvIII heterogeneity — not a stable lineage trait but a population-level fluctuation. Snuderl M/Iafrate AJ (2011)Cancer CellMulti-region tumor sampling from 18 primary EGFR-amplified GBMs; FISH and IHC for EGFRvIII; single-cell-level antigen mapping18 primary tumors; 3-5 regions eachNot applicable (descriptive)Not applicable (descriptive)EGFRvIII is expressed in a subset of cells within EGFR-amplified GBM, often in non-overlapping spatial clones with other EGFR variants (vIII, A289V, etc). The intratumoral heterogeneity means that any single-antigen-directed therapy leaves antigen-negative subclones to repopulate the tumor.EGFRvIII positivity is heterogeneous within tumors and between regions in the same tumor — almost always co-existing with EGFRvIII-negative subclones in the same lesion. This is the underlying biology that explains the rindopepimut ACT IV failure and the antigen-loss escape seen in the O'Rourke 2017 CAR-T trial. Single-antigen targeting cannot work without addressing the negative subpopulation.stronghighstrong22137795DOIDescriptive heterogeneity study — no therapeutic intervention. The clinical implication is structural: any monovalent EGFRvIII therapy (vaccine, ADC, CAR-T) carries built-in resistance. Justifies the move toward dual-target (EGFR + IL13Ra2) and synNotch (E-SYNC) designs.

docs.title: Humanized EGFRvIII CAR-T validation (Penn — the construct used in O'Rourke 2017)
docs.text:
intervention_id: cart-egfrviii-penn · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Johnson LA/June CH (2015)Science Translational MedicineHumanized scFv panel screened against EGFRvIII vs WT EGFR; NSG mouse with U87-EGFRvIII subcutaneous and orthotopic xenograftMultiple scFv clones tested; n=8-10 mice/arm in xenograft validationEmpty CAR or untransduced T cellsIV CAR-T infusion in NSG xenograft; lymphodepletion in some armsThe team generated a panel of humanized scFvs and selected a low-affinity binder specific for EGFRvIII over WT EGFR — the affinity tuning is what prevents on-target/off-tumor activity against normal EGFR-expressing skin, gut, and lung. Then incorporated into a second-generation CAR.The humanized EGFRvIII CAR-T controlled xenogeneic human EGFRvIII+ glioblastoma in NSG mice and showed minimal cross-reactivity with WT EGFR-expressing tissues at clinically relevant doses. The construct went directly into the NCT02209376 phase 1 (Penn) that O'Rourke 2017 STM reported.moderatemedpartial25696001DOINSG mice have no functional immune system, so the tumor-microenvironment immunosuppression seen in the human trial (intratumoral PD-L1, IDO, Tregs in O'Rourke 2017) is absent in the model. The xenograft validation is necessary but not sufficient — the clinical activity was substantially lower than the preclinical signal would predict.

docs.title: CAR-T secreting bispecific T-cell engagers (TEAMs) — preclinical of the MGH construct
docs.text:
intervention_id: carv3-team-e-mgh · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Choi BD/Maus MV (2019)Nature BiotechnologyNSG mouse intracranial U87-EGFRvIII / WT EGFR mixed xenograft; antigen-heterogeneous tumor modeln=8-10 mice/armEGFRvIII CAR-T without TEAM secretion; untransduced T cellsSingle intracranial CAR-T-TEAM infusionCAR targets EGFRvIII directly through the CAR; the engineered T cells also secrete a CD3 x WT-EGFR bispecific antibody (the TEAM) that redirects endogenous T cells against neighboring EGFRvIII-negative, WT-EGFR-positive tumor cells. docs.title: CAN-3110 (rQNestin34.5v.2) preclinical toxicology and design rationale
docs.text:
intervention_id: can-3110 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Chiocca EA/Oglesbee M (2020)Molecular Therapy — Methods & Clinical DevelopmentMurine intracranial glioma model; non-human primate biodistribution; nestin-promoter glioma vs normal-brain cell selectivity assaysMouse cohorts n=8-10/arm; NHP biodistribution n=3Sham injection; parental HSV-1 backbonesIntratumoral rQNestin34.5v.2 at escalating PFU dosesrQNestin34.5v.2 places the neurovirulence gene ICP34.5 under control of the nestin promoter, which is selectively active in high-grade glioma and glioma stem cells. The virus replicates and lyses tumor in nestin-expressing cells, while normal CNS cells (which don't drive the nestin promoter) restrict ICP34.5 expression and avoid neurovirulence.rQNestin34.5v.2 was cytotoxic for all tested glioma cell lines (cell survival <20% of control) while sparing nestin-low normal CNS cells. Mouse and non-human primate biodistribution showed restricted replication in nestin-active tissue. The toxicology package supported the IND for the NCT03152318 phase 1.stronghighpartial32373649DOINestin expression is not glioma-specific (also expressed in neural stem cells and some adult progenitors) — the safety margin comes from differential promoter activity, not absolute selectivity. The preclinical toxicology package is the most thorough in the modern oncolytic-HSV space and is the backstop for the clinical Nature 2023 readout.

docs.title: PVSRIPO mechanism — CD155-targeted oncolysis and myeloid immunoactivation
docs.text:
intervention_id: pvsripo · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Yang Y/Gromeier M (2023)Neuro-OncologyMouse intracerebral injection of PVSRIPO; immunohistochemistry and scRNA-seq of microglia and infiltrating myeloid cellsMouse cohorts n=6-10/group; multiple time points post-injectionSham; UV-inactivated PVSRIPOSingle intracerebral PVSRIPO injectionPVSRIPO triggers diffuse, sustained microglial activation extending well beyond the injection site through the CNS. The activation is type-I-interferon-dominant and persists for weeks, providing a prolonged immunostimulatory window in which adaptive antitumor responses can develop.A single intratumoral PVSRIPO injection drove diffuse microglia activation through the CNS for weeks, with type-I-IFN gene signatures persisting beyond the local injection site. The finding explains the long-tail clinical responder pattern (Desjardins 2018 21% 24-month OS plateau) — the response is not from acute lysis alone but from delayed myeloid-driven adaptive immunity.strongmedpartial36864784DOIMouse work — the human translation rests on CSF and tumor analysis from clinical samples, which the Brown/Gromeier group has begun publishing separately. The mechanism is the most coherent published explanation for why PVSRIPO has long-tail benefit despite a modest median-OS signal. Brown MC/Nair SK (2017)Science Translational MedicineHuman dendritic cell and macrophage cultures; CD155-expressing tumor lines (glioma, melanoma); ex-vivo tumor explantsMultiple human DC and macrophage donors; cell lines in replicateWild-type poliovirus; CD155-negative cells; non-replicating virusPVSRIPO at varying MOI; sublethal infection of antigen-presenting cellsPVSRIPO is a recombinant poliovirus chimera with the internal ribosomal entry site swapped from rhinovirus type 2, ablating neuropathogenicity. CD155 (the poliovirus receptor) is ectopically expressed on glioma cells and constitutively expressed on glioma-associated macrophages and microglia. Sublethal infection of CD155+ antigen-presenting cells produces sustained type-I-interferon-dominant activation.Sublethal PVSRIPO infection of CD155+ dendritic cells and macrophages produced sustained type-I-IFN-dominant activation and primed antigen-specific CTL responses against tumor neoantigens. The dual mechanism (direct lysis of tumor cells + immune-priming of antigen-presenting cells) is the proposed reason for the long-tail responder pattern seen clinically in the Desjardins 2018 NEJM phase 1.strongmedpartial28931654DOIMechanism paper, mostly in-vitro. The in-vivo confirmation of myeloid activation came later (Mosaheb 2020 Neuro-Oncology). The CD155 expression data is the part to read carefully — broad CD155 expression on tumor and myeloid cells is exactly what you want, but it is not glioma-specific.

docs.title: M032 — oncolytic HSV-1 expressing IL-12 (preclinical)
docs.text:
intervention_id: m032-ohsv · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Roth JC/Markert JM (2014)Human Gene Therapy Clinical DevelopmentAotus non-human primate intracerebral inoculation; mouse intracranial tumor models; biodistribution + neurovirulence safetyNHP n=3-6 per dose; mouse efficacy n=8-10/armParental HSV-1; vehicle; G207 head-to-head in some experimentsIntracerebral M032 dose escalation from 1e6 to 1e8 PFUM032 is a γ134.5-deleted HSV-1 carrying a transgene encoding murine or human IL-12. Tumor-restricted replication kills tumor cells directly; IL-12 secreted locally activates NK and T cells and shifts the tumor microenvironment toward a Th1 program.M032 was non-pathogenic in Aotus NHPs across the full dose range and produced durable tumor regression in mouse intracranial models. IL-12 expression was confirmed in tumor tissue but not in normal brain — the local IL-12 payload is what differentiates M032 from G207 (its non-armed predecessor). The toxicology package supported the human phase 1 (NCT02062827).moderatemedpartial24649838DOIAotus is the standard primate model for HSV neurovirulence but is not a perfect human predictor. Mouse efficacy used implanted tumor lines, not GEMMs. M032 is conceptually attractive (IL-12 locally) but has not yet shown the clinical signal that CAN-3110 has — phase 1 readout pending.

docs.title: Depatux-m (ABT-414, EGFR-directed ADC) preclinical
docs.text:
intervention_id: depatux-m · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Reilly EB/Phillips AC (2015)Molecular Cancer TherapeuticsEGFR-amplified and EGFRvIII+ GBM PDX panel; non-EGFR-amplified controls; xenograft and orthotopicMultiple PDX lines; n=8-10 mice/armIsotype-control ADC; vehicle; head-to-head with temozolomideDepatux-m IV 3-10 mg/kg, dose-dependent regression studiesDepatux-m is an antibody-drug conjugate: the antibody portion (ABT-806) is selective for activated or amplified EGFR including EGFRvIII; the payload is monomethyl auristatin F (MMAF), a microtubule disruptor. EGFR-amplified tumors internalize the ADC, MMAF kills the cell, and bystander effects extend to nearby cells with lower EGFR.Depatux-m produced regressions in EGFR-amplified GBM PDX models including EGFRvIII-positive lines. Activity was strictly EGFR-amplification-dependent — non-amplified controls did not respond. Synergy with temozolomide was observed in head-to-head xenograft studies, motivating the INTELLANCE-1 design.stronghighpartial25731184DOIStrong preclinical signal, negative phase 3 (INTELLANCE-1, Lassman 2023). Classic example of preclinical-to-clinical mismatch — the ocular toxicity from MMAF and the heterogeneous EGFR expression in real human GBM both limited clinical effect. Logged here as the canonical preclinical-to-clinical caution for the EGFR-ADC class.

docs.title: CSF-1R inhibition reshapes glioma myeloid microenvironment (TME context)
docs.text:
intervention_id: tme-myeloid-context · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Akkari L/Joyce JA (2020)Science Translational MedicinePDGFB-driven glioma GEMM with fractionated cranial RT; CSF-1R blockade combined with RTn=8-12 mice/arm across multiple GEMM cohortsRT alone; CSF-1R alone; vehicleCranial RT 10 Gy in 2 Gy fractions ± PLX3397 oralAfter RT, monocyte-derived macrophages repopulate the tumor and adopt a wound-healing / pro-tumorigenic program that drives recurrence. CSF-1R blockade during the post-RT window blocks this repopulation and prevents the resistance trajectory.Adding CSF-1R blockade to RT in PDGFB GEMM glioma extended survival far beyond either modality alone. The post-RT macrophage influx was identified as a tractable resistance node — same biology as the immune-suppressive TME in untreated tumors but kinetically amplified after radiation injury.strongmedpartial32669424DOIGEMM models — clinical translation of the CSF-1R + RT concept has not yet shown a definitive phase 2/3 signal. Mechanism is the part to carry forward: it explains why standard RT in GBM almost always leads to recurrence with an adaptive immune escape that the patient's IDH-WT GBM will face on its Stupp track. Klemm F/Joyce JA (2020)CellHuman brain tumor resections (gliomas IDH-WT and IDH-mutant, brain metastases); flow cytometry, RNA-seq, mass cytometry across 119 patients119 patients across glioma subtypes and brain metastasisBrain metastases and IDH-mutant glioma as biology comparatorsNot applicable (descriptive)IDH-WT GBM is dominated by tissue-resident microglia and monocyte-derived macrophages that express immunosuppressive markers (TGFBI, CD163, MARCO) and lack the activation signatures seen in IDH-mutant tumors or brain metastases. T cells are sparse and exhausted; the dominant immune-cell pool is myeloid.IDH-WT GBM has a uniquely myeloid-dominated immune microenvironment with minimal T-cell infiltration — substantially more immunosuppressive than IDH-mutant glioma or brain metastases. The signature predicts why generic PD-1 blockade fails (no T cells to unleash) and why myeloid-targeted strategies (CSF-1R, TGF-β, CD47) and locoregional T-cell delivery (intraventricular CAR-T) are the mechanistically supported alternatives.stronghighstrong32470396DOIDescriptive immunology — no therapeutic intervention. The IDH-WT vs IDH-mutant contrast is the part most directly relevant to the patient (who is IDH-WT). Justifies the case-level skepticism about generic ICI and the case-level interest in neoadjuvant pembrolizumab (Cloughesy 2019) and oncolytic-virus immune priming (CAN-3110). Pyonteck SM/Joyce JA (2013)Nature MedicinePDGFB-driven RCAS GEMM glioma; CSF-1R inhibitor PLX3397; orthotopic transplant modelsn=8-12 mice/arm; multiple GEMM cohortsVehiclePLX3397 oral, continuous dosingTumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in glioma express CSF-1R and are educated by glioma-derived CSF1 toward an M2-like, immunosuppressive phenotype. CSF-1R blockade does not deplete macrophages but reprograms them toward an antitumor program — reducing IL-10, TGF-β, and Arg1, increasing MHC-II and IFN-γ-responsive genes.PLX3397 produced durable regressions in PDGFB-driven glioma GEMM by reprogramming TAMs rather than depleting them. Survival was extended substantially. The paper is the canonical demonstration that the myeloid compartment is the dominant immunosuppressive node in glioma — more so than T-cell-intrinsic checkpoints.strongmedpartial24056773DOIPDGFB-driven GEMM is a proneural-subtype model; the same logic may not hold for mesenchymal GBM. Clinical translation has been disappointing — the Butowski / Quail follow-up work showed adaptive PI3K reactivation in TAMs after long-term PLX3397, blunting durable benefit. The mechanism evidence is the part to carry forward: it is the strongest published reason why generic checkpoint inhibition fails in GBM, and why myeloid-targeted combinations are the next move.

docs.title: PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combination — preclinical synergy (cross-tumor with GBM implications)
docs.text:
intervention_id: prmt5-cdk46-combo-class · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Smith K/Wilcoxen K (2025)Cancer Research / AACR 2025 abstract 2996MTAP-null CDX and PDX panel (NSCLC, pancreatic, bladder); TNG462 ± palbociclib or abemaciclib combination dosingMultiple PDX lines; n=8-10 mice/armEither agent alone; vehicleOral TNG462 + oral palbociclib or abemaciclib at clinically achievable dosesTNG462 inhibits PRMT5 selectively in MTAP-null cells; CDK4/6 inhibitors block Rb phosphorylation. The combination converges on G1/S blockade through two distinct nodes — PRMT5-dependent splicing of cell-cycle genes plus direct cyclin-D/CDK4/6 inhibition. Particularly attractive in MTAP+CDKN2A co-deleted tumors (the 9p21 co-deletion phenotype the patient carries).TNG462 + CDK4/6 inhibitor produced deeper and more durable regressions than either agent alone across MTAP-null PDX models. The combination was tolerated and showed clear additivity in MTAP+CDKN2A co-deleted lines — the sponsor explicitly nominated this as a development path for GBM (using a CNS-penetrant PRMT5i in place of TNG462, since TNG462 itself does not cross the BBB).strongmedstrong—DOIConference abstract — full peer-reviewed manuscript pending. No GBM cohort in the actual preclinical models tested; the GBM development path is the sponsor's stated intent, not yet executed. Still the most directly relevant preclinical combination data for this patient's MTAP+CDKN2A co-deletion phenotype. Vilgelm AE/Richmond A (2019)PNASMelanoma cell lines and PDX (MTAP status mixed); CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib) + PRMT5 inhibitor (GSK3326595) in vitro and in vivo; MDM4 splicing as molecular endpointMultiple lines and PDX; n=8-10 mice/arm in vivoEither agent alone; vehiclePalbociclib + GSK3326595 oral, combination at clinically relevant dosesCDK4/6 inhibition indirectly suppresses PRMT5 activity through cell-cycle-dependent regulation of PRMT5 cofactors; PRMT5 in turn regulates MDM4 pre-mRNA splicing, which controls p53 activity. The MDM4 axis links the two enzymes — dual inhibition converges on p53 reactivation and synthetic lethality.Combined palbociclib + GSK3326595 produced deeper and more durable regressions than either agent alone in melanoma models, and delayed emergence of CDK4/6i resistance. The MDM4-p53 axis was the proposed convergent node. Subsequent work in breast cancer (Wang 2024 Nat Commun PMID 38493145) extended the same logic to ER+/Rb-deficient tumors.strongmedcross tumor only31439820DOIMelanoma, not GBM. The biology — MDM4 splicing and p53 reactivation — is general but the GBM-specific test has not been done in published preclinical work. Relevant to the case because TNG462 has reported preclinical combination signals with CDK4/6 inhibitors in MTAP-null preclinical models (AACR 2025 abstract 2996), and a PRMT5i + CDK4/6i combination in CDKN2A/MTAP co-deleted GBM is the most mechanistically attractive doublet on this patient's chart.

docs.title: PRMT5 inhibition + temozolomide — preclinical synergy in glioma
docs.text:
intervention_id: prmt5-tmz-combo · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Onishi S/Banasavadi-Siddegowda YK (2025)Research Square (preprint; Cell Death & Disease in press)Patient-derived GBM neurospheres; orthotopic mouse xenograftMultiple neurosphere lines; n=8-10 mice/arm in vivoTMZ alone; PRMT5i alone; vehicleLLY-283 (PRMT5i, brain-penetrant) + TMZ at clinically relevant doses; sequential and concurrent schedules testedPRMT5 methylates components of the Fanconi anemia / homologous recombination DNA-repair machinery. docs.title: Bevacizumab vascular and tumor-cell effects in GBM (dose-dependent)
docs.text:
intervention_id: bevacizumab · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats von Baumgarten L/Winkler F (2011)Clinical Cancer ResearchU87 and U251 GBM xenografts and orthotopic intracranial models; dose-ranging anti-VEGF (bevacizumab)n=8-10 mice/arm across dose levelsVehicle / IgG isotypeBevacizumab IV at 1, 5, and 10 mg/kg twice weeklyBevacizumab binds and neutralizes VEGF-A, blocking VEGF-receptor signaling on tumor endothelium. The clinical bevacizumab story (no OS benefit in newly diagnosed GBM, modest PFS gain in recurrent) is consistent with the preclinical hint that vascular regression alone is insufficient. docs.title: Rindopepimut — phase 2 with immune-escape mechanism (ACTIVATE / ACT II)

docs.title: IDE397 — second-generation MAT2A inhibitor (preclinical and early clinical)
