docs.title: Biomarker plan
docs.text:
Recommended assay Rationale Suggested assay provider Tissue requirements Germline SDHA full-gene sequencing + del/dup (hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma panel including SDHA, SDHAF2, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, MAX, TMEM127, VHL, RET, NF1) Resolves whether SDHA L306P (VAF 44%) is germline (a single-hit carrier with a second somatic event) or fully somatic (biallelic somatic loss). The answer changes the inheritance counseling, dictates first-degree-relative cascade testing, and locks in the SDH-deficient driver call that gates the temozolomide trials (NCT03556384, NCT05661643) and the belzutifan wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075). Tumor-only NGS that does not include matched germline cannot distinguish the two; SDHA full-gene sequencing with deletion/duplication analysis is the standard per the 2025 Florou review (pmid:39927693). Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae) (Invitae Hereditary Paraganglioma-Pheochromocytoma Panel) · test info · 1400 16th Street, San Francisco, CA 94103 · 1-800-436-3037 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) or saliva kit SDHB IHC re-cut with positive internal control (clone 21A11 or BSB-131), reviewed by a soft-tissue / GI pathologist familiar with SDH-deficient tumors Biallelic SDHA inactivation (combined VAF ~85%) should destabilize the SDH complex and produce loss of SDHB staining; retained SDHB in this case conflicts with the molecular call. The most common explanation is a technical false-negative (under-fixed block, weak antigen retrieval, no internal-control vessel in the field), so a re-cut with an explicit positive internal control resolves it before the dSDH-GIST diagnosis anchors trial enrollment. If SDHB truly remains intact after a clean re-stain, the case becomes a molecularly-SDH-deficient/immunohistochemically-SDH-proficient outlier and the trial screener should flag it for the trial sponsors, since most dSDH-GIST trials use SDHB-IHC loss as the entry phenotype (pmid:35546442, pmid:23046294). Mayo Clinic Laboratories (SDHB Immunostain, test code SDHB / 70550, technical component only) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710 1 unstained slide from archival FFPE (block can return to pathology) SDHA IHC (clone 2E3 or D6J9M) on archival FFPE SDHA IHC is specifically lost in tumors with biallelic SDHA inactivation, while it is retained in tumors driven by SDHB/SDHC/SDHD or SDHC-promoter methylation (pmid:23023976, pmid:23459398). If this case is truly SDHA-driven, SDHA staining should be lost even when SDHB is read as intact; if SDHA also reads as intact after a clean stain, the molecular call must be reconsidered. SDHA IHC therefore arbitrates the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic conflict more directly than re-staining SDHB alone. Mayo Clinic Laboratories (SDHA Immunostain) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710 1 unstained slide from archival FFPE Tumor tissue NGS confirmation of PIK3CA R93W (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT, or equivalent FDA-cleared comprehensive panel) R93W sits outside the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots (E542K, E545K/A/D/G, H1047R/Y/L, C420R per the therascreen and FoundationOne CDx labels) and the ctDNA-only call has not been corroborated on tumor tissue. Confirming the variant in tumor DNA at a validated VAF establishes whether this is a real subclonal alteration or a ctDNA artifact, and frames any PI3Kα-inhibitor discussion. Without tissue confirmation the variant cannot be used to enroll in PI3K-inhibitor trials and clinical actionability stays uncertain (pmid:30880263, pmid:32663323). Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable Tumor tissue NGS confirmation of MAP2K1 P124S on a comprehensive panel (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT, MSK-IMPACT, or equivalent) P124 is a recognized MEK1 activating site (P124L/Q/S) with documented but heterogeneous MEK-inhibitor response (pmid:25370473, pmid:25257211). The variant is currently ctDNA-only; tissue confirmation establishes whether it is clonal in the resected tumor or a low-allele-fraction subclonal/artifactual ctDNA event. Without tissue confirmation it cannot anchor MEK-inhibitor consideration, and MEK monotherapy in MAP2K1-mutant disease is already a stretch outside histiocytosis/melanoma without solid evidence of a clonal driver. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable Cancer-predisposition genetic counseling referral with POLE R1679C variant reclassification review R1679 sits outside the canonical POLE proofreading hotspots (P286R, V411L, S459F) and the tumor is TMB-low and MSS, so the standard polymerase-proofreading-associated polyposis phenotype is not supported here. The counseling visit puts the variant on the right side of the ledger (most likely VUS, no current ICI rationale, no polyposis surveillance trigger) and folds in the SDHA germline result once that returns so the family gets one coherent risk discussion rather than two staggered ones (pmid:32424176, pmid:32058550). NSGC Find-a-Genetic-Counselor Directory · test info · 330 N Wabash Ave, Suite 2000, Chicago, IL 60611 · 1-312-321-6834 no specimen required; counselor reviews the existing germline report Tumor tissue NGS for SDHA E350fs (same comprehensive panel as the PIK3CA/MAP2K1 confirmation) The E350fs frameshift was called from ctDNA but not seen in the tumor NGS that already reported L306P and Y408N. Confirming or refuting E350fs in tissue clarifies whether it is a true third SDHA hit, a subclonal event present in a region not sampled by the original tumor block, or a ctDNA artifact. Decision impact is incremental rather than gating because biallelic inactivation is already established by L306P + Y408N; the value is in mapping clonal architecture before any future recurrence is biopsied. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 shared with PIK3CA/MAP2K1 block Tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay (Signatera) or tumor-naive comprehensive ctDNA panel (Guardant360, FoundationOne Liquid CDx) The case is post-R0 with no measurable disease and the existing ctDNA call surface already showed SDHA E350fs plus PIK3CA and MAP2K1 variants, so plasma is informative in this patient. Serial ctDNA gives a lead-time signal for recurrence well ahead of cross-sectional imaging, and the assay can be either tumor-informed (Signatera; lower limit of detection but bespoke design takes 4-6 weeks) or tumor-naive (Guardant360 / FoundationOne Liquid CDx; off-the-shelf but less sensitive for low-tumor-fraction MRD). GIST has weaker prospective MRD validation than colorectal or lung, so frame this as informative rather than gating. Natera (Signatera, tumor-informed ctDNA MRD) · test info · 13011 McCallen Pass, Building A, Austin, TX 78753 · 1-650-249-9090 5-10 mL plasma (Streck tube). Signatera baseline also needs an FFPE block. Baseline paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma surveillance: rapid-sequence whole-body MRI (skull base to pelvis) plus Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT SDHx carriers carry a lifetime paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma risk that warrants imaging surveillance even when the index tumor is a GIST; current consensus (Endocrine Society 2014, ENS@T) recommends biennial rapid-sequence whole-body MRI from skull base to pelvis, with Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT as the most sensitive functional tracer for SDHx-driven PGL (pmid:31369093, pmid:23934599). Establishing a clean baseline now also gives the recurrence-monitoring strategy a clean comparison point for the resected GIST. Whether to defer DOTATATE until the SDHA germline result returns is a reasonable cost discussion, but baseline whole-body MRI should not wait. Treating-center academic radiology (NCI-designated center with a neuroendocrine-tumor program) no specimen; imaging only Plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines (LC-MS/MS) and/or 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines and catecholamines An undetected functional paraganglioma in an SDHx carrier going to surgery or anesthesia for any reason is a hypertensive-crisis hazard, so biochemical screening pairs with the imaging surveillance as the standard SDHx workup (Endocrine Society 2014 guideline). Plasma free metanephrines by LC-MS/MS is the most sensitive single test; 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines is the established alternative when plasma testing is unavailable. Mayo Clinic Laboratories (PMETF / Metanephrines, Fractionated, Free, Plasma) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710 10 mL plasma (EDTA) and/or 24-hour urine collection in acid-preservative container SDHC promoter methylation analysis by pyrosequencing or methylation-specific PCR (research / academic referral assay) Only relevant as a fallback if the SDHA story collapses on the SDHA IHC / germline / E350fs workup; in that scenario, SDHC promoter epimutation is the next-most-likely Carney-triad-pattern driver and most dSDH-GIST trials accept methylation-driven cases as SDH-deficient (pmid:31308404, pmid:25540324). Clinically-available testing is limited and the assay is mostly run at academic referral labs, so flag it now but defer the order until the SDHA workup returns. NIH Pediatric and Wild-Type GIST Clinic · test info · 10 Center Drive, Bethesda, MD 20892 · 1-240-760-6000 FFPE block or 10 unstained slides MGMT promoter methylation by pyrosequencing or methylation-specific PCR Recent data show preferential MGMT promoter hypermethylation in SDH-deficient wild-type GIST and a corresponding rationale for temozolomide activity (pmid:38132569). If the temozolomide trials (NCT03556384, NCT05661643) become the leading systemic option at recurrence, MGMT status helps predict response and prioritize patients likely to benefit. The result does not gate enrollment but adds depth to the decision once disease becomes measurable. Mayo Clinic Laboratories (MGMTM / MGMT Promoter Methylation, Tumor) · test info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710 FFPE block or 10 unstained slides; bundle with the SDHC methylation order if both are needed NF1 assessment: somatic NF1 sequencing + del/dup on the comprehensive tumor panel; germline NF1 covered by the row-1 hereditary PGL/PCC panel NF1-related GIST is the other KIT/PDGFRA-WT subtype that keeps SDHB staining intact, so it sits squarely in the differential raised by this case's retained-SDHB result. It is RAS/MAPK-driven through neurofibromin loss (pmid:16096406, pmid:27011036), which would also give the ctDNA MAP2K1 P124S call a coherent mechanistic home. Assessing NF1 matters mainly if the SDHA workup fails to confirm SDH deficiency; skipping it in that scenario would leave the WT-GIST subtype call, and the imatinib-sparing rationale, on weaker footing. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 shared FFPE block with the PIK3CA/MAP2K1 panel for somatic NF1; germline NF1 is included in the row-1 PGL blood/saliva panel

Decision support, not medical advice. Confirm assay availability and current standards with the treating team and the local pathology service.

docs.title: Workup considerations (the shared first steps)
docs.text:
This is a biomarker-gated case. Three actions are shared first steps to take regardless of what happens later, and the entire systemic-therapy ranking below is conditional on confirming SDH-deficiency (dsdh_ihc:positive) on the re-cut:

  1. Active surveillance (lead action while NED) — see Rank 1.
  2. SDHB + SDHA IHC re-cut with a positive internal control, germline SDHA panel, and tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants, in one tissue pull — see Rank 2. This resolves the SDHB-intact / biallelic-SDHA paradox and locks the dSDH label that every recurrence trial screens on.
  3. NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study enrollment + cancer-genetics counseling — see Rank 3.

Cross-cutting caveat. The ranking is scoped to the patient's targetable features. If the SDHB/SDHA re-cut does not confirm SDH-deficiency, the systemic options (ranks 4–10) foreclose and the next call is SDHC promoter-methylation testing; standard-of-care for the indication then becomes a separate conversation with the treating team. The ctDNA-only PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S calls are less-certain predictors than tissue-confirmed alterations and must be confirmed in tissue before the PI3Kα or MEK pathways are acted on.

docs.title: Rank 1. Active surveillance — structured imaging + PGL/PCC screening; no adjuvant systemic therapy
docs.text:
Board: endorsed by all five personas (agreement 1.0).

Every persona lands here as the now-move. Four ranked it first outright (advocate, concensusite, conservative, critic); the risktaker, who led with a systemic agent, states plainly that an NED patient gets no adjuvant therapy. No adjuvant agent bends the recurrence curve in this subset, so committing chronic toxicity now buys nothing and forecloses option space. NCCN and ESMO both place SDH-expression-negative GIST in the avoid-adjuvant column.

  • Likelihood of desired effect: the effect is option-preservation, not tumor control. Cross-society guidelines plus Boikos 2016 (imatinib 1/49 PR) close adjuvant systemic therapy in this subset.
  • Toxicity: none (imaging + biochemical screening; the soft cost is scan anxiety).
  • Why this rank: it is the guideline-aligned lead for NED dSDH-GIST and the unanimous board position.
  • Key risks / open questions: recurrence is the expectation (~71%), so the imaging schedule must actually run on time; multifocal-primary + resected-M1 places this patient past the cleanest localized natural-history cohorts (the ~2.5-yr median EFS is a floor, not a ceiling); an undetected functional paraganglioma in an SDHx carrier going to anesthesia is a hypertensive-crisis hazard, which is why PGL/PCC baseline screening pairs with the imaging plan. Whole-body MRI vs CT backbone and the patient's travel tolerance are unresolved.
  • Evidence: PMID 27011036, PMID 29413424, PMID 30383140.

docs.title: Rank 2. SDHB + SDHA IHC re-cut + germline SDHA panel + tumor NGS confirmation (one-tissue-pull diagnostic gate)
docs.text:
Board: endorsed by all five personas (agreement 1.0).

All five personas demand this. The biallelic SDHA call (~85% combined VAF) should destabilize the complex and abolish SDHB staining, yet the report reads SDHB intact. The critic put it most sharply: every dSDH-GIST trial entry phenotype runs through SDHB-IHC loss, so this is a structural threat to the whole trial portfolio, not a footnote. The germline SDHA result drives cascade testing and the lifetime PGL program; the SDHA IHC arbitrates whether this is SDHA-driven or a non-SDHA SDHx driver (where SDHC methylation is the fallback).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: diagnostic certainty — resolves the SDHB paradox, confirms the driver, and gates trial eligibility.
  • Toxicity: none (germline blood draw, IHC re-cut on archival FFPE, comprehensive tumor NGS).
  • Why this rank: load-bearing for everything downstream; it adds only 2–4 weeks before any recurrence contingency can move.
  • Key risk: if SDHB and SDHA IHC both read intact after a clean re-stain, the dSDH label collapses, the trial-route options foreclose, and SDHC promoter methylation becomes the next fallback (academic referral, 4–8 weeks). Whether PIK3CA R93W / MAP2K1 P124S confirm in tissue determines whether the PI3Kα / MEK pathways survive at all.
  • Evidence: PMID 39927693, PMID 35546442, PMID 23023976.

docs.title: Rank 3. NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) + cancer-genetics counseling
docs.text:
Board: endorsed by advocate, concensusite, conservative, risktaker (agreement 0.8).

The patient is NED, so most contingency trials are blocked by measurable-disease requirements, but the registry is not; it provides NIH wt-GIST clinic access, the SDHC-methylation fallback pathway, biospecimen banking, and family cascade testing. The counseling visit folds the germline SDHA result and the POLE R1679C VUS framing into one coherent family-risk conversation. NCCN mandates genetic-counseling referral for every SDH-deficient GIST.

  • Likelihood of desired effect: high infrastructure yield; no tumor-control claim.
  • Toxicity: none (observational enrollment + a counseling visit; one in-person NIH baseline).
  • Why this rank: the only move that honors the trial preference today at zero toxicity. The open variable is whether the patient's geography supports the baseline visit (OHSU / Texas Children's are alternative operational fits).
  • Evidence: NCT03739827, PMID 21173220, PMID 32424176.

Ranks 4–10 are recurrence contingencies, each conditional on SDH-deficiency confirmed on the re-cut (If SDH-deficiency is confirmed on SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut). None is a now-move while the patient is NED.

docs.title: Rank 4. Sunitinib at first measurable recurrence (not adjuvant)
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Board: endorsed by advocate, concensusite, conservative, critic (agreement 0.8).

The one FDA-approved, guideline-preferred contingency with dSDH-specific data. It is reached at measurable recurrence regardless of the exact WT-GIST subtype.

  • Likelihood of desired effect: moderate-to-low — 7/38 (18%) objective response in dSDH-GIST (Boikos 2016), the best-replicated systemic signal but well below KIT-mutant activity. The critic reads 18% as directional rather than dependable (retrospective, ROBINS-I Moderate).
  • Toxicity: Moderate (fatigue, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, diarrhea) — the most predictable toxicity tail on the table.
  • Counter-productive MoA: Low — anti-angiogenic VEGFR blockade can impair wound healing if a future re-resection is on the table.
  • Why this rank: the consensus opening move at recurrence; predictable where the newer agents are not. The advocate's only push (a preference qualification, not a dissent) is that the trial menu should sit alongside sunitinib for a trial-preferring patient.
  • Evidence: PMID 27011036, PMID 17046465.

docs.title: Rank 5. Temozolomide (MGMT-methylation-enriched), trial route preferred
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by concensusite, conservative, critic, risktaker (agreement 0.8).

Doubly gated: it needs both dSDH confirmation and MGMT methylation (~24% prevalence, status unknown here), and the entire clinical signal rests on a 5-patient series.

  • Likelihood of desired effect: moderate only if MGMT-methylated — 2/5 PR (Yebra 2022); low or absent in unmethylated tumors. Order the MGMT test now so the result is ready if recurrence makes this live.
  • Toxicity: Moderate (thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, fatigue, nausea) — not worth incurring in an MGMT-unmethylated tumor.
  • Counter-productive MoA: Low — alkylator exposure without MGMT methylation incurs cytopenias for little effect.
  • Why this rank: what is guideline-aligned is the trial-enrollment route, not temozolomide as a standard agent; n=5 is hypothesis-generating. Enrolling trial NCT05661643 (Asan, Korea) requires measurable disease.
  • Evidence: PMID 34426440, PMID 36198483, NCT05661643.

docs.title: Rank 6. Olverembatinib (HQP1351), trial route only
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by conservative, critic, risktaker (agreement 0.6).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: moderate — 6/26 (23.1%) PR, mPFS 25.7 mo (Qiu 2025) in the exact subtype, but a single phase-1b cohort, unreplicated.
  • Toxicity: Low (anemia, transaminitis, hyperuricemia, leukocytosis; all G3+ rates < 20%) — the cleanest safety sheet of the new agents, though figures are pooled across the full 66-patient basket, not the 26-patient GIST cohort.
  • Counter-productive MoA: Moderate — non-canonical mechanism in a KIT-WT tumor; efficacy borrows from VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, not the labeled KIT/ABL target.
  • Why this rank: two structural caveats, agreed rather than dissented. The "phase 3" NCT06640361 is single-arm with a PFS-rate endpoint and no comparator, so it will not deliver randomized evidence; and its SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion is one this patient may not currently meet until the re-cut resolves the intact stain. Access outside China (Ascentage) is uncertain.
  • Evidence: PMID 41184234, NCT06640361.

docs.title: Rank 7. Rogaratinib (pan-FGFR1–4), trial route only
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by conservative, critic, risktaker; dissent by concensusite (agreement 0.4).

The most contested row on the board. The risktaker ranked it first as the biggest swing; the concensusite is the clean dissent (a single-arm n=24 cohort closed to accrual appears in no guideline and cannot head the plan).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: highest reported — 10/24 (41.7%) PR, mPFS 31 mo (Merriam 2026) — but single-arm n=24 and unreplicated; the 91.7% DCR may be inflated by dSDH indolence, though the 41.7% PR fraction stands as genuine regression.
  • Toxicity: unresolved — the per-grade AE table is not retrievable from the abstract, the empty ClinicalTrials.gov results tab, or the paywalled full text (class effects: hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, diarrhea, reported without grades). This is the conservative's dissent (on toxicity, not a veto, since nothing is treated today).
  • Counter-productive MoA: Moderate — single-arm DCR may reflect indolence rather than drug effect; FGFR dependence unreplicated.
  • Why this rank: a real, possibly best-in-subtype efficacy signal held to trial-route-only by an access wall (closed to accrual; Bayer has stepped back) and an unverifiable safety table. The recruiting pemigatinib cohort (Rank 9) is the practical way to cash the FGFR bet.
  • Evidence: PMID 42191879, PMID 31666694, NCT04595747.

docs.title: Rank 8. Belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor), off-label or LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by advocate, risktaker (agreement 0.4).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: uncertain in GIST — no readout; the only efficacy anchor is the cross-indication PPGL cohort (ORR 26%, LITESPARK-015) in sibling SDH-loss biology.
  • Toxicity: Moderate (anemia, fatigue, hypoxia) — anemia compounded here by the Roux-en-Y anatomy (B12/iron malabsorption).
  • Counter-productive MoA: Low — direct driver-axis blockade, but a mechanism-matched agent (guadecitabine) returned 0/9 in this subtype, so target engagement may not translate.
  • Why this rank: what belzutifan has that the FGFR agents lack is access (approved, usable off-label without a trial slot). The HIF-2α pipeline beyond it has thinned (DFF332, NKT-2152 discontinued). Watch the LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075) for an ASCO 2026 / WCGIC readout.
  • Evidence: NCT04924075, PMID 35324464, PMID 15652751.

docs.title: Rank 9. Pemigatinib (FGFR1–3), PEMIGIST trial (NCT07434843, recruiting, DFCI)
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by advocate, risktaker (agreement 0.4).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: unknown — no clinical readout in dSDH-GIST; the rationale rests entirely on the rogaratinib FGFR signal and a shared PDX response. Another 24-patient single-arm design.
  • Toxicity: Moderate (hyperphosphatemia, stomatitis, serous retinal detachment, nail/skin changes) on a days-1–14-of-21 schedule needing phosphate + ophthalmologic monitoring.
  • Counter-productive MoA: Low — shares rogaratinib's unreplicated-pathway uncertainty.
  • Why this rank: for a trial-preferring patient this is the more actionable FGFR option because it is recruiting and US-based, even though rogaratinib carries the higher published number — lead with the door that opens. Suzanne George (DFCI) is the logical referral.
  • Evidence: NCT07434843, PMID 31666694, PMID 42191879.

docs.title: Rank 10. Regorafenib — guideline-sequenced 3L TKI after sunitinib
docs.text:
Conditional on dSDH confirmation. Status: considered with caveats. Board: endorsed by concensusite (agreement 0.2).

  • Likelihood of desired effect: low/modest — no dSDH-specific data; GRID HR 0.27 is a KIT-mutant result, dSDH activity extrapolated.
  • Toxicity: Moderate (hand-foot skin reaction G3+ 20%, hypertension G3+ 23%, diarrhea).
  • Counter-productive MoA: Low — anti-angiogenic; dSDH benefit extrapolated, not demonstrated.
  • Why this rank: the established 3L rung once sunitinib is exhausted, with the inference gap stated out loud rather than letting the HR 0.27 carry weight it did not earn in this genotype (NCCN sequencing is category-2A consensus).
  • Evidence: PMID 23177515, PMID 40045030.

docs.title: Rank 11. DRUP off-label matched-therapy basket (NCT02925234) — post-board re-screen addition
docs.text:
Post-board addition, not board-voted. A recurrence-contingent access route to matched trametinib (for MAP2K1 P124S) or alpelisib (for PIK3CA R93W), not a variant-matched efficacy readout.

Status: considered with caveats. Not deliberated by the board — surfaced by a post-board re-screen of the trial registry, so agreement is 0.0 by absence of a vote, not by neutral consensus.

A registry re-screen after the board adjourned turned up the Drug Rediscovery Protocol, which matches an approved drug to a genomic profile through its own molecular tumor board rather than a fixed gene list. On paper that opens two routes for this patient: trametinib against the ctDNA MAP2K1 P124S call, alpelisib against the ctDNA PIK3CA R93W call. What it does not open is an efficacy readout — DRUP publishes pooled clinical benefit across all its cohorts, never per-arm, so no number attaches to either route here.

  • Likelihood of desired effect: unknown at these variants. The only figure DRUP reports is pooled: 34% clinical benefit (objective response or SD ≥16 weeks), median duration 9 months (95% CI 8–11), across 215 patients spanning many drug-variant pairs (PMID 31570881). Neither the MAP2K1 nor the PIK3CA arm has a published effect size, both calls are ctDNA-only, and R93W is non-canonical.
  • Toxicity: Moderate — pooled treatment-related grade ≥3 AEs ran 18% (rare-cancer subgroup) to 24% (common-cancer subgroup) in the 500-patient DRUP update, with no fatal treatment-related events (PMID 35046062). There is no per-arm AE table; trametinib-arm (rash, diarrhea, retinopathy, cardiomyopathy) and alpelisib-arm (hyperglycemia, rash, diarrhea) class effects come from each drug's label, not from DRUP.
  • Counter-productive MoA: Moderate — the MEK / PI3Kα match rests on ctDNA-only, non-canonical variants; R93W outside the alpelisib hotspots may not confer the pathway dependence the match assumes.
  • Why this rank: it lands low for the same reason the board declined to rank any PI3Kα or MEK option in round 1 — the critic and the concensusite both passed on that axis because R93W and P124S are ctDNA-only and non-canonical, and that objection carries straight over. The same gates that hold the other MAP2K1/PIK3CA baskets (MEGALiT, tersolisib, RLY-2608) at weak fit apply here: tissue confirmation of the variants, R93W outside the alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots, a protocol that requires progression on standard therapy with measurable disease, and Dutch-only siting. It is logged so the enrollment door is visible, framed as an access route rather than evidence of benefit — the board did not endorse, dissent from, or veto it, and this row does not manufacture a vote it never received.
  • Evidence: NCT02925234, PMID 31570881, PMID 35046062.

docs.title: Rank 12. Adjuvant imatinib — NOT RECOMMENDED
docs.text:
Status: not recommended (veto by advocate; agreement −0.4).

Logged so the reflex "GIST means imatinib" reach is documented and not re-litigated on the post-op note. KIT is wild-type and the response rate is ~2% (1/49 PR, Boikos 2016); the subset was never represented in the adjuvant RCTs and does not respond. There is no version of the efficacy-toxicity weight that rescues a 2% response against three years of periorbital edema, fatigue, cytopenias, and monitoring burden, which would also spend the screening eligibility for the contingency trials the patient prefers. Kept in the table (not dropped) per the no-silent-veto rule.

  • Evidence: PMID 27011036, PMID 19303137, PMID 30383140.

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib, inavolisib, RLY-2608) as standalone recs — the only PIK3CA call is R93W, a non-canonical, out-of-hotspot variant detected on ctDNA only; predictive validity is not established at this variant, so none is ranked on its own merits. Alpelisib appears only as one arm of the DRUP access route at Rank 11, contingent on tissue confirmation and molecular-tumor-board sign-off.
  • MEK inhibitors (trametinib, cobimetinib) as standalone recs — rest on the ctDNA-only MAP2K1 P124S call; cross-tumor and unconfirmed. Trametinib appears only as the other arm of the DRUP access route at Rank 11, not as an evidenced pick.
  • Glutaminase inhibition (telaglenastat / CB-839) — a dedicated SDH-deficient GIST trial cohort existed but the program was discontinued, and the metabolic rationale is mechanistically undercut (pyruvate carboxylation, not glutamine, is the dominant anaplerotic route in SDH-loss). Not enrollable.
  • Mechanism-matched agents already closed by negative subtype-specific trials: guadecitabine (0/9), linsitinib / IGF1R (0/20), vandetanib (0/9).
  • Tumor-agnostic ICI (pembrolizumab) for POLE — excluded: POLE R1679C is outside the proofreading hotspots and the tumor is TMB <1 / MSS, so this is a counseling item, not a therapy.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text:
Full end-to-end re-run on 2026-06-26 under the updated Libby workflow. The research tier was refreshed (trials 22, clinical-evidence 28, preclinical-evidence 27, target-validation 13, accessibility 25), the virtual tumor board was run for the first time on this case (5 positions, 20 cross-critiques), and this synthesis was produced from the board plus the refreshed dossier. The refresh surfaced new positive dSDH-GIST systemic signals that postdate the case's initial run — olverembatinib (Qiu 2025) and rogaratinib (Merriam 2026) — which enter as recurrence contingencies. The recommendations table was authored by the PI agent; this page was finalized deterministically after repeated infrastructure interruptions to the long-form generation, preserving the agent's ranking and board appraisal verbatim. ctDNA-only and non-canonical calls (PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S) carry the predictive-certainty hedge. The case has no low-positive IHC expression markers, so that rule did not fire.

Refreshed on 2026-07-09 (lighter re-run, no board re-vote). A post-board trial re-screen added the DRUP molecular-tumor-board basket (NCT02925234, trametinib/alpelisib arms) and the clinician appended one evidence row anchored on van der Velden 2019 (PMID 31570881, the primary DRUP outcomes paper) with safety from Hoes 2022 (PMID 35046062). DRUP folds in at Rank 11 as considered_with_caveats with empty endorsed/dissent/veto and a 0.0 agreement score, because the board did not deliberate on it — it is a recurrence-contingent access route to matched trametinib or alpelisib, not a variant-matched efficacy readout, and DRUP publishes only pooled clinical benefit (34%, no per-arm figure). All board-derived rankings and agreement scores for ranks 1–10 and the imatinib veto row (now rank 12) are unchanged. Reference-verification on this refresh confirmed all three promoted DRUP identifiers resolve and match their claims (NCT02925234 recruiting; PMID 31570881 the Nature DRUP paper; PMID 35046062 the Clin Cancer Res rare-cancers safety update).

docs.title: 1. sunitinib (Sutent) — 2L TKI for dSDH-GIST contingency sunitinib, SU011248, Sutent
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

If the patient recurs, sunitinib 50 mg PO 4-on/2-off is the first-line TKI of choice on the strength of Boikos 2016 plus the von Mehren / Dedousis 2025 reviews. The drug is approved, widely stocked, and the prescription is straightforward — the practical question is timing (wait for measurable progression, then start) rather than access.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (advanced GIST after imatinib failure/intolerance; RCC; pNET; adjuvant RCC). EMA-approved. GuidelinesNCCN-supported as 2L TKI in advanced GIST regardless of subtype; Boikos 2016 (NIH wt-GIST clinic) provides the dSDH-specific anchor — 18% ORR vs imatinib's 2%, the empirical reason sunitinib is the preferred first systemic option at recurrence. Geographic scopeGlobal; approved in US, EU, AU, JP, and most major markets.

Next steps

  1. At first measurable recurrence, start sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off. Confirm dosing with the prescribing oncologist; some dSDH-GIST patients tolerate 37.5 mg continuous better.
  2. Baseline TSH, BP, LFTs, CBC; recheck cycles 1-3 then quarterly.
  3. Pfizer Oncology Together: have the patient enroll up front for copay support (1-877-744-5675).
  4. If progression on sunitinib, move to regorafenib (3L).

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Patient-assistance line: 1-877-744-5675.

Payer / coverage notes. GIST is an on-label indication; Medicare and commercial payers cover sunitinib for advanced GIST without molecular stratification. Prior auth is routine but uncomplicated. Pfizer Oncology Together copay-assistance program available for eligible commercially insured patients.

Notes. Technically off-label in the sense that the GIST label is anchored on KIT-mutant cohorts and the dSDH subset was barely represented in the registration trial — but no payer treats this as off-label; reimbursement is routine.

docs.title: 2. temozolomide (Temodar) — targeted off-label or trial-based for dSDH-GIST temozolomide, TMZ, Temodar, Temodal
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Two access paths here. Trial-only via the Asan/Korea trial (NCT05661643) is the cleanest if the patient can travel; UCSD's NCT03556384 is no longer enrolling. Off-label TMZ via generic Rx is the practical fallback at first recurrence — supported by Yebra 2022 and the MGMT-methylation rationale, but expect a prior-auth fight with most US payers.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (newly diagnosed glioblastoma with radiotherapy and as maintenance; anaplastic astrocytoma; refractory anaplastic astrocytoma — also approved 2024 for additional indications under Project Renewal). EMA-approved. Widely available as generic. GuidelinesNot on NCCN GIST guidelines. Off-guideline but supported by Yebra 2022 (PMID 34426440; 2/5 PR, 100% DCR in dSDH-GIST mini-cohort) plus the parallel preclinical PDX data. MGMT promoter methylation (Flego 2024 PMID 38132569, Giger 2022 PMID 36198483) is the candidate response biomarker. Geographic scopeTrial: Korea-only currently. Off-label Rx: US + EU + AU + JP — temozolomide is approved and generic everywhere.

Next steps

  1. At first recurrence with measurable disease, order MGMT promoter methylation on tumor tissue (or re-cut from the resection block) — this is the load-bearing biomarker for off-label approval and trial enrollment.
  2. If MGMT-methylated and travel-capable: email Min-Hee Ryu (miniryu@amc.seoul.kr) about an Asan slot in NCT05661643.
  3. If not travel-capable: prepare an off-label prior-auth packet with the Yebra 2022 PMID, MGMT result, dSDH diagnosis, and the failed-imatinib/sunitinib lines once those occur. Generic TMZ keeps cash-pay viable.
  4. Watch for the NCT03556384 readout (UCSD) — primary completion June 2025 per the registry; data could change the off-label-prior-auth calculus.

Trial pathways

docs.title: 3. olverembatinib (HQP1351) — multikinase inhibitor for dSDH-GIST contingency olverembatinib, HQP1351, GZD824, D824, 耐立克
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Expanded access program Not yet accessible Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

There is no clean US route to this drug right now, which is the honest headline despite it having the best dSDH-GIST efficacy data of the newer agents. The phase 3 sits at a single Guangzhou site, and the named-patient program is geared toward the approved leukemia indications rather than GIST. If the patient recurs, the realistic moves are to ask Ascentage whether named-patient GIST supply is possible and, separately, whether the China trial is feasible.

RegulatoryNMPA-approved in China (TKI-resistant T315I chronic- or accelerated-phase CML), and used in China for Ph+ ALL per CSCO guidance. Investigational for GIST everywhere; no FDA or EMA approval for any indication. GuidelinesNot on NCCN or ESMO GIST guidelines. The dSDH-GIST signal comes from Qiu 2025 (PMID 41184234): 23.1% ORR and 25.7-month median PFS in a 26-patient SDH-deficient cohort, which is what the phase 3 NCT06640361 is built on. Geographic scopeApproved in China only (CML / Ph+ ALL). The dSDH-GIST phase 3 is single-site in Guangzhou, China. No US or EU access outside a case-by-case named-patient request.

Next steps

  1. Treat olverembatinib as a watch item, not an actionable option, while the patient is NED in the US.
  2. If the patient recurs with measurable disease, resolve the SDHB-IHC re-stain first, since SDHB-IHC loss is the trial's entry biomarker and her current stain reads intact.
  3. Email NPP-olverembatinib@ascentage.com to ask whether named-patient supply is available for SDH-deficient GIST, and on what terms, in the US.
  4. Only if the patient is willing and able to travel: contact Yifan Zhai (yzhai@ascentage.com, +86-20-28068501) about the Guangzhou phase 3.

docs.title: 4. rogaratinib (BAY 1163877) — pan-FGFR inhibitor for dSDH-GIST rogaratinib, BAY 1163877, BAY1163877
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Frustrating one. Rogaratinib has the best dSDH-GIST numbers of any systemic agent so far, but the only trial is closed to accrual, Bayer has stepped back, and there is no approval or compassionate route. The live way to test the same FGFR idea is the recruiting pemigatinib trial (NCT07434843) at DFCI, which is why that row, not this one, is the actionable FGFR path.

RegulatoryInvestigational; no FDA or EMA approval. Bayer has stepped back from the broader rogaratinib program, and the surviving study is the NCI sarcoma / dSDH-GIST phase 2. GuidelinesNot on GIST guidelines, but this is the strongest dSDH-GIST readout to date: Merriam 2026 (PMID 42191879, Nature Medicine) reported 41.7% ORR and 31-month median PFS in the 24-patient SDH-deficient cohort of NCT04595747. Geographic scopeUS — 18 NCI-network sites ran the study, but it is closed to new enrollment.

Next steps

  1. Use this row as the evidence anchor for the FGFR-inhibitor rationale, not as an enrollment route, since NCT04595747 is closed to new patients.
  2. For a live FGFR option at recurrence, go to the pemigatinib trial (NCT07434843) and contact Suzanne George at DFCI.
  3. Ask the dSDH-GIST trial network whether a rogaratinib successor or expansion is planned given the positive Merriam 2026 readout.
  4. Watch for any FDA filing or new sponsor for rogaratinib, which would reopen this path.

docs.title: 5. belzutifan (Welireg) — HIF-2α inhibitor for dSDH-GIST contingency belzutifan, MK-6482, PT2977, Welireg
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Two real paths. The LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort is recruiting at 14 US sites — that is the cleanest entry point if the patient relapses with measurable disease. Approved in US and EU for non-GIST indications.

  5. Watch ASCO 2026 / WCGIC for the LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort interim readout — could shift this to a stronger off-label case.

docs.title: 7. regorafenib (Stivarga) — 3L TKI for dSDH-GIST contingency regorafenib, BAY 73-4506, Stivarga
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Standard 3L option after sunitinib failure. The dSDH-GIST evidence base is thinner than for sunitinib (GRID enrolled mostly KIT-mutant disease), but regorafenib is the accepted 3L per NCCN and is reimbursed without controversy. Toxicity counseling matters more than access here.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (advanced GIST after imatinib + sunitinib; metastatic CRC; HCC after sorafenib). EMA-approved. GuidelinesNCCN-supported as 3L TKI for advanced GIST. dSDH-GIST cohort data is by extrapolation; Dedousis 2025 review (PMID 40045030) calls activity 'modest, similar to KIT-mutant 3L'. Geographic scopeGlobal; approved in US, EU, JP, and most major markets.

Next steps

  1. On sunitinib progression, start regorafenib 160 mg PO daily 3 weeks on / 1 week off.
  2. Pre-treatment: BP optimization, dental check, dermatology baseline for HFSR.
  3. Enroll in Bayer's $0 copay program if commercially insured (1-866-581-4992).
  4. Plan dose modifications proactively — most patients need to drop to 120 mg or alternate-week dosing within the first 2-3 cycles.

docs.title: 11. RLY-2608 (zovegalisib) — mutant-selective PI3Kα inhibitor for PIK3CA R93W RLY-2608, RLY2608, zovegalisib
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Trial-only, and the most forgiving of the PI3Kα baskets for this patient's situation: it reads ctDNA, has an 'other solid tumors' group, and the sponsor can approve non-canonical variants one by one. The catch is the variant itself. R93W sits outside the hotspots these mutant-selective drugs are designed around, so the real gate is getting Relay to confirm it qualifies, on top of tissue-confirming the call. Lowest-confidence of the PIK3CA rows alongside tersolisib.

RegulatoryInvestigational; no approval anywhere. Phase 1 in advanced solid tumors, advancing toward later-phase study in PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer. GuidelinesOff-guideline; investigational. Geographic scopeUS + EU + AU recruiting sites.

Next steps

  1. Order tissue NGS (FoundationOne CDx or paired tumor/normal) to confirm PIK3CA R93W is clonal in tumor rather than ctDNA noise.
  2. Email ClinicalTrials@relaytx.com (or call 617-322-0731) to ask whether PIK3CA R93W is on the trial's accepted variant list; this is the load-bearing question before any screening visit.
  3. If accepted, find the nearest recruiting site through the registry sites list and request a slot at first measurable recurrence.
  4. If not accepted, drop RLY-2608; there is no compassionate route and the variant is too weak to justify off-label PI3Kα inhibition.

docs.title: 14. alpelisib (Piqray) — PI3Kα inhibitor for PIK3CA R93W (non-canonical) alpelisib, BYL719, Piqray
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Burke 2012 biochemistry classifies ABD-domain variants like R88Q/R93 as weakly activating compared with the canonical helical/kinase hotspots, and there is no histology rationale for PI3Kα blockade in GIST. R93W is not on the validated label hotspot list. Geographic scopeUS + EU + AU + JP — approved in major markets for HR+/HER2- mBC indication.

Next steps

  1. Confirm PIK3CA R93W on tissue NGS before pursuing this path (currently ctDNA-only).
  2. Default to the tersolisib trial (NCT05768139) if PI3Kα inhibition is on the table — selective inhibitor with a better therapeutic window than alpelisib.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer with palbociclib + fulvestrant 2024). EMA-approved (2025). GuidelinesNCCN-supported only for HR+/HER2- mBC with canonical PIK3CA hotspots per the registration trial population. Not on NCCN GIST guidelines. Geographic scopeUS + EU — recently approved in both markets for the HR+/HER2- mBC indication.

Next steps

  1. Tissue NGS confirmation of PIK3CA R93W (currently ctDNA-only) is the gate.
  2. Default to the tersolisib trial (NCT05768139); off-label inavolisib has no advantage over alpelisib without comparative data in non-canonical variants.
  3. If commercial-payer denial cycle becomes the question, the Genentech Access Solutions team handles the appeals (1-877-436-3683).

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label for GIST and for non-canonical PIK3CA variants. The INAVO120 trial used canonical hotspots; payers will mirror the label. Approximate WAC similar to alpelisib (~$17,000-20,000/month).

docs.text:

Closed door. SARC's phase 2 returned 0/20 RECIST responses and the parent program was shelved. The IGF-1R hypothesis in dSDH-GIST has been tested and is off the table; kept in the dossier as the audit trail for why the board does not need to revisit it.

RegulatoryInvestigational; never approved. Astellas terminated development after multiple negative trials (adrenocortical carcinoma, GIST). GuidelinesOff-guideline; discontinued. Geographic scopen/a — drug discontinued globally.

Next steps

  1. Mark IGF-1R inhibition as off the table.
  2. If a next-generation IGF-1R agent ever re-enters trials, re-evaluate the hypothesis — but the dSDH-GIST clinical signal was a hard negative.

docs.title: 20. olaparib + temozolomide combination — PARP + alkylator for dSDH-GIST contingency olaparib, AZD2281, Lynparza, temozolomide, TMZ, Temodar
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Mechanism-sound but evidence-thin. The Sulkowski 2018/2020 papers establish the BRCA-like phenotype in SDH-loss models, and Singh 2023 reports one durable response in a multiply-relapsed patient. With no trial currently enrolling this combination in dSDH-GIST and an aggressive prior-auth fight ahead, this is a late-line option after the temozolomide and pemigatinib trials are exhausted.

RegulatoryBoth components individually FDA- and EMA-approved (olaparib: BRCA1/2-mutated breast/ovarian/pancreatic/prostate cancer, HRD-positive ovarian maintenance; temozolomide: glioblastoma, anaplastic astrocytoma, others). Combination is not approved. GuidelinesNot on NCCN GIST guidelines. The mechanism rationale rests on Sulkowski 2018 (Nat Genet) + Sulkowski 2020 (Nature) — SDH/FH-loss creates a BRCA-like phenotype at chromatin via succinate-mediated KDM4B inhibition. Singh 2023 (PMID 36151992) is the single-patient case report showing clinical response in multiply-relapsed dSDH-GIST + PGL. Geographic scopeUS + EU + AU + JP — both drugs approved in major markets, off-label for this combination and this indication.

Next steps

  1. Reserve for late-line use after sunitinib/regorafenib/ripretinib and after temozolomide and pemigatinib trial paths are exhausted.
  2. If pursued: order MGMT methylation (response biomarker for the TMZ component) and HRD assay on tumor tissue.
  3. Off-label prior-auth packet should cite Sulkowski 2018 (PMID 30013182), Sulkowski 2020 (PMID 32494005), and Singh 2023 (PMID 36151992).
  4. AstraZeneca Access 360 (1-844-275-2360) for copay support if approved; Merck patient-assistance for temozolomide (1-800-727-5400) — note that generic TMZ keeps the alkylator cost low.

Cash-pay olaparib is prohibitive; AstraZeneca Access 360 patient-assistance is the realistic financial path if approved.

Notes. No active trial of this combination in dSDH-GIST. If a trial opens, that becomes the dominant path.

docs.title: 21. ripretinib (Qinlock) — 4L+ TKI for dSDH-GIST contingency ripretinib, DCC-2618, Qinlock
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Fourth-line option once sunitinib and regorafenib are exhausted. The drug is FDA-approved and Deciphera's patient-access program (AccessPoint) is unusually robust — rapid-start, bridge coverage, and full free drug for uninsured. Practical access is rarely the barrier; the question is whether ripretinib outperforms simply rotating to a clinical trial at this stage in dSDH-GIST.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (advanced GIST after ≥3 prior TKIs including imatinib). EMA-approved. GuidelinesNCCN-supported as 4L+ TKI for advanced GIST. Mavroeidis 2025 review notes the dSDH-GIST evidence base for ripretinib is the weakest of the three post-imatinib TKIs because INVICTUS enrolled vanishingly few wt-GIST patients; use is by extrapolation. Geographic scopeUS + EU + JP; approved in most major markets.

Next steps

  1. Document prior imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib lines in the chart before submitting prior auth (label requires ≥3).
  2. Call Deciphera AccessPoint (1-833-432-2237) to enroll before the first prescription — they handle the prior-auth paperwork.
  3. Re-evaluate the trial landscape at the 4L transition point — the temozolomide and pemigatinib SDH-deficient-GIST trials may be the better answer at recurrence than ripretinib, depending on what reads out by then.

Closed door. Calithera wound the company down and sold off telaglenastat after its kidney and lung trials failed, and the SDH-deficient GIST cohort never read out positive. docs.title: 23. tersolisib (STX-478) — selective PI3Kα inhibitor for PIK3CA R93W tersolisib, STX-478
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Investigational trial-only path. The patient's PIK3CA R93W sits outside the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots — Burke 2012 biochemistry shows ABD-domain variants like R88/R93 region are weakly activating, not strong drivers. Lilly's sponsor team will need to confirm R93W is on the trial's variant-eligibility list before screening; even with that, this is the lowest-confidence row in the dossier.

RegulatoryInvestigational; no regulatory approval anywhere. IND-cleared phase 1/2. GuidelinesOff-guideline; investigational. Geographic scopeUS + EU + Japan recruiting sites.

Next steps

  1. Order FoundationOne CDx tissue NGS to confirm PIK3CA R93W as clonal in tumor (currently ctDNA-only).
  2. Email LillyTrials@Lilly.com or call 1-877-285-4559 to ask whether PIK3CA R93W is on the trial's accepted variant list — this is the load-bearing question before any screening visit.
  3. If accepted: find the nearest US site through the ClinicalTrials.gov sites URL and request a screening slot at first measurable recurrence.
  4. If not accepted: drop tersolisib from the actionable plan; the variant is too weak to justify off-label PI3Kα inhibitor cash-pay.

docs.title: 24. trametinib (Mekinist) — MEK inhibitor for MAP2K1 P124S trametinib, GSK1120212, Mekinist
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Two real questions before this becomes actionable. First: is the MAP2K1 P124S real and clonal? It is ctDNA-only right now and tissue confirmation is gated by FoundationOne CDx re-test. Second: trial vs off-label. The Tianjin trial (NCT06739395) is geographically blocked for most patients, MEGALiT looks closed, so off-label trametinib via Novartis is the practical path if the variant confirms — expect a prior-auth fight.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (BRAF V600E/K melanoma in combination with dabrafenib; BRAF V600E NSCLC; BRAF V600E anaplastic thyroid; BRAF V600E pediatric low-grade glioma). EMA-approved. GuidelinesNot on NCCN GIST guidelines. The MAP2K1 P124S rationale rests on Gao 2018 functional characterization (RAF-dependent class I activator, MEK-inhibitor sensitive in Ba/F3) plus the Gounder 2018 NEJM histiocytic sarcoma case report (MAP2K1 F53L → durable CR on trametinib). Cross-tumor extrapolation. Geographic scopeTrial: China (NCT06739395 only currently enrolling). Off-label Rx: US + EU + JP. Trametinib is approved in major markets but only for BRAF-mutant indications.

Next steps

  1. Order FoundationOne CDx tissue NGS (or paired tumor + normal) to confirm MAP2K1 P124S as clonal in tumor rather than ctDNA noise.
  2. If confirmed clonal: prepare an off-label prior-auth packet citing Gao 2018 (PMID 36442478), Gounder 2018 (PMID 26222557), and the Wagle 2014 P124 αC-helix mechanism (PMID 24265154).
  3. Confirm no new MAP2K1 basket trial has opened in the US/EU since the MEGALiT/MyCustom-02 cohorts — recheck quarterly.
  4. If the trial path is the patient's priority and US travel-only: monitor MATCH-II / NCI-MATCH-style successor protocols for a MAP2K1 arm.

docs.title: 10. NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (registry + specialty referral) NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study, NCI Pediatric Oncology Branch rare-tumor protocol
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-06-26

The cleanest specialty-care path for this patient right now. The NCI Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic is the reference center for SDH-deficient GIST, and registry enrollment opens the door to SDHC-methylation testing, longitudinal biospecimen banking, and specialist follow-up alongside community surveillance. No drug treatment is administered through the protocol — it is the gateway, not the destination.

Regulatoryn/a — observational registry, no investigational drug. Guidelinesn/a — entry point into the NCI Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic referral network. Geographic scopeUS — NIH Clinical Center (Bethesda, MD), OHSU (Portland, OR), Texas Children's Hospital (Houston, TX).

  4. Couple registry enrollment with PGL screening and genetic counseling (Carney-Stratakis risk).

docs.title: 13. active surveillance (NED post-R0 dSDH-GIST) active surveillance, watch-and-wait, imaging surveillance
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-06-26

This is the recommended pathway right now. The patient is NED after R0 resection of a multifocal SDH-deficient GIST, and the published natural history (Mei 2018, NIH 76-pt cohort: median EFS ~2.5 years, ~71% eventually recur) argues for structured surveillance rather than adjuvant imatinib. The ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guideline is explicit on avoiding adjuvant imatinib in this molecular subset.

Regulatoryn/a — surveillance pathway GuidelinesESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 and NCCN GIST guidelines both support surveillance over adjuvant TKI in SDH-deficient GIST given the near-zero imatinib response rate and indolent natural history. Geographic scopeAnywhere with access to standard oncology surveillance imaging. NIH registry enrollment requires US travel to Bethesda for the in-person visits.

Next steps

  1. Schedule cross-sectional imaging (CT abdomen/pelvis or whole-body MRI) every 3-6 months for the first 2-3 years post-resection, then space out per response.
  2. Refer to genetic counseling for the SDHA L306P germline-vs-somatic question and the POLE R1679C germline call — needed for cascade testing and for paraganglioma screening.
  3. Add baseline plasma/urine metanephrines + neck-to-pelvis MRI for PGL screening, repeat every 1-2 years given the Carney-Stratakis risk.
  4. Enroll in the NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) for specialty follow-up and biospecimen banking.
  5. Document the recurrence-contingency plan now: if relapse, first-line is sunitinib, not imatinib.

Trial pathways

Payer / coverage notes. Surveillance imaging (cross-sectional CT or whole-body MRI) is covered under standard oncologic follow-up. Whole-body MRI for SDH-mutation carriers may need prior auth depending on payer; the Mei/Boikos 2018 review and ESMO PPGL screening guidance are the citations to use.

Notes. The single most consequential 'access path' for this patient today is the decision not to start adjuvant imatinib. The systemic-therapy rows below are all contingency plans for first recurrence.

docs.title: 17. imatinib (Gleevec) — adjuvant or first-line imatinib, imatinib mesylate, STI-571, Gleevec, Glivec
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-26

Imatinib is FDA-approved and easy to get on-label, but it does not belong in this patient's plan. Boikos 2016 showed a 1/49 (2%) PR rate in dSDH-GIST, and the ESMO guideline recommends against it. The off-label classification is technical — there is no rationale to use the off-label path here.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (KIT-positive GIST, adjuvant and unresectable/metastatic; CML and several other indications). EMA-approved. GuidelinesESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 explicitly recommends against adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST. NCCN lists imatinib as standard adjuvant only for KIT-mutant high-risk GIST; KIT/PDGFRA-WT subtypes including dSDH-GIST are flagged as imatinib-insensitive. Geographic scopeGlobal; widely available as generic.

Next steps

  1. Document the explicit decision against adjuvant imatinib in the chart citing Boikos 2016 (PMID 27011036) and the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guideline.
  2. If the surgical team asks about 3-year adjuvant imatinib (PERSIST-5, SSGXVIII), note that those trials excluded the dSDH-GIST population structurally and the imatinib-insensitive genotypes recurred regardless of treatment duration.

Trial pathways

docs.title: Active surveillance — structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years then space out; no adjuvant systemic therapy (active-surveillance)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic1highThe adjuvant decision is the one place in this dossier where the high-quality evidence points somewhere, and it points away from drugs. The registration-grade adjuvant-imatinib RCTs (Z9001; SSGXVIII at 10 years; PERSIST-5; all RoB2 Low) enrolled KIT-driven disease and structurally excluded SDH-deficient GIST, and ESMO recommends against imatinib here because Boikos 2016 saw 1/49 (2%) responses in this subset. No RCT, and no single-arm trial, supports any adjuvant systemic therapy in dSDH-GIST. docs.title: sunitinib (guideline-preferred 2L TKI at first recurrence) (sunitinib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative2moderateAt first recurrence with measurable disease, sunitinib is the best-characterized systemic option on the table: FDA-approved since 2006, anchored by a placebo-controlled phase 3 (TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001; Demetri 2006) and roughly two decades of post-marketing safety, so its AEs (fatigue, diarrhea, hand-foot reaction, skin discoloration, hypertension) come with well-worn management algorithms. The dSDH-specific efficacy is modest but genuine, and this is the published preferred 2L TKI here, with 7/38 (18%) objective responses versus imatinib's 2% (Boikos 2016). I am not overselling it; the response rate sits below the newer FGFR and multikinase agents. What it offers is a predictable toxicity tail, which matters most when the alternative is an indolent tumor and an unfamiliar safety profile.18% ORR is honest but unimpressive; if the recurrence is bulky or fast-moving, a more active agent may be worth a less-charted safety profile.; Hypertension and hand-foot reaction need baseline BP and skin monitoring built in from cycle 1. critic3moderateAt measurable recurrence, sunitinib is the best-evidenced systemic option here, which is a low bar met rather than a strong endorsement. Its own pivotal is RCT-grade (Demetri 2006, n=312, TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001, RoB2 Low) but did not stratify SDH status and was overwhelmingly KIT-mutant, so the subtype-specific claim rests on Boikos 2016: 7/38 (18%) SDH-deficient responders on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, retrospective and ROBINS-I Moderate. Read the 18% as directional, not as a dependable response estimate. It edges out regorafenib and ripretinib only because their dSDH evidence base is thinner still.Indirectness: the pivotal RCT population was KIT-mutant with no SDH stratification, so the HR 0.33 does not transport cleanly to this subtype.; Boikos 2016 is retrospective (ROBINS-I Moderate) with small per-drug n and no per-AE capture; selection and confounding risk sit inside the 18% response figure. concensusite3moderateWhen measurable disease returns, the guideline-endorsed first systemic move in this subtype is sunitinib, not imatinib. NCCN GIST v1.2026 carries sunitinib as a second-line option, and for SDH-deficient disease specifically the NIH cohort (Boikos 2016) reports objective response 7/38 (18%) on sunitinib versus 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, which is the published basis ESMO 2022 cites for preferring it here. The effect is modest, but it is the consensus opening move for the contingency plan.The Boikos response figures are retrospective with small per-drug n; activity in dSDH-GIST is genuine but lower than in KIT-mutant disease.; Not applicable while the patient is NED. This is a contingency anchor for first recurrence, not an action for now. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocateconservativequalifiedpreference_fitBundling the NCI registry into rank 1 is the right instinct, it honors prefers_trials while the patient is NED, and your call to run the SDHB re-cut now is exactly what keeps trial eligibility from lapsing. Where we part is the recurrence ladder: ranking sunitinib ahead of the trial agents optimizes for the toxicity you can predict, but the stated preference is trials, so the trial route belongs alongside sunitinib rather than behind it. With no toxicity vetoes on file, the predictability premium buys this patient less than it would a tox-averse one. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitPutting sunitinib first at recurrence is exactly where NCCN GIST v1.2026 and ESMO 2022 land for this subtype, and the MGMT-gating before temozolomide keeps the off-guideline alkylator honest. The toxicity-first ordering tracks the guideline sequence rather than fighting it, so there is nothing for me to qualify on guideline-fit. Sunitinib over imatinib here rests on the same Boikos 2016 figures, 18% versus 2%, that ESMO cites. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitCritic reads the 18% sunitinib response (Boikos 2016) as directional rather than dependable, but that retrospective figure is precisely the evidence ESMO 2022 weighed when it preferred sunitinib over imatinib in this subtype. The guideline preference is collective expert calibration of the same data the critic is discounting, not a separate claim that has to outrank it. On that basis I would keep sunitinib at the front of the contingency ladder.

docs.title: clinical-trial enrollment at recurrence: SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643) (temozolomide)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowIf the tumor is MGMT-methylated, this could be the highest-yield oral option on the list. The Yebra series hit 40% ORR (2/5) with 100% disease control (PMID 34426440), the patient-derived models showed on-target killing while imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing, and about 24% of dSDH-GIST carry the MGMT methylation that predicts response (PMID 36198483). Order the MGMT test now; if it reads methylated, I would push hard for the recruiting NCT05661643 at recurrence. The honest weakness is n=5, the patient's MGMT status is unknown, and most dSDH tumors are unmethylated, so this is biomarker-gated rather than a sure thing.MGMT methylation status unknown; only ~24% of dSDH-GIST are methylated, so the predictive biomarker may not flag; Clinical signal rests on a 5-patient series; The enrolling trial NCT05661643 is in Korea, so travel feasibility is a real constraint conservative3moderateTemozolomide is a decades-old alkylator with a thoroughly mapped, predictable toxicity profile, mostly myelosuppression, fatigue, and nausea, all with standard dose-modification and antiemetic algorithms, so the safety side is well understood even though the dSDH efficacy base is thin (2/5 PR, 40% ORR; Yebra 2022). The reason it ranks here rather than lower is that the benefit is biomarker-selectable: MGMT promoter methylation sits in ~24% (8/33) of dSDH-GIST and predicts the alkylator response (Giger 2022, Flego 2024). I would gate any TMZ commitment on MGMT methylation testing first, which keeps us from pushing an unselected patient through avoidable cytopenias. An enrolling trial exists (NCT05661643) and satisfies the trial preference, though it is Korea-based and requires measurable disease.Myelosuppression is the predictable cost; without MGMT methylation the expected benefit may not justify the cytopenias.; n=5 is the entire prospective efficacy base in this subtype, so the 40% ORR is fragile. critic6lowTemozolomide is a contingency, not a recommendation, and the evidence is thin enough that I would only run it on a trial with MGMT enrichment. The clinical anchor is Yebra 2022: 2/5 (40%) PR in SDH-mutant GIST, which is n=5, a translational case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4, with no per-AE table. The one biomarker lever is real (Giger 2022: MGMT promoter hypermethylation in 8/33 (24%) SDH-deficient tumors and 0% elsewhere), so methylation testing could enrich for the likely responders before exposing anyone to an alkylator. A 5-patient series is hypothesis-generating; it does not support TMZ as a default off-label move.n=5 case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4: severe small-sample and selection bias, with a 40% ORR whose confidence interval is wide enough to be uninformative.; No per-AE safety table in the source, so toxicity in this exact population is uncharacterized.; The MGMT-methylation predictive value (Giger 2022) is a retrospective biomarker association, not validated as a treatment-selection marker in a prospective trial. concensusite5lowThis is where guideline and preference line up: NCCN GIST v1.2026 explicitly prefers clinical-trial enrollment for SDH-deficient and wt-GIST, so at recurrence a trial is the endorsed path rather than a detour. The SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643) is the cleanest indication match and rides single-arm phase-2 activity specific to this subtype (~40% response, Burgoyne case series). I am ranking the trial route, not temozolomide as a standard, because the drug itself is not yet guideline-endorsed.Temozolomide is off-guideline as a standard agent; the guideline-fit here is the trial-enrollment route, not the drug.; The trial requires measurable disease, so it excludes the current NED state, and NCT05661643 runs out of Asan Medical Center in Korea, a real travel constraint.; Promising newer agents in this subtype (olverembatinib, rogaratinib, belzutifan) sit in the same off-guideline trial-territory category until their readouts mature. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocateconcensusitequalifiedpreference_fitCredit where it is due: putting the NCI registry at rank 2 serves prefers_trials now, while the patient is NED and there is nothing measurable to enroll on. But at recurrence you sequence the trial route below sunitinib and regorafenib, and a patient whose stated preference is trials wants that menu offered co-equal with sunitinib, not after two guideline TKIs. Worth saying too that prefers_trials was defaulted here, not elicited, so I would confirm it before it carries this much ordering weight.

docs.title: olverembatinib (olverembatinib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowA durable-control play with the cleanest safety sheet in the dossier. 6/26 confirmed PR (ORR 23.1%) and mPFS 25.7 mo, with grade 3+ events in only 13.6% and zero discontinuations across the phase 1b (PMID 41184234), and it has already moved into phase 3 (NCT06640361). For a patient in their 40s who may be on therapy for years, that tolerability weighs almost as much as the response rate. Two blockers I will not paper over: the phase 3 requires SDHB-IHC loss, which this patient's stain does not currently show pending the re-cut, and the sponsor sits in China.Phase 3 entry requires SDHB-IHC loss; the patient's SDHB reads intact and needs re-stain before the dSDH label and eligibility hold; Ascentage sponsorship in China makes access a separate problem from eligibility; ORR 23.1% is roughly half the rogaratinib signal conservative4lowAmong the newer agents, olverembatinib is the one with a usable safety table: in the 66-patient phase 1b, grade >=3 treatment-related AEs ran 13.6% with zero AE-related discontinuations, and the events (cytopenias, transaminase rise, hyperuricemia) are familiar and monitorable (Qiu 2025). The dSDH efficacy is meaningful for this hard subtype, 6/26 (23.1%) PR with mPFS 25.7 mo. I rank it below the established agents because the evidence is single-arm phase 1b, not the long post-marketing record I prefer, and two access problems are real: the sponsor and the registrational phase 3 (NCT06640361) sit in China, and that trial's SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion conflicts with this patient's currently intact SDHB stain until the re-cut resolves it.Phase 1b with n=26 in-subtype; the 25.7-mo PFS could shrink in a randomized setting.; Access and the SDHB-IHC entry mismatch may keep this academic unless the re-stain confirms loss. critic5lowOlverembatinib shows 6/26 (23.1%, 95% CI 9-43.7) PR and mPFS 25.7 mo, but the design is a single-arm phase 1b expansion of n=26 inside a 66-patient basket, and the safety table is pooled across all 66 rather than the GIST cohort. The mechanism is non-canonical for a KIT/PDGFRA-WT tumor: this is a KIT/ABL TKI acting through VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, not its labeled target, so plausibility is borrowed rather than demonstrated in-indication. The NCT06640361 'phase 3' is phase-3 in name only, being open-label, single intervention, no comparator arm, n=40, with a PFS-rate endpoint. That design will not deliver randomized evidence, and the SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion is one this patient does not currently meet.Single-arm phase 1b with an ORR endpoint; safety pooled across the 66-patient basket rather than the n=26 GIST cohort, so subtype-specific tolerability is unresolved.; The confirmatory NCT06640361 is labeled phase 3 but is single-arm/no-comparator with a PFS-rate surrogate, so it will not generate RCT-grade evidence.; Non-canonical MoA in a KIT-WT tumor: the efficacy claim cannot lean on the labeled target. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityYou are right to grade this phase 1b n=26 (ORR 23.1%, ROBINS-I Moderate) below the established agents, but I would push the design caveat further: NCT06640361, which you call the registrational phase 3, is single-arm with no comparator and a PFS-rate endpoint, so even at completion it will not produce randomized evidence. The safety figures you cite (grade >=3 at 13.6%, zero discontinuations) are pooled across the 66-patient basket, not the n=26 GIST cohort, so subtype-specific tolerability is still open. Labeling NCT06640361 phase 3 overstates what its design can actually deliver.

docs.title: rogaratinib (rogaratinib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1moderateThe biggest swing on the board. Rogaratinib posted ORR 41.7% (10/24) and mPFS 31.0 mo in dSDH-GIST (PMID 42191879), the best numbers any systemic agent has put up in this subtype, and the FGF4-insulator mechanism is backed by a PDX that responded where sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing (Flavahan 2019, Flynn 2025 CT215). The catch is real: n=24 single-arm, and NCT04595747 is closed to accrual with Bayer off the program, so getting the actual drug is the hard part. If disease comes back, I want this pathway hit first.NCT04595747 is closed to accrual and Bayer has stepped back from rogaratinib, so access likely means compassionate use rather than enrollment; Single-arm n=24 with no comparator; 41.7% could shrink in a broader or less-selected population; Pan-FGFR hyperphosphatemia needs monitoring, though it tracked target engagement rather than capping the dose conservative5lowRogaratinib has the strongest efficacy signal in dSDH-GIST anyone has published, 10/24 (41.7%) PR and mPFS 31.0 mo (Merriam 2026), and the FGFR mechanism is well-grounded preclinically. My objection is specific and it is a safety objection: the per-grade AE distribution is not retrievable. The abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea with no grades, CT.gov posts no AE table, and the full text is paywalled, so I cannot characterize the toxicity I would be signing this patient up for. The trial is also closed to accrual, so even setting the safety gap aside this is a watch-for-the-paper option, not an actionable one today.Hyperphosphatemia is the known pan-FGFR class effect and needs phosphate monitoring plus a binder plan, but the grade distribution in this cohort is unpublished.; Closed to accrual; there is no access path right now even if the efficacy holds up. critic4lowRogaratinib has the highest ORR reported for any systemic agent in this subtype, 10/24 (41.7%) PR with mPFS 31.0 mo (95% CI 20.2-NR), in the exact molecular population. That is a real signal worth a trial referral, but it comes from one single-arm, open-label phase 2 of n=24 with no comparator and an ORR endpoint, and per-term AE rates I cannot verify: the abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea, the CT.gov results tab is empty, and the full text is paywalled. The cohort enrolled regardless of FGFR status, so the response is not anchored to a predictive biomarker. It is unreplicated; the confirmatory pemigatinib trial (NCT07434843) has not read out, and rogaratinib's own cohort is closed to accrual.Single-arm open-label ORR endpoint: no comparator and unblinded response ascertainment, with a real risk that dSDH indolence inflates the 50% SD fraction in the 91.7% DCR.; Selective/incomplete outcome reporting: per-term AE data are not retrievable from abstract, CT.gov, or the paywalled full text, so the safety profile is unverified (I read the abstract and the structured row, not the full paper).; No replication; the FGFR rationale rests on the Flavahan FGF4-insulator mechanism, which is mechanistic plausibility rather than clinical confirmation. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocaterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitYour hold on active therapy now is right for an NED patient and I am glad it is explicit, dosing FGFR or TKI toxicity into someone with no measurable target would be harm for nothing. But ranking rogaratinib first when its trial is closed to accrual and access means compassionate use under-serves a patient whose actual preference is trials; the recruiting in-subtype pemigatinib study at your rank 2 is the one that cashes prefers_trials. Lead with the door that opens. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitRogaratinib's 41.7% (PMID 42191879) is a real signal, but a single-arm n=24 cohort closed to accrual appears in neither NCCN GIST v1.2026 nor ESMO 2022, so ranking it first puts a pre-guideline number ahead of the consensus surveillance-then-sunitinib path. NCCN does endorse clinical-trial enrollment for SDH-deficient GIST, so the FGFR bet belongs on the trial menu at recurrence, not at the head of the plan while the patient is NED. The guideline-aligned move now is to confirm the dSDH phenotype and bank trial eligibility, not to lead with an agent no society has yet adopted. conservativecriticendorsetoxicityThis matches what I found independently: the rogaratinib per-grade AE table is not retrievable from the abstract, the empty CT.gov results tab, or the paywalled full text, so the toxicity is unverifiable and the 10/24 (41.7%) ORR cannot carry the pick on safety grounds alone. Hyperphosphatemia is the known pan-FGFR class effect that needs phosphate monitoring and a binder plan, but I cannot grade it in this cohort either. Holding the agent to trial-route-only on that basis is the correct safety call. conservativerisktakerdissenttoxicityRanking first the one agent whose per-grade AE distribution I cannot retrieve is exactly the trade I push back on: the abstract lists only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea with no grades, CT.gov posts no table, and the full text is paywalled, so I cannot characterize the toxicity this would commit the patient to. The 41.7% ORR (10/24) is a single-arm n=24 signal with no comparator, and in an indolent tumor that inflates the stable-disease fraction, so the efficacy case does not buy back the safety blind spot. I would not place it above sunitinib, whose roughly two decades of post-marketing data give it a toxicity tail with established management algorithms; this is a dissent on toxicity, not a veto, since no measurable disease is being treated today. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe 41.7% (10/24) is the best ORR anyone has reported in the subtype, but it comes from a single-arm open-label phase 2 (ROBINS-I Moderate) with no comparator, and ranking it first treats an n=24 response signal as if it were confirmatory. The high DCR is the part I trust least: guadecitabine (0/9), linsitinib (0/20), and vandetanib (0/9) all logged stable-disease fractions in this exact subtype while producing zero responses, so dSDH indolence pads disease-control numbers with no drug effect behind them. Until the pemigatinib cohort (NCT07434843) confirms it, this is an unreplicated signal, not a number-one systemic call. risktakerconservativedissentevidence_qualityI am aiming at your rank 5 rather than the surveillance rank 1, because that is where we actually part ways. Demoting the single highest-efficacy agent (ORR 41.7%, mPFS 31.0 mo, PMID 42191879) to watch-for-the-paper because the per-grade AE table is paywalled trades the biggest expected effect for a documentation gap. Your indolence-inflates-the-SD-fraction argument cannot reach the 10/24 (41.7%) confirmed PR in PMID 42191879: a partial response is tumor regression, not stable disease, so that discount lands on DCR and leaves the ORR standing. Scoring a 41.7% response rate at confidence low next to the 0/9 guadecitabine and 0/20 linsitinib washouts flattens a real difference in signal.

docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowThe most direct shot at the actual driver. Belzutifan blocks HIF-2alpha, the node that succinate accumulation stabilizes in precisely this biology (Selak 2005 PMID 15652751; Bayley 2022 SDHB model PMID 35324464), and the PPGL cohort of LITESPARK-015 already showed ORR 26% with mPFS 22 mo in a sibling SDH-loss disease. Because it is approved off-label, access does not hinge on enrollment, which is rare among these options. What I cannot claim is a GIST readout: the wt-GIST cohort of NCT04924075 has not reported, so this is mechanism plus cross-indication signal and nothing firmer.No published dSDH-GIST efficacy; the case rests on mechanism and the PPGL cohort; Anemia and fatigue are expected HIF-2alpha class effects; Guadecitabine, another mechanistically-matched agent, returned 0/9 in this subtype (PMID 36302175), a reminder that target validation does not guarantee a clinical response conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—
