docs.title: Rank 11. Abemaciclib + aromatase inhibitor (CDK4/6 + AI, NCT04469764)
docs.text: Post-board addition — not board-voted. A speculative oral later-line ER/CDK combination adjacent to letrozole, but the published ovarian CDK4/6+AI signal is weak and driven by low-grade serous, not this high-grade tumor.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: A post-board re-screen surfaced NCT04469764 (NCT04469764), a recurrent-disease phase 2 pairing the CDK4/6 inhibitor abemaciclib with an aromatase inhibitor on the ER axis. The trial has no readout and enrolls behind molecular-tumor-board confirmation of a qualifying alteration. The published CDK4/6 + AI ovarian anchor is ribociclib + letrozole (PMID 33109627): in its 20-patient ovarian cohort the ORR was 5% and PFS12 was 50%, but the durable multi-year responses sat entirely in the three low-grade serous patients — not the high-grade serous biology here. The read across drugs and histology is weak.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low for high-grade serous specifically. The CDK4/6 + AI combination has produced durable benefit in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, but the ovarian-cohort ORR was 5% overall and the high-grade serous signal is essentially absent in the published anchor. NCT04469764 has no readout, so there is no direct estimand. This is the most speculative therapeutic option on the list.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• CDK4/6-class cytopenias: the ribociclib + letrozole anchor ran grade 3+ neutropenia 15% and leukopenia 23%. This touches the myelosuppression veto but sits below the febrile-neutropenia threshold.
  • Abemaciclib diarrhea is the characteristic non-heme toxicity.
  • Oral administration fits the modality preference.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No board persona evaluated this option. CDK4/6 plus endocrine blockade has no plausible counter-productive vector in ER-positive disease; the limiting factor is weak activity in high-grade serous histology, not a counter-mechanism.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The trial is recruiting, but entry hinges on molecular-tumor-board confirmation of a qualifying alteration, so eligibility is uncertain until that review. Oral and relatively low-toxicity, it sits adjacent to letrozole as a later-line ER-axis option — but the histology mismatch in the supporting data is the reason it ranks last of the therapeutic options.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It ranks 11, last of the therapeutic options and above only the not-recommended disitamab vedotin, because the published ovarian CDK4/6 + AI signal is weak (ORR 5%) and its durable benefit was confined to low-grade serous. Below the DDR options because those act on the axis of this tumor's dominant biology, where this combination's ovarian evidence points away from high-grade serous.

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• Disitamab vedotin (RC48) — not recommended, board-vetoed unanimously. The open solid-tumor basket (NCT06003231) does accept HER2 IHC 1+ ovarian, so on biomarker and tumor type it is the most directly enrollable HER2 option — yet all five personas rejected it, because its MMAE payload runs peripheral sensory neuropathy at 68% any-grade / 18.7% grade 3+ and neutropenia at 12.1% grade 3+ (PMID 37988648), hitting both of the patient's named vetoes head-on. Its only HER2-low efficacy read is an abstract-only PAM-pathway-selected breast series, and the accessibility pass flags that the US basket is now active-not-recruiting and the only recruiting trial is China-only. Kept as a not-recommended row so the rejection is visible, not silent.
  • Trastuzumab duocarmazine (SYD985) — unavailable. A second HER2 ADC with documented IHC 1+ breast activity, but the program is discontinued after the FDA complete response letter and it never enrolled ovarian patients; mechanism context only, with no access route.
  • Olaparib monotherapy (SOLO1) — not recommended, foreclosed. BRCA-mutation-gated; both germline and somatic BRCA resulted as wild-type, so this indication does not apply to this tumor.
  • PI3K/AKT-pathway inhibitors (PIK3CA-directed) — investigational only. The tumor carries a focal somatic PIK3CA amplification, but amplification is a poorly-validated predictive marker versus an activating hotspot mutation, there is no approved PI3K-directed therapy in HGSC, and the only options are phase 1 trial-matching tags with no efficacy estimand (NCT05216432, NCT05683418).
  • MAP2K4-directed agents — investigational only. The focal somatic MAP2K4 deletion is a phase 1 trial-matching tag with no validated preclinical target and no approved matched therapy (NCT05557045, NCT05691504, NCT03340506, NCT03454035).

A second later-line DDR option on the ATR axis of her genomic instability, but with no ovarian efficacy estimand, an unconfirmed DDR entry route for her genotype, and conference-only data. 11 Abemaciclib + aromatase inhibitor (CDK4/6 + AI, NCT04469764)post-board addition — not board-voted Low for high-grade serous: CDK4/6 + AI ovarian anchor (ribociclib+letrozole, pmid:33109627) posted ORR 5% with durable benefit only in low-grade serous; NCT04469764 has no readout. Low (CDK4/6-class cytopenias — grade 3+ neutropenia 15%, leukopenia 23%; abemaciclib diarrhea; below febrile-neutropenia threshold) Low (CDK4/6 + endocrine blockade has no plausible counter-productive vector in ER-positive disease; the limit is weak high-grade-serous activity.) A speculative oral later-line ER/CDK combination adjacent to letrozole, but the published ovarian CDK4/6+AI signal is weak (ORR 5%) and driven by low-grade serous, not this high-grade tumor.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity — the cytopenias, hypertension, ILD, and bleeding a patient would actually experience. Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that a treatment could blunt its own therapeutic goal. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; ranks 8-11 were surfaced by a post-board re-screen and carry no pills because the board did not vote on them. The full per-persona rationale for the board-voted options lives on the board page. Disitamab vedotin is omitted from this table as a not-recommended, board-vetoed row; it is documented under Classes examined but not ranked.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Post-board additions (this refresh). Ranks 8-11 — T-DXd + olaparib, azenosertib, ART0380, and abemaciclib + AI — were surfaced by a post-board re-screen and were NOT part of the board's deliberation. They carry no persona endorsement, dissent, or veto (agreement_score 0) and are ranked on evidence alone at considered_with_caveats. Their evidence is correspondingly softer: the T-DXd + olaparib ORR (54%) is AACR 2026 conference-level, the azenosertib and ART0380 readouts are sponsor/conference-only with null identifiers, and the abemaciclib row has no readout and rests on a low-grade-serous-skewed ovarian anchor. Treat them as relapse-context leads to raise with the treating team, not board-vetted maintenance picks. The MATAO phase 3 (rank 5) is also a post-board add, but folded into the existing board-voted letrozole row on the same ER axis.
  • Evidence-base caveats. The two PARP options and bevacizumab rest on RoB2-low registered phase 3 trials, but bevacizumab is PFS-only with no overall-population OS gain, and ICON7 was open-label. PAOLA-1's load-bearing HR 0.33 is a pre-specified subgroup, not the ITT (HR 0.59). GEN-1's efficacy comes from a sponsor topline and a 2025 abstract with no peer-reviewed safety table. Letrozole is now enrollable on the randomized MATAO phase 3, but that readout is pending, and the observed endocrine magnitude rests on PARAGON (34.6% clinical benefit at 3 mo, ER histoscore non-predictive) and the earlier ROBINS-I-serious retrospective series. T-DXd at IHC 1+ ovarian has no indication data at all — the case is cross-tumor extrapolation from HER2-low breast plus a preclinical bystander mechanism, with a 10-12% ILD rate that has been fatal — and disitamab vedotin's only HER2-low read is an abstract-only PAM-selected breast series.
  • Compartment / biomarker dependencies. The maintenance ranking is stable across the GIS result except for rank 6: olaparib + bevacizumab is foreclosed unless a validated MyChoice CDx GIS returns at least 42, and the Altera qualitative instability call does not satisfy the companion-diagnostic definition. The HER2-directed option depends on the confirmatory re-stain: the IHC 1+ rests on a single specimen Altera could not evaluate, and a re-stain reading HER2 0 would take T-DXd off the table. SOLO1 olaparib monotherapy is foreclosed by confirmed BRCA-wild-type status, and the MSS/TMB-low profile forecloses tumor-agnostic checkpoint inhibition.
  • What would change the ranking. A MyChoice GIS at least 42, paired with a documented anticoagulation/BP-management plan, would move olaparib + bevacizumab from last of the maintenance options toward first. A documented hematology-supported dose plan would lift the conservative's conditional veto on niraparib and close its gap with rucaparib. A confirmatory HER2 re-stain that holds at 1+ keeps both HER2 options (T-DXd, T-DXd + olaparib) as documented relapse leads; a re-stain of HER2 0 forecloses them, while a 2+/3+ result would move single-agent T-DXd toward (or onto) the tumor-agnostic label. A board re-vote on the four post-board additions would replace their neutral agreement_score of 0 with real board signal and could reorder ranks 8-11 substantially. A published MATAO readout would convert letrozole's endocrine rationale from a pending design assumption to observed evidence.
  • Re-scoping caveat. If the patient's preference shifts to accept myelosuppression risk with hematology support, the PARP options strengthen at the top; if tolerability concerns deepen, bevacizumab or letrozole rise as the veto-clearing, lower-burden choices, and T-DXd stays a relapse-only HER2 option regardless.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text:
Refreshed 2026-07-09 by the PI agent as a lighter PI-REFRESH (no board re-vote). A post-board re-screen added five on-axis trials (MATAO letrozole maintenance NCT04111978, T-DXd + olaparib NCT04585958, azenosertib NCT05128825, ART0380 NCT04657068, abemaciclib + AI NCT04469764) and seven clinical-evidence rows (MATAO, PARAGON anastrozole, ribociclib + letrozole, T-DXd + olaparib CTEP #10355, azenosertib DENALI, adavosertib + gemcitabine, ART0380). The board did NOT re-deliberate these, so the seven board-voted interventions keep their prior ranks (1-7) and agreement scores unchanged, and the material new options enter as post-board additions at considered_with_caveats with empty board arrays and a neutral agreement_score of 0 — no fabricated endorsement or veto. The strongest new fit, letrozole maintenance on the randomized MATAO phase 3, folds into the existing board-voted rank-5 letrozole row (same drug, same ER axis) rather than displacing anything; it is tempered by PR-negativity and by PARAGON's finding that ER histoscore did not predict benefit. T-DXd + olaparib (rank 8) carries the HER2-low predictive-certainty hedge (IHC 1+ is a weaker predictor than 3+). The DDR pair (azenosertib rank 9, ART0380 rank 10) and abemaciclib + AI (rank 11) are later-line / future-relapse options. Disitamab vedotin moves to rank 12, unchanged as a not-recommended board-vetoed row. HRD-pending gating is unchanged: every biomarker reads confirmed, so the ranking stays a single unbranched list with scenario: null, and the GIS and HER2 re-stain remain under Workup considerations. Reference-verification (this run): the promoted new identifiers were checked against PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov — PMIDs 31328463 (PARAGON), 33485453 (adavosertib), 33109627 (ribociclib+letrozole) resolve and match their claims; NCTs NCT04111978, NCT04585958, NCT05128825, NCT04657068, NCT04469764 all resolve, recruiting, with matching titles/phases. Conference-only data (CTEP #10355, DENALI, ART0380) carry null identifiers by design. All 12 recommendation rows validate against the schema.

Prior run: authored 2026-06-26 by the PI agent on the re-run after a HER2-low (IHC 1+) targetable feature was added and the full dossier and board were refreshed. Supplied: a scrubbed profile (now seven targetable features), preferences, the target-validation file (with five HER2 workup rows), 21 trials, 14 clinical-evidence and 17 preclinical-evidence rows, and a fresh board record (5 positions, 20 critiques regenerated with HER2 in the mix). Every biomarker reads confirmed, including HER2-low, so the ranking stays a single unbranched list with scenario: null on each row; the GIS and the HER2 re-stain are surfaced under Workup considerations rather than as ranked diagnostic rows. The HER2-low ADCs were integrated per Hard Rule 6: trastuzumab deruxtecan is ranked seventh as a real but investigational, relapse-context option (status considered_with_caveats, target her2_low), never as approved standard care, and disitamab vedotin is kept as a rank-8 not-recommended row on a unanimous MMAE-toxicity veto. Two departures from the prior six-feature synthesis are recomputed from the refreshed board and worth flagging: rucaparib rose to agreement_score 0.8 (the refreshed board added conservative and advocate endorsements and dropped risktaker, who now ranks niraparib first), and olaparib + bevacizumab now carries a single conservative toxicity veto plus critic and advocate dissents (refreshed critic ranked it fourth rather than vetoing, so it is scored as a dissent), landing at -0.4. The clinical order of the six prior options is preserved. Agreement scores, ranks, vetoes, and dissents were computed from the board files; the DESTINY-Breast06 PFS HR is reported as the published 0.62 (the screener row's 0.64 was reconciled to the publication). All eight recommendation rows validate against the schema. The letrozole design-source mismatch is inherited from the dossier and logged for a screener re-run.

docs.title: 1. Rucaparib (1L maintenance) rucaparib, AG-014699, CO-338, Rubraca
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-24

Rucaparib is an approved oral PARP inhibitor the treating oncologist can prescribe now, though all-comer 1L maintenance for this BRCA-wild-type tumor falls outside the strict label and may need a prior-authorization step. The practical constraint is hematologic rather than regulatory: grade 3 or higher anemia ran near 29 percent in ATHENA-MONO, which sits against the patient's stated myelosuppression concern. No trial enrollment is required.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (Rubraca). On-label uses are BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer (treatment) and platinum-sensitive recurrent maintenance; the 2018 1L-maintenance all-comer indication studied in ATHENA-MONO is not a separately approved label, so all-comer 1L maintenance in a BRCA-wild-type tumor is an off-label use of an approved drug. GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 lists single-agent PARP maintenance, category 2A, for all-comers after a 1L platinum response. Geographic scopeUS — routine prescription nationwide.

Next steps

  1. Have the prescriber confirm formulary placement and submit a prior authorization citing NCCN category 2A and ATHENA-MONO (PMID 35658487) if the plan flags the all-comer use as off-label.
  2. Call pharma& medical information (1-844-779-7707) to confirm the current US Rubraca medical-information contact and ask about patient-assistance eligibility for this insurance type.
  3. Document a baseline CBC and an anemia/cytopenia monitoring plan with hematology before starting, given the patient's WBC of 3.5 and the myelosuppression concern.
  4. Rucaparib effect size is the primary JCO ITT HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68, PMID 35658487).

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT035222463newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer, post-platinum responseactive not recruitingeligible: notrial sitesThe trial that anchors the rucaparib rationale, but it is no longer enrolling, so it is not an access route. The patient would receive rucaparib by routine (off-label) prescription rather than through this study.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Companypharma& (Rubraca; formerly Clovis Oncology) CountryAustria (pharma& Schweiz / pharma& group); US operations for Rubraca Medical info phone1-844-779-7707 Medical info emailmedinfo@pharmaand.com Product informationhttps://www.rubraca.com/ Notespharma& acquired Rubraca from Clovis Oncology in 2022. Confirm the current US medical-information line when calling, since the contact moved with the asset transfer.

Payer / coverage notes. As an FDA-approved oral oncolytic, rucaparib is generally covered under Medicare Part D rather than Part B. Off-label 1L all-comer maintenance can draw a prior-authorization request or a compendia challenge from the plan; NCCN category 2A listing and the ATHENA-MONO data are the supporting citations the prescriber would attach. Manufacturer co-pay and patient-assistance support exists for commercially insured and uninsured patients but not for Medicare beneficiaries.

Notes. Access route is off-label prescription of an approved drug, not a trial. The rank-1 placement rests on replicated all-comer phase 3 efficacy, not on an open study slot.

docs.title: 2. Niraparib (1L maintenance) niraparib, MK-4827, Zejula
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-24

Niraparib is the one PARP option here that is on-label standard of care for all-comer 1L maintenance, so the treating oncologist can prescribe it without an off-label justification. The gate is deliverability, not access: grade 3 or higher thrombocytopenia near 29 percent and anemia near 31 percent hit the patient's named myelosuppression concern, and a baseline WBC of 3.5 in the 70-79 band leaves thin marrow reserve. A platelet-based individualized starting dose and a written cytopenia plan are what make it usable.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (Zejula) for 1L maintenance of advanced epithelial ovarian/fallopian-tube/primary-peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum, regardless of biomarker status (all-comers; PRIMA-based label). GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 single-agent PARP maintenance, category 2A (all-comers); ESMO endorses 1L PARP maintenance in this setting. Geographic scopeUS — routine on-label prescription nationwide.

Next steps

  1. Have hematology document a platelet/body-weight-based individualized starting dose (200 mg likely given baseline counts) and a written cytopenia-management pathway before starting; this is also what lifts the board's conditional veto.
  2. Confirm Part D formulary placement and submit any required prior authorization (on-label, so this is usually routine).
  3. Screen GSK and foundation patient-assistance options for the patient's insurance type via the Zejula support line (1-888-825-5249).
  4. Set a CBC monitoring cadence (weekly for the first month per label) and a dose-modification trigger plan.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT026550163newly-diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer, post-platinum responsecompletedeligible: notrial sitesRegistration trial; completed and closed. Niraparib is now obtained by routine on-label prescription, so no trial slot is involved.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

GSK does not publish a general medical-information email for Zejula; route written queries through the Response Center.

Payer / coverage notes. On-label 1L all-comer maintenance, so coverage is the cleanest of the PARP options. Oral oncolytic billed under Medicare Part D. GSK's Zejula patient-assistance and co-pay programs cover commercially insured and uninsured patients; Medicare beneficiaries are excluded from manufacturer co-pay but may qualify for foundation support.

Notes. Only intervention on the board that is true standard-of-care on-label for this exact indication. The clinical hesitation is toxicity deliverability, recorded as a hematology plan, not an access barrier.

docs.title: 3. Olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1 maintenance, contingent on validated HRD-positive) olaparib, AZD2281, KU-0059436, Lynparza, bevacizumab, Avastin
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Not yet accessible Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-24

This is the highest-magnitude maintenance option, but the patient cannot reach it yet: the FDA combination indication and NCCN category 1 listing both require HRD-positive status, and her BRCA-wild-type tumor has no validated genomic-instability score. A Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS of 42 or higher is the single gate. The board also carried a double veto on stacked anti-angiogenic plus PARP toxicity against her IVC-filter history, which becomes addressable only with a documented anticoagulation/BP plan and a confirmed HRD-positive result.

RegulatoryBoth components FDA-approved. The olaparib + bevacizumab combination carries a specific FDA indication for 1L maintenance of HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer (HRD defined by deleterious BRCA mutation or genomic instability via an FDA-approved companion diagnostic). On-label only if HRD-positive is established; otherwise the combination would be off-label. GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 category 1 — but only for HRD-positive disease defined by tumor BRCA or a validated GIS >=42, which this BRCA-wild-type tumor does not yet meet. Geographic scopeUS — on-label prescription contingent on a validated companion-diagnostic GIS result; no geographic barrier beyond the test.

Next steps

  1. Order the validated GIS (Myriad MyChoice CDx or FDA-approved equivalent) on archival FFPE; this is the gating step and is captured as the essential workup row below.
  2. If GIS >=42 returns, the combination becomes on-label; assemble a documented anticoagulation/blood-pressure plan to address the toxicity veto before starting.
  3. If GIS <42, treat as HRD-negative and route to all-comer niraparib (PRIMA) instead; the combination is foreclosed below 42.
  4. For drug-specific questions, call AstraZeneca Medical Information (1-800-236-9933) for olaparib and Genentech (1-800-821-8590) for bevacizumab.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT024776443newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer receiving 1L bevacizumabcompletedeligible: notrial sitesRegistration trial; completed. Access would be on-label prescription contingent on a validated GIS >=42, not trial enrollment.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAstraZeneca (Lynparza/olaparib) and Genentech-Roche (Avastin/bevacizumab); Lynparza co-developed with Merck CountryUnited Kingdom (AstraZeneca) / United States-Switzerland (Genentech-Roche) Medical info phone1-800-236-9933 Product informationhttps://www.lynparza.com/ Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.astrazeneca-us.com/our-science/clinical-trials/expanded-access.html Notes1-800-236-9933 is AstraZeneca US Medical Information (for the olaparib half). For the bevacizumab half use Genentech Medical Communications (1-800-821-8590). Both components are already approved, so an expanded-access request is not the relevant path; the gate is the companion-diagnostic result, not drug availability.

Payer / coverage notes. Coverage hinges entirely on documented HRD-positive status. With a validated GIS >=42 the combination is on-label NCCN category 1 and reimbursable. Without it, payers will deny the combination for a BRCA-wild-type tumor and the patient defaults to all-comer niraparib. Olaparib is Part D; bevacizumab is Part B.

Notes. Both drugs are fully available; the only barrier is the missing companion-diagnostic score. Classified not_yet_accessible because the patient cannot currently reach the indication, with off_label_use noted as the fallback descriptor if a clinician pursued the combination without a qualifying GIS.

docs.title: 4. Bevacizumab (continued maintenance) bevacizumab, Avastin, rhuMAb-VEGF
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: monoclonal_antibody   Verified: 2026-06-24

Bevacizumab is on-label standard-of-care maintenance for this exact setting, and the patient is already on it, so continuation is the lowest-friction path on the board. It clears both of her named toxicity vetoes (no added neuropathy, no myelosuppression). The live caution is vascular: anti-angiogenic VTE and bleeding risk against her high VTE history and prior IVC filter, managed with blood-pressure and bleeding monitoring rather than dose escalation. The honest ceiling is PFS-only, with no overall-population survival gain.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (Avastin, and biosimilars Mvasi, Zirabev, Alymsys, Vegzelma) for stage III/IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube, and primary-peritoneal cancer with carboplatin/paclitaxel followed by single-agent bevacizumab maintenance. On-label for this patient's setting. GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 bevacizumab maintenance, category 2A (all-comers after 1L platinum). Geographic scopeUS — routine on-label prescription nationwide (Avastin and biosimilars).

Next steps

  1. Continue the existing bevacizumab maintenance per the established plan; no new authorization needed if already covered.
  2. Keep the hypertension and bleeding-monitoring algorithm active and coordinate anticoagulation decisions against the IVC-filter/VTE history.
  3. If a biosimilar is substituted by the plan, switch the medical-information contact to that product's marketer (Amgen/Mvasi, Pfizer/Zirabev).
  4. Revisit with the team whether to layer a PARP onto bevacizumab once the GIS resolves, versus continuing bevacizumab alone given the cleared Signatera MRD state.

Genentech Access Solutions and the Avastin co-pay program assist commercially insured patients; Medicare patients are routed to independent foundations.

Notes. Already in use. The access question is really a maintenance-intensity question, not a how-to-obtain question.

docs.title: 6. Letrozole (endocrine maintenance) letrozole, Femara, CGS-20267
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-24

Letrozole is a cheap oral generic the oncologist can prescribe off-label today, which makes it the lowest-burden and lowest-toxicity option on the board and a clean fit for the patient's age and oral preference. The catch is evidence, not access: the supporting data is a single retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series, and PR-negativity tempers the expected benefit from the roughly 80 percent ER reading. Best positioned as a gentle later-line or adjunct option rather than a randomized-backed maintenance regimen.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (Femara and generics) for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer. No ovarian-cancer indication, so use in ER-positive HGSC is off-label use of a widely available generic. GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 includes aromatase inhibitors among hormone-therapy options; a softer recommendation tier than the category 2A PARP and bevacizumab choices. Geographic scopeUS — routine off-label prescription nationwide.

Next steps

  1. Have the prescriber write letrozole 2.5 mg once daily off-label; submit a prior authorization citing NCCN's hormone-therapy listing if the plan requests one.
  2. Set expectations with the patient that the evidence is retrospective and the magnitude is modest, especially given PR-negativity.
  3. Plan bone-density monitoring and arthralgia management for prolonged aromatase-inhibitor use.
  4. Reconcile the upstream design-source flag (trials row described a single-arm phase 2; the source PMID 29157627 is a retrospective translational series).

docs.title: 7. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) trastuzumab deruxtecan, T-DXd, DS-8201, DS-8201a, fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki, Enhertu
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-06-26

Enhertu is FDA-approved and a treating oncologist can order it, just not on-label for this tumor: the tumor-agnostic approval needs HER2 IHC 3+ and her ovarian tumor is 1+, so this is off-label use. The efficacy case is borrowed, with the DESTINY-PanTumor02 ovarian cohort enrolling IHC 2+/3+ and the IHC 1+ evidence coming from breast trials. Expect a prior-authorization fight and weigh the roughly 10-12% ILD/pneumonitis risk. No T-DXd study is enrolling her now; the open HER2-directed ovarian trials use disitamab vedotin instead, covered in that row.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (Enhertu) across several HER2 settings: HER2-positive and HER2-low/ultralow breast (DESTINY-Breast04/06), HER2-positive gastric, HER2-mutant NSCLC, and a 2024 tumor-agnostic approval for HER2 IHC 3+ solid tumors. The tumor-agnostic label requires IHC 3+, so use in this HER2-low (IHC 1+) ovarian tumor is off-label use of an approved drug. GuidelinesNot NCCN/ESMO-listed for HER2-low ovarian cancer; the tumor-agnostic NCCN listing tracks the IHC 3+ approval, so off-guideline at IHC 1+. Next steps

  2. Order a confirmatory HER2 re-stain first; the 1+ call rests on a single surgical-path specimen and the Altera platform could not evaluate HER2.
  3. If pursued, plan for a payer denial (the tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+) and build an appeal around the DESTINY-PanTumor02 ovarian cohort and DESTINY-Breast04/06.
  4. Call AstraZeneca Medical Information (1-800-236-9933) or Daiichi Sankyo (1-877-437-7763) for off-label dosing and ILD monitoring; set up baseline and serial chest imaging given the pneumonitis rate.
  5. For a HER2-directed trial route, see the disitamab vedotin row.

docs.title: 8. Disitamab vedotin (RC48) disitamab vedotin, RC48, RC48-ADC, hertuzumab vedotin, Aidixi
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Not yet accessible Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-06-26

Disitamab vedotin has no FDA or EMA approval; it is cleared only in China (Aidixi, for gastric and urothelial cancer), so a US patient reaches it through a trial. The Pfizer/Seagen solid-tumor basket (NCT06003231) does accept HER2 IHC 1+ ovarian, but it has stopped enrolling, and the only recruiting study (NCT06660511) is in China, limited to platinum-resistant relapse, and pairs the drug with anlotinib, whose bleeding and clotting risk runs against her VTE and IVC-filter history. She is in first remission with no measurable disease, so neither study fits today, and the MMAE payload carries the peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia she has named as vetoes. Best held as a watch-list option for a future relapse.

RegulatoryNo FDA or EMA approval. Approved in China only (NMPA; marketed as Aidixi) for HER2-positive gastric and urothelial cancer. docs.title: 10. Validated genomic-instability score (Myriad MyChoice CDx companion diagnostic / FDA-approved equivalent) MyChoice CDx, Myriad MyChoice, GIS, genomic instability score, HRD companion diagnostic, FoundationOne CDx LOH, Caris HRD
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: companion diagnostic (NGS panel)   Verified: 2026-06-24

This is the test that unlocks the highest-magnitude maintenance option, not a therapy. Myriad MyChoice CDx is the FDA companion diagnostic whose GIS >=42 cutoff defines HRD-positive status; ordering it resolves whether the olaparib + bevacizumab combination is on the table. Foundation and Caris offer LOH/HRD readouts, but only MyChoice maps directly to the PAOLA-1 label, so it is the preferred order. Use archival FFPE; expect a 2-3 week turnaround.

RegulatoryMyriad MyChoice CDx is an FDA-approved companion diagnostic. It is the assay whose GIS threshold (>=42) defines HRD-positive status for the olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1) and niraparib (PRIMA) labels. GuidelinesNCCN Ovarian v1.2025 recognizes validated HRD testing (BRCA plus genomic instability) to inform PARP-maintenance selection. MyChoice CDx is the label-recognized assay tied to the PAOLA-1 indication. Geographic scopeUS — central-lab send-out testing (Salt Lake City) accepting nationwide FFPE specimens.

Next steps

  1. Order Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS on the archival surgical resection block (preferred for tumor content); call 1-800-469-7423 to set up the requisition.
  2. If GIS >=42, the patient becomes PAOLA-1 / olaparib+bevacizumab eligible (on-label category 1); if <42, she is HRD-negative and niraparib all-comer maintenance is the cleaner PARP option.
  3. Use MyChoice as the preferred assay rather than Foundation/Caris LOH scores, since only MyChoice's threshold maps to the olaparib+bevacizumab label.
  4. Confirm payer coverage and turnaround (~2-3 weeks) so the maintenance decision is not delayed.

Trial pathways

docs.title: Bevacizumab (continued maintenance) (bevacizumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative2moderateShe is already on bevacizumab, and continuing it is the lowest-disruption maintenance choice with the deepest safety track record (GOG-218 and ICON7 both reported in 2011, and the AE profile has been mapped ever since). Neither named veto applies here: no neuropathy, no marrow suppression. The PFS gain is real but modest (HR 0.717, 95% CI 0.625-0.824 in GOG-218; OS not improved overall), and the operative worry is hers specifically: G2+ hypertension ran 22.9% in the bev-throughout arm, and with a high VTE history plus a prior IVC filter, bleeding and thrombosis need active management. I rank it as the safe continuation, not the high-efficacy play.High VTE history plus prior IVC filter against bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding class effect; G2+ hypertension 22.9% requiring therapy; needs ongoing BP monitoring; PFS-only benefit, with no OS improvement in the overall GOG-218 population critic3moderateReplicated across two phase 3 trials she matches on indication (GOG-218 HR 0.717, 0.625-0.824; ICON7 HR 0.81, 0.70-0.94), and she is already on the backbone. The hard limit is that this is PFS only. GOG-218 found no OS benefit in the overall population, and ICON7's OS gain sat in a high-risk subgroup, which is a subgroup result from an open-label trial (RoB2 some-concern). VTE and bleeding risk is the operative safety problem given her VTE history and prior IVC filter.PFS-only benefit; no OS gain in the GOG-218 overall population; ICON7 OS benefit is a high-risk subgroup finding, and ICON7 was open-label (RoB2 some-concern: outcome ascertainment); VTE and bleeding risk against her VTE history and prior IVC filter concensusite1moderateShe is already on the bevacizumab backbone, and that is where the guidelines land for an all-comer at this stage. NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 lists bevacizumab maintenance at category 2A with no biomarker gate, and the ESMO 2026 express update keeps bevacizumab for 15 months on the menu for HRD-negative disease. GOG-218 (pmid 22204724) and ICON7 (pmid 22204725) are the anchors here, both phase 3, both with a real PFS signal. The honest caveat: the benefit is PFS, not OS in the overall population, so this buys time rather than cure.GOG-218 and ICON7 enrolled all-comers, but the OS gain in ICON7 sat in the high-risk (stage IV / suboptimal) subset; this stage IIIc R0 patient is adjacent to, not inside, that subset.; Bevacizumab's VTE and bleeding risk runs against her documented high VTE history and prior IVC filter, which is the operative caution here rather than her named neuropathy or marrow vetoes. advocate2moderateThis is the one maintenance option that clears both of her named vetoes outright: no added peripheral neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression, on a backbone she already tolerates. The honest cost is the ceiling. GOG-218 buys PFS (HR 0.717, 14.1 vs 10.3 mo) with no overall-population survival gain, which sits uneasily against her 0.7 efficacy lean. The live caution is her own: anti-angiogenic VTE and bleeding risk against a high VTE history and a prior IVC filter, which I would handle with BP and bleeding monitoring rather than treat as a stop.Clears both named vetoes: no added neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression; Modality tension: VTE and bleeding risk against her high VTE history and prior IVC filter, managed rather than escalated; Efficacy ceiling is PFS-only (HR 0.717) with no OS gain, in tension with her 0.7 efficacy lean; Low-infusion: partial (IV q3w, but she already tolerates it)

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocateconcensusitedissentpreference_fitHer own words set the order: "treat its confirmatory assay as the rank-1 shared workup" yet concensusite files that assay into the notes and hands rank-1 to a continued PFS-only anti-angiogenic. She is already on bevacizumab, so continuing it is not the harm; the harm is letting the guideline default outrank the sequencing she explicitly asked for, when the GIS result is what decides whether bev stands alone or earns a PARP partner. Honor her rank-1, then let the score pick the maintenance. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitYour surrogate-endpoint discount on bevacizumab is a fair reading of GOG-218 (pmid:22204724), but NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 lists it at category 2A and the ESMO 2026 express update still keeps it, both with full knowledge the benefit is PFS rather than OS. That category is the panel's calibration of exactly the PFS-only data you are reading, not a separate evidence tier you can discount past it. Where we do agree: you correctly kept T-DXd off the ranked maintenance lane, since no guideline endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian. conservativeconcensusitequalifiedguideline_fitNo quarrel with bevacizumab as the veto-clean continuation, since she is already on it and neither named veto applies. My caveat is the one the concensusite half-flags: the ICON7 OS gain lived in the high-risk (stage IV / suboptimally debulked) subset, and a stage IIIc R0 patient sits adjacent to that group rather than inside it, so this buys PFS more than survival for her specifically. The operative safety watch here is not her vetoes but bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding class effect against her VTE history and prior IVC filter, which needs active BP and thrombosis monitoring rather than a footnote. criticconcensusitequalifiedevidence_qualityCat-2A is panel consensus, not an effect-size ranking, and it does not make bevacizumab the strongest maintenance on the board. GOG-218 (pmid:22204724) bought PFS only at HR 0.717 with no OS gain in the overall population, and ICON7's OS signal sat in a high-risk subgroup of an open-label trial (RoB2 some-concern) she is adjacent to rather than inside. The two all-comer PARPs carry larger pre-specified PFS effects (PRIMA 0.62, ATHENA-MONO 0.52) at the same RoB2-low grade, so ranking bevacizumab first reads as guideline-anchoring over evidence weight. risktakerconcensusitedissentevidence_qualityBevacizumab is the lowest ceiling on the board: GOG-218 bought PFS at HR 0.717 with no OS gain in the overall population (pmid:22204724), and leading with it underweights effect size for a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7. The all-comer PARPs (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52) and a possible olaparib+bev HR 0.33 are far bigger swings she can take. Guideline-clean is not the same as her best shot.

docs.title: Letrozole (endocrine maintenance) (letrozole)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative3lowFor a patient aged 70-79 who wants an oral, low-burden option, letrozole is the gentlest thing on the list: aromatase-inhibitor toxicity is arthralgia and slow bone-density loss, the class has decades of post-marketing data from breast cancer, and none of her vetoes are in play. Her tumor is ER-positive at ~80% of nuclei, which gives a real rationale, though PR-negativity tempers the expected size of any benefit. Be honest about the evidence: this is a tier-4 retrospective letrozole-maintenance series (60% vs 38.5% RFS at 24 months, p=0.035), not a randomized trial, so I hold it at low confidence. It earns its place on tolerability, not on the strength of the efficacy data.Evidence is tier-4 retrospective, not randomized; PR-negativity tempers expected magnitude despite strong ER positivity; Likely lower absolute efficacy than PARP or bevacizumab maintenance critic——did not pick— concensusite5lowLow-burden, oral, and a fit for her stated preference and age band. That is the case for letrozole, not the evidence grade. NCCN lists hormone therapy as an option in this disease, but the maintenance signal here is a non-randomized retrospective series (pmid 29157627), not a phase 3, and her ER-positive (~80%) but PR-negative profile predicts a real-but-modest effect.The supporting data is a retrospective comparison nested in a translational study, well below the phase 3 evidence behind the PARP and bevacizumab options.; PR-negativity tempers expected magnitude, so this reads as a tolerability-driven later option rather than a primary maintenance choice. advocate3lowOral, once daily, no infusion, and it trips none of her vetoes, so for the 70-79 band and her oral preference this is the gentlest thing on the list. The catch is the evidence: a single retrospective ROBINS-I-serious series (60% vs 38.5% recurrence-free at 24 months), not a randomized result, and her PR-negativity likely trims the ER-driven signal. I would hold this as a low-toxicity adjunct or later-line floor, not a substitute for a trial-backed regimen. It earns its place because it costs her almost nothing in tolerability.Best oral and age-band fit on the board; clears every veto; Evidence is the weak point: retrospective, non-randomized, ROBINS-I serious; PR-negativity likely trims the ER-driven magnitude

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment concensusiteconservativequalifiedguideline_fitWe agree letrozole is the gentlest option here and clears both named vetoes, and NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 does list hormone therapy in this disease. But the panel does not grade aromatase-inhibitor maintenance at the tier it gives the PARPs, and the only maintenance signal in the file is a retrospective series (pmid:29157627), so ranking it third, above rucaparib at category 2A, overstates where the consensus actually puts it. As a tolerability-driven later option I have no quarrel; at rank 3 it sits ahead of better-graded consensus maintenance.

docs.title: GEN-1 / IMNN-001 (IL-12 immunogene, OVATION 2) (gen1-imnn001)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowShe is already on it and responding, with R0, CA-125 normalized, and ctDNA undetectable, so continuing the IL-12 immunogene is the low-regret piece of an aggressive plan. The topline reads HR 0.79 for PFS and, the part that interests me, HR 0.69 for OS with about a 13-month median OS gain (OVATION 2, nct:NCT03393884), and the IL-12 route works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment rather than the MSI/TMB checkpoint axis her MSS, TMB-low tumor forecloses. The evidence is early-phase and the OS curve is immature, so I hold this loosely. It is well tolerated by IP delivery, trips none of her vetoes, and she prefers trials.Efficacy is sponsor topline from an early-phase trial with immature OS and no published CI, so the 0.69 could soften.; It is already her current therapy, so ranking it mostly argues against abandoning a working regimen rather than adding new ground. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4moderateShe is already on this one, which matters: she prefers trials and she is at R0 on this backbone. It works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment, so her MSS, TMB-low status does not foreclose it the way it kills single-agent checkpoint inhibition, and the OVATION 2 OS signal (HR 0.69) is real if immature. The cost against her preferences is the route: intraperitoneal delivery is not the oral or low-infusion option she asked for, and access outside the trial is not guaranteed. Efficacy still rests on a sponsor topline with no published grade 3+ table, so I rank it on immaturity and route, not on any veto.Satisfies prefers_trials and she is already on it at R0; Modality conflict: intraperitoneal, not oral or low-infusion; No named veto triggered; immature efficacy (sponsor topline, no published grade 3+ table)

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticdissentevidence_qualityI am targeting GEN-1, which you left off the list, because that is our sharpest split. Discarding it as sponsor topline rather than RCT-grade throws away the OS signal (HR 0.69, OVATION 2, nct:NCT03393884) on the one regimen she is already on with R0 and ctDNA undetectable. Holding out for peer-reviewed CIs before continuing a working IL-12 immunogene that trips none of her vetoes is the kind of inaction that costs in advanced disease.

docs.title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), HER2-low, investigational at IHC 1+ (trastuzumab-deruxtecan)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowHere is my long shot, held for relapse: treat an HER2-low ovarian tumor the way HER2-low breast gets treated, where T-DXd posted a PFS HR of 0.51 (95% CI 0.40-0.64) in the hormone-receptor-positive subgroup that mirrors her ER-positive biology (pmid:35665782), with Breast06 holding the signal down to ultralow at HR 0.62. The mechanism travels: freed DXd kills HER2-low and neighboring cells by bystander effect, shown in ovarian and uterine carcinosarcoma in vivo (pmid:36610380). The thin part is real, since she is IHC 1+, under the 2+/3+ ovarian cohort that hit 45% ORR and under the IHC 3+ tumor-agnostic approval, so this is investigational off a single stain I would re-confirm first. None of her named vetoes fire; the cost of entry is IV dosing and a 10-12% ILD rate that has been fatal, so lung monitoring is not optional.IHC 1+ sits below every threshold that carries actual ovarian efficacy data, so this is extrapolation resting on one specimen.; ILD at 10-12% with fatal cases, plus IV against her oral preference; this is a relapse option, not something to launch in remission. conservative——did not pick— critic5lowFor ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ there is no direct efficacy evidence. The ovarian datapoint (PanTumor02, ORR 45%, n=40) enrolled IHC 2+/3+, not 1+, and is single-arm on a response-rate surrogate; the tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+. The IHC 1+ efficacy that exists is breast (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS HR 0.51; Breast06 HR 0.62), so the case for her tumor is cross-tumor extrapolation standing in for indication data. Layer on a single-specimen HER2 call (Altera could not stain HER2) and 10-12% ILD, and this is an investigational future-relapse option, not a maintenance pick I can support now.No ovarian HER2-low IHC 1+ efficacy data; the case rests on cross-tumor extrapolation from breast plus the DXd bystander mechanism (preclinical); Ovarian evidence (PanTumor02) is single-arm, ORR surrogate, n=40, and enrolled IHC 2+/3+ above her tier; tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+; HER2 1+ rests on a single surgical-path IHC (Altera could not evaluate HER2); a confirmatory re-stain is needed before acting; ILD/pneumonitis 10-12% including fatal cases concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowThe new HER2-low axis gives her a HER2-directed option that, unlike disitamab vedotin, clears both of her named vetoes: T-DXd's headline toxicities are ILD and nausea, not peripheral neuropathy or febrile neutropenia. Two real costs keep it here rather than higher. It is IV every three weeks against her low-infusion preference, and for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor it is investigational, since the tumor-agnostic approval needs 3+ and the supporting signal is extrapolated from HER2-low breast (DESTINY-Breast04/06). Her 1+ also rests on a single specimen, so I would want the rank-1 re-stain to confirm before committing, ideally on a HER2 solid-tumor basket trial.Clears both named vetoes: ILD and nausea profile, not neuropathy or febrile neutropenia; Modality tension: IV q3w against the low-infusion preference, plus ILD risk; Investigational at IHC 1+ ovarian (tumor-agnostic approval needs 3+); efficacy extrapolated from HER2-low breast; Single-specimen HER2 basis; confirm with the rank-1 re-stain

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocatecriticendorsepreference_fitCritic lands T-DXd at rank-5 relapse-only on the evidence, and her preferences put it in the same place for a reason worth naming: of the two HER2 options, T-DXd's headline toxicities are ILD and nausea, so it clears both vetoes, while disitamab vedotin's MMAE payload hits "additional peripheral neuropathy" and severe neutropenia at once and is disqualified outright. The brake on T-DXd is hers, not the data's: IV q3w plus 10-12% ILD runs against "oral or low-infusion-burden preferred", so it stays a confirmed-relapse option behind a re-stain, not something to launch now. Same rank as critic, carried on the patient's stated tradeoffs. concensusiteadvocatedissentguideline_fitNo society endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian cancer: the tumor-agnostic T-DXd approval requires IHC 3+, the ovarian cohort (pmid:37870536) enrolled 2+/3+, and the IHC 1+ data are all breast (pmid:35665782). Seating it at rank 5, above rucaparib, which NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 lists at category 2A as an all-comer PARP, inverts the consensus order for an investigational pick. You already named the confirmatory re-stain and a basket trial in your own rationale, and that is the guideline-aligned route for an off-guideline agent, not a ranked therapeutic seat. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitRanking T-DXd at 3 for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor runs on breast data (pmid:35665782) and preclinical bystander work, which is pre-guideline by definition: no NCCN Ovarian v3.2025, ESMO, or SGO text endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian, and the tumor-agnostic approval requires IHC 3+. A cross-tumor signal read off a single un-confirmed stain is a trial hypothesis, not a consensus maintenance pick. The guideline-aligned route is a confirmatory re-stain and then a HER2 basket trial, not a rank-3 therapeutic seat. conservativerisktakerqualifiedtoxicityI'll meet the risktaker halfway: holding T-DXd for relapse instead of launching it in remission is the right instinct. What stops me going further is the missing safety datum, since there is no ovarian IHC 1+ tolerability read at all (PanTumor02 enrolled 2+/3+, the tumor-agnostic label needs 3+), and adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis of 10.5-12.1% including fatal cases is an IV long-tail risk I will not underwrite off a single surgical-path stain. Confirm the HER2 1+ on a re-stain before this is a real option, even at relapse. conservativecriticendorsetoxicityAgreed, and this is not a maintenance pick: the critic has the toxicity right, with no ovarian HER2-low efficacy or safety at IHC 1+, 10-12% ILD including fatal cases, and a single-specimen call that needs a re-stain before anyone acts. The contrast worth banking is that T-DXd is at least the lesser evil on the HER2 axis, because disitamab vedotin's MMAE payload (68% any-grade and 18.7% G3+ peripheral neuropathy, 12.1% G3+ neutropenia) trips both named vetoes outright, so any HER2 route has to avoid MMAE and run on trial. criticadvocatequalifiedevidence_qualityYou carry T-DXd on a toxicity argument (ILD and nausea, not neuropathy or marrow), and that part holds, but there is no ovarian HER2-low efficacy estimand to rank it on. The one ovarian read, PanTumor02 (pmid:37870536), is single-arm ORR 45% in n=40 enrolled at IHC 2+/3+, and the tumor-agnostic label is 3+; for her IHC 1+ tumor the case is breast-only extrapolation (DESTINY-Breast04 pmid:35665782) resting on a single specimen Altera could not stain for HER2. Reasonable to hold as a relapse option, but say plainly there is no ovarian data behind it rather than framing it as a HER2-directed pick she has evidence for. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityRanking T-DXd at 3 for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor on the bystander mechanism (pmid:36610380, preclinical in vivo) plus breast data (pmid:35665782) is mechanism standing in for an indication estimand that does not exist. The only ovarian read, PanTumor02 (pmid:37870536), is single-arm ORR in n=40 enrolled at IHC 2+/3+, the tumor-agnostic approval is 3+, and her 1+ comes from one specimen Altera could not stain for HER2. Mechanistic plausibility without an ovarian 1+ clinical signal does not earn a slot ahead of GEN-1; hold it as an investigational relapse option, not a rank-3 pick.

docs.title: Rucaparib (1L maintenance) (rucaparib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative4lowRucaparib is the other all-comer 1L PARP maintenance option, with an ITT PFS HR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) in ATHENA-MONO and benefit that held in the HRD-negative subgroup, so a BRCA-WT, GIS-unquantified tumor still qualifies. It sits behind niraparib for me on two counts: it triggers the same myelosuppression veto (G3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%), and it adds G3+ transaminase elevation in 10.6%, which matters more here because her baseline bilirubin is 1.5. The transaminitis is usually transient and her ALT/AST are normal at baseline, so it is watchable rather than disqualifying. Reasonable alternative if niraparib is not tolerated, again only with serial CBC and LFT monitoring.Same severe-myelosuppression veto as niraparib (G3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%); G3+ transaminase elevation 10.6% against a mildly elevated baseline bilirubin of 1.5; 11.8% AE-related discontinuation in ATHENA-MONO critic2highATHENA-MONO replicates the all-comer PARP-maintenance signal in a separate phase 3 (n=538, 4:1): pre-specified ITT PFS HR 0.52 (0.40-0.68, p<0.0001), RoB2 low, JCO. Two independent registered trials hitting the same endpoint is what actually moves me on this class for a BRCA-WT tumor, and the benefit holds in the ITT and HRD-negative strata rather than only a BRCA subgroup. The surrogate-endpoint and myelosuppression caveats from niraparib carry over (grade 3+ anemia 28.7%).Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); no mature OS in the primary report; Grade 3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6% against the myelosuppression veto; ALT/AST elevation 10.6% (usually transient; her baseline LFTs are normal) concensusite4lowSecond all-comer PARP option if niraparib's marrow profile is the sticking point. ATHENA-MONO (pmid 35658487) showed an ITT benefit that held in the HRD-negative stratum, so a BRCA wild-type tumor still qualifies without a BRCA gate, and ESMO scores it on MCBS v2.0 for HRD-negative disease. It is a maintenance PARP like niraparib, so it sits a notch below the bevacizumab-anchored options for this patient rather than ahead of them.Anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% (pmid 35658487) still engage her myelosuppression veto, so a swap from niraparib trades one marrow risk for another.; Transaminase elevations run about 10%; baseline LFTs are normal, but a bilirubin of 1.5 is worth watching. advocate6moderateFor a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7, this is the strongest oral maintenance on the board: ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52 (20.2 vs 9.2 mo), qualifying her BRCA-wild-type tumor with no GIS gate. I rank it below the clean options for one reason: grade 3+ anemia near 29% presses her severe-myelosuppression veto, and her baseline WBC of 3.5 leaves thin reserve. But that veto is hers to lift, not mine to rank past on her behalf, so if she chooses the efficacy with a hematology-supported dose and monitoring plan on file, this moves up. I would put niraparib a step behind it, since thrombocytopenia plus anemia hit the marrow veto harder.Strongest oral PFS signal for her 0.7 efficacy lean (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52); Presses the severe-myelosuppression veto (grade 3+ anemia ~29%); thin marrow reserve (WBC 3.5); Veto is hers to lift; moves up with a hematology-supported dose and monitoring plan on file

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativeadvocatequalifiedtoxicityThe advocate is right that the autonomy call belongs to the patient, but "hers to lift" undersells what is being lifted: G3+ anemia ~29% and neutropenia 14.6% against a baseline WBC of 3.5 is a thin-marrow setup, not a paperwork formality. I would keep the myelosuppression veto in force until a hematology-supported starting dose and a serial CBC plus dose-hold plan are on file, and at that point the ITT HR 0.52 is a fair trade. Credit where it is due on the HER2 axis: the advocate's outright rejection of disitamab vedotin for its MMAE neuropathy and neutropenia is the call I would make too.

docs.title: Olaparib + bevacizumab (maintenance) (olaparib-bevacizumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2lowThis is the biggest number on the board, HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45) with mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 months in HRD-positive disease, and she is already running the bevacizumab backbone it needs. The bet: send a validated MyChoice GIS, and given her documented chromosomal instability I expect it to clear 42, which opens PAOLA-1 and the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive HR of 0.43. Preclinical work shows anti-angiogenics manufacture an HR defect in BRCA-proficient cells and sensitize them to PARP trapping (pmid:31092693), so the combination has a real reason to work in her exact genotype. Two toxicities stack, PARP myelosuppression and bevacizumab VTE/bleeding against her prior IVC filter, though the bev risk is one she is already carrying.The whole case rests on a MyChoice GIS that has not been run; come back under 42 and she is HRD-negative, dropping this to the ITT HR 0.59.; Layering PARP marrow toxicity onto bevacizumab clotting and bleeding risk in a woman with a prior IVC filter is the combination I worry about most. conservative5lowThis is the highest-magnitude PARP option on paper (HRD-positive PFS HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.45; the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup HR is 0.43), and she is already on the bevacizumab backbone PAOLA-1 requires. But eligibility is contingent: the label-relevant benefit lives in HRD-positive disease defined by Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not meet that bar. Below a validated GIS >=42 she is HRD-negative and defaults to all-comer niraparib. I rank it last and strictly conditional, because the combination ran G3+ AEs around 57% (hypertension 19%, anemia 17%), and the bevacizumab-driven hypertension and VTE/bleeding risk compound her thrombotic history.Eligibility contingent on a validated MyChoice GIS >=42 the patient does not yet have; Combination G3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19% and anemia 17% touch both the VTE caution and the myelosuppression veto; Highest toxicity burden of the maintenance options critic4moderatePAOLA-1 is RoB2 low, but the headline HR 0.33 is the HRD-positive subgroup, defined by MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and she has neither. Her qualitative Altera instability call does not clear that companion-diagnostic bar, so on today's data she falls into the ITT estimand (HR 0.59, 0.49-0.72) or defaults to HRD-negative. I put it below the all-comer PARPs precisely because the impressive number is subgroup-derived and contingent on a validated GIS she has not had. Bevacizumab toxicity also stacks on PARP myelosuppression.The label-relevant HR 0.33 is a subgroup estimand she does not yet qualify for; ITT HR is 0.59; Eligibility contingent on a validated GIS (MyChoice >=42) she has not had; qualitative Altera call does not meet it; Combination grade 3+ AE ~57%; hypertension 19% plus PARP anemia 17%, stacking bev VTE/bleeding risk on myelosuppression concensusite2moderateIf a validated genomic-instability score comes back at or above threshold, this is the highest-category play she has: NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 puts olaparib + bevacizumab at category 1 for HRD-positive disease, and ESMO scores the BRCA/HRD-positive combination on MCBS v2.0. She is already on the bevacizumab half, so it is an add rather than a switch. The catch is the gate: PAOLA-1 (pmid 31851799) concentrates its benefit in HRD-positive tumors defined by Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not clear that bar.Eligibility is contingent: she is BRCA wild-type with only a qualitative Altera instability read, so the cat-1 HRD-positive estimand (HR 0.33) does not yet apply, and below a validated GIS >=42 she defaults to the HRD-negative pathway.; Stacking PARP-related anemia on bevacizumab's hypertension and clotting risk is a real load for a patient in her age band with a VTE history and prior IVC filter. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativedissentevidence_qualityI am aiming at your rank-5 placement, not niraparib, because that is where we actually diverge. Burying the HR 0.33 combo (mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 mo, pmid:31851799) at the bottom and calling it strictly conditional treats an unrun GIS as a wall when it is a cheap test, and her documented chromosomal instability makes clearing 42 a live bet. If it comes back positive this is the single biggest play she has, so it belongs on deck, not at the floor.

docs.title: Niraparib (maintenance) (niraparib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1moderatePRIMA enrolled all-comers and still cut progression risk at HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76); in genomically unstable disease like hers the HRD-positive subgroup ran HR 0.43, and that is the upside I am betting on without waiting for a GIS score. The preclinical pharmacology points straight at her genotype: niraparib partitions into tumor at roughly 16-fold higher dose-normalized exposure than olaparib and shrank a BRCA-wild-type PDX by 58% (pmid:30647846), the BRCA-proficient setting she sits in. It is oral, which she wants. The honest catch is myelosuppression at 31% grade 3+ anemia and 28.7% thrombocytopenia, which bumps her veto, so I would start at the individualized weight/platelet dose and watch her baseline WBC of 3.5.Myelosuppression is a named veto and niraparib delivers it; her baseline WBC of 3.5 leaves little headroom even with individualized dosing.; The all-comer HR 0.62 is solid, but the larger 0.43 benefit is a subgroup bet, not a guarantee for her unscored tumor. conservative1moderateNiraparib carries the longest post-marketing PARP safety record in this setting (recurrent-disease approval 2017, 1L all-comer maintenance 2020), so the toxicity is predictable and the management algorithm is settled. PRIMA's all-comer PFS HR was 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76), the cleanest fit here because enrolment never required a BRCA mutation or a validated GIS, and this tumor has neither. The catch is her myelosuppression veto: G3+ anemia 31%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%, against a baseline WBC already at 3.5. I rank it first only with an individualized starting dose, which lowered G3+ thrombocytopenia in PRIMA, plus serial CBCs and dose holds; absent that gating I would veto.Triggers the severe-myelosuppression/febrile-neutropenia veto; the rank is conditional on an individualized starting dose and serial CBC monitoring; Baseline WBC 3.5 leaves little marrow reserve in a patient aged 70-79; PFS benefit only; OS immature at primary report (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.44-1.11) critic1highPRIMA is the cleanest evidence in the file: a 2:1 randomized double-blind phase 3 (n=733) with a pre-specified PFS hit in the all-comer population, HR 0.62 (0.50-0.76, p<0.001), RoB2 low, NEJM. All-comer enrollment is the point. She qualifies without a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score, so the rank-1 claim does not lean on a subgroup. Two honest caveats: PFS is a surrogate and OS was immature at the primary report (HR 0.70, 0.44-1.11, crossing 1), and grade 3+ thrombocytopenia (28.7%) and anemia (31%) run into her myelosuppression veto.Surrogate primary endpoint (PFS); OS immature at primary report with CI crossing 1; Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% collide with the severe-myelosuppression veto; HRD-positive subgroup HR 0.43 is larger but is a subgroup; the overall-population estimand is what applies here concensusite3lowNiraparib is the cleanest all-comer maintenance option that does not wait on a companion-diagnostic result. NCCN Ovarian v3.2024 lists it at category 2A for patients who received bevacizumab, PRIMA (pmid 31562799) enrolled regardless of BRCA or HRD score, and ESMO gives it an MCBS v2.0 score of 2 in the HRD-negative setting. Two things temper it: the NCCN panel itself flags minimal PARP benefit in HR-proficient tumors, and the toxicity collides with her stated veto.Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% (pmid 31562799) trip her severe-myelosuppression veto; the individualized weight/platelet starting dose softens but does not remove that.; Her benefit likely tracks the overall estimand (HR 0.62) rather than the HRD-positive one (HR 0.43), since she is BRCA wild-type with HRD unconfirmed. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocateconservativeendorsepreference_fitThis is how you carry a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7 but drew a hard line on the marrow: conservative ranks niraparib for the efficacy, then gates it on an individualized starting dose plus serial CBCs and says plainly "absent that gating I would veto." That respects the "severe myelosuppression / febrile neutropenia" veto without pretending it forecloses the strongest oral all-comer option, which is the exact tradeoff she set. Her WBC of 3.5 means the gating is not optional, and conservative treats it that way. advocaterisktakerdissentpreference_fitRisktaker ranks the most marrow-toxic agent on the board first (31% grade 3+ anemia, 28.7% thrombocytopenia against a baseline WBC of 3.5) and books the "severe myelosuppression / febrile neutropenia" veto as a dosing footnote to be managed. The 0.7 efficacy lean is real, but it does not dissolve a hard veto; that veto is hers to lift, not the board's to rank past on a subgroup HR she is betting on without a GIS. To risktaker's credit those same vetoes got disitamab vedotin rejected, so apply the standard consistently and let her, not the ranking, decide whether the marrow risk is acceptable. criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityYour rank-1 case leans on niraparib's longest post-marketing safety record, but a safety track record is not an efficacy or risk-of-bias argument, and on the pre-specified numbers ATHENA-MONO's ITT HR 0.52 (pmid:35658487) is larger than PRIMA's 0.62 (pmid:31562799). Both are tier-1b, RoB2-low, all-comer phase 3, so the niraparib-over-rucaparib ordering rests on familiarity rather than evidence quality. Defensible as a management-predictability call, but name it as that, not as the stronger evidence base.

intervention_id: cediranib-olaparib · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Kaplan/Glazer (2019)Sci Transl MedBRCA-wild-type ovarian lines (IGROV1, SKOV3, PEO14) plus BRCA2-mutant PEO1/PEO4 and breast lines; IGROV1 and hypoxia-reporter xenografts in nu/nu micemulti-line panel; xenograft arms (group sizes per arm not specified in text)vehicle; single-agent olaparib; single-agent cediranibcediranib 3-18 mg/kg in vivo (0.25-32 uM in vitro); olaparib 50 mg/kg in vivoCediranib drives down BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 through two routes: VEGFR2-mediated tumor hypoxia, and a hypoxia-independent PDGFR-blockade pathway that activates PP2A and E2F4/p130 transcriptional repression. The result is a contextual, drug-induced HR defect in cells that are genetically HR-proficient.Cediranib produced an HR-deficient state in BRCA-wild-type ovarian cells and sensitized them to olaparib both in culture and in xenografts. This is the mechanistic basis for combining a VEGFR inhibitor with a PARP inhibitor in BRCA-proficient HGSC, the exact genetic context of this tumor.stronghighstrong31092693DOICediranib is the tool VEGFR-TKI here, not the patient's bevacizumab; the induced-HRD concept transfers to anti-angiogenic plus PARP strategy but the specific agent differs. Subcutaneous and reporter xenografts rather than orthotopic peritoneal disease. Lin/Ratner (2018)PLoS OneBRCA-wild-type, PARP-inhibitor-resistant EOC: SKOV3 and OVCAR3 subcutaneous in nude mice; PEO4ip intraperitoneal in SCID-Beige miceper-arm group sizes not stated in abstract; survival cohortsvehicle and lower-order single/double agent armstriapine 10 mg/kg/day, olaparib 50 mg/kg/day, cediranib 0.75 mg/kg/dayTriapine inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and adds replication stress; cediranib suppresses HR via hypoxia and PDGFR blockade; olaparib traps PARP. Stacking the three converges on the same DNA-repair vulnerability in tumors that are genetically HR-proficient and have escaped single-agent PARP inhibition.In the intraperitoneal PEO4ip model the triple combination extended median survival to 89 days versus 62 in controls and beat every lower-order arm. Supports layering anti-angiogenic and replication-stress agents onto a PARP inhibitor in BRCA-wild-type, PARP-resistant disease.moderatemedstrong30444904DOITriapine is not on this patient's option list, so the directly transferable insight is the cediranib-plus-olaparib backbone in BRCA-wild-type disease. PEO4ip carries a reverted BRCA2, a resistance model rather than a naive maintenance setting.

docs.title: VEGF immunoneutralization controls ovarian tumor growth and ascites
docs.text:
intervention_id: bevacizumab · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Mabuchi/Kimura (2012)Br J CancerHuman epithelial ovarian carcinoma xenografts (including HOC22) in mice; chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in concurrent, maintenance, and sequential schedulesmultiple xenograft arms (per-arm group sizes not stated in abstract)cisplatin plus paclitaxel without bevacizumabcisplatin plus paclitaxel induction; bevacizumab concurrent, as maintenance after induction, or started after chemotherapyAdding bevacizumab to platinum-taxane chemotherapy suppresses VEGF-driven angiogenesis during and after cytotoxic treatment. Continuing it as maintenance keeps the residual tumor vasculature suppressed once chemotherapy stops.Bevacizumab with cisplatin and paclitaxel delayed progression, and continuing it as maintenance after chemotherapy gave the longest survival, with complete responses in the HOC22 model. Preclinical mirror of the GOG-218/ICON7 maintenance schedule this patient is on.moderatemedstrong—DOIPMID not independently confirmed in this run; DOI verified (10.1038/bjc.2012.261). Schedule-comparison xenograft work; the maintenance arm is the load-bearing result for the patient's current bevacizumab continuation. Mesiano/Jaffe (1998)Am J PatholHuman SKOV-3 ovarian carcinoma, subcutaneous and intraperitoneal, in immunodeficient mice; treated with anti-VEGF antibody A4.6.1 (the murine antecedent of bevacizumab)xenograft cohorts (group sizes per arm not specified in abstract)untreated tumor-bearing miceA4.6.1 anti-VEGF antibody after 7-10 day engraftmentVEGF supports ovarian tumor growth by driving neovascularization and raises vascular permeability to produce malignant ascites. Blocking VEGF starves the angiogenic supply and shuts down the permeability that fills the peritoneal cavity.A4.6.1 significantly slowed subcutaneous SKOV-3 growth, partly slowed intraperitoneal growth, and abolished ascites formation; tumor regrew once antibody was withdrawn. This is the founding preclinical rationale for the VEGF-maintenance axis the patient is already on with bevacizumab.strongmedstrong9777956DOIA4.6.1 is the precursor antibody clone, not clinical bevacizumab, and growth resumed off-therapy, mirroring the maintenance-not-cure clinical pattern. Older study; the ascites-control finding remains the cleanest mechanistic anchor for anti-VEGF here.

docs.title: Aromatase inhibition in ER-alpha-positive ovarian cancer xenografts
docs.text:
intervention_id: letrozole · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Hirakawa/Mizunuma (2014)J Ovarian ResOvariectomized nude mice with peritoneal carcinomatosis: OVCAR-3 (strong ER-alpha) versus DISS (weak ER-alpha)survival cohorts per line (sizes not stated in abstract)untreated tumor-bearing miceletrozole 5 mg/kg/day POAromatase inhibition lowers local estrogen and blunts ER-alpha signaling in ER-positive ovarian tumors. Downstream it reduces VEGF and tumor microvessel density, tying the endocrine effect to an anti-angiogenic, anti-ascites readout.Letrozole prolonged survival in the strongly ER-alpha-positive OVCAR-3 model but did nothing in the weakly positive DISS model, and lowered tumor VEGF and microvessel density. The ER-magnitude dependence fits this patient's ~80% ER-positive but PR-negative profile as a real-but-modest endocrine signal.moderatemedpartial24410765DOIBenefit tracked ER-alpha intensity, and this tumor is ER-positive but PR-negative, predicting a tempered response. No HGSC-specific orthotopic arm; OVCAR-3 is a serous-type line.

docs.title: IL-12 plasmid lipopolymer (GEN-1 / EGEN-001) intraperitoneal immunogene therapy: ID8 preclinical basis
docs.text:
intervention_id: gen-1-il12 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Anwer/Fewell (2010)Gene TherMurine ID8 intraperitoneal ovarian tumor model dosed with mouse IL-12 plasmid formulated in PEG-PEI-cholesterol lipopolymer (pmIL-12/PPC); plus first-in-human phase Itumor-bearing mouse cohorts plus 13-patient phase Iuntreated/empty-vector tumor-bearing micepmIL-12/PPC ~100 ug/treatment IP, dosing from ~day 18 post-implant, with or without carboplatin/paclitaxelLocal intraperitoneal delivery of an IL-12-encoding plasmid produces sustained, compartment-restricted IL-12 and IFN-gamma rather than a short systemic protein bolus. That shifts the peritoneal immune microenvironment toward a Th1 program and lowers ascitic VEGF.In ID8 mice, pmIL-12/PPC raised peritoneal IL-12 and IFN-gamma, drove a Th1 gene-expression shift, dropped ascitic VEGF, and improved survival alone and with chemotherapy. Mechanistic foundation for the GEN-1/IMNN-001 program this patient received, working through the TME rather than the foreclosed MSI/TMB checkpoint axis.moderatemedstrong20033066DOIThe ID8 preclinical package is reported alongside the phase I in this and companion Imunon/EGEN sources rather than as a single standalone mouse paper; treat as the preclinical-plus-early-clinical anchor. Syngeneic ID8 immunogenicity may exceed human HGSC, and MSS/TMB-low status argues against single-agent checkpoint blockade, not against this IL-12 route.

docs.title: PI3K inhibition (BKM120) plus olaparib in PIK3CA-altered ovarian cancer
docs.text:
intervention_id: pi3k-pathway-investigational · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Wang/Cheng (2016)OncotargetPIK3CA-altered ovarian lines (SKOV3, HEYA8, IGROV1, EFO27); intraperitoneal SKOV3-luciferase dissemination xenograft in NOD/SCID micemulti-line panel; IP xenograft cohort (per-arm sizes not stated in abstract)vehicle; single-agent BKM120; single-agent olaparibBKM120 (buparlisib) plus olaparib, single-agent and combination per protocolPan-class-I PI3K inhibition with BKM120 lowers BRCA1/2 expression in responsive PIK3CA-altered ovarian cells, manufacturing a homologous-recombination defect. That induced HRD then makes otherwise HR-proficient cells vulnerable to PARP trapping.BKM120 plus olaparib was synergistic, raising DNA damage and apoptosis and shrinking tumor burden in the intraperitoneal model; cells that dropped BRCA1/2 most on PI3K inhibition responded best. Investigational rationale connecting the patient's PIK3CA amplification to the PARP/HRD axis, distinct from the foreclosed BRCA-mutation route.moderatemedpartial26909613DOIModels carry PIK3CA point mutations; the patient has PIK3CA amplification, so the dependency may differ in degree. Strictly investigational, with no approved PI3K-directed therapy in HGSC; surfaced as a mechanism-level link, not a near-term option.

docs.title: T-DXd (DS-8201a) foundational pharmacology versus T-DM1
docs.text:
intervention_id: trastuzumab-deruxtecan · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Mauricio/Santin (2023)Gynecol Oncol12 primary carcinosarcoma cell lines (8 uterine, 4 ovarian) across HER2/neu 3+/1+/0; in vivo SARARK-9 HER2 3+ uterine flank xenograft in mice12 primary lines (3 used in vitro); n=5 mice/arm in vivo (n=4 vehicle, days 4-11)isotype-control ADC MAAA-9199 (4 mg/kg) and PBS vehicleDS-8201a 4 mg/kg, single retro-orbital IV injectionSame DXd topoisomerase I payload and membrane-permeable bystander spillover, tested in gynecologic carcinosarcoma. Cytotoxicity scaled with HER2/neu, and the freed payload reached adjacent HER2-null cells in coculture.In HER2 3+ ovarian and uterine lines DS-8201a IC50 ran about 0.03 uM against roughly 9 uM for the isotype control, with no separation in the HER2-0 line. Coculture gave 52% killing of HER2-0 cells next to 3+ cells, and the 3+ xenograft regressed with 60% of mice disease-free at day 52.strongmedpartial36610380DOIThe only ovarian in-vivo T-DXd data in this dossier, but the tissue is carcinosarcoma rather than high-grade serous and the xenograft used a HER2 3+ line. In-vitro potency was quantified at 3+ and 0, not at the patient's 1+ tier, so activity at IHC 1+ rests on the bystander route rather than direct proof. Ogitani/Agatsuma (2016)Clin Cancer ResHER2-positive breast and gastric cell lines plus breast PDX models, including low-HER2 and T-DM1-refractory PDX, in micemulti-line panel plus several PDX arms; per-arm group sizes not stated in the abstractT-DM1DS-8201a IV; tumor regression at doses above 1 mg/kg in gastric modelsDS-8201a carries about 8 exatecan-derivative topoisomerase I payloads per antibody against T-DM1's roughly 3.5, and the freed DXd crosses cell membranes. The heavier payload load plus a diffusible toxin reaches tumor cells that take up little HER2.Growth inhibition tracked HER2 level but did not need high expression: DS-8201a regressed breast PDX models with low HER2 and tumors that had stopped responding to T-DM1. Chk1 and gamma-H2AX phosphorylation confirmed the topoisomerase I DNA-damage route.strongmedcross tumor only27026201DOIBreast and gastric models, no ovarian arm. The low-HER2 activity is the load-bearing point for an IHC 1+ tumor, but the proof here sits in a different tissue. Ogitani/Agatsuma (2016)Cancer SciCoculture of HER2-positive KPL-4 with HER2-negative MDA-MB-468; mixed NCI-N87 (HER2+) and luciferase-tagged MDA-MB-468 (HER2-) xenografts in nude mice, with a separate opposite-flank HER2-negative tumorin-vitro cocultures plus mixed-population and dual-flank xenograft cohorts; group sizes not stated in the abstractT-DM1; opposite-flank HER2-negative tumor as a spatial controlnot detailed in the abstractDXd freed inside a HER2-positive cell is membrane-permeable, so it passes into neighboring cells whatever their HER2 level. T-DM1's charged Lys-SMCC-DM1 payload stays trapped and produces no such spillover.In mixed cultures and co-implanted xenografts DS-8201a killed the HER2-negative population, but it left HER2-negative tumors growing on the opposite flank untouched. Bystander reach is local and needs HER2-positive cells nearby.strongmedcross tumor only27166974DOIBreast and gastric lines, not ovarian. An IHC 1+ tumor carries sparse HER2-positive cells, so how far the local bystander effect extends at that antigen density is the open question this study cannot answer.
