docs.title: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance in the PIK3CA-pathway-altered patient, sequenced around the surgical bleeding window (aspirin-pik3ca)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic1moderateThis is the only RoB2:Low randomized phase 3 in the dossier where the biomarker matches the patient and the pre-specified primary endpoint actually cleared alpha. ALASCCA (Frödin 2025 NEJM, n=626, aspirin 160 mg vs placebo x3 yr) hit HR 0.49 for time to recurrence in Group A (PIK3CA exon 9/20, which is the allele class M1043I sits in), 95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044; Group B ran HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21-0.83. The direction replicates in the pre-specified PIK3CA-activating subgroup of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (celecoxib DFS HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.88; OS HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.79) and in the Liao 2012 NHS+HPFS observational data (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06-0.61). Three datasets, two of them RCT-grade, all pointing the same way, with a coherent COX-2 / PGE2 / PI3K mechanism underneath. What I won't paper over: every one of those trials enrolled resected stage I-III disease, not stage IV with active peritoneal spread. The biology travels to this patient; the trial population does not. So I rank it first as a feature-targeting adjunct for the post-CRS window, not as antitumor therapy for active metastatic disease, and the whole thing rides on top of a real chemo backbone, not instead of one.Indication gap. ALASCCA and 80702 randomized resected stage I-III. This patient is stage IV with active peritoneal disease. The biomarker match is real; the endpoint validation does not extend to the metastatic setting.; RoB2 D5, selective reporting / fragility: the Group A upper CI bound is 0.98. Direction is durable across three datasets, magnitude is not.; 80702 celecoxib is a biomarker subgroup of a trial whose overall primary endpoint was negative. Pre-specified, but still a subgroup, with the effect-size precision caveats that implies.; Liao 2012 is ROBINS-I:Moderate observational. It earns its place as a third concordance signal, not as a standalone hazard estimate.; M1043I is exon 20 kinase-domain. ALASCCA Group A pools exon 9/20; the M1043I-specific subset within Group A is not reported, so the allele-class match is right but the exact-allele read is unmeasured. concensusite——did not pick— advocate4moderateALASCCA (pmid:40961426) is a 2025 phase 3 that met its primary endpoint: in resected CRC with a PI3K-pathway alteration, 160 mg aspirin cut time-to-recurrence with an HR of 0.49 in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 group — and M1043I is a kinase-domain (exon 20) allele that falls squarely in that Group A. The older Liao cohort (pmid:23094721) and the celecoxib subset of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (pmid:38889377) point the same direction. This is not a substitute for a targeted agent; it is a low-cost, oral, well-tolerated layer that the patient's own PIK3CA biology argues for, which is exactly the kind of option the surface-everything preference set asks me to carry. The metastatic setting differs from the resected adjuvant trials, so I am framing this as a post-HIPEC adjuvant-equivalent adjunct, not a metastatic-disease treatment claim.Bleeding risk is the real constraint: aspirin has to be sequenced around bevacizumab co-administration and paused across the CRS-HIPEC operative window per surgical protocol. This is a timing question the treating team owns, not a contraindication.; The evidence base is adjuvant/resected disease; extrapolating to a metastatic patient is a mechanism-and-safety argument, not a direct efficacy claim — I am labeling it as such.; Best deployed as an adjunct layered on top of the systemic backbone, not as a standalone move, so it should not compete for the primary-therapy slot.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticdissentevidence_qualityAspirin is a defensible cheap adjunct, but ranking it first is an evidence-pyramid reflex that mistakes a resected-stage-I-III recurrence HR of 0.49 with a 0.98 upper bound (pmid:40961426) for something that controls active peritoneal stage-IV disease, which it does not. The critic dismisses every pan-RAS agent as 'codon-agnostic structural binding, not efficacy' yet the RAS(ON) glue binds GTP-loaded RAS at a site A59T does not disrupt (pmid:38778099), which is exactly the switch-II biology this atypical allele needs and no other option on the board reaches. For a patient with a real driver and 0.70 efficacy weight, an adjunct that halves recurrence in a different disease setting is not the number-one swing. conservativeadvocateendorseevidence_qualityThis is the one pick where my do-no-harm prior and the advocate land in the same place. ALASCCA (NEJM 2025, n=626, RoB2:Low) hit its primary endpoint with time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (0.24-0.98) in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 Group A that M1043I maps into, and the AE picture is why it clears my bar without hedging - G3+ bleeding ~3% vs 2%, decades of post-marketing data, a fully-mapped management algorithm - with the advocate framing the adjuvant-vs-metastatic gap and the peri-operative bleeding hold honestly. Confirm M1043I is somatic and clonal on the pending NGS before leaning on the Group A match and reintroduce in the post-HIPEC window; beyond that I have nothing to add. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitWe land in the same place, and I'll take the qualified agreement, but the fragility read (Group A upper CI 0.98) is the same evidence NCCN weighed before adopting ALASCCA (pmid:40961426) into v4.2025 for stage II-III; a 2A-grade recommendation reflects expert calibration of exactly the CI the critic is reading, so fragile-RCT and guideline-endorsed are both true at once. The guideline-fit point the strict-evidence frame underweights: the binding limiter for this patient is the indication gap, since NCCN's adoption is adjuvant/resected, not the width of the confidence interval. The celecoxib subgroup concordance (pmid:38889377) is why the direction survived that scrutiny. advocatecriticqualifiedpreference_fitThe critic is right on the evidence, and I want to concede it cleanly: aspirin is the one biomarker-matched RoB2:Low phase 3 on the board (ALASCCA, HR 0.49 in the exon-9/20 group M1043I sits in), and the A59T pan-RAS efficacy gap the critic keeps naming is real - those trials rest on codon-agnostic binding, not an A59T response curve. Where I qualify is the ranking lens. Aspirin is a resected-disease adjuvant signal, honestly flagged by the critic as not transferring verbatim to active peritoneal metastatic disease; the patient weights efficacy at 0.70 and prefers trials. For her preference set, a low-cost post-HIPEC adjunct earns a place on the plan but not the top slot ahead of the first trials that can act on her actual driver. So: keep aspirin, layer it in the post-HIPEC window where its evidence lives, and let the codon-agnostic RAS and CGT6297 CRC-PIK3CA referrals sit above it - the evidence pyramid the critic defends and the preference set the patient stated point at different rank orders, and for the advocate seat the preference set wins the tie.

docs.title: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) and other RAS(ON) inhibitors on codon-agnostic pan-RAS baskets — lead the inquiry with the trials whose written eligibility does not name a codon (Jacobio JAB-23E73 NCT06973564, Pfizer PF-07934040 NCT06447662 'any KRAS variant', Roche RO7673396 NCT06884618, RevMed RAS(ON)+ivonescimab NCT07397338, Adlai AN9025 NCT07252479) (daraxonrasib-rmc6236)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate1moderateThis is the pick the user has been waiting for. The prior codon-selective drugs could not touch a switch-II A59T, and the case sat in that gap. The new sweep brings in pan-RAS agents whose written eligibility asks only for a documented KRAS/NRAS/HRAS mutation — Pfizer's PF-07934040 spells out 'any KRAS variant' for its CRC cohort, which is the cleanest codon-agnostic gate on the board, and Jacobio, Roche, Adlai and the RevMed RAS(ON)+ivonescimab study read the same way. Mechanistically the RAS(ON) tri-complex binds GTP-loaded RAS regardless of the mutation site, and RMC-6236 regressed KRAS-mutant CRC/PDAC/NSCLC models across G12/G13/Q61 alleles (pmid:38778099, pmid:38778097); A59T applicability is a structural read-across, not direct A59T efficacy data, and I am saying that plainly. Prefers-trials, efficacy-leaning, surface-every-option — this pick clears all three, and the single sponsor call confirming A59T counts as a qualifying RAS allele is the highest-leverage action on the whole dossier.A59T eligibility rests on sponsor interpretation of codon-agnostic protocol text. The written gate reads open; whether a switch-II A59 allele counts as a qualifying RAS mutation is the one confirmation that makes or breaks enrollment, and it is a phone call, not a biopsy.; Several of the strongest-worded codon-agnostic baskets are China-sponsored (YL-17231, GH55, BPI-572270), which is an access barrier for a US patient — so I am leading with the US-feasible programs (Pfizer, Roche, Jacobio, RevMed, Adlai) and keeping the China rows as fallback.; Class-typical RAS(ON)/pan-RAS toxicity (rash, GI) is real but preferences.json carries no toxicity veto and the efficacy weight is 0.70, so this is counseling burden, not a blocker.; Sequencing: dose-finding enrollment competes with the planned CRS-HIPEC window. If the surgery is near-term, the honest framing is that a phase 1 slot may be a post-operative or post-progression option rather than something that displaces the operative plan now.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocateendorseevidence_qualityAgreed on the ranking and the honesty flag: the pan-RAS RAS(ON) class is the first real shot at A59T and A59T applicability is a structural read-across, not allele-matched data (pmid:38778099). One sharpening, not a disagreement: the NCT07397338 suite mixes codon-selective agents (elironrasib G12C, zoldonrasib G12D) that are mechanism-mismatched to a switch-II A59T, so lead specifically with the codon-agnostic daraxonrasib/PF-07934040 gates (nct:NCT06447662, 'any KRAS variant') rather than the whole basket. Endorse the pick and the sponsor-call-first action. conservativeadvocatedissentevidence_qualitySame objection I raised to the risktaker, with equal force: the advocate's own rationale concedes A59T applicability is a structural read-across pending a sponsor phone call, then ranks it #1 anyway. A codon-agnostic protocol gate is an eligibility question, not evidence the drug works on this allele - the empirical daraxonrasib readouts are all canonical codons and the CRC signal is a ~9% corporate ORR without CIs. Surfacing these trials is fine and the sponsor call is worth making; the rank is the problem, because a mechanism bet with no allele-matched efficacy sits below the standard backbone and below aspirin, not at the top. criticadvocatedissentevidence_qualityYou flag the A59T read-across honestly in the rationale, and I still land on dissent, because the rank does not match what the evidence supports. 'Any KRAS variant' on Pfizer's protocol and the structural argument from Knox 2025 (pmid:40056080, A59T untested) put this at hypothesis-grade for the patient's actual allele; the peer-reviewed daraxonrasib data is PDAC codons 12/13/61 (Wolpin 2026, pmid:42090791), and the CRC monotherapy signal is a corporate ORR ~9% with no N and no CI. Your rank 2, CGT6297, has the cleaner story on paper, an explicit CRC-plus-PIK3CA cohort, but the pharmacology behind mutant-selective PI3K-alpha at a kinase-domain allele lives entirely in breast and gynecologic conference abstracts: RLY-2608 kinase-domain ORR 66.7% (95% CI 38.4-88.2) is ASCO 2025 abstract 1086 in breast plus fulvestrant (informal:high, PMID-null), and tersolisib is ESMO 2024. A protocol slot that names CRC is an eligibility fit, not CRC efficacy, and M1043I is non-canonical relative to the H1047R/E545K data those agents were built on. concensusiteadvocatedissentguideline_fitSame guideline problem as the risktaker seat, sharper here because it is rank 1 on codon-agnostic protocol text plus a sponsor call: that is off-guideline for the indication. NCCN Colon v5.2025 routes A59T mCRC to comprehensive NGS (category 1) and trial enrollment (category 2A); daraxonrasib itself carries no category, and its peer-reviewed pivotal readout (Wolpin, pmid:42090791) is PDAC on canonical codons. I endorse it as a trial referral once the workup finishes, not as the day-one move ahead of the NGS that gates it.

docs.title: Botensilimab + balstilimab (Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 + anti-PD-1) (NCT05608044) (botensilimab-balstilimab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2moderateThe patient is the exact phenotype where bot/bal actually worked — peritoneal-dominant disease after liver-met resection is the no-liver-mets subset that hit ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo where the liver-mets group managed only 5% (pmid:38871975). The randomized update called out confirmed responses at peritoneal sites specifically, which is this patient's whole disease compartment. MSS/TMB-low usually kills the immuno-oncology conversation, but Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 is the one construct with a real MSS signal, and I would rather chase a 20%-plus response at the right anatomy than write immunotherapy off on marker status alone.Eligibility is 2L+ — the patient is on 1L FOLFIRI-bev now and has to progress before enrolling, which the pick's timing depends on; G3+ immune-mediated AE rate around 35% (colitis, hepatitis) is not trivial ahead of major cytoreductive surgery; The A59T immuno-oncology-enrichment literature does not apply here: this patient is MSS/TMB-low/PD-L1-neg, the opposite of the A59T-enriched pattern (pmid:33945173), so response is not a given conservative——did not pick— critic2lowBest MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal on the table, and the reason it earns rank 2 is compartment-specific: this patient's peritoneal-only, post-liver-resection disease is exactly the no-liver-mets phenotype where the drug works. Bullock 2024 Nat Med (phase 1b expansion, r/r MSS mCRC, n=101) reported all-comer ORR 17%, 95% CI 10-26, with the NLM subset at ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo against ORR 5% when liver mets were active. The 2024 randomized phase 2 update (n=123 NLM, BOT+BAL vs BOT mono) held the combination at ORR 19% with mOS near 21 mo and specifically flagged responses at peritoneal sites, which is the patient's dominant disease compartment. That peritoneal-site call is the single most decision-relevant fact I can pull for this individual. Now the bias read: it is a single-arm phase 1b plus a randomized phase 2 against monotherapy, not against BSC or chemo. NLM was carved out as the responder phenotype post-hoc, not locked as a pre-specified primary stratum, so the 22% ORR and 20.9 mo mOS are subgroup numbers without CIs in the dossier row. The registrational test that matters, CCTG NCT07152821 vs BSC, has not read out. It sits below aspirin because it is a 2L+ proposition that only activates on progression past current 1L, not because the signal is weaker.No randomized readout against BSC or SoC yet. Single-arm phase 1b plus a phase 2 whose comparator is monotherapy; CCTG phase 3 NCT07152821 is the pending confirmatory test.; Selection on the NLM phenotype was post-hoc in the Bullock expansion, not a pre-specified primary stratum. The 22% subgroup ORR carries that caveat.; Dossier risk-of-bias is informal:med, not RoB2:Low, with open-label outcome ascertainment for ORR.; G3+ irAE 35% in phase 1 and 38% in the phase 2 update. That is the real toxicity envelope in a patient also heading into CRS.; Not a 1L pick. Sequencing-dependent, contingent on FOLFIRI-bev progression. concensusite——did not pick— advocate3highBullock 2024 (pmid:38871975) put ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo on the board for the no-liver-mets MSS mCRC cohort, and the randomized phase 2 update called out peritoneal-site responses specifically. This patient is the exact phenotype that signal came from — liver mets resected, peritoneal-dominant disease — which is the strongest MSS-CRC immunotherapy read available and the one that actually maps to her disease compartment. The USC protocol takes any KRAS mutation on its face, so A59T is in without a codon argument. MSS keeps single-agent ICI off the table, and I am being clear that the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 mechanism is what makes this an exception rather than the rule. Required prior fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + irinotecan means she enrolls after progressing past 1L, so this is the 2L+ pivot, not a displacement of FOLFIRI-bev now.Sequencing and prior-therapy gate: the USC protocol requires prior oxaliplatin, which her FOLFIRI-bev history does not yet include — so realistically this is post-1L-progression or post-HIPEC, and the Agenus expanded-access route (NCT06751524) is the off-trial channel if standard options are exhausted first.; G3+ irAE around 35% (diarrhea/colitis, hepatitis); no veto bars it and the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 management algorithms are codified, but it is a genuine counseling point at 0.70 efficacy weight.; The fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C arm on the USC protocol adds patient burden that preferences.json does not flag against — surface it at consent rather than treating it as a blocker; the plain Agenus bot/bal protocol is the lower-burden alternative.; Peritoneal cavity is an immunologically distinct compartment (omental milky-spot biology), so response there is not guaranteed to track liver-met data — but the phase 2 update specifically reported peritoneal responses, which is the reassuring signal for this patient.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativecriticendorsetoxicityI endorse the critic's read here, placement included. Bullock 2024 (Nat Med, n=101) gave ORR 22% in the no-liver-mets subset that is this patient's exact post-resection phenotype, and the randomized update flagged confirmed responses at peritoneal sites - the dominant compartment here - which is the strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal of the modern era. What I want explicit on the record is the toxicity the critic already names: G3+ irAE ~35-38%, immune-mediated colitis 12-13%, hepatitis ~8%, in a patient also facing CRS - an envelope with a codified steroid/infliximab algorithm, which is why this is a right-center, 2L+ pick rather than a first move, exactly where the critic ranked it.

docs.title: CGT6297 mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor, CRC + PIK3CA cohort (NCT07383506) (cgt6297-pi3ka)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowThis is the cleanest PIK3CA-and-CRC match on the board — phase 1b Cohort 3 names PIK3CA-mutant colorectal cancer explicitly, and M1043I is a kinase-domain activating allele that fits the oncogenic-mutation gate. The upside case is a mutant-selective agent that hits the driver while sparing wild-type PI3K, which is what limited alpelisib (G3+ hyperglycemia ~20%, pmid:29401002); the double-mutant biology (pmid:31699932) and INAVO120's HR 0.43 in PIK3CA-mutant breast (pmid:39476340) say this axis is genuinely druggable. I concede the CRC PI3K-alpha monotherapy track record is thin — 2 CRC PRs of 134 in the alpelisib first-in-human — so the real play may be pairing this with the RAS-pathway pick rather than solo.KRAS co-activation historically blunts PI3K-alpha monotherapy in CRC — vertical RAS+PI3K blockade is the mechanistically sound play but doubles the toxicity load; M1043I is a non-canonical hotspot (not H1047R/E545K), so 'oncogenic PIK3CA' eligibility and mutant-selectivity against this specific allele both need confirming; Diabetes and prior PI3K/AKT/mTOR exposure gate enrollment; hyperglycemia management overlaps poorly with the peri-operative window conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

intervention_id: smad4-prognosis · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Sjoblom/Schweiger (2021)Mol Cancer ResEngineered SMAD4-R361 mutant CRC cell lines; pull-down + reporter assays; xenograft growthn=3 biological replicates; xenograft n=6/armWT SMAD4 isogenic; SMAD4-nullnot applicable (mechanism)R361 hotspot mutants in the MH2 domain disrupt heterodimer formation with SMAD2/3 (canonical TGF-beta loss-of-function) while simultaneously gaining enhanced binding to LEF1, amplifying Wnt/beta-catenin transcription. ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Waight/Wilson (2024)Cancer DiscovMouse surrogate of botensilimab (mFc-engineered anti-mouse CTLA-4); syngeneic models including poorly immunogenic and ICI-refractory tumors; FcgammaR-knockout micen=8-12 mice/arm; multiple syngeneic modelsisotype Fc-wildtype anti-CTLA-4; anti-PD-1 alone10 mg/kg IP weeklyFc-engineering increases affinity for activating FcgammaRs (especially FcgammaRIV/CD16a), which (i) enhances Treg depletion in tumors, (ii) promotes myeloid antigen-presenting cell activation, and (iii) potentiates T-cell priming - the constellation needed to convert immune-cold MSS tumors into responsive ones.Surrogate botensilimab regressed multiple ICI-refractory syngeneic models that resisted Fc-WT anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1, with rejection of rechallenge. Provides the mechanistic basis for the clinical activity of botensilimab + balstilimab in MSS CRC where conventional ipilimumab/nivolumab fails.stronghighstrong—DOIMouse Fc-engineered surrogate, not the clinical human IgG1. Tumor models are syngeneic, not orthotopic peritoneal. Clinical CRC ORR in early reports was ~22%, consistent with the preclinical 'turns cold tumors warm' framing. Carozza/Li (2023)Cancer Res (AACR abstract LB323)CT26 mouse CRC; in vitro PBMC IFN-beta induction; combination with anti-PD-1 or anti-CTLA-4n=8-12 mice/armvehicle, ICI aloneSR-8541A 10-30 mg/kg PO QDENPP1 hydrolyzes the STING agonist 2'3'-cGAMP in the tumor microenvironment, dampening innate immune activation. ENPP1 inhibition raises extracellular cGAMP, activates STING in DCs and macrophages, and increases type-I IFN signaling - a complement to Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade in cold tumors.SR-8541A produced CT26 tumor regression as monotherapy and synergized with ICI to extend survival. Rangel-Moreno/Randall (2010)J ImmunolMouse peritoneal cavity / omentum immunohistology; tumor-cell seeding; B1 lymphocyte and DC characterizationn=5-10 mice per experimentsplenectomized + lymph-node-deficient comparatorsnot applicable (immune anatomy)Omental milky spots are organized immune aggregates rich in B1 lymphocytes, peritoneal macrophages, and DCs. They serve as the primary lymphoid niche for the peritoneal cavity but are skewed away from canonical antitumor adaptive responses, biasing the peritoneal microenvironment toward myeloid-suppressed states.Omental milky spots preferentially trap disseminating tumor cells and modulate local T-cell priming; the peritoneal cavity is dominated by B1 cells rather than conventional B2 follicular cells. docs.title: What this page is
docs.text:
Libby is a tool that looks for treatments aimed at the specific genetic changes in one person's cancer. It read the details of your case, searched the published studies and open clinical trials, and put together four options that target the particular mutations found in your tumor. This page walks through those four in plain language: what each one is, what the upside might look like, what the risks are, and where the evidence is strong or thin.

A few things to hold onto as you read. Libby only looks at options tied to your tumor's targetable features. The rest of your care — the chemotherapy you're on now, the surgery that's being planned, and the standard drugs that go with all of that — is your oncology team's job, and it isn't on this page. That doesn't make those things less important. It just means they live in a different conversation. And none of what follows is a treatment plan. It's material to bring to your oncologist so you can ask sharper questions.

docs.title: What we know about your cancer
docs.text:
You have colon cancer that has spread beyond the colon. It reached your liver, where the spots were removed with surgery, and it's now present on the peritoneum — the lining of the belly. You're on your first course of chemotherapy (a combination called FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab), and a specialized operation is being planned: surgery to remove visible disease, followed by heated chemotherapy washed through the abdomen during the same procedure. That operation is usually written as CRS-HIPEC.

Your tumor's genetic testing turned up two changes that most of these options aim at. One is in a gene called KRAS — specifically a form called A59T, which is unusual. Most KRAS-targeting drugs were built for the common forms of the mutation, not this one. The other is in a gene called PIK3CA, a change written as M1043I, which switches on a growth pathway inside the cancer cells. Your tumor also tested as what's called MSS (microsatellite stable) with low TMB and negative PD-L1 — three findings that, taken together, usually mean the standard immunotherapy drugs won't help. One of the options below is an exception to that rule, which is why it's here.

One practical note: some of the genetic results are still being confirmed with a fuller round of testing. That confirmation matters for a couple of the options, and we flag where.

docs.title: What you told us matters most
docs.text: You said you lean toward going after the cancer, and you're willing to accept more side effects to do it — you set that dial at about 70 percent toward effectiveness. You didn't rule out any particular side effect ahead of time, and you didn't rule out any type of treatment (pills, infusions, and so on are all on the table). You also said you're open to clinical trials, and you'd rather see specific named trials than vague categories. The options below reflect that: a couple of them are trials.

docs.title: A first step that shapes everything below
docs.text:
Before leaning hard on some of these options, your team will likely want one more round of tumor testing to nail down the exact genetic results. This isn't a treatment — it's a lab test on tissue that's already been collected, so it carries no risk to you. It matters because two of the options below (the aspirin and the PI3K-pathway trial drug) rest on confirming that the PIK3CA change is really driving the cancer, and the KRAS option depends on pinning down the exact KRAS result so a trial can decide whether you qualify. It's worth getting that testing moving early so the answers are in hand when decisions come up.

The other thread running through all of this is timing around your surgery. Several of these options interact badly with an operation — some raise bleeding risk, some slow wound healing, some can cause inflammation that would complicate recovery. None of them are things to start the day before surgery. Where timing matters, we say so.

docs.title: Option 1 — Low-dose aspirin aimed at the PIK3CA change
docs.text:
This is the most solid option on the page, and the simplest: a low daily dose of ordinary aspirin. It's here because of your PIK3CA mutation. A large, well-run randomized trial (called ALASCCA) gave aspirin to colon cancer patients whose tumors carried a PIK3CA-type change, and the group that got aspirin had fewer cancers come back. In numbers you can hold: over three years, about 8 percent of the aspirin patients had a recurrence, versus about 14 percent of those who didn't get it. Two other studies pointed the same direction. So the signal is real and it lines up with your tumor's biology.

The honest limit is this: that trial studied people whose cancer had been fully removed and hadn't spread, not people with active disease in the belly like yours. So the biology travels to your case, but the exact size of the benefit doesn't carry over cleanly — I can't give you a precise number for how much it would help you specifically. The fair way to think about it is as a low-risk extra layer you add on top of your other treatment to lower the odds of the cancer returning, not as a drug that fights the disease that's active now.

The main risk with aspirin is bleeding, and it's modest — in the trial, serious bleeding from the gut happened in about 3 percent of aspirin patients versus about 2 percent without it. The one real catch is timing: aspirin thins the blood, so it has to be paused around your surgery and it stacks with the bevacizumab you're already on. The plan would be to hold it through the operation and add it back afterward, during the recovery-and-maintenance stretch, which is exactly where the trial's evidence lives. It fits what you told us — it's a pill, it's cheap, over the counter, and it doesn't cross any of your lines. The main open question is just the confirmation testing on the PIK3CA result.

docs.title: Option 2 — An immunotherapy pair (botensilimab plus balstilimab)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats. Here's the tradeoff to weigh.

This is two immunotherapy drugs given together that wake up the immune system against the cancer. It's notable because the standard immunotherapy drugs usually don't work for tumors like yours (the MSS, low-TMB, PD-L1-negative combination normally closes that door). This particular pair is the one exception with a genuine track record in this setting — and, importantly, the strongest signal showed up in exactly your situation: people whose liver spots had been removed and whose disease was mainly in the belly. In that group, roughly 1 in 5 saw their tumors shrink, and the study specifically noted responses in the peritoneum, your main area of disease.

Here's what to weigh against that. The evidence is early — it comes from a small study where everyone got the drugs, with no proper comparison group, so those response numbers are promising but not yet confirmed by the kind of head-to-head trial that settles the question (that larger trial is underway but hasn't reported). And the side effects are real: because these drugs unleash the immune system, it can turn on healthy organs. Serious immune-related problems — most often inflammation of the colon or the liver — happened in roughly a third of patients. That's a lot, and it matters more for you because immune inflammation overlapping with your planned surgery could delay or complicate recovery. No one died from the treatment in the reported group, and there's a well-established playbook (steroids and other medicines) for managing these reactions.

There's also a timing point that isn't a caveat so much as a fact about when this becomes available: the trials that would enroll you require having tried and progressed through standard chemotherapy first. So this isn't a right-now move — it's an option for later, if your current chemo stops working or after your surgery. If you go this route, it should be at a center that runs these immunotherapy trials regularly and has a standing plan for catching and treating the immune side effects early.

docs.title: Option 3 — A targeted pill for the PIK3CA pathway (a mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats. Here's the tradeoff to weigh.

This is a newer class of pill designed to shut down the same growth pathway your PIK3CA mutation switches on — but more precisely than older drugs, hitting the mutated version while mostly sparing normal cells. The appealing part is that one of these trials (a study of a drug called CGT6297) has a group written specifically for colon cancer with a PIK3CA change, which is an unusually good match on paper for your tumor.

Two things pull the certainty down, and they're worth being straight about. First, there's almost no evidence yet for how this class works in colon cancer specifically. The encouraging results so far come from other cancers — mostly breast — and some of them are early conference reports rather than finished, published studies. In colon cancer, the track record is only a couple of responses out of a larger group. Second, and this is the more technical point: your particular PIK3CA change (M1043I) is a less common, "off-hotspot" version. The drugs in this class were built and tested mainly against the more usual PIK3CA changes. When a mutation sits off the well-studied hotspots like this, it's a weaker signal that the drug will help — a less sure bet than if you'd had one of the classic changes. That makes this a more uncertain option than it might first appear, and the confirmation testing could sharpen the picture. There's also a wrinkle from your KRAS mutation: it can partly route around this kind of drug, which is another reason to keep expectations measured and why the drug might work better in combination than alone.

The main side effect of this class is high blood sugar, which needs monitoring and can usually be managed; the newer, more selective versions cause much less of it than the older ones. High blood sugar is also awkward to manage right around surgery, so timing would matter here too. This is a trial-only option, which fits your openness to trials — the practical first step would be checking whether that colon-and-PIK3CA trial group is actually open and taking patients.

docs.title: Option 4 — Drugs that go after your specific KRAS mutation (pan-RAS / RAS(ON) inhibitors)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats. Here's the tradeoff to weigh.

This is the only option on the page that reaches your KRAS mutation directly, and that's the entire reason it's here. Your KRAS change (A59T) is an unusual one that the well-known KRAS drugs can't touch. A newer group of drugs works differently — they grip the KRAS protein at a spot that doesn't depend on which exact mutation you have — and on that basis they might be able to engage your A59T change. Some of the newest trials are written to accept "any KRAS mutation," which could open a door for you.

Now the honest part, and it's important: no one has ever shown these drugs actually work on your specific A59T mutation. Not in a trial, not in a person. The reason to think they might is a laboratory and structural argument — the way the drug binds suggests it could reach your mutation — but that's a well-reasoned hunch, not proof. The published results for this class come from a different cancer (pancreatic) and from the common KRAS mutations, not yours; the colon cancer numbers that do exist are low and come from a company update rather than a full published study. So the right way to hold this is as a mechanism bet: a scientifically reasonable idea worth exploring through a trial, not a treatment shown to help people with your mutation. It should never be presented to you as more than that.

Because it's a bet rather than a proven option, the single most useful next step is a phone call: someone on your team asking a trial's sponsor whether they'll accept your specific A59T result as qualifying. That's an eligibility question, and it turns on how the sponsor reads their own rules — it's separate from whether the drug works. The side effects of the lead drug in this class are meaningful (rash, mouth sores, diarrhea, at a rate similar to other targeted drugs), and some of the trial versions combine it with other drugs — including one that affects blood-vessel growth and would need to wait until after your surgery has healed. This is a later-line, trial-based path, to line up once your KRAS result is locked in and your surgery is behind you.

docs.title: Questions to ask your oncologist
docs.text:
• The aspirin option is built on a trial in patients whose cancer had been fully removed, not active disease like mine. Do you think it's still worth adding as a low-risk layer, and when — before or after my surgery?
  • If I take aspirin, how will we handle the bleeding risk alongside the bevacizumab I'm on and around the operation?
  • What's the timeline for the confirmatory tumor testing, and does it change any of these options depending on what comes back?
  • For the immunotherapy pair, what would the plan be for catching and treating immune side effects early, given I have surgery coming up — and does that center have experience running these trials?
  • When would the immunotherapy or the trial options realistically become available for me, relative to where I am now with chemotherapy and surgery?
  • For the PI3K-pathway trial drug: given my PIK3CA change is an off-hotspot type, how much less certain does that make it, and is there a trial group actually open for colon cancer?
  • For the KRAS option, can someone contact a trial's sponsor to ask whether my specific A59T result qualifies me to enroll?
  • Is there any of this we should be lining up now versus waiting until after the surgery, so we don't lose time?

Toxicity burden is patient-level G3+ AE severity (Low / Moderate / High) summarized from trial publications. docs.title: Research question
docs.text: In metastatic osteosarcoma after first-line MAP, what interventions can target DLL3 and PRAME, gated on protein-level confirmation (DLL3 IHC SP347; PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing)?

docs.title: Patient profile (scrubbed)
docs.text:
• Primary site / histology: bone — osteosarcoma
  • Stage: IV (metastatic)
  • Performance status (assumed): ECOG 1
  • Age band (assumed): 18-29 (typical osteosarcoma demographics; not user-supplied)
  • Sex: unknown
  • Biomarkers:
    • DLL3 — RNA only (confirmation_status: rna_only); IHC SP347 status unknown. Decision-relevant resolution: ≥1% (preferably ≥25%) by IHC for DLL3-directed clinical trials.
    • PRAME — RNA only (confirmation_status: rna_only); IHC and HLA-A*02:01 status unknown. Decision-relevant resolution: PRAME IHC positive AND HLA-A02:01-positive (every PRAME-directed ImmTAC and TCR-T in clinical development is HLA-A02:01-restricted).
  • Prior therapy (assumed): MAP frontline; response not provided.

docs.text:

docs.title: Target validation paths
docs.text: The case has two RNA-only targetable features, each with its own protein-level confirmation step. DLL3 IHC (clone SP347) gates the DLL3-directed pathway: tarlatamab via NCT06788938, and the tarlatamab-plus-radiation combination via NCT06814496. PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 typing together gate the PRAME-directed pathway: IMA203 via NCT03686124 (Immatics ACTengine), plus the PRAME ImmTAC class, brenetafusp via NCT04262466 and its successor IMC-P115C via NCT07156136. The two pathways are independent. The patient may have neither, either, or both. All three workup tests can run in parallel on archival tissue and a single blood draw. If both workups return negative, this report has no within-scope recommendations, and the next conversation about standard 2L+ care is the treating team's, not Libby's.

docs.title: DLL3
docs.text:
Before any DLL3-directed therapy decision: DLL3 IHC SP347 on archival FFPE, ≥1% (preferably ≥25%) per NCT06788938's enrollment threshold. Turnaround is one to three weeks; cost is trivial relative to a treatment cycle. First, confirm SP347 assay availability at the treating institution. Not every reference lab carries the Roche Tissue Diagnostics clone used in the tarlatamab development program.

Two refinements sit one tier down. Spatial heterogeneity is a known confounder in solid-tumor DLL3 (Zhang 2023): if multiple tumor blocks are available, IHC on a metastatic site as well as the primary refines confidence in whether the gating result generalizes. Neuroendocrine context (ASCL1 / NEUROD1 / chromogranin / synaptophysin / INSM1 panel) is research-grade for an osteosarcoma. DLL3 is normally a Notch-pathway target on neuroendocrine lineage, so an unexpectedly positive DLL3 IHC in a non-NEC tumor is worth contextualizing before the trial enrollment paperwork.

Germline TP53 sequencing (Li-Fraumeni panel) is a separate kind of finding. It does not affect tarlatamab eligibility, but late-teens / twenties osteosarcoma carries a meaningful prior probability for germline TP53. A positive result changes radiation-sensitivity planning, prompts screening for synchronous tumors, and triggers cascade testing for first-degree relatives. Discuss with a genetic counselor before ordering.

docs.title: PRAME
docs.text:
Two essential tests gate the entire PRAME-directed pathway: PRAME IHC confirms tumor protein expression, and HLA-A*02:01 typing confirms the patient can present the PRAME peptide. Every PRAME-directed ImmTAC and TCR-T in clinical development (IMA203, brenetafusp, IMC-P115C) is HLA-A02:01-restricted; typing-negative patients are foreclosed even when PRAME IHC is strongly positive. PRAME IHC is positive in roughly 56% of osteosarcoma (Iura 2017, n=82); HLA-A02:01 prevalence is ~40–50% in Caucasian populations. Order both alongside the DLL3 IHC: same block, same blood draw, same turnaround window.

Spatial heterogeneity refines confidence at the next tier. PRAME IHC on a metastatic site as well as the primary helps rule out the case where one biopsy hits a focal expression hotspot. Tumor NGS for B2M loss-of-function and HLA-A*02:01 loss-of-heterozygosity is a resistance check: TCR-mediated killing depends on intact antigen presentation, and tumor-specific HLA-LOH is a documented escape mechanism that the IHC and HLA-typing workup will miss by design. Quantifying baseline CD8 T-cell infiltrate density via IHC (or multiplex CD3 / CD8 / FoxP3) is the microenvironment companion: an immune-cold tumor predicts diminished response even when PRAME and HLA are both positive.

docs.title: Biomarker plan
docs.text:
Recommended assay Rationale Suggested assay provider Tissue requirements DLL3 IHC (clone SP347) RNA expression establishes that the DLL3 gene is being transcribed; it does not establish that DLL3 protein sits on the cell surface where a BiTE can engage. NCT06788938 enforces IHC ≥ 25% (stage 1) or ≥ 1% (stage 2) for enrollment, and every approved DLL3-directed therapy gates on protein-level confirmation. Skipping the test forecloses every DLL3-directed candidate downstream by definition. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx (DLL3 IHC reflex)) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 archival FFPE; fresh biopsy not required if stored tissue is adequate DLL3 IHC on multiple tumor regions / metastatic biopsy Osteosarcoma metastases can diverge from primary tumors in surface-marker expression, and the cross-tumor DLL3 literature in solid tumors (Zhang 2023) flags spatial heterogeneity as a frequent confounder. Testing one site can over- or under-estimate enrollment-grade DLL3 status. If only one block is available the workup proceeds with that block, but the result should be interpreted with this caveat in mind. NeoGenomics Laboratories · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 additional archival blocks from a different site if available ASCL1 / NEUROD1 IHC + chromogranin / synaptophysin / INSM1 panel DLL3 is a Notch-pathway target normally expressed in neuroendocrine lineage. In a non-NEC tumor like osteosarcoma, surfacing or excluding any neuroendocrine differentiation pattern (Notch-low / ASCL1-high state) provides mechanistic context for whether DLL3 expression is biologically plausible or a stochastic finding. Does not gate enrollment; informs how the tarlatamab trial outcome should be interpreted. A positive germline TP53 result changes radiation-sensitivity considerations, screening for synchronous tumors, and family screening for first-degree relatives. Does not affect tarlatamab eligibility, but is the kind of finding that would change the surrounding care plan. Invitae (Invitae Common Hereditary Cancers Panel) · test info · 1400 16th Street, San Francisco, CA 94103 · 1-800-436-3037 5–10 mL EDTA whole blood PRAME IHC (clone EPR20330 or equivalent) RNA expression establishes that the PRAME gene is being transcribed; it does not establish that the PRAME peptide is presented at sufficient density to engage a TCR or ImmTAC. PRAME-targeting therapies in development (IMA203 ACTengine, brenetafusp, IMC-P115C) require IHC-confirmed PRAME protein expression on tumor cells. PRAME IHC is positive in ~56% of osteosarcoma (Iura 2017, n=82). Skipping the IHC forecloses every PRAME-directed candidate downstream by definition. NeoGenomics Laboratories · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; same block as the DLL3 IHC HLA Class I high-resolution typing (HLA-A*02:01 specifically) Every PRAME-directed ImmTAC and TCR-T in clinical development is HLA-A02:01-restricted; the PRAME peptide is presented on HLA-A02:01, and patients without this allele cannot present the target. HLA-A02:01 prevalence is ~40–50% in Caucasian populations; without typing, the patient's eligibility for the entire HLA-restricted PRAME class is unknown. Every PRAME-directed program (IMA203 via NCT03686124, brenetafusp, IMC-P115C via NCT07156136) is foreclosed if HLA-A02:01 typing returns negative. Multi-region IHC refines confidence that the binary positive call is representative of the dominant disease. docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text: The dossier surfaces 41 trials on the DLL3 and PRAME axes, 7 clinical-evidence rows (6 included, 1 excluded for sponsor discontinuation), and 6 preclinical rows. Seven rows are ranked: a shared biomarker-workup gate at rank 1, then six antigen-directed therapeutics — three on the DLL3 axis (tarlatamab; tarlatamab + RT) and four on the PRAME axis (IMA203; brenetafusp; IMC-P115C; NW-101C). Agreement scores span 1.0 down to −0.2. All five personas placed their entire ranking behind the workup and none issued a veto. The board split on which drug leads: the critic and conservative rank tarlatamab first on RCT-tier evidence and managed safety, while the risktaker and advocate lead IMA203 on the 0.85 efficacy weight — a genuine efficacy-versus-safety disagreement, not a consensus. The case scopes to the DLL3/PRAME features the user nominated; the guideline TKIs regorafenib and cabozantinib sit off that axis and are named as scope in the caveat below, not ranked.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
Both nominated features are RNA-only, and RNA is not a target. DLL3 RNA does not put DLL3 protein on the cell membrane where a BiTE can engage it; PRAME RNA does not establish that the PRAME peptide is presented on HLA-A02:01 at a density a TCR or ImmTAC can see. The decision resolution is protein-level: DLL3 IHC SP347 at ≥1% (≥25% preferred for stage-1 entry) for the BiTE class, and PRAME IHC plus HLA-A02:01 typing for the entire PRAME class. Until those return, the ranking below is provisional — which is why the workup is rank 1 and every therapeutic rec is tagged conditional.

  • The ranking is scoped to the nominated antigen axis. Only the workup and the DLL3/PRAME-directed therapeutics appear. The DLL3 IHC gate opens the tarlatamab options; PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 together open the PRAME class. The two axes are independent — the patient may have neither, either, or both.
  • Standard care is outside this ranking, on purpose. NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 lists regorafenib as category 1 for relapsed osteosarcoma (SARC024, REGOBONE) and cabozantinib as a listed option (CABONE). Neither acts on DLL3 or PRAME, so neither is a Libby recommendation here — Libby scoped to the features the user supplied, not to the full 2L+ guideline. The concensusite ranked both and the board flagged the tension explicitly; they are named here as the guideline-endorsed path the treating team owns, not because Libby ignored them.
  • If DLL3 is negative, this case has no within-scope DLL3 recommendation; if PRAME IHC or HLA-A*02:01 is negative, no within-scope PRAME recommendation. If all three are negative, this case has no within-scope recommendations; standard-of-care for relapsed osteosarcoma lies outside Libby's targetable-feature ranking and should be pursued through the treating team's normal care channel.
  • Workup logistics. All three tests are non-toxic and batch on archival FFPE plus one blood tube for HLA typing, one to three weeks turnaround, trivial cost against a treatment cycle. Run them in parallel on day one rather than sequencing. Confirm the SP347 clone is stocked at the treating institution — not every reference lab carries it. HLA-A*02:01 is genetic and lifetime-stable, so a single typing is sufficient; its ~40–50% population prevalence means roughly half of patients are foreclosed from the whole PRAME class regardless of PRAME status.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• DLL3 × CD3 BiTEs (biomarker-conditional, actionable via NCT06788938): tarlatamab, alone and combined with radiation (NCT06814496). Anchor evidence: DeLLphi-301 (PMID 37861218) and the confirmatory DeLLphi-304 phase 3 (PMID 40454646) — both SCLC.
  • PRAME TCR-T (biomarker-conditional, actionable via NCT03686124, sarcoma cohort named): IMA203, plus the registry-only successor NW-101C (NCT07266298). Anchor: Wermke et al., Nat Med 2025 (PMID 40205198; ORR 54% in a PRAME+ HLA-A*02:01+ pan-solid basket).
  • PRAME × CD3 ImmTAC bispecifics (biomarker-conditional): brenetafusp / IMC-F106C (NCT04262466, sarcoma cohort active-not-recruiting) and its next-generation successor IMC-P115C (NCT07156136, recruiting). Class-validated by tebentafusp. Anchor: brenetafusp ASCO 2024 abstract 9507 (DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.9507).
  • Guideline TKIs for relapsed osteosarcoma (off the nominated axis — scope context, not ranked): regorafenib (NCCN category 1) and cabozantinib. Named in the cross-cutting caveat as the treating team's standard path; neither targets DLL3 or PRAME.

docs.title: Rank 1. DLL3 IHC (SP347) + PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing — diagnostic gate
docs.text: Resolves which antigen axes are open. Batch all three tests day one; the RNA signal opens no trial on its own.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Two RNA-only features, two protein-level gates. DLL3 IHC (SP347) at ≥1%, with ≥25% preferred for stage-1 entry, gates the tarlatamab options; NCT06788938 enforces that threshold, and every approved DLL3-directed therapy gates on protein, not transcript (PMID 35983951). PRAME IHC plus HLA-A02:01 typing together gate the entire PRAME class (NCT03686124): the PRAME peptide is presented on HLA-A02:01, so a patient without the allele cannot present the target no matter how strongly PRAME stains. PRAME IHC runs positive in roughly half of osteosarcoma; HLA-A*02:01 sits at ~40–50% population prevalence.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Not a therapy — a gate. It determines whether any downstream antigen-directed rec applies at all. The PRAME axis is more likely than not to survive the IHC given the ~56% osteosarcoma positivity, but HLA-A*02:01 is a coin-flip, and DLL3 protein status in bone is genuinely unknown because RNA says nothing about membrane localization. A negative result on either axis forecloses that half of the ranking outright.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text: • None. IHC on archival FFPE plus one blood tube for HLA typing.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was unanimous. The workup is non-toxic and gates everything, so no persona dissented or vetoed. The one preference genuinely in tension — flagged by the advocate — is the one-to-three-week delay before any antigen-directed therapy can start; the board judged it clearly worth paying, because skipping the workup forecloses the entire preferred option set.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Batch all three on day one rather than sequencing. DLL3 IHC and PRAME IHC run on the same archival block; HLA-A*02:01 needs one EDTA tube and is genetic, so a single lifetime test suffices. Confirm the SP347 clone is stocked at the treating institution — the Roche Tissue Diagnostics clone used in the tarlatamab program is not universally carried. The risktaker would run the HLA typing first-in-line to fail fast on the PRAME half if resources force a sequence.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: The board placed its whole ranking behind this step. It is a gate, not a therapy, and skipping it would put the drug before the biomarker that qualifies it.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Test / trial Efficacy context Toxicity Reference DLL3 IHC SP347 (assay) Gates enrollment in the DLL3-directed BiTE trials None — diagnostic NCT06788938 PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing (assay pair) Gates enrollment in the PRAME ImmTAC and TCR-T trials None — diagnostic NCT03686124

docs.title: Rank 2. Tarlatamab (DLL3 × CD3 BiTE) via NCT06788938
docs.text: Conditional on dll3_ihc:positive. Foreclosed if the IHC is negative.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The mechanistic case rests entirely on SCLC. DeLLphi-304 is a randomized phase 3 with a pre-specified OS primary that hit: HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.47–0.77), median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 months, RoB2 Low (PMID 40454646), pointed the same direction by the DeLLphi-301 phase-2 ORR of 40% (95% CI 29–52) (PMID 37861218). NCT06788938 is a single-arm phase-2 basket that accepts non-SCLC tumors clearing the DLL3 IHC gate. No published osteosarcoma efficacy — or even osteosarcoma DLL3-protein — data exist with this drug; the IHC gate carries the whole extrapolation.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, assuming the IHC confirms. This is the best-validated mechanism on the board, but "best-validated" describes SCLC, not bone. Whether the SCLC OS curve transfers to osteosarcoma is the open question the basket exists to answer, and DLL3 in osteosarcoma may sit intracellularly or below the membrane density a BiTE needs to kill — RNA elevation gives no read on that. A negative IHC forecloses this rec entirely.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• CRS any-grade ~56%, grade ≥3 ~1% (DeLLphi-304); inpatient cycle-1 step-up dosing required
  • ICANS-like neurologic events ~10–12%
  • Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 24%, against 53% on the chemo comparator arm
  • Step-up dosing: 1 mg D1, 10 mg D8/D15, then 10 mg q2w

The user set no toxicity vetoes, so the CRS/ICANS burden violates no stated constraint. The offsetting point is that this toxicity has a written management algorithm — step-up dosing, inpatient cycle-1 monitoring, tocilizumab — which is exactly what the conservative wanted before treating a young patient.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona dissented on the drug, but the board split on where it ranks. The critic and conservative put it first among the enrollable options precisely because it is the only RCT-grade mechanism in the set and its safety is characterized. The risktaker pushed back on that ordering — ranking tarlatamab over IMA203 rewards RCT tier while ignoring that every tarlatamab efficacy row is SCLC and IMA203's higher-ceiling number comes from a basket that names a sarcoma cohort. That is a ranking argument, not a dissent on tarlatamab, which stayed on all five lists. The mechanism-level risk is on-target CNS/neuro bystander activation and antigen-density-dependent escape if DLL3 expression is low or heterogeneous.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text:
• Trial recruiting; confirm osteosarcoma is on the NCT06788938 per-protocol enrolling list before counting on the slot.
  • Inpatient cycle-1 monitoring for CRS step-up is required — deliverable but not trivial at every center.
  • No consensus category in bone sarcoma; endorsed only under the NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 clinical-trial pathway, not as a listed regimen.
  • Off-the-shelf, no manufacturing wait — the practical contrast with the TCR-T route below.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It ties IMA203 nowhere and beats it on agreement: five personas back tarlatamab, none dissent on the drug, and its toxicity is managed. IMA203 outscores it on raw ORR but carries three dissents and a fatality, which is why the RCT-tier BiTE leads the therapeutics and the high-ceiling TCR-T follows.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Tarlatamab — NCT06788938 DLL3-IHC-selected basket (osteosarcoma admissible), n=29 planned ORR at 18 mo (primary); no osteosarcoma data yet Per class: CRS ~50%, ICANS ~10%, inpatient C1 NCT06788938 Tarlatamab — DeLLphi-301 SCLC (cross-tumor mechanism), n=220 ORR 40% (95% CI 29–52); mPFS 4.9 mo CRS ~51% (G3+ ~1%); ICANS ~10%; G3+ TRAEs 30% PMID 37861218 Tarlatamab — DeLLphi-304 SCLC (cross-tumor confirmatory), n=509 OS HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.47–0.77), p<0.001; median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 mo G3+ TRAEs 24% vs 53% chemo PMID 40454646

docs.title: Rank 3. IMA203 (PRAME TCR-T) via NCT03686124 — ACTengine pan-solid basket
docs.text: Conditional on prame_hla:positive (PRAME IHC AND HLA-A02:01 both positive). Foreclosed if either is negative.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is the pick that lands squarely on the PRAME axis with the biggest number in the dossier. The Wermke phase-1 trial reports ORR 54% (95% CI 34–73) in 28 evaluable PRAME+ HLA-A02:01+ patients across solid-tumor types, median duration of response not reached at 9 months, mPFS 5.1 months (PMID 40205198, Nat Med* 2025). NCT03686124 names a sarcoma cohort outright, so an osteosarcoma patient is admissible in principle rather than by cross-tumor argument. The honest limit: n=28, single-arm, no comparator, and the responders skewed melanoma — no osteosarcoma-specific response is reported.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: A high ceiling if both biomarkers confirm, but from an unstable base. A 95% CI of 34–73 on 28 patients is a signal, not a rate you can quote to a patient, and no osteosarcoma patient contributed to it. The sarcoma-cohort activity so far leans on synovial histology, so osteosarcoma-specific benefit stays a hypothesis. Durability could also be blunted by tumor HLA-LOH, B2M loss, or a CD8-cold microenvironment even with PRAME and HLA both positive. A negative PRAME IHC or absent HLA-A*02:01 forecloses this rec entirely.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• One treatment-related death from septic shock (1/28, 4%) — the single data point most responsible for its dissents
  • CRS ~100% (grade ≥3 ~11%), ICANS-like neurotoxicity ~25%
  • Universal grade ≥3 cytopenias after Cy/Flu lymphodepletion — a real immunosuppression window in a metastatic patient
  • Autologous manufacturing: leukapheresis, a ~4–6-week vein-to-vein window, and CAR-T-style infusion infrastructure

No toxicity veto is on file, so this profile violates no stated constraint — but it is the heaviest tail in the dossier, and a death in a 28-person series is not a footnote to rank past.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The efficacy-first personas lead it and three others dissent on ranking it high — honestly, on different grounds. The risktaker and advocate read the patient's 0.85 efficacy weight and explicit high-risk appetite as pointing here: the biggest response number on the nominated antigen with a named sarcoma cohort. The conservative and critic dissent on the safety tail — the septic death, uniform CRS, ~25% ICANS, universal post-lymphodepletion cytopenias — with the critic adding the imprecision of a wide CI on 28 patients. The concensusite dissents on guideline fit: no consensus category, trial-enrollment pathway only. The mechanism-level risk is antigen-loss / HLA-LOH escape plus the lymphodepletion immunosuppression window.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text:
• Trial recruiting; confirm the sarcoma-cohort slot directly with Immatics.
  • The treating institution needs full cell-therapy infrastructure — leukapheresis, Cy/Flu, inpatient CRS monitoring, tocilizumab, ICU step-up — and bridging-therapy planning for the manufacturing window.
  • No consensus category; guideline-consonant only under the NCCN clinical-trial recommendation.
  • The workup at rank 1 should include the CD8-TIL and HLA-LOH/B2M reads to frame durability before infusion.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Ranked below tarlatamab because the underlying evidence is single-arm phase 1/2 against a randomized OS readout, and because three personas dissented on ranking it higher — the mechanical agreement score lands at −0.2. Ranked above the ImmTAC and the registry-only options because it carries the strongest efficacy signal on the patient's own antigen and the only explicitly named sarcoma cohort; the efficacy-first case for placing it first is real and is preserved here, not buried.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference IMA203 — NCT03686124 ACTengine pan-solid PRAME+ HLA-A*02:01+ basket (sarcoma cohort named) ORR 54% (95% CI 34–73); mDoR not reached at 9 mo; mPFS 5.1 mo CRS ~100% (G3+ ~11%); ICANS ~25%; universal post-Cy/Flu cytopenia; 1 TRAE death NCT03686124, PMID 40205198

docs.title: Rank 4. Brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME × CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT04262466 / successor IMC-P115C
docs.text: Conditional on prame_hla:positive. Foreclosed if PRAME IHC or HLA-A02:01 is negative.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The evidence is cross-tumor melanoma and modest. The ASCO 2024 readout shows ORR 9–11% (4 partial responses of 36 at active doses), with the durable benefit concentrated in the PRAME-positive subset: mPFS 4.5 vs 2.1 months and 6-month OS 94% vs 40% (DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.9507). The osteosarcoma-accepting basket cohort (NCT04262466) is active-not-recruiting, and the NCI's dedicated sarcoma trial (NCT07686367) enrolls synovial and myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma, not bone. The subset OS separation is an unadjusted post-hoc split on an open-label phase-1 abstract — hypothesis-generating, not a survival claim to carry across drugs and tumor types.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low-to-moderate, and honestly stated. The 9–11% overall ORR is a genuine but thin single-agent signal; the meaningful benefit lives in a PRAME-positive responder subset that may or may not include bone. It sits below IMA203 on efficacy by a wide margin — the conservative ranks it above IMA203 anyway, trading response rate for tolerability, not efficacy.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• CRS ~85% any-grade but predominantly grade 1–2; no grade ≥3 CRS reported in the melanoma cohort
  • Rash ~70% (on-target/off-tumor ImmTAC signal), transient hypotension ~35%
  • Grade ≥3 TRAEs ~30%; managed with dexamethasone pre-medication
  • Off-the-shelf, no lymphodepletion, no marrow wipeout — the safety-for-access trade that earns it this rank

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent — the pushback here is enrollability, not mechanism. The conservative ranks it the best-tolerated agent in the PRAME class and places it above IMA203 on that basis; the risktaker and critic keep it on the list as a defensible pathway. The critic's qualifier is specific: the 6-month OS separation is an unadjusted subgroup split on an open-label phase-1 abstract, and should not be deployed as a survival claim. The on-mechanism risk is limited to on-target/off-tumor rash and antigen-density dependence, with no plausible counter-productive vector against the therapeutic goal.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text:
• The osteosarcoma-relevant slot is not open today: the basket sarcoma cohort is active-not-recruiting and the NCI trial excludes bone.
  • Enrollability hinges on the cohort re-opening or the IMC-P115C successor (rank 5) accepting osteosarcoma.
  • Weekly IV infusion, outpatient after step-up — a lower-burden route onto the PRAME axis than TCR-T.
  • No consensus category; trial-enrollment pathway only.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It draws no dissent, which lifts it above IMA203 on agreement score despite far weaker numbers. It sits below tarlatamab because the ImmTAC efficacy is thin and cross-tumor while tarlatamab carries RCT-grade mechanism evidence. And it edges out the tarlatamab+RT combination at the same score because it has real phase-1 efficacy data where the combination has none.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Brenetafusp — NCT04262466 melanoma cohort (cross-tumor; sarcoma slot active-not-recruiting) ORR 9–11%; PRAME+ subset mPFS 4.5 vs 2.1 mo; 6-mo OS 94% vs 40% CRS predominantly G1-2, no G3+ CRS; rash ~70%; G3+ TRAE ~30% NCT04262466, DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.9507 Brenetafusp — NCT07686367 NCI sarcoma phase 2 (synovial + myxoid/round-cell lipo; osteosarcoma not on list) ORR endpoint; not-yet-recruiting, no data Per ImmTAC class NCT07686367

docs.title: Rank 5. IMC-P115C (next-gen PRAME × CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT07156136
docs.text: Conditional on prame_hla:positive AND sponsor confirms osteosarcoma is on the per-protocol list. Foreclosed if PRAME IHC or HLA-A02:01 is negative.*

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is no IMC-P115C efficacy readout — it is a recruiting first-in-human dose-escalation (NCT07156136). The rank buys the ImmTAC class and the PRAME target off brenetafusp's data, since IMC-P115C is Immunocore's next-generation successor engineered from it (DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.9507). The eligibility is written pan-tumor for PRAME-positive HLA-A*02:01-positive disease, so non-melanoma histologies are admissible in principle once the sponsor confirms sarcoma is on the list.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown for the molecule itself. The class read suggests the ImmTAC platform produces durable but lower-frequency responses than TCR-T. What earns it a rank over the registry-only options is that it is actually recruiting where brenetafusp's sarcoma slot is closed — for a patient who wants the gentler PRAME route and an open door today, this is the one to call about. A negative PRAME IHC or absent HLA-A*02:01 forecloses it.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No drug-specific data yet; class expectation is the brenetafusp profile — CRS predominantly grade 1–2, rash, transient hypotension
  • Dexamethasone pre-medication manages CRS in the ImmTAC class
  • Weekly IV infusion, outpatient cycle-1 monitoring after step-up

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent. The risktaker and advocate rank it as the open-door version of brenetafusp. The critic's qualifier lands here too: the borrowed brenetafusp OS figures are an unadjusted phase-1 melanoma subset and should not be deployed as an IMC-P115C survival expectation. Same on-target/off-tumor and antigen-density dependence as the ImmTAC class; no drug-specific counter-productive signal exists yet.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text:
• Trial recruiting. First action: contact Immunocore medical affairs to confirm sarcoma is on the per-protocol list and what the PRAME IHC threshold is.
  • Concurrent enrollment with IMA203 is unlikely to be permitted; if both biomarkers confirm, the choice is ImmTAC weekly outpatient infusion versus TCR-T autologous manufacturing.
  • No consensus category; investigational.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below brenetafusp because it is a pure platform-and-target bet with no data of its own, and above the registry-only options because it is genuinely recruiting today. It is the ImmTAC a patient could enter now if brenetafusp's slot stays shut.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text:
Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference IMC-P115C — NCT07156136 pan-tumor PRAME+ HLA-A*02:01+ (sarcoma fit pending sponsor confirmation) DLT, MTD primary; no efficacy data yet ImmTAC class: CRS predominantly G1-2; rash; transient hypotension NCT07156136

Ranks 6 (tarlatamab + radiation, dll3_ihc:positive) and 7 (NW-101C PRAME TCR-T, prame_hla:positive) are carried in recommendations.jsonl and the ranked-prioritization table below with status: considered_with_caveats. Both are tier-5 registry-only — the critic and conservative declined to rank the tarlatamab+RT combination and the critic dissented on NW-101C — so their narratives are deliberately thin: tarlatamab+RT layers an untested abscopal RT arm on the rank-2 backbone with zero combination data, and NW-101C is a second PRAME TCR-T fallback with no clinical data under its own name, borrowing its entire efficacy expectation from IMA203. Neither carries enough substantiation for a deep narrative; both are named as verify-first fallback slots.

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• Tarlatamab + radiation (NCT06814496) and NW-101C (NCT07266298): both feature-targeting but tier-5 registry-only, carried at ranks 6–7 with caveats rather than given deep narratives. Tarlatamab+RT has no published combination AE profile — the conservative and critic decline to rank an uncharacterized RT-on-BiTE combination — and NW-101C has no clinical data under its name, so its efficacy is borrowed from IMA203.
  • Other DLL3- and PRAME-targeting pipeline agents (SCLC/NEC- or melanoma-only enrollment): the DLL3 BiTE/ADC/radioligand/CAR-T constructs (ZL-1310, ²²⁵Ac agents, LB2102, DLL3-CAR-NK and similar) and the PRAME TCER/mRNA-combination rows carry no osteosarcoma-axis data that beats the basket-eligible picks and, in most cases, no osteosarcoma eligibility. They remain in the dossier as evidence-base context for the mechanism classes; none is enrollable for a bone-sarcoma patient absent a basket that explicitly accepts the histology.

Reading the columns

Toxicity burden is patient-level G3+ AE severity (Low / Moderate / High) summarized from the trial publications. Counter-productive MoA is the mechanism-level risk that the intervention's own pathway could blunt the therapeutic goal — distinct from patient AEs. The board's endorse / dissent / veto state appears as pills under each intervention; full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence base. The therapeutic ranks rest on thin, mostly cross-tumor data. Tarlatamab's OS signal is a randomized phase 3 but entirely in SCLC. IMA203's 54% ORR is single-arm, n=28, one treatment-related death, with responders skewed to melanoma. Brenetafusp's PRAME-positive subset separation is an unadjusted split on an open-label phase-1 ASCO abstract. IMC-P115C, tarlatamab+RT, and NW-101C have no efficacy readouts of their own. None of these has published osteosarcoma-specific response data.
  • Biomarker dependencies. The whole ranking assumes protein-level confirmation. Tarlatamab and tarlatamab+RT (ranks 2, 6) assume DLL3 IHC ≥1% (≥25% for stage-1 entry); without it they are foreclosed. IMA203, brenetafusp, IMC-P115C, and NW-101C (ranks 3, 4, 5, 7) assume both PRAME IHC positivity and HLA-A*02:01 typing; either negative forecloses the entire PRAME class. The two axes are independent — a negative DLL3 IHC does not foreclose the PRAME ranks, and vice versa.
  • What would change the ranking.
    • An independent replication of PRAME TCR-T or DLL3 BiTE activity in a bone-sarcoma cohort — as opposed to the current cross-tumor extrapolation — would tighten the confidence on rank 2 or rank 3.
    • A negative DLL3 IHC moves ranks 2 and 6 to non-applicable; a negative PRAME IHC or absent HLA-A*02:01 moves ranks 3, 4, 5, and 7 to non-applicable.
    • If the user declared a toxicity veto on CRS, ICANS, or lymphodepletion — none is on file — IMA203 and NW-101C would drop sharply, since the septic-death and cytopenia burden is their load-bearing dissent.
  • Re-scoping. If the user's stated preference shifts away from high-risk/high-reward toward tolerability, or the clinical state changes, the guideline TKIs regorafenib and cabozantinib — named as scope context, not ranked here — become the more relevant conversation with the treating team.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text: Re-run 2026-07-09 for a full board re-deliberation after the trial screen added the DLL3 + PRAME/HLA-A02:01 pipeline. Inputs: profile (two RNA-only features, DLL3 and PRAME), preferences (efficacy weight 0.85, accepts high-risk/high-reward, prefers trials, no toxicity veto), 5 board positions, 31 critiques, and the refreshed dossier. Synthesis: one shared workup gate plus six antigen-directed therapeutics, no vetoes issued. Ranking follows agreement score, with the efficacy-toxicity tiebreak keeping IMA203 above the tier-5 registry-only options despite its −0.2 score, since all five personas listed it and two led it. Scope: regorafenib and cabozantinib (concensusite ranks 1–2) are off the nominated DLL3/PRAME axis and are named as scope context, not ranked — the board flagged this tension explicitly. Reference check corrected the IMA203 citation from the dossier's PMID 38821093 (which resolves to an unrelated Lancet Oncol letter) to the verified Wermke Nat Med* 2025 primary publication, PMID 40205198; the dossier's PMID 28315425 for the Iura PRAME-osteosarcoma prevalence figure resolves to an unrelated hepatocellular paper and no single PubMed record cleanly supports the "56%, n=82" claim, so that figure is carried as free text without a promoted identifier and the case should be re-screened to repair the source row. Humanizer pass applied over all prose sections.

docs.title: 1. tarlatamab (Imdelltra) tarlatamab, AMG 757, Imdelltra
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: BiTE   Verified: 2026-05-06

Two real access paths: (1) off-label prescription — Imdelltra is FDA-approved for SCLC and can be prescribed off-label for DLL3+ osteosarcoma by a clinician willing to navigate payer review; (2) clinical trial — NCT06788938 (UCLA basket) accepts DLL3-IHC-positive non-SCLC tumors and is the on-protocol pathway. The trial path is preferred when accessible because it carries trial-billing infrastructure and protocolized monitoring; off-label is the fallback if the trial is foreclosed.

RegulatoryFDA accelerated approval (2024) for ES-SCLC after platinum-based chemotherapy. EMA conditional approval (2025). NOT approved for osteosarcoma — but the SCLC approval makes off-label prescription a real access path in addition to trial enrollment. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for relapsed ES-SCLC; off-guideline for osteosarcoma — basket-trial enrollment is the on-protocol route. Geographic scopeUS — UCLA-led trial with potential satellite arrangements. Off-label prescription is available wherever Imdelltra is commercially distributed (US, EU).

Next steps

  1. Confirm DLL3 IHC SP347 result first — required for both paths (the trial mandates ≥1% / preferably ≥25%; off-label use should not proceed without protein confirmation).
  2. Trial path: Email NCT06788938 central contact (istteam@mednet.ucla.edu) or call 888-798-0719 to request a screening slot. If outside a UCLA-affiliated geography, ask about satellite or referral arrangements.
  3. Off-label path: If the trial is foreclosed (slot unavailable, geography mismatch, screening exclusion), discuss off-label Imdelltra with the treating oncologist and institutional pharmacy. Pre-authorization with the payer is the load-bearing step; a biomarker-justified appeal letter is typically required.
  4. Contact Amgen medical information (1-800-772-6436) for technical product information and compassionate-use guidance if both trial and off-label paths are blocked.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT067889382DLL3-expressing advanced solid tumors (osteosarcoma included)recruitingeligible: likelyCRU Hotlineistteam@mednet.ucla.edu888-798-0719trial sitesEligibility gates on DLL3 IHC ≥1% (preferably ≥25%). Confirm IHC SP347 result first; the protocol's DLL3 criterion is the load-bearing screening step.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAmgen CountryUS Medical info phone1-800-772-6436 Product informationhttps://www.amgenmedinfo.com/ Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.amgen.com/about/compassionate-use NotesImdelltra is commercially available for SCLC and can be obtained through standard specialty-distribution channels for off-label use, subject to institutional pharmacy and payer review.

Payer / coverage notes. Medicare bills the SCLC indication under standard biologic codes; off-label use for a non-SCLC tumor type is generally not reimbursed without prior authorization, an appeal citing biomarker rationale, or a clinical-trial billing path. Manufacturer patient-assistance through Amgen Assist (www.amgenassist360.com) may help with co-pay support.

Notes. Imdelltra label specifies SCLC after platinum failure; osteosarcoma is off-label. Trial enrollment is the on-protocol route; off-label prescription is a real fallback. The cycle-1 inpatient step-up dosing for CRS mitigation is the same regardless of which access path is used.

docs.title: 2. IMA203 (PRAME-TCR-T) IMA203, ACTengine PRAME
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: CAR-T   Verified: 2026-05-06

Best-evidenced PRAME pathway with explicit pan-solid sarcoma-inclusive basket eligibility. Conditional on PRAME IHC AND HLA-A*02:01 positivity. Trial enrollment via ACTengine NCT03686124 is the realistic path; direct sponsor outreach to Immatics is the first action.

RegulatoryInvestigational. No FDA/EMA approval. Phase 3 in cutaneous melanoma (NCT06743126); pan-solid phase 1/2 basket (NCT03686124) is the path for non-melanoma tumors. GuidelinesOff-guideline. Pan-solid basket eligibility is published and protocolized. Geographic scopeUS, EU. Confirm specific site availability with Immatics medical affairs.

Next steps

  1. Confirm PRAME IHC result AND HLA-A*02:01 typing first — both required for eligibility.
  2. Email Immatics ctgovinquiries@immatics.com or call +1 346 204-5400 to confirm sarcoma-cohort slot availability and screening procedure.
  3. Confirm the treating institution has CAR-T / TCR-T infrastructure (Cy/Flu lymphodepletion + CRS monitoring + ICU step-up).
  4. Plan for 4-6-week manufacturing turnaround between leukapheresis and infusion.

Trial pathways

Sarcoma cohorts on protocol. Patient must be PRAME IHC-positive AND HLA-A*02:01-positive. Lymphodepleting Cy/Flu chemotherapy precedes T-cell infusion; CRS / neurotoxicity monitoring infrastructure required. Listed as pivotal-evidence reference.

CountryUS (Houston) / Germany (parent: Immatics Biotechnologies) Medical info phone+1 346 204-5400 Medical info emailctgovinquiries@immatics.com Product informationhttps://www.immatics.com/ Compassionate use emailctgovinquiries@immatics.com NotesMid-cap biotech with active sarcoma-cohort engagement on the ACTengine basket. Direct email to ctgovinquiries@immatics.com is the realistic outreach channel for screening questions and sponsor-level discussion.

Payer / coverage notes. Investigational autologous TCR-T; no payer coverage outside trial enrollment. Trial-billing infrastructure handles drug + manufacturing; the treating institution typically bills supportive-care and lymphodepletion components.

Notes. Lymphodepleting Cy/Flu chemo + autologous TCR-T infusion. Wermke 2024 reported 54% ORR (pan-solid PRAME+ HLA-A*02:01+ basket) — best signal in PRAME class to date.
