docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference INCB161734 monotherapy, pretreated G12D PDAC ORR 37%, DCR 78% (n=41; PFS not reached at ~5 mo) GI 50-60% grade 1-2; rash/stomatitis absent DOI 10.1200/JCO.2026.44.2_suppl.654 INCB161734 + chemo vs placebo + chemo, front-line (DAWN-303) OS readout pending; requires KRAS G12D Combination-cohort G3+ neutropenia ~40% NCT07522073 INCB161734 phase 1 parent (mono + combinations) Safety / ORR / DCR Cohort-defined NCT06179160

docs.title: Rank 5. HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel — front-line via NCT07232875
docs.text: The highest front-line ORR on the exact allele, held at considered_with_caveats. Two personas kept it; three dissented on a 90.3% grade >=3 rate with a treatment-related death. No veto.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The front-line combination read is a phase 1b/2 single-arm study, HRS-4642 added to gem/nab-paclitaxel, reported in Nature Medicine (DOI 10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9): confirmed ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive KRAS G12D PDAC patients, the primary endpoint met. That is the highest front-line response on the patient's exact allele and line anywhere in the dossier. The problem the critic cannot get past is attribution: the 63.3% is measured on top of a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone that delivers roughly 20-23% ORR on its own, and the same program's HRS-4642 monotherapy read was only 20.8% (DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484, ESMO 2025 915O), so without a control arm the drug's independent contribution is not isolable. The enrollable option, the confirmatory phase 3 NCT07232875, is not yet recruiting. One evidence-integrity note carried honestly: the Nature Medicine paper has no PubMed record yet, so it is cited by DOI and the enrollable slot is anchored on the NCT.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: High as an observed front-line number in the exact setting, but confounded. A treatment-naive patient is in the population the 63.3% was measured in, which is the risktaker's point — the confound cuts the effect, it does not erase a doubling over historical gem/nab-paclitaxel. The critic's point stands alongside it: 20.8% is the honest ceiling on HRS-4642's own contribution, and the rest is chemotherapy the patient would receive anyway. What the drug adds, net of the backbone, is the open question a randomized trial has not yet answered.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 90.3%, mostly hematologic, driven by the gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone
  • One treatment-related death (1/84) in the monotherapy safety set — the datum the conservative and critic weight most at 79
  • HRS-4642 monotherapy adds a metabolic signature: hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, neutropenia
  • IV route, not oral; no dose-limiting toxicities in phase 1b, but the combination toxicity tracks the chemotherapy rather than a novel drug signal
  • The user logged no toxicity veto, so nothing here is formally disqualifying — but the 90.3% grade >=3 rate is exactly the profile the free_text's age-79 note argues against

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: This is the case's one persistent down-rank. The risktaker and critic kept it on their lists (ranks 2 and 4) for the exact-line response; the conservative, concensusite, and advocate dissented on putting it high. The conservative's dissent is the load-bearing one: a 90.3% grade >=3 rate with a treatment-related death is a tolerability floor they will not top-rank in a 79-year-old the free_text flags as likely more toxicity-averse than the neutral 0.5 weight encodes, and the monotherapy metabolic signature has no combination-specific management algorithm published. The advocate reached the same place on preference-fit (IV doublet, phase 3 not recruiting, so prefers_trials only half-served), and the concensusite on guideline-fit (China-based, front-line slot pairs with a full chemo backbone). The critic's own dissent is on evidence: the confounded ORR does not settle the question. No formal veto was issued — every objection is a dissent, not a safety contraindication.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCT07232875 requires KRAS G12D and enrolls first-line advanced/metastatic PDAC, matching the patient on allele, tumor type, and line — but it is not yet recruiting, so the door is not currently open. HRS-4642 is IV every 2-3 weeks on a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone. The program is China-based (Jiangsu Hengrui); NCCN just says profile-and-enroll and does not rank sponsors by geography, so the geographic caveat is about population generalizability and current enrollability, not disqualified evidence. No NCCN category. If a growth-factor and metabolic-monitoring plan were in place and the phase 3 opened, this becomes a live conversation for a patient who prioritized response ceiling over tolerability — which is not where this 79-year-old's unstated preference points.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 5 and considered_with_caveats because it carries the single highest front-line ORR on the board yet lands at a negative agreement score (-0.2): two endorse, three dissent. It sits below the four cleaner KRAS-directed options because the 90.3% grade >=3 rate, the treatment-related death, the IV backbone, and the not-yet-recruiting phase 3 stack against a toxicity-averse 79-year-old, and above the pre-data pan-KRAS class at rank 6 because it has an actual front-line efficacy read, confounded or not.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel, 1L G12D PDAC (phase 1b/2) ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1, n=30); primary endpoint met G3+ TRAE 90.3%, mostly hematologic DOI 10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9 HRS-4642 monotherapy, 2L+ G12D solid tumors PDAC ORR 20.8%, DCR 79.2%; mPFS 4.4 mo G3+ TRAE 23.8%; 1 treatment-related death (1/84) DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484 HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel vs placebo + chemo, 1L (phase 3) Readout pending; not yet recruiting Backbone hematologic toxicity NCT07232875

docs.title: Rank 6. Pan-KRAS(ON) first-in-human inhibitors (BBO-11818, BLU-924, PF-07934040, LY3962673) — phase 1 baskets covering G12D
docs.text: On-axis but pre-data. No persona ranked them; surfaced at considered_with_caveats / low because they target the driver and have recruiting slots. No dissent, no veto.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Four pan-KRAS or G12D-selective agents sit at tier 5 with no efficacy denominator: BBO-11818 (KONQUER-101, NCT06917079), BLU-924 (Blueprint/Sanofi, NCT07629960), PF-07934040 (Pfizer, NCT06447662), and LY3962673 (MOONRAY-01, Lilly, NCT06586515). The only public efficacy signal across the four is a December 2025 sponsor update citing one BBO-11818 PDAC partial response (56% tumor shrinkage) with no denominator and no ORR; the rest are registry-stage. There is no per-term grade >=3 safety table for any of them.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unquantified. These cover G12D through pan-KRAS baskets, so the target rationale is sound, but a mechanism without an efficacy denominator cannot support a likelihood estimate. The honest read the conservative and critic gave in round 1 is that ranking these would be ranking novelty, not evidence — so they are banked, not recommended, until an abstract-level readout arrives (BBO-11818 expected in the second half of 2026).

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No per-term grade >=3 safety table published for any of the four (empty toxicities across the dossier rows)
  • Early monotherapy escalation reads describe predominantly grade 1-2 GI toxicity with no dose-limiting toxicities
  • The safety base does not yet exist, so the tier reflects absence of data, not a benign profile

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona ranked these, so there was no target row for a round-2 critique to attach to — the conservative logged the missing-AE-data flag for the record. That silence is not endorsement and not dissent; it is the board declining to score a pre-data mechanism. No plausible counter-productive vector is established because there is no clinical read to establish one from.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: All four have recruiting phase 1 slots, but most enroll after standard therapy, so line-fit for a treatment-naive patient depends on the specific cohort — BBO-11818's combination arms with gem/nab-paclitaxel, mFOLFIRINOX, cetuximab, and pembrolizumab open front-line-compatible options that the monotherapy escalations do not. Oral. A tissue or ctDNA G12D call is the enrollment token. No NCCN category; investigational and pre-data.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 6 and considered_with_caveats because they genuinely target the driver and recruit, but no efficacy denominator exists, so they cannot be ranked among the agents that have one. Below HRS-4642 (rank 5), which at least has a front-line efficacy read; above ceralasertib (rank 7) only in that these hit the lead KRAS driver directly rather than the secondary ARID1A axis — but on a present-day recommendation basis both are bank-for-later.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference BBO-11818 (KONQUER-101), pan-KRAS(ON) 1 PDAC PR (56% shrinkage), no denominator No per-term table; GI-predominant, no DLTs NCT06917079 BLU-924 (SAR449336), pan-KRAS No readout No data NCT07629960 PF-07934040, KRAS G12D No readout No data NCT06447662 LY3962673 (MOONRAY-01), KRAS G12D-selective No readout No data NCT06586515

docs.title: Rank 7. ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor (ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis) — via NCT03682289, gated on BAF250a IHC loss
docs.text: A mechanistically independent banked second axis off the ARID1A frameshift. Every persona ranked it last; it is the thinnest in-indication evidence on the board for this patient.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The clinical read is a phase 2 Simon two-stage monotherapy study (NCT03682289, n=29) requiring ARID1A loss by IHC (PMID 41686845): confirmed ORR 14% (4/29) across all ARID1A-deficient tumors. The 31% figure people quote is a gynecologic-histology subset (endometrioid endometrial, ovarian clear cell), with no pancreatic responder shown. Reading that subset across to basal-like PDAC is cross-tumor extrapolation, and the preclinical ATR-ARID1A work (PMID 27958275) was done in colorectal and ovarian models with no PDAC line tested. The synthetic-lethal logic is sound — ARID1A loss strands topoisomerase 2A and ATR inhibition forces premature mitotic entry onto the unresolved tangles — but it has not engaged a pancreatic tumor in the clinic.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low for this patient. No pancreatic responder exists in the ARID1A clinical data, and the activity concentrates in gynecologic histologies, so the PDAC rationale is inference rather than evidence. The personas keep it on the list as a banked, mechanistically independent shot if the KRAS routes fail, not because the current PDAC signal is strong. It is genuinely a second axis, which is why a treatment-naive man deserves to have it documented; it is not a present recommendation.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• ATR-class cytopenias — anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia — are the class signature; class anemia is the dose-limiting effect (grade 3 anemia ~26-36% in related agents camonsertib and tuvusertib)
  • Per-term grade >=3 rates were not broken out in the abstract; the only number in the toxicity table is zero treatment-related deaths
  • The unquantified ATR-class anemia burden is the specific safety gap in a 79-year-old

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No persona issued a round-2 dissent or veto on this row, but that silence is not endorsement — the board spent its critiques on the top-tier disagreement among the KRAS agents. Three personas (conservative, critic, concensusite) ranked it, each at their own floor; the risktaker and advocate left it off their picks entirely once the KRAS field ran this deep. The concensusite's round-2 note (directed at the conservative) names the load-bearing problem as guideline fit: no society endorses ATR inhibition for PDAC, and the only positive read is a gynecologic subset with zero pancreatic responders. The mechanism-level risk is that cross-tumor extrapolation may simply not translate to basal-like PDAC, and class anemia limits exposure at 79.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: NCT03682289 takes pancreatic tumors stratified by ARID1A status, so it directly targets the secondary axis, but it is active-not-recruiting, so the open door a trials-leaning patient wants is not currently available. Entry is gated on BAF250a IHC loss, and only ~67% of ARID1A-mutant tumors lose the protein, so the ctDNA/tissue frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility — order the BAF250a IHC before treating this as concrete. The EZH2 arm of this axis lost its lead agent when tazemetostat was withdrawn in March 2026 on an unfavorable benefit-risk read, leaving ATR as the live route. Oral, intermittent schedule.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 7, the floor, by unanimous round-1 consensus — every persona placed it below all the KRAS agents. The synthesis formula scores it 0.6 (it drew no round-2 down-rank critiques because the personas argued about the KRAS-agent ordering instead), but that score is an artifact, not a signal that ceralasertib outranks HRS-4642 or the pre-data pan-KRAS class; it is placed last to match the board's actual placement. It is last on in-indication evidence grade: cross-tumor extrapolation with no PDAC responder, not-confirmed enrollable, and the lead basket's door is closed. It stays on the page because the ARID1A frameshift is a real, independent target worth banking if the KRAS axis fails.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference ceralasertib monotherapy, ARID1A-deficient (phase 2) ORR 14% (4/29) overall; 31% gynecologic subset; no PDAC responder ATR-class cytopenias (per-term G3+ unreported); 0 treatment-related deaths PMID 41686845 ceralasertib ± olaparib or durvalumab, ARID1A-stratified basket ORR / disease control; takes PDAC Oral, intermittent NCT03682289

docs.title: Classes examined but not ranked
docs.text:
• HLA-agnostic KRAS peptide vaccines (ELI-002; Hopkins pooled vaccine + nivolumab/ipilimumab). These clear the HLA gate the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T fails, and ELI-002's safety is the cleanest in the case (no grade >=3 events across 25 patients, PMID 40790272). But the data come from resected, minimal-residual-disease PDAC, and this man has a large primary and liver metastases, so the efficacy read does not transfer to bulky metastatic disease. The ELI-002 hazard ratios (RFS HR 0.12, OS HR 0.23) split patients by on-treatment T-cell response, not randomization, so they anchor the vaccine mechanism rather than a metastatic benefit estimate. Excluded on setting, not on biology.
  • HLA-C08:02-restricted anti-KRAS-G12D TCR-T (NT-112, NCT06218914) and the C08:02/A*11:01-restricted mRNA KRAS vaccine. Excluded on HLA mismatch: the patient is C05:01/C06:02 and A01:01/A02:01, so these products cannot present his mutant epitope (PMID 35648703). This is the concrete negative behind the case's second judgment call.
  • EZH2 inhibition for the ARID1A axis (tazemetostat). On-axis mechanism, but the lead agent was withdrawn from all trials in March 2026 after the negative NRG-GY014 read, so the EZH2 route lost both its supporting efficacy signal and its drug. ATR inhibition (ceralasertib, rank 7) is the surviving route.
  • MRTX1133, first-generation KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor. Validated the target and the FAS/CD8 immune mechanism preclinically (PMID 36216931, PMID 37625401), but the clinical program was terminated for formulation problems, not loss of target validity. Carried forward as mechanism history by zoldonrasib and INCB161734.
  • Single-agent checkpoint blockade (pembrolizumab on the dMMR/MSI-H or TMB-high label). Foreclosed: MSS, TMB 8.6 (below the >=10 threshold), and a somatic MLH1 variant that most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology. MMR IHC is the gate before any dMMR/MSI-H claim. Not recommended on that label here.

docs.title: Ranked prioritization
docs.text:
RankInterventionLikelihood of effectToxicity burdenCounter-productive MoAOverall 1 daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) pan-RAS(ON) front-line on NCT07491445endorse: risktaker conservative critic concensusite advocate High in 2L RAS G12 PDAC — OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53), RASolute 302 (n=500); first-line benefit inferred from the unread RASolute 303. Moderate (rash G3+ 14%, stomatitis G3+ 12%; G3+ TRAE 43.6% overall, below chemo) Low (Mucocutaneous toxicity can force dose reductions that erode the exposure the survival signal depends on; no mechanism-level antagonism) The only feature-targeting option with randomized phase 3 survival evidence; first-line benefit inferred from an unread trial and the allele estimate borrowed from a RAS G12 subgroup. 2 GFH375 / VS-7375 G12D-selective + cetuximab, 1L cohort on NCT07644559endorse: risktaker conservative critic concensusite advocate High allele-matched response — ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52), ESMO 2025 LBA84 (n=59), but single-country phase 1/2 and one line beyond the treatment-naive patient. Moderate (neutropenia G3+ 8%, anemia G3+ 8%, diarrhea G3+ 3%; cetuximab rash/hypomagnesemia uncharacterized in combination) Low (Cytopenias and cetuximab dermatologic toxicity can force dose reductions; no mechanism-level antagonism of the therapeutic goal) The highest allele-matched single-agent response on the board with an open 1L slot, but the read is China-based, one line early, and the cetuximab doublet's tolerability at 79 is uncharacterized. 3 zoldonrasib (RMC-9805) G12D-selective front-line on NCT07621718endorse: risktaker conservative critic concensusite advocatedissent: critic concensusite Moderate, allele-matched — ORR 30% / DCR 80% in G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=40, no CI; PFS/DoR immature). RASolute 305 will test it front-line. Low (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, rash 10%; no G4/5 events at monotherapy dose) Moderate (Critic and concensusite dissented on the thin single-arm base; durability unmeasured, so on-target activity may not translate to a durable effect) The allele-matched, gentlest agent in the set — best tolerability for a 79-year-old, but the evidence is a single-arm n=40 abstract with no durability readout. 4 INCB161734 G12D-selective + chemo front-line on NCT07522073 (DAWN-303)endorse: risktaker conservative concensusite advocatedissent: conservative Moderate to high single-agent — ORR 37% / DCR 78% in pretreated G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=41, no CI; PFS not reached at ~5 mo). DAWN-303 tests it front-line. High (combination-cohort G3+ neutropenia ~40%; monotherapy GI 50-60% grade 1-2) Moderate (Conservative dissented on additive marrow toxicity: chemo-combination neutropenia can force dose reductions that erode delivered intensity at 79) Strongest single-agent response number in the dossier, but the enrollable front-line construct bundles chemotherapy with ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia and no dedicated combination-safety data. 5 HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel front-line on NCT07232875endorse: risktaker criticdissent: conservative concensusite advocate High front-line response but confounded — ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1, n=30) on a chemo backbone; monotherapy contribution only ~20.8%. High (grade >=3 TRAE 90.3%, mostly hematologic; one treatment-related death; hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia signature) Moderate (Backbone myelosuppression plus one treatment-related death can force intensity cuts that erode delivered benefit in an older marrow-limited patient) The highest front-line ORR on the exact allele, but a 90.3% grade >=3 rate with a treatment-related death, an IV backbone, and a not-yet-recruiting phase 3 down-rank it against a toxicity-averse 79-year-old. 6 Pan-KRAS(ON) FIH inhibitors (BBO-11818, BLU-924, PF-07934040, LY3962673) (phase 1 baskets covering G12D)no persona ranked (pre-data) Low / unquantified — no efficacy denominator; the only public signal is a single BBO-11818 PDAC partial response with no ORR (registry-stage class). Low (none characterized — early reads describe predominantly grade 1-2 GI, no per-term G3+ table published) Low (Pre-data mechanism with no plausible counter-productive vector established; the risk is absence of evidence, not a mechanistic antagonism) On-axis pan-KRAS agents covering G12D with recruiting phase 1 slots, but no efficacy denominator exists yet, so they are a bank-for-later class rather than a present recommendation. 7 ceralasertib (AZD6738) ATR inhibitor on NCT03682289 (ARID1A axis; gated on BAF250a IHC loss)endorse: conservative critic concensusite Low for PDAC — confirmed ORR 14% across ARID1A-deficient tumors (PMID 41686845), activity concentrated in gynecologic histologies with zero pancreatic responders shown. Moderate (ATR-class anemia / thrombocytopenia / neutropenia; per-term G3+ rates unreported, zero treatment-related deaths) Moderate (Cross-tumor extrapolation with no PDAC responder; the synthetic-lethal effect may not engage in basal-like PDAC, and class anemia limits exposure at 79) A mechanistically independent banked second axis off the ARID1A frameshift, but no PDAC responder exists, entry is BAF250a-IHC-gated, and the lead basket is not recruiting.

Reading the columns

Toxicity burden is patient-level G3+ AE severity (Low / Moderate / High) summarized from the trial publications. Counter-productive MoA is the mechanism-level risk that the intervention's own pathway could blunt the therapeutic goal — distinct from patient AEs. The board's endorse / dissent / veto state appears as pills under each intervention; full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. Only one ranked option carries randomized evidence: daraxonrasib's RASolute 302 (PMID 42223072, n=500, RoB2:Some, open-label, 2L). Everything below it rests on thinner ground — GFH375/VS-7375, zoldonrasib, and INCB161734 are uncontrolled n=40 to n=66 phase 1/2 conference abstracts, several China-based, with wide or absent CIs on ORR and immature PFS/DoR; HRS-4642's front-line combination read is a single-arm phase 1b/2 whose 63.3% ORR is confounded with the chemo backbone and whose Nature Medicine paper has no PubMed record yet (cited by DOI); the pan-KRAS FIH agents have no efficacy denominator at all; and ceralasertib's only positive read is a gynecologic subgroup with zero pancreatic responders. The RoB judgments on the abstract-stage agents are provisional until full-text publication.
  • Compartment / biomarker dependencies. Rank 7 (ceralasertib) is contingent on BAF250a IHC loss — the frameshift call alone does not confirm it, and only ~67% of ARID1A-mutant tumors lose the protein. Every KRAS-directed rank assumes tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA KRAS G12D call, which the RAS(ON) trials require at screening. The immunotherapy axis is foreclosed pending MMR IHC: MSS plus TMB 8.6 plus a somatic MLH1 variant most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology, and the dMMR/MSI-H pembrolizumab label is not established until IHC shows protein loss.
  • What would change the ranking.
    • The RASolute 303 first-line OS readout landing would convert rank 1's inferred first-line benefit into measured benefit and tighten its confidence over the single-arm allele-selective agents.
    • A captured toxicity-averse preference for this 79-year-old would reorder the top: the risktaker and advocate already read a G12D-selective agent (GFH375 or the gentler zoldonrasib) as the patient-facing lead, and it would push HRS-4642 and the INCB161734 chemo combination further down.
    • A BAF250a IHC showing retained protein would foreclose rank 7 (ceralasertib) entirely, since entry requires protein loss.
    • The GFH375 1L cohort or the RASolute 303/305 and DAWN-303 front-line readouts arriving would move the allele-selective agents up relative to the 2L-anchored daraxonrasib evidence.
    • An MMR IHC showing protein loss would re-open the dMMR/MSI-H immunotherapy axis that is currently foreclosed — a change to the option set, not just the order.
  • Re-scoping caveat. If performance status proves worse than the assumed ECOG 1, the chemo-combination options (INCB161734 on DAWN-303 and HRS-4642 on gem/nab-paclitaxel, both with heavy grade >=3 hematologic toxicity) drop on additive-toxicity grounds, and the willingness to surface aggressive trial-only options narrows; re-run intake if PS, goals-of-care, or a preferred efficacy/toxicity balance become available.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text: Re-run July 2026 after a full board re-deliberation over 9 new on-axis KRAS trials. Inputs: 16 trials, 13 clinical-evidence rows, 8 preclinical rows, 6 target-validation rows, 5 fresh board positions with 31 cross-critiques. Every biomarker reads as confirmed on the Tempus plasma/germline/RNA profiling, so this is a non-gated case with scenario: null on all seven recommendation rows and a single unbranched ranking scoped to KRAS-G12D-directed and ARID1A-directed interventions. The re-run added GFH375/VS-7375 (rank 2) and HRS-4642 (rank 5) as on-axis options and grouped the four pre-data pan-KRAS FIH agents as a single considered_with_caveats class (rank 6). No workup-hardening row appears in the ranking; the MMR IHC, tissue NGS, BAF250a IHC, HLA typing, and ASXL1 CHIP adjudication are surfaced under Workup considerations and on the Target Validation paths report instead. Three clinical judgment calls are honored throughout: the somatic MLH1 variant most likely reflects MMR-proficient biology (checkpoint monotherapy low-yield, MMR IHC the gate); the patient is HLA-C05:01/C06:02, not C08:02, so the published anti-KRAS-G12D TCR-T and the A11:01-restricted programs do not apply; and the ASXL1 plasma frameshift may be CHIP. Reference-checked: the load-bearing PMIDs and DOIs resolved and matched their claims, the HRS-4642 Nature Medicine paper confirms it has no PubMed record (cited by DOI, enrollable option anchored on NCT07232875), and one workup-supporting citation (PMID 32152268) was dropped because it resolves to an unrelated hepatocellular-carcinoma paper — its descriptive detail was moved into free text. ECOG 1, US geography, treatment-naive status, and the neutral 0.5 efficacy/toxicity weight are all assumed and flagged; re-run intake if performance status or goals-of-care become available. Humanizer pass applied to all prose sections per .claude/skills/humanizer/SKILL.md.

docs.title: 1. daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib, RMC-6236
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Expanded access program Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

The realistic path right now is a front-line trial: RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) takes treatment-naive metastatic PDAC and accepts the KRAS G12D under its RAS-mutant arm, with RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) as a backup that adds combination cohorts. There's also an FDA-authorized expanded access program, but it only opens after a prior line of metastatic therapy, so it isn't a door for him until he's progressed on first-line chemo. The one thing worth nailing down before screening is a tissue NGS G12D result to back up the ctDNA call.

Regulatoryinvestigational; FDA breakthrough therapy designation in PDAC; NDA expected on the strength of RASolute 302 but no approval yet (as of June 2026) Guidelinesnot in NCCN as an approved therapy; pivotal RASolute 302 read out at ASCO 2026 (OS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40), filing pending Geographic scopeUS sites; Revolution Medicines runs trials in the US and internationally

Next steps

  1. Call the Revolution Medicines study line (1-844-2-REVMED) or email medinfo@revmed.com to find the nearest RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) site with an open first-line slot
  2. Ask the treating team to confirm a tissue NGS KRAS G12D result, since the current call is ctDNA-only and tissue confirmation strengthens trial eligibility
  3. If no RASolute 303 site is reachable, ask the same line about RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) G12D subprotocols
  4. Keep the daraxonrasib EAP (NCT07573215) on file as the off-trial route for later, once he has had a line of metastatic chemotherapy

docs.title: 2. zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor zoldonrasib, RMC-9805
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

Zoldonrasib is the G12D-selective agent that maps to this patient's exact allele, and the front-line trial RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) takes treatment-naive metastatic KRAS G12D PDAC, so it's the most precisely matched enrollable option on the KRAS axis. RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) is the platform-study backup. No approval and no standalone expanded-access program exist, so enrollment is the only route.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no approval anywhere Guidelinesnot in NCCN/ESMO; phase 1 ORR ~30% in pretreated G12D PDAC (ASCO GI 2025) Geographic scopeUS sites; sponsor also runs trials internationally

Next steps

  1. Call 1-844-2-REVMED or email medinfo@revmed.com to locate the nearest RASolute 305 (NCT07621718) site with an open first-line slot
  2. Confirm the tissue/ctDNA KRAS G12D result is documented, since this trial requires G12D specifically
  3. If RASolute 305 isn't reachable, ask the same line about zoldonrasib cohorts in RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062)
  4. Note that the first-in-human NCT06040541 basket requires prior therapy and won't take a treatment-naive patient yet

The parent phase 1 (NCT06179160) also enrolls at first line and offers combination cohorts. No approval exists; enrollment is the route, with a case-by-case expanded-access ask as a fallback.

docs.title: 4. ceralasertib (AZD6738), oral ATR inhibitor ceralasertib, AZD6738
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

Ceralasertib is the cleanest live option on the ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis, and the UCSF basket (NCT03682289) explicitly takes pancreatic cancer and assigns by ARID1A/BAF250a status. Two things stand between the patient and a slot: the trial is active-not-recruiting, so a new opening isn't guaranteed, and entry depends on BAF250a (ARID1A) protein loss by IHC rather than the frameshift call alone. The validation step is ordering ARID1A IHC before pursuing this.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no approval anywhere Guidelinesnot in NCCN/ESMO; phase 2 activity in ARID1A-deficient tumors concentrated in gynecologic histologies, weaker non-gynecologic signal Geographic scopeUS (UCSF-sponsored)

Next steps

  1. Have the treating team order ARID1A (BAF250a) IHC on tumor tissue; the frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility
  2. Contact the NCT03682289 site (UCSF; PI Rahul Aggarwal) through the cancer center to ask whether the ARID1A pancreatic arm has any remaining slot despite the active-not-recruiting status
  3. For drug-level questions, call AstraZeneca medical information at 1-800-236-9933
  4. Keep this secondary to the KRAS axis; pursue in parallel only if ARID1A IHC confirms loss

Trial pathways

Two constraints: the trial is active-not-recruiting (so a new slot may not exist), and eligibility turns on BAF250a protein loss by IHC, which only ~two-thirds of ARID1A-mutant tumors show. No central contact is posted on the registry; the lead is the UCSF PI (Rahul Aggarwal).

docs.title: 5. ELI-002 (amphiphile mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine, G12D/G12R + Amph-CpG-7909) ELI-002, ELI-002 7P, ELI-002 2P, Amph-Peptides, Amph-CpG-7909
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Expanded access program Modality: vaccine   Verified: 2026-06-06

The KRAS vaccine axis is HLA-agnostic, so this patient's alleles don't rule it out, but the practical problem is setting, not biology: both the ELI-002 trial and its expanded-access protocol are written for the post-resection MRD/adjuvant population, and he has newly diagnosed unresectable metastatic disease. There is no enrollable ELI-002 path for metastatic disease right now. The most a treating team could do is email Elicio to ask whether any metastatic-eligible protocol is planned.

Regulatoryinvestigational; no approval anywhere Guidelinesnot in NCCN/ESMO; phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 showed 84% mKRAS T-cell responses in the MRD/adjuvant setting Geographic scopeUS (expanded access protocol is US-only)

Next steps

  1. Treat ELI-002 as informational for now; neither the trial nor the EAP fits unresectable metastatic disease
  2. If the team still wants to ask, email clinicaltrialinquiries@elicio.com to check whether any metastatic-setting ELI-002 protocol is open or planned
  3. Revisit only if the disease ever becomes resectable / MRD-state, which would change eligibility

docs.title: 6. MRTX1133, KRAS G12D-selective noncovalent inhibitor MRTX1133
docs.text:
Access status: Unavailable Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

This one is a dead end. MRTX1133 was the first clinical KRAS G12D-selective small molecule, but the program was terminated for formulation problems before any efficacy read-out, so there is no trial slot, no expanded access, and no approval. The mechanism it validated lives on in zoldonrasib and INCB161734, which are the agents to pursue instead.

Regulatoryinvestigational; program discontinued Guidelinesnone Geographic scopenot applicable (discontinued)

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue MRTX1133 directly; the program is closed
  2. Route the same KRAS G12D-selective rationale to zoldonrasib (RASolute 305, NCT07621718) and INCB161734 (DAWN-303, NCT07522073), which carried the mechanism forward

9. pooled mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine + nivolumab + ipilimumab mKRAS peptide vaccine, pooled mutant KRAS vaccine

Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: vaccine   Verified: 2026-06-06

The vaccine itself is a finished single-center academic study with no open slot and no manufacturer to supply it, so the combination as studied is not obtainable. The checkpoint backbone (nivolumab plus ipilimumab) is FDA-approved in other cancers and could in theory be prescribed off-label, but for this MSS, TMB-8.6 tumor that would be low-yield, off-guideline, and very likely denied by payers. The useful read from this row is mechanistic: the immunotherapy route into this tumor runs through KRAS-inhibitor-driven antigen restoration plus checkpoint, not checkpoint or vaccine alone.

Regulatoryinvestigational vaccine (no approval); the nivolumab and ipilimumab backbone components are FDA-approved in other tumor types Guidelinesthe vaccine is not in any guideline; nivolumab/ipilimumab are not NCCN-recommended for MSS PDAC and checkpoint monotherapy is low-yield here given MSS, TMB 8.6 Geographic scopeUS (single-center academic study, completed)

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue off-label nivolumab + ipilimumab as a standalone strategy here; the MSS / TMB-8.6 profile predicts low benefit and payers will likely deny it
  2. Confirm MMR protein IHC (MLH1/PMS2/MSH2/MSH6) on tumor tissue before any checkpoint-based claim, per the case's validation gate
  3. Route the checkpoint rationale instead toward KRAS-inhibitor-plus-anti-PD-1 cohorts (e.g. the retifanlimab cohort in INCB161734 NCT06179160)
  4. If a research team wants the academic protocol detail, contact nzaidi1@jhmi.edu

The BMS line covers the nivolumab/ipilimumab components only. Academic correspondence: nzaidi1@jhmi.edu (N. Zaidi, Johns Hopkins).

Payer / coverage notes. The investigational vaccine has no payer pathway. Off-label nivolumab + ipilimumab for MSS PDAC would face prior-authorization denial in most plans, since there is no on-label indication, no NCCN listing, and the MSS / TMB-8.6 profile predicts low benefit from checkpoint blockade. 10. tazemetostat (EPZ-6438), EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat, EPZ-6438, Tazverik

Access status: Unavailable Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

Tazemetostat is off the table. Although it was FDA-approved in epithelioid sarcoma and follicular lymphoma, Ipsen voluntarily withdrew it from all markets in March 2026 over secondary-malignancy safety signals and shut down every trial and expanded-access program, so there is no supply route, no off-label path, and no ARID1A basket left. The EZH2 route into this patient's ARID1A axis has lost its lead agent; the ATR route (ceralasertib) is the one still standing.

Regulatorypreviously FDA-approved (epithelioid sarcoma; relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma); voluntarily withdrawn from all markets by Ipsen on 9 March 2026 over secondary-malignancy safety signals; all trials and expanded-access programs closed Guidelinesprior NCCN listings in its approved indications are moot post-withdrawal; never guideline-supported for PDAC Geographic scopenot applicable (withdrawn worldwide)

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue tazemetostat; it has been withdrawn from all markets and all programs are closed
  2. Direct the ARID1A synthetic-lethal rationale to the ATR axis (ceralasertib, NCT03682289) instead
  3. Note for the board that the EZH2-in-ARID1A hypothesis lost both its lead agent and its supporting efficacy signal (negative NRG-GY014)

11. tuvusertib (M1774), oral ATR inhibitor tuvusertib, M1774

Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-06-06

Tuvusertib targets the same ATR axis as ceralasertib, but its ARID1A loss-of-function cohort (Part A3 of DDRiver 320) is built around endometrial cancer, and the relevant parts don't name pancreatic cancer. The trial is also active-not-recruiting. So this is mechanism support for the ATR route, not a slot a PDAC patient can take right now. docs.title: GFH375 / VS-7375, KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor (VS-7375 + cetuximab, 1L PDAC cohort, NCT07644559) (gfh375-vs7375)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1lowThis is the exact allele on the exact target, and the response rate is the loudest signal in the whole dossier: 41% confirmed ORR (90% CI 30-52) with 97% disease control in pretreated G12D PDAC. The upside I am chasing is that a 1L, chemo-sparing oral drug reproduces or beats that in a treatment-naive tumor, where response fractions in this disease usually run in the teens. The efficacy read is second-line and single-arm so it is not proof, and mPFS was only 5.52 months, but for a 79-year-old who would otherwise face FOLFIRINOX I want the allele-matched shot on goal first.ORR and mPFS come from previously-treated patients; the treatment-naive 1L number is unknown and could regress; grade >=3 TRAE 30% with neutropenia and anemia, and the cetuximab pairing adds a rash/hypomagnesemia burden that a 79-year-old may tolerate poorly; durability is thin at 5.52-month mPFS, so acquired resistance may arrive fast conservative4lowThis is the G12D-selective agent with the most quantified toxicity table after daraxonrasib: ESMO 2025 gave grade >=3 TRAE 30.3% (one grade 4 neutropenia), with a myelosuppression-plus-GI signature — neutrophils decreased 49% any-grade / 8% grade >=3, anemia 42% / 8% grade >=3, diarrhea 56% / 3% grade >=3 — and no dose-limiting toxicities at 600 mg. The cytopenias have standard management algorithms, which is why it clears my bar for a ranked slot. What drops it to fourth is the cetuximab pairing in the 1L cohort: cetuximab adds its own well-known acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion-reaction burden, and the doublet has no dedicated combination safety characterization in PDAC. The efficacy base is also one line beyond this patient (previously-treated, ORR 41%).Myelosuppression is real (neutrophils 8% and anemia 8% at grade >=3) and the cetuximab partner adds a separate, uncharacterized-in-combination toxicity layer for PDAC; Single-arm efficacy sits at 2L+ (ORR 41%, mPFS 5.52 mo); the 1L benefit is unproven; China-only phase 1/2 data; population and supportive-care context may not transfer directly to a US 79-year-old critic3moderateThe highest single-arm response number for an allele-matched agent here, ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52) in 59 evaluable previously-treated G12D PDAC, with mPFS 5.52 mo. Two things temper it and I will name both: it is a single-country study (GFH375X1101, China) reported as an ESMO abstract, so geographic generalizability to a US population and full-manuscript RoB are both open questions, and the interval is a 90% CI, a wider alpha than the 95% I would want quoted. The randomized phase 3 against chemotherapy (NCT07262567) is the design that would actually test this, but it sits at 2L and has no readout, so for a treatment-naive patient this is evidence one line removed. I rank it below zoldonrasib only because zoldonrasib carries a registered 1L phase 3 in progress; on response magnitude alone GFH375 is the stronger single-arm number.ROBINS-I:Moderate single-arm; ORR reported with a 90% (not 95%) CI and no comparator arm; geographic generalizability: single-country (China) phase 1/2, US applicability untested; directness: evaluable efficacy is 2L+ (68% had >=2 prior lines), the patient is treatment-naive, so the 1L cohort of NCT07644559 is the fit but has no efficacy read concensusite4lowVS-7375 gives a fourth front-line-eligible G12D-selective slot: NCT07644559 has a 1L cohort admitting treatment-naive patients at ECOG 1, and the monotherapy read was presented at ESMO 2025 (LBA84) in previously treated G12D PDAC at ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52), doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099. That Western congress presentation and the US sponsor keep it inside the guideline-consonant, trial-enrollment frame under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 rather than resting on non-Western data alone. It ranks below the phase-3-anchored options because its own controlled evidence is a phase 3 that sits at second line (NCT07262567), not first.The 1L cohort is phase 2 single-arm; the randomized read (NCT07262567) is second-line and still recruiting.; Cetuximab adds a rash/hypomagnesemia burden that the single-agent RAS(ON) trials do not carry.; The efficacy anchor is a China-based phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101); enrollment should confirm the US cohort's line and ECOG fit before relying on it. advocate1moderateThis is the pick that best serves what the patient actually stated. prefers_trials is the one preference carrying weight, and GFH375 has a recruiting first-line PDAC cohort he can enter now (NCT07644559 admits treatment-naive G12D PDAC at ECOG 1), so the door a trials-leaning patient wants is open. It is allele-matched to his exact KRAS G12D, oral, and the ORR of 41% (90% CI 30-52) in previously-treated G12D PDAC is the strongest single-agent response on his own driver anywhere in this dossier. With no toxicity_veto and no modality_constraint to hold against it, the only thing I flag for a 79-year-old is the myelosuppression (grade >=3 neutropenia 8%, anemia 8%) that sits behind the 30% grade >=3 TRAE rate.prefers_trials, the KRAS G12D axis, and the oral modality are all satisfied cleanly; the neutral 0.5 weight is the only soft spot, and the free_text itself warns 0.5 may understate how toxicity-averse a 79-year-old is; the 41% ORR read comes from a mostly >=2-prior-line population (68% had >=2 prior lines); the 1L cohort pairs the drug with cetuximab, and that combination's tolerability at his age is not separately reported

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocateendorseevidence_qualityThis is the pick I would lead with too: the highest single-agent ORR on his exact allele at 41% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), oral, with an open recruiting 1L cohort (NCT07644559). You are honest that the number comes from a mostly >=2-prior-line set and that the cetuximab pairing is uncharacterized at his age — that is the right thing to flag while still putting the loudest allele-matched signal first. conservativerisktakerqualifiedtoxicityI can plan around the GFH375 backbone itself: grade >=3 TRAE 30.3%, neutrophils 8% and anemia 8% at G3+, cytopenias with standard algorithms. What the rank-1 slot skips over is the cetuximab partner, which adds acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions that a 79-year-old tolerates poorly, and the PDAC doublet has no dedicated combination safety table. Chasing the 41% single-arm ORR is defensible; treating the doublet's tolerability as solved when the second agent's toxicity was never characterized in this combination is not. conservativeadvocatequalifiedtoxicityYour rank 1 serves prefers_trials cleanly, and I do not fault the enrollment logic, but the 1L cohort pairs the drug with cetuximab and you concede its tolerability at age 79 is not separately reported. That is exactly the uncharacterized toxicity layer I qualify on: acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions added to GFH375's 8%/8% G3+ cytopenias, with no combination safety table in PDAC. Your own free_text flag that the neutral 0.5 understates a 79-year-old's toxicity-aversion points to the gentler zoldonrasib (no grade 4-5 TRAE) as the better-tolerated door if one is open. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityRanking GFH375 above daraxonrasib puts a single-arm China phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101, doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099) over the only randomized OS result on the board (RASolute 302, pmid:42223072, HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53). The 41% ORR is quoted with a 90% CI, not 95%, on 59 evaluable patients who were 68% two-plus lines deep, so the interval is wider than it looks and the number is 2L, not the 1L slot he needs. A loud uncontrolled response rate does not outrank a registered survival endpoint; bank the allele match as upside, not as the headline. criticadvocatequalifiedevidence_qualityprefers_trials is the only preference carrying weight, and it does not separate GFH375 from daraxonrasib since both have open 1L cohorts, so the tiebreak should not fall to the higher single-arm ORR. That 41% comes from a China phase 1/2 with a 90% CI in a mostly 2L population (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), while daraxonrasib carries the randomized OS HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072). Serving the patient's trial preference is fine; ranking the thinner evidence first on top of it is where I qualify. concensusiterisktakerqualifiedguideline_fitI share the driver logic, but leading with a China-based phase 1/2 (GFH375X1101) single-arm ORR over daraxonrasib inverts the evidence order that NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025's trial-enrollment frame would rank on. VS-7375 stays inside the guideline-consonant frame because it has a US-sponsor 1L cohort and an ESMO 2025 presentation, so it is a defensible pick, just not a defensible number-one over the phase-3-anchored option. The cetuximab pairing also adds a toxicity layer the RAS(ON) monotherapy trials do not carry for a 79-year-old. concensusiteadvocatedissentguideline_fitServing prefers_trials does not by itself justify ranking VS-7375 above daraxonrasib, because both have open recruiting 1L slots, so the preference is satisfied either way and the tie-break falls to evidence strength. On that axis the guideline-consonant order under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 puts the FDA-breakthrough, randomized-phase-3 agent first and the China-based single-arm ORR second. A 41% response number one line removed from this patient is a weaker anchor than an OS hit, even for a trials-leaning patient. advocaterisktakerendorsepreference_fitThis is the top pick I share, and for the patient's reasons rather than the ORR alone. GFH375 is oral, matched to his exact G12D, and has an open recruiting 1L PDAC cohort (nct:NCT07644559), which lands prefers_trials, the driver, and the gentler-route instinct in one option. Grade >=3 TRAE sat at 30.3% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), well under the HRS-4642 backbone, so it also fits the toxicity-aversion the free_text warns 0.5 understates. advocateconcensusitequalifiedpreference_fitRanking VS-7375 fourth on strength of controlled evidence is defensible, but from the patient's chair it does better than fourth: oral, exact-allele, ORR 41% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099), with an open recruiting 1L cohort that lands prefers_trials directly (nct:NCT07644559). Worth separating two things you rightly kept apart, the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T and the A*11:01 programs are genuine HLA ineligibilities for his C*05:01/C*06:02 genotype, not preference conflicts, so leaving them off the ranking is correct and not a call I would reopen.

docs.title: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, first-line (phase 3 NCT07232875; phase 1b/2 Nat Med) (hrs-4642)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2lowThe front-line combination hit a 63.3% ORR (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive G12D PDAC patients, which is roughly double what gem/nab-paclitaxel alone delivers and the single most striking 1L number I found. If that holds, layering an allele-matched inhibitor onto a standard backbone is exactly the kind of high-ceiling move worth taking early. The catch is a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate driven by the chemo backbone, and the phase 3 is not-yet-recruiting, so this may be an intent-to-enroll rather than a today slot.90.3% grade >=3 TRAE, largely hematologic, is a real problem at age 79 with an assumed rather than measured ECOG; n=30 for the efficacy readout is small and PFS/OS were not reported, so the ORR could be a soft surrogate; the phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so timing may not match the patient's window conservative——did not pick— critic4lowThis is the only allele-directed agent with front-line data at the patient's exact line, ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive patients, peer-reviewed in Nature Medicine. The single-arm design is the problem I cannot get past: 63% ORR is measured on top of a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone that delivers roughly 20-23% ORR on its own, so without a control arm I cannot apportion how much is the drug, and the HRS-4642 monotherapy read was only 20.8% ORR, which is the honest ceiling on its independent contribution. Grade >=3 TRAEs ran 90.3%, driven by the chemo backbone, and this is a China-based study with the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) not yet recruiting. I rank it fourth because the setting fit is exact but the attributable effect is confounded and the toxicity is heavy for a 79-year-old.ROBINS-I: single-arm, so the 63.3% combination ORR is confounded with the chemo backbone and not attributable to HRS-4642; monotherapy ORR was only 20.8%; grade >=3 TRAE 90.3% (backbone-driven) is a marrow-reserve concern at age 79; geographic generalizability (China) plus a confirmatory phase 3 that is not yet recruiting; no randomized evidence exists concensusite——did not pick— advocate4moderateI am surfacing this because it carries the highest front-line response signal on his driver in the whole dossier, a confirmed 63.3% ORR (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in treatment-naive G12D PDAC, and the phase 3 (NCT07232875) matches him on allele, tumor type, and 1L. But I rank it fourth and I am plain about why, because this is where I carry the patient's interests rather than the headline number. The regimen is IV, not oral, and the grade >=3 TRAE rate is 90.3% driven by the gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone, which is a lot of hematologic toxicity to put on a 79-year-old whose free_text already hints he may want a gentler course. And prefers_trials is only half-served here: the phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so the door is not currently open.highest 1L ORR on his allele, but IV rather than oral and a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE burden from the chemo backbone cut against a 79-year-old; with modality_constraints empty I cannot veto on route, only flag it; the enrollable phase 3 is not yet recruiting, so prefers_trials is not fully met today; mPFS/mOS from the phase 1b/2 are still immature

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativedissenttoxicityYou left the 63.3% front-line ORR off the ranked list entirely because grade >=3 TRAE ran 90.3% (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9), but the safety_summary attributes that rate to the gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone, not a new HRS-4642 signal, so you are declining the highest 1L response on his exact allele over toxicity the standard chemo arm carries anyway. That said, the one treatment-related death in the monotherapy set (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484) and the metabolic signature are fair reasons to keep it off rank 1 — dropping it out of the top five altogether overcorrects. risktakerconcensusitedissentguideline_fitYou declined to rank HRS-4642 despite its 63.3% front-line ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) partly because 'a US patient's guideline-consonant path runs through the Western-sponsored trials first' — but NCCN just says profile-and-enroll, it does not rank sponsors by geography, and a China-run phase 2 in Nature Medicine is not disqualified evidence. The real caveats are the 90.3% G3 backbone burden and a phase 3 not yet recruiting; leaning on sponsor nationality understates the response ceiling you are passing over. conservativerisktakerdissenttoxicityRanking this second puts a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE regimen with one treatment-related death (1/84) in front of a 79-year-old, and I dissent on that. The 63.3% ORR is real, but even read as chemo-backbone-driven a 90.3% G3+ rate against unmeasured marrow reserve is a floor the intake free_text explicitly warns about when it says the neutral 0.5 weight likely understates how toxicity-averse this patient is. HRS-4642 monotherapy also carries a hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia signature on top, which is a second metabolic layer with no combination-specific management algorithm published yet. conservativecriticqualifiedtoxicityWe land in the same place and I want to sharpen one datum you carried lightly. You flag the 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE as a marrow-reserve concern, which is right, but the harder stop is the single treatment-related death (1/84 in the phase 1b/2), because a fatal event in an 84-patient safety set is not a number I discount at age 79 even when the ORR is 63.3%. Rank 4 reads fine on evidence grounds; from the safety lens I would hold it below any agent whose G3+ union rate has a published management algorithm rather than a chemo-backbone rationalization. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe 63.3% front-line ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9, n=30) is measured on top of a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone with no control arm, and the same program's monotherapy read was only 20.8% (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.08.1484), so most of that headline is chemo you cannot separate out. It is a China single-arm phase 1b/2 whose Nat Med paper has no PubMed record yet, so I have not seen the bias profile of the primary analysis. Ranking it at #2 over daraxonrasib treats a confounded ORR as if it settled the question; the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) is not yet recruiting. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitRanking the Hengrui HRS-4642 program at rank 2, ahead of daraxonrasib, puts a China-based front-line phase 3 that is not yet recruiting above the one agent on this axis with FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation and a positive randomized phase 3. NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 assigns no category to any KRAS G12D agent, so the tie-break is which trial a US patient can actually enter on the guideline-consonant path, and that favors the Western-sponsored RASolute slots. The 63.3% ORR is real but single-arm on a full gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone; I would not let it outrank the controlled evidence. advocaterisktakerdissentpreference_fitRanking the highest-ORR option second reads the number and not the man. HRS-4642 here is IV on a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone that ran a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate, and its phase 3 (nct:NCT07232875) is not yet recruiting, so it half-serves the one preference that carries weight, prefers_trials. For a 79-year-old the free_text already flags as likely toxicity-averse past the neutral 0.5, an IV chemo doublet at that grade-3 rate is the wrong front of the ranking. advocateconservativeendorsepreference_fitKeeping the 63.3% ORR off your top five on a 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate is the right call from the patient's side, and I will say so plainly. Even read as chemo-backbone toxicity, that grade-3 burden on an IV doublet is what a 79-year-old flagged as toxicity-averse would most want to avoid. You reached it on characterized-safety grounds and I reach it on preference_fit; either way the headline number does not earn a front-line slot for this man.

docs.title: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor, first-line (RASolute 303, NCT07491445) (daraxonrasib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3moderateThis is the one option with randomized survival data behind it: RASolute 302 showed OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) with median OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months and grade >=3 toxicity actually lower than chemotherapy. Even though it is pan-RAS rather than G12D-selective, it covers G12D, and the enrollable 1L RASolute 303 randomizes against gem/nab-paclitaxel, so the downside is capped by an active comparator. I rank it below the selective agents only because I am hunting for the higher response ceiling, but this is the pick with the firmest floor.pan-RAS mechanism hits wild-type RAS too, so the rash/stomatitis skin-mucosal burden is characteristic and near-universal at any grade; the OS anchor is second-line; the 1L readout is not yet mature; randomization in RASolute 303 means a chance of assignment to the chemo-only arm conservative1moderateOf everything on the KRAS axis this is the only agent with a randomized phase 3 readout and a per-term grade >=3 table I can actually plan around: RASolute 302 gave OS HR 0.40 in the RAS G12 stratum, and the drug's grade >=3 TRAE rate ran 43.6% against 57.5% on chemotherapy, so the toxicity trades under the comparator rather than adding to it. The G3+ burden is skin and mucosa — rash 14%, stomatitis 12% — both of which have settled dermatologic and oral-care management algorithms, and TRAE-driven discontinuation was 1.2% versus 11.2% on chemo. Follow-up is still short by post-marketing standards (2L pivotal cut in 2026, no 5-year safety) and the front-line RASolute 303 slot is investigational, so I hold at moderate. For a 79-year-old this is the least-surprising toxicity profile in the option set.No long-term (>=5 yr) safety follow-up; the pivotal data are 2L and read across to the treatment-naive 1L slot rather than being generated in it; Any-grade rash approaches 91% in the phase 1/2 PDAC set — low-grade but near-universal, and dose modification ran ~48%, which matters for adherence in an older patient; RASolute 303 randomizes to monotherapy, mono+chemo, or chemo; the mono+chemo arm layers the daraxonrasib rash onto chemo myelosuppression, a combination without its own dedicated safety characterization critic1highOne intervention on this board clears the bar I actually hold: RASolute 302 is a randomized phase 3 (n=500) with a pre-specified OS primary endpoint hit at HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53, p=4.6e-11), published in NEJM, and the RAS G12 stratum that contains G12D holds the effect at HR 0.40 (CI 0.30-0.54). That is registration-grade, not a signal. Two honest caveats keep me from calling it settled: the trial is open-label, so PFS and ORR carry detection bias (OS is largely immune to it, which is why I lean on the OS number), and the pivotal data are 2L while the enrollable slot for a treatment-naive patient is 1L RASolute 303 (NCT07491445), which has not read out. The 1L benefit is a cross-line inference, not yet demonstrated, but the mechanism and the 2L magnitude make this the defensible lead.RoB2 domain 4 (measurement of outcome): open-label design biases PFS/ORR ascertainment; I weight OS, which the design does not compromise; directness/applicability: registration efficacy is 2L, the 1L RASolute 303 slot is unread, so front-line benefit is extrapolated across line not proven; pan-RAS rather than G12D-selective, so target coverage is broader than the allele but the allele-specific contribution is not isolable from this trial concensusite1moderateNo KRAS G12D therapy is approved, so NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2025 puts a newly diagnosed metastatic patient on comprehensive somatic and germline profiling plus clinical-trial enrollment; there is no consensus category to assign, and this is the guideline-consonant route rather than an off-guideline gamble. Of the enrollable trials, daraxonrasib has by far the strongest controlled evidence: RASolute 302 read out an OS HR of 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) in the RAS G12 stratum that carries his G12D (pmid:42223072), and it holds FDA breakthrough designation, which is the nearest thing to cross-body agreement this axis has before approval. RASolute 303 (NCT07491445) opens the matching first-line slot for a treatment-naive ECOG-1 patient.The randomized phase-3 evidence sits at second line; first-line benefit is inferred from RASolute 303's design, not yet demonstrated.; The G12D call is plasma ctDNA — tissue NGS confirmation is the enrollment token the RAS(ON) protocols expect.; RASolute 303 randomizes against gem/nab-paclitaxel, so an assigned patient may draw the chemo control arm rather than the drug. advocate2moderateFor a patient who wants a trial, this is the option with the most under it: the only randomized phase 3 evidence on his driver (RASolute 302, OS HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53), and a recruiting front-line slot he qualifies for in RASolute 303 (NCT07491445 takes treatment-naive metastatic PDAC and accepts his G12D under its RAS-mutant criterion). It is oral, which costs him nothing under a silent modality field but is worth naming at 79, and pan-RAS covers G12D so it speaks to the lead driver. I put it second rather than first only because GFH375 gives him a G12D-selective agent with a higher on-axis ORR at the same open-1L-trial bar; on evidence depth daraxonrasib is the stronger anchor.prefers_trials and oral modality both met; the registration safety read is from 2L, so a longer front-line course of rash (grade >=3 14%) and stomatitis (12%) in a 79-year-old is not yet characterized at 1L; the 1L benefit rests on RASolute 303, which has not read out; the OS HR 0.40 is a 2L number the patient's line does not yet own

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityThe daraxonrasib RCT floor is real and I take it too (OS HR 0.40, pmid:42223072), so no fight on the pick itself. But ranking it #1 buries the loudest response signals: GFH375 at 41% ORR (doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2025.09.099) and HRS-4642+chemo at 63.3% (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) both outrun daraxonrasib's 31.6%, and with an empty toxicity_veto list and a neutral 0.5 weight there is no stated reason to trade that ceiling away for the safer table. risktakercriticqualifiedevidence_qualityAgreed daraxonrasib is the only registration-grade read on the board (pmid:42223072), and I keep it as my floor too. Where we part: sorting the whole list by RoB tier pushes HRS-4642's exact-line 63.3% ORR (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04538-9) down to rank 4 as 'confounded backbone', but for a treatment-naive 79-year-old the attributable question matters less than the observed 1L number in the setting he is actually in — the confound cuts the effect, it does not erase a doubling over historical gem/nab-paclitaxel. risktakerconcensusitequalifiedevidence_qualityFine to anchor on daraxonrasib for its breakthrough designation and OS HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072); it is the defensible consensus lead. My objection is only to the ordering logic — you rank purely by strength of controlled evidence, which is exactly the axis where a high-ceiling patient loses the 41% GFH375 and 63.3% HRS-4642 reads, both allele-matched, to a 31.6% ORR agent with a firmer table. conservativeconcensusiteendorsetoxicityThis is the rank-1 I would defend on tolerability alone, so I endorse it. RASolute 302 gave a grade >=3 TRAE rate of 43.6% against 57.5% on chemotherapy, with TRAE-driven discontinuation 1.2% versus 11.2%, so the toxicity trades under the comparator rather than adding to it, and the G3+ burden is rash 14% and stomatitis 12% with settled dermatologic and oral-care algorithms. My only carried caveat is the same one you named: this is 2L pivotal safety read across to a 1L slot, and any-grade rash runs near 91% in the phase 1/2 PDAC set, so dose modification is likely even though the high-grade profile is the most predictable in the option set. criticconcensusitequalifiedevidence_qualitySame agent at #1, no dissent on the rank. But FDA breakthrough designation is a regulatory fast-track flag resting on the same RASolute 302 data (pmid:42223072), not independent RCT weight, so 'proximity-to-listing' should not be doing the work the trial result already does. And the G12D estimate is borrowed from the RAS G12 stratum (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.54), not a pre-specified per-allele analysis, so the allele-specific benefit is inferred from the subgroup. Rank it on the registered OS endpoint; let the breakthrough flag describe the path, not the strength of evidence. criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityWe land on the same agent and the same n=500 randomized base, so this is a qualifier, not a fight. The grade >=3 table your safety-depth rank leans on (rash 14%, stomatitis 12%) is RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072), a 2L registration trial that RoB2 rates Some on open-label design, so the PFS and ORR read carry detection bias even where OS is largely insulated. That safety datum was characterized in pretreated patients, not the treatment-naive 79-year-old he is; the 1L read still sits with RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445), unposted. I also concede your point that the zoldonrasib allele match is genuine biology, not just a cleaner AE table. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitSame lead, same reasoning. Under NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 no KRAS G12D agent carries a consensus category, so among trial-enrollment options daraxonrasib is the one nearest a future listing: positive randomized phase 3 (RASolute 302, OS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo) plus FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation. Your planning-around-a-per-term-safety-table logic and my proximity-to-consensus logic converge here, which is the cross-frame agreement I weight most. advocatecriticendorseevidence_qualityI keep daraxonrasib in my own top tier and your evidence-grade rank-1 is the anchor I want under any trials-forward recommendation to this patient: the only randomized OS result on his driver, HR 0.40 (pmid:42223072), with a recruiting front-line slot he qualifies for (nct:NCT07491445). It is oral too, which costs him nothing under a silent modality field and matters at 79.
