docs.title: 5. zolbetuximab (anti-CLDN18.2 mAb) + chemotherapy VYLOY, IMAB362, zolbetuximab-clzb
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: monoclonal antibody   Verified: 2026-08-12

FDA- and EMA-approved for CLDN18.2-positive (75% or more at 2+/3+) HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, so a US oncologist can mechanically prescribe it off-label in PDAC today. The evidence and the assay both cut against doing so: the GLEAM phase 2 in PDAC missed its primary OS endpoint (13.7 vs 13.6 months), and this tumor's 60% staining sits below the label-defining cutoff, so expect payer denial and little support from the data. Astellas' early-access program (NCT06048081) is gastric/GEJ-only with US enrollment closed, so it adds nothing here.

RegulatoryFDA-approved October 2024 and EMA-approved for CLDN18.2-positive gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; no PDAC indication GuidelinesOn-guideline for gastric/GEJ 1L; off-guideline in PDAC Geographic scopeUS and EU prescription (on-label gastric/GEJ); off-label PDAC at prescriber discretion

Next steps

  1. Run the 43-14A CDx re-stain first; if the CDx read comes back at or above 75% the off-label conversation changes materially.
  2. If the treating team still wants to pursue it, call Astellas Medical Communications (800-727-7003) for the PDAC data file and any single-patient options.
  3. Weigh the CLDN18.2 trial rows (ADCs, engagers, CAR-T) before committing to an off-label antibody with a negative randomized PDAC readout.

docs.title: 14. 177Lu-DOTA-SNA040 (CLDN18.2-directed lutetium-177 radioligand therapy) SNA040, [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-SNA040, 68Ga-NODAGA-SNA014 (imaging companion)
docs.text:
Access status: Not yet accessible Modality: radioligand   Verified: 2026-08-12

The biomarker fit is the best in the whole CLDN18.2 file, and the honest verdict is still that a US patient cannot get this drug. The only trial is a 12-patient investigator-initiated dose escalation at a single Shanghai center (Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center), with 2 to 6 treatment cycles after a 68Ga-PET gate, meaning months of care inside the Chinese health system. Single-center Chinese IITs at this scale do not have a mechanism for enrolling foreign patients: consent, insurance, safety follow-up, and China's human-genetic-resources rules all assume local residents, and nothing on the record suggests the sponsor has built an exception. Stated travel willingness does not bridge that; this is the satri-cel situation one stage earlier, minus the approval.

RegulatoryInvestigational; no approval anywhere, no US IND posted Geographic scopeMainland China only; single center (Shanghai)

Next steps

  1. One email to mengru.wu@smartnucl.com from the treating team, asking two questions: does the IIT have any mechanism for a non-resident patient, and is a US or multinational sponsor study planned. Expect the first answer to be no; the second is the useful one.
  2. Set a registry alert for new SNA040 or SmartNuclide postings; a US IND would change this row's verdict outright.
  3. Keep the 43-14A CDx re-stain report on file; if this class ever opens in the West, this tumor walks in on biomarker.

docs.title: 17. olaparib maintenance (gated on the pending germline panel) LYNPARZA
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small molecule (PARP inhibitor)   Verified: 2026-08-12

Approved and pharmacy-orderable, but doubly gated for this patient: the label requires a germline BRCA mutation, which is unknown until the dedicated panel returns, and it specifies maintenance after 16 or more weeks of first-line platinum without progression, whereas this patient progressed about 4 months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy. If the panel comes back BRCA- or PALB2-positive, the realistic shape is off-label maintenance after a response to a new platinum-containing line, argued case-by-case with the payer. Captured now so the pathway is ready the day the germline result lands.

Next steps

  1. Wait for the germline panel; nothing to do before it returns.
  2. If BRCA1/2-positive, document with BRACAnalysis CDx and plan a platinum-containing line whose response would set up maintenance.
  3. If PALB2-positive, expect an off-label prior-auth argument; the treating team should collect the supporting literature before submitting.

docs.title: 38. CLDN18.2 re-stain on the FDA companion-diagnostic assay (VENTANA CLDN18 43-14A RxDx)
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: diagnostic assay   Verified: 2026-08-12

The FDA-approved 43-14A CDx assay is available as a send-out from at least three US reference labs, so re-staining the archival 2025 resection block can happen this week without waiting for a biopsy. NeoGenomics runs it in 1 to 2 days, Labcorp Oncology (test 452390) in about 3, and Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists it as test CLD18. We could not confirm that Tempus or Caris offer the 43-14A CDx assay, which matches what the target validator found, so route the order to one of the three verified labs. The prior 60% 2+/3+ call was on an unstated clone; the CDx re-stain settles where this tumor really sits against the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff and the lower trial cutoffs (FG-M108's phase 3 uses 40% or more at 2+ or higher).

Geographic scopeUS send-out from any pathology department

Next steps

  1. Send the December 2025 resection block (or 5 unstained slides) to NeoGenomics or Labcorp now; the archival stain is informative even before the recurrence is biopsied.
  2. When recurrence cores exist, repeat the stain on current tissue, since CAR-T and ADC sponsors often require it and expression can shift after chemotherapy.
  3. File both reports with the percentage at 2+/3+ stated explicitly, so each CLDN18.2 program's cutoff can be checked without re-review.

docs.title: Selected general biomarker report — pdac-recurrent-cldn18-2-kras-g12r-tp53-y220c-p25m
docs.text: Which biomarkers on the selected panel this patient has been tested for, and which have never been measured. The panel covers targets established in this tumor type, targets relevant across a subset of tumor types, and biomarkers that predict benefit regardless of where the tumor started, such as MSI-H/dMMR and high tumor mutational burden gating PD-1 blockade.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Selected general biomarker report (offline HTML) — the same survey, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Selected general biomarker report (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by recommended action

20 biomarkers surveyed: 16 with no usable result on file (0 essential), 2 measured but not to decision resolution, 2 already established. Panel coverage: 9 tumor-agnostic biomarkers plus 11 of 72 protein targets in scope for this tumor.

Twenty biomarkers were surveyed: sixteen never measured, and the two measured short of decision grade are the essential ones. Germline status is effectively unknown. The "none detected" on file is incidental tumor-NGS reporting, not the germline panel NCCN has recommended for every PDAC patient since 2019, and onset in the 50s sharpens it. BRCA1/2, PALB2, and ATM gate olaparib maintenance and platinum re-challenge. One blood draw, no tissue, an approved drug class behind a positive: the survey's highest-value order. The other essential gap, CLDN18.2, is a threshold call, not a yes-or-no. The tumor stained 2+/3+ in 60% of cells: below the 75% cutoff of zolbetuximab's registrational trials, clear of satri-cel's 2+ in 40%, ASP2138's 1+, and the radioligand protocol's 2+ in 20%, which 60% clears threefold. Which threshold applies decides which route is open; the clone went unnamed and the stain is archival.

Archival is the deeper problem: everything on file describes the December 2025 resection, not the July 2026 recurrence, with ten cycles of FOLFIRINOX in between. Two orders close the gaps: the blood draw (HLA class I typing rides along) and a recurrence biopsy, rank 1 for target validator and PI alike; one pass yields DNA and RNA sequencing and a six-stain block cut, CLDN18.2 re-stain included. Primary-to-recurrence concordance is 83.3%, but losses cluster in local recurrence and liver metastasis, this patient's setting, and biopsy sensitivity is 54.6%, so a negative stain on a small core is weak evidence of true loss.

The two finished results are answers, not gaps: microsatellite stability at TMB 0.83 mut/Mb closes single-agent PD-1 blockade, and the ranking says so. KRAS G12R is confirmed, but no G12C- or G12D-selective agent covers it. KMT2C S2816fs stays at the user's request despite no clinical route, and everything else on the panel is absent on purpose. Most of what remains will test negative. The case for testing is the size of the option a positive opens, not an implied likelihood of one.

docs.title: What this collapses to
docs.text:
The gaps above resolve onto this many distinct orders. Biomarkers that ride along on the same assay are grouped together.

  • single IHC block cut (CLDN18.2, HER2, mesothelin, TROP2, B7-H3, CEACAM5) on recurrent-lesion tissue if biopsied, otherwise on the December 2025 resection block — B7-H3 (CD276) protein expression, CEACAM5 (CEA) protein expression, Cadherin-17 (CDH17) protein expression, HER2 protein overexpression (IHC 3+), Integrin beta-6 (alpha-v beta-6) expression, Mesothelin (MSLN) protein expression, Prostate stem cell antigen (PSCA) expression, ROR1 protein expression, TROP2 (TACSTD2) protein expression
  • recurrent-lesion biopsy: one pass supplies comprehensive DNA plus RNA tumor NGS and a block for the IHC stains below — BRAF V600E mutation, NTRK1 / NTRK2 / NTRK3 gene fusion
  • FAPI PET/CT, or FAP IHC on tumor tissue — Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression on cancer-associated fibroblasts
  • PD-L1 IHC using the clone and scoring system named by the protocol requesting it — PD-L1 protein expression
  • Tn-MUC1 glycoform IHC (5E5-type antibody), not standard MUC1 IHC — MUC1 protein expression (including aberrant Tn-MUC1 glycoform)
  • one blood draw shared with germline multigene panel and HLA class I typing — HLA class I genotype (4-digit)
  • recurrent-lesion biopsy: one pass supplies comprehensive DNA plus RNA tumor NGS and a block for the IHC stains below; same assay as the NTRK row — RET gene fusion

Taken with microsatellite-stable status, single-agent PD-1 blockade has no biomarker support in this case.

Reading this report

This page answers one question per biomarker: has this patient been tested for it, and was the test at a resolution that can carry a treatment decision. Not measured means nothing is on file, which is not the same as a negative result. Measured, not decision-grade means a result exists but cannot be acted on as it stands; those gaps are worked into the Target validation paths report. Priority weighs what is going unassessed against how routine the assay is. Most of these biomarkers will be negative if tested; the case for testing rests on the size of the option that opens if positive, not on how likely a positive is.

Back to case · Target validation · Recommendations · Trials · Evidence · Board

Decision support, not medical advice

Libby is experimental. An unmeasured biomarker on this page is a gap in the record, not a prediction that the patient carries it. Assay availability, current approval status, and whether any of this testing is worth the tissue are decisions for the treating team. See PHI policy.

docs.title: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor) (daraxonrasib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1moderateHR 0.40 for OS, 13.2 versus 6.6 months, in a randomized phase 3 whose RAS G12 estimand contains G12R, and the drug is free right now under an FDA-authorized expanded-access protocol. Upside case: roughly a doubling of expected survival against an 8.8-month gem/nab-paclitaxel floor, without burning a trial slot. The weakness I will not paper over is that G12R was never analyzed on its own, and the matched GEMM work has G12R initiating tumors in about 10% of mice against rapid multifocal disease for G12D, so the allele-level effect could land well below the pooled HR. Staging decides access: the EAP and RASolute 303 both gate on confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 shuts its window 6 weeks after that diagnosis, so the site call has to be teed up before the biopsy reads out.G12R sits inside a pooled G12 estimand rather than a prespecified subgroup, and the 2L ORR of 35% rests on n=26 with a 95% CI of 17-56.; If the biopsy and restaging read locally recurrent rather than metastatic, both the EAP and RASolute 303 close on the same day.; The 6-week consent clock on RASolute 303 starts at metastatic diagnosis, which means outreach has to precede the pathology result.; Grade >=3 AEs were 61.8% (rash and GI dominate), and absorption of a once-daily oral after pancreatic resection has not been checked in this patient.; Going first with daraxonrasib closes KST-6051 and the other pan-KRAS phase 1s that require RAS-inhibitor-naive status. conservative1moderateI did not expect to put an unapproved drug at rank 1, but the tolerability data made the argument for me: RASolute 302 showed fewer grade >=3 AEs on daraxonrasib than on chemotherapy (61.8% vs 69.6%) and a fraction of the TRAE discontinuations (1.2% vs 11.2%), alongside OS of 13.2 vs 6.6 months (HR 0.40, P<0.001) in the RAS G12 population that covers G12R. The safety base behind that is 168 PDAC patients at <=300 mg with grade >=3 TRAEs in 30%, mostly rash and GI events with workable management. Access through the FDA-authorized EAP (NCT07573215) means free drug under a monitored protocol, a very different risk posture from off-label improvisation. Two gates first: restaging has to confirm metastatic disease, and someone has to draw baseline labs, because no organ-function numbers exist in this chart since the resection.No long-tail safety record: first-in-human dosing started in 2022, so follow-up beyond about three years does not exist and there is no post-marketing experience anywhere.; The per-term grade >=3 AE table lives in the NEJM full text; what is priced here is the 61.8% union rate from the abstract.; Both the EAP and RASolute 303 require confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 adds a 6-week consent clock from the metastatic diagnosis; a locally-recurrent read on restaging closes both doors.; Undocumented organ function could fail EAP entry labs before the tolerability argument ever gets tested. critic1moderateRASolute 302 is the only RCT-grade evidence in this dossier that is in PDAC and contains this allele: n=500, mOS 13.2 vs 6.6 months in the pre-specified RAS G12 population, HR 0.40, P<0.001. G12R sits inside that estimand but was never studied as a population, no allele-resolved efficacy has been published, neither RMC-7977 paper has a G12R arm (the KPC work is Kras G12D-driven), and the only G12R-specific daraxonrasib data is an un-peer-reviewed bioRxiv preprint. Two transfer problems that nobody has closed: eligibility required metastatic disease, which an unbiopsied pancreatic-body mass has not been shown to be, and the trial population had prior therapy for advanced disease where this patient's only exposure is perioperative. It still ranks first for me, because a doubled median OS on a pre-specified primary endpoint outranks everything else in this file even after both discounts.RoB 2, measurement of the outcome: RASolute 302 is open-label. OS survives that, but the PFS estimate (7.3 vs 3.5 months, HR 0.45) carries detection-bias risk and the abstract does not say the reads were blinded.; Calling it replicated overstates the case. RMC-6236-001 shares sponsor and senior authorship with the phase 3, so ORR 35% (95% CI 17-56) in 26 second-line RAS G12 patients is internal support rather than independent confirmation, and that CI is 39 points wide.; Disclosure: no CT.gov results posted at review, and I have only the abstract-level extraction of the NEJM paper. I have not read the full text, so I cannot honestly score the deviations-from-intended-intervention or missing-outcome-data domains.; On the allele, the correction runs both ways. PMID 41556816 and PMID 31649109 describe tumour initiation and p110alpha binding, not response to RAS(ON) inhibition, so that work does not license a downgrade of the expected effect any more than the trial licenses a G12R point estimate. What it licenses is a wider interval than the HR 0.40 implies. concensusite1moderateNo guideline names daraxonrasib yet: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (April 22, 2026) went to press before the RASolute 302 publication (mOS 13.2 vs 6.6 months, HR 0.40, P<0.001 in the RAS G12 population) and the July 2026 NDA acceptance. What the guidelines do say for a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion is switch regimens, with trial enrollment preferred, and this pick is trial-or-EAP enrollment. The FDA-authorized expanded access protocol is listed as available and RASolute 303 counts an adjuvant-only history as first-line. I expect NCCN to add this within a cycle or two of FDA action; today it rides on the trial-preferred clause, not on a listed regimen.Both the EAP and RASolute 303 require confirmed metastatic disease, and NCCN wants suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy anyway, so the unbiopsied radiographic mass keeps this patient outside every relevant population until the EUS biopsy and staging are done.; Whether adjuvant FOLFIRINOX with recurrence at 4 months satisfies the EAP's prior-line rule is a sponsor question; trial conventions mostly count it, but nothing in guideline text settles it.; As of August 2026 this sits in no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text, so no evidence category can honestly be assigned; the endorsement here is anticipatory. advocate1highThe only option in this dossier with a randomized survival win in exactly this population: OS 13.2 vs 6.7 months (HR 0.40) in previously treated RAS G12 PDAC, and the mechanism covers G12R where every allele-selective program does not. It also clears every stated preference at once: the patient wants trials and will travel, RASolute 303 is recruiting, the phase 1/2 stays open, and the FDA-authorized EAP supplies drug free of charge if no slot materializes. Oral dosing with rash and GI events as the main grade >=3 toxicities steers around the one toxicity this patient most likely already carries, the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy. Nothing else here comes close on evidence, and nothing in the preference file argues against it.Every fast route is gated on confirmed metastatic disease: the EAP and RASolute 303 both require it, so a local-only read on restaging closes both and leaves the phase 1/2 as the door.; RASolute 303 requires consent within 6 weeks of the metastatic diagnosis. The site call has to be teed up before the biopsy result lands; running the workup first and the outreach second could close this door by scheduling alone.; A G12R-specific resistance path (EGFR/RAS-WT rebound) is already described (pmid:42465401, preprint), so the post-progression plan should be drafted at the start, not at progression.; Preference fit: trials-first and travel fully satisfied; no toxicity veto in play. The 0.7 efficacy weight is an assumed default rather than the patient's number, but this pick wins under any plausible weighting.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocatequalifiedevidence_qualitySame rank 1, but 'high' confidence overshoots what pmid:42223072 can carry: the 302 population was previously treated metastatic disease, while this recurrence is unstaged with only perioperative exposure behind it, so the HR 0.40 arrives with two open transfer questions. I will also concede a correction that cuts both ways: I misread the G12R GEMM work in round 1, since pmid:41556816 speaks to tumor initiation rather than RAS(ON) response, which widens the interval around the pooled estimate instead of lowering it. A wider interval is exactly what a 'high' label cannot survive; keep the rank, drop the confidence to moderate. criticadvocatequalifiedevidence_quality'Exactly this population' plus a high confidence label sells more than the abstract contains. RASolute 302 (pmid:42223072) enrolled patients previously treated for metastatic disease; this patient's only systemic exposure is perioperative and the recurrence is unstaged, so the allele sits inside the estimand while the clinical situation does not, and 13.2 vs 6.7 months should not be quoted as this patient's expected numbers. The rank survives on my read too, since nothing else in the file has a pre-specified RCT primary endpoint, but the transfer gap plus the 39-point-wide CI on the supporting 2L ORR (35%, 95% CI 17-56, n=26, pmid:42090791) argues moderate confidence, and I say that while working from the same abstract-level extraction they are. criticconcensusitequalifiedguideline_fitThey flagged the version gap themselves, and it should be promoted from footnote to a caveat on everything: NCCN Pancreatic v2.2026 (April 22, 2026) predates the RASolute 302 publication (pmid:42223072) and a later paywalled release could not be excluded, so every guideline-silence claim in this position is a dated snapshot, and 'no guideline names daraxonrasib' means 'none did in April' until the on-file copy is checked. Riding the pick on the trial-preferred clause rather than a category number was the defensible move; the line predicting NCCN will add the drug within a cycle or two is forecast, not evidence, and should carry no weight in the ranking. The same transfer caveat lands here as on every rank 1 including mine: the trial population was previously treated metastatic disease, which this perioperative-only, unstaged recurrence has not yet been shown to be. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitEndorse, and the two gates deserve defending as guideline work rather than extra caution: NCCN wants suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy, tumor NGS for every treatment candidate (March 2026 update), and tissue in hand before trial entry, so the EUS biopsy is the pathway itself, not a delay on the way to it. On critic's line-transfer objection, the two readings answer different questions and can both hold: NCCN's under-6-months recurrence rule counts FOLFIRINOX as spent when choosing the next regimen, RASolute 303 (nct:NCT07491445) counts only metastatic-setting therapy at the door, and carrying the RASolute 302 estimate (pmid:42223072) to a less pretreated patient errs in the forgiving direction, which leaves staging rather than line arithmetic as the live gate. One update to my own round-1 caveat: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v3.2026 has now posted, superseding the v2.2026 I audited, and since I cannot open it from outside the paywall, someone with access should read it before the PI repeats 'no guideline names daraxonrasib' as current. concensusiteadvocatequalifiedguideline_fitSame rank-1, but 'high' confidence claims more than an unlisted drug can carry: no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text names daraxonrasib as of my audit (the current posting is now v3.2026, unread behind the paywall), so the pick stands on the trial-preferred clause plus a staging call nobody has made yet. The slate underneath worries me more: all five picks are trial doors, several close together on a locally-recurrent read, and the one regimen NCCN, ESMO, and ASCO all list for this sequence, gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (ESMO Express Update 2025, grade I,B; AGEO cohort pmid:26372701), appears nowhere, so a string of screen failures leaves this patient outside every guideline page at once. Credit for sending the germline panel in the notes, but a notes line ranks nothing and olaparib is absent from the slate.

docs.title: IBI343 (CLDN18.2 ADC, exatecan payload) (ibi343)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2low22.7% confirmed ORR at 6 mg/kg in previously treated PDAC selected at CLDN18.2 >=60%, which is the largest prospective dataset any CLDN18.2 agent has in this disease. The scoring rule matters here: IBI343 counts 1+ and above, so a tumor with 2+/3+ in 60% of cells almost certainly scores above 60% on their scale rather than balancing on the cutoff. An exatecan payload kills without needing T cells, which is the argument for it in an MSS, TMB 0.83 tumor where every immune approach starts uphill. Against that: the number is a conference abstract with no per-term grade >=3 table, the registrational phase 3 is mainland China only, and the US door is a phase 1 whose live cohorts skew first-line.The 22.7% figure has no peer review and no toxicity breakdown; TEAEs ran 98.8%, led by anemia and neutrophil decreases.; Marrow reserve after 10 cycles of FOLFIRINOX is undocumented and this is a myelosuppressive payload.; CLDN18.2 on the recurrence is unmeasured, and concordance losses cluster in local recurrence; with biopsy sensitivity at 54.6% a negative stain would not settle it either.; US phase 1 slots may not exist for a previously treated PDAC patient even if the biology fits. conservative3lowOf the CLDN18.2 routes, this is the one whose toxicity I can actually manage on paper: mostly hematologic (grade >=3 TRAEs 52.6% in the gastric phase 1, led by neutropenia at 28.4%), TRAE discontinuation 0.9%, no ILD, and no grade >=3 nausea or vomiting. The PDAC expansion, 44 patients at 6 mg/kg with CLDN18.2 >=60%, read out ORR 22.7% and mOS 9.1 months, which clears the AGEO benchmark without touching the neuropathy problem, and the phase 1 (NCT05458219) is recruiting at US sites. Compare satri-cel: 99% grade >=3 TEAEs, near-universal CRS, a gastric mucosal injury the mouse work never predicted, and no reachable access route anyway. Rank 3 rather than higher because the PDAC data are a conference abstract with no per-term grade >=3 table, and 60% sits exactly on the eligibility boundary under a different scoring convention than the resection report used.Per-term grade >=3 rates for the PDAC cohort are unpublished; the safety picture borrows from the gastric cohort.; Expression needs a fresh read on recurrent tissue: the trial tiers 1+/2+/3+ at >=60% while the resection was called 2+/3+ in 60%, and the recurrence has never been stained.; An exatecan payload lands after 10 cycles of irinotecan-containing FOLFIRINOX; topoisomerase-1 cross-resistance in that sequence is an open question with no published answer. critic2lowThe 44-patient dose-expansion cohort is the largest prospective CLDN18.2 efficacy dataset in previously treated PDAC, and it is a single-arm phase 1 reported in an ASCO abstract with no CI on the 22.7% confirmed ORR and no per-term grade >=3 table. Its mOS of 9.1 months does not separate from the 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7) that a plain gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel class switch produced after FOLFIRINOX failure in the AGEO cohort (cross-study comparison, but somebody should say it before 22.7% gets called impressive). The mOS 12.1 in the 17 patients with one prior line is an unadjusted subgroup at n=17 and I would not plan around it. Second because the randomized trial that would settle this is actually running and the phase 1 has US sites open, not because the current number has persuaded me.Indirectness on the biomarker: the efficacy cohort was defined as CLDN18.2 1+/2+/3+ in >=60% of cells, pooled across intensities. This patient's report says 2+/3+ in 60% from a clone the report never names, so 'clears the cutoff' is an assumption rather than a match.; Archival tissue is doing the selecting. Recurrent lesions matched the primary in 83.3% of cases and the losses clustered in local recurrence and liver metastases (PMID 40694660), so roughly one in six risk of target loss is weighted against exactly this presentation.; GLEAM (n=393) missed OS at 13.7 vs 13.6 months in >=75% expressers and exists only as a topline release with nothing posted on CT.gov. It bears most directly on a naked antibody rather than on an exatecan payload, but it is the only randomized CLDN18.2 readout in PDAC and it cannot be audited by anyone outside the sponsor.; Kerper (PMID 42080920) found positivity less common in neoadjuvant-treated resections. Cross-sectional, so it cannot separate treatment-induced antigen loss from selection, and this tumour has since taken four more cycles. concensusite3lowCLDN18.2 in pancreatic cancer is guideline-silent territory, and I want that on the record: NCCN's CLDN18.2 text lives in Gastric Cancer v3.2026 at the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff, and the PDAC trial guidelines would have weighed (GLEAM) missed its OS endpoint. Where guidelines are silent their own default is a trial, and IBI343 carries the most prospective data in treated PDAC of any CLDN18.2 agent (confirmed ORR 22.7%, mOS 9.1 months at >=60% expression, the boundary this tumor sits on) plus a randomized phase 3 already enrolling. That phase 3 is China-only, so the realistic US door is the phase 1 PDAC cohort.The 60% 2+/3+ call is archival, from the December 2025 resection, on an unstated assay; the sponsor's central IHC on recurrence tissue could land either side of its cohort threshold.; The PDAC efficacy data are a single-arm conference abstract, and no guideline framework will exist for any of this until the phase 3 reads out.; Zolbetuximab is not a fallback: this tumor fails the 75% CDx cutoff and GLEAM was negative even above it, so off-label use has neither an eligibility nor an efficacy basis. advocate2moderateThe best-evidenced CLDN18.2 route this patient can actually reach: ORR 22.7% in previously treated PDAC (n=83), the largest prospective dataset for this target in this disease, with the phase 1 recruiting at US and Australia sites. CLDN18.2 at 2+/3+ in 60% of cells is the strongest handle the user asked us to work, and a topoisomerase-payload ADC does not lean on the checkpoint biology this MSS, TMB-low tumor lacks. The honest caveats: the registrational phase 3 is mainland-China only, so US access rides on phase 1/2 cohorts, and whether a 60% archival result clears the cohort's expression tier needs sponsor confirmation before anyone books travel.Cohort expression thresholds are sponsor-defined and the dose-optimization cohorts prefer moderate-to-high expressers; where 60% 2+/3+ lands is unconfirmed.; The stain is from the pre-adjuvant primary. Biopsy sensitivity for CLDN18.2 runs around 54.6% (pmid:40694660), so a negative stain on a small recurrence specimen should not be read as loss of the target.; GLEAM's negative zolbetuximab result in PDAC tempers the antibody class; the ADC mechanism differs, but expectations should carry that context.; Preference fit: trial route, US-reachable, no veto or modality conflict. Fully inside the stated preferences.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconcensusitequalifiedevidence_qualityOn your rank 3, the boundary framing needs one correction: cells scored 2+/3+ also count at the 1+ tier, so 60% at 2+/3+ on the same block cannot fall below the cohort's 1+/2+/3+ >=60% line (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.4017), and the live risk is a different assay on a never-stained recurrence, not the arithmetic. Where I give ground is the benchmark, because the cohort's mOS 9.1 sits on top of AGEO's 8.8 (pmid:26372701) and nobody should call that separation. What is left is the 22.7% confirmed ORR with 81.8% DCR in expression-selected disease, a real tail for a trials-first patient and thin grounds for ranking it below a chemotherapy class switch. criticrisktakerqualifiedevidence_qualityThe claim that 2+/3+ in 60% 'almost certainly' clears the 1+-pooled >=60% cutoff is arithmetic done inside the archival report: on that slide it holds by definition, but eligibility gets called on the sponsor's central assay, probably on recurrence tissue nobody has stained, with an unnamed local clone doing the conversion. Primary-to-recurrence concordance runs 83.3% and the losses cluster in local recurrence (pmid:40694660), so a value sitting exactly on the boundary has real mass on the failing side; advocate's confirm-with-the-sponsor version is closer to right. Separately, before 22.7% carries the pick, the same abstract's mOS of 9.1 months sits inside AGEO's 8.8 (95% CI 6.2-9.7, pmid:26372701) for a plain chemotherapy switch, so the ADC has not yet shown it beats the class-switch floor it would displace (doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.4017).

docs.title: olaparib maintenance, germline BRCA-mutated mPDAC (gated on pending germline panel) (olaparib-maintenance)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative4lowThis pick exists mostly to keep the germline panel from slipping: guidelines call for dedicated germline testing in every PDAC patient, and the incidental tumor-NGS reporting here does not rule out BRCA1/2 or PALB2. If the panel returns positive and a platinum-containing regimen then holds the disease for >=16 weeks, POLO's maintenance route opens, and it is the best-characterized targeted option in this file: FDA-approved since 2019, grade >=3 AEs 40% vs 23% on placebo, 5% discontinuation, no new signals at the final analysis. The honest framing is chemotherapy-free time rather than survival; final OS was 19.0 vs 19.2 months. Low probability, deep familiarity.Inert until a germline panel is drawn; that blood draw should happen this week regardless of what the board picks.; Recurrence 4 months after oxaliplatin-containing adjuvant therapy argues against platinum sensitivity, which also lowers the prior on an unexpected gBRCA hit.; The maintenance route presumes a platinum re-challenge the rest of this dossier argues against. critic——did not pick— concensusite4lowThis pick is really about the test behind it. NCCN has recommended germline testing for every confirmed pancreatic cancer patient since 2019, and it has not been done here; 'no incidental findings' on tumor NGS is not a germline panel. A positive BRCA1/2 result opens the POLO maintenance route (PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.53), the only biomarker-directed option in this disease with a randomized base and an FDA label. The panel is a blood draw orderable this week, and it gates a whole branch of the dossier.Even with a positive panel this patient sits outside the POLO population: POLO required at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression, and this tumor progressed about 4 months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy, so a platinum re-response would have to be demonstrated first.; Pre-test probability is low; roughly 5-7% of unselected PDAC carries a germline BRCA1/2 variant.; POLO's final OS was null (19.0 vs 19.2 months), so the honest framing even in a carrier is chemotherapy-free time, not survival gain. advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: ASP2138 (CLDN18.2 x CD3 2+1 bispecific T-cell engager) (asp2138)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowThe >=1+ central IHC gate is the easiest CLDN18.2 door in this dossier for a 2+/3+ 60% tumor, there is a dedicated metastatic PDAC cohort across 46 sites, and archival tissue may start the screen while the biopsy is still being scheduled. Engagers can produce deep responses when they connect, and that ceiling is the reason to take a phase 1 that has published no PDAC efficacy at all. What exists is a 41.7% 12-week unconfirmed DCR in gastric, with CRS at 23.4% in the PDAC cohort and no grade >=3 gastritis on monotherapy. My real worry is mechanistic rather than regulatory: across syngeneic models, pretreatment intratumoral T-cell density drove BiTE response, and PDAC is exactly where that density bottoms out.No PDAC efficacy readout has been shown; the 41.7% DCR is gastric and unconfirmed.; Monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable disease, so a non-metastatic staging call closes this too.; On-target gastric mucosal injury and CRS in a patient whose upper GI anatomy is already surgically altered.; Source is a congress abstract whose identifiers could not be verified against Crossref. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate3lowThe widest-open CLDN18.2 door: the PDAC monotherapy arm takes patients with no line limit, the >=1+ escalation cutoff sits far below this tumor's 60% at 2+/3+, and 46 sites across the US, Japan, Europe, and Asia suit a patient who said travel is fine. The efficacy shown so far is gastric and abstract-level (12-week DCR 41.7% at >=420 ug) with the PDAC readout still pending, so this is an access-and-fit pick rather than an evidence pick, and the patient deserves that distinction stated plainly.No PDAC efficacy data exist yet for this drug; ranking it above better-published options would be selling hope, which is why it sits third.; CD3-engager class toxicity (CRS) has no published PDAC-specific characterization here.; Monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable patients, so the staging read decides which arms are even open.; Preference fit: clean on every stated axis; the only friction is the ungraded neuropathy, which several protocols cap at grade 1 and which must be graded before screening anywhere.

docs.title: JAB-30355 (oral p53 Y220C reactivator) (jab-30355)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowWith PYNNACLE's registrational monotherapy cohort excluding known KRAS SNVs, this is the Y220C door that stays open, US sites recruiting and no KRAS exclusion posted. I am ranking an eligibility fact, not an effect size. The public record is one sponsor sentence about a positive efficacy signal at high dose, and nothing has been published since. Mechanistically I expect less than the target promises, since restoring p53 in KRAS-driven tumors with low mitochondrial priming produces cell-cycle arrest rather than apoptosis, and every rezatapopt phase 1 responder was KRAS wild-type. Still worth the screening call, because ECOG 0 travels well in dose escalation and the variant is the one this chemistry was built around.Zero published effect size: no paper, no abstract, no posted results, so there is no toxicity profile to weigh either.; The KRAS co-mutation that keeps rezatapopt's responders wild-type is the same one this patient carries.; Needs confirmation that Y220C persists in the recurrence; ctDNA would answer that without a needle.; Dose escalation can assign a subtherapeutic dose, and this class already showed secondary TP53 alterations in cis with Y220C at progression. conservative——did not pick— critic4lowY220C is a real variant with a real drug class, and this patient can reach neither of the things that have data behind them. The registrational rezatapopt monotherapy cohort excludes any known KRAS SNV, and in the published phase 1 (n=77) every responder was KRAS wild-type: ORR 30% in KRAS-WT at >=1150 mg against 20% overall. JAB-30355's whole efficacy record is one sponsor phrase about a signal at high dose, with nothing published and nothing posted, so ranking it says something about an open door and nothing about evidence. Fourth, and it does not move up until a number with an n attached exists.There is no published effect size for any Y220C reactivator in a KRAS-mutant tumour, in any indication. The phase 1 report as extracted does not give the KRAS-mutant denominator, so zero responders among them is weak evidence of no effect rather than proof of none, and I am reading the abstract, not the full paper.; Sponsor-only disclosure with no independent analysis and no registry results is the reporting-bias scenario in its purest form. NTS071 (NCT07060989) is thinner still, with no source of any kind.; Even granting target engagement, the Sanchez-Rivera work (PMID 34074758) argues a KRAS-driven, low-priming tumour may arrest rather than die when p53 function returns. Mouse lung and sarcoma lines, so I am not weighting it heavily, but it points the same way as the clinical responder pattern.; Resistance to this class is on-target and heterogeneous (PMID 41504628), so a second-generation reactivator likely inherits much of it. concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowThe user asked for every variant kept on the table, and this is what the TP53 Y220C axis actually offers: rezatapopt's registrational monotherapy cohort excludes any KRAS SNV, so G12R blocks the flagship, and JAB-30355 is the US-recruiting reactivator with no posted KRAS exclusion. Its entire efficacy record is one sponsor phrase, 'positive efficacy signal', with nothing published as of August 2026. I rank it because the preference file says trials first and this keeps a second biological axis live, not because anyone should expect a known effect size.Zero published effect sizes; even rezatapopt's phase 1 responders were exclusively KRAS wild-type, so reactivator benefit in a KRAS-co-mutated tumor is unproven at best.; The registry posts no KRAS exclusion but the full protocol might; confirm with the sponsor before any screening trip.; Needs Y220C persistence confirmed in the recurrence (ctDNA acceptable) plus a baseline echo, since LVEF <=50% excludes.; Preference fit: satisfies trials-first and the user's keep-every-variant instruction; NTS071 (nct:NCT07060989) gives this axis redundancy if this door narrows.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativeadvocatedissenttoxicityRank 1 we agree on; rank 5 is the problem. JAB-30355 has no published AE table at any dose and no posted results, one sponsor sentence total (nct:NCT06386146), where rezatapopt at least brought a phase 1 safety profile to the table (pmid:41740031), and this patient's renal, hepatic, and marrow function has not been measured since resection, so neither side of the risk equation has a number. Make the screening call, by all means; the ranked slot is what I dissent from, and any per-dose safety readout with an n attached would move me. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitI share the rank-1 call, so this aims at rank 4 instead. JAB-30355 (nct:NCT06386146) appears in no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text and its efficacy record is one sponsor sentence, which makes the rank an open door and nothing more; meanwhile this is the only position on the board that never mentions the germline panel, an NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma requirement for every confirmed PDAC patient since 2019 and the gate on the one FDA-labeled option in this file with a randomized base (POLO, pmid:31157963). A zero-data trial slot outranking an unmet guideline mandate is a compliance gap, not a difference in taste.

docs.title: mKRASvax + balstilimab + botensilimab (mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade) (mkrasvax)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowG12R is in the peptide pool, the mandatory ECOG 0 is a criterion this patient actually holds, and the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 partner has produced responses in MSS disease where single-agent PD-1 blockade does nothing. AMPLIFY-201 proved G12R-specific CD4 and CD8 immunity can be raised in PDAC patients, though its HR 0.12 for RFS is a T-cell-threshold split inside a single-arm MRD trial, not a treatment effect. That MRD framing is the catch: a radiographic pancreatic mass is not minimal residual disease, and vaccines rarely shrink bulk pancreatic tumors. I would keep the Hopkins coordinator conversation warm as a post-cytoreduction move rather than pretend it competes with daraxonrasib now.Single US site in Baltimore, and the posted prior-therapy clause wants 4 to 6 months of first-line therapy for metastatic disease, which perioperative FOLFIRINOX may not satisfy.; On-treatment biopsy requirement runs into the vascular invasion around the recurrent mass.; No efficacy data for this construct in PDAC; the supporting HR comes from a different vaccine in a different disease state.; Dual checkpoint blockade brings immune-related toxicity in a patient whose organ function is entirely undocumented. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativerisktakerdissenttoxicityWe share the rank 1, so my dissent lands on rank 5: Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 plus PD-1 blockade in a patient with no post-resection labs means the irAE downside has no number on either side, drug or host. The supporting HR 0.12 is a T-cell-threshold split inside a different vaccine's single-arm MRD trial (pmid:38270373), and this patient has a radiographic mass with vascular invasion, not minimal residual disease. The risktaker's own notes say to keep the Hopkins conversation warm rather than pretend it competes now (nct:NCT06411691); hold to that and give the slot back. advocaterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitOur top four barely differ, so I am aiming at rank 5: the posted prior-therapy clause wants 4 to 6 months of first-line treatment for metastatic disease, her only exposure is perioperative, and the on-treatment biopsy runs into the vascular invasion you flagged yourself (nct:NCT06411691), so a rank tells her Baltimore is reachable while your own notes call it a warm phone line to keep for later. Nowhere in your row does the germline panel get sent, and that blood draw gates the one FDA-labeled biomarker route in this disease (pmid:31157963); NCCN has asked for it in every PDAC patient since 2019, so skipping it is a dropped ask, not triage. Your qualified on my daraxonrasib confidence lands, and I will take it: moderate is the honest label for an unstaged recurrence with perioperative-only exposure.

docs.title: ASP5834 (IV pan-KRAS inhibitor), phase 1 NCT07094204 (asp5834)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowInsurance for the scenario where daraxonrasib's doors fail on staging: this phase 1 names G12R explicitly, writes down the exact line-counting rule this recurrence satisfies (adjuvant therapy with recurrence inside 6 months counts as the prior line), and takes locally advanced unresectable disease as well as metastatic. docs.title: satri-cel (CT041, autologous CLDN18.2 CAR-T) (satri-cel)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic3lowCT041-ST-01 is the only randomized win anywhere in the CLDN18.2 class: n=156, mPFS 3.25 vs 1.77 months, HR 0.37 (0.24-0.56), P<0.0001. It is gastric, open-label, PFS-primary, and the absolute gain is about six weeks against a physician's-choice arm, with grade >=3 TEAEs in 87 of 88 treated patients. The PDAC record is a two-patient research letter, one of whom stained 3+ in 60%, which is an expression match and not an effect estimate. Third on strength of design alone; the North American study is closed to enrolment, so this is a sponsor question rather than a plan.Open-label design with an active-comparator physician's-choice arm and PFS as the registrational endpoint is the combination most exposed to assessment bias under RoB 2. OS was not what the trial was built to prove.; Cross-tumor extrapolation carries the entire argument. PDAC is desmoplastic and T-cell poor, and the construct's preclinical package (PMID 30203099) is gastric xenograft work whose clean mouse safety did not predict the gastric mucosal injury patients later had.; Toxicity is not a footnote at 99% grade >=3 and CRS in 95%, on top of modelled on-target gastric injury (PMID 41176533), in a patient whose post-resection upper-GI anatomy is nowhere in the record.; The single-arm base (PMID 38830992, n=98) reports mOS 8.8 months across GI cancers, which is the same neighbourhood as a chemotherapy class switch. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticdissentotherI went after your rank 3 because that is the real split between us; our lists barely differ elsewhere. The access row is unambiguous: the North American trial (nct:NCT04404595) is active-not-recruiting, the approval is dispensed only in mainland China, and no named-patient route exists, so 'third on strength of design alone' ranks a door with no handle. I wanted satri-cel's ceiling badly enough to put the CARsgen email in my notes and still kept it out of the ranking, because a rank should be something a coordinator can act on this month. conservativecriticdissenttoxicityThe critic's line-of-therapy catch on our shared rank 1 is fair and binds my row too, which is why the restaging gate stays; the dissent here is rank 3. Satri-cel's randomized safety read is grade >=3 TEAEs in 87 of 88 treated patients with CRS in 95% (pmid:40460847), the preclinical package missed the gastric mucosal injury patients later showed (pmid:30203099), and the one US study is closed to enrollment (nct:NCT04404595), so a ranked slot hands the PI a regimen with the worst tolerability numbers in the file and no door to reach it through. A two-patient expression match is worth a sponsor email, which the critic's own row concedes is all this is; the notes column is where it belongs. advocatecriticdissentpreference_fitTo a patient who said trials are welcome and travel is fine, a rank in this table reads as a door someone can call, and satri-cel has no door: the North American study stopped enrolling (nct:NCT04404595), the label is gastric and dispensed only in mainland China, and the only published contact is a PR inbox, which you yourself filed under sponsor question rather than plan. Design strength belongs in the evidence discussion, not the ranking; put the CARsgen email in notes, where risktaker and I both left it. Your IBI343 objection scores a half-hit on me: the pooled-tier arithmetic actually favors her, since 60% at 2+/3+ cannot score below 60% at >=1+ on the same block, but the unnamed clone and the never-stained recurrence are real gaps, which is why my rank 2 already gates any travel on sponsor confirmation and a re-stain. concensusitecriticdissentguideline_fitThis targets rank 3, not the rank-1 we agree on, because rank 3 is where guideline silence gets misread. Silence on CLDN18.2 in PDAC (NCCN's only CLDN18.2 text sits in Gastric Cancer v3.2026, at the 75% zolbetuximab cutoff) does not forbid working the target; it routes you to a trial, which is what makes IBI343 via nct:NCT05458219 defensible and satri-cel not, since nct:NCT04404595 is closed to enrollment and the NMPA label is gastric, dispensed only in China. A rank turns CT041-ST-01's design strength (pmid:40460847) into a recommendation with no reachable route, and risktaker and advocate read the same two-patient PDAC letter and correctly left it in their notes.

Reduced collagen in human G12R tumors cuts against the desmoplastic-barrier story for this allele, but that part is an association in tissue, not an intervention. docs.title: Chemosensitivity is agent-specific in PDAC organoids (bearing on FOLFIRINOX-to-gemcitabine cross-resistance)

docs.title: What this page is
docs.text:
Libby searched published studies and open clinical trials for treatments aimed at the specific features of your cancer, the ones you told us about. This page walks through what came back: one first step, five treatment options worth discussing with your care team, two options you may have heard of that are on the page as not recommended, and one that fits your tumor well but cannot be reached right now. Where the research has real numbers, we give them in plain terms. Where it does not, we say so instead of dressing anything up.

One thing to be honest about at the start. A recurrence about four months after finishing chemotherapy is a serious situation, and this page does not pretend otherwise. It also does not mean there is nothing to do. There are real options here, and there is one clear next step.

docs.title: What we know about your cancer
docs.text:
You have pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the most common form of pancreatic cancer. You went through a long and hard course of treatment: six cycles of chemotherapy (mFOLFIRINOX) that shrank the tumor, then surgery in December 2025 that removed it completely with all 34 lymph nodes clean, then four more cycles of chemotherapy afterward, finished as planned. That is ten cycles of chemotherapy in total. In July 2026 a new mass appeared in the body of the pancreas on a scan, sitting close to blood vessels. It has not yet been biopsied.

Testing on the tumor removed in December found several things worth knowing:

  • CLDN18.2. About 60% of the tumor cells carried a surface protein called claudin 18.2, at moderate-to-strong levels. Several experimental treatments are built to home in on this protein, so this is a genuine asset. It comes with a catch we explain under Option 6.
  • KRAS G12R. A change in a gene called KRAS, of a specific type called G12R. KRAS is the engine driving most pancreatic cancers, and a new class of drugs now targets it directly.
  • TP53 Y220C. A change in a gene called TP53. There are early-stage drugs aimed at this exact change, though, as it turns out, they tend not to work well when KRAS is also mutated. They are not among the options below for that reason.
  • MSI-negative, low mutation count. Two markers that predict whether standard immunotherapy will help. Yours predict it will not. That closes one door, and it is addressed head-on under Option 7.

One fact shapes this whole page: every one of those results comes from the tumor removed in December 2025, not from the new mass. Ten cycles of chemotherapy happened in between, and cancers can change under that pressure. The new mass has not been sampled or tested at all yet.

A recurrence this soon after chemotherapy, despite a clean surgery, tells us the cancer did not stay sensitive to the chemotherapy you received. That is part of why the options on this page look beyond simply running the same regimen again.

docs.title: What you told us matters most
docs.text:
You said clinical trials are welcome, including ones that require travel, and you set no geographic limit. You named no side effects you refuse to accept and ruled out no type of treatment. The options below reflect that: most of them are trials, and the list leans toward effectiveness over gentleness. One note: we assumed you would weight effectiveness more heavily than side effects, because you did not say otherwise. That was our default, not your words, and it is worth revisiting with your team.

One practical flag. After ten cycles of oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy, most people carry some lingering numbness or tingling in the hands and feet. Yours has never been formally graded, and several trials will not enroll people whose numbness is above a certain level. Getting it graded is quick and matters more than it sounds.

docs.title: The first step everyone agreed on
docs.text:
Before any treatment decision, the new mass needs a biopsy, along with updated scans, a fresh stain for CLDN18.2, and new genetic sequencing. This can feel like a delay when the instinct is to start treatment now. It is not stalling. It is the step that makes everything else possible.

Here is why. Every test result on file describes a tumor that no longer exists, removed from your body eight months ago, before four more cycles of chemotherapy. The biopsy answers four questions at once: whether the new mass really is the pancreatic cancer coming back, whether it has spread beyond the pancreas or stayed local, whether the KRAS and TP53 changes are still there, and how much CLDN18.2 the current tumor carries. Nearly every trial on this page requires this information before you can enroll, and one tissue sample can feed all four tests.

The biopsy itself is done with a thin needle guided by an internal ultrasound. Its risks are modest, mainly bleeding and a small chance of pancreas inflammation afterward, and the blood vessels near the mass may shape how your doctors approach it. If it turns out the mass cannot be sampled safely, a blood test that picks up tumor DNA in the bloodstream can answer some of the same questions.

One caution about reading the CLDN18.2 result when it comes: on a small needle sample, the stain misses the protein about half the time when it is really there. So a positive result settles the question, but a negative result does not prove the protein is gone, and it should not close that door by itself.

There is a clock, and it runs the opposite way from what most people expect. The leading trial for the top-ranked drug below only accepts patients within six weeks of a diagnosis of metastatic disease, meaning cancer that has spread. That window starts when the scans and biopsy make the call, not when you feel ready. So the phone call to the trial site should happen before the biopsy result comes back, not after, so that everything is teed up if the answer opens that door. And starting chemotherapy first can quietly shut it, because it changes which trial groups you fit into. If chemotherapy is on the table, ask the specific question: will this dose close any trial doors? This is probably the single most useful practical fact on this page.

Two more things ride alongside and need no tissue at all, just blood. First, a dedicated germline genetic test, explained under Option 4. It is the cheapest, highest-value item on this list, and guidelines recommend it for every person with pancreatic cancer. Second, the formal grading of your leftover numbness. Both can be ordered this week.

And the flip side: if the biopsy shows something other than recurrent pancreatic cancer carrying these features, the treatment options below come off the table. Libby's rankings only cover treatments aimed at the specific targets you told us about, so in that situation there would be nothing further ranked on this page. Standard care for pancreatic cancer would still exist and would still be worth pursuing, but that is a separate conversation that belongs to your oncologist, not to this page.

docs.title: Option 1 — Daraxonrasib (a pill that targets KRAS)
docs.text:
Only on the table if the biopsy confirms the cancer is back and still carries the KRAS change.

This is the lead option, and the best-evidenced one. Daraxonrasib is a daily pill that switches off the mutated KRAS protein driving the cancer, including your G12R type, which older KRAS drugs could not touch.

It is the only option on this page backed by a large randomized trial in pancreatic cancer. In that trial, 500 people whose pancreatic cancer had spread and grown despite chemotherapy were assigned to either daraxonrasib or more chemotherapy. Among those with KRAS changes like yours, half of the people on daraxonrasib lived longer than 13 months; among those on chemotherapy, half died within about six and a half months. The drug also held the cancer still for about twice as long. In a smaller earlier study, about one in three people saw their tumors shrink.

Now the honest part, because those numbers are not automatically your numbers. The trial studied people whose cancer had already spread and who had been treated after it spread. Your situation is different: your chemotherapy came before and after surgery, and whether the new mass has spread is exactly what the biopsy and scans will determine. Also, your specific G12R type was studied inside a larger group of KRAS changes, never on its own. The direction of the result is solid. How big the benefit would be for you specifically is genuinely uncertain, and I can't give you a precise number there without data that does not yet exist.

Side effects are real: mostly rash and gut trouble (diarrhea, nausea, mouth sores). About six in ten people on the trial had at least one severe side effect, though that was actually fewer than on the chemotherapy arm, and only about one person in a hundred had to stop the drug because of side effects. The drug is new; the first person ever to take it did so in 2022, so nobody knows what year four looks like. And because you have had pancreatic surgery, it is worth asking whether pill absorption could be an issue for you.

There are three ways to get it, and they close in different ways. The big trial has the six-week clock described above and requires that the cancer has spread. There is also an FDA-authorized expanded-access program: your oncologist requests the drug from the company, it is supplied free of charge, and you take it under a monitored protocol rather than as improvisation. That route also requires confirmed spread. A third, earlier-phase study does not hinge on that call. One sequencing note worth raising with your team: several other KRAS trials only take people who have never had a KRAS drug, so starting daraxonrasib closes those doors. That is not a reason to wait. It is a reason to plan.

docs.title: Option 2 — IBI343 (an antibody that delivers chemotherapy to CLDN18.2 cells)
docs.text:
Only on the table if the biopsy confirms the recurrence, and the trial will re-test CLDN18.2 with its own assay.

This is recommended as the strongest of the CLDN18.2 routes you can actually reach. IBI343 is an antibody-drug conjugate: an antibody finds cells carrying CLDN18.2 and delivers a chemotherapy payload directly to them, sparing more of the rest of the body. The study behind it enrolled pancreatic cancer patients whose tumors carried CLDN18.2 in at least 60% of cells, which is exactly where your December result sits, though the trial's own lab will make the final call on fresh tissue.

The evidence is early: one study without a comparison group, reported so far only as a conference summary. In it, about one in five patients saw their tumors shrink, and most saw the cancer at least held in place for a time. Half of patients lived longer than about nine months. Here is the context that number needs: after this kind of chemotherapy stops working, switching to a different standard chemotherapy gives people a broadly similar amount of time. So this drug has not yet shown it beats the ordinary next move. It may earn that; it has not yet.

The main side effects are drops in blood counts, which about half of patients experienced at a severe level in the related stomach-cancer study. After ten cycles of chemotherapy, how much reserve your bone marrow has left is an open question your team should look at first. One more open question worth asking the sponsor: the payload is a cousin of irinotecan, a drug you have already had ten cycles of, and nobody has published whether prior irinotecan blunts it. The trial has sites in the US and Australia.

docs.title: Option 3 — ASP2138 (a drug that drags immune cells onto CLDN18.2 cells)
docs.text:
Only on the table if the biopsy confirms the recurrence. Some parts of this trial also require that the cancer has spread rather than stayed local.

This option carries caveats. It is an early study of a "T-cell engager," a molecule with two hands: one grabs the CLDN18.2 protein on cancer cells, the other grabs your own immune cells and forces the two together. It is on the page because the door is unusually wide open, not because the evidence is strong: the trial's CLDN18.2 entry bar is low and your tumor clears it several times over, it runs at dozens of sites including many in the US, and your stored tissue from surgery may be enough to start the screening process while the biopsy is being scheduled.

The evidence side is the thinnest of the recommended-or-caveated options above this line. There are no effectiveness results in pancreatic cancer at all yet; the pancreatic patients treated so far have only contributed safety information. In stomach cancer, the drug held disease in place at twelve weeks in about four in ten patients, and that is a soft, early way to measure benefit. There is also a biological concern to weigh: this drug needs immune cells already inside the tumor to do its work, and pancreatic tumors are notoriously poor in them. That is the open question hanging over this whole drug class in this disease.

The characteristic side effect is cytokine release syndrome, an immune overreaction with fever and low blood pressure, seen in about one in four pancreatic patients in the study so far, mostly mild and managed in experienced centers.

docs.title: Option 4 — Olaparib, only if a germline blood test comes back positive
docs.text:
This option carries caveats, and it is really about the test behind it. Olaparib is a pill approved for pancreatic cancers in people who carry an inherited change in the BRCA genes. Whether you carry one has never actually been checked. The line on your tumor report saying no incidental germline findings came from a tumor test, which is not designed to answer that question and can miss real inherited changes. A proper germline test is a simple blood draw, guidelines have recommended it for every person with pancreatic cancer since 2019, and it can be ordered this week without waiting for anything else.

Straight odds: roughly five to seven people in a hundred with pancreatic cancer carry such a change, and the fast return of your cancer after platinum chemotherapy makes a positive result somewhat less likely still. So this is a long shot. But the test is cheap, the result also matters to your blood relatives, and a positive would open an entire treatment class with an FDA label behind it, which nothing else on this page has.

If the test is positive, here is what olaparib actually offers: in its main trial, taken as maintenance after chemotherapy had the cancer under control, it roughly doubled the time before the cancer started growing again (about seven and a half months versus about four), but people did not live longer overall. What it buys is time off chemotherapy, not proven extra survival, with its own side effects (mainly anemia, fatigue, and nausea, severe in about four in ten people). Your team would also have to think through the fact that this strategy assumes another round of platinum chemotherapy works first, which your recurrence timing puts in doubt. If the test is negative, this option simply comes off the table, and nothing else on the page changes.

docs.title: Option 5 — ASP5834 (an intravenous KRAS drug in its first human trial)
docs.text:
Only on the table if the biopsy confirms the recurrence.

This option carries caveats: it has no published results of any kind. Not on effectiveness, not on side effects. It is a brand-new pan-KRAS drug, given by vein, in its very first human study, where early participants may receive doses too low to work because finding the dose is the study's purpose.

So why is it here at all? Insurance. The two main routes to daraxonrasib require that the cancer has spread. If your scans instead show the cancer has come back only locally, those routes close on the same day, and this trial is the KRAS-targeting door that stays open: it accepts locally recurrent disease, it names your exact G12R type in its entry criteria, and its rules explicitly count a history like yours (chemotherapy around surgery, recurrence within six months) as qualifying. Being given by vein also sidesteps the pill-absorption question after your surgery. Think of it as the backup to have already scoped out on the day the staging result arrives, not as a rival to Option 1.

docs.title: Option 6 — Zolbetuximab, used off-label
docs.text:
This option was considered but not recommended. It's on the page because Libby surfaces what was weighed and rejected, not just what was kept, and because this is a drug a US oncologist could legally prescribe tomorrow, so you may well hear about it. It is the one approved CLDN18.2 drug, and the approval is for stomach cancer.

There are two independent reasons to pass. First, the approval requires strong CLDN18.2 staining in at least 75% of tumor cells, and your December result was 60%. Second, and more decisive: the drug was tested head-to-head in a randomized trial in pancreatic cancer, added to chemotherapy, and it added nothing. People lived essentially the same length of time with it or without it. Paying for an off-label drug, with its substantial side effects, against a flat randomized result in exactly your disease is a poor trade.

One thing this should not do is discourage you about CLDN18.2 itself. Being under the cutoff for this one drug is not the same as being negative. Your 60% is above the entry bar for Options 2 and 3 and for the out-of-reach option below. The marker is still an asset; this particular drug is just the wrong way to use it.

docs.title: Option 7 — Single-agent immunotherapy (pembrolizumab and similar drugs)
docs.text:
This option was considered but not recommended. Checkpoint immunotherapy drugs have transformed some cancers, and it is natural to ask about them. For these drugs to work on their own, a tumor generally needs one of two features: a repair defect called MSI-high, or a very large number of mutations for the immune system to recognize. Your tumor was tested for both. It has neither: it is MSI-negative, and its mutation count is very low, roughly a twelfth of the level where these drugs are approved. These are not borderline results.

Given that, single-agent immunotherapy would carry its real risks of immune side effects with essentially no realistic chance of benefit. This is not a judgment about immune approaches in general. Treatments that force an immune attack rather than waiting for one, like the engager in Option 3, remain on the table. It is specifically the checkpoint-drug-alone route that your tumor's own test results close.

docs.title: One option that fits well and is out of reach
docs.text:
There is one more thing you deserve to know about, even though nobody can act on it today. A treatment in early testing attaches a radioactive particle to a molecule that homes in on CLDN18.2. What makes it interesting for you specifically: the radiation kills not only the cell it lands on but its close neighbors too, so it matters much less that only 60% of your tumor cells carry the protein. On paper, this mechanism matches your tumor's staining pattern better than anything else Libby found, and your level clears the study's entry bar three times over.

The hard part is access. The only human studies are small, single-hospital trials in China, and studies of that kind have no mechanism for enrolling patients from abroad, however willing to travel you are. Right now there is no US or European program in this class at all. That can change, sometimes quickly. It is worth asking your team to keep a registry alert on this class, because a US trial opening would make this option real.

docs.title: Questions to ask your oncologist
docs.text:
1. Can we schedule the biopsy of the new mass now, and can one procedure collect enough tissue for the CLDN18.2 re-stain, the genetic sequencing, and trial screening all at once?
  2. Can we contact the daraxonrasib trial site and the expanded-access program before the biopsy result is back, so the six-week enrollment window does not close while we wait?
  3. If you are considering starting chemotherapy first, would that dose make me ineligible for the daraxonrasib trial or any other trial on this list?
  4. Can you order the dedicated germline genetic blood test this week, and formally grade the numbness in my hands and feet, since trials screen on both?
  5. If the biopsy shows something other than recurrent pancreatic cancer, or shows the markers have changed, what is our plan then?
  6. If the scans say the cancer is locally recurrent rather than spread, which options close, and can we have the ASP5834 trial screened as the backup before that answer arrives?
  7. For the CLDN18.2 trials, will the sponsors accept my stored surgical tissue to start screening, and where does my staining level land against each trial's own cutoff?
  8. If I start daraxonrasib, what is the plan for monitoring and managing rash and gut side effects, and what would we reach for when it eventually stops working?

Reading the columns

These are candidate ideas that are earlier than clinical development, or not yet developed at all. Stage is how far the candidate has progressed (conceptual through IND-enabling). Evidence strength is the qualitative weight of the preclinical support. Counter-productive MoA is the mechanism-level risk that the candidate's own pathway could blunt its therapeutic goal. None of these options is enrollable today; they are a horizon scan, not the ranked clinical recommendations on the Recommendations table.

Decision support, not medical advice

Libby is experimental. These are early-stage research directions, not treatment recommendations, and have not been reviewed by a clinician treating this patient. See PHI policy.

docs.text: The treatment strategies that are standard for this patient's situation, meaning a regulator approved them for a population that includes this patient or a major academic or clinical-society guideline carries them. This report runs alongside the targetable-feature ranking rather than in place of it, and it does not narrow what that ranking surfaces.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Standard of care options (offline HTML) — the same standard-of-care assessment, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Standard of care options (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by next step

12 standard options assessed: 6 to consider now, 2 behind an open gate, 1 already received.

Twelve standard options were assessed for this recurrence. Six are open to consider now, two sit behind workup gates, two belong to a later decision point, one has already been given, and one was set aside. The honest headline is that the standard of care here is thin. NCCN's own pathway marks a clinical trial as preferred for a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion, and this one came at about 4 months. The default chemotherapy is a class switch to a gemcitabine-based regimen, in US practice usually gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, and the right benchmark for it is the post-FOLFIRINOX AGEO cohort: response rate 17.5%, median survival 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7). ESMO's April 2025 Express Update grades gemcitabine plus conventional paclitaxel I, B in this position and gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel III, C; no grading changes how modest all three are. NCCN was verified at v2.2026; v3.2026 has posted and could not be read.

Already spent: 10 cycles of FOLFIRINOX across the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings, which is why neither FOLFIRINOX re-challenge nor NALIRIFOX, an approved first-line regimen built from the same three drug classes, appears as a live option.

Gated: radiotherapy waits on the staging call that would make this an isolated local recurrence; olaparib waits on the germline panel that has never been drawn; and every taxane-containing row waits on a CTCAE grade for the residual oxaliplatin neuropathy.

This report adds the standard options and does not narrow the experimental options ranked elsewhere on this page. The workup at the top of both tables is the same step, and the one hard conflict between the tracks is timing: starting chemotherapy spends the six-week RASolute 303 consent window.

docs.text:
Carried so the report reads as a complete account of the standard options rather than a list that quietly omits what has been tried.
