docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Entries are ordered to match the Recommendations table: by therapeutic target group, then by rank within each group. The number in the first column links to the per-intervention section further down the page.

#InterventionTargetAccess statusRegulatoryRecommended first action 1Adavosertib (AZD1775) and next-generation WEE1 inhibitors (azenosertib)—Clinical trial UnavailableAdavosertib has no FDA or EMA approval. AstraZeneca discontinued adavosertib in 2021 over tolerability across multiple programs. Azenosertib (Zentalis ZN-c3) is the next-generation successor, currently in phase 1/2/3 (ASPENOVA phase 3 in cyclin-E1+ platinum-resistant ovarian cancer started May 2026). No breast indication trial open for azenosertib today.Do not pursue adavosertib — no supply path. 2Alpelisib (Piqray)—Off-label useFDA-approved May 2019 for HR+/HER2-, PIK3CA-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with fulvestrant (SOLAR-1). Also approved as Vijoice for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum. No TNBC label; EPIK-B3 (alpelisib + nab-paclitaxel in PIK3CA-mut / PTEN-loss mTNBC) terminated early for slow accrual and a missed Part B1 ORR endpoint.Do not pursue alpelisib in TNBC. The EPIK-B3 negative readout is the load-bearing fact. 3Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel (IMpassion130 regimen)—UnavailableUS accelerated approval voluntarily withdrawn Aug 2021 after IMpassion131 failed confirmatory readout. EMA approval also withdrawn. Atezolizumab is FDA-approved for other indications (NSCLC, HCC, melanoma adjuvant) but the mTNBC indication is no longer labeled in the US or EU.Do not pursue. The pembrolizumab + chemo row is the operational 1L ICI path. 4Capivasertib (Truqap)—Off-label useFDA-approved Nov 2023 for HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with PIK3CA / AKT1 / PTEN alteration, in combination with fulvestrant after endocrine progression (CAPItello-291). No TNBC indication. CAPItello-290 (capivasertib + paclitaxel in 1L mTNBC) primary OS readout was negative at 2025 ESMO, including in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum.Do not pursue capivasertib in TNBC. CAPItello-290 negative OS in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum is the load-bearing evidence. 5Carboplatin / cisplatin (platinum chemotherapy)—Standard of care Off-label useBoth agents are FDA-approved across multiple solid tumor indications since the 1980s; generic for decades. Carboplatin is not specifically labeled for breast cancer, but it is on-compendium and ubiquitously used. Cisplatin similarly off-label in breast cancer.Confirm renal function (CrCl for AUC dosing) and baseline hematology. 6Ceralasertib (AZD6738, ATR inhibitor) + olaparib—Clinical trialCeralasertib is investigational with no FDA or EMA approval. Olaparib carries the breast cancer indications separately (see olaparib row). The combination has no labeled use.Do not pursue the combination outside a trial — no open protocol today. 7Datopotamab deruxtecan (Datroway, Dato-DXd)—Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved Jan 2025 for unresectable or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer after prior endocrine and chemo (TROPION-Breast01). Granted FDA Priority Review (Feb 2026) for 1L mTNBC ICI-ineligible based on TROPION-Breast02; approval expected mid-2026. EMA filing in parallel.Wait on the PD-L1 CPS result before pursuing this drug — the access path branches on CPS >=10 (TROPION-Breast05) vs CPS <10 (TROPION-Breast02 label, compassionate use, or watchful waiting for the 2026 approval). 8Inavolisib (Itovebi)—Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved Oct 2024 for endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated, HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with palbociclib + fulvestrant (INAVO120). No TNBC indication. EMA filing in parallel.Do not pursue inavolisib in TNBC outside a trial. 9Niraparib (Zejula)—Off-label useFDA-approved for maintenance treatment of advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary peritoneal cancer after platinum response. No FDA approval in breast cancer; BRAVO phase 3 failed on central PFS and the program was not refiled in breast.Default to olaparib or talazoparib before considering niraparib — same mechanism, on-label access, easier payer path. 10Olaparib (Lynparza)—Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved for germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (OlympiAD, Jan 2018) and for high-risk adjuvant germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-neg early breast cancer (OlympiA, Mar 2022). EMA-approved with comparable wording.Order germline BRCA1 testing (saliva or blood) to resolve germline vs somatic — this is the single load-bearing question for on-label vs off-label prescribing. 11Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-355 1L mTNBC)—Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved Nov 2020 for 1L locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, in combination with chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine/carboplatin). Also approved as tumor-agnostic monotherapy for TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb by F1CDx) post-progression. EMA-approved with parallel wording.Confirm PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 from the diagnostic biopsy — this is the only gating biomarker for the 1L pembro + chemo decision. 12Pembrolizumab monotherapy in TMB-H solid tumors (KEYNOTE-158)—Off-label useFDA-approved Jun 2020 as tumor-agnostic monotherapy for unresectable or metastatic TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb by FoundationOne CDx) solid tumors that have progressed on prior therapy and lack satisfactory alternatives. Breast cancer was NOT in the KEYNOTE-158 basket — application here is cross-tumor extrapolation under the agnostic label.Confirm the TMB-14 call was made on FoundationOne CDx specifically — the label only recognizes that assay. 13Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)—Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic TNBC after >=2 prior systemic therapies (>=1 in the metastatic setting) — the ASCENT label. Also approved 2L+ HR+/HER2- mBC after endocrine + 2 chemo lines. EMA-approved 2L+ mTNBC.Reserve SG for the 2L decision. The 1L choice is pembrolizumab + chemo (CPS >=10), Dato-DXd (CPS <10 pending approval), or carboplatin + PARPi maintenance. 14Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT, MK-2870)—Clinical trialInvestigational. No FDA or EMA approval. Filed in China for 2L+ TNBC (Kelun-Biotech, 2024); Merck holds ex-China rights and is running the global phase 3 program.Wait on the PD-L1 CPS result. If CPS <10, contact the Merck trial sites line at 1-888-577-8839 (Trialsites@msd.com) for TroFuse-011 screening. 15Samuraciclib (CT7001, CDK7 inhibitor)—Clinical trialInvestigational. FDA Fast Track designation for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer post-CDK4/6i and for locally advanced or metastatic TNBC. No approval. Carrick Therapeutics plans phase 3 initiation in 2026 (HR+ focus).No open TNBC trial today; recheck Carrick's pipeline (https://www.carricktherapeutics.com/pipeline/cdk7-inhibitor) in 3-6 months. 16Stereotactic body / ablative radiotherapy (SBRT/SABR) and IR ablation for the solitary liver oligometastasis—Standard of care Clinical trialNot a drug — SBRT and IR ablation are procedural modalities, available at any academic radiation oncology / interventional radiology service. Equipment-and-credentialing path, not regulatory.Plan systemic therapy first; the consolidation question becomes relevant after 3-6 months of response. 17Surgical resection of the intact primary tumor in de novo M1 breast cancer—Standard of careSurgical procedure — not a drug. Available at any breast surgical oncology service.Do not pursue primary surgery as part of the 1L systemic plan. 18Talazoparib (Talzenna)—Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trialFDA-approved for germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (EMBRACA, Oct 2018) and for HRR-mutant mCRPC + enzalutamide (TALAPRO-2, 2023). EMA-approved with similar mBC wording.Resolve germline vs somatic BRCA1 testing alongside the olaparib decision — both drugs hinge on the same question. 19Veliparib + carboplatin + paclitaxel (BROCADE3 / BrighTNess regimen)—UnavailableNo FDA or EMA approval in any indication. AbbVie discontinued the veliparib development program; the NCI CTEP / AbbVie expanded-access protocol (NCT03123211) has been listed as 'no longer available' since 2022, and clinical supply was terminated.Do not pursue veliparib — there is no supply path. 20Xentuzumab (BI 836845) — IGF-1/IGF-2 neutralising antibody, and the IGF-1R inhibitor class—UnavailableNo FDA or EMA approval in any indication. Boehringer Ingelheim has not pursued a marketing authorization. The phase 2 HR+ breast trial (XENERA-1) was negative and the program has been wound down for breast cancer; sponsor-driven trial closures since 2016-2017. Newer IGF-1R targeting assets (e.g., ganitumab, dalotuzumab, figitumumab) were all discontinued in oncology after class-wide negative readouts.Do not pursue. No supply path exists. 21ZEN-3694 (BET inhibitor) + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel / + talazoparib—Clinical trialInvestigational. No FDA or EMA approval in any indication. Zenith Epigenetics holds the asset; NCI sponsors the TNBC combination trials.Confirm PD-L1 CPS first — this trial requires PD-L1-negative.

docs.title: 1. Adavosertib (AZD1775) and next-generation WEE1 inhibitors (azenosertib) adavosertib, AZD1775, MK-1775, azenosertib, ZN-c3
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Unavailable Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Adavosertib is gone; azenosertib is alive but its trials are not yet open in TNBC. The mechanistic rationale (TP53-mut + replication stress, BRCA1-mut + WEE1 inhibition) is preclinically strong but the clinical-evidence base is thin — the DFCI adavosertib + cisplatin TNBC trial (NCT03012477) missed its primary ORR endpoint and VIOLETTE closed the adavosertib + olaparib arm for toxicity. Watch for Zentalis to open a TNBC azenosertib trial in late 2026 or 2027.

RegulatoryAdavosertib has no FDA or EMA approval. AstraZeneca discontinued adavosertib in 2021 over tolerability across multiple programs. Azenosertib (Zentalis ZN-c3) is the next-generation successor, currently in phase 1/2/3 (ASPENOVA phase 3 in cyclin-E1+ platinum-resistant ovarian cancer started May 2026). No breast indication trial open for azenosertib today. GuidelinesNot in NCCN or ESMO guidelines. Geographic scopeAdavosertib not available anywhere. Azenosertib trials currently US/EU in ovarian only; TNBC scope pending.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue adavosertib — no supply path.
  2. Azenosertib has no open TNBC trial today. Watch Zentalis' pipeline updates (https://ir.zentalis.com/) for a TNBC protocol — AACR 2026 preclinical data signals interest but no protocol is registered yet.
  3. If a TNBC azenosertib trial opens during the patient's treatment course, contact Zentalis medical affairs (1-858-263-4400) to confirm eligibility.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAstraZeneca (adavosertib, discontinued); Zentalis Pharmaceuticals (azenosertib) CountryUnited Kingdom / United States Medical info phone1-800-236-9933 (AstraZeneca); 1-858-263-4400 (Zentalis) Product informationhttps://www.zentalis.com/our-research/azenosertib NotesAdavosertib supply discontinued. Azenosertib is investigational; the phase 3 ASPENOVA trial (NCT06850781) is enrolling cyclin-E1+ platinum-resistant ovarian, not TNBC. Zentalis is signaling TNBC trials based on AACR 2026 preclinical data but no public protocol is open yet.

Payer / coverage notes. Not applicable — both agents are investigational or discontinued. Trial supply is the only route.

Notes. Included to close both the adavosertib (discontinued) and the azenosertib (not yet TNBC-open) questions explicitly. The user requested both — neither is a current option.

docs.title: 2. Alpelisib (Piqray) alpelisib, Piqray, BYL719, Vijoice
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Alpelisib is approved for HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut mBC, not TNBC. The dedicated TNBC trial (EPIK-B3) terminated early after missing its primary ORR endpoint, which removes alpelisib from the practical TNBC option set even though the patient's PIK3CA-mut + PTEN-loss profile would have been the targeted subgroup. Off-label use is technically possible but the evidence base does not support it.

RegulatoryFDA-approved May 2019 for HR+/HER2-, PIK3CA-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with fulvestrant (SOLAR-1). Also approved as Vijoice for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum. No TNBC label; EPIK-B3 (alpelisib + nab-paclitaxel in PIK3CA-mut / PTEN-loss mTNBC) terminated early for slow accrual and a missed Part B1 ORR endpoint. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut mBC. Not endorsed in TNBC NCCN guidelines or the compendium. Geographic scopeGlobally available for the on-label HR+ indication; off-label TNBC use anywhere requires payer override.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue alpelisib in TNBC. The EPIK-B3 negative readout is the load-bearing fact.
  2. If the PI3K/AKT pathway is the priority, the inavolisib + eribulin TNBC trial (NCT07441512) is the clean trial-only path — see that row.
  3. If PIK3CA hotspot confirmation is still pending, get that resolved alongside the broader treatment decision; the hotspot call gates the ovarian / HR+ alpelisib precedent but does not change the TNBC story.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyNovartis Oncology CountrySwitzerland Medical info phone1-888-669-6682 Product informationhttps://www.us.piqray.com/ Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.novartis.com/research-development/research-development-policies/managed-access-programs NotesNovartis Patient Navigator: 1-800-282-7630 for benefits investigation and copay support. Novartis runs managed-access programs case-by-case via the Managed Access portal.

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label in TNBC without compendium support, and the EPIK-B3 negative readout makes the evidence base actively unfavorable. Payers will almost certainly deny, and the medical-exception appeal is weakened by EPIK-B3. Hyperglycemia (the dose-limiting AE) further complicates the cost-benefit calculus.

Notes. EPIK-B3 Part B1 missed ORR threshold; Part B2 never initiated. Sponsor statement is the public record.

docs.title: 3. Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel (IMpassion130 regimen) atezolizumab, Tecentriq, MPDL3280A, RG7446
docs.text:
Access status: Unavailable Modality: monoclonal_antibody   Verified: 2026-05-19

Functionally unavailable for this case. The IMpassion130 indication was withdrawn in 2021 after IMpassion131 failed confirmation, and the labeled 1L ICI in mTNBC is now pembrolizumab + chemo. Do not pursue atezolizumab for this patient.

RegulatoryUS accelerated approval voluntarily withdrawn Aug 2021 after IMpassion131 failed confirmatory readout. EMA approval also withdrawn. Atezolizumab is FDA-approved for other indications (NSCLC, HCC, melanoma adjuvant) but the mTNBC indication is no longer labeled in the US or EU. GuidelinesRemoved from NCCN TNBC guidelines after the US withdrawal. NCCN Compendium no longer lists the mTNBC indication. Geographic scopeIndication withdrawn in US and EU. Some non-US, non-EU markets may still carry historical approval but this is not a realistic access path.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue. The pembrolizumab + chemo row is the operational 1L ICI path.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyHoffmann-La Roche / Genentech CountrySwitzerland / United States Medical info phone1-800-821-8590 Product informationhttps://www.gene.com/patients/medicines/tecentriq NotesGenentech Medical Communications handles the off-label inquiry, but they will confirm the indication was withdrawn and steer the call toward pembrolizumab + chemo. Atezolizumab is still available for other on-label uses, but not for 1L mTNBC.

Payer / coverage notes. No payer in the US will cover atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel for 1L mTNBC — the indication is withdrawn and the alternative (pembrolizumab + chemo) is on-label with category 1 evidence.

Notes. Included to close the option explicitly. The IMpassion130 evidence is preserved in the dossier for context but the access path is closed.

docs.title: 4. Capivasertib (Truqap) capivasertib, Truqap, AZD5363
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Capivasertib is HR+ on-label only. CAPItello-290 just read out negative in 1L mTNBC, including in the patient's likely benefit stratum (PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered) — that result effectively closes the off-label TNBC question. Do not pursue.

RegulatoryFDA-approved Nov 2023 for HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with PIK3CA / AKT1 / PTEN alteration, in combination with fulvestrant after endocrine progression (CAPItello-291). No TNBC indication. CAPItello-290 (capivasertib + paclitaxel in 1L mTNBC) primary OS readout was negative at 2025 ESMO, including in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for HR+/HER2- PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered post-endocrine. Not endorsed in TNBC NCCN guidelines; CAPItello-290 negative readout actively argues against TNBC use. Geographic scopeGlobally available for on-label HR+ use; off-label TNBC use anywhere requires payer override that is unlikely to succeed.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue capivasertib in TNBC. CAPItello-290 negative OS in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum is the load-bearing evidence.
  2. If the AKT-axis hypothesis is still compelling, the remaining option is ipatasertib (also negative in IPATunity130) — neither agent has a viable TNBC path today.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAstraZeneca CountryUnited Kingdom / Sweden Medical info phone1-800-236-9933 Product informationhttps://medicalinformation.astrazeneca-us.com/home/prescribing-information/truqap.html Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.azandmeapp.com/ NotesSame Access 360 / AZ&Me infrastructure as olaparib. Sponsor will steer TNBC inquiries toward the negative CAPItello-290 readout.

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label in TNBC without compendium support; the CAPItello-290 negative phase 3 readout makes the medical-exception appeal nearly unwinnable. Hyperglycemia, diarrhea, and rash are the dose-limiting toxicities — adding payer pushback to a regimen with no efficacy gain in TNBC is not a winning trade.

Notes. CAPItello-290 OS HR 0.92 (overall) and 1.05 (PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered) reported at ESMO 2025; full publication Ann Oncol 2025. The trial is the cleanest available answer to the off-label TNBC question and the answer is no.

docs.title: 5. Carboplatin / cisplatin (platinum chemotherapy) carboplatin, Paraplatin, cisplatin, Platinol
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Carboplatin is the cleanest, fastest standard-of-care lever for a BRCA1-mut TNBC patient. TNT showed double the ORR of docetaxel in the BRCA-mut subset (68% vs 33%), and the NCCN Compendium covers the use. The practical question is which backbone to pair it with — gemcitabine + carboplatin + pembrolizumab if CPS >=10, carboplatin + paclitaxel if CPS <10, or platinum-based induction followed by PARPi maintenance.

RegulatoryBoth agents are FDA-approved across multiple solid tumor indications since the 1980s; generic for decades. Carboplatin is not specifically labeled for breast cancer, but it is on-compendium and ubiquitously used. Cisplatin similarly off-label in breast cancer. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 / preferred for 1L mTNBC, with explicit support for platinum-containing regimens in germline BRCA-mut TNBC based on the TNT trial (ORR 68% carbo vs 33% docetaxel in BRCA-mut subset). NCCN Compendium covers the breast indication for both agents. Geographic scopeGlobally available.

Next steps

  1. Confirm renal function (CrCl for AUC dosing) and baseline hematology.
  2. Plan the 1L backbone: gem/carbo + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-355) if CPS >=10; carbo + paclitaxel (TNT-style) if CPS <10 or platinum monotherapy preferred; carbo induction followed by olaparib maintenance is a defensible off-trial design for the BRCA1-mut phenotype (DORA template).
  3. If platinum induction is the chosen path, plan for PARPi maintenance once response is established — see the olaparib row.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT056336543post-neoadjuvant residual TNBCrecruitingeligible: no—Not applicable here — patient is M1, not post-surgical. Listed only to flag that platinum is embedded in current trial backbones.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyMultiple generic manufacturers (Hospira/Pfizer, Teva, Sandoz, others) CountryGlobal NotesGeneric; available through hospital and infusion pharmacies. No single sponsor medical-information line; product inquiries go through the prescribing institution's pharmacy.

Payer / coverage notes. Routine coverage across all US payers with NCCN Compendium support for breast cancer. No prior auth challenges. The TNT trial provides specific evidence for BRCA-mut TNBC platinum sensitivity, which strengthens documentation if needed.

Notes. TNT (Tutt 2018 Nat Med) is the cleanest BRCA-mut platinum-sensitivity evidence in advanced TNBC. CALGB 40603 supports the neoadjuvant pCR gain (60% vs 44%); BrighTNess 4-year confirmed carbo (not veliparib) drives the EFS benefit.

docs.title: 6. Ceralasertib (AZD6738, ATR inhibitor) + olaparib ceralasertib, AZD6738, olaparib, Lynparza
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

VIOLETTE closed without a positive readout, so there is no current path to ceralasertib + olaparib outside a trial, and the trial that mattered is now closed. The mechanistic rationale (BRCA1-mut + ATR inhibition restoring replication-fork dependence) is strong preclinically but the clinical translation has not arrived. The labeled olaparib monotherapy row carries the actionable BRCA1 axis for this patient.

RegulatoryCeralasertib is investigational with no FDA or EMA approval. Olaparib carries the breast cancer indications separately (see olaparib row). The combination has no labeled use. GuidelinesNot in NCCN or ESMO guidelines. VIOLETTE phase 2 was negative for the combination over olaparib alone in BRCA-mut TNBC. Geographic scopeTrial-only access historically; no current trial open in TNBC.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue the combination outside a trial — no open protocol today.
  2. Watch the AstraZeneca pipeline for a next-generation ATR+PARPi combination trial; the mechanistic case is alive even if VIOLETTE was negative.
  3. Use the labeled olaparib pathway (see olaparib row) as the actionable BRCA1 axis.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT033308472Metastatic TNBC with HRR mutation stratificationactive not recruitingeligible: no—Closed to enrollment. The adavosertib arm closed early for toxicity; the ceralasertib arm did not improve PFS over olaparib alone. Result available; no open ATR+PARPi TNBC trial today.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAstraZeneca CountryUnited Kingdom / Sweden Medical info phone1-800-236-9933 Product informationhttps://medicalinformation.astrazeneca-us.com/ NotesCeralasertib supply is restricted to active trials. AstraZeneca has not opened a breast-cancer-specific ATR+PARPi combination protocol after VIOLETTE.

Payer / coverage notes. Not applicable — investigational.

Notes. VIOLETTE BRCA-mut PFS HR ~0.81 (not significant) is the negative readout. The combination is on hold pending next-generation ATR inhibitors.

docs.title: 7. Datopotamab deruxtecan (Datroway, Dato-DXd) datopotamab deruxtecan, Dato-DXd, DS-1062, DS-1062a, Datroway, datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-05-19

Dato-DXd is in label-approval limbo for 1L mTNBC. The realistic path today is TROPION-Breast05 enrollment if PD-L1 CPS returns >=10, or a Daiichi Sankyo compassionate-use request if CPS <10 and trial timing does not work. The full label expansion is expected mid-2026 and should make commercial 1L access routine within weeks of FDA action.

RegulatoryFDA-approved Jan 2025 for unresectable or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer after prior endocrine and chemo (TROPION-Breast01). Granted FDA Priority Review (Feb 2026) for 1L mTNBC ICI-ineligible based on TROPION-Breast02; approval expected mid-2026. EMA filing in parallel. GuidelinesNCCN listed for HR+/HER2- 2L+ post-endocrine; not yet in NCCN TNBC guidelines pending the 2026 TNBC label expansion. The 1L mTNBC indication will likely land as category 1 once the label drops. Geographic scopeTROPION-Breast05 recruiting globally including US, EU, AU. TROPION-Breast02 closed to enrollment. Compassionate use available case-by-case via Daiichi Sankyo.

Next steps

  1. Wait on the PD-L1 CPS result before pursuing this drug — the access path branches on CPS >=10 (TROPION-Breast05) vs CPS <10 (TROPION-Breast02 label, compassionate use, or watchful waiting for the 2026 approval).
  2. If CPS >=10, contact the AstraZeneca Clinical Study Information Center at 1-877-240-9479 / information.center@astrazeneca.com for TROPION-Breast05 site screening.
  3. If CPS <10 and the team wants Dato-DXd now, submit a compassionate-use request via Daiichi Sankyo medical affairs (1-908-992-6400) — the framework exists and the TROPION-Breast02 data plus pending Priority Review give a clean evidence base.
  4. Monitor the FDA action date for the TNBC indication (expected Q2-Q3 2026) — once approved, the off-label question disappears.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT061038643PD-L1 CPS >=10 locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC, 1Lrecruitingeligible: likelyAstraZeneca Clinical Study Information Centerinformation.center@astrazeneca.com1-877-240-9479trial sitesIf the patient's pending PD-L1 CPS returns >=10, this is the cleanest open 1L trial — TROP2-ADC mechanism plus durvalumab arm leverages the TMB-H / TIL-rich phenotype. AstraZeneca Breast Cancer Study Locator: 1-877-400-4656, az-bcsl@careboxhealth.com. NCT0537451231L mTNBC, ICI-ineligible (PD-L1 CPS <10 or other)active not recruitingeligible: no—Trial closed to new enrollment. Pivotal data already read out (mPFS 10.8 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.57). The label expansion anchored on this trial is the near-term path if PD-L1 CPS <10.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyDaiichi Sankyo (developed with AstraZeneca) CountryJapan / United Kingdom Medical info phone1-908-992-6400 Product informationhttps://www.daiichisankyo.us/products/datroway/ Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.daiichisankyo.com/about_us/policies/compassionate_use_policy/ NotesDaiichi Sankyo runs a global compassionate-use program for Dato-DXd in life-threatening conditions when no trial slot is available and the patient cannot wait for label approval. Submission goes through the treating physician.

Payer / coverage notes. Currently covered on-label for HR+/HER2- 2L+. TNBC use today is off-label until the 1L mTNBC indication lands in mid-2026 — until then payer access requires either trial enrollment (TROPION-Breast05 for CPS >=10) or a compassionate-use request through Daiichi Sankyo (CPS <10, ICI-ineligible, no trial slot).

Notes. FDA accepted the sBLA for 1L mTNBC ICI-ineligible under Priority Review in Feb 2026 — action date should land mid-2026.

docs.title: 8. Inavolisib (Itovebi) inavolisib, GDC-0077, Itovebi, RG6114
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Inavolisib is HR+ on-label only and the TNBC trial sits in mainland China not yet recruiting. The PI3K/AKT pathway rationale for this patient is real, but inavolisib is not a practical reach today. If the team wants to act on the PIK3CA-mut + PTEN-loss biology, the cleaner option is to wait for the NCT07441512 trial to open or to consider the labeled HR+ regimen as a non-starter and look at capivasertib (also negative in TNBC, see that row).

RegulatoryFDA-approved Oct 2024 for endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated, HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with palbociclib + fulvestrant (INAVO120). No TNBC indication. EMA filing in parallel. GuidelinesNCCN listed for HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut endocrine-resistant mBC. Not endorsed in TNBC NCCN guidelines or compendium. Geographic scopeOn-label HR+ use available globally. TNBC trial mainland-China-only; not yet recruiting.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue inavolisib in TNBC outside a trial.
  2. If the team wants the trial path, NCT07441512 is mainland-China-only — confirm geography acceptance before any further work.
  3. If PIK3CA hotspot confirmation is still pending, get it resolved; the call matters for downstream HR+ precedents even if not for TNBC use.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT074415122PIK3CA-mutant metastatic TNBCnot yet recruitingeligible: noHai Hu, MDhjoyh@126.com+86-15958192550trial sitesMainland-China-only single-center trial (Zhejiang Cancer Hospital). Not yet recruiting; estimated start Mar 2026. Also requires taxane pretreatment, so the patient would need to progress on 1L taxane-containing chemo before this trial is even theoretically open.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Genentech runs an expanded-access framework but inavolisib is unlikely to be granted for TNBC outside the trial — the sponsor will steer toward INAVO120 evidence base in HR+ disease.

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label in TNBC, no compendium support, and the dedicated TNBC trial is in mainland China only. Payer denial is essentially guaranteed; the medical-exception path is weak because there is no published TNBC efficacy data.

Notes. INAVO120 PFS HR 0.43 in HR+ is the precedent; TNBC extrapolation is not supported by published efficacy data.

docs.title: 9. Niraparib (Zejula) niraparib, Zejula, MK-4827
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Niraparib is approved in ovarian cancer but has no breast cancer label and no NCCN Compendium support — payer access is the bottleneck. The TOPACIO BRCA-mut TNBC ORR signal is mechanistically interesting, but the labeled PARP inhibitors (olaparib, talazoparib) cover the same ground with fewer payer obstacles, so niraparib rarely makes practical sense as a first reach in TNBC.

RegulatoryFDA-approved for maintenance treatment of advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary peritoneal cancer after platinum response. No FDA approval in breast cancer; BRAVO phase 3 failed on central PFS and the program was not refiled in breast. GuidelinesNot endorsed in NCCN breast cancer guidelines. NCCN Compendium does not list niraparib for breast cancer; off-label coverage in mBC will not have compendium support, which makes payer approval substantially harder than olaparib or talazoparib. Geographic scopeAvailable wherever ovarian indication is approved; off-label use anywhere requires payer override.

Next steps

  1. Default to olaparib or talazoparib before considering niraparib — same mechanism, on-label access, easier payer path.
  2. If pursuing niraparib for a specific reason (e.g., olaparib/talazoparib intolerance), GSK Medical Information (1-877-475-6448) can help with the medical-exception request packet.
  3. Document the basis for off-label use — TOPACIO BRCA-mut ORR, prior PARPi failure / intolerance — for the inevitable payer denial appeal.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT026578891/2Advanced or metastatic TNBCcompletedeligible: no—Completed in 2019. The 47% ORR in BRCA-mut TNBC is the headline mechanistic signal but the trial is closed.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyGSK CountryUnited Kingdom Medical info phone1-877-475-6448 Product informationhttps://zejula.com/ NotesTogether with GSK Oncology support line: 1-844-447-5662 for benefits investigation and copay assistance. Adverse-event reporting: 1-888-825-5249.

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label in breast cancer without NCCN Compendium support, so commercial and Medicare payers will typically deny. Possible appeals lever is the TOPACIO BRCA-mut TNBC ORR signal plus mechanistic equivalence to olaparib, but expect 2-3 rounds of denial. Most teams reach for labeled olaparib or talazoparib first and only consider niraparib if those agents fail.

Notes. BRAVO central-vs-local PFS discordance is the published interpretation caveat. GSK has not pursued a breast indication.

docs.title: 10. Olaparib (Lynparza) olaparib, Lynparza, AZD2281, KU-0059436
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Olaparib is the cleanest near-term option once the germline-versus-somatic BRCA1 question is answered. If germline, it is on-label 1L for HER2-negative mBC and covered routinely. If somatic-only, the same prescription is off-label but mechanistically identical, and the NCCN Compendium plus the Stanford somatic-BRCA talazoparib trial make medical-exception coverage achievable.

RegulatoryFDA-approved for germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (OlympiAD, Jan 2018) and for high-risk adjuvant germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-neg early breast cancer (OlympiA, Mar 2022). EMA-approved with comparable wording. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for previously treated recurrent or metastatic germline BRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative breast cancer; listed on the NCCN Drugs & Biologics Compendium, which drives Medicare and commercial off-label coverage. Geographic scopeGlobally available — US, EU, UK, AU, Japan all carry the mBC label.

Next steps

  1. Order germline BRCA1 testing (saliva or blood) to resolve germline vs somatic — this is the single load-bearing question for on-label vs off-label prescribing.
  2. If germline, write the script; AstraZeneca Access 360 (1-844-275-2360) handles benefits investigation and copay support.
  3. If somatic-only, submit a medical-exception request citing the NCCN Compendium entry and the BRCA1-knockdown / HCC1937 preclinical data; expect 1-2 rounds of payer pushback.
  4. Consider sequencing around the carboplatin-containing induction the patient is likely to start, with olaparib maintenance after response — the DORA design supports this even though DORA itself is not enrollable.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT038013692Platinum-pretreated advanced TNBC, maintenanceactive not recruitingeligible: no—Requires prior platinum exposure; the patient is 1L treatment-naive, so DORA is not enrollable today. Strategy template, not an open door. NCT027340041/2Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast canceractive not recruitingeligible: no—Cohort closed to enrollment; useful as the mechanistic precedent for PARPi + ICI maintenance.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyAstraZeneca CountryUnited Kingdom / Sweden Medical info phone1-800-236-9933 Product informationhttps://medicalinformation.astrazeneca-us.com/home/prescribing-information/lynparza-tablets.html Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.azandmeapp.com/ NotesAccess 360 case-management line for benefits investigations and prior-auth support: 1-844-275-2360 (1-844-ASK-A360). AZ&Me Application provides free product for uninsured patients meeting income criteria.

Payer / coverage notes. On-label for germline BRCA1/2 mBC, so Medicare and major commercial plans cover with prior auth requiring a germline test report. If the patient's BRCA1 mutation turns out to be somatic-only, the breast indication is off-label — payer pushback is likely; the standard workaround is to lean on the NCCN Compendium entry plus the Stanford NCT03990896 somatic-BRCA precedent and request medical-exception coverage.

Notes. OlympiAD remains the registrational evidence; OlympiA adjuvant approval added the post-surgical setting. The somatic-BRCA workaround is the active uncertainty for this case.

docs.title: 11. Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-355 1L mTNBC) pembrolizumab, MK-3475, Keytruda, lambrolizumab
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: monoclonal_antibody   Verified: 2026-05-19

Pembrolizumab + chemo is the 1L standard if the patient's PD-L1 CPS comes back >=10. Get the CPS result first — it is the single fork in the 1L decision tree. If CPS <10, this regimen is off-label and the access path shifts to Dato-DXd or carboplatin + PARPi.

RegulatoryFDA-approved Nov 2020 for 1L locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, in combination with chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine/carboplatin). Also approved as tumor-agnostic monotherapy for TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb by F1CDx) post-progression. EMA-approved with parallel wording. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 preferred regimen for 1L mTNBC PD-L1 CPS >=10. ESMO recommends I-A in the same population. Geographic scopeGlobally available — US, EU, UK, AU, Japan all carry the 1L mTNBC CPS >=10 label.

Next steps

  1. Confirm PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 from the diagnostic biopsy — this is the only gating biomarker for the 1L pembro + chemo decision.
  2. If CPS >=10, write the script (pembro 200 mg q3w + investigator-choice chemo). Merck Access Program (1-855-257-3932) handles prior auth and reimbursement.
  3. If CPS <10, do not pursue this regimen as 1L — see the Dato-DXd row (TROPION-Breast02 / compassionate use) and the carboplatin row.
  4. TMB-H monotherapy indication (KEYNOTE-158) is technically open as cross-tumor extrapolation but requires prior progression and no satisfactory alternatives, so it is a 2L+ option not a 1L one for this patient.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT0610386431L PD-L1 CPS >=10 mTNBCrecruitingeligible: likely—Control arm carries pembro + chemo; if the patient enrolls and is randomized to control she still gets the 1L SoC. See the Dato-DXd row for full contact details.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyMerck Sharp & Dohme CountryUnited States Medical info phone1-800-672-6372 Product informationhttps://www.merck.com/product/usa/pi_circulars/k/keytruda/keytruda_pi.pdf Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.merck.com/research/clinical-trials/expanded-access/ NotesMerck Access Program: 1-855-257-3932 (Mon-Fri 8 AM-8 PM ET) handles benefits investigation, prior auth, and the KEY+YOU patient program (1-855-398-7832). Merck Patient Assistance Program for uninsured patients: 1-800-727-5400.

Payer / coverage notes. Routine Medicare and commercial coverage when PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 is documented >=10 in the metastatic setting. The single load-bearing requirement is the CPS test result. If CPS <10, the regimen is off-label and payers will deny without an exception; in that case the practical pivot is to Dato-DXd (TROPION-Breast02) or trial enrollment.

Notes. KEYNOTE-355 final OS HR 0.73 (mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo in CPS >=10) is the survival anchor. The TIL-3+ / TMB-14 phenotype reinforces the ICI rationale but the label is anchored on CPS, not TMB or TILs.

docs.title: 12. Pembrolizumab monotherapy in TMB-H solid tumors (KEYNOTE-158) pembrolizumab, MK-3475, Keytruda
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: monoclonal_antibody   Verified: 2026-05-19

The tumor-agnostic TMB-H label is real but mostly relevant as a 2L+ option, not 1L — the FDA wording restricts use to progression on prior therapy with no satisfactory alternatives. For a treatment-naive mTNBC patient, pembro + chemo (KEYNOTE-355, on-label if CPS >=10) is the operative path. Hold the TMB-H indication in reserve.

RegulatoryFDA-approved Jun 2020 as tumor-agnostic monotherapy for unresectable or metastatic TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb by FoundationOne CDx) solid tumors that have progressed on prior therapy and lack satisfactory alternatives. Breast cancer was NOT in the KEYNOTE-158 basket — application here is cross-tumor extrapolation under the agnostic label. GuidelinesTumor-agnostic pathway recognized in NCCN Biomarkers Compendium; breast cancer-specific use as monotherapy is not endorsed in NCCN breast guidelines and is uncommon practice. Geographic scopeUS tumor-agnostic indication is unique; EU and other agencies have not adopted the TMB-H tumor-agnostic wording.

Next steps

  1. Confirm the TMB-14 call was made on FoundationOne CDx specifically — the label only recognizes that assay.
  2. Do not pursue TMB-H monotherapy in 1L; the label does not support it and payers will deny.
  3. Carry the TMB-H option forward as a 2L+ lever if standard options are exhausted, with documentation of progression on prior lines and no satisfactory alternatives.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyMerck Sharp & Dohme CountryUnited States Medical info phone1-800-672-6372 Product informationhttps://www.merck.com/product/usa/pi_circulars/k/keytruda/keytruda_pi.pdf NotesSame Merck contact apparatus as the pembro + chemo row; the monotherapy indication runs through the same Access Program.

Payer / coverage notes. Tumor-agnostic indication is recognized but requires the TMB call to be from FoundationOne CDx specifically and the patient must have progressed on >=1 prior line with no satisfactory alternatives. Payers will deny in the 1L setting even at TMB 14 mut/Mb because the label restricts use to post-progression with no alternatives. Becomes practical only in 2L+ when other options are exhausted.

Notes. Decision-relevant context, not a 1L action item. The CPS-anchored KEYNOTE-355 indication is the operational pembro path for this patient.

docs.title: 13. Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy) sacituzumab govitecan, sacituzumab govitecan-hziy, IMMU-132, Trodelvy
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-05-19

Sacituzumab govitecan is the labeled 2L+ TNBC ADC. Not a 1L option today, but it is the most likely second-line drug after progression on a 1L pembro + chemo or carboplatin + PARPi regimen. The 1L expansion via ASCENT-04 (SG + pembrolizumab) is pending label.

RegulatoryFDA-approved for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic TNBC after >=2 prior systemic therapies (>=1 in the metastatic setting) — the ASCENT label. Also approved 2L+ HR+/HER2- mBC after endocrine + 2 chemo lines. EMA-approved 2L+ mTNBC. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for 2L+ mTNBC. 1L use is off-label and off-guideline pending the ASCENT-04 label update (1L SG + pembrolizumab in PD-L1 CPS >=10 — pivotal readout 2025; expected label update in 2026). Geographic scopeGlobally available — US, EU, UK, AU all carry the 2L+ mTNBC label.

Next steps

  1. Reserve SG for the 2L decision. The 1L choice is pembrolizumab + chemo (CPS >=10), Dato-DXd (CPS <10 pending approval), or carboplatin + PARPi maintenance.
  2. When the patient progresses, Gilead Oncology Support (1-844-876-3358) handles benefits investigation; expect routine 2L+ approval.
  3. Watch the ASCENT-04 label update — if 1L SG + pembrolizumab gets PD-L1 CPS >=10 indication, the 1L decision shifts.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT056336543TNBC with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant + surgeryrecruitingeligible: no—Patient is de novo M1, not post-neoadjuvant residual disease, so she does not fit ASCENT-05. Listed for completeness because the trial is recruiting and would matter only after oligometastatic conversion + surgical consolidation.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyGilead Sciences CountryUnited States Medical info phone1-844-876-3358 Product informationhttps://www.trodelvyhcp.com/ Compassionate / expanded accesshttps://www.gilead.com/science/clinical-trials/compassionate-use-and-managed-access NotesGilead Oncology Support: 1-844-876-3358 (1-844-TRODELVY), 9 AM-7 PM ET. Gilead Patient Assistance Program PAP enrollment fax: 1-833-851-4344. Compassionate-use route exists but Trodelvy is commercially available, so the typical path is on-label or off-label prescription, not EAP.

Payer / coverage notes. Routine coverage in 2L+ mTNBC. 1L use is off-label until the ASCENT-04 label update lands; commercial payers and Medicare will deny 1L prescriptions today unless the patient has a PD-L1 CPS <10 + ICI-ineligible profile and the prescriber documents the ASCENT-04 evidence base. NCCN Compendium does not yet list 1L use.

Notes. ASCENT-04 readout (Tolaney 2026, NEJM) showed PFS HR 0.65 for SG + pembro vs chemo + pembro in CPS >=10 1L — the label expansion is the near-term inflection point.

docs.title: 14. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT, MK-2870) sacituzumab tirumotecan, sac-TMT, SKB264, MK-2870
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: ADC   Verified: 2026-05-19

Sac-TMT is investigational outside China. The only realistic US access path is TroFuse-011 enrollment, which is open and recruiting for the 1L PD-L1-low mTNBC patient. Trial supply is the access path; no off-label or compassionate route exists for US patients today.

GuidelinesNot in NCCN or ESMO guidelines. Geographic scopeAvailable in China commercially (Kelun-Biotech approval). Global trial in US, EU, AU via Merck.

  1. Wait on the PD-L1 CPS result. If CPS <10, contact the Merck trial sites line at 1-888-577-8839 (Trialsites@msd.com) for TroFuse-011 screening.
  2. Compare against TROPION-Breast05 (CPS >=10) and TROPION-Breast02-anchored Dato-DXd label (CPS <10) before committing — these are the three TROP2-ADC paths in this case.
  3. Confirm an open site that accepts the patient's geography (US-only acceptable for the TroFuse-011 sites we found).

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT0684135431L mTNBC, PD-L1 CPS <10recruitingeligible: likelyMerck Toll Free NumberTrialsites@msd.com1-888-577-8839trial sitesOpen and enrolling at multiple US sites. If the patient's PD-L1 CPS comes back <10, this trial is the parallel option to TROPION-Breast02 / Dato-DXd. docs.title: 15. Samuraciclib (CT7001, CDK7 inhibitor) samuraciclib, CT7001, ICEC0942
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Samuraciclib has Fast Track in TNBC but no open TNBC trial actively recruiting at scale, and the published TNBC data is abstract-only. The asset is alive but the practical access path for this patient today is essentially nonexistent. Watch Carrick's pipeline for a TNBC protocol opening in 2026.

RegulatoryInvestigational. FDA Fast Track designation for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer post-CDK4/6i and for locally advanced or metastatic TNBC. No approval. Carrick Therapeutics plans phase 3 initiation in 2026 (HR+ focus). GuidelinesNot in NCCN or ESMO guidelines. Geographic scopeTrial-only when trials open; no current TNBC trial.

Next steps

  1. No open TNBC trial today; recheck Carrick's pipeline (https://www.carricktherapeutics.com/pipeline/cdk7-inhibitor) in 3-6 months.
  2. If a TNBC trial opens, contact Carrick medical affairs through the corporate channel; they are responsive to MYC-driven TNBC inquiries given the mechanism.

docs.title: 16. Stereotactic body / ablative radiotherapy (SBRT/SABR) and IR ablation for the solitary liver oligometastasis SBRT, SABR, stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy, thermal ablation, microwave ablation, radiofrequency ablation
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Clinical trial Modality: other   Verified: 2026-05-19

Local therapy for the solitary liver oligomet is broadly available at academic centers — SBRT, microwave / radiofrequency ablation, or surgical metastasectomy are all on the table after systemic response is established. NRG-BR002 was negative for routine consolidation, so the operative framing is biology-driven tumor-board discussion rather than guideline-driven routine practice. The MSK phase 2 (NCT05534438) is the cleanest trial path if the team wants randomized-trial scaffolding.

RegulatoryNot a drug — SBRT and IR ablation are procedural modalities, available at any academic radiation oncology / interventional radiology service. Equipment-and-credentialing path, not regulatory. GuidelinesNCCN does not endorse routine SBRT consolidation in oligometastatic breast cancer after the NRG-BR002 phase IIR negative readout. SABR-COMET (mixed histologies, including 18% breast) was numerically favorable but underpowered. Local therapy for a solitary liver lesion remains a case-by-case tumor-board call, not a guideline recommendation. Geographic scopeSBRT / IR ablation broadly available at academic centers globally. MSK trial US-only.

Next steps

  1. Plan systemic therapy first; the consolidation question becomes relevant after 3-6 months of response.
  2. Refer to radiation oncology and interventional radiology early for joint planning — the 1.5 cm liver lesion is a candidate for SBRT or thermal ablation depending on the segment.
  3. If trial scaffolding is desired, contact Dr. Amy Xu (xua@mskcc.org, 646-888-6863) at MSK for NCT05534438 screening once the patient has demonstrated systemic response.
  4. Tumor board discussion is the right venue — NRG-BR002 makes 'routine SBRT for breast oligomets' inappropriate, but case-by-case consolidation for a single liver lesion in a young patient with curative-intent framing remains defensible.

Second central contact: Atif Khan, MD (khana7@mskcc.org, 848-225-6334). The patient's solitary 1.5 cm liver lesion fits the enrollment frame after some systemic response is established.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Payer / coverage notes. SBRT for oligometastatic disease is covered by Medicare and most commercial payers with prior auth when there are <=5 lesions and the primary is controlled. Coverage is generally easier when documented as consolidation after systemic response. IR thermal ablation has similar coverage patterns.

Notes. NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS HR ~1.31 (favoring control) tempers the curative-intent framing. SABR-COMET 5-year OS update (Palma 2024) maintained the OS signal but with overlapping CIs. The clinical question is whether to proceed despite the negative breast-specific phase IIR — most centers will if biology and tumor board agree.

docs.title: 17. Surgical resection of the intact primary tumor in de novo M1 breast cancer primary tumor resection, locoregional therapy, mastectomy, breast-conserving surgery
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-05-19

Primary-tumor resection is technically available but is no longer routine after E2108 showed no OS benefit. Practical use is reserved for symptom control (locoregional progression, ulceration, bleeding) or for selected patients with sustained oligometastatic conversion where the tumor board is comfortable reframing toward curative intent.

RegulatorySurgical procedure — not a drug. Available at any breast surgical oncology service. GuidelinesNCCN does not recommend routine primary-tumor resection in de novo M1 breast cancer after the ECOG-ACRIN E2108 phase 3 OS-negative readout. Locoregional therapy is reserved for symptom control or after exceptional systemic response in selected patients. Geographic scopeGlobally available.

Next steps

  1. Do not pursue primary surgery as part of the 1L systemic plan.
  2. Revisit the question at 6-12 months if oligometastatic conversion is sustained and the liver lesion has been locally ablated — at that point the patient's biology may justify primary resection even though E2108 says no routine OS benefit.
  3. Tumor board is the right venue for the eventual decision.

Payer / coverage notes. Routine coverage when symptomatic or after sustained systemic response with curative-intent reframing. Not a payer obstacle.

Notes. E2108 (Khan 2022 JCO) 3-yr OS 68.4% vs 67.9%, HR 1.11 — definitive against routine resection but does not foreclose case-by-case decisions after exceptional response.

docs.title: 18. Talazoparib (Talzenna) talazoparib, Talzenna, BMN 673, BMN-673, MDV3800
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-05-19

Talazoparib is interchangeable with olaparib for the on-label germline-BRCA case and faces the same somatic-only off-label question. The differentiator is tolerability — talazoparib runs heavier on anemia and thrombocytopenia, so most teams default to olaparib unless once-daily dosing is preferred or olaparib is not tolerated. The Stanford NCT03990896 somatic-BRCA expansion is the active trial path if the germline test is negative.

RegulatoryFDA-approved for germline BRCA1/2-mutant HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (EMBRACA, Oct 2018) and for HRR-mutant mCRPC + enzalutamide (TALAPRO-2, 2023). EMA-approved with similar mBC wording. GuidelinesNCCN category 1 for previously treated recurrent or metastatic germline BRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative breast cancer, alongside olaparib. Listed on the NCCN Drugs & Biologics Compendium. Geographic scopeGlobally available — US, EU, UK, AU all carry the mBC label.

Next steps

  1. Resolve germline vs somatic BRCA1 testing alongside the olaparib decision — both drugs hinge on the same question.
  2. If germline, run the olaparib-vs-talazoparib tolerability conversation; talazoparib's anemia profile may matter if the patient is starting from a borderline hemoglobin.
  3. If somatic-only, contact Neelima Vidula (nvidula@mgh.harvard.edu) for NCT03990896 screening or pursue medical-exception coverage with NCCN Compendium support.
  4. Pfizer Oncology Together (1-877-744-5675) handles benefits investigation and copay assistance once a prescription is written.

Notes. EMBRACA remains the pivotal evidence. The somatic-BRCA single-arm extension at Stanford / MGH is the cleanest open path for off-label conversion.

docs.text:

docs.title: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin AUC2 / gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (KEYNOTE-355 backbone) (pembrolizumab-chemo-keynote355)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative1highThis is the 1L regimen with the longest confirmatory follow-up in metastatic TNBC: KEYNOTE-355 read out final OS at 44-month median follow-up (mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo, HR 0.73), so I am not extrapolating from an interim signal. The G3+ AE rate was 68.1% vs 66.9% for chemo alone, meaning pembrolizumab adds little incremental high-grade toxicity over the backbone the patient would receive anyway, and the immune-mediated G3+ events (5.3%) map onto the well-codified irAE algorithm every treating center already runs. The TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype is the subgroup that benefits most, which reinforces the choice without my having to lean on off-label TMB extrapolation. One hard gate: the regimen requires PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, and CPS is pending. Confidence is high on the regimen but conditional on that assay returning >=10; if CPS <10 this drops out and rank 3 leads.PD-L1 CPS is pending; the entire pick is contingent on 22C3 CPS >=10 returning, and roughly 20-30% of primary-vs-liver-met pairs are discordant, so score the breast primary block.; Adds pembrolizumab irAE risk (G3+ immune-mediated 5.3%) on top of the chemo backbone — manageable with the standard algorithm, but a B2M/HLA class I check is cheap insurance against primary ICI resistance in an MSS tumor. critic2highPhase 3, n=847, pre-specified primary PFS in the CPS>=10 stratum at HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, p=0.0012), with a confirmed OS gain at final readout (median +7 mo). RoB 2 low across domains. The label tracks the biomarker rather than the mechanism, which is exactly why I trust it: the CPS<10 subset showed no benefit and the indication respected that. TMB 14 mut/Mb and 3+ TILs are real features of this tumor, but KEYNOTE-355 was not powered on either, so they cannot substitute for the CPS gate. The new ASCENT-04 SG+pembrolizumab 1L row (n=443) points at the same CPS>=10 population but is a 2025 presentation still in press with no published primary I can risk-of-bias; I am not ranking a regimen on a slide deck.Eligibility is entirely gated on 22C3 CPS>=10, which is pending. CPS<10 closes the regimen and the patient does not inherit benefit from TMB-14 or 3+ TILs; that is unsanctioned biomarker extrapolation.; The KEYNOTE-158 TMB-H basket (n=102, single-arm, ORR 29%) cannot bridge a CPS<10 gap in 1L treatment-naive disease. It is 2L+ label, no comparator, and breast was not in the original basket, so the 29% is uninterpretable here.; RoB 2: low across allocation, blinding, missing-data, measurement, selective-reporting. Sponsor-run analysis noted, not de-rated; KEYNOTE-522 replicates direction of effect in a different setting. concensusite——did not pick— advocate2highThe registrational 1L standard if CPS returns >=10, and for this patient the carboplatin flavor does two jobs at once: the TNT data show BRCA1-mutant TNBC doubles its response rate on platinum versus taxane, so the ICI backbone and the BRCA1 axis get served by one regimen. Final OS in CPS>=10 was 23 vs 16 months, which is the efficacy-forward answer a 0.7 weight consents to. Her TIL-3+ / TMB-14 phenotype is the exact subset that pulls the largest benefit in the KEYNOTE analyses. If CPS lands under 10, this drops off and the CPS-low ADC route takes over.Same CPS-gating dependency as pick 1; the whole ICI-backbone plan rests on the pending 22C3 result.; Trials preference only partially honored: this is off-trial standard of care, honored on the trial axis mainly as TROPION-Breast05's control arm.; Efficacy/toxicity weight satisfied; no veto or modality preference to violate.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativequalifiedpreference_fitI will take the 23.0 vs 16.1 mo OS (pmid:35857659) as the floor, but leading with a CPS-gated regimen when 22C3 is still pending leaves her with no plan if it lands under 10, and it buries the deeper-response route her genotype earns. For a solitary liver lesion where conversion to ablation is on the table, talazoparib's 62.6% ORR (pmid:30110579) chases depth this gem/carbo doublet does not, and it starts today regardless of the CPS result. criticconservativequalifiedevidence_qualityNo quarrel with the conservative dossier work here; KEYNOTE-355 is low RoB 2 with the maturest 1L follow-up in mTNBC (n=847, PFS HR 0.65, final OS HR 0.73), and gating it on 22C3 CPS>=10 is the correct read of the label. My one evidence-quality note is on the rank order, not the regimen. In a patient with a BRCA1 finding, the PARP axis carries two independent registered phase-3 hits (OlympiAD n=302, HR 0.58; EMBRACA n=431, HR 0.54), while KEYNOTE-355 is a single phase 3 whose gating biomarker is also pending. If germline BRCA1 resolves before 22C3 returns, replication count argues the PARP monotherapy should lead. Ranking the CPS-gated single-trial regimen at 1 and olaparib at 2 is defensible on tolerability breadth, but it slightly understates the replication the PARP option brings. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitThis is NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 and an ESMO class I recommendation for 1L CPS>=10 metastatic TNBC, and leading with the 22C3 CPS gate is exactly what the label asks for rather than leaning on the TMB-14 or TIL-3+ phenotype. One qualifier on the ordering below it: the rank-2 olaparib carries NCCN category 1 only while BRCA1 reads germline, so a somatic-only call drops it off-label and the platinum doublet becomes the germline-agnostic hold. The CPS-first, gate-honest posture tracks the consensus cleanly. advocateconservativequalifiedpreference_fitThe mature OS readout (23.0 vs 16.1 mo, pmid:35857659) is the floor I want for her, and I do not dispute the regimen. My preference objection is that prefers_trials is set to true and this exact carbo/gem/pembro backbone is the control arm of a recruiting 1L randomized trial (TROPION-Breast05, nct:NCT06103864) she is CPS-eligible for, so leading with it off-trial spends the trials-first preference for no gain when the on-protocol route delivers the same floor plus a TROP2-ADC shot at the ceiling.

docs.title: Datopotamab deruxtecan +/- durvalumab on TROPION-Breast05 (NCT06103864) (datopotamab-deruxtecan-durvalumab-tropion-breast05)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate1highThis is still the trial the preference file reads as written for, and nothing in the re-run knocks it off the top. Recruiting, 1L, randomized against the exact KEYNOTE-355 backbone she would otherwise get off-trial, gated on the pending CPS. The TROP2-ADC arm goes straight at her basal feature and the durvalumab arm cashes in the TMB-14 / TIL-3+ signal. Trial-first preference met, efficacy lean at 0.7 met by the experimental arm, and the control arm is standard of care, so the floor is bounded no matter which way she randomizes.Gated on the pending PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 >=10. If CPS returns <10 she is out of this trial and pick 1 collapses to the CPS-low ADC options (TROPION-Breast02, TroFuse-011).; Preference axes fully satisfied: trials preference honored (recruiting, on-axis), efficacy weight honored (experimental TROP2-ADC + ICI), no toxicity_vetoes to breach, no modality_constraints to breach.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocatedissentpreference_fitThe trial-first read is honored here, but a 1:1 randomization risks assigning her to the control arm — the very gem/carbo+pembro she could get off-trial — and Dato-DXd has no BRCA1 synthetic-lethal mechanism, so it spends her curative-intent window on TROP2 rather than the DDR axis that could actually shrink the liver lesion to a resectable target. Given prefers_trials plus the oligomet conversion goal, I would put her on the somatic-talazoparib deep-response slot (nct:NCT03990896) or a PARP+PD-1 chemo-free combination ahead of a randomized ADC where she might never touch the experimental arm. concensusiteadvocatedissentguideline_fitDatopotamab deruxtecan carries no NCCN Breast v4.2025 category and no ESMO recommendation in 1L metastatic TNBC, so putting the trial at rank 1 over KEYNOTE-355 places an investigational ADC ahead of the CPS>=10 category-1 standard. prefers_trials=true is honored by enrolling her, and that is the guideline-aligned route for an investigational agent, but the consensus framing keeps KEYNOTE-355 (NCCN category 1) as the standard the trials control arm reproduces, not a fallback the trial demotes. Rank the trial as the enrollment vehicle, not as evidence that dato-DXd outranks the endorsed 1L regimen.

docs.title: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD, BRCA1-directed PARP inhibitor) (olaparib-monotherapy-olympiad)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative2moderateAmong the BRCA1-directed options this has the maturest safety record and the most predictable toxicity of any oral agent on the list. OlympiAD reported G3+ AEs at 36.6% (vs 50.5% for chemo), discontinuation at 4.9%, with anemia as the single dominant grade-3 event at 16.1% and a management pathway (dose hold, transfusion, growth-factor support) that oncology teams run in their sleep. The OlympiA adjuvant dataset (n=1836) extends the safety window and, importantly, showed no MDS/AML excess over placebo at the 300 mg BID dose, which matters for a 42-year-old who may live years on or after this drug. Eligibility gates on the germline-vs-somatic call: FDA labeling in breast is germline-restricted, so I want the germline BRCA1 result before writing it. If the variant reads somatic-only, olaparib becomes off-label and I would defer to the platinum backbone rather than an off-label PARP write.Germline-vs-somatic status is unresolved; the labeled breast indication is germline-only, so a somatic-only BRCA1 call moves this to off-label and I would not lead with it.; Anemia (G3+ 16.1%) is the expected dominant AE — check baseline CBC and iron studies and set a transfusion/hold threshold before starting, but this is a characterized, low-surprise toxicity. critic1highNothing in the 14 new trials or the DDR evidence tier displaces this. Two independent registrational phase 3 trials sit under PARP inhibition in germline BRCA1/2 HER2-negative mBC: OlympiAD (n=302, PFS HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43-0.80) and EMBRACA (n=431, PFS HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.71). Both pre-registered, both a registered primary-endpoint hit at conventional alpha, both low RoB 2 with BICR-adjudicated PFS, both replicating the synthetic-lethality preclinical anchor. That is the whole evidence bar the persona exists to defend, and the new saruparib/HS-10502 PARP1-selective abstracts don't clear it. Saruparib's 48.4% breast ORR (PETRA, n=31 at 60 mg) reads well, but it is an AACR conference abstract with a mixed HR+/TNBC subset, no per-term AE table, and a null PMID. Do not let a next-generation single-arm ORR outrank a replicated RCT for the same axis. The gating step is unchanged: germline-vs-somatic BRCA1. Somatic-only collapses olaparib to off-label in breast, and the somatic-talazoparib expansion (NCT03990896) is still a single-arm 1L-3L cohort, not a phase 3 substitute.RoB 2, deviations from intended interventions: both trials open-label. I accept it because the PFS primary is BICR-adjudicated, but it goes in the ledger.; Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 is still unresolved on tumor NGS and it gates the breast label. The somatic-talazoparib row (NCT03990896) is single-arm, ORR-only, not a randomized readout.; Cumulative MDS/AML risk runs 1-2% across the pooled registrational PARP dataset; serial CBC monitoring is mandatory over a 12-18 month horizon. concensusite——did not pick— advocate3moderateOral, single-agent, guideline-backed the moment the germline BRCA1 test confirms. OlympiAD and EMBRACA sit close on efficacy; talazoparib carries the heavier anemia load, so I put olaparib first because the gentler hematologic margin keeps her on drug longer and slots more cleanly around later liver-directed consolidation. The preference file sets no modality constraint, so oral is my advocacy tilt for a 42-year-old with a curative framing, not a rule I am reading in. As a 1L single agent it honors the efficacy lean without maximizing it, which is why it sits behind the ICI backbone rather than ahead of it.Eligibility gated on germline BRCA1 resolution. A somatic-only call takes her off the OlympiAD/EMBRACA label and onto the somatic-BRCA Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) instead, which is still on-axis and preference-compatible.; Single-agent PARPi is less aggressive than ICI+chemo in 1L; fits the 0.7 weight but does not push it. Reads best as a bridge or as the post-induction maintenance answer.; No toxicity_veto and no modality_constraint in the file, so nothing here breaches a stated preference; the oral-preference framing is advocate judgment, flagged as such.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticqualifiedevidence_qualityOlympiAD and EMBRACA are both registrational, so this is a within-axis quibble, not a dissent. But when the goal is a deep enough response to convert a solitary hepatic met, olaparib's 60% ORR trails talazoparib's 62.6% and, more to the point, talazoparib traps PARP on DNA hardest (pmid:30110579) — I would default to the higher-trapping agent and pay the anemia, not lead with the gentler one and leave response depth on the table. conservativeadvocateendorsetoxicityThis is the pick I have the least to argue with, and choosing olaparib over talazoparib on the hematologic margin is the same read I made. OlympiAD put olaparib G>=3 AEs at 36.6% with anemia the single dominant grade-3 event at 16.1% and discontinuation at 4.9%, and the OlympiA adjuvant dataset (n=1836) showed no MDS/AML excess over placebo at 300 mg BID, which is the safety follow-up window that matters for a 42-year-old who may live years on drug. Only caveat: the germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 call gates the label, so hold the write until germline is confirmed. conservativecriticendorseevidence_qualityWe land on the same top of the order and for compatible reasons: two replicated phase 3 RCTs with a labeled indication beat every abstract-level DDR agent in the dossier, and the critic is right to refuse to let a next-generation single-arm ORR outrank them. The one thing I would add to his ledger from the safety side is the 1-2% cumulative MDS/AML signal across the pooled PARP dataset he already flags, which OlympiA's 300 mg BID follow-up did not show excess of, so the maturity argument cuts in olaparib's favor rather than against it. Same germline gate applies before either of us writes it. concensusitecriticqualifiedguideline_fitWe land on the same pick by different routes: the critic gets there on replicated RoB-2-low RCTs, and NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 plus ESMO class I already encode that exact OlympiAD/EMBRACA read as uniform expert consensus, so the two lenses reinforce rather than the RoB audit standing alone. The qualifier is the one the critic already flags and I want to keep load-bearing: the category-1 status is germline-gated, and a somatic-only BRCA1 call moves olaparib off-label with the somatic-talazoparib row (NCT03990896) being a single-arm cohort, not a category basis. advocatecriticdissentpreference_fitRanking olaparib first on replicated-RCT purity answers a question the preference file did not ask: with prefers_trials true and a curative-intent free_text on a solitary liver lesion, a treatment-naive patient should hear the enrollable options first, and a single-agent 1L PARPi does not chase the conversion depth her genotype earns. I accept the NRG-BR002 point that off-protocol SBRT is negative (HR 1.31, pmid:33885704), and E2108 too (OS HR 1.11, pmid:34995128), for unselected patients, which is exactly why I am pointing at the MSK trial slot rather than off-protocol ablation, not walking the consolidation idea back.

docs.title: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-agnostic, germline-agnostic 1L backbone in BRCA1-mut TNBC) (carboplatin-gemcitabine-brca1)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative3moderateThis is my no-biomarker-needed fallback and the reason it sits at rank 3 rather than lower: it works regardless of how the PD-L1 CPS and germline BRCA1 questions resolve, so it is the one option that cannot be gated out from under the patient. The BRCA1 platinum-sensitivity evidence is direct — in TNT the BRCA-mut subgroup had an ORR of 68.0% on carboplatin vs 33.3% on docetaxel (interaction p=0.01, mPFS HR 0.44) — and carboplatin's myelosuppression is as predictable and management-algorithmed as any cytotoxic we use. As single-agent carboplatin in TNT the G3+ neutropenia was 12% and thrombocytopenia 7%, lower than the combination regimens; adding gemcitabine raises the count but keeps the AE profile inside familiar, dose-modifiable territory. It also doubles as the induction backbone if the board later wants an olaparib or ICI maintenance strategy.Additive myelosuppression from the carbo/gem doublet — day-8 counts drive frequent dose modification; predictable but demands proactive CBC monitoring and a growth-factor plan.; A cytotoxic doublet gives up the OS advantage that the pembrolizumab arm carries if CPS >=10 returns, so this should stay a fallback rather than the default unless the biomarker gates close it off. critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: Talazoparib 1 mg PO daily (EMBRACA, alternate BRCA1-directed PARP inhibitor) (talazoparib-monotherapy-embraca)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative4moderateTalazoparib is the equally-labeled alternative to olaparib and I rank it just below rather than beside it purely on the hematologic-tolerability delta. EMBRACA is a mature registrational RCT (PFS HR 0.54, mPFS 8.6 vs 5.6 mo), so the efficacy is not in question. The reason it is rank 4 and not rank 2 is the AE-grade distribution: G3+ anemia ~39%, neutropenia ~21%, thrombocytopenia ~15% — a substantially heavier hematologic burden than olaparib's 16.1% anemia at comparable PFS. For a patient who may also need myelosuppressive chemo before or after, I prefer the PARP inhibitor that spends less marrow reserve. Same germline gate as olaparib applies. If the patient has a specific reason to favor once-daily dosing or tolerates anemia well, it moves up; otherwise olaparib is the cleaner first PARP choice.Higher-grade hematologic toxicity than olaparib at similar efficacy (G3+ anemia ~39%, thrombocytopenia ~15%) — the deciding factor for ranking it below olaparib rather than beside it.; Germline-restricted label, same as olaparib; a somatic-only BRCA1 call makes this off-label too. critic3highThe second independent phase 3 anchor in the same indication: n=431, PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), p<0.001, low RoB 2. Two sponsors, two molecules, one gating biomarker, replicated direction and magnitude. That mutual replication is what I want to see before I credit an axis, and it is why the PARP RCTs sit above every new DDR agent in the dossier regardless of how clean the mechanism looks on a poster. Ranks below olaparib on tolerability alone: grade >=3 anemia 39% on talazoparib versus 16.1% on olaparib. Evidence quality is at parity with pick 1.Same germline BRCA1 gating as pick 1.; Grade >=3 anemia 39% compresses deliverable dose intensity; a tolerability concern, not an evidence-quality one.; Same open-label RoB 2 caveat; BICR-adjudicated PFS is the mitigation. concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—
