docs.title: Biomarker plan
docs.text:
Recommended assay Rationale Suggested assay provider Tissue requirements Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF and global longitudinal strain A documented pre-treatment LVEF is the precondition for giving doxorubicin, and the LMS-04 schedule carries the anthracycline to a cumulative dose that puts a patient into the cardiotoxicity surveillance band (PMID 35835135). ASCO and the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guideline both call for baseline ventricular imaging, with strain where available, before anthracycline exposure (PMID 27918725; PMID 36017568). Nothing cardiac is on file here, so cycle 1 would otherwise be given with no reference value against which a later fall in function could be read. Treating institution (echocardiography service; no send-out provider) no tissue; transthoracic echocardiogram (5-10 mL blood only if natriuretic peptides are added) Baseline comprehensive metabolic panel with bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, transaminases, creatine kinase and calculated creatinine clearance Trabectedin dosing and its hepatic dose-modification rules run off bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase and transaminases, and hepatotoxicity plus rhabdomyolysis were the dose-limiting toxicities in the registration trial (PMID 26371143). Doxorubicin is also dose-reduced for hyperbilirubinaemia. No laboratory value of any kind was supplied at intake, so there is currently no baseline against which a treatment-emergent transaminase rise could be interpreted. Labcorp Oncology · test info · 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 · 1-800-845-6167 5-10 mL whole blood (serum chemistry); no tumor tissue Baseline CBC with differential, reticulocyte count and ferritin, interpreted against an altitude-adjusted haemoglobin reference Residence at roughly 8,500 ft raises steady-state haemoglobin by an amount that varies by population and is not captured by sea-level reference ranges (PMID 31257609), so a sea-level-normed CBC will make chemotherapy-induced anaemia look milder than it is and will delay transfusion and dose-modification decisions. Grade 3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were both common on the doxorubicin plus trabectedin arm of LMS-04 (PMID 35835135), which makes the pre-treatment counts the reference for every subsequent dose decision. No blood count is on file. Labcorp Oncology · test info · 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 · 1-800-845-6167 3-5 mL whole blood (EDTA); no tumor tissue Baseline pulmonary function tests with DLCO, plus resting and ambulatory pulse oximetry recorded at residence altitude Bilateral infiltrative pulmonary disease in a never-smoker at 8,500 ft needs a measured baseline before induction, because a resting saturation that looks abnormal at sea-level norms may be her physiological steady state, and a saturation that looks acceptable may hide real loss of reserve. The same numbers later decide whether metastasectomy or SBRT is survivable once systemic control is achieved, which the consulting sarcoma oncologist explicitly kept on the table. Without a pre-treatment measurement, any on-treatment desaturation cannot be separated into progression, pneumonitis, or altitude physiology. Treating institution (pulmonary function laboratory; record residence altitude) no tissue; spirometry with DLCO and oximetry Documented clinician-assessed ECOG performance status (with Karnofsky equivalent) recorded at the pre-treatment visit The ECOG of 1 carried through this case was assigned at intake as an assumption, not recorded by a clinician, and the intake note says so explicitly. Nearly every sarcoma trial sets an ECOG ceiling of 1 or 2 at screening, so an undocumented score will either stall an application or produce a screen failure after tissue and time have been spent. It is free to fix and should be written into the chart at the same visit as the pre-induction labs. Treating clinician, at the pre-treatment visit no tissue; clinician assessment at the pre-treatment visit Tumor NGS covering BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM and the wider HRR gene set, with a reported genomic-instability / LOH score Of everything untested here, homologous-recombination status is the entry this histology most earns: olaparib plus temozolomide produced a 27% objective response rate and a median PFS of 6.9 months in pretreated advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma, and 31% of the enrolled patients carried an HRR gene mutation (PMID 37467452). Uterine leiomyosarcoma has a recognised HR-deficient subset including BRCA2 deletion and mutation (PMID 37143137). Skipping it leaves the one non-cytotoxic branch in this case unopened at the point where first-line chemotherapy fails. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE acceptable; the 2024 resection block is preferred for tumor content and volume, with the 2026 lung core held in reserve RNA-based fusion NGS panel covering NTRK1, NTRK2, NTRK3 (and RET, ALK, ROS1 in the same run) This must be an RNA-based assay: NTRK breakpoints sit in large introns and a DNA-only panel misses them, so ordering comprehensive profiling without confirming RNA fusion calling would produce a false negative that reads as a closed question. Prevalence in uterine leiomyosarcoma is very low, but spindle-cell morphology is exactly the setting in which an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm is misclassified, and this tumor was already signed out as a benign leiomyoma once. A positive converts a chemotherapy-only plan into an oral TRK inhibitor with durable response rates. Caris Life Sciences (Whole transcriptome sequencing (MI Profile)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE acceptable; runs on the same 2024 resection block as the DNA panel, no separate procedure Mismatch-repair protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation and BRAF V600E if MLH1 is lost Four stains on a block that is already being cut close a tumor-agnostic PD-1 indication that would otherwise sit open as a question at progression. Uterine leiomyosarcoma is nearly always mismatch-repair proficient, so a negative is the expected result and the value is in settling it cheaply and early. Loss of any one protein in a woman in her thirties also carries Lynch syndrome implications for her and for first-degree relatives, which is a second reason not to leave it unmeasured. NeoGenomics Laboratories (MMR IHC panel) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 4-5 unstained slides from either block, bundled with the other IHC in one cut Validated comprehensive genomic profiling panel reporting TMB in mutations per megabase (with MSI and the BRAF codon 600 call in the same report) TMB here is unknown rather than low, because no sequencing of any kind has been performed. Leiomyosarcoma is copy-number driven and usually low-TMB, so a value at or above 10 mut/Mb would be unusual, but the same order returns MSI, BRAF V600E, the HRR genes and the TP53/RB1/ATRX/MED12 backbone, which makes TMB close to free once the panel is placed. Specify a validated comprehensive assay: a TMB figure from a small hotspot panel does not satisfy the tumor-agnostic indication and is not portable between platforms. Foundation Medicine (FoundationOne CDx) · test info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639 archival FFPE acceptable; same 2024 resection block and same accession as the HRR panel Expert sarcoma pathology review of both specimens with formal grading: mitotic index per 10 high-power fields, coagulative tumor cell necrosis, nuclear atypia, FNCLCC grade, plus an assessment of whether the 2024 block was adequately sampled The diagnosis itself has now been confirmed by a reference laboratory, but the parameters that drive prognosis and trial eligibility (mitotic count, coagulative necrosis, grade) are not on file, and a 6.0 cm myometrial mass handled as a benign leiomyoma in 2024 was very unlikely to have been sampled at the one block per centimetre standard applied to a suspected sarcoma. Major diagnostic revisions occur in a quarter of sarcoma cases sent for expert second opinion (PMID 33061792), and this case has already produced one. Without documented grade and mitotic index, several trial screening forms cannot be completed and the prognostic conversation rests on assumption. MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology · test info · 1515 Holcombe Boulevard, Houston, TX 77030 · 1-877-632-6789 archival FFPE blocks and slides from both specimens; additional levels may be cut from the 2024 block, which will consume tissue HLA class I genotyping at 4-digit (allele-level) resolution Every HLA-restricted agent that could reach this patient names its restricting allele, most often HLA-A*02:01, so without a genotype the PRAME and MAGE-A4 rows sit as unassessable rather than negative. It is a blood draw that spends no tumor tissue and costs little, and the result either opens the TCR-T and ImmTAC class for later consideration or closes it cleanly. Ordering it now avoids a two-step delay if she progresses through first-line chemotherapy while a trial slot is open. Histogenetics (Allele-level HLA class I typing) · test info · 300 Executive Boulevard, Ossining, NY 10562 · 1-914-762-0400 5-10 mL whole blood (ACD or EDTA) or a buccal swab; no tumor tissue consumed B7-H3 (CD276) IHC on tumor tissue B7-H3 carries the best odds of a positive result of any surface target in this histology: 97% of soft tissue sarcomas stained positive and about 69% were high in a 153-patient series across 15 subtypes (PMID 39478506). Nothing is approved against it, so a positive buys trial access rather than a prescription, but the ADC and bispecific programs generally require documented expression at screening and a later referral should not stall while tissue is hunted down. Expression is spatially heterogeneous, which argues for reading the larger resection rather than the core alone. NeoGenomics Laboratories (Custom IHC / pharma services) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2-3 unstained slides, bundled into the same block cut as the MMR, PD-L1 and HER2 stains Retrieval of the ER and PR IHC report: specimen of origin (2024 uterine resection versus 2026 lung core), antibody clone, scoring system and internal control adequacy ER and PR are recorded as confirmed at <1%, and that negative closes a door which is genuinely open in this histology: letrozole met its activity criterion in ER and/or PR-positive uterine leiomyosarcoma, with the longest PFS in tumors staining strongly and diffusely (PMID 24222211). Before a foreclosure of that weight is relied on, the report should state which specimen was stained, which clone was used and whether the internal control worked, because a failed stain on an old block reads identically to a true negative at the <1% cutoff. This is a records step rather than a new assay, and it costs nothing but a phone call. MD Anderson Cancer Center, Department of Pathology · test info · 1515 Holcombe Boulevard, Houston, TX 77030 · 1-877-632-6789 no new tissue; existing report and stained slides retrieved from the originating laboratory TP53, RB1, ATRX and MED12 status from the comprehensive tumor NGS panel These four genes are the mutational backbone of uterine leiomyosarcoma on exome sequencing (PMID 26891131) and they ride along free on the panel already being ordered for HRR, TMB and MSI. ATRX loss in particular tracks with the alternative lengthening of telomeres phenotype, aggressive histology and shorter survival in leiomyosarcoma (PMID 25229770), so it feeds the prognostic conversation and the urgency of the treatment plan. None of the four is directly druggable today, which is why this is a high rather than an essential row. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 no additional tissue; reported from the same 2024 resection accession as the HRR and TMB panel Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report and gross pathology description: route of hysterectomy, whether power or manual morcellation was used, specimen integrity and margin status A 6.0 cm myometrial mass removed as a presumed benign fibroid in 2024 may have been morcellated, and morcellation of an unrecognised leiomyosarcoma disperses tumor through the peritoneum and has been linked to worse outcomes (PMID 28209496; PMID 26646120). The current staging picture is pulmonary only; if the specimen was disrupted, peritoneal and pelvic disease has to be actively excluded rather than assumed absent. The answer sits in an operative note that nobody has yet had reason to re-read. Records request to the 2024 institution (pair with the block release) no tissue; operative note and gross description from the September 2024 hysterectomy Pre-treatment CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with measurable RECIST target lesions, read against any imaging from the September 2024 to July 2026 interval Induction has not started, so there is still a clean window to fix a pre-treatment baseline with named target lesions; once cycle 1 is given, that window is gone and response assessment becomes an argument about which prior scan counts. Any imaging from the 23-month interval would bound the growth rate of the pulmonary disease, which is the closest thing available to a measure of tempo in a systemic-therapy-naive patient. The infiltrative, possibly inflammatory appearance also needs to be documented before treatment, because it will complicate the reading of every subsequent scan. Treating institution (radiology); request 2024-2026 outside imaging on disc no tissue; contrast-enhanced CT, with prior outside imaging requested on disc Germline multigene hereditary cancer panel including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM, TP53 and the Lynch genes A germline result matters twice over here: it settles whether any somatic HRR finding is inherited, and at 39 with a high-grade sarcoma it carries direct implications for her siblings, children and any future pregnancy decisions. Uterine leiomyosarcoma is part of the Li-Fraumeni tumor spectrum, so TP53 belongs on the panel rather than being inferred from a somatic result. Somatic-only testing leaves this open, which is why the blood panel should go out alongside the tumor panel rather than as a reflex after it. Myriad Genetics (MyRisk Hereditary Cancer Test) · test info · 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 1-800-469-7423 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA); drawn on the same visit as HLA typing Repeat ER and PR IHC on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core, reported with percentage and intensity rather than a binary call If the <1% result came off the 2024 uterine primary, it describes a specimen taken 23 months and one metastatic step away from the disease being treated, and hormone receptor expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma is not uniformly retained between primary and metastasis. The letrozole trial selected on ER and/or PR positivity and found the longest PFS in strongly and diffusely positive tumors (PMID 24222211), so the question worth answering is not positive versus negative but whether any meaningful expression exists on current disease. If the original stain was already run on the lung core with working controls, skip this row. NeoGenomics Laboratories (ER / PR IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core, added to the same block cut as the other IHC PRAME IHC on archival tissue, ordered only if HLA class I typing returns a restricting allele PRAME cannot be called in either direction right now, because neither the antigen nor the restricting HLA allele has been tested. Sequence the two: if HLA typing returns A*02:01, PRAME IHC gates entry to the ImmTAC and TCR-T programs, and if it does not, this row closes with no tissue spent. Reported PRAME expression in leiomyosarcoma runs below the levels seen in synovial sarcoma, so a negative stain would not be surprising. NeoGenomics Laboratories (PRAME IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides, ideally from the 2024 resection to preserve the lung core MAGE-A4 IHC on archival tissue, ordered only if HLA class I typing returns a restricting allele MAGE-A4 stays unknown until the HLA type is back, since the whole class is allele-restricted. Even a positive stain would not make her eligible for afamitresgene autoleucel, which was studied and licensed in synovial sarcoma and myxoid round cell liposarcoma rather than in sarcoma generally (PMID 38554725), so the realistic destination is a MAGE-A4 solid-tumor TCR-T trial of the kind run across histologies in HLA-A*02-positive patients (PMID 36624315). Stain it in the same antigen set as PRAME rather than as a separate order. NeoGenomics Laboratories (MAGE-A4 IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides from the same cut as the PRAME stain RAD51 foci immunofluorescence assay for functional homologous-recombination deficiency In NCI protocol 10250 the RAD51 functional assay, not the mutation list, was what separated outcomes: median PFS was 11.2 months in homologous-recombination-deficient tumors versus 5.4 months in proficient ones (PMID 37467452). That makes it the most direct read on whether this tumor would benefit from olaparib plus temozolomide, and it can be positive in tumors with no HRR gene mutation. Clinical availability is the problem: it is largely an academic and research assay with no widely offered CLIA version, which is why this ranks medium rather than essential. Discovery Life Sciences · test info · 601 Genome Way, Huntsville, AL 35806 archival FFPE; feasibility should be confirmed with the receiving laboratory before slides are cut ATRX IHC on both the September 2024 primary and the 2026 pulmonary metastasis Paired sequencing of both blocks was floated and is not worth the cost here: no systemic therapy was given in the 23-month interval, so there is no treatment-driven selection pressure to have produced genomic divergence, and the 2024 resection has the tumor content the panel needs. Paired ATRX IHC is the cheap version of the same question, and ATRX loss with the ALT phenotype tracks with aggressive histology and shorter survival in leiomyosarcoma (PMID 25229770). Two stains on blocks already being cut will show whether the primary is representative of the metastatic disease. NeoGenomics Laboratories (ATRX IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 1-2 unstained slides from each block, bundled with the other IHC PD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system matched to the intended agent, plus CD3 and CD8 T-cell infiltrate density, on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core PD-L1 gates no approval in soft tissue sarcoma, so this informs rather than decides, and the results that would actually open checkpoint blockade for her are MSI and TMB. It earns a row because the pulmonary lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and someone will ask whether that appearance reflects an immune infiltrate or tumor growth pattern; a CD3 and CD8 read on the lung core answers that directly. Run it on the 2026 metastasis rather than the 2024 primary, since current immune phenotype is the point. NeoGenomics Laboratories (PD-L1 IHC (22C3, 28-8, SP142, SP263) with CD3 / CD8) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 3-4 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core, bundled with the MMR and B7-H3 stains

Decision support, not medical advice. Confirm assay availability and current standards with the treating team and the local pathology service.

docs.title: Workup considerations
docs.text:
The rank-1 row below carries the gating items. These non-gating or conditional items from the target-validation report belong alongside it, ordered so the 2024 block is cut once:

  • Expert sarcoma pathology review of both specimens with formal grading (mitotic index, coagulative necrosis, FNCLCC grade). A 6.0 cm mass handled as a benign fibroid was very unlikely to have been sampled at the one-block-per-centimetre standard, and major revisions occur in about a quarter of sarcoma second opinions (PMID 33061792). Order the deeper levels before the molecular orders exhaust the block.
  • ER/PR provenance check, then a conditional restain. The letrozole trial that keeps aromatase inhibition alive in ER-positive uLMS found durable benefit only in tumours staining above 90% (PMID 24222211), so the <1% negative genuinely forecloses the endocrine branch, but only if the stain was run on current disease with working controls. A failed stain on a 2024 block reads identically to a true negative. If the result came off the primary, repeat ER/PR on the 2026 lung core with percentage and intensity reported.
  • TP53, RB1, ATRX and MED12 ride along free on the NGS panel (PMID 26891131); ATRX loss with the ALT phenotype tracks with aggressive histology and shorter survival (PMID 25229770). Paired ATRX IHC on both blocks answers whether the 2024 primary represents the 2026 disease for the price of two stains.
  • PD-L1 with CD3/CD8 on the lung core answers whether the infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic read reflects an immune infiltrate; it gates nothing on its own.
  • HLA class I typing (blood draw) with reflex PRAME and MAGE-A4 IHC only if a restricting allele returns; this prices the TCR-T and ImmTAC class without spending tissue speculatively.
  • The RAD51-foci functional HRD assay that best separated outcomes in the PARP trial has no CLIA provider anywhere; do not hold the somatic panel for it, and ask any PARP-trial site whether they run it at screening.
  • Pre-treatment CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with named RECIST target lesions, plus a request for any 2024-2026 interval imaging on disc. Once cycle 1 is given, the clean baseline window is gone.
  • Two tumor-agnostic doors open through this same workup and would be approved, on-label care if positive: an NTRK fusion would gate a TRK inhibitor (ORR 79% pooled, PMID 32105622) and TMB >=10 mut/Mb or dMMR would gate pembrolizumab (PMID 32919526). Both are rare in uLMS and cheap to close; either positive would route to the standard-of-care surface, not this table.

docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text: 29 trial rows, 25 clinical-evidence rows, 37 preclinical rows, 15 biomarker-survey rows, 23 target-validation rows and 32 accessibility rows feed this synthesis, alongside five board positions and twenty cross-critiques. This page is the Experimental table, one of two co-equal therapeutic surfaces; approved and guideline-carried options (gemcitabine + docetaxel, pazopanib, eribulin, trabectedin monotherapy, metastasectomy and SBRT among them) belong to the separate Standard-of-care table, which runs after this synthesis. The table holds 23 rows: a rank-1 shared workup, five ranked therapeutic options, one pick recorded as considered-and-declined, and sixteen feature-targeting investigational options surfaced with a flag for why they are not ranked. Agreement scores run from 1.0 down to -0.4. Zero vetoes were issued; all five personas ranked LMS-04 first and all five carried the olaparib + temozolomide branch, the board's only two unanimous calls. The one pre-registered veto, from the conservative against induction scheduled over the missing baseline battery, was withdrawn in round 2 with an explicit re-arm clause, and the three phase-1 doors each drew dissent from at least two chairs.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
Two things shape every rank on this page, and neither is a drug. First: induction is imminent and not one baseline exists. No LVEF, no ECOG documented by a clinician, no CBC, no PFTs, no liver panel, days before an anthracycline in a patient whose 8,500 ft residence bends every sea-level reference range. The echocardiogram and the documented ECOG were LMS-04 eligibility criteria and are true gates on cycle 1; the rest are baselines that run alongside it, and the conservative's withdrawn veto re-arms the day a cycle 1 date is placed ahead of the echocardiogram. Second: the molecular landscape is entirely unmeasured, and HRR/HRD status (tissue NGS with a germline panel, 2-3 week turnaround) gates the only non-cytotoxic ranked branch. An RNA-inclusive panel, one IHC block and one blood draw open or close nearly every targeted option in this dossier, and all of it runs in parallel with induction at zero cost in treatment days.

  • This ranking is scoped to the stated targetable features, and it is one of two co-equal tables. The Experimental table carries feature-targeting investigational options only: the off-label first-line LMS-04 regimen, the HRD-conditional PARP branch, and the stain- or scan-gated phase-1 doors. Guideline-carried options for this disease, including the gemcitabine + docetaxel fallback if cardiopulmonary screening fails and the pazopanib second-line anchor, live on the Standard-of-care table and were deliberately not ranked here.
  • If HRR/HRD testing returns proficient, the rank-3 conditional branch is foreclosed for practical purposes: expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month proficient arm and the off-label payer case collapses with it. The scenario-independent rows (ranks 2, 4, 5, 6) are unaffected. Beyond this table, standard-of-care for metastatic uLMS lies outside Libby's targetable-feature ranking and should be pursued through the treating team's normal care channel and the Standard-of-care page.
  • The lung-directed consolidation branch every persona carried (metastasectomy or SBRT after systemic control) is gated twice before it is real: the September 2024 operative report must settle the morcellation question, because BSG 2025 states morcellation is contraindicated in uterine sarcoma and the Park series logged abdominopelvic dissemination in 44% vs 12.9% (PMID 21565389), so if morcellation happened, peritoneal restaging comes before any consolidation planning; and her current bilateral infiltrative anatomy is exactly what the surgical series screened out. The branch is a question to re-ask if induction converts the anatomy, not a survival number to quote today.
  • Workup logistics: the 2024 resection block is the right specimen for the molecular work (more tumor, no intervening therapy) and it should be allocated across pathology review, NGS and the IHC set in one conversation before any single order exhausts it. The germline TP53 draw goes out before cycle 1 per ERN GENTURIS, and only after the consent conversation it actually is; a records request to the 2024 institution covers the operative report and the block release in one letter.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• First-line cytotoxic backbone, off-label at this line: doxorubicin + trabectedin with maintenance (PMID 35835135, PMID 39231341, NCT02997358); the nearest confirmatory read, unreported (NCT06088290); the only randomized maintenance question, Taiwan-only (NCT06981637).
  • PARP/HRD branch, biomarker-conditional: olaparib + temozolomide (PMID 37467452, NCT03880019, NCT05432791), the uLMS HRD subset (PMID 37143137) and the RAD51 functional assay (PMID 30377213); a preclinical trabectedin + olaparib synergy note (PMID 28454547).
  • Surface-target phase-1 doors, all gated on unmeasured markers: B7-H3 ADCs (NCT06242470, PMID 39478506, PMID 37775116); FAP radioligands (NCT07156565, NCT04939610, PMID 35608703, PMID 23712432); CDK7 inhibition after RB1-null IHC (NCT07633756, PMID 31883968).
  • Workup and staging anchors: morcellation cohorts (PMID 24923260, PMID 21565389), germline TP53 timing (PMID 32457520), sarcoma NGS standing (PMID 38834388), guideline texts (PMID 38734790, PMID 34303806).
  • Routed to the Standard-of-care table, not ranked here: gemcitabine + docetaxel (PMID 28882536, PMID 18534250), pazopanib, eribulin, trabectedin monotherapy, doxorubicin + ifosfamide, and lung-directed local therapy (PMID 9011700, PMID 21867989, PMID 32588468, PMID 25686482).

docs.title: Rank 1. Gating workup run alongside cycle 1
docs.text: What it resolves: the two true gates on induction (LVEF, documented ECOG), the germline TP53 answer before the anthracycline plan is fixed, the morcellation question that gates lung-directed consolidation, and the molecular landscape that opens or closes every targeted branch below.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: This is a requisition set and two records requests rather than a therapy, so its evidence is the eligibility criteria and guideline text of what it opens. Baseline LVEF and ECOG 0-1 were eligibility criteria of the trial the planned regimen comes from (NCT02997358); neither exists in her chart. ERN GENTURIS 2020 puts germline TP53 testing before genotoxic chemotherapy, ideally with the result in hand before the cumulative anthracycline plan is fixed (PMID 32457520), and uLMS sits in the Li-Fraumeni tumor spectrum. The ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group now recommends tumor NGS in sarcoma (PMID 38834388), which makes the panel guideline-backed workup rather than clinician preference. On morcellation, two retrospective cohorts point the same way: adjusted HR 3.18 (1.5-6.8) for recurrence (PMID 24923260) and abdominopelvic dissemination 44% vs 12.9% (PMID 21565389), replication across two health systems with the size confounder running toward the null, and BSG 2025 cites the same series when it calls morcellation contraindicated in uterine sarcoma (PMID 38734790).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: As a gate it does not have a response rate; it has a decision yield, and the yield is high. The echocardiogram and ECOG either clear the planned regimen or trigger the fallback conversation on the standard-of-care surface. The panel and IHC block price the PARP branch, all three phase-1 doors, the two tumor-agnostic approvals, and the representativeness of the 2024 block, in one pass, inside the induction window.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Nothing from the assays: blood draws, an echocardiogram, stains on archival tissue, a CT, and two records requests.
  • The cost is scheduling, and the tiering keeps it from becoming delay: LVEF, ECOG and the hepatic-renal panel are gates; DLCO, ferritin, reticulocytes and altitude oximetry are baselines that run alongside cycle 1. Veto-grading a baseline would delay induction in a patient who already lost 23 months to a misread pathology report.
  • No toxicity vetoes exist to check against, because no preferences were stated.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was effectively unanimous; the round-2 argument was about tiering and sequence, not about whether to run any of it. The conservative's pre-registered veto (induction scheduled over the missing battery) was withdrawn because the dossier shows induction imminent and the battery undone, not a cycle 1 date placed over the missing tests; its re-arm clause survives into this synthesis verbatim. The risktaker's gates-versus-baselines distinction governs the tiering above. The concensusite moved the germline draw ahead of cycle 1 on ERN GENTURIS, and the advocate's correction is kept with it: germline TP53 is a consent conversation with consequences for her relatives, and whether she wants that information at all has never been asked.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Send the somatic and germline panels together, not in sequence, and draw HLA typing on the same venipuncture. Specify RNA-inclusive fusion calling on the requisition (several widely used panels are DNA-only, and an NTRK false negative would read as a closed question). Record the residence altitude on the CBC and oximetry requisitions and have the adjusted reference interval stated in the chart. One letter to the 2024 institution covers the operative report and the block release. Agree the tissue allocation across pathology review, NGS and the IHC set in one conversation.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 1 because the echocardiogram and ECOG gate cycle 1 of the rank-2 regimen, the germline result should precede the anthracycline plan, and the panel decides whether the rank-3 branch exists. The agreement score of 1.0 is real rather than ceremonial: every persona ordered some version of this, and the only disputes were about which items may not wait.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Workup item What it gates Turnaround / tissue Reference Echocardiogram with LVEF (strain if available) Doxorubicin; LMS-04 eligibility; the conservative's re-arm clause Same day to 1 week; no tissue NCT02997358 Clinician-documented ECOG LMS-04 fitness call; nearly every trial door Next clinic visit NCT03880019 Hepatic-renal panel with CK Trabectedin dosing and dose-modification rules 24-48 h; blood PMID 26371143 Germline TP53 (with HRR genes and Lynch genes), after consent conversation Anthracycline planning in a possible carrier; cascade testing 2-4 weeks; blood PMID 32457520 September 2024 operative report + gross description The lung-directed consolidation branch; abdominopelvic surveillance field Days; records request PMID 24923260, PMID 21565389 Tumor NGS with HRR/BRCA2, LOH score, TMB, MSI + RNA fusion calling (2024 block) Rank 3; TRK and pembrolizumab tumor-agnostic doors 2-3 weeks; archival FFPE PMID 38834388 One-pass IHC block: MMR, B7-H3, RB1, PD-L1/CD3/CD8, ER/PR provenance ± restain Ranks 4 and 6; checkpoint context; endocrine foreclosure integrity 1 week; archival FFPE PMID 39478506 HLA class I typing, allele-level PRAME/MAGE-A4 TCR-T and ImmTAC class (reflex stains only if positive) 1-2 weeks; blood NCT03686124 CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin; PFTs with DLCO; oximetry at 8,500 ft; RECIST baseline CT Dose-modification and transfusion thresholds; later consolidation math; response assessment 1 week; run alongside cycle 1 PMID 31257609

docs.title: Rank 2. Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04), first line
docs.text: The planned regimen and the best-evidenced option are the same regimen: the largest replicated effect in the dossier, bought with the heaviest first-line toxicity profile and an off-label authorization.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: LMS-04 is the only RCT-grade, indication-matched result in this dossier and it survived the critic's scrutiny: randomized phase 3, n=150, first-line metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, median PFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months with doxorubicin alone (adjusted HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.58, p<0.0001) on a pre-specified primary read by blinded independent central review (PMID 35835135). The 55-month final analysis held on survival: median OS 33 vs 24 months, adjusted HR 0.65 (0.44-0.95) (PMID 39231341). RoB2 Low. The limitations are equally plain: uterine primaries were 67 of 150, a stratified subgroup with no separately powered effect estimate; 107 deaths among 150 patients puts the OS upper bound at 0.95, so the survival claim is real but not robust to one contradicting trial; and no replication exists yet, with SaLuDo (NCT06088290) the nearest confirmatory read and unreported.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: High, for a patient who clears the gates. This is her exact population (first line, LMS, chemo-naive), the effect held at both endpoints, and the EORTC pooled prognostic model reads her age, line and long interval since initial diagnosis as favourable (p=0.0004 for the time-lapse covariate, PMID 10458228). The critic's qualifier on that last point is adopted: the covariate was measured in patients whose sarcoma had been diagnosed and followed, whereas her 23-month interval encodes a pathology error, so it stands as reassurance about tempo and not as a number to quote her. How much the maintenance phase contributes to the 12.2 months is unmeasured, because continuation was never randomised against stopping.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Combination arm: grade 3-4 neutropenia 80% (vs 13% doxorubicin alone), thrombocytopenia 47% (vs 0%), febrile neutropenia 28% (vs 9%). Primary G-CSF prophylaxis belongs in the cycle 1 orders, not discovered at cycle 2.
  • One treatment-related death in the trial, in the doxorubicin-alone arm.
  • Maintenance-phase safety is the published gap: NCT02997358 has no posted results and the 2024 report gives no per-term rates, so monitoring defaults to the single-agent trabectedin dossier: G>=3 ALT elevation 25%, rhabdomyolysis 1.2%, treatment-related deaths 2.1% (PMID 26371143); CK and LFTs stay on the recurring schedule through maintenance, with the uLMS subset mirroring the parent trial (PMID 28651804).
  • At 39, cumulative anthracycline exposure is a lifetime ledger; the dexrazoxane and dose-cap conversation belongs before cycle 1.
  • Altitude effects cut across all of it: a polycythemic baseline masks chemotherapy anaemia against sea-level ranges (PMID 31257609), and her presenting dyspnea cannot be split between disease, pneumonitis and altitude without the measured local baseline ordered at rank 1.
  • No stated toxicity vetoes exist to check against. The advocate's consent gap stands: the 80%/28% trade has never been put to her.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent and no veto; this was the board's one unanimous therapeutic call across all five chairs, and the qualified round-2 rows were boundary-setting rather than objection. The conservative's withdrawn veto and its re-arm clause are documented at rank 1. The nearest thing to a mechanism concern is the maintenance design itself: the preclinical basis for the pairing was additive at best (combination indices just under 1, PMID 12783202), no preclinical support for the maintenance phase exists at all, and an untested continuation can accrue hepatotoxicity without measurable contribution. That is an evidence gap inside an endorsed regimen, and it is priced into the monitoring plan rather than the rank.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: First-line use is off-label: the trabectedin label requires a prior anthracycline and she is naive, so the prior authorization is filed as off-label from day one, citing PMID 35835135 and PMID 39231341, because a payer denial is the one thing that could actually delay induction. The guideline picture is adoption lag and reimbursement, not opposition, and it should be stated precisely: BSG 2025 keeps single-agent doxorubicin at grade I,A and records the combination as "not yet supported by NICE" (PMID 38734790); ESMO's operative STS guideline is the 2021 edition and predates the trial (PMID 34303806); NCCN carriage is confirmed only through secondary sources behind a login wall (PMID 38994959), so this page quotes no NCCN category. No society text argues against the regimen. If the echocardiogram or pulmonary reserve fails, the fallback conversation (gemcitabine + docetaxel) lives on the Standard-of-care table.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Rank 2 only because the workup gates it; among therapies it is first without argument. Agreement 1.0, the largest effect size in the dossier, and the board's rare case where the aggressive option and the best-evidenced option coincide. The gap to rank 3 is categorical rather than incremental: rank 3 is conditional on a biomarker nobody has measured and on this regimen having already been used.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Doxorubicin + trabectedin vs doxorubicin, 1L LMS (n=150) mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 mo, aHR 0.41 (0.29-0.58) G3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, FN 28% PMID 35835135 Same trial, final OS at 55 months mOS 33 vs 24 mo, aHR 0.65 (0.44-0.95) AEs and dose reductions more frequent; no per-term maintenance rates PMID 39231341 Trial registration (LMS-04) No posted results Maintenance-phase safety not publicly retrievable NCT02997358 Trabectedin monotherapy vs dacarbazine (maintenance monitoring proxy, n=518) mPFS HR 0.55 G>=3 ALT 25%, rhabdomyolysis 1.2%, treatment-related deaths 2.1% PMID 26371143 uLMS subset of the same trial (n=232) mPFS HR 0.57 Cytopenias and transaminitis; 2 treatment-related deaths in subset PMID 28651804

docs.title: Rank 3. Olaparib + temozolomide, queued for first progression
docs.text: Conditional on hrd:positive. Foreclosed for practical purposes if HRR/HRD testing returns proficient: expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month arm and the off-label case collapses with it.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: NCI protocol 10250 pre-specified a one-stage binomial bar of five or more responses in 22 patients and hit it: ORR 27% overall, best ORR within 6 months 23%, median PFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE) in pretreated advanced uLMS, with responses lasting around a year (PMID 37467452, NCT03880019). Everything past that is hypothesis-grade: n=22, single arm, no comparator, an erratum on the record, and the RAD51-foci split everyone quotes (mPFS 11.2 vs 5.4 months by functional HR status, p=0.05) comes from 9 of 18 evaluable patients in an exploratory analysis sitting exactly on the alpha boundary with no multiplicity control. The biology behind the branch is real: uLMS carries a recognised HR-deficient subset, and in the reference series confirmed HRD ran 5 of 58 tumours, every confirmed case a homozygous BRCA2 deletion (PMID 37143137); BRCA2-deleted uLMS PDX models respond to PARP inhibition, and the RAD51 assay itself calls PARP response beyond BRCA mutation (PMID 30377213).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, assuming the positive branch: if her tumor lands in the HRD subset, this is the strongest second-line bet in the disease, oral and potentially durable, with the exploratory split suggesting the deficient stratum carries most of the 27%. If the panel returns proficient, expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month arm, and this rec is foreclosed as a preferred branch rather than merely discounted. The stratifier that produced the 11.2-month figure cannot be measured on her: the RAD51 functional assay has no CLIA provider anywhere, so the orderable substitute is HRR sequencing, and presenting the panel as the same test that generated the split would be false.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade 3-4 neutropenia is published two ways in the same trial: 75% in the abstract, 13/22 (59%) for the neutropenia term in full-text Table 2. A 16-point gap between two published figures for one event in a 22-patient trial is a reporting problem, and both numbers belong in the consent conversation.
  • Thrombocytopenia 32%, anemia 32%; dose reductions were frequent, 3/22 discontinued for toxicity, no treatment-related deaths.
  • The stacking risk is the practical brake: this marrow will have just absorbed an induction that ran 80% grade 3-4 neutropenia. A documented CBC recovery threshold precedes any prescription.
  • No stated toxicity vetoes exist to check against.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: All five personas carried the branch (board ranks 2 through 5), so there is no dissent to override; the critic's round-2 row was a qualified agreement that sharpened the consent language rather than the rank. Its ruling is adopted whole: the rank was already set by the n=22 single-arm design, the toxicity discrepancy changes the sentence she hears and the CBC threshold, and both figures are quoted. The mechanism-level caveat is the biomarker asymmetry itself: in an HR-proficient tumor the synergy premise collapses toward temozolomide alone, in a disease where single-agent dacarbazine managed 9% in a randomized setting.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Both dedicated trials are active-not-recruiting (NCT03880019, NCT05432791), so the interim route is an off-label combination authorization built on one phase 2, anchored to a positive HRR result; an unmeasured HRD status makes the payer case and the clinical case equally weak, which is exactly why the panel goes out now. The randomized successor's eligibility (two or more prior lines including an anthracycline, no prior temozolomide or dacarbazine) constrains sequencing between now and any reopening. Oral administration would matter if she cares about infusion-chair time; nobody knows whether she does.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below the induction regimen because it is a next-line branch conditional on a biomarker nobody has measured, and above every phase-1 door because it is the only experimental option with response data in her exact histology. The agreement gap is wide: 1.0 here versus -0.2 for the best of the phase-1 rows.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Olaparib + temozolomide, advanced uLMS >=1 prior line (n=22) ORR 27%; mPFS 6.9 mo (5.4-NE); RAD51-deficient split 11.2 vs 5.4 mo (exploratory) G3-4 neutropenia 75% (abstract) vs 59% (Table 2); thrombocytopenia 32%; anemia 32% PMID 37467452 Randomized successor, uLMS >=2 prior lines incl. anthracycline Active, not recruiting; no results — NCT05432791

docs.title: Rank 4. B7-H3 ADC approach (MGC026), stain-gated referral at second line or later
docs.text: One stain on the 2024 block decides whether the most reachable experimental door is worth booking; the class carries a terminated predecessor and no LMS response data.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: B7-H3 is the surface target most likely to actually be present in this histology: 97% of 153 soft-tissue sarcomas stained positive across 15 subtypes, and 69% at high level (PMID 39478506). The duocarmycin bystander data say heterogeneous expression is survivable for this drug class (PMID 37775116), and MGC026 is recruiting US sites with sarcoma on the named cohort list and no expression gate (NCT06242470). What does not exist: any B7-H3 agent response data in leiomyosarcoma, or any LMS model for the class in this dossier. The critic's precision point governs how the prevalence number is read: efficacy in the CAR-T antigen-density work fell away below an expression threshold (PMID 30655315), so the 69% high-level stratum is the operative number, not the 97%.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown, honestly. A strong positive stain raises the odds the target is drug-reachable; it does not supply a response estimate, because none exists in this disease for any agent in the class. The gating stain costs two slides off a block already being cut, which is why the screen is ranked even though the treatment cannot yet be priced.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No published MGC026 grade profile; ADC-class cytopenias and infusion reactions are the expectation.
  • The class carries a corpse: the predecessor vobramitamab duocarmazine was halted after safety findings in prostate cancer (NCT05551117). Payload liability is the live question for the whole class until the successor's own data answer it.
  • Any referral follows documented marrow recovery from induction, on a CBC that currently does not exist.
  • No stated toxicity vetoes exist to check against.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The risktaker alone ranked it. The critic's dissent (filed against the CDK7 pick but naming ranks 4 and 5 explicitly) is carried here at full weight: positivity is not dependency, and no LMS model exists for any B7-H3 agent. The conservative's dissent on the FAP row extends here by its own words, the missing-baseline problem, minus the on-target marrow signal. The synthesis accepts both and keeps the row as a screen: the objections price the referral, not the stain.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Run B7-H3 IHC in the bundled one-pass block cut at rank 1. No standardised clinical scoring exists, so a local result is a screening signal that may need repeating on the sponsor's assay. The advocate's hold applies to this and every trial door: no referral gets booked until her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft are asked directly, because prefers_trials: true came from intake, not from her.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Top of the phase-1 block because its gate has the best prior of a positive (69% high-level expression in sarcoma) and its liability is class-historical rather than on-target. It sits below rank 3 by a wide agreement gap (-0.2 vs 1.0) and above the FAP row on the marrow-stroma distinction.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference MGC026, advanced solid tumors incl. named sarcoma cohort Phase 1 dose escalation; no readout No published grade profile NCT06242470

docs.title: Rank 5. FAP-targeted alpha radioligand ([225Ac]RTX-2358), FAPi-PET-gated screen at progression
docs.text: A forward-running gate at zero tissue cost: the PET either finds the target or closes the branch. The open safety question is marrow-stroma dosimetry.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Sarcoma sits near the top of the FAP expression range, and unusually the antigen is on the malignant cells themselves rather than only stroma: tumour-cell FAP at intensity >=2 in 50.7% of sarcomas, the malignant cell being fibroblastic (PMID 37333052). Radioligand crossfire does not depend on the antigen homogeneity that undermines ADC and cell-therapy cutoffs, and the beta-emitting sibling compound produced regressions in sarcoma PDX models (PMID 35608703), with combined-isotope preclinical work extending the class (PMID 39237746). NCT07156565 is recruiting relapsed/refractory soft-tissue sarcoma after one prior line, FAP-positivity established by FAPi PET. No human sarcoma efficacy exists for this agent.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown for treatment effect; well-defined for the screen. The PET scan settles whether the target exists at no tissue cost, and a negative closes the branch cleanly. That gate direction is the reason this row outranks the CDK7 door: a positive scan means the target is there, where the RB1 stain mostly routes toward an arm with no LMS data.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No human grade profile for [225Ac]RTX-2358; radioligand-class cytopenias are expected.
  • The on-target concern is real and specific: FAP sits on bone marrow stromal cells, FAP-directed CAR-T caused cachexia and lethal marrow toxicity in mice, and human marrow stromal cells were recognised by the same cells (PMID 23712432). A renally cleared peptide is a different exposure question from a persisting engineered T cell, but that distinction is an argument for dosimetry the trial has not yet generated.
  • Sequencing an alpha emitter after an induction that ran 80% grade 3-4 neutropenia requires documented marrow recovery. ECOG 0-1 is required against an ECOG that was assumed, never documented.
  • No stated toxicity vetoes exist to check against.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The conservative dissented, and its objection is the strongest single argument in the phase-1 block: an alpha emitter pointed at a target expressed on marrow stroma, in a patient whose CBC has never been drawn, straight after heavy myelosuppression. The risktaker's counters are also real: the exposure biology differs from CAR-T, the tumour-cell expression prior is decent, and the PET gate costs nothing. The critic's prevalence-is-not-dependency pattern critique applies here as at rank 4. The adjudication keeps the option as a screen-first branch: the scan and the marrow baseline are cheap and already ordered; any treatment decision waits on human dosimetry from the trial and a recovered CBC.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Screen the month LMS-04 progresses; the FAPi PET is the entire eligibility question and can be scheduled around the restaging scan. The beta-emitter LuMIERE route (NCT04939610) runs on the same PET gate and may be the gentler first pass if uptake confirms; it is consolidated into this row rather than ranked separately. The advocate's referral hold applies unchanged.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Below B7-H3 because the marrow-stroma signal is an on-target liability the ADC class does not carry, above REC-617 because the gate runs forward and the physics does not depend on a response estimate that does not exist. Agreement -0.2 with the dissent adjudicated rather than dismissed.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference [225Ac]RTX-2358, R/R soft-tissue sarcoma, FAPi-PET-positive Phase 1 dose escalation; no readout No human grade profile; marrow-stroma dosimetry pending NCT07156565 [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286, advanced solid tumors with FAP-2286 uptake (LuMIERE) Phase 1/2; no sarcoma readout No sarcoma grade profile NCT04939610

docs.title: Rank 6. REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line
docs.text: A one-slide stain opens a first-in-class door, but the gate runs backwards in this histology: RB1 loss is near-universal, and the arm it routes to holds no LMS data.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: NCT07633756 is a phase 1b of a selective CDK7 inhibitor recruiting RB1-negative metastatic leiomyosarcoma after at least one prior systemic line, single site, safety and RP2D primary. No CDK7 data of any kind exist in leiomyosarcoma at any phase. The mechanistic case, replication-stress vulnerability in RB1-null tumors, is borrowed from YKL-5-124 in RB1/TP53-null small-cell lung cancer, a different compound in a different lineage (PMID 31883968).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown, with the structure of the bet working against her. Because RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology, the IHC most often routes a patient into the arm with zero efficacy data rather than away from it, which is a strange way to design a decision and is why the risktaker itself conceded the pick belongs below B7-H3. Dose escalation adds the standard risk of a subtherapeutic dose.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No published REC-617 grade profile; CDK7-class cytopenias and GI toxicity are the expectation, with a safety primary endpoint doing the characterizing.
  • Requires a biopsy-amenable lesion and RECIST-measurable disease, both uncertain against her infiltrative pulmonary pattern.
  • The missing-baseline problem applies as everywhere in this block.
  • No stated toxicity vetoes exist to check against.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Three chairs objected. The critic dissented on the borrowed mechanism and the backwards gate. The concensusite dissented on the slate: a run of unlisted phase-1 agents with no on-label anchor leaves nothing a payer recognizes when the stain, the biopsy requirement or the single-site logistics fail, which is part of why the approved second-line backbone lives on the Standard-of-care table. The conservative's missing-baseline objection extends here by its own words. The risktaker held the pick but conceded the ordering, and that concession is the rank.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The RB1 stain joins the bundled IHC pass at rank 1 and costs one slide. The trial is one site (Houston); her travel tolerance from 8,500 ft has never been asked, and the advocate's condition, doors ranked but no referral booked until she answers, applies with the most force here.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Last among the ranked doors: same missing evidence as ranks 4 and 5 plus a gate that runs backwards and the heaviest logistics. Agreement -0.4, the lowest score of any ranked row.

docs.title: Per-trial detail
docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference REC-617, RB1-negative metastatic LMS >=1 prior line Phase 1b dose escalation; safety/RP2D primary; no readout No published grade profile NCT07633756

docs.title: Also considered — not ranked (feature-targeting investigational)
docs.text:
One pick was considered and declined by the board itself, and sixteen further feature-targeting investigational options are surfaced with a flag for why they hold no live rank.

Considered and declined: abemaciclib + gemcitabine (NCT06498648). The advocate ranked it solely because it was the one recruiting first-line trial taking systemic-treatment-naive LMS and because nobody has asked her whether she wants a trial; after the critic and the risktaker independently raised the concurrent-schedule contradiction, the advocate withdrew it. CDK4/6 inhibition protects RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy, with viable populations recurring afterwards (PMID 22751436); the priming that worked in Rb-positive LMS xenografts was sequential (PMID 28619757), and the trial runs the drugs concurrently. The conservative added the marrow math: two myelosuppressives with no combination safety data, met at an unmeasured, altitude-confounded baseline, spending the chemo-naive slot that buys the 33-month arm. The question the pick existed to force survives it: her trial appetite and travel tolerance from 8,500 ft have never been asked.

  • Consolidated into a ranked approach: GSK5764227 / HS-20093 (NCT06551142, NCT05830123) is the backup sponsor for the rank-4 B7-H3 approach, with its sarcoma cohort sited in China. [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 (NCT04939610, PMID 35608703) is the beta-emitter form of the rank-5 approach and owns the sarcoma PDX regressions; the same FAPi PET prices both doors.
  • Unavailable: vobramitamab duocarmazine (NCT05551117, terminated) is the B7-H3 predecessor whose bystander data motivate rank 4 and whose safety termination is rank 4's biggest caveat.
  • Thin evidence, no LMS efficacy to weigh: ivonescimab (NCT07516925), a recruiting LMS-named phase 2 for the post-LMS-04 conversation; ATRA + cemiplimab (NCT06528769), a mechanism-first checkpoint combination resting on two-decade-old preclinical MDSC work (PMID 12907617); zanzalintinib (NCT06571734), a third-line TKI trial whose whole case is beating the approved drug already occupying that slot; IMA203 PRAME TCR-T (NCT03686124), double-gated on an unmeasured HLA type and an antigen whose LMS prior runs low, priced by the rank-1 blood draw and reflex stains; trastuzumab deruxtecan (PMID 37870536), gated on a HER2 stain nobody has run, with no sarcoma cohort in DESTINY-PanTumor02 and a pneumonitis liability her lungs are poorly placed to absorb (an IHC 3+ result would move it to the standard-of-care surface under the tumor-agnostic approval); trabectedin + olaparib (PMID 28454547), a preclinical synergy note whose proposed predictor, PARP1 expression, has never been measured in her; ATR inhibition for ATRX/ALT (PMID 25593184), whose founding sensitivity claim failed replication twice (PMID 27602331, PMID 33344901).
  • Not enrollable: lurbinectedin + doxorubicin (NCT06088290), closed to accrual with no results, worth watching as the nearest replication read on the rank-2 design; brenetafusp (NCT07686367), whose sarcoma protocol restricts to synovial sarcoma and MRCLS; afamitresgene autoleucel (PMID 38554725), approved for a different sarcoma and unreachable for LMS outside a cross-histology MAGE-A4 trial (PMID 36624315); anlotinib (NCT03016819), LMS arms closed and no US route; PLD maintenance (NCT06981637), the only randomized read anywhere on the maintenance question the rank-2 regimen leaves open, recruiting in Taiwan only; pulmonary suffusion + metastasectomy (NCT03965234), a feasibility study attached to a consolidation branch gated by the morcellation record and by an anatomy she does not currently have.

Two categories are absent by design. Approved and guideline-carried options for this disease (gemcitabine + docetaxel, pazopanib, eribulin, trabectedin monotherapy, doxorubicin + ifosfamide, metastasectomy, SBRT) are routed to the Standard-of-care table rather than surfaced here; the local-therapy literature in particular is retrospective and operability-selected (PMID 9011700, PMID 21867989), reports 90% local control at 24 months alongside 46% survival at 24 months in the same 44 patients (PMID 32588468), and screened out bilateral infiltrative disease, so it supports re-asking the question after induction, and no survival number for her. And letrozole is foreclosed rather than surfaced: at ER <1% / PR <1% the endocrine door is closed, since durable benefit in the letrozole study occurred only in tumours staining above 90% (PMID 24222211), subject only to the specimen-provenance check at rank 1.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity, tiered Low/Moderate/High by grade-3+ rates and any treatment-related death. Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that an intervention could work against the therapeutic goal, such as a CDK4/6 inhibitor shielding tumor cells from the chemotherapy given alongside it, or radioligand crossfire reaching FAP on marrow stroma. Those are not patient side effects. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. One trial carries this whole page: LMS-04 is a single phase 3 from one cooperative group with no replication yet, a stratified uterine subgroup of 67/150 with no separately powered estimate, and an OS upper bound of 0.95. The maintenance phase she will spend the longest on is its weakest-evidenced part: continuation was never randomised against stopping, the registry entry has no posted results, the 2024 report has no per-term adverse-event rates, and no preclinical support for the maintenance design exists. The PARP branch rests on n=22 single-arm with an internal toxicity-reporting discrepancy (75% vs 59% for the same event) and an exploratory stratifier with no orderable assay. The three phase-1 doors have no LMS response data at all. The morcellation and local-therapy literatures are retrospective with serious risk of bias, and the local-therapy series report local control and survival that should never be conflated (90% and 46% at 24 months in the same 44 patients).
  • Compartment and biomarker dependencies. Rank 3 assumes HRR/HRD confirmation; a proficient result drops expected benefit toward the 5.4-month arm and forecloses the branch as a preferred option. Rank 4 assumes a strong B7-H3 stain, rank 5 a positive FAPi PET, rank 6 an RB1-null IHC, and none of the three markers has been measured. The ECOG that half these protocols require is an intake assumption. The endocrine foreclosure (ER/PR <1%) holds only as firmly as the unverified specimen provenance behind it. The lung-directed consolidation branch is gated by the unretrieved 2024 operative report and by anatomy she does not currently have.
  • What would change the ranking. A cycle 1 date placed ahead of the echocardiogram re-arms the conservative's veto against the rank-2 regimen as scheduled. An HRD-deficient panel result hardens rank 3 into the presumptive second line and strengthens its payer case; a proficient result forecloses it. SaLuDo reporting in favour of its combination would replicate the rank-2 design logic in class and raise confidence in the effect; a null would complicate it. A negative B7-H3 stain, FAPi PET or RB1 stain closes the corresponding door at no cost; a documented Y220C-class germline TP53 result would reshape the anthracycline plan itself. A failed cardiopulmonary screen moves the first-line conversation to the Standard-of-care table entirely.
  • Re-scoping caveat. Nothing in the preference file came from her. If the four unasked questions return answers (the neutropenia trade, trial appetite and travel, ovarian and hormonal aftermath at 39, tolerance for authorization fights), the weighting under every rank on this page should be re-run against her actual answers rather than the intake defaults.

docs.title: 1. Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04) doxorubicin, Adriamycin, trabectedin, ET-743, Yondelis
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-12

Both drugs are FDA approved and any sarcoma infusion center can give them, but the combination she is about to start sits outside the trabectedin label: Yondelis is approved for liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen (verified against the current label, revised 12/2025), and she is anthracycline-naive. First-line use with doxorubicin is therefore off-label prescribing carried by the LMS-04 phase 3 data, not by the label. The realistic obstacle is trabectedin prior authorization, and the time-critical items before cycle 1 are diagnostic, not access.

RegulatoryBoth components FDA-approved: doxorubicin (generic, long-approved); trabectedin (Yondelis, FDA 2015) for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. The first-line combination is off-label relative to that label. GuidelinesSecondary summaries report NCCN lists doxorubicin + trabectedin among first-line options for LMS post-LMS-04; category not independently verified this run Geographic scopeUS-wide; any sarcoma-capable infusion center

Next steps

  1. Complete the gating diagnostics before cycle 1, all routine and orderable locally: echocardiogram with LVEF, hepatic and renal panels with CK, CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin read against altitude-adjusted references, PFTs with DLCO and oximetry performed at her residence altitude, a documented ECOG score, and RECIST baseline imaging.
  2. Request the September 2024 operative report to settle whether morcellation occurred; it changes surveillance imaging, and it costs nothing but a records request.
  3. Submit the trabectedin prior authorization as an off-label first-line request citing LMS-04 (PMID 35835135 and PMID 39231341) rather than waiting for a denial.
  4. Arrange central venous access; trabectedin runs as a 24-hour infusion through a central line.
  5. For label or access questions, call Janssen medical information at 1-800-526-7736.

Trial pathways

Completed; listed as the evidence anchor for the payer request, not as an enrollment option.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyJanssen Products, LP (Johnson & Johnson); trabectedin originator PharmaMar CountryUS marketer; originator Spain Medical info phone1-800-526-7736 Product informationhttps://www.yondelis.com NotesPhone taken verbatim from the current FDA label ('For more information, call 1-800-526-7736 or go to www.YONDELIS.com'). The label also directs patients to J&J withMe support resources.

Payer / coverage notes. Doxorubicin is generic and uncontroversial. Trabectedin is the expensive component and its label requires prior anthracycline, so the prior authorization should be built as an off-label first-line request from the start: cite the LMS-04 primary report (Lancet Oncol 2022, PMID 35835135), the final overall survival analysis (NEJM 2024, PMID 39231341), and whatever NCCN compendium listing the treating center's pharmacy can pull. Centers that treat sarcoma routinely win this appeal; the case should not be filed as if it were on-label.

Notes. The single most decision-relevant access finding in this case: the planned regimen is deliverable everywhere, but it is off-label at this line and the payer file should be assembled that way from day one.

docs.title: 2. Abemaciclib + gemcitabine abemaciclib, LY2835219, Verzenio, gemcitabine
docs.text:

Both drugs are separately marketed, so off-label use is possible in principle, but the preclinical antagonism data for concurrent dosing in Rb-intact tumors argues for doing this inside the protocol or not at all.

RegulatoryAbemaciclib (Verzenio, Lilly) FDA-approved in breast cancer; gemcitabine generic. The sarcoma combination is investigational. Geographic scopeUS: single site (Houston, TX)

Next steps

  1. Order RB1 IHC on the archival block now; it costs one slide and decides between this trial and REC-617.
  2. If Rb-intact, call the MD Anderson site line (866-632-6789) to ask about phase 2 LMS cohort slots and whether treatment-naive entry or post-LMS-04 entry fits the current cohort.
  3. Confirm her actual ECOG before any screening call; the assumed 1 has never been documented.

docs.title: 9. Olaparib + temozolomide olaparib, AZD2281, Lynparza, temozolomide, Temodar
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-12

Both drugs are marketed (olaparib branded, temozolomide generic), so this combination is reachable off-trial by ordinary prescribing even though both dedicated uLMS trials are closed to new patients: NCI 10250 and the randomized successor NCT05432791 are each active-not-recruiting as of this check. The practical path at progression is an off-label prescription with a payer appeal built on the published phase 2 (ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months in pretreated uLMS), while watching the randomized trial for readout or reopening. The HRR and RAD51 story decides how hard to push for it.

docs.title: 10. Trabectedin + olaparib (preclinical combination) trabectedin, Yondelis, olaparib, Lynparza
docs.text:

This row exists to say the door is technically open and should not be walked through outside a protocol.

Next steps

  1. Treat as a research idea, not an access pathway. If a protocol testing PARP-plus-trabectedin ever opens in sarcoma, the trial screener should catch it on a re-run.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

No manufacturer information captured.

Payer / coverage notes. No payer will cover the pairing as such, and there is no publication to anchor an appeal; coverage would ride on each drug's separate justification.

Notes. PARP1 expression, the proposed synergy predictor, has never been measured in this patient.

  4. Skip ARTEMIS-002 unless circumstances put her in China.

docs.title: 21. Altitude-adjusted baseline diagnostics LVEF, echocardiogram, PFTs, DLCO, oximetry, CBC, ECOG documentation, RECIST baseline
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-12

Every gating test here is routine and orderable close to home: echocardiogram with LVEF before doxorubicin, PFTs with DLCO plus resting and exertional oximetry, CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin, hepatic and renal panels with CK before trabectedin, a formally documented ECOG, and RECIST baseline imaging before cycle 1. The one trap is geographic: her oximetry, hemoglobin and dyspnea baselines only mean something if measured at her 8,500 ft residence altitude, so these tests should be done locally rather than at a distant referral center at low elevation.

RegulatoryRoutine clinical diagnostics; no regulatory gate. Geographic scopeLocal to her residence; deliberately not referral-center work

Next steps

  1. Book the echocardiogram first; LVEF is mandatory before any doxorubicin dose and is the likeliest scheduling bottleneck.
  2. Do PFTs with DLCO and pulse oximetry at a facility at her residence altitude, and record the altitude on the report.
  3. Draw CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin now so chemotherapy-era anemia calls have an altitude-adjusted reference point.
  4. Have the oncologist document an examined ECOG score; the 1 on file is an intake assumption that several trial ceilings depend on.
  5. Complete RECIST baseline imaging before cycle 1, with target-lesion selection mindful of the infiltrative pattern.

Notes. The molecular workup runs in parallel and is covered in the rows it gates: comprehensive DNA+RNA panel (Caris-style exome plus transcriptome, closing NTRK), MMR IHC and TMB (pembrolizumab row), HRR somatic and germline plus the RAD51 caveat (olaparib row), HLA typing (IMA203 row), RB1 IHC (abemaciclib and REC-617 rows), B7-H3 and HER2 IHC (ADC rows), ATRX IHC (ATR row), PD-L1 with CD3/CD8 on the lung core.

docs.title: 26. Larotrectinib (TRK inhibition, NTRK fusion-gated) larotrectinib, LOXO-101, Vitrakvi, repotrectinib, Augtyro, entrectinib, Rozlytrek
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-12

This branch is gated on a test, not on supply: larotrectinib and repotrectinib both hold tumor-agnostic FDA approvals for NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, so a positive fusion result makes an oral TRK inhibitor label-available rather than off-label. No fusion assay of any kind has been run on her tumor, and a DNA-only panel like FoundationOne CDx can miss NTRK fusions; the ordered panel must be RNA-capable. The repotrectinib basket TRIDENT-1 is also still recruiting across 49 US sites if trial access ever suits better.

RegulatoryLarotrectinib (Vitrakvi, Bayer): FDA tumor-agnostic approval for NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors. Repotrectinib (Augtyro, Bristol Myers Squibb): FDA accelerated approval June 13, 2024 for NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, adult and pediatric >=12. Fusion-negative or untested use has no basis. Geographic scopeUS-wide

Next steps

  1. Confirm the comprehensive panel order is RNA-capable for fusion detection (the Caris exome-plus-transcriptome order already queued covers this; FoundationOne CDx alone would not).
  2. If a fusion returns, choose between label-available larotrectinib or repotrectinib and TRIDENT-1 enrollment; call the BMS contact center at 855-907-3286 if the trial route is preferred.
  3. Treat as a cheap-to-close long shot: prevalence in true uLMS is very low, but her spindle-cell morphology with an earlier benign sign-out is exactly where a fusion-driven mimic hides.

docs.title: 29. Pembrolizumab pembrolizumab, MK-3475, Keytruda
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: monoclonal_antibody   Verified: 2026-08-12

Marketed everywhere; the question is not whether she can get pembrolizumab but under what banner. If the queued TMB and MMR testing comes back TMB-high (on a validated CGP platform; KEYNOTE-158 eligibility ran on the Foundation Medicine readout) or dMMR/MSI-high, the tumor-agnostic approvals make it label-available after progression on prior therapy, and coverage follows. Without one of those results, sarcoma use is off-label with weak histology-level evidence, since LMS sits in the immune-low microenvironment classes.

RegulatoryFDA-approved, including tumor-agnostic indications for TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb) and MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors after prior therapy. uLMS use without one of those biomarkers is off-label. Geographic scopeUS-wide

Next steps

  1. Close the cheap gates: MMR four-stain IHC plus TMB and MSI from the comprehensive genomic panel already queued; specify a platform with validated TMB reporting.
  2. Add PD-L1 with CD3/CD8 on the 2026 lung core for context; informative in sarcoma, not gating.
  3. If TMB-H or dMMR returns, revisit at first progression, where the tumor-agnostic label applies.

Trial pathways

Without it, expect denial and a thin appeal; the biomarker is the whole access story here. A dMMR result would also open dostarlimab under the same tumor-agnostic logic.

docs.title: 30. Pulmonary metastasectomy pulmonary metastasectomy, lung metastasectomy
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-12

A standard surgical service at any sarcoma-capable thoracic program, requiring a referral rather than any special access machinery; her oncologist has explicitly kept it on the table for after systemic control. The obstacles are anatomical and physiological, not logistical: bilateral infiltrative disease may never become resectable anatomy, and surgical fitness will be judged on pulmonary reserve that must be measured against her 8,500 ft baseline, with PFTs still undone.

RegulatorySurgical procedure; no regulatory gate. GuidelinesGuideline-recognized for resectable oligometastatic sarcoma at experienced centers Geographic scopeUS-wide at sarcoma-capable thoracic surgery programs

Next steps

  1. Complete PFTs with DLCO and oximetry at residence altitude now; they serve both the chemotherapy baseline and any future operability assessment.
  2. Revisit resectability at the first post-induction response scan with a high-volume sarcoma thoracic surgeon.
  3. Keep the infiltrative-pattern caveat explicit in that conversation; the favorable metastasectomy literature describes discrete, countable lesions.

Trial pathways

No registered trials in the dossier.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Payer / coverage notes. Covered as standard surgical care when a thoracic surgeon documents resectability and fitness.

docs.title: 31. SBRT to pulmonary metastases SBRT, stereotactic body radiotherapy
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: other   Verified: 2026-08-12

Routinely available at any radiation oncology department with stereotactic capability; no access barrier exists beyond a referral. Whether her lesions ever become SBRT-appropriate targets is the real question, since the published series treat up to about four discrete lesions and her current pattern is bilateral and infiltrative. If induction converts the disease to oligometastatic anatomy, this is the non-surgical local option, with local control above 90% in sarcoma series.

RegulatoryStandard radiotherapy technique; no regulatory gate. GuidelinesGuideline-recognized local-therapy option for oligometastatic disease Geographic scopeUS-wide

Next steps

  1. Nothing until response assessment; then have radiation oncology review lesion count and geometry against SBRT criteria.
  2. Baseline PFTs matter here too; pulmonary reserve at altitude bounds how much lung can be treated.

Trial pathways

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

Payer / coverage notes. Covered as standard radiotherapy with documentation of lesion number and intent; prior authorization is routine paperwork at any center that does this weekly.

docs.title: 32. Trabectedin monotherapy trabectedin, ET-743, Yondelis
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-12

On-label and routinely covered once she has anthracycline exposure, which the planned LMS-04 induction provides; the maintenance phase of that regimen is effectively this drug continued. Today, before any anthracycline, standalone trabectedin would be off-label, but that sequencing question resolves itself the day induction starts. Access is a prescription plus central line, not a fight.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (2015) for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. GuidelinesSecondary summaries report NCCN treats single-agent trabectedin as a preferred later-line regimen for LMS Geographic scopeUS-wide

Next steps

  1. No separate access work; this arrives bundled inside the LMS-04 plan as the maintenance drug.
  2. Keep hepatic panels and CK on the recurring lab schedule through maintenance.
