docs.title: Selected general biomarker report — ulms-highgrade-pulm-mets-er-pr-neg-qqvt
docs.text: Which biomarkers on the selected panel this patient has been tested for, and which have never been measured. The panel covers targets established in this tumor type, targets relevant across a subset of tumor types, and biomarkers that predict benefit regardless of where the tumor started, such as MSI-H/dMMR and high tumor mutational burden gating PD-1 blockade.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Selected general biomarker report (offline HTML) — the same survey, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Selected general biomarker report (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by recommended action

15 biomarkers surveyed: 15 with no usable result on file (4 essential), 0 measured but not to decision resolution, 0 already established. Panel coverage: 9 tumor-agnostic biomarkers plus 6 of 72 protein targets in scope for this tumor.

Every one of the fifteen biomarkers surveyed here is a gap, and none is measured to decision grade. No sequencing exists from either specimen; the only stains ever run are ER and PR. Twelve were never measured; three, PRAME, MAGE-A4 and NY-ESO-1, are unassessable rather than negative: no HLA class I type is on file to score them against. Four gaps are essential, all order-now: NTRK fusion, MSI/dMMR (four stains on an existing block, plus Lynch implications for a woman in her thirties), TMB, and HRD/BRCA, the entry this histology most earns: olaparib plus temozolomide gave a 27% response rate and 6.9-month median PFS in pretreated uLMS.

The list collapses to three orders and no new biopsy; tissue exists from the 2024 hysterectomy and the 2026 lung core. Comprehensive DNA plus RNA profiling on the 2024 resection is the highest-value order: it closes NTRK, TMB and HRD at once and returns TP53, RB1, ATRX and MED12 without a separate test. It must include RNA. NTRK breakpoints sit in introns that DNA-only panels miss, and this spindle-cell tumor was already misread once as benign. Second, one archival block cut for MMR, PD-L1, HER2 and B7-H3 IHC, with PD-L1 read on the lung core. Third, a blood draw for HLA typing and the germline HR panel. All three can run beside the planned LMS-04 induction without delaying it, and since the tumor-agnostic indications require prior therapy anyway, the results land exactly when they can be acted on: at progression.

Two absences are deliberate. ER and PR <1% are confirmed decision-grade negatives with no survey row because neither reference panel lists them; the validation track is checking which specimen was stained, since at that cutoff a failed stain on the 2024 block reads the same as a true negative. The other 66 of 72 protein targets were set aside as epithelial markers a mesenchymal tumor does not plausibly express. B7-H3 stayed, with the best odds of a positive here: 97% of soft tissue sarcomas stain positive, roughly 69% high, though a positive buys trial screening, not a prescription. Most of what remains will be negative if tested. The argument for testing is the size of the option a positive opens, not the odds of one.

docs.title: What this collapses to
docs.text:
The gaps above resolve onto this many distinct orders. Biomarkers that ride along on the same assay are grouped together.

  • Single archival block cut for the IHC set (MMR, PD-L1, HER2, B7-H3) — B7-H3 (CD276) surface protein expression, Microsatellite instability / mismatch-repair deficiency (MSI-H / dMMR), PD-L1 protein expression
  • Cancer/testis antigen IHC set (PRAME, MAGE-A4, NY-ESO-1) on one archival block, ordered only if HLA typing returns a restricting allele — MAGE-A4 (HLA class I-presented cancer/testis antigen), PRAME (HLA class I-presented cancer/testis antigen)
  • Archival IHC block if a FAP-directed program is in play; otherwise the trial's own screening assay — Fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP)
  • Cancer/testis antigen IHC set (PRAME, MAGE-A4, NY-ESO-1) on one archival block — NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B, HLA class I-presented cancer/testis antigen)
  • Comprehensive DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tissue — BRAF V600E mutation
  • Comprehensive DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tissue (same order as NTRK) — RET gene fusion
  • Comprehensive DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tissue (the single order that also carries MSI, NTRK, RET, BRAF and the HR genes) — Tumor mutational burden, high (TMB-H)
  • Comprehensive DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tissue, which also returns TMB, MSI, RET and BRAF, the HR genes, and the TP53 / RB1 / ATRX / MED12 backbone of this histology — NTRK1 / NTRK2 / NTRK3 gene fusion
  • Comprehensive DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tissue; germline panel on the same blood draw as HLA typing — Homologous recombination deficiency / BRCA1 / BRCA2 pathogenic variant
  • Single archival block cut for the IHC set (MMR, PD-L1, HER2, B7-H3); ERBB2 copy number also comes off the comprehensive NGS panel — HER2 protein overexpression (IHC 3+)
  • Single blood draw shared with the germline HR gene panel — HLA class I genotype
  • Would ride on the archival IHC block if an AXL-directed program required documented expression — AXL receptor tyrosine kinase surface expression

66 of 72 panel targets were screened and set aside

Reading this report

This page answers one question per biomarker: has this patient been tested for it, and was the test at a resolution that can carry a treatment decision. Not measured means nothing is on file, which is not the same as a negative result. Measured, not decision-grade means a result exists but cannot be acted on as it stands; those gaps are worked into the Target validation paths report. Priority weighs what is going unassessed against how routine the assay is. Most of these biomarkers will be negative if tested; the case for testing rests on the size of the option that opens if positive, not on how likely a positive is.

Back to case · Target validation · Recommendations · Trials · Evidence · Board

Decision support, not medical advice

Libby is experimental. An unmeasured biomarker on this page is a gap in the record, not a prediction that the patient carries it. Assay availability, current approval status, and whether any of this testing is worth the tissue are decisions for the treating team. See PHI policy.

docs.title: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04) (doxorubicin-trabectedin-lms04)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker1highStart it now and wait on nothing. An adjusted PFS HR of 0.41 with median OS 33 vs 24 months (aHR 0.65) in her exact first-line population is the biggest effect size anywhere in this dossier, and for once the aggressive option and the best-evidenced option are the same regimen. The toxicity is heavy (G3-4 neutropenia 80%, febrile neutropenia 28%), but she is 39 and I will trade a hard six months of induction for a shot at the 33-month arm. The off-label first-line authorization is paperwork, not a reason to hesitate, and the molecular workup I want runs in parallel at zero cost in treatment days.Febrile neutropenia in 28%: growth-factor support should be planned before cycle 1, and her altitude-shifted hemoglobin baseline will confound anemia and dose-modification calls; The maintenance phase is empirical, with no preclinical support of any kind; its contribution cannot be separated from induction outside the trial design; Off-label at this line: a payer denial is the one thing that could actually delay induction, so the authorization file should go in before the first fill; Baseline LVEF and a documented ECOG are still missing and the trial required both conservative1moderateThis is the rare case where the safety argument and the efficacy argument land on the same regimen: randomized phase 3 in her histology, mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.58), and at 55 months median follow-up an OS of 33 vs 24 months (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44-0.95). The price is printed on the trial itself, G3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28%, and I want it priced into the cycle 1 orders as primary G-CSF prophylaxis rather than discovered at cycle 2. My endorsement is conditional on a baseline battery that does not exist yet, because not one organ-function value is on file days before an anthracycline: echocardiogram with LVEF, hepatic and renal panels with CK, CBC with reticulocytes and ferritin, PFTs with DLCO and oximetry done at her 8,500 ft residence, and an examined ECOG. These toxicities are cytopenias and transaminitis with forty years of management algorithms behind them, which is why I can rank a regimen this rough first.No baseline organ function of any kind is documented: no LVEF, no hepatic or renal panel, no CBC, no PFTs. Every gating test for this regimen is missing with induction imminent.; Febrile neutropenia ran 28% vs 9% in LMS-04; primary G-CSF prophylaxis belongs in the cycle 1 orders.; She is 39. Cumulative doxorubicin dose planning and a dexrazoxane conversation belong before cycle 1, not at cycle 6; her survivorship horizon for anthracycline cardiomyopathy runs decades past this regimen.; Altitude changes three baselines at once: polycythaemia at 8,500 ft will mask chemotherapy anaemia, sea-level oximetry thresholds do not apply to her, and her presenting dyspnea cannot be split between disease and altitude without a measured local baseline.; Maintenance-phase trabectedin safety detail from LMS-04 is not publicly retrievable, so monitoring defaults to the SAR-3007 single-agent dossier (G>=3 ALT elevation 25%, rhabdomyolysis 1.2%, treatment-related deaths 2.1%); CK and LFTs stay on the recurring schedule through maintenance.; First-line use sits outside the trabectedin label, which requires prior anthracycline; the prior authorization should be filed as off-label from day one with the LMS-04 papers attached. critic1highRandomized phase 3, n=150, pre-specified primary PFS endpoint read by blinded independent central review: 12.2 vs 6.2 months, adjusted HR 0.41 (0.29-0.58), p<0.0001, and the 55-month analysis held on survival at 33 vs 24 months, adjusted HR 0.65 (0.44-0.95). This is the only RCT-grade, indication-matched result in the dossier, and it survives my scrutiny. Two things I will not let pass unstated: uterine primaries were 67 of 150, a stratified subgroup rather than a separately powered population, and the trabectedin maintenance phase was never tested against stopping, so how much of the 12.2 months it contributes is unmeasured. One trial, one cooperative group, no replication yet; SaLuDo (NCT06088290) is the nearest confirmatory read and has not reported.RoB 2, outcome measurement: the trial is open label. Blinded central review on the PFS primary handles most of the detection-bias worry and OS is not exposed to it, so this is the one open-label design I am comfortable with.; Indirectness. Uterine LMS was 67/150. Stratified randomisation is not power, and no uterine-specific effect estimate with its own confidence interval is printed in the abstract.; Maintenance is an untested component of a tested regimen. Nothing in this dossier randomises trabectedin continuation against stopping, and the preclinical basis for the pairing itself was additive at best (combination indices just under 1, pmid:12783202). MELODY (NCT06981637) asks the analogous maintenance question with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, and it is in Taiwan.; Imprecision. 107 deaths among 150 patients and an OS upper bound of 0.95. The survival claim is real but it is not robust to one contradicting trial.; Selective reporting on the maintenance phase specifically: NCT02997358 has no posted results and the 2024 survival report gives no per-term adverse-event rates, so the toxicity of the part she may stay on longest is the part with the thinnest published detail.; Eligibility drift against her own file. The trial required ECOG 0-1 and cardiac clearance; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption and no LVEF exists. concensusite1highThe planned regimen is the only first-line option in this dossier with randomized survival data in her histology (mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months, aHR 0.41; final mOS 33 vs 24 months, aHR 0.65), and NCCN Uterine Neoplasms lists doxorubicin plus trabectedin among first-line systemic options for metastatic uLMS. I could confirm that carriage only through secondary sources this run because the guideline PDF sits behind a login, so I am not quoting an NCCN evidence category I have not seen. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2021 (Ann Oncol 32:1348-65) predates LMS-04 and does not carry the combination, and the UK BSG 2025 guideline cites its PFS benefit while noting NICE has not adopted it, so cross-society convergence is incomplete but moving in one direction. Trabectedin's FDA label requires a prior anthracycline, which makes first-line use off-label; the payer request should lead with the NCCN listing and both trial publications rather than the label.LMS-04 required ECOG 0-1; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption no clinician has documented.; Baseline LVEF, PFTs, and labs are all missing, so the trial's own cardiac and fitness screens have not been run, and her 8,500 ft baseline will confound anemia and oximetry calls on treatment.; G3-4 neutropenia 80% and febrile neutropenia 28% on the combination arm, heavier than any alternative first-line listing.; Off-label at this line under the trabectedin label's prior-anthracycline clause; the prior authorization should be filed as off-label from day one. advocate1moderateThis is the plan her sarcoma oncologist already made, and it carries the best evidence in the file: mPFS 12.2 vs 6.2 months (adjusted HR 0.41) and final OS 33 vs 24 months (HR 0.65) in chemo-naive LMS. I back it, but the record should show that nobody has asked her whether she accepts 80% G3-4 neutropenia and 28% febrile neutropenia for that gain; the 0.7 efficacy weight that would settle the question is an intake default, not her answer. First-line use also sits outside the trabectedin label, which requires prior anthracycline, so the authorization request should go in now, citing LMS-04, rather than surfacing as a denial at the pharmacy. Every gating test (LVEF, altitude-read PFTs and oximetry, documented ECOG, RECIST baseline imaging) runs in parallel without delaying cycle 1.Consent gap: the 80% G3-4 neutropenia / 28% febrile neutropenia trade has never been put to her, and efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7 is an assumed default; Off-label first line: the current Yondelis label requires prior anthracycline, so prior authorization is a real fight to start now; No measured baselines exist: LVEF, PFTs, labs, and ECOG are all assumptions or absences before an anthracycline at 8,500 ft

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativequalifiedtoxicityYour pre-registered veto covers a whole battery and I will concede half of it: the echocardiogram and cardiac clearance were LMS-04 eligibility criteria (nct:NCT02997358), and at 39 with an anthracycline coming they are gates I would enforce too. DLCO, ferritin, reticulocytes and a locally read oximetry baseline are baselines, not gates, and calling them veto-grade lets a pulmonary function slot delay induction in a woman who already lost 23 months to a misread pathology report. Add the germline TP53 draw to the short pre-cycle-1 list (pmid:32457520), since that one is a tube of blood, and run the rest alongside cycle 1 instead of ahead of it. criticconcensusitequalifiedguideline_fitYour BSG 2025 read is the most useful thing anyone brought this round and it needs one distinction stated for the PI: BSG keeping single-agent doxorubicin at I,A and noting no NICE support is an adoption lag plus a reimbursement decision, not a finding against the trial. LMS-04 is RoB2 Low with a pre-specified BICR-read PFS primary (12.2 vs 6.2 months, aHR 0.41) and a 55-month survival analysis (33 vs 24 months, aHR 0.65) in pmid:35835135 and pmid:39231341, and ESMO 2021 predates it and cannot speak to it either way. Your rank-3 runs the opposite way, because the lung-directed carriage in those guidelines names selection criteria (disease-free interval, lesion count, complete resection) drawn from ROBINS-I Serious retrospective series (pmid:9011700, pmid:21867989, pmid:32588468), so guideline listing there records a practice, not a measured benefit, and her bilateral infiltrative pattern is what those series excluded. conservativecriticqualifiedtoxicitySame rank 1, so this is boundary-setting, not a quarrel. Your concern list names the unmet trial gates (assumed ECOG, no LVEF) and then rates confidence high; I want those gates written as conditions precedent to cycle 1, with the germline TP53 draw added to them per ERN GENTURIS (pmid:32457520), because genotoxic chemotherapy raises second-primary risk in carriers and that result only helps her before the anthracycline starts. On my pre-registered veto: the trigger was induction scheduled over the missing baseline battery, and nothing in the file shows that has happened (induction is imminent, the battery is simply undone), so no veto this round and the condition stands; the day a cycle 1 date lands ahead of the echocardiogram, it becomes one. advocateconservativeendorsepreference_fitA veto threat in a case with an empty toxicity_vetoes list looked at first like the substitution I was sent to catch, and it is the opposite: the list is empty because nobody asked her, and the conservative's conditions (LVEF, examined ECOG, PFTs read at 8,500 ft) are what turn the 80% G3-4 neutropenia and 28% febrile neutropenia trade (pmid:35835135) from an assumption into something she can actually consent to. Their notes also say flatly that none of the rankings treat the 0.7 weight or the trials flag as her position, the cleanest handling of the intake defaults on this board. Endorse: the conditional structure defends her decision space rather than filling it in for her. advocateconcensusitequalifiedpreference_fitTwo places where the guideline seat slid past her voice. BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) keeps single-agent doxorubicin as its graded first-line standard and notes NICE has not adopted LMS-04, so the off-label authorization is contestable, and she should hear the denial-letter scenario before cycle 1 as part of consent rather than at the pharmacy counter. And 'the germline draw should go out before cycle 1, not after' treats TP53 testing (pmid:32457520) as a scheduling item when it is a consent conversation with consequences for her family: the timing case is sound, but whether she wants germline information at all is a preference nobody has collected, and preferences.json says on its face that every stored value is an intake default. concensusiteconservativeendorseguideline_fitThe guideline picture behind this pick needs stating precisely: BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) keeps single-agent doxorubicin as standard first line (their I,A), cites the LMS-04 PFS benefit, and records that the combination is 'not yet supported by NICE'; ESMO's operative STS guideline is still the 2021 edition (pmid:34303806), written before the trial; and NCCN carriage I could confirm only through secondary sources against a login-gated PDF, so I quote no category. That is lag, not opposition: no society text argues against the regimen, and the clinical case rests squarely on the randomized data (pmid:35835135, pmid:39231341) all five of us ranked first. The consequence is a payer one rather than a clinical one, and the conservative's 'file the authorization as off-label from day one' is exactly the right handling of it. concensusiteadvocatequalifiedguideline_fitThe rank-1 framing runs every outstanding test in parallel with induction, and for the germline arm of the workup that ordering is backwards: ERN GENTURIS 2020 (pmid:32457520) advises germline TP53 testing before genotoxic treatment starts, because carriers are the patients in whom chemotherapy and radiotherapy raise second-primary risk. She is 39 with a high-grade sarcoma and doxorubicin imminent, so the draw goes out before cycle 1, and the result should be in hand before anyone fixes a cumulative anthracycline plan; this is a scheduling instruction, not a footnote. The tumor-side profiling the advocate queues has guideline standing of its own now (ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group 2024, pmid:38834388, names sarcoma for tumor NGS), which makes it orderable as guideline-backed workup rather than clinician preference.

docs.title: Olaparib + temozolomide (queued for first progression, HRD workup during induction) (olaparib-temozolomide)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2moderateThis is where the upside hides in her untested genome. If the tumor lands in the HRD subset, the NCI 10250 numbers (ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months, and an 11.2 vs 5.4 month split by RAD51 foci) plus the BRCA2-deleted PDX work make this the strongest second-line bet in the disease, oral and potentially durable. Twenty-two patients, single-arm, I know. Order the HRR panel and HRD-relevant tissue work during induction so the answer is already sitting in the chart the day LMS-04 stops working.n=22 single-arm; the RAD51-foci split is exploratory and could evaporate in the randomized successor; Hematologic toxicity (G3-4 neutropenia 75% per abstract) stacks badly on marrow that just absorbed LMS-04 induction; Both trials are closed to accrual, so access is an off-label combination authorization; no RAD51 assay has a CLIA catalogue provider; If HRD testing comes back proficient, the expected benefit drops toward the 5.4-month arm and this pick loses most of its case conservative4lowI will carry one non-cytotoxic branch, olaparib plus temozolomide, and hold it behind two gates: her still-unmeasured HRR/HRD status and the exhaustion of better-characterized options. The signal is real but small, ORR 27% and mPFS 6.9 months in 22 patients, and the RAD51-deficient split (11.2 vs 5.4 months) is exploratory. What keeps it on my list is that both drugs have been marketed for years and the trial managed heavy hematologic toxicity with dose reductions rather than discontinuations (3/22 stopped for toxicity, no treatment-related deaths). Until the randomized successor reads out, this stays a biomarker-anchored off-label appeal.Single-arm, n=22, and the confirmatory randomized trial (NCT05432791) is closed to new accrual, so the evidence will not improve on any near-term clock.; G3/4 neutropenia around 75% stacked after LMS-04's 80% assumes marrow recovery that should be shown on a CBC before this is ever prescribed.; The somatic HRR and germline panels off the archival block gate this branch entirely; send them now, because an unmeasured HRD status makes the payer case and the clinical case equally weak. critic3lowCredit where it is due: NCI 10250 pre-specified a one-stage binomial bar of 5 or more responses in 22 patients and hit it, with best ORR within 6 months of 23% and mPFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE). Everything past that is hypothesis-grade. n=22, single arm, no comparator, an erratum on the record, and the RAD51-foci split everyone quotes (11.2 vs 5.4 months, p=0.05) comes from 9 of 18 evaluable patients in an exploratory analysis sitting exactly on the alpha boundary with no multiplicity control. The practical problem is worse than the statistical one: the RAD51 assay has no CLIA provider anywhere, so the stratifier that produced the signal cannot be measured on her, and the measurable substitute is HRR sequencing, where confirmed HRD ran 5 of 58 uLMS and in every confirmed case was a homozygous BRCA2 deletion.Internal reporting inconsistency worth naming: grade 3-4 neutropenia is 75% in the abstract and 13/22 (59%) for the neutropenia term in full-text Table 2. When the two published figures for the same toxicity disagree by 16 points in a 22-patient trial, I read the safety claim cautiously.; Both trials are active-not-recruiting (NCT03880019, NCT05432791), so this is off-label prescribing on single-arm data, not trial access. The randomised successor also requires 2 or more prior lines including an anthracycline and excludes prior temozolomide or dacarbazine, which constrains what can be given in between.; The biomarker branch that gates this is the one that cannot be run as published. Ordering HRR/BRCA2 sequencing is right; presenting it as the same test that generated the 11.2-month figure is not.; Response rate without a control arm in a disease where dacarbazine produced 9% in a randomised setting. 23% is a signal, not an effect estimate. concensusite5lowI could not verify NCCN carriage of this combination for uLMS this run, and the evidence is a 22-patient single-arm phase 2 (ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months), so from a guideline seat this is trial-preferred territory rather than a listed standard, and I am reporting it that way. The guideline-aligned move is the one already queued: somatic HRR panel plus germline testing now, and a watch on the randomized successor NCT05432791, currently closed to accrual, which is the study that would move this onto a pathway. ESMO's 2024 precision-medicine recommendations now name sarcoma among the tumors where NGS is recommended, so the profiling that gates this branch is itself guideline-backed.Both dedicated uLMS trials are closed to new accrual (verified against CT.gov this run); off-label access would rest on a payer appeal built around one phase 2.; HRD status is unmeasured, and the RAD51 functional assay that best separated outcomes has no orderable CLIA version. advocate2lowThe strongest non-cytotoxic signal in uLMS: ORR 27% and mPFS 6.9 months, with responses lasting around a year. It is also oral, which would matter if she turns out to care about time in the infusion chair; nobody knows, because nobody asked. The branch only exists if the HRD-relevant NGS goes in now: results take 2-3 weeks, both dedicated trials are closed to accrual, and the interim route is off-label prescribing with payer friction. At n=22 and single-arm this stays a next-line branch rather than a challenger to LMS-04.n=22, single-arm; the 27% ORR is hypothesis-grade until NCT05432791 reads out; Both dedicated uLMS trials closed to accrual, so the interim route is an off-label prescription her insurer can push back on; Gated on HRD/NGS testing that has not been ordered yet; G3-4 neutropenia up to 75% lands on a marrow already hit by LMS-04

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticconservativequalifiedtoxicityYou quote G3/4 neutropenia 'around 75%' from NCI 10250 and stack it against LMS-04's 80%, but that trial publishes the same toxicity two ways: 75% in the abstract and 13/22 (59%) for the neutropenia term in full-text Table 2 (pmid:37467452). In a 22-patient single-arm study a 16-point gap between two published figures for one event is a reporting problem rather than a rounding one, and both numbers belong in the consent conversation instead of whichever is convenient. It does not move your rank-4 placement, which the n=22 design already earned; it changes the sentence she hears and the count threshold you would want on a CBC before prescribing.

docs.title: REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756) (rec-617-cdk7)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowI am taking the thinnest branch in the case on purpose, because the stain that opens it costs one slide and RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology. If the IHC reads null, she has a first-in-class CDK7 inhibitor recruiting at MD Anderson for exactly her genotype after one prior line, and the RB1-null replication-stress mechanism from small-cell lung cancer is a real one even though nobody has run it in leiomyosarcoma. Zero LMS data, phase 1b, safety primary endpoint; that is the honest price of being early. She can pay it at second line rather than instead of LMS-04, which is the only way I would offer it.No CDK7 data of any kind in leiomyosarcoma; the mechanistic case is borrowed from RB1-null SCLC and YKL-5-124 is not REC-617; Phase 1b dose escalation means she could be treated at a subtherapeutic dose; Requires a biopsy-amenable lesion and RECIST-measurable disease, both uncertain against her infiltrative pulmonary pattern; Single site (Houston) and her travel tolerance was never actually stated conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityTaking your rank-3 rather than your rank-1, since on LMS-04 we agree. The mechanism you are borrowing is YKL-5-124 in RB1/TP53-null small-cell lung cancer (pmid:31883968), a different compound in a different lineage, with no CDK7 data in leiomyosarcoma at any phase, and the gating stain runs backwards: RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology, so the IHC most often routes her into the arm with zero efficacy data rather than away from it. Ranks 4 and 5 repeat the pattern one step down, where 97% B7-H3 positivity (pmid:39478506) is prevalence and the number that tracked response was antigen density above a threshold (pmid:30655315), and FAP sits on marrow stroma where FAP-directed cells killed mice (pmid:23712432). advocaterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitTargeting rank 3 rather than the unanimous rank 1 because my objection lives in the investigational block: ranks 3 through 5 read as a trial roadmap for a woman whose prefers_trials: true came from intake, not from her, and nct:NCT07633756 is one site in Houston she never agreed to travel to, as the risktaker himself notes. Credit where due: he flagged the inference in his own notes and built all three doors as stains and scans running alongside induction, costing her nothing today, which is how you hold options open without deciding on her behalf. So qualified, not dissent: keep the doors ranked, but no referral gets booked until someone asks her the trial and travel questions directly, because burying these options would have been a choice made for her too. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitI chose this pick over the rank-1 because it carries the objection: no guideline anywhere mentions CDK7 inhibition in sarcoma, and silence is not itself the problem, since trial entry is how guidelines expect unlisted agents to be reached (BSG 2025, pmid:38734790, builds specialist MDT care explicitly around trial recruitment) and screening for NCT07633756 after an RB1-null stain is compatible with that. My dissent is with what sits around it: ranks 3 through 5 are all unlisted phase 1 agents, while pazopanib, the on-label second line with placebo-controlled randomized backing (pmid:22595799) and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2021 carriage (pmid:34303806), appears nowhere in the slate. Guideline silence licenses trial screening; it supplies no compendium listing and no payer path outside the trial, so when the RB1 stain, the biopsy requirement, or the Houston logistics fail, this plan is standing on nothing a payer recognizes.

docs.title: MGC026 (B7-H3 ADC), phase 1 with named sarcoma cohort (NCT06242470) (b7h3-adc)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowB7-H3 is the surface target most likely to actually be there: 97% of soft-tissue sarcomas stain positive and 69% at high level, and the duocarmycin bystander data say heterogeneous expression is survivable for this drug class. MGC026 is recruiting US sites with sarcoma on the named list and no expression gate, so a single stain on the 2024 archival block tells us whether the referral is worth booking. The class carries a corpse: MacroGenics' previous B7-H3 ADC was terminated after safety findings, and there is no LMS efficacy signal yet for the successor. I still want the stain run during induction, because a strong positive would make this the most reachable experimental door at second or third line.Predecessor vobramitamab duocarmazine was halted on safety in prostate cancer; payload liability is the live question for the whole class; Phase 1 dose escalation with no LMS response data at all; Positivity is not dependency: the CAR-T antigen-density work says low expressors gain little, so the 69% high-level stratum is the number that matters, not the 97% conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: [225Ac]RTX-2358 FAP-targeted alpha radioligand (NCT07156565), FAPi PET as gate (fap-radioligand)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowAn alpha emitter whose eligibility question is answered by a PET scan she can get after one prior regimen, in a tumor family near the top of the FAP expression range with the antigen on the malignant cells themselves rather than only stroma. Radioligand crossfire does not care about the antigen heterogeneity that undermines ADC and cell-therapy cutoffs, and 177Lu-FAP-2286 already produced regressions in sarcoma PDX. The marrow-stroma FAP toxicity from the CAR-T mouse work is what I watch, though a renally cleared peptide is a very different exposure from a persisting engineered T cell. Screen her the month LMS-04 progresses; the scan itself settles whether the target exists.FAP sits on bone marrow stromal cells and FAP CAR-T caused lethal marrow toxicity in mice; dosimetry, not IHC, will decide whether that transfers; Phase 1 dose escalation with no human sarcoma efficacy for this specific agent; FAP PET uptake is unmeasured and ECOG 0-1 is required against an ECOG that was assumed at intake, never documented conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativerisktakerdissenttoxicityWe share the rank-1 call, so I am aiming where my objection actually bites, your rank 5. FAP-directed effectors caused cachexia and lethal bone toxicity in mice, and human marrow stromal cells were recognised by the same cells (pmid:23712432); you would point an alpha emitter at that target in a patient whose CBC has never been drawn, sequenced right after an induction that ran 80% G3-4 neutropenia. The renal-clearance distinction you make is fair, but it is an argument for dosimetry NCT07156565 has not generated yet, so this stays off any ranked list of mine until a marrow baseline and human marrow-stroma dosimetry both exist, and the same missing-baseline problem runs under your REC-617 and MGC026 picks, just without the on-target marrow signal.

docs.title: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine (NCT06498648, first-line LMS cohort) (abemaciclib-gemcitabine)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowIf she wants a trial, this is the only recruiting first-line study in the dossier that takes systemic-treatment-naive LMS, and since only prior gemcitabine is barred, the door stays open after LMS-04 too. But prefers_trials: true is an intake default; her actual appetite for a single-site study in Houston, and the travel that means from a home at 8,500 ft, is something no one has asked her. Phase 1/2 with no LMS efficacy readout yet. I list it so someone asks her, because the evidence on its own does not compete with LMS-04.prefers_trials is an assumed default; trial appetite and travel tolerance were never stated; Single site (Houston); travel burden from an 8,500 ft residence unquantified; Phase 1/2, no LMS efficacy data yet

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocatedissentevidence_qualityI am taking your rank 4 instead of the unanimous rank 1, because this is the rare place where I sit to the cautious side of the advocate seat and that belongs on the record. Concurrent CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from genotoxic therapy and let viable populations recur afterwards (pmid:22751436), while the priming schedule that did work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts is sequential (pmid:28619757) and is not the schedule nct:NCT06498648 runs. I will fund thin evidence all day, but not a first-line cohort whose schedule argues against its own mechanism and which would spend her only chemotherapy-naive slot, the asset that buys the 33-month arm. criticadvocatedissentevidence_qualityNCT06498648 gives the two drugs concurrently, which is the schedule the preclinical work argues against: CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy and viable populations regrew afterwards (pmid:22751436), while the priming result that did work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts was sequential (pmid:28619757). Listing it as 'phase 1/2, no LMS efficacy data yet' undersells that, because the mechanistic case for pairing these drugs is schedule-specific and this trial uses the other schedule. Your reason for ranking something here holds up, that nobody has asked her whether she wants a trial at all, but you hung it on the weakest first-line study in the dossier. conservativeadvocatedissenttoxicityI am on your rank 4, where the safety problem lives. The critic already made the mechanism case (concurrent CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from genotoxic killing, pmid:22751436); my objection is the marrow math, since abemaciclib and gemcitabine are both myelosuppressive, the pairing has no characterized combination safety data in LMS, and she would meet it with no baseline CBC while an altitude-raised hemoglobin at 8,500 ft hides the anemia until it is deep. She is 39 with a randomized 33 vs 24 month OS benefit on the table (pmid:39231341), so a chemo-naive phase 1/2 slot is not a neutral question to put to her, and I would move this from the ranking to the post-progression notes.

docs.title: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
docs.text:
intervention_id: doxorubicin-trabectedin-lms04 · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Pautier/Duffaud (2024)N Engl J Med150same 150-patient ITT population as the 2022 primary report; analyses adjusted for uterine vs soft-tissue origin and disease stage1Lfinal overall-survival analysis of the randomized phase 3 LMS-04 trial (median follow-up 55 months)doxorubicin aloneas in primary report; trabectedin maintenance continued to progressionOSmedian OS33.00 months26.00–48.00—mOS 33 mo (combo) vs 24 mo (dox)Abstract reports only that adverse events and dose reductions were more frequent with doxorubicin-trabectedin; per-term combination-phase rates are on the 2022 primary-report row.RoB2:Low1bstrong39231341DOIThis is the OS readout that turns LMS-04 from a PFS result into a survival benefit, and the main reason the regimen was chosen for her. Toxicities left empty after the full fallback chain failed: abstract has no per-term data, NEJM has no PMC deposit, CT.gov NCT02997358 hasResults=false, publisher page returns 403. Pautier/Duffaud (2022)Lancet Oncol150ECOG 0-1 required; 67 of 150 patients (45%) had uterine LMS; randomization stratified by uterine vs soft-tissue origin; surgery for residual disease allowed after 6 cycles in both arms1Lrandomized open-label phase 3 (French Sarcoma Group, 20 centres), BICR-assessed primary endpointdoxorubicin 75 mg/m2 alonedoxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + trabectedin 1.1 mg/m2 IV q3w x6, then trabectedin maintenance to progression; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6PFSmedian PFS (BICR)12.20 months10.10–15.60<0.0001mPFS 12.2 mo (combo) vs 6.2 mo (dox)Combination is substantially more myelotoxic than doxorubicin alone: G3-4 neutropenia 80% vs 13%, thrombocytopenia 47% vs 0%, febrile neutropenia 28% vs 9%. One treatment-related death, in the doxorubicin-alone arm (cardiac failure).RoB2:Low1bstrong35835135DOIPrimary report of the regimen she is about to start; pivotal for the LMS-04 strategy. The PMID a search commonly surfaces, 36174625, is a letter about this trial, not the trial. Per-term G3-4 rates above are from the combination phase; maintenance-phase safety detail sits behind the paywall (no PMC; CT.gov NCT02997358 has no posted results).

docs.text:
intervention_id: doxorubicin-ifosfamide · 1 row(s)

docs.title: Gemcitabine + docetaxel vs doxorubicin (GeDDiS)
docs.text:
intervention_id: gemcitabine-docetaxel · 3 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Seddon/Beare (2017)Lancet Oncol257LMS-enriched: 118/257 (46%) leiomyosarcoma, of whom 71 (28% of trial) uterine LMS; Trojani grade 2-31Lrandomized controlled phase 3 (GeDDiS, ISRCTN07742377), 24-week PFS-rate primary endpointdoxorubicingemcitabine 675 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 d8 q3w x6; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6HR_PFSalive and progression-free at 24 weeks1.28 HR0.99–1.650.06mPFS 23.7 wk (gem-doce) vs 23.3 wk (dox)Different toxicity trade: doxorubicin gave more neutropenia, febrile neutropenia and mucositis; gem-doce more fatigue. No treatment-related deaths reported.RoB2:Low1bpartial28882536DOIThe head-to-head that keeps anthracycline first: gem-doce showed no superiority even in an LMS-enriched population, including the uterine subset (interaction p=0.38). Its practical role for her is first-line fallback if baseline LVEF or pulmonary reserve at 8,500 ft rules out doxorubicin. Hensley/Rose (2008)Gynecol Oncol42uLMS only; first-line; multicentre cooperative-group setting1Lsingle-arm phase 2 (Gynecologic Oncology Group)—gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 over 90 min d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 q3w with G-CSF d9; lower doses after prior pelvic RTORRORR35.80 %23.50–49.60—mPFS 4.4 mo; median response duration 6 moMyelosuppression was the major toxicity; one possibly-related grade 4 pulmonary event — relevant given her bilateral infiltrative lung disease and altitude-shifted oximetry baseline.ROBINS-I:Moderate2bstrong18534250DOIThe uLMS-specific first-line estimate for the fallback regimen: ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months — respectable but well short of LMS-04's 12.2-month PFS. Single-arm, n=42; no comparator. Hensley/Spriggs (2002)J Clin Oncol34mixed-line: 18 chemo-naive, 16 doxorubicin-pretreated; 85% uterine primariesanysingle-arm phase 2 with pharmacokinetic substudy—gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 q3w with G-CSF d9-15; 25% dose reduction after prior pelvic RTORRORR53.00 %35.00–70.00—median TTP 5.6 moMyelosuppression frequent but febrile neutropenia rare (6%) with G-CSF support; no bleeding events.ROBINS-I:Moderate2bpartial12065559DOIThe 53% ORR that made gem-doce a uLMS standard is from 34 patients at one centre with mixed lines of therapy; the GOG first-line trial (PMID 18534250) halved that estimate. Read the two together before quoting a response rate.

docs.title: Trabectedin vs dacarbazine after anthracycline failure (ET743-SAR-3007)
docs.text:
intervention_id: trabectedin-monotherapy · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Hensley/Demetri (2017)Gynecol Oncol232232 of 577 randomized patients had uLMS (trabectedin 144, dacarbazine 88) — the largest uLMS randomized dataset in this line2L+post hoc subgroup analysis of the randomized phase 3 SAR-3007 trialdacarbazinetrabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 24-h IV q3w; dacarbazine 1 g/m2 q3wHR_PFSmedian PFS (uLMS subset)0.57 HR0.41–0.810.0012mPFS 4.0 vs 1.5 mo; mDoR 6.5 vs 4.1 mouLMS-subset toxicity mirrors the parent trial: transaminitis and cytopenias dominate; two treatment-related deaths in the trabectedin subset (acute renal failure, respiratory distress); discontinuation for related AEs 13% vs 9%.RoB2:Some2bpartial28651804DOIThe uLMS-specific randomized evidence for trabectedin after anthracycline: PFS benefit holds (HR 0.57), OS does not. Post hoc subgroup of a trial not powered for it — treat the point estimates accordingly. AE data from PMC full text (PMC5783302). Demetri/Patel (2016)J Clin Oncol518L-sarcomas only; uLMS was 40% of enrolment (see companion subgroup row); ECOG 0-12L+randomized open-label phase 3, 2:1 allocation, OS primary endpointdacarbazinetrabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 24-h IV infusion q3w; comparator dacarbazine 1 g/m2 q3wHR_PFSmedian PFS0.55 HR—<0.001mPFS 4.2 vs 1.5 mo; mDoR 6.5 vs 4.2 moMyelosuppression and transient transaminitis dominate; treatment-related death rate 2.1% (sepsis, rhabdomyolysis, renal and multiorgan failure) vs 0 with dacarbazine; discontinuation for toxicity 12.6% vs 7.7%.RoB2:Low1bpartial26371143DOIBasis of the US trabectedin approval. docs.title: Pulmonary metastasectomy (International Registry of Lung Metastases)
docs.text:
intervention_id: pulmonary-metastasectomy · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Burt/Jaklitsch (2011)Ann Thorac Surg82single-institution 1989-2004; LMS patients were mostly women (77%), had fewer lesions (mean 1.9) and 48% underwent repeat metastasectomyanyretrospective single-institution cohort——OSmedian OS, LMS vs non-LMS metastasectomy70.00 months—0.049mOS 70 mo (LMS) vs 24 mo (non-LMS)Surgical complications not reported in the abstract.ROBINS-I:Serious4partial21867989DOIWhy the consulting oncologist keeps surgery on the table: resected LMS lung metastases can run an indolent course, and repeat resection is compatible with long survival. n=31 LMS at one hospital, all selected for operability — her bilateral infiltrative pattern is exactly what these series screen out, so this is a best-case ceiling, not an expectation. Pastorino/Putnam (1997)J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg52065,206 metastasectomies from 18 thoracic-surgery units; 88% complete resections; surgical candidates only — a fitness- and biology-selected populationanyinternational multi-institutional registry, retrospective prognostic analysis——OS5-year OS after complete metastasectomy36.00 %——median OS 35 mo after complete resection vs 15 mo incompletePerioperative morbidity and mortality not reported in the abstract; pre-CTCAE-era surgical registry.ROBINS-I:Serious4partial9011700DOIThe reference dataset behind offering lung surgery at all, and the source of the prognostic strata (completeness, DFI, lesion number) her team would apply. Entirely retrospective and surgeon-selected: the 5-year figures describe patients healthy and oligometastatic enough to be operated on, not bilateral infiltrative disease like hers unless induction converts it.

docs.title: SBRT for sarcoma pulmonary metastases (MGH/Penn)
docs.text:
intervention_id: sbrt-pulmonary-metastases · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Baumann/Chen (2020)J Surg Oncol4444 patients / 56 lesions; 82% prior chemotherapy, 66% prior pulmonary resection; median lesion 2.0 cmanyretrospective two-institution cohort—median 50 Gy, various fractionationsotherlocal control at 24 months90.00 %84.00–96.00——No grade >=3 events: three grade 2 chest-wall toxicities and one grade 2 pneumonitis in 44 patients.ROBINS-I:Serious4partial32588468DOILargest multi-institution SBRT series in sarcoma lung metastases: excellent lesion-level control, low toxicity, but OS tracks systemic disease. Navarria/Scorsetti (2015)Eur J Cancer2828 patients / 51 lesions; ECOG 1-2; LMS the commonest histology (36%); median interval from diagnosis to lung metastases 51 monthsanyretrospective single-institution cohort—risk-adapted: 30 Gy/1 fr, 60 Gy/3 fr, 48 Gy/4 fr, 60 Gy/8 fr (VMAT)otheractuarial 5-year local control96.00 %———No grade 3-4 toxicity recorded; no hospitalisations.ROBINS-I:Serious4partial25686482DOISmall, highly selected (<=4 lesions, controlled primary, long median disease interval), which explains the striking survival figures; that selection is the caveat to carry, not the local-control number. docs.title: Prognostic factors for first-line anthracycline chemotherapy in advanced STS (EORTC pooled)
docs.text:
intervention_id: prognostic-context · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes Seagle/Shahabi (2017)Gynecol Oncol74557,455 women, US National Cancer Database 1998-2013; matched-cohort analyses for surgery/chemotherapy questionsanyretrospective national registry cohort with matched analysesno chemotherapy (matched, metastatic subset)—OSmedian OS with vs without chemotherapy, metastatic uLMS19.40 months16.40–23.00<0.001—Registry analysis; no treatment-safety data.ROBINS-I:Serious3bpartial28317559DOIPopulation-level anchor for metastatic-uLMS prognosis in the pre-LMS-04 era: median OS around 10-19 months depending on chemotherapy receipt, against which LMS-04's 33-month combination-arm median reads as a different disease course. Van Glabbeke/Tursz (1999)J Clin Oncol21852,185 patients pooled from seven EORTC trials; LMS included among histologies1Lpooled prognostic-factor analysis of prospective trial data (Cox and logistic models)——otherindependent prognostic factors for OSmedian OS 51 weeks; ORR 26% mixed———Prognostic analysis; no treatment-safety data.ROBINS-I:Moderate2bpartial10458228DOIThe trial-grade basis for reading her ~23-month interval as favorable: a long time lapse between initial diagnosis and advanced-disease treatment independently predicted longer survival in 2,185 first-line anthracycline patients. docs.title: Intraperitoneal morcellation and outcomes of localized uLMS (DFCI/BWH)
docs.text:
intervention_id: morcellation-outcomes · 2 row(s)

ReportnPopulationLineDesignComparatorDose / scheduleEndpointOutcomeEffectCIpDurabilitySafetyRoBTierCase fitPMIDDOINotes George/Muto (2014)Cancer5858 women, 2007-2012: 19 morcellated vs 39 total abdominal hysterectomy at first surgeryanyretrospective two-institution cohort, multivariate-adjustedtotal abdominal hysterectomy without morcellation—otherrecurrence-free survival, morcellated vs intact3.18 HR1.50–6.800.003mRFS 10.8 vs 39.6 moSurgical-outcomes cohort; no systemic-therapy safety data.ROBINS-I:Serious3bpartial24923260DOIDirectly on the target_validator's open question: if her September 2024 hysterectomy for presumed benign leiomyoma used morcellation, recurrence risk roughly triples and shifts toward peritoneal dissemination — which changes staging imaging (abdomen/pelvis surveillance), not just history-taking. docs.title: Trabectedin — mononuclear-phagocyte depletion
docs.text:
intervention_id: trabectedin-monotherapy · 4 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Belgiovine/D'Incalci (2021)Eur J Immunolmurine fibrosarcoma poorly responsive to PD-1 blockade, in immunocompetent mice—anti-PD-1 alone, trabectedin alone, and untreated tumourstrabectedin given before anti-PD-1 (sequential, not concurrent)Removing tumour-associated macrophages lifts myeloid suppression; T-cell and interferon-response transcription rises, Pdcd1 goes up, and the tumour becomes answerable to PD-1 blockade.Treated tumours upregulated CD3, CD8, perforin, granzyme B and IFN-response genes, with a marked rise in Pdcd1. Trabectedin given ahead of anti-PD-1 improved efficacy in a model that otherwise resists checkpoint blockade.moderatemedcross tumor only34570376DOIMouse fibrosarcoma, not LMS, and the benefit depended on trabectedin coming first. No preclinical data exist for adding checkpoint blockade to an LMS-04-style doxorubicin-trabectedin schedule. Germano/Allavena (2013)Cancer Cellfour syngeneic mouse tumour models plus human blood monocytes; myeloid-cell transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumours—vehicle-treated tumour-bearing mice; trabectedin-resistant tumour variants used to separate tumour-cell from myeloid effects—Caspase-8 apoptosis triggered through TRAIL receptors. Monocytes carry signalling TRAIL receptors where neutrophils and lymphocytes carry decoys, which confines the killing to the mononuclear phagocyte compartment.Trabectedin killed monocytes and macrophages in blood, spleen and tumour while leaving other leukocytes intact, and tumour angiogenesis fell alongside them. Transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumours placed the myeloid kill inside the antitumour effect rather than beside it. Monocyte counts, including tumour-associated macrophages, dropped in treated patients as well.strongmedpartial23410977DOINone of the four models is leiomyosarcoma, and the human confirmation is peripheral monocyte counts rather than sarcoma biopsies. Whether any of this reaches an infiltrative pulmonary metastasis is untested. Aune/Pommier (2008)Clin Cancer Resisogenic repair-mutant human fibroblasts (CSB, XPA, XPC, XPD, XPF, XPG) and VHL-deficient cells, with complemented counterparts; several cancer cell lines—repair-proficient parental lines and genetically complemented mutants; proteasome inhibition with MG132—Trabectedin adducts recruit transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair, and the stalled complex is resolved by proteasomal degradation of elongating RNA Pol II, which needs both TC-NER and an intact VHL complex.Transcribing RNA Pol II was degraded rapidly after trabectedin exposure, and cells defective in TC-NER or VHL failed to degrade it. VHL-deficient cells also resisted trabectedin killing, while XPC cells, defective only in global-genome repair, behaved like wild type.strongmedcross tumor only18927284DOIRepair-mutant fibroblasts and epithelial lines, no sarcoma model. This is the reason trabectedin sensitivity tracks repair proficiency rather than proliferation rate, which is what separates it from a conventional cytotoxic. Allavena/D'Incalci (2005)Cancer Reshuman blood monocytes, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages, and tumour-associated macrophages freshly isolated from ovarian cancer; monocyte counts in treated patients—untreated monocytes/macrophages; lymphocytes as the comparator leukocyte population5 nmol/L for cytotoxicity; sub-cytotoxic concentrations for differentiation and cytokine readoutsDNA minor-groove binding with selective interference in inducible transcription; monocytes die at low nanomolar exposure, and below that concentration the drug shuts down CCL2 and IL-6 transcription.Monocytes underwent apoptosis at 5 nmol/L while lymphocytes tolerated roughly five-fold more drug. Sub-cytotoxic exposure blocked monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation and cut CCL2 and IL-6 output from monocytes, macrophages, ovarian TAMs and tumour cells alike.moderatemedcross tumor only15805300DOIHuman cells in vitro plus ovarian TAMs; no sarcoma tissue anywhere in the paper. CCL2 suppression is the proposed link to reduced monocyte recruitment, inferred rather than measured in tumour.

docs.title: ET-743 (trabectedin) + doxorubicin — preclinical basis for the combination
docs.text:
intervention_id: doxorubicin-trabectedin-lms04 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Meco/Riccardi (2003)Cancer Chemother PharmacolTE-671 rhabdomyosarcoma clonogenic assay and nude-mouse xenograft; C3H mice bearing UV2237M fibrosarcoma and its P-gp-overexpressing doxorubicin-resistant subline—each drug alone and untreated controls; pharmacokinetic sampling in both single-agent and combination armsET-743 1 h before doxorubicin, simultaneously, or 1 h after (three sequences compared)Two non-overlapping DNA-damage mechanisms — minor-groove alkylation whose cytotoxicity runs through transcription-coupled repair, versus topoisomerase II poisoning — combined without any pharmacokinetic interaction to account for the gain.Isobologram analysis gave combination indices just under 1, so the in-vitro interaction is additive at best. In vivo the pair produced log cell kill of 0.85-1.12 in TE-671 where either agent alone reached only 0.13-0.33, and the combination worked in a P-gp-positive subline resistant to both single drugs. Giving ET-743 one hour ahead edged out simultaneous or reversed dosing (LCK 1.12 vs 0.85 and 0.92), and doxorubicin levels in tumour, liver, heart and kidney were unchanged by co-administration.moderatemedpartial12783202DOIRhabdomyosarcoma and fibrosarcoma models from 2003; no leiomyosarcoma and no uterine model. The sequencing advantage rests on one small in-vivo comparison, and nothing in this or any other preclinical study addresses the trabectedin maintenance phase, which is an empirical clinical design.

docs.title: Lurbinectedin — macrophage and monocyte depletion
docs.text:
intervention_id: lurbinectedin-doxorubicin · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Belgiovine/D'Incalci (2017)Br J Cancertumour-bearing mice including a lurbinectedin-resistant tumour variant; purified human monocytes in vitro—untreated tumour-bearing mice; resistant variant used to separate tumour-cell kill from microenvironment effects—Same structural class as trabectedin: transcription and repair inhibition in tumour cells, plus caspase-8-dependent apoptosis of monocytes and suppression of CCL2, CXCL8 and VEGF at sub-lethal concentrations.Circulating monocytes, intratumoural macrophages and vessel density all fell, including in the resistant variant where the tumour cells themselves were untouched. Below the apoptotic dose, monocyte adhesion and migration collapsed alongside downregulation of Rho-GTPase family genes.moderatemedcross tumor only28683469DOINo sarcoma model and no doxorubicin combination, which is what the LMS trial (NCT06088290) actually tests. Accrual on that trial closed before this patient's diagnosis was corrected, so the row is mechanistic context.

docs.title: Trabectedin + olaparib (PARP1-dependent synergy)
docs.text:
intervention_id: trabectedin-olaparib · 1 row(s)

docs.title: Palbociclib in Rb-positive vs Rb-negative LMS cell lines
docs.text:
intervention_id: abemaciclib-gemcitabine · 4 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Böhm/Barth (2019)SarcomaSK-LMS-1 (Rb-expressing) and SK-UT-1 (Rb-negative) leiomyosarcoma cell lines; genomic profiling of 18 LMS samples; p16/CDK4/CDK6/p-Rb IHC across 159 samples from 99 LMS patients18 tumour samples across 9 patients for profiling; 99 patients / 159 samples for IHCuntreated cells; the Rb-negative line serves as the internal biological control—Palbociclib blocks CDK4/6-mediated Rb phosphorylation. With no Rb protein present there is nothing downstream to hold, and the drug has no substrate through which to arrest the cycle.Palbociclib collapsed phospho-Rb (Ser780), slowed proliferation and forced G0/G1 arrest in Rb-positive SK-LMS-1, while Rb-negative SK-UT-1 was unaffected. CDK4 amplification turned up in 5 of 18 LMS samples, and an IHC-defined potential-responder phenotype in 29 of 99 patients.moderatemedstrong30804704DOITwo cell lines, no in-vivo arm, and the responder phenotype is an IHC construct never tested prospectively. It is nonetheless the cleanest LMS-specific demonstration that one Rb stain sorts responders from non-responders. Francis/Hunt (2017)Mol Cancer TherSK-LMS1 leiomyosarcoma and HT-1080 fibrosarcoma lines; SK-LMS1 xenografts and Rb-positive patient-derived xenografts from leiomyosarcoma patients—single-agent palbociclib, single-agent AZD1775, vehicle; concurrent versus sequential dosing comparedpalbociclib to arrest, then drug removal followed by doxorubicin or the Wee1 inhibitor AZD1775 (sequential scheduling)Palbociclib holds Rb-positive cells in a reversible G1 arrest; on release they move through the cycle within 6-24 hours, and a synchronised S-G2 population is more vulnerable to agents that act there.Palbociclib arrest was fully reversible, and priming Rb-positive sarcoma cells this way made them more sensitive to doxorubicin and to Wee1 inhibition. The palbociclib-AZD1775 synergy held in SK-LMS1 xenografts and in Rb-positive leiomyosarcoma PDX.strongmedpartial28619757DOILMS PDX but no stated uterine primary. The sensitisation depends on sequencing — arrest, release, then the S-G2 agent — which is the opposite of concurrent dosing (see McClendon 2012). McClendon/Knudsen (2012)Cell CycleRB-proficient and RB-deficient triple-negative breast cancer cell lines treated with palbociclib plus doxorubicin—doxorubicin alone; RB-deficient lines as the internal control for RB dependenceCDK4/6 inhibitor and doxorubicin given together (concurrent exposure)Genotoxic cytotoxicity needs cells to cycle. An RB-mediated G1 arrest pulls them out of the phase where the damage is lethal, so the arrest shields the cell rather than adding to the kill.In RB-proficient models the pairing was cytostatically cooperative but protected cells from doxorubicin-mediated killing, and viable populations recurred after treatment. In RB-deficient cells palbociclib changed nothing about the doxorubicin response, confirming the protection runs through RB.negativemedcross tumor only22751436DOIBreast models and doxorubicin rather than gemcitabine, but gemcitabine is likewise S-phase-dependent. This is the mechanistic caution to raise against a concurrent abemaciclib-plus-gemcitabine schedule in an Rb-intact tumour. Dean/Knudsen (2010)Oncogenepanel of breast cancer cell lines plus RB knockdown in immortalised mammary epithelium and multiple breast cancer subtypes; PD-0332991 (palbociclib)—RB-proficient parental lines and non-targeting shRNA controls—CDK4/6 inhibition works by keeping RB active as a transcriptional repressor of E2F targets and by holding down CDK2 activity. Chronic RB loss moves cells into a CDK4/6-independent state; acquired resistance follows the same logic through loss of CDK2 restraint.Chronic RB loss produced CDK4/6 independence and resistance to palbociclib, and direct RB knockdown reproduced it. Acquired resistance in initially sensitive models mapped to attenuated CDK2 inhibitors, so redundancy within the cell-cycle machinery is a second route to failure.strongmedcross tumor only20473330DOIBreast models throughout. Carried here because it supplies the mechanistic reason an Rb-intact requirement is a real eligibility gate rather than an enrichment preference.

docs.title: Selective CDK7 inhibition (YKL-5-124) in RB1/TP53-null tumours
docs.text:
intervention_id: rec-617-cdk7 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Zhang/Wong (2020)Cancer Cellhuman small-cell lung cancer lines and multiple aggressive murine SCLC models; SCLC is near-universally RB1- and TP53-null. YKL-5-124 given with and without anti-PD-1—vehicle; anti-PD-1 alone; CDK7 inhibitor alone—CDK7 sits at the junction of cell-cycle CDK activation and RNA Pol II transcription. Inhibiting it in cells that have already lost the RB1 restriction point disrupts cycle progression, forces replication stress and genome instability, and the resulting cytosolic DNA drives immune signalling.CDK7 inhibition blocked cycle progression and induced replication stress and genome instability while switching on immune-response signalling. The consequent T-cell surveillance was amplified by checkpoint blockade, and YKL-5-124 plus anti-PD-1 extended survival across several aggressive SCLC models.stronglowcross tumor only31883968DOISCLC is RB1-null like the trial's target population but is a different lineage entirely, and YKL-5-124 is not REC-617. No CDK7 data of any kind exist in leiomyosarcoma, which makes the RB1-null CDK7 door the thinnest mechanistic branch in this case.

docs.title: ATRX loss and ALT in uterine leiomyosarcoma (target biology)
docs.text:
intervention_id: atr-inhibition-alt · 5 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Goncalves/Tomita (2020)ACS Pharmacol Transl Sci17 osteosarcoma-derived cell lines characterised for telomere maintenance mechanism and telomere length; AZD-6738 (ceralasertib), VE-822 and BAY-1895344n=17 cell lines (8 ALT-positive)ALT-positive and telomerase-positive long-telomere lines compared against short-telomere lines—ATR sustains chromosome stability when telomeres are critically short; the dependency follows telomere length rather than the mechanism used to maintain it.Short telomeres, not ALT, predicted hypersensitivity to all three ATR inhibitors, with chromosome bridges and cell death inside 24 hours. ALT-positive lines carried excessive telomere length and were no more sensitive than telomerase-positive controls.negativemedcross tumor only33344901DOIOsteosarcoma rather than LMS, and in-vitro only. Within sarcoma this is the most directly damaging evidence against treating ALT positivity as an ATR-inhibitor biomarker, and it points to telomere length as the measurement that would actually matter. Chudasama/Fröhling (2018)Nat Communwhole-exome and transcriptome sequencing of leiomyosarcoma tumours plus short-term cultured LMS cells treated with olaparib or cisplatin—untreated cultured LMS cells for the drug-sensitivity work—Near-universal TP53 and RB1 inactivation with widespread copy-number change, chromothripsis and whole-genome duplication; telomere maintenance runs through ALT, and structural-rearrangement burden with the associated mutational signatures produces a BRCAness state that PARP inhibition can act on.TP53 and RB1 were inactivated in nearly every tumour, alternative telomere lengthening was present in 78% of cases, and recurrent alterations hit ATRX, RBL2 and SP100. Most tumours carried hallmarks of BRCAness, and cultured LMS cells were sensitive to olaparib and to cisplatin.moderatemedstrong29321523DOIMixed LMS sites rather than uterine-only, and the drug sensitivity is short-term culture with no in-vivo arm. The near-universal RB1 loss is the single most decision-relevant number here: it shifts the prior for an Rb IHC toward null and away from the abemaciclib door. Mäkinen/Vahteristo (2016)PLoS Genetwhole-exome sequencing of 19 uterine leiomyosarcomas; ATRX IHC in 44 uLMS; telomere-specific FISH for the ALT phenotypen=19 exomes; n=44 tumours for IHCnot applicable — descriptive human tumour series—ATRX loads H3.3 at telomeric chromatin; losing it destabilises telomere maintenance and permits recombination-based lengthening, which is the ALT phenotype that ATR inhibition was proposed to exploit.TP53 was mutated in 6/19, ATRX in 5/19 (every alteration nonsense or frameshift) and MED12 in 4/19. ATRX expression was clearly reduced in 23 of 44 tumours by IHC, and every ATRX-low tumour tested ALT-positive by telomere FISH.—highstrong26891131DOIDescriptive human series with no therapeutic arm; the ATR-inhibitor suggestion in its discussion is an extrapolation from Flynn 2015, not a result. The tight ATRX-IHC-to-ALT concordance is what makes one stain a usable surrogate here. Deeg/Rippe (2016)Front Oncolpanel of ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cell lines plus isogenic pairs in which ALT was active or suppressed; ATR inhibitor VE-821—isogenic ALT-suppressed counterparts — the control Flynn 2015 lackedVE-821 across a concentration rangeSame premise as Flynn 2015, tested with isogenic controls that hold genetic background constant while switching ALT on or off.No general ATR-inhibitor sensitivity followed from ALT status. Sensitivity differences tracked with line-to-line background rather than with the telomere maintenance mechanism.negativelowcross tumor only27602331DOISmall line panel and a single ATR inhibitor, so it does not exclude a narrower ALT-related vulnerability. It does undercut any claim that ATRX loss alone predicts ATR-inhibitor benefit. Flynn/Zou (2015)ScienceALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cancer cell lines, including ATRX-manipulated pairs; ATR inhibitors in vitro—telomerase-positive (non-ALT) cell lines—ATRX loss uncouples cell-cycle control of the telomeric transcript TERRA, leaving RPA bound to telomeres after replication. That nucleoprotein structure is recombinogenic and depends on ATR, which RPA itself recruits.ATR inhibition disrupted the ALT process and caused chromosome fragmentation and apoptosis, with killing reported as selective for ALT-dependent cancer cells.stronglowcross tumor only25593184DOICell lines only, no in-vivo arm, and the central selectivity claim was not reproduced by Deeg 2016 or by the osteosarcoma panel in Goncalves 2020. Treat as the hypothesis that opened the field rather than as a settled vulnerability.

docs.title: PARP inhibition in HR-deficient uterine leiomyosarcoma (PDX)
docs.text:
intervention_id: olaparib-temozolomide · 4 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Dall/Barker (2023)J Exp Clin Cancer Respatient-derived xenografts from HRD uterine leiomyosarcoma, including a paired PDX derived after PARP-inhibitor exposure; WGS/WES/panel screening of a 58-patient uLMS cohort58 patients screened; 5 (9%) HRD; PDX generated from HRD cases including one post-PARPi pairolaparib alone and olaparib plus cisplatin compared against the PARP1-selective AZD5305—Homozygous BRCA2 deletion and COSMIC signature 3 with high genome-wide LOH define an HR-deficient subset; PARP inhibition converts unrepaired single-strand damage into lethal double-strand breaks, and PARP1-selective trapping does so with less of the off-target PARP2 burden.All 13 uLMS analysed by WGS carried a dominant signature 3, and 5 of 58 patients had HRD uLMS, in every confirmed case through homozygous BRCA2 deletion. PDX responses were fastest, deepest and most durable with the PARP1-selective AZD5305 rather than olaparib or olaparib plus cisplatin, holding even in a PDX derived after clinical PARPi exposure that had acquired PRKDC resistance mutations.stronghighstrong37143137DOISmall PDX numbers and a paper that interleaves patient outcomes with model pharmacology. The agent that worked best, AZD5305, is not the one this patient could reach; the accessible branch is olaparib plus temozolomide. Castroviejo-Bermejo/Serra (2018)EMBO Mol Medbreast cancer patient-derived xenograft panels treated with olaparib, plus archival clinical tumour samples including PALB2-related cancers—genomic HRD score and exome/BRCA1-methylation analysis run head-to-head against the RAD51 score—RAD51 nuclear foci in replicating cells report whether homologous recombination is actually executing at the time of testing, which a sequencing panel cannot show — a gene may be intact and the pathway still broken, or mutated and functionally reverted.The RAD51 score separated PARPi-sensitive from PARPi-resistant PDX and outperformed the genomic HRD score in an independent panel. In archival samples the assay classified every PALB2-related tumour as HR-deficient, extending the deficient population beyond BRCA1/2 carriers.strongmedcross tumor only30377213DOIBreast PDX and breast archival tissue; the assay needs proliferating cells and geminin co-staining, so specimen quality governs interpretability. Its only uLMS outcome data are the 22-patient NCI 10250 trial, where RAD51-defined HR deficiency separated PFS of 11.2 from 5.4 months. Smith/Houghton (2015)Clin Cancer ResPediatric Preclinical Testing Program in-vitro panel and xenografts, including 10 Ewing sarcoma models; talazoparib with temozolomide or topotecan10 Ewing sarcoma xenograft models among a broader paneltalazoparib alone, temozolomide alone, vehicletalazoparib 0.1 mg/kg BID × 5 d with temozolomide 30 mg/kg/d × 5 (combination A); or talazoparib 0.25 mg/kg BID × 5 d with temozolomide 12 mg/kg/d × 5 (combination B)Trapping-competent PARP inhibition converts temozolomide base damage into replication-blocking lesions; pharmacodynamic loss of PARP appeared only in models that responded.Talazoparib potentiated temozolomide up to 85-fold in vitro, with the largest shifts in Ewing sarcoma and leukaemia lines. In vivo the combination was significantly synergistic in 5 of 10 Ewing xenografts and only modestly active in most other models, and both schedules represented the maximum tolerated combination.moderatemedcross tumor only25500058DOIEwing sarcoma, where PARPi sensitivity is driven by EWS-FLI1 rather than HR deficiency, so the mechanism is not the one proposed for uLMS. Talazoparib traps far more strongly than olaparib, making the potentiation an upper bound, and the myelosuppression that dominates the clinical regimen is exactly what the tolerability ceiling here predicts. Murai/Pommier (2014)J Pharmacol Exp Thergenetically modified chicken DT40 lymphoma lines with human DU145 prostate and SF295 glioblastoma cells; olaparib and veliparib against temozolomide, camptothecin, cisplatin and etoposide—veliparib, a potent catalytic inhibitor that traps poorly, as the mechanistic contrast to olaparib—PARP inhibitors kill in two separable ways: catalytic blockade, and trapping of PARP-DNA complexes at damage sites. Which one matters depends on the partner drug — temozolomide-induced N-methylpurine lesions recruit PARP1 to base-excision intermediates, where a trapped complex becomes the lethal lesion.Temozolomide combinations needed trapping as well as catalytic inhibition, and olaparib, the stronger trapper, outperformed veliparib. Camptothecin combinations ran on catalytic inhibition alone, and cisplatin or etoposide gained little or nothing from either drug.moderatemedcross tumor only24650937DOIAvian and epithelial cell lines, no sarcoma and no in-vivo arm. Its value here is explaining why the uLMS trial regimen pairs olaparib with temozolomide specifically rather than with a platinum.

docs.title: Sarcoma immune classes and B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures
docs.text:
intervention_id: pembrolizumab · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Guo/Li (2025)Front Immunolsingle-cell RNA sequencing of four metastatic lesions (pelvic cavity, rectum, peritoneum, bladder) from one treatment-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma patient, against five normal myometrium samples; multiplex immunofluorescence validation and TCGA-SARC survival correlationn=1 patient (4 metastatic sites); n=5 normal myometrium controlsnormal uterine myometrium—An immunosuppressed niche built from exhausted CD8 T cells (LAG3, HAVCR2, TIGIT), M2-polarised CD163+ macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils, with MIF-CD74/CD44 and CXCL8 signalling sustaining angiogenesis and macrophage polarisation.The metastatic microenvironment was dominated by exhausted CD8 T cells and M2 macrophages rather than by any effector population, with naive markers (CCR7, MAL) lost along the pseudotime trajectory. The macrophage-heavy composition is the same compartment trabectedin depletes.—lowstrong40948800DOIOne patient. Descriptive, hypothesis-generating, and no therapy was given; it earns its place only because uLMS-specific microenvironment data at single-cell resolution are otherwise almost absent. Petitprez/Fridman (2020)Naturegene-expression profiling of 608 soft-tissue sarcoma tumours with in-situ validation in an independent cohort and a phase 2 pembrolizumab trialn=608 tumours for classificationnot applicable — classification study with a prospective response cohort attachedpembrolizumab per the phase 2 trial protocolResponse to PD-1 blockade in sarcoma tracks with the composition of the microenvironment rather than with tumour mutational burden. B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures mark the class where antigen presentation is organised enough for checkpoint blockade to act on.Five microenvironment phenotypes emerged: two immune-low, two immune-high, one highly vascularised. B-cell content was the strongest prognostic factor even after accounting for CD8 T cells and cytotoxic signature, and the TLS-rich class E showed both better survival and a high response rate to pembrolizumab.moderatehighpartial31942077DOILeiomyosarcoma falls predominantly into the immune-low and highly vascularised classes, which is the structural reason checkpoint blockade underperforms in this histology. Response rates are reported by class, not by histology, so no LMS-specific number can be read off this paper.

docs.title: ATRA differentiating immature myeloid suppressor cells

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Kusmartsev/Gabrilovich (2003)Cancer Resmultiple tumour-bearing mouse models with adoptive transfer of immature myeloid cells; ATRA combined with two cancer vaccines—vaccine alone and untreated tumour-bearing miceATRA administered in vivo to tumour-bearing mice (schedule per original protocol)ATRA drives immature myeloid cells to differentiate into dendritic cells, macrophages and granulocytes, which removes the suppressive population rather than killing tumour cells directly.ATRA sharply reduced immature myeloid cells across every model tested, and adoptive transfer confirmed the cells had differentiated rather than died.
