docs.title: B7-H3 expression across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes
docs.text:
intervention_id: b7h3-adc · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Lynch/Pollack (2024)BMC Cancerimmunohistochemistry on 153 soft-tissue sarcoma specimens spanning 15 subtypes, scored in tumour and in associated vasculaturen=153 specimens, 15 subtypesnot applicable — expression survey; PD-L1 and PD-1 status compared where previously assessed—B7-H3 (CD276) is a cell-surface immune-regulatory molecule with limited normal-tissue expression, which is what makes it usable as an ADC or CAR target rather than as a driver.B7-H3 was expressed in 97% of specimens and at high level in 69.2%, with vascular positivity in 94.7%. Expression was independent of prior treatment, tumour size, grade and patient age, and uncorrelated with PD-L1 or PD-1.—highpartial39478506DOIPrevalence only — no functional or therapeutic readout, and per-subtype numbers for leiomyosarcoma are not broken out in the abstract. High prior probability of a positive stain is not the same as a dependency, and vascular positivity raises a separate on-target question. Brignole/Ponzoni (2023)J Immunother Cancerhuman neuroblastoma cell lines, multicellular tumour spheroids, and orthotopic, pseudometastatic and resected mouse neuroblastoma models; co-culture of B7-H3-negative murine NX-S2 cells with B7-H3-positive human cells—irrelevant (anti-CD20) duocarmycin ADC; topotecan-temozolomide as the standard-of-care comparator1 mg/kg IV weekly × 3 weeks, extended to 4 weeks and repeated cycles in survival experimentsA cleavable valine-citrulline linker releases membrane-permeable duocarmycin, so payload liberated inside an antigen-positive cell can cross into neighbouring antigen-negative cells — the bystander effect that makes heterogeneous or low antigen tractable.Cytotoxicity ran from IC50 5.1-53.9 ng/mL in monolayer and 17.8-364 ng/mL in spheroids. B7-H3-negative murine cells, untouched by the ADC alone, were killed when co-cultured with B7-H3-positive cells, and treatment delayed or arrested relapse across orthotopic and resected models without weight loss or haematologic toxicity.strongmedcross tumor only37775116DOINeuroblastoma throughout, with no sarcoma model and no leiomyosarcoma. The bystander demonstration is the part that transfers, and it is the mechanistic argument for a B7-H3 ADC where expression is heterogeneous rather than uniform. Majzner/Mackall (2019)Clin Cancer Resxenograft models of osteosarcoma, medulloblastoma and Ewing sarcoma; B7-H3 CAR T cells tested against targets differing in surface antigen density—control T cells without the B7-H3 CAR; target cells expressing low versus high surface B7-H3—CAR T-cell killing scales with the number of antigen molecules per target cell. Below a threshold density the synapse fails to trigger, which is what creates a therapeutic window despite low-level B7-H3 on normal tissue.B7-H3 CAR T cells caused regression of established solid tumours across several xenograft models. Efficacy depended heavily on surface antigen density and fell away sharply against low-expressing targets.strongmedcross tumor only30655315DOIPediatric solid-tumour xenografts, no leiomyosarcoma model and no ADC. The density dependence is the transferable point: it is why an IHC-positive result alone does not establish that a B7-H3 agent will work, and why the 69% 'high' stratum matters more than the 97% positivity figure.

docs.title: FAP-2286 radioligand — preclinical imaging and therapy
docs.text:
intervention_id: fap-radioligand · 4 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Ceuppens/Breckpot (2025)Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaginghuman-FAP-expressing lung tumour model in immunocompetent mice; FAP-targeting single-domain antibody 4AH29 labelled with 225Ac or 131I, with and without PD-L1 blockade—vehicle solution; PD-L1 blockade alone[131I]I-GMIB-4AH29 and [225Ac]Ac-DOTA-4AH29 at low and high doses; high-dose 225Ac combined with PD-L1 checkpoint blockadeAlpha emission deposits high linear-energy-transfer dose over a few cell diameters while a beta emitter spreads a lower dose further; the report also links radionuclide therapy to PD-L1 upregulation, which supplies the rationale for adding checkpoint blockade.Tumour uptake was high for both radionuclides, with 225Ac retention decaying far more slowly (2.1 to 1.7 %IA/g between 1 and 24 h) than 131I (3.5 to 0.9 %IA/g). Both improved survival over vehicle, PD-L1 rose in 225Ac-treated tumours, and the 225Ac-plus-PD-L1-blockade combination was synergistic.moderatelowweak39237746DOIFAP was engineered onto the tumour cells, so this tests direct antigen targeting rather than the stromal-to-tumour crossfire that FAP therapy in a sarcoma would depend on. Lung carcinoma model, different binder chemistry from either agent this patient could reach. Crane/Federman (2023)SarcomaIHC on 63 bone and soft-tissue tumour samples with 30 adjacent normal tissues, scored separately for stromal and tumour-cell compartments; RNA-seq comparison across 10,626 samples and survival analysis in 168 sarcomasn=63 tumours; n=30 adjacent normal; n=168 sarcomas for survivaladjacent normal tissue and positive controls—FAP is a marker of activated fibroblasts. In mesenchymal tumours the malignant cell is itself of fibroblastic lineage, so the antigen is not confined to the stromal compartment the way it is in carcinomas.Intensity ≥2 with density ≥25% appeared in stromal cells of 77.7% of tumours and in tumour cells of 50.7%. Sarcomas ranked among the highest FAP-expressing cancer types by RNA-seq, and FAP level carried no overall-survival association.—highpartial37333052DOIMixed bone and soft-tissue histologies with no leiomyosarcoma breakout, and no functional or therapeutic arm. It does change the mechanistic argument: in sarcoma a FAP radioligand may deliver dose directly to tumour cells rather than relying solely on crossfire from stroma. Zboralski/Osterkamp (2022)Eur J Nucl Med Mol ImagingFAP-expressing HEK293 tumours and sarcoma patient-derived xenografts in mice; IHC and autoradiography on primary human cancer specimens including sarcoma—FAPI-46, a small-molecule FAP agent, as the head-to-head comparator; non-FAP-expressing tumours for specificity68Ga-, 111In- and 177Lu-FAP-2286 for biodistribution; 177Lu-FAP-2286 for therapyA cyclic peptide binder coupled to a chelator: it holds at FAP-positive tissue long enough for a bound beta emitter to deposit dose, with renal clearance keeping normal-tissue exposure low.Tumour uptake was rapid and persistent across all three radionuclides with minimal normal-tissue signal, and 177Lu-FAP-2286 produced antitumour activity in FAP-expressing HEK293 tumours and in sarcoma PDX without significant weight loss. Tumour retention and suppression outlasted FAPI-46.moderatemedpartial35608703DOIThe sarcoma evidence is PDX efficacy without histology-level detail, and PDX stroma is host mouse tissue, so what the ligand engaged in those tumours is not resolvable from the report. The engineered HEK293 model tests direct antigen binding rather than the stromal-crossfire premise. Tran/Rosenberg (2013)J Exp MedFAP-reactive CAR T cells transferred into mice bearing a variety of subcutaneous tumours, across two mouse strains; FAP staining of 18 human tumours and of mouse and clinical-grade human multipotent bone marrow stromal cells18 human tumours stained; two mouse strains testeduntreated and control-CAR tumour-bearing mice—FAP is not tumour-restricted. It is expressed on PDGFR-α+ Sca-1+ multipotent bone marrow stromal cells in mice and on clinical-grade human BMSCs, so any FAP-directed effector reaches the marrow niche.FAP-reactive CAR T cells were only weakly active against tumours yet caused significant cachexia and lethal bone toxicity in two mouse strains. Both mouse and human multipotent BMSCs were recognised by the same T cells.negativemedcross tumor only23712432DOIA CAR T-cell platform rather than a radioligand, and the dose delivered to marrow stroma by a peptide with renal clearance is not the same exposure. It remains the sharpest evidence that FAP positivity on a PET scan does not make FAP a tumour-exclusive target.

docs.title: Intratumoural hypoxia, HIF-1α/PLOD2 and sarcoma lung metastasis
docs.text:
intervention_id: high-altitude-hypoxia-context · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Galis/Rajtik (2023)Cardiovasc ToxicolWistar rats given doxorubicin, with or without intermittent hypoxic preconditioning beforehand; no tumour present—doxorubicin without preconditioning; untreated ratsdoxorubicin 4 mg/kg IP weekly × 4; intermittent hypoxic preconditioning for 2 weeks before the first dosePreconditioning raised SERCA2a expression, which the authors link to preserved calcium handling; HIF-1α levels did not change, and TRPV1/TRPV4 loss and suppressed CaMKII activation followed doxorubicin regardless.Preconditioned rats retained more cardiac output than rats given doxorubicin alone, with higher SERCA2a on western blot and no change in HIF-1α.weaklowweak37119387DOICycled normobaric hypoxia in healthy rats is not continuous residence at 8,500 ft, no tumour was present, and the mechanism is inferred from protein levels rather than measured function. Logged to record that the altitude question has no translatable preclinical answer — direction of effect is unresolved and should not be used either to reassure or to alarm. Eisinger-Mathason/Simon (2013)Cancer Discovautochthonous LSL-KrasG12D/+; Trp53fl/fl murine undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and allografts, with HIF-1α or PLOD2 deletion and PLOD2 rescue; human sarcoma expression analysis—HIF-1α-proficient and PLOD2-proficient tumours; ectopic PLOD2 re-expression in HIF-1α-deficient tumourspharmacologic PLOD inhibition in vivoHypoxia drives HIF-1α to induce PLOD2, which modifies and organises collagen in the primary tumour. That altered matrix supports migration and dissemination without affecting primary tumour growth.Losing HIF-1α or PLOD2 disrupted collagen modification, cell migration and pulmonary metastasis while leaving primary growth intact, and re-expressing PLOD2 restored metastatic potential in HIF-1α-deficient tumours. Human metastatic primary lesions carried elevated HIF1A and PLOD2, and pharmacologic PLOD inhibition suppressed metastases.stronglowweak23906982DOIThis is intratumoural hypoxia in a UPS model and speaks to lung tropism in sarcoma generally. It says nothing about ambient hypoxia at 2,600 m: no sarcoma model has been run under chronic hypobaric conditions, and the two forms of hypoxia are not interchangeable.

docs.title: LOXO-101 (larotrectinib) against an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion
docs.text:
intervention_id: larotrectinib · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Doebele/Low (2015)Cancer DiscovTRK-fusion-bearing human cancer cell lines in vitro and in vivo, alongside a soft-tissue sarcoma patient with lung metastases carrying an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion confirmed by in-situ proximity ligationn=1 patient; cell-line panel size not statednon-fusion cell lines for selectivityLOXO-101 orally, phase 1 dosing (NCT02122913)Selective ATP-competitive inhibition of TRKA/B/C. A fusion partner drives constitutive kinase activation, making the whole tumour dependent on that one signal, which is why response is fast when the fusion is genuinely the driver.Fusion-bearing cell lines showed inhibition of the fusion oncoprotein with reduced proliferation in vitro and tumour growth in vivo. The sarcoma patient had rapid, substantial tumour regression with improvement in dyspnea and oxygen saturation.strongmedweak26216294DOIPreclinical content is thin next to the clinical case, and NTRK fusions are rare in leiomyosarcoma. Carried because the fusion has never been tested here and spindle-cell morphology with an earlier benign sign-out is the setting where an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal tumour is missed.

Master inventory: 25 clinical (22 included, 3 considered & excluded) + 37 pre-clinical (34 included, 3 considered & excluded) + 24 additional trial publications/registrations. One row per paper, sorted by year (newest first). Excluded rows are papers a Libby agent reviewed and chose NOT to feed to the board, with the exclusion reason captured. Toxicities use CTCAE-style term · grade · n/N · rate. Pre-clinical rows leave the toxicity cell blank by design. A printable PDF version is linked from the case Downloads section.

ReportReferenceTypeInclusionInterventionIndication / modelDesignnEffect sizeVarianceToxicities (type · n/N · rate)Case fitNotes —/— (2026)—NCT07516925trial publicationincludedivonescimabunresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma, 1-3 prior lines (or declined first-line standard of care) (2L+)none requiredsingle-arm phase 2 of ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody)——ORR (primary)——partialEnrolls LMS after 1-3 prior lines, with an unusual clause admitting patients who decline first-line standard of care — so it is technically open to her now, though her planned LMS-04 induction is the better first move and keeps her eligible here afterward. ECOG ceiling is 0-2; hers is an undocumented intake assumption. Measurable disease and archival tissue are required, and the infiltrative pulmonary pattern may complicate target-lesion selection. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2026)—NCT07633756trial publicationincludedREC-617metastatic or unresectable RB1-negative leiomyosarcoma after ≥1 prior systemic line (2L+)RB1-negative by IHC (0% expression) requiredopen-label phase 1b of REC-617, a selective CDK7 inhibitor——safety/RP2D (primary)——partialRB1 loss is common in uLMS but hers has never been tested; RB1 IHC on the archival block is the assay that decides whether this trial exists for her, in mirror image to the Rb-intact requirement of the abemaciclib study. Requires ≥1 prior line, so it slots in after LMS-04, plus a biopsy-amenable lesion and measurable disease. ECOG ceiling is 2; her score is an undocumented intake assumption. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2026)—NCT07686367trial publicationincludedbrenetafuspmetastatic/unresectable synovial sarcoma or myxoid round cell liposarcoma, HLA-A*02:01-positive (2L+)HLA-A*02:01 genotype required; PRAME-directed (ImmTAC)phase 2 of brenetafusp (PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) in rare cancers (NCI)——ORR (primary)——weakThis protocol names synovial sarcoma and MRCLS only, so it is informational for her — but it marks the PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 ImmTAC class arriving in sarcoma, an off-the-shelf alternative to TCR-T on the identical eligibility platform. Whether any of this class is assessable for her turns on the same untyped HLA allele and unstained PRAME as the IMA203 row. Watch for histology expansion; the drug is in phase 3 in melanoma. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted Lefler/Basu Mallick (2025)JCO Precis OncolPMID 40601892preclinicalexcludedPan-sarcoma expression-outlier analysis that lands on chordoma; leiomyosarcoma was not among the subtypes with CDK7 outlier overexpression, and the cell-line work is chordoma only. Reviewed as the closest thing to a sarcoma-wide CDK7 rationale, and it does not support one in LMS.Pan-sarcoma CDK/cyclin outlier expression (CDK7 in chordoma)—————n/a (preclinical)—Excluded: Pan-sarcoma expression-outlier analysis that lands on chordoma; leiomyosarcoma was not among the subtypes with CDK7 outlier overexpression, and the cell-line work is chordoma only. Reviewed as the closest thing to a sarcoma-wide CDK7 rationale, and it does not support one in LMS. Guo/Li (2025)Front ImmunolPMID 40948800preclinicalincludedSingle-cell map of the metastatic uLMS microenvironmentsingle-cell RNA sequencing of four metastatic lesions (pelvic cavity, rectum, peritoneum, bladder) from one treatment-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma patient, against five normal myometrium samples; multiplex immunofluorescence validation and TCGA-SARC survival correlationAn immunosuppressed niche built from exhausted CD8 T cells (LAG3, HAVCR2, TIGIT), M2-polarised CD163+ macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils, with MIF-CD74/CD44 and CXCL8 signalling sustaining angiogenesis and macrophage polarisation.n=1 patient (4 metastatic sites); n=5 normal myometrium controlsThe metastatic microenvironment was dominated by exhausted CD8 T cells and M2 macrophages rather than by any effector population, with naive markers (CCR7, MAL) lost along the pseudotime trajectory. The macrophage-heavy composition is the same compartment trabectedin depletes.vs normal uterine myometriumtranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)strongOne patient. Descriptive, hypothesis-generating, and no therapy was given; it earns its place only because uLMS-specific microenvironment data at single-cell resolution are otherwise almost absent. Ceuppens/Breckpot (2025)Eur J Nucl Med Mol ImagingPMID 39237746preclinicalincludedAlpha versus beta FAP-targeted radionuclide therapyhuman-FAP-expressing lung tumour model in immunocompetent mice; FAP-targeting single-domain antibody 4AH29 labelled with 225Ac or 131I, with and without PD-L1 blockadeAlpha emission deposits high linear-energy-transfer dose over a few cell diameters while a beta emitter spreads a lower dose further; the report also links radionuclide therapy to PD-L1 upregulation, which supplies the rationale for adding checkpoint blockade.—moderate — Tumour uptake was high for both radionuclides, with 225Ac retention decaying far more slowly (2.1 to 1.7 %IA/g between 1 and 24 h) than 131I (3.5 to 0.9 %IA/g). Both improved survival over vehicle, PD-L1 rose in 225Ac-treated tumours, and the 225Ac-plus-PD-L1-blockade combination was synergistic.vs vehicle solution; PD-L1 blockade alonetranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)weakFAP was engineered onto the tumour cells, so this tests direct antigen targeting rather than the stromal-to-tumour crossfire that FAP therapy in a sarcoma would depend on. Lung carcinoma model, different binder chemistry from either agent this patient could reach. —/— (2025)—NCT06528769trial publicationincludedall-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) + cemiplimabadvanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma after standard-of-care chemotherapy (2L+)none requiredsingle-arm phase 2 of all-trans retinoic acid + cemiplimab——ORR (primary)——partialRequires prior standard-of-care chemotherapy, so it opens once LMS-04 fails; no cap on prior lines. ECOG 0-2 allowed, but her score is an intake assumption that needs documenting, and RECIST-measurable disease is required against an infiltrative pulmonary pattern. No biomarker gate — one of the few immunotherapy routes in LMS that does not wait on her missing profiling. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2025)—NCT07156565trial publicationincluded[225Ac]RTX-2358relapsed/refractory soft-tissue sarcoma, FAP-positive by FAPi PET (2L+)FAP expression demonstrated on [64Cu]LNTH-1363S FAPi PET — FAP never assessed in this patient; sarcomas are characteristically FAP-highphase 1 dose escalation of [225Ac]RTX-2358 (FAP-targeted alpha radioligand) with FAPi PET selection gate——safety/RP2D——partialA therapeutic alpha-emitter, not an imaging study: the 64Cu-FAPi scan is the selection gate for the 225Ac payload, and one prior regimen suffices, so she could screen directly after LMS-04. Radioligand crossfire does not require uniform antigen expression, which matters in a histology where surface-target heterogeneity undermines ADC and cell-therapy cutoffs. ECOG must be 0-1 (hers is an undocumented assumption), prior radioligand therapy and whole-pelvic RT are exclusions, and US/Canada sites are open. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2025)—NCT06981637trial publicationincludedpegylated liposomal doxorubicin (maintenance)advanced soft-tissue sarcoma with disease control after 4-8 cycles of first-line anthracycline-based treatment (MELODY) (1L (maintenance))none required; randomization within 8 weeks of last anthracycline doserandomized phase 2: pegylated liposomal doxorubicin maintenance vs active surveillance——PFS (primary)——weakThis is the randomized version of the maintenance question her LMS-04 plan answers by design (trabectedin continuation), and she would hit its enrollment window — controlled disease within 8 weeks of the last anthracycline dose — mid-2027 if induction goes well. All sites are in Taiwan, so for a US-band patient it is informational: evidence context for the maintenance decision rather than a destination. The 8-week randomization window is the kind of deadline her team should know exists in this space. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted Pautier/Duffaud (2024)N Engl J MedPMID 39231341clinicalincludedDoxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04) — final OSmetastatic or unresectable uterine or soft-tissue leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive (1L)same 150-patient ITT population as the 2022 primary report; analyses adjusted for uterine vs soft-tissue origin and disease stagefinal overall-survival analysis of the randomized phase 3 LMS-04 trial (median follow-up 55 months)150mOS: 33.00 months combination armmOS: 24.00 months doxorubicin armOS HR: 0.65 adjusted HR for death; 107 of 150 patients had diedmPFS: 12.00 months combination arm, updatedPFS HR: 0.37 adjusted HR, updated at final analysismedian OS95% CI 26.00–48.0095% CI 19.00–31.0095% CI 0.44–0.9595% CI 10.00–16.0095% CI 0.26–0.53Abstract reports only that adverse events and dose reductions were more frequent with doxorubicin-trabectedin; per-term combination-phase rates are on the 2022 primary-report row.strongThis is the OS readout that turns LMS-04 from a PFS result into a survival benefit, and the main reason the regimen was chosen for her. Toxicities left empty after the full fallback chain failed: abstract has no per-term data, NEJM has no PMC deposit, CT.gov NCT02997358 hasResults=false, publisher page returns 403. Sun/Italiano (2024)Mol CancerPMID 38374062preclinicalexcludedPhase I/II clinical trial with paired on-treatment biopsies rather than a preclinical study. Logged because it is the human counterpart of the trabectedin macrophage literature: CD68+CD163+ macrophages fell in 9 of 28 biopsied sarcoma patients and the shift tracked with clinical benefit.Metronomic trabectedin + low-dose cyclophosphamide (TARMIC)—————n/a (preclinical)—Excluded: Phase I/II clinical trial with paired on-treatment biopsies rather than a preclinical study. Logged because it is the human counterpart of the trabectedin macrophage literature: CD68+CD163+ macrophages fell in 9 of 28 biopsied sarcoma patients and the shift tracked with clinical benefit. Lynch/Pollack (2024)BMC CancerPMID 39478506preclinicalincludedB7-H3 expression across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypesimmunohistochemistry on 153 soft-tissue sarcoma specimens spanning 15 subtypes, scored in tumour and in associated vasculatureB7-H3 (CD276) is a cell-surface immune-regulatory molecule with limited normal-tissue expression, which is what makes it usable as an ADC or CAR target rather than as a driver.n=153 specimens, 15 subtypesB7-H3 was expressed in 97% of specimens and at high level in 69.2%, with vascular positivity in 94.7%. Expression was independent of prior treatment, tumour size, grade and patient age, and uncorrelated with PD-L1 or PD-1.vs not applicable — expression survey; PD-L1 and PD-1 status compared where previously assessedtranslatability: highn/a (preclinical)partialPrevalence only — no functional or therapeutic readout, and per-subtype numbers for leiomyosarcoma are not broken out in the abstract. High prior probability of a positive stain is not the same as a dependency, and vascular positivity raises a separate on-target question. —/— (2024)—NCT06498648trial publicationincludedabemaciclib + gemcitabineadvanced leiomyosarcoma or dedifferentiated liposarcoma (phase 2 may be systemic-treatment naive) (1L)intact Rb protein by IHC required (phase 2); prior gemcitabine not allowedphase 1/2 of abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor) + gemcitabine——MTD/RP2D (phase 1); PFS (phase 2)——partialThe phase 2 LMS cohort accepts systemic-treatment-naive patients, and prior doxorubicin/trabectedin would not exclude her later since only prior gemcitabine is barred — so this stays open before and after LMS-04. Entry is gated on Rb-intact IHC, a single stain she has not had; the same stain read the other way gates the REC-617 trial, so one assay settles which of the two doors exists. ECOG ceiling 0-2, undocumented in her case. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2024)—NCT06571734trial publicationincludedzanzalintinibmetastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma after ≥2 prior lines (cohort 1) (3L+)none requiredphase 2 of zanzalintinib (multi-targeted TKI) with LMS-specific cohort——ORR/PFS (primary per cohort)——partialThe LMS cohort requires at least two prior lines, so this is a third-line-or-later option that becomes reachable only after LMS-04 and one further regimen. Pathology review at an NCCN center is required, which her pending expert re-review would satisfy. Kept as the successor-generation TKI alternative to label-approved pazopanib. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2024)—NCT05649956trial publicationincludedletrozolenewly diagnosed FIGO stage I uterine leiomyosarcoma, ER-positive (>10% IHC), adjuvant setting (adj)ER expression >10% by IHC requiredrandomized phase 2 of adjuvant letrozole vs observation (GOG Foundation)——disease-free survival (primary)——noneExcluded twice over: her tumor is ER <1% against a >10% requirement, and the trial takes stage I disease with no measurable lesions where she has bilateral pulmonary metastases. Recorded deliberately as the concrete face of the endocrine foreclosure her confirmed ER/PR negative creates — the one biomarker answer this case already has. If the pending specimen-provenance check overturned the receptor result, this class would need re-screening, though the stage criterion would still exclude her here. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted Meric-Bernstam F/Lee JY (2024)J Clin OncolPMID 37870536trial publicationincludedtrastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)HER2-expressing (IHC 3+/2+) advanced solid tumors after prior therapy (DESTINY-PanTumor02) (2L+)HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+ — never stained in this patient; tumor-agnostic approval is IHC 3+ onlymulticohort single-arm phase 2 basket267ORR 0.371ORR 37.1% overall; 61.3% in IHC 3+——weakHER2 has never been stained here and meaningful expression in uLMS is uncommon, so this is a low-prior gate that the already-planned IHC bundle closes for the cost of one slide; only an IHC 3+ result would make T-DXd label-available (after prior systemic therapy), and sarcoma was not among the trial's named cohorts. The drug's ILD risk deserves an early note: her bilateral infiltrative lung disease and 8,500 ft baseline oximetry would make pneumonitis surveillance genuinely hard to read.toxicity table not extracted D'Angelo SP/Van Tine BA (2024)LancetPMID 38554725trial publicationincludedafamitresgene autoleuceladvanced synovial sarcoma / myxoid round cell liposarcoma (SPEARHEAD-1) (2L+)HLA-A*02 allele + MAGE-A4 expression ≥1+ in ≥10% of cells (central IHC); both unassessable in this patient (HLA untyped, antigen unstained)single-arm phase 2 of afamitresgene autoleucel (MAGE-A4 TCR-T)52ORR 0.37ORR 37% (synovial sarcoma 39%)——weakIncluded for informational value only: the trial and the resulting approval are restricted to synovial sarcoma and MRCLS, so she cannot enroll or receive it on label, and no MAGE-A4 program currently enrolls LMS. It anchors what the engineered-T-cell class can do in sarcoma once the two gates she has never been tested for — HLA-A*02 genotype and MAGE-A4 IHC — are known; the trial also required prior anthracycline/ifosfamide, LVEF ≥50% and ECOG 0-1, all axes undocumented or pending in her case. HLA typing is a blood draw and settles half of this class in one step.toxicity table not extracted —/— (2024)—NCT06242470trial publicationincludedMGC026advanced solid tumors including sarcoma (named cohort) (2L+)B7-H3-directed; no expression gate at entry (97% of soft-tissue sarcomas B7-H3-positive, PMID 39478506)phase 1 dose escalation/expansion of MGC026 (B7-H3 ADC)——safety/RP2D——partialSarcoma is on the named tumor-type list and US sites are recruiting, making this the most accessible B7-H3 ADC route for her once standard options are exhausted after LMS-04. Entry is not gated on B7-H3 IHC, but the planned local stain still earns its place by telling the board whether a referral is worth the trip — a strong positive is the single most likely surface-target finding in this histology. Archival tissue is required and available from the 2024 resection. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2024)—NCT06551142trial publicationincludedGSK5764227 (HS-20093)advanced/metastatic solid tumors after progression on available standard therapy (EMBOLD) (2L+)B7-H3-directed; no expression gate at entryphase 1 dose escalation/expansion of GSK5764227 (HS-20093, B7-H3 ADC) alone and in combinations——safety/RP2D——partialAll-comers dose escalation with US sites for the B7-H3 ADC that already has sarcoma-specific activity signals from its Chinese sister studies; monotherapy escalation requires progression on or intolerance of all standard options, which places it after LMS-04 and probably one further line. ECOG 0-1 is required with no recent deterioration — her score is an undocumented intake assumption, and this trial's ceiling is stricter than most of the sarcoma rows. Measurable disease per RECIST is required against her infiltrative pulmonary pattern. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted Ingham/Schwartz (2023)J Clin OncolPMID 37467452clinicalincludedOlaparib + temozolomide (NCI Protocol 10250)advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after >=1 prior line (2L+)22 evaluable; median age 55; 59% had >=3 prior lines; no HRD entry gate — all comers with paired biopsies (WES/RNAseq + RAD51 foci assay)single-arm open-label multicentre phase 2, one-stage binomial design (>=5/22 responses = promising)22ORR: 27.00 % 6/22 overall; primary endpoint (best ORR within 6 months) 23% (5/22), meeting the prespecified barmPFS: 6.90 monthsmDoR: 12.00 monthsmPFS: 11.20 months (RAD51-assay HR-deficient (9/18)) vs 5.4 months in HR-proficient; exploratoryBiomarker: 31% (HRR-mutant (5/16 by WES)) RAD51B, PALB2, ATR carriers had PFS 31.5, 27.3, 7.1 months; the two ATRX-mutant patients 5.4 and 2.7 monthsORR (overall)—95% CI 5.4 to not estimable95% CI 9.5 to not estimablep=0.05—neutropenia G>=3 — n=22 · 75%thrombocytopenia G>=3 — 7/22 · 32%anemia G>=3 — 7/22 · 32%discontinuation for toxicity — 3/22 · 14%olaparib dose reduction — 8/22 · 36%partialThe strongest non-cytotoxic signal in uLMS and the branch her pending HRD/RAD51-relevant profiling gates. n=22 and single-arm: the 27% ORR and the 11.2 vs 5.4-month RAD51 split are hypothesis-grade until the randomized successor (NCT05432791) reads out. An erratum (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:5205) was issued. AE and subgroup detail from PMC full text (PMC10852403). Dall/Barker (2023)J Exp Clin Cancer ResPMID 37143137preclinicalincludedPARP inhibition in HR-deficient uterine leiomyosarcoma (PDX)patient-derived xenografts from HRD uterine leiomyosarcoma, including a paired PDX derived after PARP-inhibitor exposure; WGS/WES/panel screening of a 58-patient uLMS cohortHomozygous BRCA2 deletion and COSMIC signature 3 with high genome-wide LOH define an HR-deficient subset; PARP inhibition converts unrepaired single-strand damage into lethal double-strand breaks, and PARP1-selective trapping does so with less of the off-target PARP2 burden.58 patients screened; 5 (9%) HRD; PDX generated from HRD cases including one post-PARPi pairstrong — All 13 uLMS analysed by WGS carried a dominant signature 3, and 5 of 58 patients had HRD uLMS, in every confirmed case through homozygous BRCA2 deletion. PDX responses were fastest, deepest and most durable with the PARP1-selective AZD5305 rather than olaparib or olaparib plus cisplatin, holding even in a PDX derived after clinical PARPi exposure that had acquired PRKDC resistance mutations.vs olaparib alone and olaparib plus cisplatin compared against the PARP1-selective AZD5305translatability: highn/a (preclinical)strongSmall PDX numbers and a paper that interleaves patient outcomes with model pharmacology. The agent that worked best, AZD5305, is not the one this patient could reach; the accessible branch is olaparib plus temozolomide. Brignole/Ponzoni (2023)J Immunother CancerPMID 37775116preclinicalincludedVobramitamab duocarmazine (MGC018) with bystander killinghuman neuroblastoma cell lines, multicellular tumour spheroids, and orthotopic, pseudometastatic and resected mouse neuroblastoma models; co-culture of B7-H3-negative murine NX-S2 cells with B7-H3-positive human cellsA cleavable valine-citrulline linker releases membrane-permeable duocarmycin, so payload liberated inside an antigen-positive cell can cross into neighbouring antigen-negative cells — the bystander effect that makes heterogeneous or low antigen tractable.—strong — Cytotoxicity ran from IC50 5.1-53.9 ng/mL in monolayer and 17.8-364 ng/mL in spheroids. B7-H3-negative murine cells, untouched by the ADC alone, were killed when co-cultured with B7-H3-positive cells, and treatment delayed or arrested relapse across orthotopic and resected models without weight loss or haematologic toxicity.vs irrelevant (anti-CD20) duocarmycin ADC; topotecan-temozolomide as the standard-of-care comparatortranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyNeuroblastoma throughout, with no sarcoma model and no leiomyosarcoma. The bystander demonstration is the part that transfers, and it is the mechanistic argument for a B7-H3 ADC where expression is heterogeneous rather than uniform. Crane/Federman (2023)SarcomaPMID 37333052preclinicalincludedFAP expression in sarcoma: stroma and tumour cellsIHC on 63 bone and soft-tissue tumour samples with 30 adjacent normal tissues, scored separately for stromal and tumour-cell compartments; RNA-seq comparison across 10,626 samples and survival analysis in 168 sarcomasFAP is a marker of activated fibroblasts. In mesenchymal tumours the malignant cell is itself of fibroblastic lineage, so the antigen is not confined to the stromal compartment the way it is in carcinomas.n=63 tumours; n=30 adjacent normal; n=168 sarcomas for survivalIntensity ≥2 with density ≥25% appeared in stromal cells of 77.7% of tumours and in tumour cells of 50.7%. Sarcomas ranked among the highest FAP-expressing cancer types by RNA-seq, and FAP level carried no overall-survival association.vs adjacent normal tissue and positive controlstranslatability: highn/a (preclinical)partialMixed bone and soft-tissue histologies with no leiomyosarcoma breakout, and no functional or therapeutic arm. It does change the mechanistic argument: in sarcoma a FAP radioligand may deliver dose directly to tumour cells rather than relying solely on crossfire from stroma. Galis/Rajtik (2023)Cardiovasc ToxicolPMID 37119387preclinicalincludedHypoxic preconditioning and doxorubicin cardiomyopathyWistar rats given doxorubicin, with or without intermittent hypoxic preconditioning beforehand; no tumour presentPreconditioning raised SERCA2a expression, which the authors link to preserved calcium handling; HIF-1α levels did not change, and TRPV1/TRPV4 loss and suppressed CaMKII activation followed doxorubicin regardless.—weak — Preconditioned rats retained more cardiac output than rats given doxorubicin alone, with higher SERCA2a on western blot and no change in HIF-1α.vs doxorubicin without preconditioning; untreated ratstranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)weakCycled normobaric hypoxia in healthy rats is not continuous residence at 8,500 ft, no tumour was present, and the mechanism is inferred from protein levels rather than measured function. Logged to record that the altitude question has no translatable preclinical answer — direction of effect is unresolved and should not be used either to reassure or to alarm. —/— (2023)—NCT06088290trial publicationincludedlurbinectedin + doxorubicinmetastatic leiomyosarcoma, first line (SaLuDo) (1L)none required; anthracycline-naive with ECOG ≤1 and LVEF >50% requiredrandomized phase 3: lurbinectedin + doxorubicin vs doxorubicin alone——PFS (primary)——partialShe matches this trial's eligibility profile almost exactly — anthracycline-naive metastatic LMS, ECOG ≤1, documented LVEF — but accrual closed before her diagnosis was corrected, so the row is informational. It is the clearest illustration of how narrow the first-line trial window is in LMS, and its readout will bear directly on how the LMS-04 backbone evolves. Her ECOG and LVEF, both required here, remain undocumented. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2023)—NCT05432791trial publicationincludedolaparib + temozolomideadvanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after ≥2 prior lines including an anthracycline (3L+)no HRD gate; prior PARP inhibitor, temozolomide or dacarbazine excludedrandomized phase 2/3: olaparib + temozolomide vs investigator's choice (trabectedin or pazopanib)——PFS (primary)——partialThe confirmatory successor to NCI 10250 and the natural destination if LMS-04 and one further line fail: she would arrive anthracycline-exposed as required, and having received trabectedin but not pazopanib still permits the investigator's-choice arm. Currently closed to new accrual, so the practical move is to watch for reopening or readout rather than plan enrollment. Requires measurable disease, which the infiltrative pulmonary pattern may complicate. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2023)—NCT05830123trial publicationincludedHS-20093relapsed/refractory osteosarcoma and other sarcomas after first-line systemic treatment (ARTEMIS-002) (2L+)B7-H3-directed; no expression gate; prior B7-H3 therapy excludedphase 2 of HS-20093 (B7-H3 ADC) in sarcoma——ORR (primary)——weakThe sarcoma-dedicated trial of the same ADC as the EMBOLD row, and 'other sarcomas' after first-line failure would read on her post-LMS-04 — but every site is in China, which makes it geographically impractical for a US-band patient and the fit weak. Kept because its sarcoma cohorts are what give the EMBOLD/GSK program its disease-specific rationale. ECOG 0-1 required, undocumented in her case. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2023)—NCT05551117trial publicationincludedvobramitamab duocarmazinemetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and other solid tumors (TAMARACK program context) (2L+)B7-H3-directedphase 2 of vobramitamab duocarmazine (B7-H3 ADC, duocarmycin payload); terminated——ORR/rPFS (primary)——weakLegacy context, not an option: MacroGenics halted this B7-H3 ADC program after safety findings in the prostate-cancer studies, and the row is here so the board reads the class with its failures in view — payload choice, not the target, is where B7-H3 ADCs have differed. The same sponsor's successor ADC (MGC026, different payload) is the recruiting row above. Different tumor type; she was never a candidate. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted —/— (2023)—NCT06074692trial publicationincludedPARP inhibitor + SBRT + immune checkpoint blockademetastatic or advanced high-grade bone/soft-tissue sarcoma after ≥1 systemic regimen (PRIMA) (2L+)no PARP-inhibitor pretreatment; SBRT-amenable lesions requiredphase 2 of PARP inhibition + stereotactic body radiotherapy + PD-1 blockade——ORR/PFS (primary)——weakThe only registered trial marrying two of this case's axes — PARP sensitization and SBRT to metastatic sarcoma lesions — so it stays as proof the combined systemic-plus-local strategy her oncologist sketched is being formally tested. All sites are in China (age 10-70, ECOG 0-2), which makes it informational rather than actionable for her. Her pulmonary lesions' infiltrative pattern would need to be SBRT-amenable, a question the pre-treatment imaging work-up will answer. · Trial registration only — no peer-reviewed publication yetregistration only — no peer-reviewed publication yet; toxicity table not extracted; primary endpoint not extracted Pautier/Duffaud (2022)Lancet OncolPMID 35835135clinicalincludedDoxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)metastatic or unresectable uterine or soft-tissue leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive (1L)ECOG 0-1 required; 67 of 150 patients (45%) had uterine LMS; randomization stratified by uterine vs soft-tissue origin; surgery for residual disease allowed after 6 cycles in both armsrandomized open-label phase 3 (French Sarcoma Group, 20 centres), BICR-assessed primary endpoint150mPFS: 12.20 months combination arm, BICRmPFS: 6.20 months doxorubicin arm, BICRPFS HR: 0.41 adjusted HRmedian PFS (BICR)95% CI 10.10–15.6095% CI 4.10–7.1095% CI 0.29–0.58 · p=<0.0001neutropenia G>=3 — 59/74 · 80%thrombocytopenia G>=3 — 35/74 · 47%anemia G>=3 — 23/74 · 31%febrile neutropenia G>=3 — 21/74 · 28%serious adverse event — 15/74 · 20%treatment-related death (cardiac failure) G5 — 0/74 · 0%strongPrimary report of the regimen she is about to start; pivotal for the LMS-04 strategy. The PMID a search commonly surfaces, 36174625, is a letter about this trial, not the trial. Per-term G3-4 rates above are from the combination phase; maintenance-phase safety detail sits behind the paywall (no PMC; CT.gov NCT02997358 has no posted results). Schöffski/Patel (2016)LancetPMID 26874885clinicalincludedEribulin vs dacarbazine (Study 309)advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after >=2 prior regimens including an anthracycline (2L+)intermediate/high-grade L-sarcomas; OS benefit was driven by the liposarcoma stratum (see LMS-subgroup row and excluded liposarcoma-subgroup row)randomized open-label phase 3, OS primary endpoint452mOS: 13.50 months eribulin; vs 11.5 (9.6-13.0) dacarbazineOS HR: 0.77AE rate: 67.00 % grade >=3 AEs, eribulin arm (152/226); vs 56% (126/224) dacarbazinemedian OS95% CI 10.90–15.6095% CI 0.62–0.95 · p=0.0169—any adverse event G>=3 — 152/226 · 67%death on treatment G5 — 10/226 · 4%partialWhole-trial OS win that FDA translated into a liposarcoma-only label because the benefit concentrated there; for her LMS the drug is off-label with a neutral subgroup (next row). Per-term G3 rates not in abstract; Lancet full text paywalled, no PMC. Mäkinen/Vahteristo (2016)PLoS GenetPMID 26891131preclinicalincludedATRX loss and ALT in uterine leiomyosarcoma (target biology)whole-exome sequencing of 19 uterine leiomyosarcomas; ATRX IHC in 44 uLMS; telomere-specific FISH for the ALT phenotypeATRX loads H3.3 at telomeric chromatin; losing it destabilises telomere maintenance and permits recombination-based lengthening, which is the ALT phenotype that ATR inhibition was proposed to exploit.n=19 exomes; n=44 tumours for IHCTP53 was mutated in 6/19, ATRX in 5/19 (every alteration nonsense or frameshift) and MED12 in 4/19. ATRX expression was clearly reduced in 23 of 44 tumours by IHC, and every ATRX-low tumour tested ALT-positive by telomere FISH.vs not applicable — descriptive human tumour seriestranslatability: highn/a (preclinical)strongDescriptive human series with no therapeutic arm; the ATR-inhibitor suggestion in its discussion is an extrapolation from Flynn 2015, not a result. The tight ATRX-IHC-to-ALT concordance is what makes one stain a usable surrogate here. Deeg/Rippe (2016)Front OncolPMID 27602331preclinicalincludedATR inhibition in ALT cells — failed replicationpanel of ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cell lines plus isogenic pairs in which ALT was active or suppressed; ATR inhibitor VE-821Same premise as Flynn 2015, tested with isogenic controls that hold genetic background constant while switching ALT on or off.—negative — No general ATR-inhibitor sensitivity followed from ALT status. Sensitivity differences tracked with line-to-line background rather than with the telomere maintenance mechanism.vs isogenic ALT-suppressed counterparts — the control Flynn 2015 lackedtranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlySmall line panel and a single ATR inhibitor, so it does not exclude a narrower ALT-related vulnerability. It does undercut any claim that ATRX loss alone predicts ATR-inhibitor benefit. Navarria/Scorsetti (2015)Eur J CancerPMID 25686482clinicalincludedSBRT for lung metastases from soft-tissue sarcoma (Humanitas)lung metastases from soft-tissue sarcoma, unsuitable for resection, <=4 lesions, controlled primary (any)28 patients / 51 lesions; ECOG 1-2; LMS the commonest histology (36%); median interval from diagnosis to lung metastases 51 monthsretrospective single-institution cohort28Other: 96.00 % actuarial 5-year local control from SBRTOS rate: 96.20 % 2-yearOS rate: 60.50 % 5-year; all deaths were from distant progressionactuarial 5-year local control———any adverse event G>=3 — 0/28 · 0%partialSmall, highly selected (<=4 lesions, controlled primary, long median disease interval), which explains the striking survival figures; that selection is the caveat to carry, not the local-control number. Supports SBRT as the non-surgical local option if induction converts her disease to oligometastatic anatomy. Flynn/Zou (2015)SciencePMID 25593184preclinicalincludedATR inhibition in ALT-positive cells (original claim)ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cancer cell lines, including ATRX-manipulated pairs; ATR inhibitors in vitroATRX loss uncouples cell-cycle control of the telomeric transcript TERRA, leaving RPA bound to telomeres after replication. That nucleoprotein structure is recombinogenic and depends on ATR, which RPA itself recruits.—strong — ATR inhibition disrupted the ALT process and caused chromosome fragmentation and apoptosis, with killing reported as selective for ALT-dependent cancer cells.vs telomerase-positive (non-ALT) cell linestranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyCell lines only, no in-vivo arm, and the central selectivity claim was not reproduced by Deeg 2016 or by the osteosarcoma panel in Goncalves 2020. Treat as the hypothesis that opened the field rather than as a settled vulnerability. Smith/Houghton (2015)Clin Cancer ResPMID 25500058preclinicalincludedPARP inhibitor + temozolomide in sarcoma xenograftsPediatric Preclinical Testing Program in-vitro panel and xenografts, including 10 Ewing sarcoma models; talazoparib with temozolomide or topotecanTrapping-competent PARP inhibition converts temozolomide base damage into replication-blocking lesions; pharmacodynamic loss of PARP appeared only in models that responded.10 Ewing sarcoma xenograft models among a broader panelmoderate — Talazoparib potentiated temozolomide up to 85-fold in vitro, with the largest shifts in Ewing sarcoma and leukaemia lines. In vivo the combination was significantly synergistic in 5 of 10 Ewing xenografts and only modestly active in most other models, and both schedules represented the maximum tolerated combination.vs talazoparib alone, temozolomide alone, vehicletranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyEwing sarcoma, where PARPi sensitivity is driven by EWS-FLI1 rather than HR deficiency, so the mechanism is not the one proposed for uLMS. Talazoparib traps far more strongly than olaparib, making the potentiation an upper bound, and the myelosuppression that dominates the clinical regimen is exactly what the tolerability ceiling here predicts. Doebele/Low (2015)Cancer DiscovPMID 26216294preclinicalincludedLOXO-101 (larotrectinib) against an LMNA-NTRK1 fusionTRK-fusion-bearing human cancer cell lines in vitro and in vivo, alongside a soft-tissue sarcoma patient with lung metastases carrying an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion confirmed by in-situ proximity ligationSelective ATP-competitive inhibition of TRKA/B/C. A fusion partner drives constitutive kinase activation, making the whole tumour dependent on that one signal, which is why response is fast when the fusion is genuinely the driver.n=1 patient; cell-line panel size not statedstrong — Fusion-bearing cell lines showed inhibition of the fusion oncoprotein with reduced proliferation in vitro and tumour growth in vivo. The sarcoma patient had rapid, substantial tumour regression with improvement in dyspnea and oxygen saturation.vs non-fusion cell lines for selectivitytranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)weakPreclinical content is thin next to the clinical case, and NTRK fusions are rare in leiomyosarcoma. Carried because the fusion has never been tested here and spindle-cell morphology with an earlier benign sign-out is the setting where an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal tumour is missed. Judson/van der Graaf (2014)Lancet OncolPMID 24618336clinicalincludedDoxorubicin + ifosfamide (intensified) vs doxorubicin alone (EORTC 62012)advanced or metastatic high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma, first line (1L)age 18-60, WHO PS 0-1; all histologies of high-grade STS, not LMS-specificrandomized controlled phase 3 (EORTC 62012), OS primary endpoint455mOS: 14.30 months combination arm; 95.5% CImOS: 12.80 months doxorubicin arm; 95.5% CIOS HR: 0.83 not significant; 95.5% CImPFS: 7.40 months combination armPFS HR: 0.74ORR: 26.00 % combination arm; vs 14% (31/228) doxorubicinmedian OS95% CI 12.50–16.5095% CI 10.50–14.3095% CI 0.67–1.03 · p=0.07695% CI 6.60–8.3095% CI 0.60–0.90 · p=0.003p=<0.0006febrile neutropenia G>=3 — 103/224 · 46%leukopenia G>=3 — 97/224 · 43%neutropenia G>=3 — 93/224 · 42%anemia G>=3 — 78/224 · 35%thrombocytopenia G>=3 — 75/224 · 33%partialThe trial behind the rule that combination cytotoxics buy response and PFS but not OS in aggregate STS; the age band (18-60) matches her. Pooled STS, not uLMS-specific, so it is weaker evidence for her than LMS-04, which reversed the OS conclusion in histology-selected LMS. George/Krasner (2014)CancerPMID 24222211clinicalincludedLetrozole in ER/PR-expressing uLMSunresectable uterine leiomyosarcoma with ER and/or PR expression by IHC (any)27 patients, median 2 prior regimens (range 0-9); entry required ER and/or PR positivity — a population her ER/PR <1% tumor cannot joinsingle-arm phase 2, primary endpoint 12-week PFS27PFS rate: 50.00 % 12-week landmarkDCR: 54.00 % best response was stable disease in 14/26; no objective responses reported in abstractOther: 3 patients >24 wk on therapy (ER and PR expression >90% of cells) all prolonged-benefit patients had strong, diffuse ER/PR expressionPFS rate at 12 weeks95% CI 30.00–67.00 · 90% CI95% CI 36.00–71.00 · 90% CI—Reported as well tolerated; the dominant discontinuation reason was progression (85%). Per-term toxicity table sits behind the Wiley paywall.noneIncluded as the evidence that makes her ER <1%/PR <1% a genuine foreclosure: the only durable letrozole benefit occurred in tumors expressing ER and PR in >90% of cells, the opposite end of the expression spectrum from hers. Toxicities empty after the fallback chain failed: abstract has no per-term data, no PMC deposit, Europe PMC subscription-only, Wiley page returns 402, and no trial registration is given in the abstract to reach a CT.gov AE tab. George/Muto (2014)CancerPMID 24923260clinicalincludedIntraperitoneal morcellation and outcomes of localized uLMS (DFCI/BWH)uterus-limited uLMS discovered at surgery for presumed leiomyoma (any)58 women, 2007-2012: 19 morcellated vs 39 total abdominal hysterectomy at first surgeryretrospective two-institution cohort, multivariate-adjusted58mRFS: 10.80 months morcellated; vs 39.6 months intact hysterectomyRFS HR: 3.18 multivariate-adjusted risk of recurrence with morcellationOther: abdominal/pelvic recurrence excess morcellation specifically increased abdominopelvic recurrencesrecurrence-free survival, morcellated vs intactp=0.00295% CI 1.50–6.80 · p=0.003p=0.001Surgical-outcomes cohort; no systemic-therapy safety data.partialDirectly on the target_validator's open question: if her September 2024 hysterectomy for presumed benign leiomyoma used morcellation, recurrence risk roughly triples and shifts toward peritoneal dissemination — which changes staging imaging (abdomen/pelvis surveillance), not just history-taking. The operative report is the cheap decisive document. Murai/Pommier (2014)J Pharmacol Exp TherPMID 24650937preclinicalincludedPARP trapping as the reason olaparib pairs with temozolomidegenetically modified chicken DT40 lymphoma lines with human DU145 prostate and SF295 glioblastoma cells; olaparib and veliparib against temozolomide, camptothecin, cisplatin and etoposidePARP inhibitors kill in two separable ways: catalytic blockade, and trapping of PARP-DNA complexes at damage sites. Which one matters depends on the partner drug — temozolomide-induced N-methylpurine lesions recruit PARP1 to base-excision intermediates, where a trapped complex becomes the lethal lesion.—moderate — Temozolomide combinations needed trapping as well as catalytic inhibition, and olaparib, the stronger trapper, outperformed veliparib. Camptothecin combinations ran on catalytic inhibition alone, and cisplatin or etoposide gained little or nothing from either drug.vs veliparib, a potent catalytic inhibitor that traps poorly, as the mechanistic contrast to olaparibtranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyAvian and epithelial cell lines, no sarcoma and no in-vivo arm. Its value here is explaining why the uLMS trial regimen pairs olaparib with temozolomide specifically rather than with a platinum. Germano/Allavena (2013)Cancer CellPMID 23410977preclinicalincludedTrabectedin — mononuclear-phagocyte depletionfour syngeneic mouse tumour models plus human blood monocytes; myeloid-cell transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumoursCaspase-8 apoptosis triggered through TRAIL receptors. Monocytes carry signalling TRAIL receptors where neutrophils and lymphocytes carry decoys, which confines the killing to the mononuclear phagocyte compartment.—strong — Trabectedin killed monocytes and macrophages in blood, spleen and tumour while leaving other leukocytes intact, and tumour angiogenesis fell alongside them. Transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumours placed the myeloid kill inside the antitumour effect rather than beside it. Monocyte counts, including tumour-associated macrophages, dropped in treated patients as well.vs vehicle-treated tumour-bearing mice; trabectedin-resistant tumour variants used to separate tumour-cell from myeloid effectstranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)partialNone of the four models is leiomyosarcoma, and the human confirmation is peripheral monocyte counts rather than sarcoma biopsies. Whether any of this reaches an infiltrative pulmonary metastasis is untested. Tran/Rosenberg (2013)J Exp MedPMID 23712432preclinicalincludedOn-target toxicity of FAP-directed therapyFAP-reactive CAR T cells transferred into mice bearing a variety of subcutaneous tumours, across two mouse strains; FAP staining of 18 human tumours and of mouse and clinical-grade human multipotent bone marrow stromal cellsFAP is not tumour-restricted. It is expressed on PDGFR-α+ Sca-1+ multipotent bone marrow stromal cells in mice and on clinical-grade human BMSCs, so any FAP-directed effector reaches the marrow niche.18 human tumours stained; two mouse strains testednegative — FAP-reactive CAR T cells were only weakly active against tumours yet caused significant cachexia and lethal bone toxicity in two mouse strains. Both mouse and human multipotent BMSCs were recognised by the same T cells.vs untreated and control-CAR tumour-bearing micetranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyA CAR T-cell platform rather than a radioligand, and the dose delivered to marrow stroma by a peptide with renal clearance is not the same exposure. It remains the sharpest evidence that FAP positivity on a PET scan does not make FAP a tumour-exclusive target. Eisinger-Mathason/Simon (2013)Cancer DiscovPMID 23906982preclinicalincludedIntratumoural hypoxia, HIF-1α/PLOD2 and sarcoma lung metastasisautochthonous LSL-KrasG12D/+; Trp53fl/fl murine undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and allografts, with HIF-1α or PLOD2 deletion and PLOD2 rescue; human sarcoma expression analysisHypoxia drives HIF-1α to induce PLOD2, which modifies and organises collagen in the primary tumour. That altered matrix supports migration and dissemination without affecting primary tumour growth.—strong — Losing HIF-1α or PLOD2 disrupted collagen modification, cell migration and pulmonary metastasis while leaving primary growth intact, and re-expressing PLOD2 restored metastatic potential in HIF-1α-deficient tumours. Human metastatic primary lesions carried elevated HIF1A and PLOD2, and pharmacologic PLOD inhibition suppressed metastases.vs HIF-1α-proficient and PLOD2-proficient tumours; ectopic PLOD2 re-expression in HIF-1α-deficient tumourstranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)weakThis is intratumoural hypoxia in a UPS model and speaks to lung tropism in sarcoma generally. It says nothing about ambient hypoxia at 2,600 m: no sarcoma model has been run under chronic hypobaric conditions, and the two forms of hypoxia are not interchangeable. van der Graaf/Hohenberger (2012)LancetPMID 22595799clinicalincludedPazopanib (PALETTE)metastatic non-adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma after standard chemotherapy (2L+)angiogenesis-inhibitor-naive, prior anthracycline required; LMS was the largest histology; uterine sarcoma subset analyzed separately (Benson 2016 row)randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, 2:1369mPFS: 4.60 months pazopanib; vs 1.6 (0.9-1.8) placeboPFS HR: 0.31mOS: 12.50 months pazopanib; vs 10.7 (8.7-12.8) placeboOS HR: 0.86 not significantmedian PFS95% CI 3.70–4.8095% CI 0.24–0.40 · p=<0.000195% CI 10.60–14.8095% CI 0.67–1.11 · p=0.25fatigue — 155/239 · 65%diarrhea — 138/239 · 58%nausea — 129/239 · 54%weight loss — 115/239 · 48%hypertension — 99/239 · 41%partialHer label-approved later-line backbone once anthracycline exposure is behind her; PALETTE required prior chemotherapy, so it does not compete with LMS-04 now. Per-term G3-4 rates not in the abstract; Lancet full text paywalled and no PMC deposit — any-grade rates above are as published in the abstract. McClendon/Knudsen (2012)Cell CyclePMID 22751436preclinicalincludedCDK4/6 inhibition antagonising concurrent cytotoxic therapyRB-proficient and RB-deficient triple-negative breast cancer cell lines treated with palbociclib plus doxorubicinGenotoxic cytotoxicity needs cells to cycle. An RB-mediated G1 arrest pulls them out of the phase where the damage is lethal, so the arrest shields the cell rather than adding to the kill.—negative — In RB-proficient models the pairing was cytostatically cooperative but protected cells from doxorubicin-mediated killing, and viable populations recurred after treatment. In RB-deficient cells palbociclib changed nothing about the doxorubicin response, confirming the protection runs through RB.vs doxorubicin alone; RB-deficient lines as the internal control for RB dependencetranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyBreast models and doxorubicin rather than gemcitabine, but gemcitabine is likewise S-phase-dependent. This is the mechanistic caution to raise against a concurrent abemaciclib-plus-gemcitabine schedule in an Rb-intact tumour. Burt/Jaklitsch (2011)Ann Thorac SurgPMID 21867989clinicalincludedRepeated pulmonary metastasectomy for leiomyosarcoma (Brigham series)pulmonary metastases from sarcoma; LMS subset analyzed (31/82) (any)single-institution 1989-2004; LMS patients were mostly women (77%), had fewer lesions (mean 1.9) and 48% underwent repeat metastasectomyretrospective single-institution cohort82mOS: 70.00 months (LMS (n=31)) vs 24 months non-LMS sarcomaOther: DFI independently prognostic disease-free interval from primary resection to lung metastasis, and from metastasectomy to second recurrence, were the independent survival predictors in multivariate analysismedian OS, LMS vs non-LMS metastasectomyp=0.049—Surgical complications not reported in the abstract.partialWhy the consulting oncologist keeps surgery on the table: resected LMS lung metastases can run an indolent course, and repeat resection is compatible with long survival. n=31 LMS at one hospital, all selected for operability — her bilateral infiltrative pattern is exactly what these series screen out, so this is a best-case ceiling, not an expectation. Park/Nam (2011)Gynecol OncolPMID 21565389clinicalincludedTumor morcellation and prognosis in apparently early uLMS (Asan)stage I-II uterine leiomyosarcoma, morcellated vs intact at surgery (any)56 consecutive patients 1989-2010: 25 with, 31 without tumor morcellation; groups balanced except smaller tumors in the morcellated groupretrospective single-institution comparative cohort56Other: 3.11 OR (OS) multivariate association of morcellation with poorer overall survivalOther: 2.59 OR (DFS) univariate; morcellation the only significant DFS factorOther: 44.00 % abdominopelvic dissemination (peritoneal sarcomatosis or vaginal-apex recurrence) with morcellation vs 12.9% withoutOS, morcellated vs intact (multivariate)95% CI 1.07–9.06 · p=0.03895% CI 1.03–6.50 · p=0.043p=0.032Surgical-outcomes cohort; no systemic-therapy safety data.partialIndependent replication of the morcellation signal in a Korean series: tripled dissemination rate and worse OS. Small ns and retrospective design in both morcellation rows; the direction is consistent, the effect sizes are imprecise. Dean/Knudsen (2010)OncogenePMID 20473330preclinicalincludedRB loss as the determinant of CDK4/6-inhibitor failurepanel of breast cancer cell lines plus RB knockdown in immortalised mammary epithelium and multiple breast cancer subtypes; PD-0332991 (palbociclib)CDK4/6 inhibition works by keeping RB active as a transcriptional repressor of E2F targets and by holding down CDK2 activity. Chronic RB loss moves cells into a CDK4/6-independent state; acquired resistance follows the same logic through loss of CDK2 restraint.—strong — Chronic RB loss produced CDK4/6 independence and resistance to palbociclib, and direct RB knockdown reproduced it. Acquired resistance in initially sensitive models mapped to attenuated CDK2 inhibitors, so redundancy within the cell-cycle machinery is a second route to failure.vs RB-proficient parental lines and non-targeting shRNA controlstranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyBreast models throughout. Carried here because it supplies the mechanistic reason an Rb-intact requirement is a real eligibility gate rather than an enrichment preference. Hensley/Rose (2008)Gynecol OncolPMID 18534250clinicalincludedGemcitabine + docetaxel, first-line metastatic uLMS (GOG 087L)metastatic uterine leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive (1L)uLMS only; first-line; multicentre cooperative-group settingsingle-arm phase 2 (Gynecologic Oncology Group)42ORR: 35.80 % CR 4.8%, PR 31%; SD in a further 26.2%mPFS: 4.40 monthsmOS: 16+ monthsmDoR: 6.00 monthsORR95% CI 23.50–49.60 · 90% CIrange 0.4-37.2+ monthsrange 0.4-41.3 monthsrange 2.1-33.4+ monthsneutropenia G3 — n=42 · 5%neutropenia G4 — n=42 · 12%anemia G3 — n=42 · 24%thrombocytopenia G3 — n=42 · 9.5%fatigue G3 — n=42 · 17%pulmonary toxicity G4 — 1/42 · 2.4%strongThe uLMS-specific first-line estimate for the fallback regimen: ORR 35.8%, mPFS 4.4 months — respectable but well short of LMS-04's 12.2-month PFS. Single-arm, n=42; no comparator. Aune/Pommier (2008)Clin Cancer ResPMID 18927284preclinicalincludedTrabectedin — TC-NER- and VHL-dependent RNA Pol II degradationisogenic repair-mutant human fibroblasts (CSB, XPA, XPC, XPD, XPF, XPG) and VHL-deficient cells, with complemented counterparts; several cancer cell linesTrabectedin adducts recruit transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair, and the stalled complex is resolved by proteasomal degradation of elongating RNA Pol II, which needs both TC-NER and an intact VHL complex.—strong — Transcribing RNA Pol II was degraded rapidly after trabectedin exposure, and cells defective in TC-NER or VHL failed to degrade it. VHL-deficient cells also resisted trabectedin killing, while XPC cells, defective only in global-genome repair, behaved like wild type.vs repair-proficient parental lines and genetically complemented mutants; proteasome inhibition with MG132translatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyRepair-mutant fibroblasts and epithelial lines, no sarcoma model. This is the reason trabectedin sensitivity tracks repair proficiency rather than proliferation rate, which is what separates it from a conventional cytotoxic. Allavena/D'Incalci (2005)Cancer ResPMID 15805300preclinicalincludedTrabectedin — macrophage differentiation and CCL2/IL-6 outputhuman blood monocytes, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages, and tumour-associated macrophages freshly isolated from ovarian cancer; monocyte counts in treated patientsDNA minor-groove binding with selective interference in inducible transcription; monocytes die at low nanomolar exposure, and below that concentration the drug shuts down CCL2 and IL-6 transcription.—moderate — Monocytes underwent apoptosis at 5 nmol/L while lymphocytes tolerated roughly five-fold more drug. Sub-cytotoxic exposure blocked monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation and cut CCL2 and IL-6 output from monocytes, macrophages, ovarian TAMs and tumour cells alike.vs untreated monocytes/macrophages; lymphocytes as the comparator leukocyte populationtranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyHuman cells in vitro plus ovarian TAMs; no sarcoma tissue anywhere in the paper. CCL2 suppression is the proposed link to reduced monocyte recruitment, inferred rather than measured in tumour. Meco/Riccardi (2003)Cancer Chemother PharmacolPMID 12783202preclinicalincludedET-743 (trabectedin) + doxorubicin — preclinical basis for the combinationTE-671 rhabdomyosarcoma clonogenic assay and nude-mouse xenograft; C3H mice bearing UV2237M fibrosarcoma and its P-gp-overexpressing doxorubicin-resistant sublineTwo non-overlapping DNA-damage mechanisms — minor-groove alkylation whose cytotoxicity runs through transcription-coupled repair, versus topoisomerase II poisoning — combined without any pharmacokinetic interaction to account for the gain.—moderate — Isobologram analysis gave combination indices just under 1, so the in-vitro interaction is additive at best. In vivo the pair produced log cell kill of 0.85-1.12 in TE-671 where either agent alone reached only 0.13-0.33, and the combination worked in a P-gp-positive subline resistant to both single drugs. Giving ET-743 one hour ahead edged out simultaneous or reversed dosing (LCK 1.12 vs 0.85 and 0.92), and doxorubicin levels in tumour, liver, heart and kidney were unchanged by co-administration.vs each drug alone and untreated controls; pharmacokinetic sampling in both single-agent and combination armstranslatability: medn/a (preclinical)partialRhabdomyosarcoma and fibrosarcoma models from 2003; no leiomyosarcoma and no uterine model. The sequencing advantage rests on one small in-vivo comparison, and nothing in this or any other preclinical study addresses the trabectedin maintenance phase, which is an empirical clinical design. Kusmartsev/Gabrilovich (2003)Cancer ResPMID 12907617preclinicalincludedATRA differentiating immature myeloid suppressor cellsmultiple tumour-bearing mouse models with adoptive transfer of immature myeloid cells; ATRA combined with two cancer vaccinesATRA drives immature myeloid cells to differentiate into dendritic cells, macrophages and granulocytes, which removes the suppressive population rather than killing tumour cells directly.—moderate — ATRA sharply reduced immature myeloid cells across every model tested, and adoptive transfer confirmed the cells had differentiated rather than died. CD4 and CD8 tumour-specific responses improved and vaccine effects lasted longer, with no direct antitumour activity of ATRA itself.vs vaccine alone and untreated tumour-bearing micetranslatability: lown/a (preclinical)cross tumor onlyVaccine-era mouse models with no sarcoma and no checkpoint blockade; the trial pairs ATRA with cemiplimab, a combination this work predates. Doi not indexed in PubMed for this record, so the identifier is left null rather than guessed. Hensley/Spriggs (2002)J Clin OncolPMID 12065559clinicalincludedGemcitabine + docetaxel in leiomyosarcoma (MSKCC phase 2)unresectable leiomyosarcoma (29/34 uterine), 0-2 prior regimens (any)mixed-line: 18 chemo-naive, 16 doxorubicin-pretreated; 85% uterine primariessingle-arm phase 2 with pharmacokinetic substudy34ORR: 53.00 % 3 CR + 15 PR of 34; 50% of doxorubicin-pretreated patients respondedmTTP: 5.60 monthsORR95% CI 35.00–70.00range 4-10 monthsneutropenia G3 — n=34 · 15%neutropenia G4 — n=34 · 6%thrombocytopenia G3 — n=34 · 26%thrombocytopenia G4 — n=34 · 3%febrile neutropenia G>=3 — n=34 · 6%partialThe 53% ORR that made gem-doce a uLMS standard is from 34 patients at one centre with mixed lines of therapy; the GOG first-line trial (PMID 18534250) halved that estimate. Read the two together before quoting a response rate. Van Glabbeke/Tursz (1999)J Clin OncolPMID 10458228clinicalincludedPrognostic factors for first-line anthracycline chemotherapy in advanced STS (EORTC pooled)advanced soft-tissue sarcoma treated with anthracycline-containing first-line regimens (1L)2,185 patients pooled from seven EORTC trials; LMS included among histologiespooled prognostic-factor analysis of prospective trial data (Cox and logistic models)2185Other: favorable OS factors good PS (p<0.0001), no liver metastases (p=0.0001), low grade (p=0.0002), long interval since initial diagnosis (p=0.0004), young age (p=0.0045) — all independent in the Cox modelOther: LMS: lower response rate leiomyosarcoma histology predicted lower chemotherapy response without a matching survival penaltyindependent prognostic factors for OS——Prognostic analysis; no treatment-safety data.partialThe trial-grade basis for reading her ~23-month interval as favorable: a long time lapse between initial diagnosis and advanced-disease treatment independently predicted longer survival in 2,185 first-line anthracycline patients. Her interval is measured from an unrecognised resected primary, an unusual variant of that variable, and her young age and (assumed) ECOG 1 sit on the favorable side of the same model. Pastorino/Putnam (1997)J Thorac Cardiovasc SurgPMID 9011700clinicalincludedPulmonary metastasectomy (International Registry of Lung Metastases)resectable lung metastases from solid tumors; sarcoma was 42% of the registry (2,173/5,206) (any)5,206 metastasectomies from 18 thoracic-surgery units; 88% complete resections; surgical candidates only — a fitness- and biology-selected populationinternational multi-institutional registry, retrospective prognostic analysis5206OS rate: 36.00 % 5-year, complete resection; 26% at 10 y, 22% at 15 yOS rate: 13.00 % 5-year, incomplete resectionOS rate: 45.00 % (disease-free interval >=36 months) vs 33% for DFI 0-11 months; DFI independently prognostic in Cox modelOS rate: 43.00 % (single metastasis) vs 27% for >=4 lesions5-year OS after complete metastasectomy————Perioperative morbidity and mortality not reported in the abstract; pre-CTCAE-era surgical registry.partialThe reference dataset behind offering lung surgery at all, and the source of the prognostic strata (completeness, DFI, lesion number) her team would apply. Entirely retrospective and surgeon-selected: the 5-year figures describe patients healthy and oligometastatic enough to be operated on, not bilateral infiltrative disease like hers unless induction converts it.
