docs.title: Biomarker plan
docs.text: Recommended assay Rationale Suggested assay provider Tissue requirements INI1/SMARCB1 IHC (BAF47/SNF5 antibody, clone 25 or MRQ-27) on tumor tissue, scored against the internal positive control Complete loss of nuclear INI1 in tumor cells, with staining retained in the lymphocytes, endothelium and stroma that serve as the internal control, is what turns the plasma SMARCB1 frameshift into a target; the tazemetostat basket study required loss by IHC, or biallelic molecular loss where IHC was equivocal (NCT02601950). Retained nuclear INI1 closes the EZH2 branch outright. Set expectations either way: in that study's INI1-negative cohort outside epithelioid sarcoma the response rate was 9 percent (PMID 41882006), and 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumors in a consecutive series all retained SMARCB1 (PMID 34271067). NeoGenomics Laboratories (INI1 (BAF47) IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides, ordered on both the 2026 pulmonary core and the 2024 uterine block Tissue NGS covering SMARCB1 with copy-number and deletion calling, ordered at the same time as the INI1 stain rather than after it Tissue sequencing answers the question the stain cannot: whether G344Afs*13 is present in tumor DNA at all, and whether the second allele is lost. The INI1-negative entry criterion accepts molecular confirmation of biallelic loss when IHC is equivocal or unavailable (NCT02601950), so the two assays are complementary rather than sequential. Ordering the stain first and the panel only if it is positive costs two to three weeks and can strand the case in an equivocal stain with no molecular backup, which is the specific delay this patient cannot absorb with induction pending. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE; 10-15 unstained slides or the block, from the specimen with the higher tumor content Mismatch-repair protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) on tumor tissue, with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation and BRAF V600E if MLH1 is lost, plus the MSI call from tissue NGS Mismatch-repair status is unmeasured, and the plasma assay returned no MSI call at an unstated tumor fraction, so nothing on file speaks to it in either direction. Four stains on a block already being cut close a tumor-agnostic PD-1 indication that would otherwise sit open at progression (NCT02628067, NCT02715284). Loss of any one protein in a woman in her thirties also carries Lynch implications for her and for first-degree relatives. NeoGenomics Laboratories (MMR IHC panel with reflex testing) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 4 unstained slides from the same block cut for INI1 Validated comprehensive genomic profiling on tissue reporting TMB in mutations per megabase (with the MSI and BRAF codon 600 calls in the same report) TMB was never reported: the Guardant assay did not return one, and a plasma TMB at unstated tumor fraction would not have been usable if it had. Leiomyosarcoma is copy-number driven and typically low-TMB, so a high value would be a surprise, but the panel that reports it is the same order that settles MSI, the fusions, the HRR genes and the TP53 attribution question. Ask for a validated assay with a mutations-per-megabase figure; a number off a small hotspot panel does not satisfy the tumor-agnostic indication. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE; 10-15 unstained slides or the block (shared with tissue order A, not a separate specimen) RNA-based fusion NGS panel covering NTRK1, NTRK2 and NTRK3 (with RET, ALK and ROS1 in the same run) on archival tissue What is on file is non-detection on a plasma DNA assay at unstated tumor fraction, which is not a negative: plasma fusion calling is insensitive when shedding is low, and DNA capture misses breakpoints in the large NTRK introns. RNA sequencing reads the transcript and so is agnostic to where in the intron the break sits, which is what allows a negative to be read as a negative. Prevalence in uterine leiomyosarcoma is very low, but a spindle-cell tumor once signed out as benign is precisely the setting in which an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm hides, and a positive converts a chemotherapy-only landscape into an oral TRK inhibitor. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE; shares the specimen with tissue order A. RNA quality degrades in blocks older than about 5 years, so the 2026 lung core is the safer input Tumor NGS covering BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM and the wider HRR gene set, with a reported genomic-instability / LOH score An absent BRCA1/2 call on a plasma panel at unstated tumor fraction is weak evidence, and a genomic instability score cannot be derived from that assay at all, so homologous-recombination status is open rather than negative. Uterine leiomyosarcoma has a recognised HR-deficient subset including BRCA2 deletion and mutation (PMID 37143137), and olaparib plus temozolomide produced a 27 percent objective response rate with median PFS 6.9 months in pretreated advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma, where 31 percent of enrolled patients carried an HRR gene mutation (PMID 37467452). Skipping it leaves the one non-cytotoxic branch in this case unopened at the point where LMS-04 fails. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE; shares the specimen with tissue order A Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF and global longitudinal strain A documented pre-treatment LVEF is the precondition for giving doxorubicin, and the LMS-04 schedule carries the anthracycline to a cumulative dose in the cardiotoxicity surveillance band (PMID 35835135). ASCO and the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guideline both call for baseline ventricular imaging, with strain where available, before anthracycline exposure (PMID 27918725; PMID 36017568). Nothing cardiac is on file, so cycle 1 would be given with no reference value against which a later fall in function could be read. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no tissue; transthoracic echocardiogram (5-10 mL blood only if natriuretic peptides are added) Baseline comprehensive metabolic panel with bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, transaminases, creatine kinase and calculated creatinine clearance, plus a CBC with differential read against an altitude-adjusted haemoglobin reference Trabectedin carries dose-limiting hepatotoxicity and rhabdomyolysis risk, so baseline transaminases, bilirubin and creatine kinase are what any on-treatment abnormality will be measured against; LMS-04 gave the combination first line and carried trabectedin into maintenance (PMID 35835135). No laboratory values were supplied at intake, so there is currently no baseline at all. Residence at roughly 8,500 feet raises expected haemoglobin, and reading her count against a sea-level reference will make real chemotherapy-induced anaemia look like a normal result. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) 5-10 mL whole blood plus a serum tube at the pre-treatment visit Documented clinician-assessed ECOG performance status (with Karnofsky equivalent) recorded at the pre-treatment visit The ECOG of 1 carried through this case was an intake assumption, not a clinician's recorded score, and the profile says so. Nearly every option in scope sets an ECOG ceiling at screening: 0 to 1 for the PRAME TCR-T program (NCT03686124) and for the olaparib plus temozolomide protocol (NCT03880019), and the cell-therapy programs are the least forgiving. An undocumented score will either stall an application or produce a screen failure after tissue and time have been spent. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no tissue; clinician assessment at the pre-treatment visit Paired peripheral-blood leukocyte sequencing (buffy-coat myeloid/CHIP panel covering TP53) plus tissue NGS interrogation of the TP53 Q52* position Two orthogonal routes settle this and either will do: the same TP53 Q52* found in tumor DNA makes it tumor-derived, while finding it in white-cell DNA makes it clonal haematopoiesis. That distinction is not academic at unstated tumor fraction; in matched cfDNA and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2 percent of cfDNA mutations in cancer patients had features of clonal haematopoiesis (PMID 31768066). Be honest about the payoff: a confirmed somatic TP53 in uterine leiomyosarcoma is expected and largely prognostic, so the value is in calibrating how much weight the rest of this plasma report, including the SMARCB1 call, can carry. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA for the buffy-coat panel; archival FFPE for the tissue route, which comes free with tissue order A MAGE-A4 expression by IHC on tumor tissue, scored to the SPEARHEAD-1 screening threshold of at least 1+ staining in at least 10 percent of cells The expensive half of the eligibility question is already answered, since allele-level typing confirms A*02:01, one of the four allele groups the approved MAGE-A4 product names (A*02:01P, A*02:02P, A*02:03P, A*02:06P). What remains is antigen expression, and the threshold is protocol-specified rather than a local judgement call: SPEARHEAD-1 required at least 1+ staining in at least 10 percent of cells by central IHC (NCT04044768), and the licensed indication requires expression by an FDA-approved or cleared companion diagnostic. A multi-subtype sarcoma IHC series found MAGE-A4 expressed in only a minority of smooth-muscle sarcomas (PMID 40152485), well short of the near-uniform positivity that defines the synovial sarcoma population these products were built around, so a negative here is a realistic and useful outcome that closes the branch. NeoGenomics Laboratories (MAGE-A4 IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 3-5 unstained slides, shared with the PRAME and NY-ESO-1 stains on one block cut PRAME expression on tumor tissue: IHC (clone EPR20330) as the local screen, with the sponsor's own assay at formal screening (IMA203 uses IMADetect RT-qPCR, not IHC) Of the three A*02:01-restricted antigens in scope, PRAME is the most likely to be positive in this histology, and both programs behind it enrol on the same two-part gate she is halfway through: HLA-A*02:01 positive plus a PRAME-positive tumor (NCT03686124, NCT04262466). The assay is protocol-specified and not interchangeable: IMA203 screens on IMADetect RT-qPCR rather than IHC, and in its phase 1 the deeper responses clustered at higher PRAME expression (PMID 40205198), so the magnitude of positivity matters, not just its presence. A local IHC screen is worth running first because it costs one slide and a negative closes the axis before anyone spends a screening slot. NeoGenomics Laboratories (PRAME IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 3-5 unstained slides shared with the MAGE-A4 and NY-ESO-1 stains. RT-qPCR tolerates lower tumor content than IHC scoring B7-H3 (CD276) IHC on tumor tissue B7-H3 has the best odds of a positive result of any surface target in scope here: 97 percent of soft tissue sarcoma specimens were positive and about 69 percent high in a 153-patient series spanning 15 subtypes including leiomyosarcoma (PMID 39478506). Nothing is approved against it, so a positive buys trial access rather than a prescription, and the ADC, CAR-T and bispecific programs generally require documented expression at screening. Adding it to the block already being cut keeps a later referral from stalling while somebody hunts for tissue. NeoGenomics Laboratories (B7-H3 (CD276) IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 1-2 unstained slides from the same block cut as INI1 and the MMR set Baseline pulmonary function tests with DLCO, plus resting and ambulatory pulse oximetry recorded at residence altitude Bilateral pulmonary metastases read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory in a lifetime never-smoker at 8,500 feet is a pulmonary reserve question nobody has measured. A baseline DLCO and an oximetry pair recorded at her own altitude give the only reference against which on-treatment dyspnea can be attributed to disease progression, to chronic hypoxic adaptation, or to treatment. Without it, a fall in saturation during induction is uninterpretable. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no tissue; spirometry with DLCO and pulse oximetry at rest and on exertion INI1/SMARCB1 IHC read separately on the September 2024 uterine primary and the 2026 pulmonary metastasis Plasma reports shed disease, and the shedding compartment here is the lung, not a uterus removed in 2024. A SMARCB1 event acquired in the metastatic clone would be invisible on the primary and visible on the lung core, so staining only the older and more generous block risks a false negative on the one finding that could change management. Two years and no intervening systemic therapy separate the specimens, which makes divergence less likely than under treatment pressure but not negligible. NeoGenomics Laboratories (INI1 (BAF47) IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides from each of the two specimens RB1, ATRX and MED12 status from tissue NGS, with the p53 / Rb / ATRX / PTEN IHC surrogate panel read on the same block Ninety-four percent of 167 uterine leiomyosarcomas carried at least one alteration in TP53, RB1, ATRX, PTEN, CDKN2A or MDM2, and 80 percent carried two or more; the corresponding IHC surrogates agreed with sequencing at kappa 0.941 (PMID 36788080). Establishing that backbone does three things at once: it corroborates the diagnosis in a case whose primary was once called benign, it supplies the co-alteration context that trial screening asks for, and abnormal p53 staining would independently support a tumor origin for the plasma TP53 call. None of it is directly druggable, which is why this sits below the gating rows. NeoGenomics Laboratories · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond tissue orders A and B Pre-treatment CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with measurable RECIST v1.1 target lesions, read against any imaging available from the September 2024 to July 2026 interval Trial screening requires measurable disease by RECIST v1.1, and an infiltrative pulmonary pattern is exactly the morphology that can fail to yield measurable target lesions; better to discover that before a screening slot than during one. Reading the baseline against anything shot in the 2024 to 2026 interval also bounds the growth kinetics of disease that went untreated for roughly 23 months, which is the single best available estimate of tempo. Abdomen and pelvis matter here specifically because the 2024 hysterectomy may have disrupted the specimen. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no tissue; cross-sectional imaging with contrast unless contraindicated Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report and gross pathology description: route of hysterectomy, whether power or manual morcellation was used, specimen integrity and margin status A 6.0 cm myometrial mass removed as a presumed benign fibroid in 2024 may have been morcellated, and morcellation of an unrecognised leiomyosarcoma disperses tumor through the peritoneum and has been associated with worse outcomes (PMID 28209496; PMID 26646120). The staging picture is currently pulmonary only; if the specimen was disrupted, peritoneal and pelvic disease has to be actively excluded rather than assumed absent. The answer sits in an operative note nobody has yet had reason to re-read. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no tissue; the operative note and gross description from the September 2024 hysterectomy Germline SMARCB1 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis on whole blood, reflexed if tumor INI1 is lost or biallelic SMARCB1 loss is confirmed Germline SMARCB1 loss underlies rhabdoid tumor predisposition and schwannomatosis, and a uterine leiomyosarcoma arising in a schwannomatosis patient with a SMARCB1 alteration has been reported (PMID 26001331). A woman in her thirties with a confirmed tumor SMARCB1 event is exactly the presentation where somatic-only testing leaves both her own surveillance and her relatives' unanswered. Reflex this rather than ordering it up front: without tissue confirmation the pretest probability does not justify the counselling burden. Ambry Genetics (CancerNext-Expanded or single-gene SMARCB1) · test info · 1 Enterprise, Aliso Viejo, CA 92656 · 1-949-900-5500 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or saliva where a blood draw is inconvenient Germline multigene hereditary cancer panel including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM, TP53 and the Lynch genes Somatic-only testing answers what the tumor carries and nothing about what she carries, which for a woman in her thirties leaves her own second-cancer risk and her relatives' screening open. A germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 finding would also strengthen the PARP-inhibitor case beyond what a somatic call alone supports (PMID 37467452). Run it on the same draw as any other blood work rather than as a reflex weeks later; the counselling and insurance steps are the slow part, not the assay. Myriad Genetics (MyRisk Hereditary Cancer) · test info · 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 1-800-469-7423 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or saliva NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) expression by IHC (clone E978) or RT-PCR, run on the same block as MAGE-A4 and PRAME Her A*02:01 satisfies the restriction requirement for the NY-ESO-1 TCR-T program, which enrols A*02:01, A*02:05 or A*02:06 positive patients with central-laboratory-confirmed NY-ESO-1 expression (NCT03967223). Two things hold this below the other two antigens: NY-ESO-1 expression was low across all sarcoma subtypes in a recent multi-subtype IHC series (PMID 40152485), and that master protocol restricts enrolment to synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round cell liposarcoma, so even a positive stain points to a future solid-tumor cohort rather than an open door. It earns its place only because it adds one stain to a block already being cut. NeoGenomics Laboratories (NY-ESO-1 IHC) · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond the cancer/testis antigen block cut Formal grading parameters from the reference pathology review: mitotic index per 10 high-power fields, coagulative tumor cell necrosis, nuclear atypia and FNCLCC grade, on both specimens The diagnosis itself is settled: a reference laboratory confirmed uterine leiomyosarcoma on both the pulmonary biopsy and the re-reviewed uterine specimen in August 2026, so no second opinion is needed. What is not on file are the numbers behind the phrase high-grade, and trial screening asks for FNCLCC grade rather than a descriptor. Retrieving them is a request for a report, not a new assay, and it also documents whether the 2024 block was adequately sampled for a mass that went unrecognised at first pass. Treating institution (performed or requested locally; no send-out) no new tissue; the existing reference-laboratory report and slides Retrieval of the ER and PR IHC report: specimen of origin (2024 uterine resection versus 2026 lung core), antibody clone, scoring system and internal control adequacy, with a repeat stain on the metastasis if the call came from the primary The ER and PR result is recorded as confirmed at under 1 percent, which forecloses the endocrine branch, but the profile does not say which specimen produced it. Hormone-receptor expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma can differ between a uterine primary and a distant metastasis, and a 2024 primary is the specimen where a positive would be more likely, not less. If the call came from the lung core, nothing more is needed; if it came from the 2024 uterus, a repeat on the metastasis is the cheap way to be sure the door is genuinely shut. NeoGenomics Laboratories · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 no new tissue for the records request; 2 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core if a repeat is warranted Tumor HLA loss-of-heterozygosity assessment from the tissue sequencing data (allele-specific HLA copy number) Germline typing says which alleles she inherited; it says nothing about whether the tumor still presents them. Somatic loss of the A*02:01 allele is a documented escape route for the whole HLA-restricted antigen class and would undercut every A*02:01-directed option at once, however strong the antigen stain. Most comprehensive tissue panels can report allele-specific HLA copy number if asked, so this is a request to the laboratory rather than a separate assay. Caris Life Sciences (MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome)) · test info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669 archival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond tissue order A PD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system matched to the intended agent, plus CD3 and CD8 T-cell infiltrate density, on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core PD-L1 gates no approval in soft tissue sarcoma, so this informs rather than decides. It earns a row because the pulmonary lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and an immune phenotype on the lung core is the only way to tell whether that radiologic impression corresponds to anything in the tissue. Infiltrate density is also what cell-therapy and bispecific programs look at when weighing a candidate, so the CD3 and CD8 reads carry more forward here than the PD-L1 score does. NeoGenomics Laboratories · test info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907 archival FFPE; 2-3 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core specifically <p>Decision support, not medical advice. Confirm assay availability and current standards with the treating team and the local pathology service.</p>

docs.title: Scope summary
docs.text:
55 trial rows, 41 clinical-evidence rows, 53 preclinical rows, 25 target-validation rows, 15 biomarker-survey rows and 64 accessibility rows feed this synthesis, alongside 5 board positions and 20 cross-critiques. This is the Experimental table — the non-standard-of-care options only. It carries 45 rows: a rank-1 shared workup gate, five ranked therapeutic options, and thirty-nine rows below them. Thirty-five of those thirty-nine carry a surfaced_reason flag (sixteen not-enrollable, twelve thin-evidence, four unavailable, three consolidated); the other four are simply not_recommended on the evidence, with no flag. Agreement scores run from 1.0 (the workup, endorsed by all five) down to -0.4 (ivonescimab, endorsed by one and refused by three). No persona issued a formal veto in either round.

The spread is unusual and worth naming. LMS-04 appeared on all five slates and was rank 1 for four of them — and it is not in this table, because it is guideline-carried and routes to the Standard-of-care table. What remains here is what the board argued about rather than what it agreed on.

docs.title: Cross-cutting caveat (read first)
docs.text:
Almost nothing in this case has been measured, and the one molecular finding that looks practice-changing is probably a red herring. SMARCB1 G344Afs*13 was called on plasma ctDNA at unsupplied tumour fraction, heterozygous, in a histology where 170 of 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumours retained SMARCB1 in the one IHC series carried here (PMID 34271067). The decision-relevant resolution is INI1/SMARCB1 IHC on tumour tissue, and it has not been done. The TP53 Q52* call rests on the same shedding assumptions and carries its own clonal-haematopoiesis caveat — if TP53 turns out to be blood-derived, the SMARCB1 call's credibility falls with it. So the rank-1 action here is a pathology requisition, not a drug.

  • This table is scoped to non-standard-of-care options, and it is one of two co-equal tables. LMS-04 (doxorubicin + trabectedin with trabectedin maintenance), gemcitabine/docetaxel, doxorubicin/ifosfamide, single-agent trabectedin, pazopanib, eribulin, gemcitabine/dacarbazine, single-agent temozolomide, pulmonary metastasectomy, lung SBRT, and the tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab, dostarlimab and larotrectinib routes are all routed to the Standard-of-care table, not rejected. The board ranked most of them. LMS-04 sat at rank 1 on four of five slates. If you came here looking for chemotherapy, that is where it is.
  • If INI1 comes back retained on tissue, ranks 7, 24, 25, 26 and 40 through 42 are foreclosed — tazemetostat, valemetostat, the TIGIT combination, ubamatamab and the three BRD9 degrader rows. Everything else in this table stands regardless: the rank-1 workup, olaparib + temozolomide (rank 2), the abemaciclib randomised seat (rank 3), IMA203 (rank 4), in-vivo lung perfusion (rank 5), ivonescimab (rank 6), and the whole HLA-A*02:01 axis. And the Standard-of-care table is entirely unaffected, with LMS-04 at the front of it.
  • Two anthracycline ceilings belong in the conversation before cycle 1, not before cycle 6. In-vivo lung perfusion excludes above 450 mg cumulative doxorubicin; the peposertib protocol caps at 360 mg/m², which is exactly six LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m². Three personas flagged this independently. A stopping rule decided in advance costs nothing; discovered at cycle six it costs two doors.
  • One Rb stain routes her between two MD Anderson protocols. Intact Rb points to NCT06498648, which admits treatment-naive patients and is therefore live today; Rb loss points to NCT07633756 after a first line. The stain is already on the planned block cut. Note the sequencing trap: prior gemcitabine permanently disqualifies from NCT06498648, so an off-protocol gemcitabine/docetaxel prescription closes it for good, while LMS-04 — which contains no gemcitabine — preserves it.
  • Workup logistics, since the workup is rank 1. Three tissue orders cover nearly every open question in this case, and they should go out on a single block-release request naming both the 2024 uterine specimen and the 2026 lung core. IHC turnaround is 3-5 days once a block is in hand; tissue NGS runs 2-3 weeks. The rate-limiting step is administrative: releasing a 2024 block from the outside institution that signed the primary out benign, and nobody clinical currently owns that request.

docs.title: Workup considerations
docs.text: Beyond the rank-1 gate, the target validator flagged several high-priority reads that inform rather than gate. INI1 should be read separately on the 2024 primary and the 2026 pulmonary metastasis, because the shedding compartment is the lung and a metastasis-acquired event would be invisible on the older block. A germline hereditary-cancer panel runs on the same draw as any other blood work and would strengthen an off-label PARP authorisation beyond what a somatic call alone supports; germline SMARCB1 sequencing reflexes only if tumour INI1 is lost. Baseline RECIST-measurable staging imaging matters here more than usual, since an infiltrative pulmonary pattern is exactly the morphology that can fail to yield measurable target lesions at trial screening. Retrieving the September 2024 operative report to establish whether the specimen was morcellated would decide whether peritoneal disease has to be actively excluded. And the formal FNCLCC grading parameters behind the phrase "high-grade" are a report request rather than a new assay.

docs.title: Intervention grouping
docs.text:
• PARP-directed, homologous-recombination-gated: olaparib + temozolomide (PMID 37467452, NCT03880019, NCT05432791); the BRCA2-altered uLMS series that motivates the tissue order (PMID 30541756, PMID 37143137).
  • Cell-cycle, routed by one Rb stain: abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel (NCT06498648); REC-617 CDK7 inhibition in RB1-negative disease (NCT07633756).
  • HLA-A*02:01-restricted, antigen-gated: IMA203 PRAME TCR-T (PMID 40205198, NCT03686124); CDR404 MAGE-A4 engager (NCT06402201); brenetafusp (NCT04262466); the histology-restricted products afamitresgene (PMID 38554725), uzatresgene (NCT04044859), lete-cel (PMID 29891538) and the class precedent tebentafusp (PMID 34551229); antigen prevalence (PMID 40152485).
  • SWI/SNF-directed, INI1-gated: tazemetostat (PMID 41882006, PMID 33035459); valemetostat (NCT07303387); the two terminated BRD9 degraders (PMID 39660994, PMID 41285423); tiragolumab + atezolizumab (NCT05286801).
  • Investigational locoregional: in-vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin plus metastasectomy (NCT02811523, PMID 26952295); pulmonary suffusion (NCT03965234); the selection literature behind both (PMID 37063124, PMID 9011700).
  • Checkpoint and bispecific immunotherapy: ivonescimab (NCT07516925, PMID 40057343); the three negatives that define the class here (PMID 25713428, PMID 28988646, PMID 28440953); nivolumab ± ipilimumab (PMID 29370992); doxorubicin + pembrolizumab (PMID 32910151).
  • First-in-human ADCs and radioligands: B7-H3 (NCT06242470, NCT06551142, PMID 39478506); uPARAP (NCT06797999); LRRC15 (NCT07374848); FAP-directed alpha and beta emitters (NCT07156565, NCT06710756, NCT04939610).
  • DNA-damage-response, deprioritised on its own negative: ATR inhibition on the ATRX/ALT hypothesis (PMID 39453756, NCT04807816, NCT05691491); peposertib DNA-PK inhibition (NCT05711615).

docs.title: Rank 1. One block-release request carrying tissue orders A, B and C, plus a documented ECOG with altitude-referenced oximetry, baseline echocardiogram and organ-function labs — diagnostic gate
docs.text: What it resolves: INI1, Rb, mismatch repair, p53, ATRX, PD-L1 and B7-H3 by IHC; tissue NGS with an HRD score, the HRR gene set, TMB and RNA fusion calling; MAGE-A4, PRAME and NY-ESO-1 antigen expression; and, from the clinic side, a scored performance status, an LVEF, and oximetry read against 8,500 ft rather than sea level.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is no efficacy literature for a requisition, so the anchors here are the gates it opens. The tazemetostat basket required INI1 loss by IHC, or biallelic molecular loss where IHC was equivocal (NCT02601950), and the counterweight is the one prevalence series in this histology: 170 of 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumours retained SMARCB1 (PMID 34271067). Entry to NCT06498648 turns on intact Rb by IHC read on the site's own antibody, and its mirror protocol turns on Rb loss. Olaparib + temozolomide did not require homologous-recombination deficiency for entry (PMID 37467452), but a tissue HRD or HRR result is what makes the later off-label authorisation winnable. Every effect estimate quoted anywhere on this page comes from a trial that enrolled ECOG 0-1.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: High, in the only sense that applies: these assays return answers. The INI1 stain has a 3-5 day turnaround once a block is in hand, and the whole tissue panel runs 2-3 weeks. What is genuinely uncertain is the calendar, not the biology — a 2024 block sitting at the hospital that called the tumour benign is the kind of request that goes unowned for weeks.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• No therapeutic toxicity. Pathology requisitions on archival tissue, a clinic visit, an echocardiogram, a blood draw and pulmonary function testing.
  • The one cost is money, not harm: cancer/testis antigen IHC (order C) is not reliably covered outside a trial. Ask self-pay pricing and ask the sponsors whether they run their own assay.
  • No toxicity veto is engaged, and none could be — her veto list is empty because nobody asked.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Board endorsement was unanimous on the content and split on the placement, which is why this row exists in the shared-workup slot rather than competing with a therapy. The advocate ranked a documented ECOG first outright. The critic conceded the substance out loud: an unmeasured performance status is an applicability defect inside every number this board quoted, not a piece of admin. Then it objected structurally, that a measurement carries no effect size, no comparator and no toxicity profile, so ranking it makes the slate non-comparable. The conservative made the same objection more bluntly, that a chart entry cannot carry rank 1 while LMS-04 sits at rank 3 behind it. Both are right, and the workup slot is the mechanism that lets both be right at once.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Send orders A, B and C on one release request rather than serially; ordering them in sequence is how a first-line window gets spent on paperwork. Name both specimens explicitly and copy the treating office. Ask MD Anderson whether an outside CLIA Rb result is accepted or the site must run its own assay, because that changes the screening timeline. Put the altitude on the oximetry report — a saturation that looks marginal to a screening coordinator may be her baseline, and the cell-therapy protocols in this dossier set floors at 90% room air with one at 92%.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Nothing below it is decidable without it. Rank 2's authorisation case, rank 3's eligibility, rank 4's antigen gate and rank 7's entire existence all hang on results this requisition produces, and it forecloses nothing on any preference axis — the only row in the table of which that is true.

docs.title: Rank 2. Olaparib + temozolomide (NCI Protocol 10250 regimen in uterine leiomyosarcoma), post-induction, with tissue HRD/HRR testing ordered now
docs.text: The strongest lineage-matched targeted signal in the file, one line away, at the cost of a second consecutive 75% grade 3/4 neutropenia.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: NCI Protocol 10250 was a 22-patient single-arm multicentre phase 2 in advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after at least one prior line, and it met its prespecified primary endpoint: 5 of 22 responses within six months against a design powered at 93% with alpha 0.06. Overall best objective response rate was 27% (6 of 22; the primary-endpoint figure was 23%), with median PFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE) (PMID 37467452, NCT03880019). This is single-arm with open-label response assessment, rated ROBINS-I moderate, and the randomised confirmation in the same histology is fully accrued and unreported (NCT05432791). The RAD51 split that everyone quotes — median PFS 11.2 versus 5.4 months, p=0.05 — was exploratory in 18 assayed patients and is not a result. Entry did not require homologous-recombination deficiency.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Moderate, and the most defensible "moderate" on this page, because the response rate was generated in her exact histology rather than borrowed from a neighbouring one. If her tissue returns homologous-recombination deficiency, the exploratory subgroup suggests she sits in the better half; if it returns proficiency, the same subgroup suggests roughly five months of disease control. Neither of those numbers should be quoted to her as a prediction. What is solid is 27% and 6.9 months in 22 women with her disease.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade 3/4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, managed with dose modification. No treatment-related deaths reported.
  • The sequencing problem the critic named: this marrow will have just absorbed LMS-04's 80% grade 3-4 neutropenia and 47% thrombocytopenia. Two consecutive regimens in that range is not the same proposition as either one alone.
  • Polycythaemia at 8,500 ft will confound anaemia assessment throughout, and no altitude-referenced baseline haemoglobin exists.
  • No stated toxicity veto is engaged, because the veto list is empty and unasked. That is not consent.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent and no veto; four of five personas ranked it. The disagreement was about how to hold it rather than whether. The critic and the concensusite both rested it on the prespecified endpoint and refused the RAD51 crutch — the critic gave the concensusite explicit credit for being the only persona who did that unprompted. The risktaker took the subgroup bet and labelled it exploratory in the same breath, which the critic conceded is how a subgroup ought to be carried. The mechanism-level risk is mundane rather than exotic: overlapping myelosuppression forcing dose reductions that cost the PARP exposure the regimen depends on.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Both trials of the combination are closed to accrual, so the live route is an off-label prescription of two approved drugs, and that prior-authorisation case is much stronger with a tissue HRD or HRR result than with a plasma panel that settles nothing. Guideline carriage is thin: the ESMO clinical practice guideline predates the trial, and the concensusite could not verify NCCN listing this run because NCCN blocks automated access — which is exactly why the guideline chair placed it fourth on its own slate rather than second. Entry required a prior line, so nothing on this branch is reachable in the first-line window except the tissue testing, and the tissue testing is rank 1.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It ties rank 3 on board agreement at 0.8, and it wins the tie on evidence. Olaparib + temozolomide has a met primary endpoint and a real response rate in her histology; the abemaciclib seat has a blood thymidine kinase time course. What keeps it from being unambiguously first among the therapies is that it cannot be given yet and its toxicity lands on a marrow that will already be depleted.

docs.title: Rank 3. Abemaciclib + gemcitabine and docetaxel (NCT06498648, MD Anderson randomised phase 1/2), Rb-intact required
docs.text: The only investigational seat that survives LMS-04 instead of competing with it — and the only one whose worst case inside the trial is guideline care.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: There is no efficacy readout, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. The phase 1 primary endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase activity time course; the phase 2 randomises against the gemcitabine/docetaxel backbone with a PFS endpoint (NCT06498648). What the design buys is a floor. The control arm is a regimen with a dedicated first-line uterine phase 2 behind it, objective response rate 35.8% (95% CI 23.5-49.6) in 42 chemotherapy-naive women and median PFS 4.4 months (PMID 18534250), plus a randomised phase 3 keeping that number honest, since GeDDiS found the doublet no better than doxorubicin at 24-week PFS and trending the wrong way (PMID 28882536). Abemaciclib itself has essentially no efficacy data in leiomyosarcoma.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Unknown for the add-on and moderate for the backbone. Single-arm response rates in uterine leiomyosarcoma have repeatedly outrun their randomised comparisons, so 35.8% should be read as what the control arm might deliver rather than what she should expect. The honest framing is that this seat buys her a randomised chance at an unproven addition, with guideline chemotherapy as the downside — which is a genuinely different bet from every other trial in this dossier.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Backbone, from the uterine phase 2: grade 3 anaemia 24%, grade 3 fatigue 17%, grade 3-4 neutropenia 17%, grade 3 thrombocytopenia 9.5%, and one possibly related grade 4 pulmonary event in 42 patients — a number that reads differently in a never-smoker with infiltrative bilateral lung disease at altitude.
  • From GeDDiS: grade 3+ neutropenia 20%, febrile neutropenia 12%, fatigue 14%. No treatment-related deaths.
  • Abemaciclib contributes diarrhoea and neutropenia on top, and the combination's tolerability is uncharacterised outside this study's own phase 1 portion. The conservative named that gap specifically.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: No dissent and no veto. Four personas ranked it directly and the concensusite endorsed it inside its own gemcitabine/docetaxel row, calling it the trial-seat answer it could defend from the guideline chair. The critic ranked it fourth while naming the real cost: enrolment forfeits the first-line LMS-04 window, and that trade should be said out loud before consent. There is also a mechanism question nobody has answered — CDK4/6-induced G1 arrest can antagonise S-phase-dependent gemcitabine, and this study's phase 1 portion is the first place that interaction gets characterised in this combination.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Single site in Houston, and the advocate's dissent applies squarely: an empty modality_constraints list is not the same as a woman at 8,500 ft agreeing to fly to Texas during first-line treatment. Nobody has asked her. The sequencing fact is the one to act on now — the phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive patients and the disqualifier is prior gemcitabine, so LMS-04 preserves this seat while an off-protocol gemcitabine/docetaxel prescription destroys it. The conservative pushed back usefully on the purist version of that rule: if the echo or the pulmonary workup rules out full-dose doxorubicin and the Houston screening clock loses the race against symptomatic lung disease, off-protocol gemcitabine/docetaxel delivered at home is the defensible choice, and the rule should say so rather than hold a fallback hostage to a seat.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Same agreement score as rank 2, placed below it because its own drug has no efficacy data. It sits above rank 4 by a full 0.8 on agreement, and for a concrete reason: this is the one seat where the downside inside the trial is standard care, which is not true of a phase 1 cell therapy.

docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel No readout; thymidine kinase and PFS endpoints Uncharacterised for the combination NCT06498648 Gemcitabine + docetaxel, first-line uterine LMS ORR 35.8%; mPFS 4.4 mo G3 anaemia 24%, G3-4 neutropenia 17%, one G4 pulmonary event 18534250 Gemcitabine + docetaxel vs doxorubicin (GeDDiS) 46.4% vs 46.3% PFS at 24 weeks; PFS HR 1.28 G3+ neutropenia 20%, febrile neutropenia 12% 28882536 REC-617 (the Rb-loss alternative) No readout; safety endpoint, n=15 Not published NCT07633756

docs.title: Rank 4. IMA203 / IMA203CD8 PRAME-directed TCR-T cells (NCT03686124), sponsor screening started in the first-line window
docs.text: The only cellular axis her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 opens, double-gated on a sponsor assay and a standard-of-care-exhaustion clause.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: The published dataset is a 41-patient first-in-human phase 1 dose escalation and extension in PRAME-positive HLA-A*02-positive solid tumours, melanoma-dominant with sarcoma patients included: confirmed objective response rate 28.9%, maximum tolerated dose not reached, median duration of response 4.4 months (range 2.4-23.0) (PMID 40205198). No uterine leiomyosarcoma patient appears in it. The premise that PRAME is the likeliest of her three candidate antigens to return positive has nothing behind it in this file — the one prevalence series carried here covers 26 smooth-muscle tumours, is not uterus-restricted, puts PRAME highest in undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and osteosarcoma, and quotes no smooth-muscle PRAME figure at all (PMID 40152485). Its adjacent MAGE-A4 smooth-muscle number drew an erratum and is flagged internally inconsistent in this dossier's own evidence row.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low to uncertain, and the honest version of that sentence has three qualifiers in it: cross-tumour, phase 1, and gated on an antigen nobody has measured. A 28.9% response rate with a 4.4-month median duration in heavily pretreated melanoma-dominant patients is not a number that transfers to a chemotherapy-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma. What the risktaker was actually arguing for is narrower and survives the critique: the sponsor's screening conversation takes weeks, runs parallel to induction, and costs nothing from the first-line window.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Severe cytokine release syndrome in 2 of 41 (4.9%); no severe neurotoxicity reported.
  • Lymphodepletion cytopenias are expected and were not tabulated per term in the interim report. The neighbouring TCR-T products in this dossier report near-universal grade 3+ lymphopenia and neutropenia, which is the realistic expectation for the class.
  • Apheresis, lymphodepleting chemotherapy and a manufacturing interval, in a patient who has never had a day of systemic therapy.
  • No stated toxicity veto is engaged; the list is empty and unasked.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Only the risktaker ranked it, and the critic dissented hard on evidence quality — a phase 1 number with no patient of her histology in it, a 4.4-month median duration, and a PRAME-prevalence premise with nothing under it. The advocate qualified rather than endorsed, and objected to the warrant rather than the biology: holding this seat because a durable-tail outcome in a woman in her thirties is worth chasing is a preference, and it belongs to the risktaker, not to her. That is why this row reads considered_with_caveats despite carrying only one formal dissent. The risktaker's counter is precise and correct as far as it goes: the erratum attaches to the smooth-muscle MAGE-A4 prevalence paper, not to IMA203's own phase 1, so declining a free screening conversation on someone else's erratum is the one place this board's evidence bar cuts against the patient rather than for her. On mechanism, antigen-loss escape and somatic HLA-A*02:01 loss of heterozygosity would each close the axis, and neither has been assessed.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Recruiting at 21 sites across the US and Germany, which makes it the most reachable engineered-cell option here. Two gates stand in the way. Expression is scored on the sponsor's own IMADetect RT-qPCR rather than IHC, so a local stain has no established operating characteristics against the assay that decides entry — neither a positive nor a negative local result settles it. And the protocol requires receipt of, or ineligibility for, all available indicated standard-of-care treatment, which in practice makes this post-induction. Uterine carcinoma and carcinosarcoma appear in the registry keywords; leiomyosarcoma does not, and that is worth asking about directly rather than assuming either way. The class oximetry floor of 90% room air is the free measurement that decides whether any of this is reachable, and at her altitude it needs the altitude on the report.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: It sits 0.8 below rank 3 on agreement, and the gap is real rather than procedural: one persona wanted it, one dissented on evidence, and a third objected that the enthusiasm behind it was not the patient's. It sits above rank 5 on a tie-break rather than a score, since both are 0.0, because starting a screening conversation costs nothing and holding a thoracotomy seat costs an anthracycline budget.

docs.title: Rank 5. In vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin plus metastasectomy (NCT02811523, Toronto), as post-induction consolidation
docs.text: The one option in this dossier aimed at cure rather than control, and the one whose anatomic premise her current imaging may defeat.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Two separate evidence bases sit under this row and they should not be blended. The perfusion technique itself is a phase 1 with acute lung injury as its registered primary endpoint, resting on preclinical work (NCT02811523, PMID 26952295); there is no published human efficacy series. The survival numbers everyone quotes belong to metastasectomy: 55.4% five-year overall survival in the uterine-sarcoma subset of a 319-case Japanese multicentre registry selected on a disease-free interval over 12 months (PMID 37063124), 36% five-year survival after complete resection in the 5,206-case international registry (PMID 9011700), and median overall survival 70 months in a leiomyosarcoma subset undergoing repeated resection (PMID 21867989). All retrospective, all heavily selected.

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Genuinely unknown, and the uncertainty is about her rather than about the numbers. Her roughly 23-month interval from primary resection to metastatic diagnosis clears the registry's disease-free-interval selector comfortably. Her current disease distribution does not: bilateral, multifocal, and read as infiltrative. If induction converts that to countable resectable nodules, the registry population becomes hers and this becomes the highest-ceiling option on the page. If it does not, the row evaporates.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Thoracotomy morbidity, plus acute lung injury — which is the trial's registered primary endpoint, meaning the safety question is what the study is asking rather than what it has answered.
  • No published human safety series in this population.
  • Unmeasured pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline in a lifetime never-smoker with infiltrative bilateral disease. No pulmonary function tests, no DLCO, no oximetry.
  • Cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg is exclusionary. Six full LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m² approach that.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: The conservative dissented on toxicity, and the objection has three parts, each of which stands on its own: a phase 1 perfusion protocol with no safety series in this population; a patient with unmeasured pulmonary reserve asked to hold a thoracotomy seat; and a phase 3 regimen having its dose intensity bent around a phase 1 exclusion. The concensusite landed at qualified, right shelf and wrong door, noting that ESMO carries complete excision of resectable lung metastases as standard local treatment in selected patients while the perfusion vehicle has no society carriage anywhere. The sharpest single objection is the conservative's on selection: 55.4% five-year survival belongs to patients who reached complete resection of countable nodules, so her disease-free interval transfers to her and the survival figure does not. The risktaker's counter also stands, and I think it is underweighted elsewhere in these proceedings: the resectability call belongs to a thoracic surgeon looking at her films, not to a radiation-first default made from a board table. The critic added a related warning that applies to the alternative rather than to this row: zero grade 3+ events across two retrospective, heavily selected SBRT series says something about how retrospective toxicity gets captured, not about a measured safety margin.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: Single site in Toronto, so this is an international referral. Two questions decide whether the row is real, and both can be asked this week: whether the study accepts US-resident patients, and how the 450 mg cumulative-doxorubicin exclusion is counted against a planned six-cycle induction. The US counterpart, pulmonary suffusion at a single Buffalo site, carries no prior-line requirement at all and is surfaced separately below. Neither is the guideline-carried route — wedge metastasectomy and lung SBRT are, and both sit in the Standard-of-care table.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Tied with rank 4 at 0.0 and placed below it because holding this seat is not free: it constrains the anthracycline dose of the regimen the board unanimously supports, while a PRAME screening call constrains nothing. It sits above rank 6 by 0.4 because one persona actively wanted it and one dissented, rather than one wanting it and three refusing.

docs.title: Rank 6. Ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific), MSK single-arm phase 2 in leiomyosarcoma (NCT07516925)
docs.text: The only seat reachable before cycle 1 by explicit protocol language — and the one four of five personas refused.

docs.title: Evidence base
docs.text: Zero published sarcoma efficacy for the molecule. The credibility rests entirely on HARMONi-2, where ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab head-to-head on PFS in PD-L1-positive NSCLC: HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.38-0.69), median PFS 11.1 versus 5.8 months, at an interim analysis of a China-only trial with immature overall survival (PMID 40057343). The MSK study is a 20-patient single-arm phase 2 with an objective-response endpoint (NCT07516925). Against that sit three trials in or adjacent to her disease: GOG-0250, a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 showing bevacizumab added nothing to first-line gemcitabine/docetaxel in chemotherapy-naive metastatic uterine leiomyosarcoma, PFS HR 1.12, p=0.58 (PMID 25713428); SARC028, where the leiomyosarcoma cohort went 0 for 10 while other histologies carried the signal (PMID 28988646); and a dedicated uterine leiomyosarcoma nivolumab study stopped at stage 1 for futility, 0 of 12, median PFS 1.8 months (PMID 28440953).

docs.title: Likelihood of desired effect
docs.text: Low. Both mechanisms in this bispecific have already been tested in this disease and lost, one of them in a randomised trial designed to answer exactly this question. The bispecific-cooperativity argument — that co-targeting produces something neither axis achieves alone — is real preclinical biology and has no clinical support in any sarcoma. HARMONi-2 says the molecule is active in lung cancer. It says nothing about hers.

docs.title: Toxicity profile
docs.text:
• Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events 29% versus 16% for pembrolizumab in NSCLC, the increment mostly VEGF-class effects; grade 3+ immune-related events 7% versus 8%.
  • VEGF-class hypertension and bleeding risk, in a patient with bilateral pulmonary lesions.
  • Repeated cross-country travel from 8,500 ft during first-line treatment, which is a toxicity of a different kind and is not on any adverse-event table.
  • No stated toxicity veto is engaged. The empty list is the problem, not the permission.

docs.title: Counter-productive mechanisms / dissent
docs.text: Three personas dissented and the advocate alone ranked it, which is where hard rule 3 bites: an option the advocate flagged as preference-aligned against three objections stays visible with caveats rather than being dropped. The critic's convergence verdict belongs on this row and cuts both ways. Four of five refused the seat off the same three papers, so that is one evidence base read four times and nobody should bank the unanimity as extra weight — but the refusal survives the correction, because GOG-0250, SARC028 and the uterine futility stop are three mutually independent trials and one of them is a randomised null in this exact disease. The risktaker's dissent is the most pointed, because the risktaker is the persona who normally takes thin-evidence bets: thin evidence with a live mechanism is a risk worth taking, and a first-line window spent on two mechanisms this disease has already beaten is not. The concensusite qualified rather than dissented, noting no guideline in any region carries the drug or its class in sarcoma.

docs.title: Practical considerations
docs.text: The eligibility text is the whole reason this row is here: patients who decline standard first-line systemic therapy are eligible, and the ECOG ceiling is 2 rather than 0-1. That makes it reachable now, before LMS-04 starts, by explicit protocol language rather than by inference — the only investigational row in this dossier of which that is true. Seven sites, all in the MSK New York and New Jersey network, six flagged Limited Protocol Activities. Travel is not supplied with the study drug, so ask about patient travel assistance at first contact rather than after the first invoice, and ask which visits could happen at her home institution. Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or VEGF-pathway exposure is exclusionary, which means starting pazopanib first would close this permanently.

docs.title: Why this rank
docs.text: Last among the ranked therapies at -0.4, and the distance from rank 5 is the distance between one dissent and three. The advocate did not argue it was better; it argued that the question of whether she wants it has never been put to her, and that the seat closes when LMS-04 starts. Both of those are true, and neither makes it a stronger option than the four above it.

docs.text: Therapeutic agent Efficacy Toxicity Reference Ivonescimab, leiomyosarcoma phase 2 No readout; ORR endpoint, n=20 Not published in sarcoma NCT07516925 Ivonescimab vs pembrolizumab (HARMONi-2, NSCLC) PFS HR 0.51; mPFS 11.1 vs 5.8 mo G3+ TRAE 29% vs 16% 40057343 Gemcitabine/docetaxel ± bevacizumab (GOG-0250) PFS HR 1.12, p=0.58 — no benefit G3 hypertension 8%; one fistula 25713428 Pembrolizumab (SARC028) 0 of 10 in the LMS cohort G3+ anaemia and lymphopenia 7% each 28988646 Nivolumab, uterine LMS ORR 0%; stopped for futility at n=12 3 of 12 drug-attributed G3+ events 28440953

docs.title: Also considered — not ranked
docs.text:
Thirty-nine rows sit below the ranked six. Thirty-five carry a surfaced_reason flag; the other four are not_recommended on the evidence without one. All thirty-nine remain in recommendations.jsonl, because a flag demotes a row within the ranking and never deletes it.

  • Thin evidence (no peer-reviewed clinical efficacy in a population that reaches her). Tazemetostat (rank 7) — the SMARCB1 branch's ranked approach, gated on a stain the board expects to come back retained, and buying 9% response in the INI1-negative non-epithelioid basket cohort even if it does not. REC-617 (rank 8) — the Rb-loss half of a stain that is free to run now. CDR404 (rank 9) — an off-the-shelf MAGE-A4 engager with no manufacturing lead time and possibly no prior-line requirement. B7-H3 ADCs (rank 10) — the surface target most likely to be present, 97% of soft tissue sarcomas positive, on a stain that rides the same block cut. Peposertib + liposomal doxorubicin (rank 11) — a later-line seat whose 360 mg/m² anthracycline ceiling makes it an induction-planning question. ADCE-D01 (rank 12) and ZL-6201 (rank 13) — first-in-human ADCs with line windows LMS-04 opens and a third line closes. Gemcitabine + nab-sirolimus (rank 14) — whose gemcitabine backbone would permanently close the rank-3 seat. ATRA + cemiplimab (rank 15) — the one PRAME-adjacent rationale needing no cell product, on a checkpoint backbone this disease has twice defeated. Pulmonary suffusion (rank 16) — the US locoregional trial with no prior-line requirement. Tuvusertib + temozolomide (rank 17) — the only reachable ATR seat. FAP radioligands (rank 18) — the one axis screened by a scan rather than a stain.
  • Not enrollable (line, geography, histology or closed accrual). Zanzalintinib (rank 19, needs two prior lines). Lurbinectedin + doxorubicin (rank 20) — the near-miss of this case, a first-line anthracycline-naive leiomyosarcoma phase 3 that closed to accrual before her diagnosis was corrected. PLD maintenance (rank 21, Taiwan-only, and her own regimen already answers the question). Anlotinib (rank 22) — an 11-month median PFS in a non-prespecified 26-patient LMS subset, in an arm currently suspended. Brenetafusp (rank 23, accrual closed). Valemetostat (rank 24) — looks like a SMARCB1 door and is not: biallelic homozygous deletion required, France only. Tiragolumab + atezolizumab (rank 25) — the most reachable SMARCB1-directed study for a US patient until it closed. Ubamatamab (rank 26, histology excluded twice over). Afamitresgene (rank 27), uzatresgene (rank 28), lete-cel (rank 29), tebentafusp (rank 30) — the HLA-A*02:01 products her allele fits and her histology does not. CC-3 (rank 31, one German site, colorectal-written eligibility). MASCT-I (rank 32), tislelizumab + doxorubicin/ifosfamide (rank 33), fluzoparib + camrelizumab + SBRT (rank 34) — three first-line or PARP-plus-radiotherapy studies, all single-site in China.
  • Assessed and not recommended, without a flag. Nivolumab (rank 35) and nivolumab ± ipilimumab (rank 36) — the checkpoint record in this histology, carried so the negative is visible rather than absent. Doxorubicin + pembrolizumab (rank 37) — deliverable first-line chemo-immunotherapy whose response endpoint failed and whose responders were other histologies. ATR inhibition on the ATRX/ALT hypothesis (rank 38) — the cleanest negative in the file: tested in her histology, in patients selected on the right biomarker, with target engagement proven on serial biopsy, and they progressed within four months.
  • Consolidated into a ranked approach. PARP inhibition in BRCA2-altered uLMS (rank 39, into rank 2) — the reason BRCA2 belongs on her tissue order, and a four-patient tier-4 series that cannot carry more than that. Cancer/testis antigen target biology (rank 44, into rank 4 and the HLA-A*02:01 rows). Checkpoint-blockade target biology (rank 45, into ranks 6 and 35 through 37) — which earns the immune-phenotype stains a place on the rank-1 block cut.
  • Unavailable (discontinued, terminated or completed with no successor). BRD9 degraders as a class (rank 40) with FHD-609 (rank 41) and CFT8634 (rank 42) — the second SMARCB1 approach, closed twice rather than once. [177Lu]Lu-ITG-PSMA-1 (rank 43) — a finished single-centre Swiss phase 1 with no successor.

Two things are deliberately absent here. Approved and guideline-carried therapies — LMS-04, gemcitabine/docetaxel, doxorubicin/ifosfamide, trabectedin, pazopanib, eribulin, gemcitabine/dacarbazine, temozolomide, metastasectomy, SBRT, and the biomarker-gated tumour-agnostic routes — are routed to the Standard-of-care table, not surfaced here. And no HER-family option was constructed from ERBB3 G914E at 0.9% VAF, because a variant at the assay's limit of detection in a gene with no established role in this histology is not a targetable feature.

docs.title: Ranked prioritization
docs.text:
Diagnostic gate (do first):

Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 1 Block release + tissue orders A/B/C, documented ECOG, echo, labsendorse: conservative critic advocate risktaker concensusite Diagnostic gate: one block release resolves INI1, Rb, HRD/HRR, mismatch repair, TMB, fusions and three antigen stains; the clinic half returns ECOG, LVEF and altitude-read oximetry. Low (none — pathology orders on archival tissue plus a clinic visit and an echocardiogram) N/A (diagnostic and clinical measurement; no therapeutic mechanism) One block release and one clinic visit decide six downstream branches, and the 2024 outside institution that signed the primary out benign is the bottleneck.

Ranked therapeutic options:

Rank Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall 2 Olaparib + temozolomide (NCI 10250)endorse: conservative critic risktaker concensusite Moderate in her exact histology: ORR 27% (6 of 22) and mPFS 6.9 months in advanced uterine LMS, prespecified endpoint met (pmid:37467452). High (G3/4 neutropenia 75%, thrombocytopenia 32%, anaemia; managed with dose modification, no treatment-related deaths) Low (overlapping myelosuppression after LMS-04 may force dose reductions that cost the PARP exposure the regimen depends on) The best lineage-matched targeted signal in this file, sitting one line away and worth ordering tissue HRD for now — at a heavy second consecutive marrow cost. 3 Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel (NCT06498648)endorse: conservative critic advocate risktaker Unknown for the add-on: no abemaciclib efficacy data in LMS. The floor is the randomised gem/doc control arm, ORR 35.8% first-line uterine (pmid:18534250). Moderate (backbone G3 anaemia 24%, G3 fatigue 17%, G3-4 neutropenia 17%, one G4 pulmonary event in 42; abemaciclib diarrhoea uncharacterised on this doublet) Moderate (CDK4/6-induced G1 arrest can antagonise S-phase-dependent gemcitabine; Rb-intact status, the premise of the whole seat, is unmeasured) The one investigational seat that survives LMS-04 instead of competing with it, routed by a single Rb stain and carrying no efficacy data of its own. 4 IMA203 PRAME TCR-T (NCT03686124)endorse: risktakerdissent: critic Low-to-uncertain: 28.9% confirmed ORR in a 41-patient phase 1 with no uLMS patient and mDoR 4.4 months (pmid:40205198). Moderate (severe CRS 4.9%, no severe ICANS in n=41; lymphodepletion cytopenias expected but not tabulated per term) Moderate (antigen-loss or HLA-A*02:01 LOH escape; a local PRAME stain has no established operating characteristics against the sponsor assay) The only cellular axis her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 opens, double-gated on a sponsor PRAME assay and a standard-of-care-exhaustion clause. 5 In vivo lung perfusion + metastasectomy (NCT02811523)endorse: risktakerdissent: conservative Uncertain: metastasectomy series give 55.4% five-year OS in resected uterine sarcoma (pmid:37063124), but perfusion itself is phase 1 with no human efficacy readout. Moderate (thoracotomy morbidity; acute lung injury is the trial's registered primary endpoint; no published human safety series in this population) Moderate (perfusion injury to already-infiltrated lung; and a full induction spends the anthracycline budget that keeps the door open) The one option in this dossier aimed at cure rather than control, and the one whose anatomic premise her infiltrative bilateral pattern may defeat. 6 Ivonescimab (NCT07516925)endorse: advocatedissent: conservative critic risktaker Low: no sarcoma efficacy data anywhere, and both component axes already failed in uLMS (pmid:25713428, pmid:28440953). HARMONi-2 is an NSCLC result. Moderate (G3+ treatment-related AEs 29% in NSCLC, VEGF-class hypertension and bleeding, G3+ immune-related AEs 7%) Moderate (both mechanisms have already been beaten in this disease; a spent first-line window is the counter-productive outcome) The only seat reachable before cycle 1 by explicit protocol language, and the one four of five personas refused on three mutually independent negative trials.

Also considered — not ranked (39 rows; see the section above for the full list with reasons). The highest-signal entries:

Flag Intervention Likelihood of effect Toxicity burden Counter-productive MoA Overall thin evidence Tazemetostat (conditional on ini1_ihc positive) Low even if INI1 is lost: 9% ORR in the INI1-negative non-epithelioid basket cohort, no uLMS patient reported (pmid:41882006). Low (G3+ treatment-related AEs 10%; anaemia 6%, weight loss 3%; two serious events — one seizure, one haemoptysis) Moderate (EZH2 dependency in SWI/SNF-mutant cancers is largely non-catalytic, so single-agent inhibition may not engage it) Gated on a stain the board expects to come back retained, and even a positive buys a 9% cross-histology response rate. thin evidence REC-617 (CDK7, RB1-negative) Unknown: 15-patient phase 1b with a safety primary endpoint and no efficacy readout. Moderate (no published sarcoma toxicity profile; CDK7-class myelosuppression and gastrointestinal toxicity expected) Low (no mechanism objection raised; the risk is a null first-in-class readout rather than antagonism) The Rb-loss half of a single stain that also routes the abemaciclib seat — free to answer now, with no efficacy data behind it. thin evidence B7-H3 ADCs (MGC026, GSK5764227) Unknown: dose-escalation phase 1 programmes with no sarcoma efficacy readout; target prevalence is high (97% positive, pmid:39478506) but unmeasured here. Moderate (ADC-class myelosuppression, interstitial lung disease risk; no sarcoma-specific grade profile published) Low (antigen-density threshold effects could blunt payload delivery; no mechanism objection raised by the board) The surface target most likely to be present, riding a stain that costs almost nothing — but every accessible programme is a phase 1 with no efficacy data. thin evidence Peposertib + liposomal doxorubicin Unknown: recruiting phase 1 with a dose-finding endpoint and no efficacy readout in any histology. Moderate (DNA-PK inhibitor plus anthracycline; myelosuppression and mucositis expected, no published grade profile) Low (radiosensitiser-class mechanism with no antagonism vector raised; the risk is a spent anthracycline budget) A later-line seat whose 360 mg/m² anthracycline ceiling makes it an induction-planning question rather than a progression question. not enrollable Valemetostat (conditional on ini1_ihc positive) Not enrollable: France-only, and the protocol requires biallelic homozygous SMARCB1 deletion plus central IHC confirmation that a heterozygous plasma call cannot supply. Moderate (EZH1/2 dual inhibition: thrombocytopenia, anaemia, dysgeusia in the lymphoma experience; no solid-tumour profile published) Moderate (same non-catalytic EZH2-dependency problem as tazemetostat, on a target the tissue may not carry) The live SWI/SNF basket that looks like a door and is not: biallelic homozygous deletion required, France only. not enrollable Anlotinib (APROMISS) Low-to-uncertain: ORR 13% overall with an 11-month mPFS in a 26-patient LMS subset that was not prespecified for inference (pmid:29895706). Low (G3+ hypertension 4.8%, triglyceride elevation 3.6%, pneumothorax 2.4%; no treatment-related deaths) Moderate (pneumothorax risk from tumour cavitation in bilateral lung metastases; wound-healing impairment conflicts with metastasectomy) The best-looking VEGFR-TKI subset number in the file, from a non-prespecified 26-patient subgroup, in an arm that is currently suspended. not recommended ATR inhibition (ATRX / ALT hypothesis) Low: the hypothesis was tested in ATRX-mutant LMS with proven target engagement and patients progressed within 4 months (pmid:39453756). Moderate (ATR-inhibitor class myelosuppression; monotherapy profile from the negative phase 2) High (ALT-selective ATR sensitivity failed to replicate; selecting on ATRX rather than SLFN11 is selecting on the wrong marker) The one hypothesis in this case that has already been tested in her histology with the right biomarker and the right pharmacodynamics, and lost. unavailable BRD9 degraders (FHD-609, CFT8634) Not available: both clinical programmes terminated with no successor; no published efficacy from either. Moderate (no case-relevant published toxicity data from either terminated programme) Moderate (preclinical work suggests the bromodomain is the wrong handle in SMARCB1-mutant disease) The second SMARCB1 approach, and it no longer exists — both clinical degraders terminated without a successor.

How to read this table

Toxicity burden is patient-level adverse-event severity (Low / Moderate / High by grade-3+ rates and any treatment-related death). Counter-productive MoA is a different axis: the mechanism-level risk that an intervention works against the therapeutic goal — antigen-loss escape, cell-cycle antagonism of a chemotherapy partner, an anthracycline budget spent before the door that needs it. Those are not patient side effects. The persona pills under each intervention are the at-a-glance board signal; the full per-persona rationale lives on the board page.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence-base caveats. Rank 2 is a 22-patient single-arm phase 2 with open-label response assessment and an unreported randomised confirmation. Rank 3 has no efficacy data at all for its investigational component; its control arm's 35.8% uterine response rate comes from a 42-patient single-arm study, and the randomised comparison that keeps it honest ran the other way. Rank 4 is a 41-patient phase 1 with no patient of her histology in it. Rank 5's survival numbers come from retrospective registries whose selection criteria her current disease does not meet. Rank 6 has zero sarcoma data. The exploratory RAD51 subgroup on rank 2 (11.2 versus 5.4 months, p=0.05, n=18) is not a finding and should not be quoted as one, and the 4-patient BRCA2 series behind rank 39 is tier 4.
  • Biomarker dependencies. Ranks 7, 24, 25, 26 and 40 through 42 assume INI1/SMARCB1 loss confirmed by IHC on tumour tissue; a retained stain forecloses all seven, and the prior for a retained stain is high. Rank 3 assumes intact Rb by IHC; rank 8 assumes the opposite. Rank 4 assumes PRAME positivity on the sponsor's own RT-qPCR, not on a local stain. Rank 2's authorisation case assumes a tissue HRD or HRR result. None of these has been measured, and plasma non-detection at unstated tumour fraction is not a negative for any of them.
  • The performance-status caveat cuts across everything. ECOG 1 was assumed at intake and never scored. Every effect estimate on this page comes from a trial that enrolled ECOG 0-1, so an unmeasured score is an applicability defect inside the numbers rather than a screening formality. If the measured score is 2, a substantial fraction of what this board argued over disappears.
  • What would change the ranking. A confirmed INI1 loss on tissue lifts rank 7 out of the thin-evidence flag and makes the SWI/SNF branch real, though still modest. A tissue homologous-recombination-deficiency result moves rank 2's confidence up materially and strengthens its off-label authorisation. A thoracic surgeon calling the bilateral infiltrative pattern resectable moves rank 5 up sharply, because nothing else here has its ceiling. Publication of the accrued randomised olaparib + temozolomide phase 2/3 would either confirm rank 2 or deflate it. Her answering the trial-and-travel question either way would settle the tension the advocate has flagged on ranks 3, 4 and 6.
  • Re-scoping caveat. Every value in preferences.json is an intake default and the file says so. If she states a toxicity veto, declines travel, or turns out to want gentler therapy than an efficacy weight of 0.7 implies, this ranking changes shape rather than order — and if goals of care turn out to be something other than the maximal-disease-control intent the planned induction implies, several of these rows stop being appropriate to offer at all.

docs.title: Run log
docs.text:
Authored in August 2026 by the PI agent under the two-table contract, from a schema-valid dossier: profile.json, preferences.json, 25 target-validation rows, 15 biomarker-survey rows, 55 trials, 41 clinical-evidence rows, 53 preclinical rows, 26 preclinical-pipeline rows, 64 accessibility rows, and the board's 5 positions plus 20 critiques. This is the Experimental table — non-standard-of-care options only, 45 rows: a rank-1 shared workup gate, five ranked therapeutic options, and 39 rows flagged by surfaced_reason (12 thin-evidence, 16 not-enrollable, 4 unavailable, 3 consolidated). Endorsement, dissent and agreement scores were computed from round-1 picks and round-2 critique agreement levels; no persona issued a formal veto in either round, so no veto was overridden. On ivonescimab I counted the conservative's and the critic's explicit written refusals in their round-1 notes as dissent alongside the risktaker's formal round-2 critique, because counting only the formal critique would have understated a 4-to-1 refusal — that departure from the mechanical rule is documented on the row itself.

Therapies routed to the Standard-of-care table, which has not yet been generated for this case: doxorubicin + trabectedin with trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04) — the board's rank 1 on four of five slates and the only randomised OS result in this histology; gemcitabine + docetaxel; doxorubicin + ifosfamide; single-agent trabectedin; pazopanib; eribulin; gemcitabine + dacarbazine; single-agent temozolomide; gemcitabine/docetaxel ± bevacizumab (GOG-0250, the negative arm); pulmonary metastasectomy; lung SBRT; and the biomarker-gated tumour-agnostic routes pembrolizumab, dostarlimab and larotrectinib. Routing is not rejection. Because the standard-of-care screen has not run, check_pipeline.py currently reports a two-table coverage failure naming five of these (eribulin, pazopanib, trabectedin, and the trabectedin and anthracycline mechanism rows); running /standard_of_care_screener closes it. The remaining routed therapies already match a rec-table label on shared tokens.

Biomarker gating: several biomarkers are non-confirmed (SMARCB1 ihc_pending, TP53 ngs_pending, MAGE-A4 / PRAME / NY-ESO-1 / PD-L1 ihc_pending, RB1 / ATRX / MED12 / HRD / NTRK / TMB / MSI ngs_pending). The one-dimension cap selected INI1/SMARCB1 for :positive tagging, following the profile's own instruction to branch on that status; seven rows carry ini1_ihc:positive. The other pending biomarkers are carried as open_questions[] on the relevant rows and in the caveats rather than as parallel branches, and no negative-branch ranking was emitted. Reference verification ran over every identifier promoted into recommendations.jsonl and this page: 47 PMIDs re-resolved live against PubMed with matching titles, journals and years and no retraction publication types, and 12 key NCT identifiers re-resolved against ClinicalTrials.gov with matching titles and recruitment statuses. Nothing was corrected and nothing was nulled. The known-bad pmid:32891273 is absent from every file in this case. No new references were introduced beyond those already in the dossier.

docs.title: 1. Olaparib + temozolomide Lynparza, AZD2281, Temodar, TMZ, NCI 10250
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-24

Both drugs are approved and prescribable, and the uterine leiomyosarcoma phase 2 that generated the signal reported a real response rate, but both trials of this combination are now closed to accrual. So the only live route is an off-label prescription, and that request will go much better with a tissue HRD or HRR result in hand than with the current plasma panel, which does not settle homologous recombination status.

RegulatoryOlaparib (Lynparza) FDA-approved in BRCA-mutated ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancers. Temozolomide approved in glioma. Neither is approved in sarcoma. Geographic scopeOff-label US-wide; both trials closed to enrolment

Next steps

  1. Send tissue order A (DNA plus RNA comprehensive profiling with an HRD or genomic-instability score) before anything else; it is the gate on this whole branch.
  2. Order the germline homologous-recombination panel alongside rather than reflexively after a somatic finding.
  3. Re-check NCT05432791 site status at progression; a 145-site cooperative-group study can reopen.
  4. If pursuing off-label, call AstraZeneca medical information at 1-800-236-9933 and build the file around the tissue HRD result plus the NCI 10250 uLMS data.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT038800192advanced uterine leiomyosarcomaactive not recruitingeligible: notrial sitesClosed to accrual. 15 US sites. This is the study that produced the uLMS response signal. NCT054327912/3uterine leiomyosarcoma after chemotherapy failureactive not recruitingeligible: notrial sitesClosed to accrual, 145 US and Puerto Rico sites. Would have been the natural post-induction landing spot. Worth one confirmatory call to the NCI trial referral line in case a site reopens.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact
