Payer / coverage notes. Olaparib off-label in sarcoma is a hard sell without a documented HRR alteration or HRD score. A somatic BRCA1/2 or high genomic-instability result on tissue changes the conversation entirely, which is one more reason tissue order A should go out now rather than after induction.

Notes. Post-induction option. Nothing here is reachable in the first-line window except the tissue testing that gates it.

docs.title: 4. Abemaciclib + gemcitabine and docetaxel Verzenio, LY2835219, abemaciclib-gemcitabine, abemaciclib, gemcitabine, docetaxel
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-24

Supersedes the earlier access row for this intervention, adding the eligibility gate that row missed: entry requires intact Rb expression by immunohistochemistry on the baseline biopsy or archived tumour, assessed at MD Anderson with a CLIA-certified antibody. That is the exact opposite gate from the RB1-negative CDK7 protocol at the same institution, so one Rb stain on the tissue-order-B block routes her between the two trials: Rb intact points here, Rb lost points to REC-617 after a first line. The first-line opening stands, and so does the trap: the phase 2 portion admits systemic-treatment-naive patients, prior gemcitabine is disqualifying, and the ECOG ceiling is 2.

RegulatoryAbemaciclib (Verzenio) FDA-approved in HR-positive HER2-negative breast cancer. No sarcoma indication. Gemcitabine and docetaxel are generic. Geographic scopeUnited States; single site, MD Anderson, Houston TX

Next steps

  1. Order Rb by IHC on the tissue-order-B block now. One stain routes her between this trial (Rb intact, first-line eligible today) and REC-617 (Rb lost, after one prior line). The block cut was already priced; this adds no tissue cost, only the instruction to read the result against both protocols.
  2. Call MD Anderson at 866-632-6789 and ask whether the site's own G3-245 assay must be run or a CLIA outside result is accepted, and whether the treatment-naive stratum is open.
  3. Do this before any gemcitabine-containing regimen; prior gemcitabine closes the phase 2 permanently. LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine and preserves eligibility.
  4. Document the ECOG; ceiling 2.
  5. Plan Houston travel and ask about screening turnaround against the LMS-04 start date.

docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: cell_therapy   Verified: 2026-08-24

This is recruiting, it is open in the US, and it accepts solid tumours generally rather than a fixed histology list, which makes it the most reachable engineered-cell option in the dossier. Two things stand between her and it: PRAME expression must be confirmed on Immatics' own RT-qPCR assay, and the protocol requires patients to have received or be ineligible for all available indicated standard-of-care treatment, which reads as post-induction rather than first-line. ECOG ceiling is 0-1, so the undocumented performance status matters here too.

  1. Email ctgovinquiries@immatics.com now, before induction, with two questions: does uterine leiomyosarcoma fall inside the current solid-tumour cohorts, and does 'received or not eligible for all available indicated standard of care' allow a patient who has declined first-line therapy.
  2. Ask in the same message how PRAME screening is initiated and whether archival tissue from a 2024 resection is acceptable input for IMADetect.
  3. Document the ECOG; this protocol caps at 0-1 and an assumed score will not screen.
  4. Order PRAME as part of tissue order C so a local result is in hand when the sponsor assay is discussed.
  5. Ask about resting room-air oxygen saturation requirements and flag the 8,500 ft residence in that first message.

The MSK protocol nominally asks for one to three prior lines, but the criteria carry an explicit carve-out: patients who decline standard first-line systemic therapy are eligible, and the performance-status ceiling is ECOG 0-2 rather than 0-1. That makes it reachable now, before LMS-04, and it is the only investigational option in the dossier where declining induction is written into the protocol rather than argued around it. The cost is geography: all seven sites are Memorial Sloan Kettering locations in New York and New Jersey, and she lives at roughly 8,500 ft on the other side of the country.

docs.title: 27. Tazemetostat Tazverik, EPZ-6438, E7438, tazemetostat-ezh2, smarcb1-ini1-target-biology
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-24

Tazverik is approved in epithelioid sarcoma, not uterine leiomyosarcoma, so every route here is off-label or trial-based cross-histology extrapolation. The gate is INI1 IHC on tumour tissue: a plasma SMARCB1 frameshift is a hypothesis, and no payer and no trial will act on it. Both tazemetostat expanded-access programs are listed as no longer available, so if INI1 loss is confirmed the realistic path is an off-label prescription with an appeal built on the INI1-negative basket data.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (accelerated) for metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection in patients 16 and older, and for relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma. Not approved in leiomyosarcoma. GuidelinesNCCN recognition is in epithelioid sarcoma; off-guideline for uterine leiomyosarcoma Geographic scopeUS-wide as an off-label prescription; no open expanded-access program

Next steps

  1. Order INI1/SMARCB1 IHC (BAF47 clone) on tumour tissue as part of tissue order B. That single stain decides whether this branch exists.
  2. Order it on both the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 pulmonary core; discordance between primary and metastasis is a known problem and one negative on a small core is not reassuring.
  3. If INI1 is lost, call Epizyme/Ipsen medical information at 855-463-5127 and ask what managed-access or named-patient route currently exists, since both registered expanded-access programs are closed.
  4. In parallel, ask about NCT07303387 (valemetostat), which requires a bi-allelic homozygous deletion her plasma frameshift does not establish.
  5. If INI1 is intact, close this branch and say so in the record rather than leaving it open.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT026019502INI1-negative and SWI/SNF-altered soft tissue sarcomacompletedeligible: notrial sitesClosed. The registration cohort plus the INI1-negative basket cohorts; the evidence to cite in an off-label appeal, not an enrolment route. NCT03874455—solid tumours on the sponsor's eligible-condition listno longer availableeligible: notrial sitesListed on the registry as no longer available. Checked so the reader can see the expanded-access door was tried and is shut. NCT04225429—epithelioid sarcomano longer availableeligible: notrial sitesAlso no longer available, and epithelioid-sarcoma-only in any case.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyEpizyme, Inc., an Ipsen Company CountryFrance (Ipsen); US operations Cambridge, MA Medical info phone855-463-5127 NotesPhone taken verbatim from the current Tazverik FDA label: 'For more information, contact Epizyme at 855-463-5127.' No separate compassionate-use email was verifiable this run; ask the medical information line for the current managed-access route.

Payer / coverage notes. Off-label EZH2 inhibition in uLMS is expensive and will be reviewed carefully. A documented loss of nuclear INI1 staining, ideally on both the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 lung core, is what makes the appeal arguable. Without it there is no filing worth making.

Notes. The load-bearing honesty in this case: SMARCB1 loss is uncommon in uterine leiomyosarcoma, and the call came from plasma at unstated variant fraction. The prior is low, the confirmatory test is cheap, and the branch should not be priced as if it were already true.

docs.title: 28. Valemetostat tosylate (EZH1/EZH2 dual inhibitor) DS-3201, Ezharmia, valemetostat
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Not yet accessible Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-24

The trial route for the SWI/SNF branch is a Gustave Roussy basket study, and it is stricter than the tazemetostat data: it requires a documented bi-allelic homozygous deletion of SMARCB1 by validated NGS plus centrally confirmed loss of expression by IHC. A single plasma frameshift does not meet that. It is also France-only, four sites, with an ECOG 0-1 ceiling and a maximum of one prior treatment line in the SMARCB1 cohort.

RegulatoryApproved in Japan (Ezharmia) for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma and peripheral T-cell lymphoma. No FDA or EMA approval; investigational in solid tumours. Geographic scopeFrance only as registered; no US site

Next steps

  1. Confirm a US or EU site is accepting international patients before anything else. As registered this is a France-only study and she is US-based.
  2. Email Dr Postel-Vinay at SOPHIE.POSTEL-VINAY@gustaveroussy.fr to ask whether a truncating SMARCB1 frameshift with confirmed INI1 loss by IHC can substitute for a documented homozygous deletion. That single answer decides whether the trial is even theoretically open to her.
  3. Order the tissue NGS and INI1 IHC now; both are prerequisites for any version of this conversation.
  4. Note the one-prior-line cap: after LMS-04 induction she would still be within it, but only just.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT073033872SWI/SNF-defective solid tumours, cohort 1.A SMARCB1-defectiverecruitingeligible: noSophie Postel-Vinay, MD, PhDSOPHIE.POSTEL-VINAY@gustaveroussy.fr+33142114343trial sitesFour sites, all in France. Criterion 8 requires bi-allelic (homozygous) deletion by validated NGS and centrally confirmed loss of expression by IHC. Cohort 1.A allows a maximum of one prior treatment line, so if she enrolled it would have to be either now or immediately after induction. ECOG 0-1.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

No manufacturer information captured.

Payer / coverage notes. Not a payer question. Study drug is supplied on trial; the cost is travel and the screening biopsy work.

Notes. A reader scanning the trial table sees a recruiting SMARCB1 study and assumes a door. The bi-allelic homozygous deletion requirement and the France-only geography are both hard, and her plasma frameshift satisfies neither.

docs.text:

docs.title: 34. CDR404 (MAGE-A4 x CD3 T-cell engager) CDR404, MAGE-A4xCD3
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: bispecific_antibody   Verified: 2026-08-24

Recruiting, open at US sites, and it takes MAGE-A4-expressing solid tumours in HLA-A*02:01 patients rather than a fixed histology list. Because it is an antibody-format engager rather than a cell product, there is no leukapheresis or manufacturing lead time. The blockers are MAGE-A4 expression, which is unmeasured, and an ECOG 0-1 ceiling against an undocumented score.

  3. Order MAGE-A4 as part of tissue order C now; a stain that takes one to two weeks is the difference between screening in this window and screening after induction.
  4. Document the ECOG.

docs.title: 35. Afamitresgene autoleucel (MAGE-A4 TCR-T, TECELRA) TECELRA, ADP-A2M4, afami-cel, afamitresgene-magea4-tcrt, ct-antigen-target-biology
docs.text:
Access status: Off-label use Not yet accessible Modality: cell_therapy   Verified: 2026-08-24

Her HLA-A*02:01 clears the allele gate, but TECELRA's label is synovial sarcoma only, and uterine leiomyosarcoma is outside it. An autologous engineered T-cell product is not something a clinician writes off-label the way they would a tablet: authorised treatment centres order it against the label indication and its companion diagnostics. Record this as a closed on-label door for her rather than an option awaiting a MAGE-A4 stain.

RegulatoryFDA-approved (TECELRA) for adults and patients 12 and older with unresectable or metastatic synovial sarcoma who have received prior chemotherapy, are HLA-A*02:01P/02:02P/02:03P/02:06P positive, and whose tumour expresses MAGE-A4 by an FDA-approved or cleared companion diagnostic. Label revised mid-2026 with the accelerated-approval statement removed. GuidelinesRecognised in synovial sarcoma; no leiomyosarcoma recommendation Geographic scopeUS authorised treatment centres, synovial sarcoma only

Next steps

  1. Do not present this as an open option on the strength of the HLA type alone. The allele is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.
  2. If MAGE-A4 IHC is being ordered anyway as part of tissue order C, order it for the trial-based MAGE-A4 programs (CDR404, and the SURPASS product if it reopens), not for TECELRA.
  3. Call USWM at 1-855-246-9232 only if a non-synovial cohort or a new protocol opens.

docs.title: 36. Uzatresgene autoleucel (ADP-A2M4CD8), alone or with nivolumab or pembrolizumab ADP-A2M4CD8, SURPASS, uzatresgene
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Not yet accessible Modality: cell_therapy   Verified: 2026-08-24

SURPASS is the MAGE-A4 TCR-T study that admits tumour types beyond synovial sarcoma, and it is closed to accrual. It also carries the criterion that recurs across this whole class and matters most in her case: at least 90% room-air oxygen saturation at rest, measured at screening and again at baseline. At 8,500 ft a resting room-air saturation in the high 80s can be physiologically normal, and the cell-therapy protocols in this class write the criterion as an absolute number with no altitude clause. Get the oximetry done and recorded with the altitude noted, and raise the interpretation with the sponsor's medical monitor before screening rather than after a failed check.

RegulatoryInvestigational; no approval anywhere. Geographic scopeUS, Canada, Spain; closed to new enrolment

Next steps

  1. Confirm with USWM at 1-855-246-9232 whether any SURPASS cohort is reopening; the registry status is 'active, not recruiting' rather than terminated.
  2. Get resting and exertional oximetry at her home altitude and record the altitude with the value, so the >= 90% criterion can be discussed with a medical monitor on facts rather than on a sea-level reading taken during a specialist visit.
  3. Document the ECOG; this protocol caps at 0-1.
  4. Order MAGE-A4 IHC as part of tissue order C only if a MAGE-A4 program is actually open to her.

Trial pathways

NCTPhaseIndicationStatusPatient eligibleCentral contactNotes NCT040448591HLA-A*02-positive, MAGE-A4-expressing solid tumoursactive not recruitingeligible: notrial sitesClosed to accrual. 17 sites in the US, Canada and Spain. Requires an HLA-A*02 inclusion allele (she has A*02:01), central-laboratory-confirmed MAGE-A4 expression, ECOG 0-1, and >= 90% room-air oxygen saturation at rest within 7 days of leukapheresis and again at baseline.

Manufacturer / sponsor contact

CompanyUSWM CT, LLC (US WorldMeds); developed by Adaptimmune Therapeutics CountryUnited States; originator United Kingdom Medical info phone1-855-246-9232 NotesPhone from the TECELRA label; USWM is the registered sponsor for the SURPASS protocol.

Notes. The 90% room-air saturation criterion is a class-wide feature, not a quirk of this protocol. It applies to the cell-therapy programs generally and is the single criterion most likely to be misread in a patient adapted to 8,500 ft.

docs.title: 37. B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates (MGC026; GSK5764227/HS-20093) MGC026, GSK5764227, HS-20093, risvutatug rezetecan, CD276, B7-H3

docs.title: 39. Tuvusertib (ATR inhibitor) + temozolomide tuvusertib, M1774, temozolomide, Temodar
docs.text:
Access status: Clinical trial Modality: small_molecule   Verified: 2026-08-24

The one live US ATR seat. The NCI dose-escalation arm admits extracranial solid tumours where temozolomide is guideline-standard, which covers soft-tissue sarcoma without requiring an MGMT result, and the ECOG ceiling is 2. It requires progression on, intolerance of, or refusal of available therapies, so in practice it opens after LMS-04. Two sequencing traps sit upstream: prior temozolomide is disqualifying, so an off-label olaparib plus temozolomide line would close this door, and the ATR-for-ALT rationale should be priced as unproven in her histology, because the ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma monotherapy cohort progressed within 4 months despite biopsy-proven target engagement.

RegulatoryTuvusertib investigational; no approval anywhere. Temozolomide FDA-approved in glioma, generic. Geographic scopeUnited States; 23 sites

Next steps

  1. After LMS-04, call the nearest recruiting site (UC Irvine 877-827-8839, Yale 203-785-5702, or Kansas 913-588-3671) and confirm the dose-escalation arm is still open to sarcoma; the phase 2 portion is colorectal-only and the arm structure decides whether a seat exists.
  2. Keep temozolomide out of any off-label interim plan if this seat is being held; prior temozolomide is disqualifying.
  3. Include ATRX in tissue order A regardless. It does not gate this trial's entry, but it determines whether the ALT rationale for choosing this seat over other 2L options has any footing.
  4. Document the ECOG; ceiling 2.

The sarcoma-eligible arm is the dose escalation; the phase 2 portion is mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancer only, so confirm the escalation is still enrolling before travelling. Registry criteria admit patients who 'refuse standard treatment', which is worth one clarifying call, though the realistic fit is post-induction. ECOG <= 2. Prior temozolomide is excluded.

docs.title: 45. Documented ECOG performance status performance status, ECOG PS, Karnofsky, ecog-performance-status-documentation
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: diagnostic   Verified: 2026-08-24

The ECOG of 1 in this record is an intake assumption, never a measured score, and it is the single most widely load-bearing missing item in the dossier. Protocols with an ECOG 0-1 ceiling include the valemetostat, IMA203, CDR404, ADCE-D01, ZL-6201, zanzalintinib, anlotinib and all three FAP radioligand studies. A clinician writing a number in the chart at the next visit is an access action, and it costs nothing.

  2. Record it alongside resting and exertional oximetry taken at her home altitude, with the altitude stated on the result.

Both drugs are stocked at any sarcoma infusion center, so delivery is not the problem. The problem is the label: Yondelis is approved for leiomyosarcoma only after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen, and she is anthracycline-naive, so the planned first-line pairing is off-label prescribing carried by the LMS-04 phase 3 result. Build the prior authorization as an off-label first-line request from the outset rather than filing it and waiting for the denial.

Geographic scopeUS-wide; any sarcoma-capable infusion center

Next steps

  1. Document an ECOG score at the next clinic visit. It is undocumented, it gates most of the trial options in this dossier, and it costs nothing.
  2. Get the baseline echocardiogram with LVEF, hepatic and renal panels, CBC read against altitude-adjusted haemoglobin references, and PFTs with DLCO and resting oximetry measured at her home altitude.
  3. File the trabectedin prior authorization as an off-label first-line request citing LMS-04, before cycle 1 rather than after a denial.
  4. Arrange central venous access; trabectedin runs as a 24-hour infusion.
  5. For label or coverage questions call Janssen medical information at 1-800-526-7736.

docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: surgery   Verified: 2026-08-24

Standard practice at any thoracic surgical centre and covered as such, with the registry data in sarcoma coming from series rather than randomised trials. Her consulting oncologist has already kept local therapy on the table after systemic control. The open question is anatomic, not administrative: bilateral disease described as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory may not be resectable, and a thoracic surgeon should look at the images early rather than after six cycles.

RegulatoryNot a drug; standard surgical practice. GuidelinesNCCN soft tissue sarcoma recognises resection of limited pulmonary metastases in selected patients Geographic scopeUS-wide at thoracic surgical centres

Next steps

  1. Get a thoracic surgical opinion on the current imaging now, not after induction. Whether she is ever a resection candidate changes how the systemic plan is framed.
  2. Ask the surgeon explicitly about the infiltrative radiologic pattern and whether it changes resectability.
  3. Request the September 2024 operative report while arranging the block release; whether morcellation occurred bears on surveillance.

docs.title: 59. Tissue order A: one comprehensive tumour DNA + RNA profile tissue NGS, comprehensive genomic profiling, whole exome plus whole transcriptome, smarcb1-tissue-ngs-concurrent, hrr-somatic-ngs-hrd-score, ntrk-rna-fusion-panel, tmb-tissue-validated-cgp
docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: diagnostic   Verified: 2026-08-24

One requisition on archival tissue that settles TMB, MSI, the homologous-recombination gene set with a genomic-instability score, NTRK and RET fusion calling, RB1, ATRX, MED12, TSC1/TSC2, and tissue confirmation of the plasma TP53 and SMARCB1 calls. It gates the olaparib branch, the tumour-agnostic checkpoint claims, the TRK branch and the CDK7 trial all at once. Ordering these serially instead of together is how a first-line window gets spent.

RegulatoryComprehensive genomic profiling on FFPE is routine clinical testing; several of the assays carry FDA approval as companion diagnostics. Geographic scopeUS-wide; specimens ship to the reference laboratory

Next steps

  1. Request release of the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 pulmonary core from the outside institution today. This is the slow step, it is administrative rather than clinical, and it sits in front of every other test in this dossier.
  2. Send one requisition, not several. Specify DNA plus RNA, TMB and MSI reporting, an HRD or genomic-instability score, fusion calling, and explicit reporting of SMARCB1, TP53, RB1, ATRX, MED12, TSC1 and TSC2.
  3. Use the 2026 lung core as the RNA input where possible; RNA quality degrades in blocks older than about five years.
  4. Ask the laboratory for expedited handling and tell them the patient is pre-treatment with induction pending. Turnaround is quoted at two to three weeks and that is the whole first-line window.
  5. Order the germline homologous-recombination panel in parallel rather than reflexing to it after a somatic finding.

docs.text:
Access status: Standard of care Modality: diagnostic   Verified: 2026-08-24

Seven stains off a single block cut, all of them routine, all of them fast once the block is in hand. INI1 is the one that decides whether the entire SMARCB1 branch exists. MMR opens or closes dostarlimab. Rb decides the CDK7 trial. B7-H3 tells her whether the ADC class has a target. Turnaround is three to five days per the target validator; the delay is the block release, not the laboratory.

RegulatoryRoutine diagnostic immunohistochemistry; PD-L1 assays carry companion-diagnostic status for specific agents. Geographic scopeUS-wide; reference laboratory or the treating institution's own pathology department

Next steps

  1. Order all seven stains on one requisition against the same block cut. Serial ordering is the failure mode here.
  2. Order INI1 on both the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 pulmonary core. Primary-versus-metastasis discordance is a known problem and a single negative core is not reassuring.
  3. Read B7-H3 on the larger 2024 resection rather than the lung core alone; expression is spatially heterogeneous.
  4. Ask the pathology laboratory to score INI1 against the internal positive control and to state the control explicitly in the report.
  5. Tell the laboratory that induction is pending; three to five days is achievable and worth asking for.

Three stains off one block cut, and they only make sense together. Her HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed, which means the allele half of TCR-T and ImmTAC eligibility is already done; this is the other half. A local positive is a reason to approach a sponsor, not a substitute for the sponsor's own assay, and every program in this class re-tests on its own device at screening.

docs.title: Selected general biomarker report — ulms-highgrade-pulm-mets-tp53-smarcb1-hla-a2-w9t4
docs.text: Which biomarkers on the selected panel this patient has been tested for, and which have never been measured. The panel covers targets established in this tumor type, targets relevant across a subset of tumor types, and biomarkers that predict benefit regardless of where the tumor started, such as MSI-H/dMMR and high tumor mutational burden gating PD-1 blockade.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Selected general biomarker report (offline HTML) — the same survey, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Selected general biomarker report (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by recommended action

18 biomarkers in scope: 15 with no usable result on file (2 essential), 2 measured but not to decision resolution, 1 already established. A further 63 panel entries were assessed against this tumor and set aside. Panel coverage: 9 tumor-agnostic biomarkers plus 9 of 72 protein targets in scope for this tumor.

Eighteen biomarkers were in scope for this tumor. Fifteen have no result at all, two were measured short of decision grade, one is settled. Four gaps are essential: MSI/dMMR, tumor mutational burden, NTRK fusion, and homologous recombination with BRCA status. The other 63 panel entries were assessed against this tumor and set aside, with reasons at the foot of the page.

Plasma against tissue is the distinction doing the work. The Guardant tumor fraction was never supplied, so its non-detections exclude nothing. NTRK and HR/BRCA are logged as measured but not hardened: a plasma negative exists for each. MSI and TMB stayed unmeasured: the plasma assay returned no call, so there is nothing to harden.

HLA class I typing is the one settled row, and typing is not eligibility. A confirmed A*02:01 turns MAGE-A4, PRAME and NY-ESO-1 into live expression questions, all three off one archival block. Leiomyosarcoma runs well below synovial sarcoma for MAGE-A4 and NY-ESO-1; PRAME is the likeliest of the three.

Three bundles and one blood draw carry nearly every actionable row: comprehensive tissue DNA plus RNA profiling, an IHC block led by INI1, the cancer/testis stain set, and a germline HR panel. Nothing here needs a fresh biopsy, and no biopsy or cost preference was recorded at intake. Every tissue order waits on release of the September 2024 outside-institution block, the rate-limiting step; with LMS-04 pending, ordering in series costs weeks. INI1 is the stain that would move the plasma SMARCB1 finding from hypothesis to actionable, against a hard prior: 170 consecutive uterine smooth-muscle tumors all retained SMARCB1. Eight rows hand off to the target-validation track.

Most of this testing will come back negative. What justifies running it is the size of the option a positive would open, not any expectation that one is coming.

docs.title: What this collapses to
docs.text:
The gaps above resolve onto this many distinct orders. Biomarkers that ride along on the same assay are grouped together.

  • Single archival block cut for the IHC set: INI1/SMARCB1, MMR (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), PD-L1, HER2 and B7-H3 — B7-H3 (CD276) protein expression, HER2 (ERBB2) protein expression, Microsatellite instability / mismatch-repair deficiency (MSI-H / dMMR), PD-L1 protein expression
  • Cancer/testis antigen IHC set (MAGE-A4, PRAME, NY-ESO-1) on one archival block, now unconditional because HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed — MAGE-A4 expression (HLA-A02:01-restricted), NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) expression, HLA-A02:01-restricted, PRAME expression (HLA-A*02:01-restricted)
  • Comprehensive tissue DNA plus RNA genomic profiling on archival tumor tissue, the single order that also returns TMB, MSI, NTRK and RET fusions, BRAF codon 600, the HR genes, the RB1 / ATRX / MED12 backbone of this histology, and tissue confirmation of the plasma TP53 and SMARCB1 calls — BRAF V600E mutation, RET gene fusion, Tumor mutational burden, high (TMB-H)
  • PSMA PET/CT, only if a PSMA-selected sarcoma protocol becomes available to her — PSMA (FOLH1) expression, tumor cell and tumor neovasculature
  • Single archival block cut for the IHC set: INI1/SMARCB1, MMR (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), PD-L1, HER2 and B7-H3; ERBB2 copy number also comes off the comprehensive tissue NGS panel — HER2 protein overexpression (IHC 3+)
  • The archival IHC block if a FAP-directed program comes into play; otherwise the trial's own screening assay — FAP (fibroblast activation protein) expression
  • Would ride on the archival IHC block if an AXL-directed program required documented expression — AXL receptor tyrosine kinase expression
  • Would ride on the cancer/testis antigen block already being cut for MAGE-A4, PRAME and NY-ESO-1 — MAGE-C2 (MAGEC2) expression, HLA class I presented

Reading this report

This page answers one question per biomarker: has this patient been tested for it, and was the test at a resolution that can carry a treatment decision. Not measured means nothing is on file, which is not the same as a negative result. Measured, not decision-grade means a result exists but cannot be acted on as it stands; those gaps are worked into the Target validation paths report. Priority weighs what is going unassessed against how routine the assay is. Most of these biomarkers will be negative if tested; the case for testing rests on the size of the option that opens if positive, not on how likely a positive is.

Back to case · Target validation · Recommendations · Trials · Evidence · Board

Decision support, not medical advice

Libby is experimental. An unmeasured biomarker on this page is a gap in the record, not a prediction that the patient carries it. Assay availability, current approval status, and whether any of this testing is worth the tissue are decisions for the treating team. See PHI policy.

docs.title: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine/docetaxel, randomised phase 2 (NCT06498648, MD Anderson) (abemaciclib-gemcitabine-docetaxel)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowThe hedge seat, and the only investigational protocol in this file that stays open on both sides of induction: phase 2 admits treatment-naive patients today, and LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine, so eligibility survives standard induction. The backbone carries real first-line uLMS activity (ORR 35.8% in the GOG phase 2), and abemaciclib on top is the unproven upside. One stain routes everything: entry requires intact Rb by IHC, untested, and the same result decides between this protocol and the Rb-loss CDK7 study. Order the stain now; holding the seat costs nothing.Rb status unmeasured; a plasma non-report at unknown tumor fraction is not a negative; No efficacy data for the abemaciclib combination itself; taking this seat first-line would trade an HR 0.41 regimen for an unproven add-on; Overlapping myelosuppression if sequenced straight after LMS-04 conservative3lowIf prefers_trials is going to mean anything in the first-line window, this is the seat I can defend: a standard cytotoxic backbone at a sarcoma center, with abemaciclib carrying a breast-cancer label since 2017 and mature algorithms for its diarrhea and neutropenia. The missing safety datum is specific and worth naming: nobody has published tolerability data for abemaciclib layered on gemcitabine and docetaxel, overlapping myelosuppression is the obvious worry, and this study's phase 1 portion is the first place that combination gets characterized. The randomised phase 2 design means the control arm is the standard backbone, so a seat here cannot leave her worse off than my rank-2 fallback. Contingent on three measurements nobody has made: intact Rb by IHC, a documented ECOG of 2 or better, and confirmation from the site that the treatment-naive stratum is open.Rb IHC has not been done; the same stain routes her here if Rb is intact or toward the CDK7 protocol (NCT07633756, after one prior line) if Rb is lost; Combination myelosuppression is uncharacterized outside this study's own phase 1 portion; Single site in Houston, and screening turnaround has to beat the LMS-04 start date critic4lowThe one first-line trial seat I can defend, and only because of its design: the phase 2 component randomises against gem-doc, so the worst case inside the trial is standard therapy. Abemaciclib itself has essentially no efficacy data in leiomyosarcoma, and the phase 1 endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase time course, so no one should enrol expecting a proven drug. Eligibility currently rests on two unmeasured facts: intact Rb by IHC, a stain she has not had, and an ECOG nobody has scored. Screening costs a stain; enrolling costs the LMS-04 window, and that trade should be named out loud before consent.No abemaciclib efficacy data in LMS; CDK4/6 blockade added to chemotherapy is an unvalidated hypothesis in this histology; Rb IHC not performed; eligibility is unknowable today; Randomised phase 2 with a PFS endpoint cannot answer the OS question LMS-04 already answered; Enrolment forfeits first-line LMS-04; that is the real cost of the seat concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowThe quiet virtue here is that LMS-04 does not close it: the phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive patients and the disqualifier is prior gemcitabine, which the planned induction does not contain. So this is the branch she keeps whichever way she answers the first question, which is what earns it a place on a preferences-driven list rather than a pure-efficacy one. Entry needs intact Rb by IHC read on MD Anderson's own antibody, a stain she has not had. Single site in Houston, so the travel question lands here too, just later.Eligibility is unconfirmed until the Rb stain reads out. A plasma panel reporting no RB1 alteration settles nothing at an unstated tumor fraction.; Ask MD Anderson whether an outside CLIA Rb result is accepted or the site must run its own G3-245 assay, since that changes the timeline.; If anyone gives gemcitabine and docetaxel off-protocol as her first line, this closes for good.; No efficacy readout exists yet; the phase 1 endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase time course, so she would be trading a published OS benefit for a pharmacodynamic study.

docs.title: Olaparib + temozolomide (planned second line, HRD testing ordered now) (olaparib-temozolomide)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker2lowThe strongest targeted signal anyone has produced in her exact histology: best ORR 27% (6 of 22) and mPFS 6.9 months, with the primary endpoint met and no HRD requirement for entry. The upside case is sharper: RAD51-deficient tumours (9 of 18 assayed) ran mPFS 11.2 months against 5.4 for the HR-proficient, and a genomic series reported 4 of 4 BRCA2-lost uLMS patients with durable benefit on PARP inhibition. Her HRD and BRCA status is the highest-yield unmeasured item in this case; order the tissue testing now so the pivot is loaded before first progression, not after. The subgroup is exploratory at n=18, and I'll take that bet.Requires a prior line, so it cannot fill the first-line window; everything hinges on block release from the 2024 outside institution, the stated rate-limiting step; HRD/BRCA status unmeasured; if she lands in the HR-proficient half, expected mPFS is 5.4 months; G3/4 neutropenia 75% on a marrow that will have just absorbed LMS-04 conservative4lowThis is my second-line plan, ranked now so the tissue work that gates it goes out today rather than at progression: overall best ORR 27% (6 of 22; primary-endpoint ORR 23%) and mPFS 6.9 months in exactly her histology, with the randomised confirmation (NCT05432791) fully accrued. Toxicity is heavy on paper, G3/4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, but the study managed it with dose modification and reported no treatment-related deaths, and both drugs have long individual prescribing histories. The exploratory RAD51 split (mPFS 11.2 vs 5.4 months) is why her unmeasured HRD and BRCA status matters; the archival-block NGS with an HRD score should ride the same block release as everything else. A 22-patient single-arm study holds a plan, not a promise.n=22, single-arm; the phase 2/3 read-out could deflate the signal; HRD and BRCA status unmeasured; without the tissue result the off-label prior-authorization case is weak and the responding-subset question stays open; Both trials of the combination are closed to accrual, so the only live route today is off-label critic3lowThe best histology-matched signal in the file, stated precisely: a 22-patient single-arm phase 2 that met its prespecified primary endpoint (5 of 22 responses within 6 months, design 93% power at alpha 0.06), overall ORR 27%, mPFS 6.9 months. The RAD51-HRD split everyone quotes, 11.2 vs 5.4 months at p=0.05 in 18 assayed patients, is exploratory and carries no weight with me until the randomised phase 2/3 (NCT05432791, accrued, unreported) says otherwise. Entry required a prior line, so this lives after induction, not instead of it. Ordering tissue HRD and BRCA testing now is cheap and makes the later decision an informed one.ROBINS-I moderate: single-arm, no comparator, open-label response assessment; The RAD51 subgroup is exploratory at p=0.05 in 18 patients and must not be quoted as if prespecified; Grade 3-4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, arriving in marrow already hit by LMS-04's 80% and 47%; Her HRD and BRCA2 status is unmeasured; the 4-patient BRCA2 series (pmid:30541756) is tier 4 and cannot carry a selection claim concensusite4lowThe strongest post-induction signal in her exact histology: NCI Protocol 10250 met its prespecified primary endpoint in advanced uterine LMS with median PFS 6.9 months, and entry did not require HRD, so her unmeasured HRD status does not gate it. It is also the pick where I sit furthest ahead of settled carriage, since ESMO 2021 predates the trial and I could not confirm NCCN listing this run, which is why it holds rank 4 rather than 2. Both trials of the combination are closed to accrual, so the live route is off-label prescription of two approved drugs.Off-label authorization will go better with tissue HRR/HRD results than with a plasma panel that settles nothing. Tissue NGS on the archival block gates that, and the block release is the delay.; Post-induction positioning only. Nothing on this branch is reachable in the first-line window except the tissue testing. advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: Ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific), MSK single-arm phase 2 (ivonescimab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowThis is the one protocol in the dossier that writes down what she might actually want: declining standard first-line therapy is an explicit eligibility route, and the ECOG ceiling of 2 tolerates a score nobody has measured. I am not going to move her across the country on it. Anti-VEGF added to first-line chemotherapy bought nothing in her exact disease in GOG-0250, single-agent PD-1 was stopped for futility at 12 uLMS patients, and ivonescimab has no published sarcoma efficacy at all, only a head-to-head PFS win in lung cancer. Worth the phone call this week because the seat closes when LMS-04 starts, and worth taking only if she tells us that repeated flights from 8,500 ft to Manhattan are something she wants.All seven sites are MSK New York and New Jersey, and six of the seven carry a Limited Protocol Activities flag. Ask on the first call which visits can happen at her home institution.; Travel is not supplied with the study drug. Ask about MSK patient travel assistance at first contact, not after the first invoice.; prefers_trials true is doing most of the work behind this pick and nobody has confirmed it with her. If she never wanted a trial, this rank is wrong.; Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or VEGF-pathway drugs are exclusionary, so starting pazopanib first would close it permanently.; Preference axis in tension: modality_constraints is empty, which is not the same as her being willing to fly to New York during first-line treatment.

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakeradvocatedissentpreference_fitI'm passing on their rank 1, since a measured ECOG feeds three of my own picks even if putting a chart entry first ducks the therapy question; the row I dissent from is ivonescimab (nct:NCT07516925). Advocate's own notes refuse to spend the defaulted preferences as consent, then this pick spends the assumed prefers_trials on the two mechanisms her histology already beat: VEGF blockade added nothing first-line (GOG-0250, pmid:25713428) and the dedicated uLMS checkpoint study stopped for futility at 0 of 12 (pmid:28440953). If honoring a trials preference is the point, NCT06498648 does it without trading away the only OS regimen in the file, which is exactly why four of five of us left this seat empty. concensusiteadvocatequalifiedguideline_fitConcession first: putting a measured ECOG above any drug is the most guideline-literate move on any slate this round, since every eligibility bound the rest of us cited assumes a score nobody has written down. On ivonescimab I stay at qualified only because advocate priced it honestly: no guideline in any region carries the drug or its class in sarcoma, the class record in her disease is GOG-0250 (pmid:25713428) plus a futility stop at 0 of 12 (pmid:28440953), and the rank leans on a prefers_trials value the notes themselves admit was defaulted at intake. If her answers come back trial-and-travel, the route that honors them without leaving consensus is the abemaciclib seat with the carried gem/doc backbone as its control arm (nct:NCT06498648); the phone call is defensible, moving her to Manhattan on this record is not.

docs.title: In vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin plus metastasectomy (NCT02811523), as post-induction consolidation (ivlp-doxorubicin)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker3lowThis is the swing at long-term survival. Metastasectomy series in sarcoma lung disease report 5-year OS of 36% after complete resection and 55.4% in a uterine subset, and the perfusion protocol was written for her anatomy: bilateral disease, three or more lesions, nothing extrapulmonary, under 65. The clinical base for perfusion itself is a phase 1 built on preclinical work, which I accept because the payoff sits in a category no systemic option in this dossier reaches. Two things can kill it: an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pattern that a surgeon may call unresectable by wedge, and the cumulative-doxorubicin exclusion above 450 mg that full LMS-04 induction approaches.Every lesion in the perfused lung must be resectable by wedge or segment, and the infiltrative radiologic pattern is exactly the finding that defeats that judgement; Cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg excludes; direct sequencing conflict with full-dose LMS-04 unless cycles are counted from the start; Pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline is unmeasured; no PFTs or oximetry on file conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment conservativerisktakerdissenttoxicityI picked this row over the shared rank 1 because it is where the consolidation framing stops surviving contact: nct:NCT02811523 is a phase 1 perfusion protocol resting on preclinical work, with no published safety series in this population, and the patient asked to hold a thoracotomy seat has unmeasured pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline plus an infiltrative pattern both of us expect a surgeon may call unresectable by wedge. Ranks 1 and 3 also draw on one anthracycline budget; with G3-4 neutropenia at 80% (pmid:35835135) dose intensity is already fragile, and writing a stopping rule to stay under the 450 mg exclusion bends a phase 3 regimen around a phase 1 seat. Consolidation after response is the right idea, but the version with a measured toxicity profile is SBRT, 7.4% local failure at 24 months and zero G3+ events in the MSK series (pmid:37532104). concensusiterisktakerqualifiedguideline_fitRight shelf, wrong door. Risktaker is the only other slate that takes lung-directed consolidation seriously, and the shelf itself has consensus footing the rest of the board mostly skipped: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS CPG 2021 (pmid:34303806) carries complete excision of resectable lung metastases as standard local treatment in selected patients. The perfusion vehicle, though, is a phase 1 with no society carriage anywhere and a cumulative-doxorubicin exclusion above 450 mg that six full LMS-04 cycles nearly spends, so if induction earns a consolidation window the carried routes are wedge metastasectomy or SBRT (pmid:37532104), and the Toronto protocol (nct:NCT02811523) is the exception a tumor board argues for, not the default plan.

docs.title: IMA203 PRAME-directed TCR-T (NCT03686124), screening started in the first-line window (ima203)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowHer confirmed HLA-A*02:01 buys entry to the one cellular axis still open, and the phase 1 read is real: confirmed ORR 28.9% in heavily pretreated solid tumours, MTD not reached, severe CRS in 2 of 41. PRAME is the likeliest of the three antigens to come back positive, but nobody has tested it, and the sponsor scores expression on its own IMADetect RT-qPCR assay, so a local stain settles nothing; start that screening conversation now because it takes weeks. No uLMS patient is in the published dataset and median response duration was 4.4 months, and I still want this seat held, because a durable-tail outcome in a woman in her thirties is worth chasing on thin numbers.PRAME expression unmeasured; the whole branch can close on one sponsor assay; Protocol requires ECOG 0-1 and exhaustion of (or ineligibility for) standard care; her ECOG 1 is an intake assumption, never measured; mDoR 4.4 months in the interim report, with no uLMS-specific efficacy shown conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment advocaterisktakerqualifiedpreference_fitHolding this seat because 'a durable-tail outcome in a woman in her thirties is worth chasing' is a preference, and it is yours; preferences.json records no risk appetite from her and goals of care were never discussed. The hold is also not free the way the rationale implies: the protocol wants ECOG 0-1 and the cell-therapy screens want 90% or better room-air saturation with one cutting off at 92%, so at her 8,500 ft baseline the free oximetry with the altitude written on the report is the real gate, and nobody has ordered it. Cost the geography while you are at it, since this axis, the Toronto perfusion protocol, and Houston all put treatment a flight from home, and no slate has asked her whether she can or wants to travel. criticrisktakerdissentevidence_qualityThe 28.9% ORR is a phase 1 number with no uLMS patient in the dataset and a median response duration of 4.4 months (pmid:40205198), and the claim that PRAME is the likeliest of the three antigens to come back positive has nothing under it in this file: the only prevalence series we carry (pmid:40152485, 26 smooth-muscle tumours and not uterus-restricted) puts PRAME highest in UPS and osteosarcoma, quotes no smooth-muscle PRAME figure at all, and its neighbouring MAGE-A4 smooth-muscle number drew an erratum and sits flagged as internally inconsistent in our own row. Entry is decided on the sponsor's IMADetect RT-qPCR, so a local IHC has no established operating characteristics against the assay that matters, and neither a negative nor a positive local stain settles the axis the way the rationale implies. I will give risktaker this much: it called the RAD51 split exploratory at n=18 in the same breath as betting on it, which is how a subgroup ought to be carried, and I would take that over anyone quoting 11.2 versus 5.4 months as a finding.

Myelosuppression forced temozolomide dose reduction in the combination.moderatemedcross tumor only25500058DOINo leiomyosarcoma model in the panel, and the responsive histology (Ewing) has a distinct DNA-damage biology. The haematologic toxicity signal is the part that carries directly into clinic. docs.title: ALT prevalence and ATRX loss in leiomyosarcoma
docs.text:
intervention_id: atr-inhibition-alt · 5 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Laroche-Clary/Italiano (2020)Sci Repsoft-tissue sarcoma cell lines and an undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma patient-derived xenograft—single-agent VE-822, single-agent gemcitabine, vehicleVE-822 combined with gemcitabine in vitro and in vivoATR inhibition removes the intra-S-phase checkpoint that would otherwise let cells survive gemcitabine-induced replication stressThe VE-822 and gemcitabine combination was synergistic in vitro with increased gammaH2AX and S-phase accumulation, and in vivo it improved tumour growth inhibition and progression-free survival over either agent. Sensitivity did not track ALT status.moderatemedpartial32366852DOIThe in-vivo model was undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, not leiomyosarcoma. Supports ATR inhibition as a chemo-sensitiser rather than as an ALT-selected strategy. Goncalves/Tomita (2020)ACS Pharmacol Transl Sciosteosarcoma cell lines of varying telomere length and telomere-maintenance mechanism—long-telomere lines within the same panel—short telomeres, rather than the recombination-based maintenance mechanism itself, create the ATR dependencyATR inhibitors selectively eliminated osteosarcoma lines with short telomeres regardless of whether those lines used ALT.moderatelowcross tumor only33344901DOIOsteosarcoma lines, in vitro. Reframes the biomarker as telomere length, which nobody has measured in this patient either. Deeg/Rippe (2016)Front Oncolpanel of ALT-positive and telomerase-positive cell lines including U2OS and ALT-positive glioma lines—telomerase-positive lines; multiple ATR inhibitors—direct test of whether the ALT phenotype itself confers ATR dependencyAcross a broader panel and several ATR inhibitors, ALT-positive lines showed no general hypersensitivity relative to telomerase-positive lines.negativelowcross tumor only27602331DOIContradicts Flynn 2015. In-vitro only, but the negative result is the reason ALT status alone should not be treated as an ATR-inhibitor selection biomarker in this case. Liau/Yang (2015)Am J Surg Pathol92 human leiomyosarcomas (uterine, retroperitoneal and other sites) by telomere FISH, ATRX/DAXX IHC and TERT promoter sequencingn=92 tumoursALT-negative tumours within the same series—ATRX inactivation permits the recombination-based telomere maintenance that defines ALTALT was present in 59% of leiomyosarcomas and ATRX expression was lost in 33%, with all but two ATRX-deficient tumours being ALT-positive. Both features went with epithelioid or pleomorphic morphology, necrosis and worse outcome.moderatehighstrong25229770DOIHuman tissue survey with no therapeutic arm. Sets a realistic pre-test probability that this tumour is ALT-positive, which matters only if an ALT-directed strategy has a real preclinical basis. Flynn/Zou (2015)ScienceALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cancer cell lines, including ATRX-deficient lines—isogenic and matched telomerase-positive lines—ALT depends on ATR-coordinated homologous recombination at telomeres, so ATR inhibition disrupts telomere maintenance selectivelyALT-positive lines were selectively killed by ATR inhibitors while telomerase-positive lines were spared, and ATRX loss was linked to the ALT phenotype.stronglowcross tumor only25593184DOIIn-vitro only, and the selectivity claim failed to replicate in later work — read alongside Deeg 2016 and Goncalves 2020 rather than on its own.

docs.title: MAGE-A4, PRAME and NY-ESO-1 prevalence across bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
docs.text:
intervention_id: ct-antigen-target-biology · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Chen/Li (2025)Cancer Medhuman sarcoma specimens by IHC and multiplex immunostaining microarray; 26 smooth-muscle sarcomas among 128 tumoursn=128 (21 UPS, 26 smooth-muscle sarcoma, 28 liposarcoma, 40 osteosarcoma, 13 chondrosarcoma)cross-subtype comparison; testis as the reference positive tissue for this antigen class—cancer/testis antigen expression as the second gate for HLA-restricted TCR and ImmTAC programsExpression was subtype-dependent, highest for MAGE-A4 and PRAME in UPS and osteosarcoma. NY-ESO-1 was low across every subtype, and the smooth-muscle sarcoma group was positive for MAGE-A4 in a minority of cases.weakmedpartial40152485DOIThe reported MAGE-A4 percentages for smooth-muscle sarcoma are internally inconsistent between the results text and its own framing, and an erratum was issued (Cancer Med 2025;14:e70971) — treat the exact figure as soft. Smooth-muscle sarcoma here is not uterus-restricted. McGranahan/TRACERx Consortium (2017)Cellmultiregion whole-exome sequencing of primary non-small-cell lung tumours (TRACERx) with an HLA-specific LOH callerLOH at the HLA locus in 40% of tumours analysedHLA-intact regions within the same tumours—somatic loss of one HLA haplotype removes the restriction element without touching the antigen, under immune-editing selectionHLA LOH occurred in around 40% of tumours, was frequently subclonal and enriched in metastatic or later subclones, and associated with a higher neoantigen burden in the affected regions.strongmedcross tumor only29107330DOILung cancer under endogenous T-cell pressure, not sarcoma under engineered T cells. The relevance is that germline HLA-A*02:01 typing does not guarantee the pulmonary metastases still present that allele. De Smet/Boon (1996)Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A20 human tumour cell lines plus primary fibroblasts; CpG methylation mapping and 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine treatment—MAGE-1-negative lines; untreated fibroblasts—CpG demethylation at Ets-binding sites in the MAGE-1 promoter permits transcription-factor binding, downstream of genome-wide demethylation in the tumourMAGE-1 promoter CpGs were demethylated in expressing lines and methylated in non-expressing ones, and 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine switched the gene on even in normal fibroblasts. Overall CpG methylation was inversely correlated with MAGE-1 expression across the 20 lines.strongmedcross tumor only8692960DOIMAGE-1 rather than MAGE-A4, and the work predates modern epigenomics. It is the reason cancer/testis antigen expression is patchy and epigenetically labile rather than a fixed lineage property — which is the honest answer to whether expression is stable enough for a TCR-T strategy.

docs.title: ADP-A2M4 (afamitresgene) affinity-enhanced MAGE-A4 TCR — preclinical potency and specificity
docs.text:
intervention_id: afamitresgene-magea4-tcrt · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Sanderson/Gerry (2020)Oncoimmunology2D and 3D human cell cultures, primary tumour material, and human primary-cell and cell-line cross-reactivity panels—non-transduced T cells; HLA-A2-negative and MAGE-A4-negative targets—affinity-enhanced TCR recognising the HLA-A*02-restricted MAGE-A4 peptide GVYDGREHTV on the tumour cell surfaceADP-A2M4 killed MAGE-A4-positive HLA-A2-positive targets potently across 2D, 3D and primary tumour material. Alanine-scanning and primary-cell screening turned up no major off-target cross-reactivity.strongmedpartial32002290DOIAdaptimmune-authored; the tumour material tested was not uterine leiomyosarcoma. Potency is contingent on antigen expression, which is exactly what has not been measured in this patient. Cameron/Jakobsen (2013)Sci Transl Medin-vitro functional analysis of an affinity-enhanced HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 TCR; post-hoc amino-acid scanning and beating-cardiomyocyte cultures—pre-SAE preclinical panels that had returned clean—affinity enhancement broadens peptide tolerance, so a structurally similar peptide from a muscle protein becomes a targetConventional preclinical screening found no off-target activity, yet the engineered T cells caused fatal cardiac toxicity in patients. Amino-acid scanning afterwards identified the titin peptide ESDPIVAQY as the cross-reactive target.strongmedcross tumor only23926201DOIA different TCR, a different antigen and a different HLA allele from the MAGE-A4 A*02:01 products in scope here. docs.title: PRAME/HLA-A2 epitope density and the immunoproteasome
docs.text:
intervention_id: prame-directed-tcr-immtac · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Chang/Scheinberg (2017)J Clin InvestPRAME-positive HLA-A2-positive human cancer and leukemia lines; mouse xenograft models of human leukemia; TCR-mimic antibody Pr20—PRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative lines; unmodified IgG—the PRAME300-309 ALYVDSLFFL peptide is presented on HLA-A*02:01 at very low copy number, and immunoproteasome subunit beta5i induction after IFN-gamma raises the amount presentedSurface PRAME/HLA-A2 complexes were present at ultra-low density, and an afucosylated TCR-mimic antibody was nonetheless therapeutically active against leukemia xenografts. IFN-gamma markedly increased Pr20 binding in some tumours by shifting proteasome cleavage away from destroying the epitope.moderatemedcross tumor only28628042DOILeukemia and melanoma models, and a TCR-mimic antibody rather than a TCR-T or ImmTAC. The transferable point is that PRAME protein positivity by IHC and PRAME epitope density on HLA-A2 are not the same quantity. docs.title: Sarcoma immune classes and B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures
docs.text:
intervention_id: checkpoint-blockade-ulms · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Guo/Li (2025)Front Immunolsingle-cell RNA sequencing of metastatic lesions from one treatment-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma patient versus normal myometrium1 uLMS patient (4 metastatic sites); n=5 normal myometriumnormal uterine myometrium—exhausted CD8 T cells, M2-polarised tumour-associated macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils together with MIF-CD74/CD44 and CXCL8 signalling produce an immunosuppressed nicheMetastatic uLMS lesions were dominated by exhausted CD8 T cells, CD163-positive M2 macrophages and CD15-positive immature neutrophils, with naive markers lost along the pseudotime trajectory. CXCL8 signalling linked angiogenesis to macrophage polarisation in the same niche.moderatemedstrong40948800DOIA single patient's metastases, so cell-type frequencies are anecdotal even if the qualitative picture matches the wider literature. No therapeutic arm. De Wispelaere/Amant (2024)Clin Transl Medhumanized and immunodeficient uterine leiomyosarcoma patient-derived xenografts; TCGA analysis of 101 LMS; serial single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing of biopsies—single-agent anti-PD-1, single-agent PI3K/mTOR inhibitor, vehiclePI3K/mTOR inhibitor with anti-PD-1 in a humanized uLMS PDXPI3K/mTOR overactivation associates with lymphocyte depletion; inhibiting it repolarises macrophages, raises antigen presentation on dendritic and tumour cells, and draws in PD-1-positive T cells that then need checkpoint releaseSingle-agent anti-PD-1 produced no response in the ICB-resistant humanized uLMS PDX, while combining it with PI3K/mTOR inhibition gave partial or complete responses. The combination reinvigorated exhausted T cells and drove clonal expansion of a cytotoxic CD8 population supported by CD4 Th1 cells.strongmedstrong38711203DOIHumanized PDX immunology is an approximation of a human immune system, and the pS6-high selection marker has not been measured in this patient. The nearest lineage-matched argument that checkpoint blockade in uLMS needs a partner rather than a companion diagnostic. Petitprez/Fridman (2020)Naturegene-expression profiling of 608 soft-tissue sarcomas with validation against a phase 2 pembrolizumab cohortn=608 tumourscross-class comparison within the same cohort—composition of the tumour microenvironment, and specifically B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures, governs whether PD-1 blockade has anything to act onFive immune phenotypes emerged, from immune-low (A, B) to immune-high (D, E). Class E, defined by tertiary lymphoid structures rich in B cells and follicular dendritic cells, had better survival and a high response rate to pembrolizumab, and B-cell content outperformed CD8 content as a predictor.stronghighpartial31942077DOILeiomyosarcoma sits predominantly in the immune-low classes, which is the structural reason single-agent checkpoint blockade underperforms in this histology. Class assignment requires an expression assay nobody has run here.

docs.title: Antiangiogenic plus anti-PD-L1 therapy and high endothelial venule formation
docs.text:
intervention_id: ivonescimab-pd1-vegf · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Zhong/Li (2025)iSciencebiophysical and cell-based assays plus mouse tumour models; cynomolgus monkey safety—parental anti-PD-1 and anti-VEGF antibodies and their combination—VEGF dimers cross-link the tetravalent antibody into soluble complexes that raise its avidity for PD-1, and PD-1 engagement reciprocally strengthens VEGF binding; Fc mutations abrogate FcgammaRI/IIIa bindingEach target enhanced binding to the other, so PD-1/PD-L1 and VEGF blockade were both more potent than with the separate antibodies. Fc silencing cut effector function in vitro, consistent with the tolerability seen in monkeys and patients, and the antibody produced a significant in-vivo antitumor response.moderatelowcross tumor only40034861DOIAuthored entirely by the sponsor, and the in-vivo work is in humanized-mouse tumour models with no sarcoma among them. Explains the molecular design; says nothing about leiomyosarcoma. Allen/Bergers (2017)Sci Transl Medmouse models of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour, mammary carcinoma and glioblastoma—single-agent anti-VEGFR2, single-agent anti-PD-L1, vehicleanti-VEGFR2 (DC101) combined with anti-PD-L1 antibodyVEGF blockade normalises tumour vasculature and induces high endothelial venules, which in turn permit cytotoxic T-cell entry that checkpoint blockade can then sustainThe combination prolonged survival and produced tumour regression in models where either agent alone did little, and the benefit tracked with intratumoural high endothelial venule formation and increased CTL infiltration. Anti-PD-L1 also sustained vessel normalisation, making the interaction reciprocal.strongmedcross tumor only28404866DOICarcinoma and neuroendocrine models, no sarcoma. This is the mechanistic ancestor of the PD-1 x VEGF bispecific rationale rather than evidence about ivonescimab itself.

docs.title: B7-H3 expression across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes
docs.text:
intervention_id: b7h3-adc · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Lynch/Pollack (2024)BMC Cancer153 human soft-tissue sarcoma specimens across 15 subtypes, scored by IHC for tumour and vessel stainingn=153 patientswithin-cohort comparison; PD-L1/PD-1 status where previously assessed—B7-H3 surface expression as the antigen available to an ADC or a T-cell engagerB7-H3 was expressed in 97% of samples and at high level in 69.2%, with vessel positivity in 94.7%. Expression was independent of prior treatment, tumour size, grade, age, and of PD-L1 or PD-1 status.stronghighpartial39478506DOIPrevalence, not density in molecules per cell, which is the quantity that actually governs CAR and ADC activity. Leiomyosarcoma is one of 15 subtypes in the cohort rather than the focus. Brignole/Ponzoni (2023)J Immunother Cancerneuroblastoma cell lines and orthotopic/metastatic mouse xenograft models with varying B7-H3 levels—isotype-ADC control; untreated micevobramitamab duocarmazine (MGC018) administered intravenously in xenograft-bearing miceB7-H3-directed antibody delivering a duocarmycin payload, with membrane-permeable released drug killing neighbouring antigen-low cellsThe ADC inhibited tumour growth and extended survival across models, with activity extending to cells expressing lower B7-H3 through bystander killing of adjacent cells.strongmedcross tumor only37775116DOINeuroblastoma only, and the payload class differs from the topoisomerase-I payloads carried by the B7-H3 ADCs in this case's trial set. The bystander principle is what transfers, not the potency numbers. Majzner/Mackall (2019)Clin Cancer Resxenograft models of osteosarcoma, medulloblastoma and Ewing sarcoma; target lines titrated for surface B7-H3—untransduced T cells; antigen-low and antigen-negative target lines—CAR engagement scales with surface antigen copy number, so a density threshold separates tumour killing from sparing of low-expressing normal tissueB7-H3 CAR T cells regressed established solid-tumour xenografts, and efficacy depended heavily on high surface antigen density. Activity fell away sharply against low-expressing targets, which is what creates the therapeutic window over normal tissue.strongmedcross tumor only30655315DOIPaediatric tumour xenografts, no leiomyosarcoma. The density-threshold result is the reason a 'B7-H3 positive' IHC call is insufficient on its own for a CAR strategy, and it applies with less force to an ADC with a bystander payload.

docs.title: CC-3, a B7-H3 x CD3 bispecific antibody, against bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
docs.text:
intervention_id: b7h3-cd3-bispecific · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Holzmayer/Märklin (2024)Front Immunolsarcoma cell lines of multiple subtypes with healthy-donor T cells; patient sarcoma specimens for expression and outcome—B7-H3-negative target cells; control bispecific/T cells alone—IgG-based B7-H3 x CD3 bispecific redirects polyclonal T cells to B7-H3-positive tumour cells independent of TCR specificity or HLAB7-H3 was found on every sarcoma line tested, and CC-3 triggered T-cell activation, cytokine release, proliferation, memory differentiation and target-restricted lysis. Higher B7-H3 in patient specimens went with shorter progression-free and overall survival.moderatemedpartial38765008DOIIn-vitro only — no xenograft arm — and the sarcoma line panel is not leiomyosarcoma-specific. HLA-independence is the practical contrast with the TCR-T options in this case.

docs.title: Trabectedin's selective depletion of mononuclear phagocytes
docs.text:
intervention_id: trabectedin-monotherapy · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Germano/Allavena (2013)Cancer Cellfour mouse tumour models with myeloid-cell transfer and depletion experiments; trabectedin-resistant tumour cells; blood and tumour from treated patients—untreated tumour-bearing mice; trabectedin-resistant tumour cells to separate direct from myeloid effects—caspase-8-dependent apoptosis restricted to mononuclear phagocytes, with selectivity over neutrophils and lymphocytes set by differential signalling and decoy TRAIL receptor expressionTrabectedin depleted monocytes and macrophages from blood, spleen and tumour across four mouse models, with angiogenesis falling alongside. Transfer and depletion experiments using trabectedin-resistant tumour cells established that killing mononuclear phagocytes is a real component of the antitumour effect, and monocyte depletion was reproduced in treated patients.strongmedpartial23410977DOINone of the four mouse models is uterine leiomyosarcoma. Directly relevant here because the metastatic uLMS niche is macrophage-rich, which makes the planned first-line agent partly an immune-modulating one. Aune/Pommier (2008)Clin Cancer Reshuman cell lines with defined defects in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair and in VHL—TC-NER-proficient and VHL-proficient isogenic lines—trabectedin-DNA adducts stall elongating RNA polymerase II, and degradation of the stalled polymerase requires both transcription-coupled NER and VHLTrabectedin caused rapid RNA polymerase II degradation that depended on both TC-NER and VHL, tying cytotoxicity to transcription rather than to replication alone.strongmedcross tumor only18927284DOIIsogenic human cell lines, no tumour model. Explains why trabectedin is a transcription-targeted drug and why repair-pathway status, not proliferation rate, is where a predictive biomarker would sit. Damia/D'Incalci (2001)Int J Canceryeast and mammalian cell panels with defined NER, mismatch-repair, DNA-PK and ATM deficiencies—repair-proficient parental lines and complemented revertants—NER machinery converts the minor-groove adduct into a lethal lesion, while double-strand-break repair capacity determines how well the cell survives itNER-deficient lines were 2- to 8-fold less sensitive to ET-743 and restoring NER re-sensitised them, the opposite of the usual pattern for DNA-damaging drugs. Cells lacking DNA-PK or ATM were more sensitive, and mismatch-repair status made no difference.moderatemedcross tumor only11304695DOIEngineered cell systems from 2001, no tumour model. The closest thing to a mechanistic biomarker of trabectedin benefit: intact NER plus impaired double-strand-break repair, which is the profile an HR-deficient uLMS would have.

docs.title: ET-743 combined with doxorubicin in sarcoma models
docs.text:
intervention_id: doxorubicin-trabectedin-lms04 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Meco/Riccardi (2003)Cancer Chemother PharmacolTE-671 rhabdomyosarcoma xenografts in nude mice; UV2237M murine fibrosarcoma and its doxorubicin-resistant Pgp-overexpressing subline—single-agent ET-743, single-agent doxorubicin, untreated controlsET-743 and doxorubicin simultaneously, or ET-743 1 h before doxorubicin, or the reverse sequencea transcription-targeted minor-groove binder combined with a topoisomerase II poison, hitting non-overlapping lesionsIsobologram analysis showed an additive interaction with combination indices slightly below 1. In TE-671 xenografts each drug alone was marginal (log cell kill 0.13 and 0.33) while the combination reached 0.85 to 1.12, best when ET-743 preceded doxorubicin by an hour, and no pharmacokinetic interaction was found.moderatemedpartial12783202DOIPre-dates the LMS-04 regimen by nearly two decades and neither model is leiomyosarcoma. The interaction was additive rather than synergistic, and in the fibrosarcoma lung-metastasis arm the combination did not beat either drug alone.

docs.title: Histone eviction as a second mechanism of anthracycline action
docs.text:
intervention_id: doxorubicin-backbone · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Pang/Neefjes (2013)Nat Communhuman cancer cell lines, mouse tissues including heart, and primary AML blasts from patients—etoposide and doxorubicin variants that break DNA without evicting histones—anthracyclines evict histones, including H2AX, from open chromatin independently of double-strand-break formation, which deregulates transcription and blunts the damage responseDoxorubicin evicted histones from open chromatin whether or not it induced double-strand breaks, and H2AX eviction was accompanied by attenuated DNA repair. The same eviction happened in heart tissue and could kill topoisomerase-negative AML blasts.strongmedcross tumor only23715267DOINo sarcoma model. Matters here for two reasons: it explains anthracycline activity in slowly proliferating tumours, and it links the same mechanism to cardiac tissue in a patient whose baseline LVEF has not yet been measured.

docs.text:
