docs.title: Remaining unmeasured molecular landscape (the gap has narrowed, not closed)
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences essentialTumor NGS covering BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM and the wider HRR gene set, with a reported genomic-instability / LOH scoreconfirmatoryNGS_panelarchival FFPE; shares the specimen with tissue order A2-3 weeksOlaparib plus temozolomide (NCI protocol 10250, NCT03880019) and PARP-inhibitor trial entry at progression.An absent BRCA1/2 call on a plasma panel at unstated tumor fraction is weak evidence, and a genomic instability score cannot be derived from that assay at all, so homologous-recombination status is open rather than negative. Uterine leiomyosarcoma has a recognised HR-deficient subset including BRCA2 deletion and mutation (PMID 37143137), and olaparib plus temozolomide produced a 27 percent objective response rate with median PFS 6.9 months in pretreated advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma, where 31 percent of enrolled patients carried an HRR gene mutation (PMID 37467452). Skipping it leaves the one non-cytotoxic branch in this case unopened at the point where LMS-04 fails.Caris Life Sciences · MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) preferredtest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669HRR genes, genomic LOH, TMB, MSI and RNA fusions off one archival order, which is the bundling this case needs.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne CDx UStest info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639Myriad Genetics · MyChoice CDx UStest info · 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 1-800-469-7423The best-validated genomic-instability score, but its threshold of at least 42 was set in ovarian carcinoma; treat the number as descriptive in sarcoma rather than as a companion-diagnostic call.NeoGenomics Laboratories UStest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Tempus AI · xT CDx with xR whole-transcriptome UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654 · 1-800-739-4137PMID 37467452PMID 37143137NCT03880019 essentialMismatch-repair protein IHC (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) on tumor tissue, with reflex MLH1 promoter methylation and BRAF V600E if MLH1 is lost, plus the MSI call from tissue NGSconfirmatoryIHCarchival FFPE; 4 unstained slides from the same block cut for INI13-5 daysPembrolizumab or dostarlimab under the tumor-agnostic dMMR/MSI-H indications at progression.Mismatch-repair status is unmeasured, and the plasma assay returned no MSI call at an unstated tumor fraction, so nothing on file speaks to it in either direction. Four stains on a block already being cut close a tumor-agnostic PD-1 indication that would otherwise sit open at progression (NCT02628067, NCT02715284). Loss of any one protein in a woman in her thirties also carries Lynch implications for her and for first-degree relatives.NeoGenomics Laboratories · MMR IHC panel with reflex testing preferredtest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Reflex MLH1 methylation and BRAF V600E are on the same requisition, which avoids a second block request if MLH1 is lost.ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108-1221 · 1-800-242-2787Labcorp Oncology UStest info · 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 · 1-800-845-6167Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710Quest Diagnostics UStest info · 500 Plaza Drive, Secaucus, NJ 07094 · 1-866-697-8378NCT02628067NCT02715284 essentialRNA-based fusion NGS panel covering NTRK1, NTRK2 and NTRK3 (with RET, ALK and ROS1 in the same run) on archival tissueorthogonal validationRNA_seqarchival FFPE; shares the specimen with tissue order A. RNA quality degrades in blocks older than about 5 years, so the 2026 lung core is the safer input2-3 weeksLarotrectinib, entrectinib or repotrectinib under the tumor-agnostic NTRK fusion indications.What is on file is non-detection on a plasma DNA assay at unstated tumor fraction, which is not a negative: plasma fusion calling is insensitive when shedding is low, and DNA capture misses breakpoints in the large NTRK introns. RNA sequencing reads the transcript and so is agnostic to where in the intron the break sits, which is what allows a negative to be read as a negative. Prevalence in uterine leiomyosarcoma is very low, but a spindle-cell tumor once signed out as benign is precisely the setting in which an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm hides, and a positive converts a chemotherapy-only landscape into an oral TRK inhibitor.Caris Life Sciences · MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) preferredtest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669Whole-transcriptome sequencing rather than a targeted fusion panel, so novel partners are callable and RET comes free.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne CDx UStest info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639DNA-based fusion calling; adequate for common partners but weaker for large-intron NTRK breakpoints, which is the failure mode this row exists to avoid.Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710NeoGenomics Laboratories · NeoTYPE RNA fusion profile UStest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Tempus AI · xR RNA sequencing UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654 · 1-800-739-4137NCT02576431NCT02568267NCT03093116 essentialValidated comprehensive genomic profiling on tissue reporting TMB in mutations per megabase (with the MSI and BRAF codon 600 calls in the same report)confirmatoryNGS_panelarchival FFPE; 10-15 unstained slides or the block (shared with tissue order A, not a separate specimen)2-3 weeksPembrolizumab under the tumor-agnostic TMB-high indication at progression.TMB was never reported: the Guardant assay did not return one, and a plasma TMB at unstated tumor fraction would not have been usable if it had. Leiomyosarcoma is copy-number driven and typically low-TMB, so a high value would be a surprise, but the panel that reports it is the same order that settles MSI, the fusions, the HRR genes and the TP53 attribution question. Ask for a validated assay with a mutations-per-megabase figure; a number off a small hotspot panel does not satisfy the tumor-agnostic indication.Caris Life Sciences · MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) preferredtest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669Exome-based TMB with the transcriptome in the same order, which is what makes this one requisition instead of three.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne CDx UStest info · 150 Second Street, Cambridge, MA 02141 · 1-888-988-3639The TMB assay with the longest companion-diagnostic track record.Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Diagnostic Molecular Pathology · MSK-IMPACT (matched tumor and normal) UStest info · 1275 York Avenue, New York, NY 10065 · 1-212-639-2000NeoGenomics Laboratories UStest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Tempus AI · xT CDx with xR whole-transcriptome UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654 · 1-800-739-4137NCT02628067 essentialPaired peripheral-blood leukocyte sequencing (buffy-coat myeloid/CHIP panel covering TP53) plus tissue NGS interrogation of the TP53 Q52* positionorthogonal validationNGS_panel5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA for the buffy-coat panel; archival FFPE for the tissue route, which comes free with tissue order A2-3 weeks (tissue route); 1-2 weeks for a blood myeloid panelAttribution of the whole plasma report to tumor versus blood, which is what licenses acting on any plasma-only finding.Two orthogonal routes settle this and either will do: the same TP53 Q52* found in tumor DNA makes it tumor-derived, while finding it in white-cell DNA makes it clonal haematopoiesis. That distinction is not academic at unstated tumor fraction; in matched cfDNA and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2 percent of cfDNA mutations in cancer patients had features of clonal haematopoiesis (PMID 31768066). Be honest about the payoff: a confirmed somatic TP53 in uterine leiomyosarcoma is expected and largely prognostic, so the value is in calibrating how much weight the rest of this plasma report, including the SMARCB1 call, can carry.Caris Life Sciences · MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) preferredtest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669The tissue route is the cheaper of the two here because it is already being ordered; TP53 comes off tissue order A with no additional specimen.ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108-1221 · 1-800-242-2787Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Diagnostic Molecular Pathology · MSK-IMPACT / MSK-ACCESS with matched normal UStest info · 1275 York Avenue, New York, NY 10065 · 1-212-639-2000Sequences a matched normal by design, which answers the CHIP question without a separate requisition.NeoGenomics Laboratories · NeoTYPE Myeloid Disorders Profile UStest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907PMID 31768066PMID 36788080 highB7-H3 (CD276) IHC on tumor tissueconfirmatoryIHCarchival FFPE; 1-2 unstained slides from the same block cut as INI1 and the MMR set1 weekB7-H3-directed trial screening (ifinatamab deruxtecan and the wider B7-H3 program).B7-H3 has the best odds of a positive result of any surface target in scope here: 97 percent of soft tissue sarcoma specimens were positive and about 69 percent high in a 153-patient series spanning 15 subtypes including leiomyosarcoma (PMID 39478506). Nothing is approved against it, so a positive buys trial access rather than a prescription, and the ADC, CAR-T and bispecific programs generally require documented expression at screening. Adding it to the block already being cut keeps a later referral from stalling while somebody hunts for tissue.NeoGenomics Laboratories · B7-H3 (CD276) IHC preferredtest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Offers CD276 as a routine stain rather than as a send-out, and can run it alongside INI1 and the MMR panel.ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108-1221 · 1-800-242-2787Discovery Life Sciences UStest info · 601 Genome Way, Huntsville, AL 35806 · 1-800-956-4472Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710PMID 39478506 highRB1, ATRX and MED12 status from tissue NGS, with the p53 / Rb / ATRX / PTEN IHC surrogate panel read on the same blockco-mutationNGS_panelarchival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond tissue orders A and B2-3 weeks (NGS); 3-5 days (IHC panel)Diagnostic corroboration and co-alteration context for trial screening; no direct therapeutic gate.Ninety-four percent of 167 uterine leiomyosarcomas carried at least one alteration in TP53, RB1, ATRX, PTEN, CDKN2A or MDM2, and 80 percent carried two or more; the corresponding IHC surrogates agreed with sequencing at kappa 0.941 (PMID 36788080). Establishing that backbone does three things at once: it corroborates the diagnosis in a case whose primary was once called benign, it supplies the co-alteration context that trial screening asks for, and abnormal p53 staining would independently support a tumor origin for the plasma TP53 call. None of it is directly druggable, which is why this sits below the gating rows.NeoGenomics Laboratories preferredtest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Can run the p53 / Rb / ATRX / PTEN stains on the same block cut as INI1 and the MMR set, which is the point of bundling order B.Caris Life Sciences · MI Profile (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) UStest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 · 1-888-979-8669Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Diagnostic Molecular Pathology · MSK-IMPACT (matched tumor and normal) UStest info · 1275 York Avenue, New York, NY 10065 · 1-212-639-2000The laboratory that published the IHC algorithm this row rests on.Tempus AI · xT CDx with xR whole-transcriptome UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654 · 1-800-739-4137PMID 36788080 highGermline multigene hereditary cancer panel including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM, TP53 and the Lynch genesgermlinegermline_panel5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or saliva2-4 weeksStrength of the PARP-inhibitor case, plus cascade testing and her own surveillance.Somatic-only testing answers what the tumor carries and nothing about what she carries, which for a woman in her thirties leaves her own second-cancer risk and her relatives' screening open. A germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 finding would also strengthen the PARP-inhibitor case beyond what a somatic call alone supports (PMID 37467452). Run it on the same draw as any other blood work rather than as a reflex weeks later; the counselling and insurance steps are the slow part, not the assay.Myriad Genetics · MyRisk Hereditary Cancer preferredtest info · 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108 · 1-800-469-7423Broadest payer coverage of the group for a patient with no family history documented, which is the practical bottleneck here rather than assay quality.Ambry Genetics · CancerNext-Expanded UStest info · 1 Enterprise, Aliso Viejo, CA 92656 · 1-949-900-5500GeneDx UStest info · 1-888-729-1206Labcorp Oncology UStest info · 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 · 1-800-845-6167Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710PMID 37467452PMID 37143137

docs.title: Bilateral pulmonary metastases with an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic pattern
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences highBaseline pulmonary function tests with DLCO, plus resting and ambulatory pulse oximetry recorded at residence altitudefunctional assayotherno tissue; spirometry with DLCO and pulse oximetry at rest and on exertion1-2 weeks to scheduleAttribution of on-treatment dyspnea, and pulmonary fitness ahead of any later metastasectomy or SBRT.Bilateral pulmonary metastases read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory in a lifetime never-smoker at 8,500 feet is a pulmonary reserve question nobody has measured. A baseline DLCO and an oximetry pair recorded at her own altitude give the only reference against which on-treatment dyspnea can be attributed to disease progression, to chronic hypoxic adaptation, or to treatment. Without it, a fall in saturation during induction is uninterpretable.—— highPre-treatment CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with measurable RECIST v1.1 target lesions, read against any imaging available from the September 2024 to July 2026 intervalfunctional assayimagingno tissue; cross-sectional imaging with contrast unless contraindicated1-2 weeks to schedule and reportRECIST measurability for trial screening, response assessment during LMS-04, and the field of view for excluding peritoneal disease.Trial screening requires measurable disease by RECIST v1.1, and an infiltrative pulmonary pattern is exactly the morphology that can fail to yield measurable target lesions; better to discover that before a screening slot than during one. Reading the baseline against anything shot in the 2024 to 2026 interval also bounds the growth kinetics of disease that went untreated for roughly 23 months, which is the single best available estimate of tempo. Abdomen and pelvis matter here specifically because the 2024 hysterectomy may have disrupted the specimen.—— mediumPD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system matched to the intended agent, plus CD3 and CD8 T-cell infiltrate density, on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis coremicroenvironmentIHCarchival FFPE; 2-3 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core specifically1 weekSupporting context for any checkpoint-blockade or cell-therapy proposal; MSI and TMB, not PD-L1, are what would open checkpoint blockade here.PD-L1 gates no approval in soft tissue sarcoma, so this informs rather than decides. It earns a row because the pulmonary lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and an immune phenotype on the lung core is the only way to tell whether that radiologic impression corresponds to anything in the tissue. Infiltrate density is also what cell-therapy and bispecific programs look at when weighing a candidate, so the CD3 and CD8 reads carry more forward here than the PD-L1 score does.NeoGenomics Laboratories preferredtest info · 9490 NeoGenomics Way, Fort Myers, FL 33912 · 1-866-776-5907Runs the PD-L1 companion clones and the CD3/CD8 stains on one requisition.ARUP Laboratories UStest info · 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108-1221 · 1-800-242-2787Labcorp Oncology UStest info · 358 South Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215 · 1-800-845-6167Mayo Clinic Laboratories UStest info · 3050 Superior Drive NW, Rochester, MN 55901 · 1-800-533-1710Quest Diagnostics UStest info · 500 Plaza Drive, Secaucus, NJ 07094 · 1-866-697-8378—

docs.title: ~23-month interval between resection of the primary (September 2024, signed out benign) and correct diagnosis (July-August 2026)
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences highRetrieval of the September 2024 operative report and gross pathology description: route of hysterectomy, whether power or manual morcellation was used, specimen integrity and margin statusconfirmatory—no tissue; the operative note and gross description from the September 2024 hysterectomydays; records requestWhether peritoneal and pelvic disease must be actively excluded, and how the staging imaging field is drawn.A 6.0 cm myometrial mass removed as a presumed benign fibroid in 2024 may have been morcellated, and morcellation of an unrecognised leiomyosarcoma disperses tumor through the peritoneum and has been associated with worse outcomes (PMID 28209496; PMID 26646120). The staging picture is currently pulmonary only; if the specimen was disrupted, peritoneal and pelvic disease has to be actively excluded rather than assumed absent. The answer sits in an operative note nobody has yet had reason to re-read.—PMID 28209496PMID 26646120

ECOG 0-2 is wide enough that the undocumented performance status does not by itself block screening, unlike the ECOG 0-1 protocols. No biomarker gate, and archival tumor tissue is required, which the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 lung core should satisfy. ——2026—NCT076337561bmetastatic or unresectable RB1-negative leiomyosarcoma2L+RB1 loss (required)15open-label phase 1bREC-617 (selective CDK7 inhibitor)—safety and adverse events————low——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 1 activeM.D. Anderson Cancer Center—Entry hinges on RB1 loss, which she has not had measured on tissue; the plasma panel reporting no RB1 alteration settles nothing at an unsupplied tumor fraction. RB1 loss is common in uterine leiomyosarcoma, so the prior is not low, and the tissue NGS the validator already ordered would answer it. Conditional on that result and on prior systemic therapy. ——2026—NCT073748481locally advanced or metastatic sarcoma and selected solid tumors2L+LRRC15 (sponsor-assessed)180phase 1a/1b dose escalation and expansionZL-6201 (LRRC15-directed antibody-drug conjugate)—incidence of dose-limiting toxicities————low——partialindicationADCphase 1 activeZai Lab—Sarcoma patients enter with no more than two prior systemic lines, which LMS-04 alone would satisfy. A pre-treatment biopsy or archival block is mandatory and she has two specimens available. ECOG 0-1 required, so the performance-status documentation gap applies. ——2026—NCT073033872metastatic or recurrent solid tumors with SWI/SNF loss (Cohort 1.A: SMARCB1-defective)1L or 2Lbi-allelic (homozygous) SMARCB1 deletion by validated NGS on tissue or plasma, plus centralised IHC confirmation of loss of expression900multi-cohort phase 2 basketvalemetostat tosylate (EZH1/2 dual inhibitor)—antitumour activity————med——partialbasketsmall moleculephase 2 activeGustave Roussy—The live SWI/SNF basket, and its SMARCB1 cohort caps prior therapy at one line, so the sequencing works if INI1 loss is confirmed after LMS-04. Two gates are unresolved: the protocol asks for bi-allelic homozygous SMARCB1 deletion, and what she has is a single frameshift call in plasma, which is a different molecular configuration; and it requires centralised IHC showing loss of expression, which has not been done. It also requires exhaustion of standard options and sits at a French site, so US access would need sponsor discussion. ——2026—NCT064986481/2advanced leiomyosarcoma or dedifferentiated liposarcoma1L or 2L+ (phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive; prior gemcitabine excluded)intact Rb expression by IHC on baseline or archival tumour (required)74phase 1/2 with randomised phase 2 componentabemaciclib + gemcitabine and docetaxelgemcitabine and docetaxelblood thymidine kinase activity time course (phase 1) and progression-free survival (phase 2)————med——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeNational Cancer Institute—Correction to the earlier row, which read this as post-induction only: the phase 2 portion explicitly admits systemic-treatment-naive leiomyosarcoma, so it is a live first-line alternative during the window before LMS-04 starts. Prior gemcitabine is disqualifying in phase 2, which cuts both ways - LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine and would preserve her eligibility, whereas starting gemcitabine/docetaxel instead would close this permanently. Entry requires intact Rb expression by IHC, a test she has not had; note this is the opposite gate from the RB1-loss CDK7 protocol, so one Rb stain routes her between the two. ECOG up to 2 accommodates the undocumented performance status. Gounder MTannir NM2026Nat CommunNCT026019502solid tumors harbouring SWI/SNF alterations (INI1-negative cohort)2L+INI1/SMARCB1 loss by IHC, or bi-allelic SMARCB1 loss by molecular testing when IHC equivocal129open-label phase 2 basket, 2-stage Green-Dahlbergtazemetostat 800 mg twice daily—objective response rate9% ORR in the INI1-negative cohort (3 partial responses of 32)———med (single-arm basket)4188200610.1038/s41467-026-69708-2weakbasketsmall moleculeapprovedEpizyme (Ipsen)—This is the trial route the SMARCB1 branch points at, and Cohort 3 took INI1-negative tumors of any histology, which would have covered a uterine leiomyosarcoma with confirmed INI1 loss. Two things hold it back: accrual is closed, and her SMARCB1 frameshift is a plasma call with no tissue confirmation, weighed against 170 consecutive uterine smooth-muscle tumours that all retained SMARCB1 (pmid:34271067). The 9% response rate is also a modest ceiling, and grade 3 or worse treatment-related events occurred in 10%. ——2025—NCT068499862advanced soft-tissue sarcoma, first line1L—45single-arm phase 2 (TAIS)tislelizumab + liposomal doxorubicin + ifosfamide—objective response rate————med——weakindicationmonoclonal antibodyphase 2 activeFudan University—Checkpoint blockade added to an anthracycline backbone in the first-line setting, with leiomyosarcoma among the listed histologies. The site is in Shanghai, so access is the binding constraint rather than eligibility. Her PD-L1 status is untested, though this protocol does not gate on it. ——2025—NCT065287692advanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma after standard chemotherapy2L+—16single-arm phase 2all-trans retinoic acid + cemiplimab—overall response rate————med——partialindicationmonoclonal antibodyphase 2 activeOhio State University (Tinoco)—Requires standard-of-care chemotherapy first, with no cap on prior lines, so this opens after LMS-04. ECOG 0-2 is permissive enough that the undocumented performance status is unlikely to exclude her. PD-L1 is untested but not required. ——2025—NCT069816372advanced soft-tissue sarcoma with disease control after first-line chemotherapymaintenance after 1L—81randomised phase 2pegylated liposomal doxorubicin maintenanceactive surveillanceprogression-free survival from randomisation————med——weakindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeNational Health Research Institutes, Taiwan—Addresses the same question the LMS-04 maintenance phase answers, in patients whose disease is controlled after first-line chemotherapy. She would only reach it after induction, and cumulative anthracycline exposure from LMS-04 would need accounting against the liposomal dose. Taiwanese sites put it outside her geography band. ——2025—NCT067979991/2metastatic or unresectable soft-tissue sarcoma after 1-2 lines2L+—270first-in-human phase 1/2ADCE-D01 (uPARAP/Endo180-directed antibody-drug conjugate)—maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase 2 dose————low——partialindicationADCphase 1 activeAdcendo ApS—A sarcoma-dedicated ADC that takes any histology after one to two prior cytotoxic lines, so LMS-04 alone would qualify her. ECOG 0-1 is required and hers is an assumption, which is the axis to close before screening. No biomarker gate at entry. ——2025—NCT069354093relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma2L+B7-H3 (CD276)117randomised phase 3HS-20093 (B7-H3 ADC)gemcitabine + docetaxelprogression-free survival by independent review————med——nonecross-tumorADCphase 3 activeHansoh BioMedical—Osteosarcoma only, so she cannot enrol. It is here because it is the first randomised phase 3 test of a B7-H3 ADC in a sarcoma, and the read-out is what the board will want when weighing whether a B7-H3 stain is worth ordering for her. Informational, not an option. ——2025—NCT069424422advanced clear cell sarcoma, HLA-A*02:01 positive2L+HLA-A*02:01 positive47randomised phase 2tebentafusp (gp100 x CD3 ImmTAC)physician's choicedisease response————med——nonecross-tumorbispecific otherphase 2 activeSarcoma Alliance for Research through Collaboration—Her allele is the entry criterion, but the histology is fixed to clear cell sarcoma, which shares melanocytic biology and therefore gp100 expression; a leiomyosarcoma does not. Not enrollable. It earns a row because it is the clearest current example of an HLA-A*02:01-gated ImmTAC being moved into a sarcoma, and it shows the pathway a leiomyosarcoma cohort would follow if an antigen were found. ——2025—NCT071565651relapsed and refractory advanced soft-tissue sarcoma2L+FAPi PET/CT or PET/MRI uptake in a measurable lesion (required)30phase 1 dose escalation with imaging selection[225Ac]RTX-2358 (FAP-directed alpha-emitting radioligand), with [64Cu]LNTH-1363S imaging—treatment-emergent adverse events————low——partialbasketradioligandphase 1 activeRatio Therapeutics—A therapeutic alpha-emitter, not an imaging study: the copper-64 agent is the selection scan and the actinium-225 conjugate is the treatment. Any soft-tissue sarcoma histology qualifies after one prior regimen, and the biomarker is a FAP PET signal rather than a stain, which sidesteps the tissue-availability problem entirely. FAP is on her biomarker survey as an untested stromal target, and mesenchymal tumours carry it on the malignant cells themselves, so the prior for a positive scan is reasonable. ——2025—NCT067107561/2locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors including sarcoma2L+[203Pb]Pb-PSV359 SPECT/CT uptake in at least one known lesion at 1 hour112phase 1/2 theranostic pair[212Pb]Pb-PSV359 (FAP-α-directed alpha-emitting radioligand), gated by [203Pb]Pb-PSV359 imaging—safety and tolerability————low——partialbasketradioligandphase 1 activePerspective Therapeutics—Sarcoma is a named condition and entry turns on a lead-203 scan showing uptake, which is a functional gate she can be tested for without another biopsy. The lead-212 arm delivers the therapeutic alpha dose, so this is a treatment protocol with an imaging selection step rather than a diagnostic study. US sites, ECOG 0-1 required, and progression on or absence of standard therapy is the line criterion. ——2025—NCT074177612progressive IDH-mutant grade 2-4 astrocytoma with confirmed ATRX and p53 mutation2L+ATRX mutation by IHC or NGS plus p53 mutation (required)—single-arm phase 2tuvusertib (ATR inhibitor) monotherapy—response by RANO 2.0————low——nonecross-tumorsmall moleculephase 2 activeGrupo Español de Investigación en Neurooncología—Not enrollable - astrocytoma only, Spanish sites. It is the only registered trial anywhere that uses ATRX mutation as the entry gate for an ATR inhibitor, which is exactly the selection logic the preclinical ALT row proposes for her tumour type. Its read-out is the nearest future test of that thesis, and if her own tissue NGS shows ATRX loss the result becomes directly decision-relevant. Cote GMShapiro GI2025Clin Cancer ResNCT037180912molecularly selected advanced solid tumors; cohort T1 was ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma2L+ATRX mutation by NGS (LMS cohort); ATM, replication-stress genes, SDH in other cohorts—translational phase 2, four molecularly defined cohorts with paired biopsiesberzosertib (ATR inhibitor) monotherapy, 240 mg/m2 IV twice weekly—progression-free survival and pharmacodynamic target engagementATRX-mutant LMS cohort progressed within 4 months; longest disease control was in SDH-mutant GIST (median PFS 229 days)———med (single-arm, small cohorts)3945375610.1158/1078-0432.CCR-24-1867weakbasketsmall moleculephase 2 activeMassachusetts General Hospital—The direct clinical test of the ATR-inhibition-for-ALT idea in her exact histology: an ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma cohort built on the same ALT rationale the preclinical file carries. It read out negative for monotherapy, with progression inside 4 months despite biopsy-proven target engagement, and on-treatment SLFN11 expression rather than ATRX status tracked with what benefit there was. Her own ATRX and ALT status remain untested, so this row bounds the branch rather than closing it - the open question after this result is combinations, not more monotherapy. ——2024—NCT062771542advanced soft-tissue sarcoma, first line1L—148phase 2MASCT-I (autologous dendritic cell and cytokine-induced killer cell therapy) + doxorubicin + ifosfamidedoxorubicin + ifosfamideprogression-free survival————med——weakindicationotherphase 2 activeHRYZ Biotech—First-line and leiomyosarcoma is a listed histology, so the line axis matches the window she is in now. Sites are in China, which puts it outside her US geography band, and the cell product is manufactured locally. Included so the first-line cell-therapy option is on the record rather than silently absent. ——2024—NCT066995761badvanced bone and soft-tissue sarcoma1L (dose-expansion) or 2L+B7-H3 (not required for entry)448phase 1b combination dose escalation and expansion (ARTEMIS-103)HS-20093 (B7-H3 ADC) + anlotinib, epirubicin, or adebrelimab—maximum tolerated dose————low——weakindicationADCphase 1 activeHansoh BioMedical—One of the few B7-H3 ADC protocols with a cohort that takes patients who have had no prior treatment for advanced disease, which is the situation she is in right now. B7-H3 is on her biomarker survey and untested, though this protocol does not require it for entry. Chinese sites and a not-yet-recruiting status make the practical odds low. ——2024—NCT065717342metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma and other sarcomas2L+—73phase 2zanzalintinib (XL092)—progression-free survival————med——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeNorthwestern University—A next-generation multikinase inhibitor in the same class as the approved pazopanib, with a dedicated leiomyosarcoma cohort. Prior systemic therapy is expected, so this belongs to the post-LMS-04 list. Antiangiogenic toxicity intersects with her undocumented pulmonary reserve and high-altitude baseline. ——2024—NCT063084191advanced leiomyosarcoma, or sarcoma with TSC1/TSC2 loss2L+TSC1/TSC2 loss (alternative entry route)18phase 1 dose findinggemcitabine + nab-sirolimus—safety and adverse events————low——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 1 activeM.D. Anderson Cancer Center—Leiomyosarcoma patients enter on histology without needing a TSC alteration, but one prior systemic therapy is required, so this is a post-induction seat. ECOG 0-2 accommodates the undocumented performance status. Nab-sirolimus is approved in PEComa, which makes the agent obtainable off-label independent of the trial. ——2024—NCT062424701advanced solid tumors including sarcoma2L+B7-H3 (CD276), correlative250phase 1 dose escalation and expansionMGC026 (B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate)—adverse events and dose-limiting toxicity————low——partialbasketADCphase 1 activeMacroGenics—Sarcoma is named in the eligible tumor list and entry does not require a B7-H3 result, so she could be screened on histology alone. B7-H3 is on her biomarker survey and untested; 97% of soft-tissue sarcomas stain positive (pmid:39478506), so the prior is high but the value is unproven at entry. Archival tissue is acceptable where a fresh biopsy is unsafe. ——2024—NCT065511421advanced or metastatic solid tumors2L+B7-H3 (CD276), central testing where tissue available845phase 1a/1b modular study (EMBOLD)GSK5764227 (risvutatug rezetecan, HS-20093), alone or with platinum or checkpoint blockade—adverse events————low——partialbasketADCphase 1 activeGlaxoSmithKline—A pan-tumor B7-H3 ADC programme with US sites, open to advanced solid tumors after progression on available standard therapy. Combination cohorts allow up to three prior lines, monotherapy requires exhaustion of standard options, so the line she is at determines which module fits. ECOG 0-1 with no deterioration in the preceding fortnight is required. ——2024—NCT059993961advanced colorectal, breast, penile carcinoma and sarcoma2L+B7-H3 (CD276)89first-in-human phase 1CC-3 (CD276 x CD3 bispecific antibody)—safety and adverse events————low——weakcross-tumorbispecific otherphase 1 activeGerman Cancer Research Center / University of Tübingen—Sarcoma is listed among the conditions but the registered eligibility text is written around heavily pre-treated colorectal cancer, so which sarcoma patients the sarcoma cohort actually takes is not readable from the registry. German sites. Kept because it is the only T-cell-engager format against B7-H3 that names sarcoma at all. ——2024—NCT064448802MUC16-expressing SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma or epithelioid sarcoma2L+loss of SMARCB1 by IHC plus serum CA-125 ≥ 70 U/mL or MUC16 IHC H-score > 2515phase 2 with two histology cohortsubamatamab (MUC16 x CD3 bispecific), alone or with cemiplimab—safety and adverse events————low——nonecross-tumorbispecific otherphase 2 activeM.D. Anderson Cancer Center—SMARCB1 deficiency is the platform gate, but the two cohorts are closed to renal medullary carcinoma and epithelioid sarcoma, so a uterine leiomyosarcoma is out regardless of INI1 status. Included because it shows SMARCB1-deficiency being used as an enrolment handle for an agent whose own target is unrelated, which is the pattern to watch if the INI1 stain comes back negative. ——2024—NCT064022011selected advanced solid tumors, MAGE-A4-expressing2L+HLA-A*02:01 positive plus MAGE-A4-positive tumor42first-in-human phase 1CDR404 (MAGE-A4 x CD3 T-cell engager)—dose-limiting toxicity————low——partialbasketbispecific otherphase 1 activeCDR-Life AG—An off-the-shelf antibody format riding the same HLA-A*02:01 restriction as the TCR-T products, with no apheresis and no lymphodepletion, which is a real practical difference for a patient who has not started chemotherapy. Two conditions stand between her and screening: MAGE-A4 expression, untested, and relapse from or refractoriness to standard therapy, which she has not reached. The 'selected' tumor list is not spelled out in the registry, so whether uterine leiomyosarcoma is on it needs a call to the sponsor. ——2024—NCT057116151metastatic leiomyosarcoma and selected soft-tissue sarcomas (MFS, UPS, synovial, DDLPS)2L+——phase 1 dose escalation with mandatory paired biopsiespeposertib (DNA-PK inhibitor) + low-dose pegylated liposomal doxorubicin—safety and recommended phase 2 dose————low——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 1 activeNational Cancer Institute—Despite the doxorubicin backbone this is not a first-line door: the protocol requires at least one prior line, so she reaches it only after LMS-04. The sharper constraint is the anthracycline cap, cumulative doxorubicin at or under 360 mg/m2 before enrolment; six full LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m2 land exactly on that limit, so whether this seat survives induction depends on cycle count and any dose reductions, and her team should know that before cycle six. ECOG up to 2 accommodates the undocumented performance status, and the mandatory biopsy needs disease amenable to sampling, which her pulmonary pattern should permit. D'Angelo SPVan Tine BA2024LancetNCT040447682advanced synovial sarcoma or myxoid round-cell liposarcoma2L+HLA-A*02:01/02:02/02:03/02:06 positive plus MAGE-A4 expression ≥1+ in ≥10% of cells by central IHC52open-label single-arm phase 2 (SPEARHEAD-1)afamitresgene autoleucel (MAGE-A4 TCR-engineered T cells)—overall response rate37% overall response rate (19 of 52); 39% in synovial sarcoma24.0051.00—med (single-arm)3855472510.1016/S0140-6736(24)00319-2nonecross-tumorotherapprovedAdaptimmune / USWM—She clears the allele gate but not the histology one: the trial took synovial sarcoma and myxoid round-cell liposarcoma only, and the Tecelra label is narrower still at synovial sarcoma alone. Prior anthracycline or ifosfamide is also required, which she has not had. Its value here is the MAGE-A4 threshold it established, ≥1+ staining in ≥10% of cells by central IHC, which is the bar any MAGE-A4 stain she orders should be read against. ——2023—NCT060882903metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, first line1L—469randomised phase 3 (LMS-05)lurbinectedin + doxorubicindoxorubicinprogression-free survival by independent review————med——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 3 activePharmaMar—A direct first-line competitor to the doxorubicin/trabectedin plan, and she meets the indication and line criteria. Accrual has closed, so this is a comparison she will read about rather than a seat she can take. Lurbinectedin is approved in small-cell lung cancer, which makes an off-label conversation possible independently of the trial. ——2023—NCT054327912/3advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after prior therapy2L+—74randomised phase 2/3olaparib + temozolomideinvestigator's choice of standard chemotherapyprogression-free survival————med——partialindicationsmall moleculephase 3 activeNational Cancer Institute—The randomised confirmation of NCI 10250 in the same histology, which is the study that would settle whether the phase 2 response rate holds up. Prior therapy is required and accrual has closed. Worth tracking for the read-out rather than for a seat. ——2023—NCT060746922metastatic or advanced high-grade bone and soft-tissue sarcoma2L+—86single-arm phase 2fluzoparib + camrelizumab with concurrent stereotactic body radiotherapy—6-month progression-free survival rate————med——weakindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeRuijin Hospital—Combines the PARP route with the radiotherapy question her oncologist has kept open for the pulmonary disease, in high-grade sarcoma of any histology after at least one systemic line. Chinese sites. The infiltrative radiologic pattern in her lungs may complicate whether her lesions are SBRT-targetable, which is a planning question independent of this protocol. ——2023—NCT054207271soft-tissue sarcoma progressing after standard therapy2L+[68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT uptake in tumour neovasculature14phase 1 theranostic, vascular-disruption approach[177Lu]Lu-ITG-PSMA-1, selected by [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT—imaging result on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT————low——weakindicationradioligandphase 1 activeCentre hospitalier universitaire vaudois (Prior)—The registered primary endpoint is an imaging measure, which reads like a diagnostic study, but a therapeutic lutetium-177 dose is administered and the target is sarcoma neovasculature rather than the tumour cell, so it is a therapy protocol under the theranostic rule. Fourteen patients, completed, Swiss single centre. Kept as proof that PSMA-directed radioligand therapy has been attempted in soft-tissue sarcoma at all, which is otherwise invisible. ——2023—NCT056914911/2advanced solid tumors; dose escalation admits soft-tissue sarcoma as a temozolomide standard-of-care histology2L+MGMT promoter hypermethylation, or a histology where temozolomide is standard per guidelines (soft-tissue sarcoma qualifies)—phase 1/2, dose escalation then MSS colorectal phase 2tuvusertib (ATR inhibitor) + temozolomide—safety and recommended phase 2 dose————low——partialbasketsmall moleculephase 1 activeNational Cancer Institute—The one live US seat the ATR sweep found that she could plausibly occupy: the dose-escalation arm takes soft-tissue sarcoma without an MGMT result because temozolomide is guideline-standard in the histology. It requires progression after available therapies, so it opens after LMS-04, and the mandatory biopsy and ECOG up to 2 are both workable. Any ALT-based rationale for putting her here specifically is conditional on ATRX/ALT testing she has not had; the entry criteria themselves do not ask for it. Ingham MSchwartz GK2023J Clin OncolNCT038800192advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after at least one prior line2L+homologous recombination deficiency (correlative, not required for entry)22single-arm phase 2 (NCI protocol 10250)olaparib + temozolomide—confirmed objective response rate27% overall objective response rate (6 of 22); median PFS 6.9 months———med (single-arm)3746745210.1200/JCO.23.00402partialindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeNational Cancer Institute / Columbia University—Her exact histology, and the response rate is the strongest signal any targeted combination has produced in uterine leiomyosarcoma. It requires at least one prior line, so it belongs to the post-LMS-04 list rather than the window she is in. Entry did not depend on a homologous-recombination result, but her HRD and BRCA status is unmeasured and would inform how likely she is to be in the responding subset. ——2022—NCT052868011/2relapsed or refractory SMARCB1- or SMARCA4-deficient tumors2L+SMARCB1 (INI1) or SMARCA4 deficiency by institutional IHC, or molecular confirmation where IHC is equivocal86phase 1/2 with adult phase 2 cohortstiragolumab + atezolizumab—dose-limiting toxicity and response————med——weakbasketmonoclonal antibodyphase 2 activeNational Cancer Institute—The eligibility list ends with 'other SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 deficient tumors', which is an explicit histology-agnostic door for a confirmed INI1-negative uterine leiomyosarcoma. Institutional IHC is the accepted evidence, so the INI1 stain the validator ordered would be the exact document required. Accrual has closed, which is why this is weak rather than partial. ——2022—NCT053557531locally advanced or metastatic SMARCB1-perturbed solid tumors2L+SMARCB1-null tumor49phase 1CFT8634 (BRD9 degrader)—frequency and severity of adverse events————low——nonebasketotherdiscontinuedC4 Therapeutics—The second BRD9 degrader to stop in SMARCB1-null disease, terminated after phase 1. Its ECOG ceiling was 2, which would have been unusually forgiving for her undocumented performance status. Included as mechanism context for how thin the SMARCB1-directed pipeline has become outside EZH2. ——2022—NCT048078162metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, up to 3 prior lines2L+——randomised phase 2, gemcitabine with or without berzosertibberzosertib + gemcitabinegemcitabineprogression-free survival————med——weakindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeInstitut Bergonié—The combination form of the ATR question in her histology: randomised, leiomyosarcoma-specific, chemotherapy backbone. Accrual is complete and no result is indexed yet as of August 2026, so this is a read-out to watch rather than a seat, and it is the study most likely to say whether ATR inhibition adds anything after the monotherapy cohort failed. Its ECOG ceiling was 0-1, the axis her chart leaves undocumented, and it excluded prior gemcitabine. Pautier PFrench Sarcoma Group2022Lancet OncolNCT029973583metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, first line1L—150randomised open-label phase 3 (LMS-04), French Sarcoma Groupdoxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenancedoxorubicin monotherapyprogression-free survivalHR 0.41 for progression or death0.290.58<0.0001low risk of bias (randomised phase 3, open-label)3583513510.1016/S1470-2045(22)00380-1strongindicationsmall moleculeapprovedGustave Roussy / French Sarcoma Group—This is the evidence behind the regimen her sarcoma oncologist has already planned, and she matches it on every axis the trial screened: metastatic leiomyosarcoma, no prior systemic therapy, uterine primaries made up a majority of the enrolled population. The trial capped performance status at ECOG 0-1, which her chart does not document; the ECOG 1 in the profile is an intake assumption. Baseline LVEF is also undocumented and is mandatory before an anthracycline. ——2021—NCT043831192metastatic or locally advanced leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline2L+—100randomised phase 2 with observational cohorttrabectedingemcitabinegrowth modulation index————med——weakindicationsmall moleculephase 2 activeItalian Sarcoma Group—Anthracycline exposure is mandatory, and the LMS-04 plan would give her trabectedin as part of induction, which would likely disqualify her from a trial randomising to that same agent. Italian sites. Kept so the sequencing conflict between the planned induction and later trabectedin trials is visible. ——2021—NCT049657531advanced synovial sarcoma or SMARCB1-loss tumors1L or 2L+bi-allelic SMARCB1 alteration or corresponding protein loss55phase 1 dose escalationFHD-609 (BRD9 degrader)—treatment-emergent adverse events————low——nonebasketotherdiscontinuedFoghorn Therapeutics—Terminated, so nothing is enrollable here. It took 'other solid tumors with SMARCB1 loss' on documented bi-allelic alteration or protein loss, which is the same door she would have knocked on. Kept so the board sees that the BRD9-degrader route into SMARCB1-deficient disease has already been tried and stopped. ——2021—NCT049396101/2advanced solid tumors with FAP-2286 uptake2L+[68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET uptake (required)222phase 1/2 theranostic (LuMIERE)[177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286, selected by [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET—dose-limiting toxicity————low——partialbasketradioligandphase 2 activeNovartis (Clovis Oncology)—A beta-emitting FAP radioligand open to solid tumors by uptake rather than histology, with the gallium-68 scan acting as the selection gate and the lutetium-177 conjugate as the therapy. Whether the tumour-type cohorts still open include sarcoma needs confirming with the sponsor, since the registry lists only 'solid tumor'. Crossfire from a beta emitter does not require every cell to express the target, which is the argument for keeping this class in play when expression is heterogeneous. ——2020—NCT042624661/2selected advanced solid tumors, PRAME-positive2L+HLA-A*02:01 positive plus PRAME-positive tumor410phase 1/2, monotherapy and checkpoint-inhibitor combinationsbrenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC)—dose-limiting toxicity and response————med——weakbasketbispecific otherphase 2 activeImmunocore—Entry is her allele plus a PRAME-positive tumor, with no cell manufacturing and no lymphodepletion, which makes it the lower-intensity way to use the same restriction. Accrual has closed, so this is now precedent rather than a seat. PRAME remains untested on her tissue. ——2020—NCT039652341/2sarcoma metastatic to the lungsn/a (locoregional)—99phase 1/2 of pulmonary suffusion with metastasectomypulmonary suffusion with cisplatin plus metastasectomy—incidence of local toxicity————low——weakindicationotherphase 2 activeRoswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center—Aimed at minimal residual disease in the lung after metastasectomy, with ECOG ≤2 and no requirement for histologic confirmation of every nodule. docs.title: Research question
docs.text: In metastatic urothelial carcinoma progressing on pembrolizumab maintenance after a 25-month first-line complete response to enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, what investigational interventions could target HER2, Nectin-4, TROP2, TP53 R175H with HLA-A*02:01, FGFR3 (unread), or the mesothelin / MUC1 / PRAME / FAP / ARID1A research leads, gated on validated HER2 IHC reconciliation of the current tumor?

docs.title: Patient profile (scrubbed)
docs.text:
• Primary site / histology: bladder, high-grade muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma, poorly differentiated (focal plasmacytoid areas at diagnosis; pleomorphic giant cells in the 2025 recurrence). Separate prostate primary treated 2020, no evidence of disease.
  • Stage: IVB at diagnosis 2023-11 with liver metastases; CR on 1L therapy 2024-08; current disease oligometastatic nodal (biopsy-proven left para-aortic node plus probable perivesical node), treated with SBRT 2026-06.
  • ECOG: 1
  • Biomarkers (confirmation status as recorded):
    • HER2 — ihc_pending, DISCORDANT. Three concordant validated IHC 3+ results (primary 2023-11, liver met 2023-11, recurrence 2025-03) against a weak HER2 signal on research-grade MXIF of 2026-08 nodal tissue. Repeat validated IHC drawn 2026-08; tier not yet in the record. Decision resolution: validated IHC (4B5 or equivalent) with reflex ISH if 2+, on contemporary tissue.
    • Nectin-4 — confirmed historically (95-100% membranous, 2023/2025); current expression after ~25 months of EV unknown; 2026-06 Nectin-4 imaging read not in the record.
    • TROP2 — ihc_pending, low positive (weak) on 2026-08 research MXIF; validated IHC drawn, tier unretrieved.
    • Mesothelin, MUC1 — ihc_pending, strong on 2026-08 research MXIF only; no validated stain.
    • PRAME — unknown; 2026-08 PRAME-directed imaging result not in the record. HLA-A*02:01 confirmed.
    • FAP (stromal) — unknown; the one FAPi PET on record (2025-09) showed no FAP-avid urothelial carcinoma.
    • TMB 12.4 mut/Mb (institutional panel; cross-assay hedge vs the FoundationOne-validated threshold). MSS. MAGE-A4 negative.
    • Somatic mutations: ARID1A, TERT promoter, TP53 (R175H seen in plasma ctDNA at 0.09% VAF, 2025-06). The tissue report counts exactly one OncoKB-actionable alteration and never names it; FGFR3 status is absent from the derived record.
    • ctDNA: chronically positive on two tumor-informed platforms, rising into 2026-06, then two zero Signatera draws after SBRT (minor internal conflict in the ops summary).
  • Prior therapy: EV + pembrolizumab 1L (CR, ~25 months; EV stopped 2025-12 for neuropathy), pembrolizumab maintenance (PD 2026), intravesical BCG, TURBT x3, two personalized neoantigen vaccine programs (peptide + mRNA, ongoing), SBRT 2026-06.
  • Current therapy: T-DXd (2 doses, severe nausea/bloating after dose 2; continuation under review), mRNA vaccine series, pembrolizumab on hold, metformin, amylase/lipase surveillance q3-4wk.
  • Organ function flags: unresolved 2026-03 vs 2026-06 chest CT discrepancy (outside read suggestive of fibrosis/ILD vs no pneumonitis); recovered 2025 pancreatitis (lipase peak 384 U/L); chronic CIPN from EV; creatinine/eGFR not in the available record.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
• Efficacy/toxicity weight: 0.7 (efficacy-leaning; all preferences INFERRED from the record, to confirm)
  • Toxicity vetoes (inferred): severe peripheral neuropathy (MMAE payloads, platinum/taxane backbones); severe GI toxicity / highly emetogenic regimens; ILD/pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoring; pancreatitis-risk agents
  • Modality constraints: no geographic/logistical constraints evident; intensive experimental modalities acceptable, including cell therapy (apheresis banked)
  • Free text: strongly experimental-leaning; surface trials prominently; tumor tissue is scarce (prefer blood/imaging screening); three near-term decision gates — reconcile HER2, T-DXd stop/continue on ctDNA and tolerability, retrieve the full NGS report
  • Trials preferred: yes

docs.title: Target validation paths
docs.text: Two orders decide most of this case and neither is a new test. A validated HER2 IHC was drawn in 2026-08 and only its tier is missing from the record; that tier governs whether trastuzumab deruxtecan continues on the tumor-agnostic footing written for IHC 3+, and whether the HER2 ADCs gated at 2+ or 3+ (the disitamab vedotin class) are reachable at all. The second is a records request for sequencing already performed between 2023 and 2025, which carries the FGFR3 and FGFR2 status behind erdafitinib (THOR, NCT03390504), the identity of the single OncoKB-actionable alteration the 2023 report counts without naming, and the ERBB2 copy number. If the tier comes back low and the sequencing returns nothing actionable, both of those branches close, and what remains are research-grade stains that have to be validated before anything can be screened against them.

docs.title: HER2
docs.text: Ask for the validated HER2 IHC (clone 4B5 or equivalent, reflex ISH at 2+) reported as a tier with tumor content stated. Retrieval of the 2026-08 report comes before any re-stain, because the stain already exists. Three IHC 3+ results describe 2023 and 2025 tumor, while the only read of the current tumor is a weak research-grade multiplex immunofluorescence signal, which is not a validated HER2 assay and settles nothing in either direction. The 2026-08 nodal core carries 5-10% tumor content and can under-read a membrane stain, so run the 2025-03 recurrence block alongside it with tumor content reported for each. That pairing is what separates real antigen loss from a tumor-poor specimen. ERBB2 copy number sits unnamed among the 12 and 13 copy-number alterations counted in the 2023 reports and refines the tier call; it rides on the same retrieval and on the next plasma draw. Serial tumor-informed ctDNA on both existing platforms (Signatera, NeXT Personal) is the other half of the continue-or-stop question on trastuzumab deruxtecan, and the conflicting 2026-06 and 2026-07 zero draws need reconciling against the source reports before the kinetics mean anything.

docs.title: ARID1A / TERT promoter / TP53
docs.text: The retrieval of the full sequencing reports is the highest-yield order in this workup and costs no tissue. Roughly 15-20% of metastatic urothelial carcinoma carries an FGFR3 alteration, and that status gates erdafitinib (NCT03390504); the derived record does not contain it. The same request closes the NTRK, RET and BRAF codon 600 questions behind larotrectinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, selpercatinib and dabrafenib plus trametinib, returns somatic homologous-recombination status next to the ARID1A synthetic-lethality hypothesis, and supplies the exome data for the TMB recomputation and the HLA analysis below. Expect most of those to read negative. That is the normal result for rare alterations in this disease, and the case for reading them is that the answers already exist. Two practical caveats: an FGFR3 alteration found on a laboratory-developed panel may still need confirmation on the approved companion assay before treatment, and a DNA-only panel reporting no structural variants does not close NTRK, whose breakpoints sit in large introns. If the reports cannot be released, a comprehensive plasma panel answers the FGFR3 question without touching tissue, though fusion coverage has to be checked before a negative is trusted.

docs.title: Nectin-4
docs.text: Both stains, 95-100% membranous, predate 25 months of enfortumab vedotin, and antigen downregulation is a recognized route to enfortumab resistance, so the historical result cannot carry a re-targeting decision now. The 2026-06 Nectin-4-directed imaging study has already been performed, and retrieving that read answers most of the question without spending tissue; a contemporary IHC on post-enfortumab tissue is the fallback. Retained expression keeps next-generation non-MMAE Nectin-4 agents live, and loss closes the axis cleanly rather than leaving it open as a standing maybe. Even with retained expression, MMAE re-exposure runs against the established neuropathy, so the practical question is whether a non-MMAE agent is reachable, and prior enfortumab is an exclusion in several Nectin-4 protocols regardless of expression.

docs.title: TROP2
docs.text: The validated TROP2 IHC was also performed in 2026-08 and, again, only the tier is missing, so retrieval comes first. Ask for it as a tier (percent membranous staining times intensity, or an H-score) rather than as positive or negative. The weak multiplex signal is a low positive and not a negative, and low expression predicts TROP2-directed ADC benefit less reliably than strong expression does. That is what the number changes: it sets the confidence on the datopotamab deruxtecan and sacituzumab tirumotecan class rather than opening or closing it, since TROP2-ADC development in urothelial carcinoma has not been strictly expression-gated.

docs.title: PRAME and HLA-A*02:01
docs.text: HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed, so expression is the only gate left on the PRAME ImmTAC and TCR-T class, and those protocols screen on validated IHC (clone EPR20330) or RT-PCR at a stated threshold rather than on the research imaging performed in 2026-08. RT-PCR tolerates the 5-10% tumor content of the nodal cores better than IHC scoring does. This is the gate on IMA203 via NCT03686124, the solid-tumor study, and on brenetafusp via NCT04262466. The other registered IMA203 study is restricted to cutaneous melanoma and does not apply here. NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) is the second A*02:01-restricted antigen with an open TCR-T bench and should be run off the same block in the same order. Separately, tumor HLA class I loss of heterozygosity can be computed from the existing tumor and normal exome data; somatic loss of A*02:01 would blunt every HLA-restricted approach here, the neoantigen vaccine programs included. That computation is research-grade and would not satisfy protocol eligibility on its own.

docs.title: Mesothelin
docs.text: Strong mesothelin in urothelial carcinoma is unusual enough that it either opens a serious cell-therapy option or turns out to be an artifact of an unvalidated research assay, and only a validated clinical stain (clone 5B2 or the candidate protocol's own assay, tumor content stated) separates those. Most mesothelin cell-therapy protocols run their own central assay at screening, so a local positive opens the door rather than satisfying it, and pleural and pericardial normal expression is the on-target risk a sponsor will weigh next. A serum soluble mesothelin-related peptide level is a low-priority add-on that rides a routine draw and flags a soluble-antigen sink before a CAR-T or engager protocol. Renal impairment raises that level independently of tumor, and creatinine and eGFR are absent from the record, so read any elevation against a current renal panel.

docs.title: MUC1
docs.text: MUC1 sits behind mesothelin: the same research assay, the same missing validation, a thinner therapeutic bench. Normal epithelium carries wild-type MUC1, so a strong signal only means something once the assay resolves the tumor-associated glycoform the candidate agent targets, Tn-MUC1 where that is the epitope, using the clone the protocol names. One slide on the block already being cut answers it. Until then the signal is a lead and not a result.

docs.title: B7-H3
docs.text: B7-H3 (CD276) has never been assessed in this patient, and it is the pan-cancer surface target with the deepest current trial bench. One extra slide on the cut already planned for HER2 and TROP2 is the only reason it earns tissue in a case this tissue-poor. Expression would open solid-tumor ADC and bispecific cohorts of the ifinatamab deruxtecan class, though sponsors differ on B7-H3 IHC standardization and a protocol may still require its own assay at screening, and a deruxtecan-payload agent would have to be weighed against the unresolved pulmonary findings.

docs.title: TMB
docs.text: The 12.4 mut/Mb figure came off an institutional 468-gene laboratory-developed panel, while the tumor-agnostic indication reads TMB-H by an FDA-approved test. Recomputing from the whole-exome data already generated costs no tissue and settles whether the number survives a cross-assay comparison; report the caller and the filtering rather than the bare number, because panel-derived and exome-derived values differ systematically. PD-L1 by a companion clone (22C3 pharmDx or equivalent) is worth repeating only once a specific protocol names a clone and a cutoff: the two results on file, CPS 5 on the primary against CPS 0 in the liver metastasis, are discordance rather than a number. Immune-infiltrate density (CD3, CD8, macrophages) can be re-queried from the 2026-08 multiplex run already performed, if that panel carried T-cell and myeloid markers, with post-SBRT inflammation stated as a caveat.

docs.title: Personalized neoantigens
docs.text: An IFN-gamma EliSpot on post-mRNA-series PBMCs against the 24 predicted neoepitope pools, with CD4 and CD8 deconvolution against a matched pre-vaccine timepoint, is the next readout on this axis. The only immunogenicity data so far is 2 of 14 evaluable pools at 4 months, CD4-skewed, with several pools not evaluable, which is too thin to say whether the vaccine axis is doing anything. Banked serial PBMCs mean no new collection. Pool-level results cannot name the peptide that drove a response, so plan deconvolution for any positive pool if the result is meant to guide an expansion product, and read it against the HLA loss-of-heterozygosity analysis: presentation loss would explain a flat result better than a failed vaccine would.

docs.title: FAP
docs.text: The one FAPI PET on record found no FAP-avid urothelial disease and lit up granulomatous prostate tissue instead, a classic false positive, so stromal positivity on an unvalidated multiplex assay does not make this a treatment lead. The 2026-06 repeat study has already been performed and its read costs nothing to retrieve. Recent SBRT to the nodal disease adds treatment-related fibroblast activation, which makes new uptake harder to attribute to tumor stroma. FAPI PET is not FDA approved and is available in the US mainly on research protocols, so a repeat study means an enrolling site rather than a clinical order.

docs.title: Biomarkers measured, but not to decision resolution
docs.text:
Nine markers on this list have a result on file that cannot carry a treatment decision as it stands. The target call is not what is in doubt for these; the resolution of the existing result is. A reader who conflates the two will think a biomarker is unproven when it is only under-measured. Each one has a matching order in the tables below, so none of them was dropped.

  • HER2. Three validated IHC 3+ results, all on 2023 and 2025 tissue; the current tumor has only a weak research-grade multiplex read. The validated 2026-08 IHC tier, reported with tumor content, closes it.
  • TROP2. A weak multiplex signal recorded as low expression, not as a negative. The validated 2026-08 IHC reported as a tier closes it.
  • Nectin-4. 95-100% membranous on two specimens, both predating 25 months of enfortumab vedotin. The 2026-06 imaging read, or a contemporary IHC on post-enfortumab tissue, closes it.
  • Mesothelin. Strong on research-grade multiplex immunofluorescence only. A validated clinical mesothelin IHC with tumor content stated closes it.
  • MUC1. Strong on the same research assay, with no validated tier and no glycoform resolution. A validated MUC1 IHC using the clone and threshold a candidate protocol names closes it.
  • PRAME. Imaging was performed in 2026-08 and the read is not in the record; imaging is not what a PRAME protocol screens on. Validated PRAME IHC (EPR20330) or RT-PCR at the protocol's threshold closes it.
  • TMB. 12.4 mut/Mb from a laboratory-developed panel against a label written for an FDA-approved test. TMB recomputed from the existing whole-exome data, or a companion-diagnostic-grade report, closes it.
  • PD-L1. CPS 5 on the primary against CPS 0 in the liver metastasis, both from 2023, on a laboratory clone validated as comparable to 22C3 rather than the companion assay itself. A companion-assay read on contemporary tissue closes it, and only when a protocol names a clone and a cutoff.
  • FAP. Stromal positivity on an unvalidated multiplex assay against a FAPI PET that showed no avid urothelial lesion. Quantitative FAPI uptake in the known nodal disease, read with the post-SBRT caveat, closes it.
