docs.title: ipilimumab addition to PD-1 blockade (nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg / TITAN-TCC boost strategy) (nivolumab-ipilimumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker4lowTITAN-TCC produced a 33% ITT response rate using high-dose ipilimumab boosts in urothelial patients who had already failed PD-1, and CheckMate 032 showed response climbing with ipilimumab dose to 38% at nivo1/ipi3. A deep 25-month response to an IO-containing regimen, TMB 12.4 mut/Mb, and progression only on maintenance is the profile where adding CTLA-4 has actually rescued patients. Both drugs are prescribable off-label today, with no screening assay, no manufacturing slot, and no washout beyond clinical judgment. The 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis is the honest hazard, and TITAN-TCC had two enterocolitis deaths in 83 patients, so this needs eyes-open consent rather than avoidance.Prior immune-related pancreatitis (lipase 3x ULN, 2025) makes recurrence on CTLA-4 escalation a genuine risk; the q3-4wk amylase/lipase surveillance already in place helps but does not remove it.; He progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance, so the marginal benefit of re-intensifying the same axis is unproven in him.; TITAN-TCC and CheckMate 032 both required prior platinum, which he never had; the transfer is imperfect.; TMB 12.4 was measured on an institutional panel, not the assay the TMB-H threshold was validated on. conservative3moderateBoth drugs are FDA-approved with roughly a decade of post-marketing irAE experience and management algorithms codified in ASCO and NCCN guidance, which is the safety infrastructure I want behind any next systemic move. TITAN-TCC tested the exact manoeuvre the care team is weighing, an ipilimumab boost after PD-1 failure: ITT ORR 33% (90% CI 24-42) against a prespecified 20% bar, but immune-mediated enterocolitis reached 11% grade 3-4 and accounted for both treatment-related deaths (2/83). CheckMate 032 shows the toxicity is dose-dependent, grade 3-4 TRAEs rising from 26.9% with nivolumab alone to 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3, so the gentler schedule is the defensible one here. The 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis (lipase peak 384 U/L) sits on the stated pancreatitis veto; continued q3-4wk amylase/lipase surveillance would need to be a formal condition, not a habit.Prior immune-related pancreatitis makes CTLA-4 addition a rechallenge with a steeper irAE curve; the pancreatitis-risk veto applies unless surveillance and stopping rules are protocolized up front; The doublet is off-label and off-guideline in urothelial carcinoma, so payer friction is part of the safety-of-execution picture; Neither trial population matches this course: TITAN-TCC required prior platinum and CheckMate 032 was checkpoint-naive, and this patient progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance critic2lowTITAN-TCC is the rare single-arm trial built the way I want one built: a registered primary endpoint with a prespecified 20% response threshold, met at 33% (90% CI 24-42, p=0.0049), testing the exact maneuver in question, an ipilimumab boost after PD-1 failure in urothelial carcinoma. CheckMate 032 independently shows response climbing with ipilimumab dose (38% at nivo1/ipi3 versus 25.6% for nivolumab alone), so the CTLA-4 contribution is replicated across two trials rather than read off one. Neither population matches this course: both required prior platinum, CheckMate 032 was checkpoint-naive, and progression here was on pembrolizumab maintenance, not nivolumab. Two enterocolitis deaths in 83 TITAN-TCC patients have to be weighed against the 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis.No randomized comparison anywhere in the class for this setting; TITAN-TCC's comparator is a historical nivolumab ORR from CheckMate 275, which is the ROBINS-I confounding domain by construction; Population transfer: both supporting trials enrolled post-platinum patients and this patient never received platinum; the boost data are after nivolumab failure, not pembrolizumab maintenance failure; ORR surrogate with no OS or PFS claim for the boost strategy; Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3 and treatment-related deaths 2/83 from enterocolitis, in a patient with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis and lipase surveillance still running concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakercriticqualifiedevidence_qualityI picked the rank-2 row because that is where the critic's own scale tips oddly: TITAN-TCC's 33% (pmid:36868252) is post-platinum, post-nivolumab data from a population this patient does not belong to, a transfer problem the critic lists and then ranks straight past. Meanwhile LY4052031 gets demoted to a 'screening lead' even though its target carries two randomized phase 3 OS wins (pmid:38446675) and this patient's own 25-month complete response. Qualified rather than dissent because the boost does belong on the list, just below the Nectin-4 rows; an unpublished 47% in the right population beats a published 33% in the wrong one. conservativerisktakervetotoxicityI am aiming at the rank-4 row rather than rank 1 because the T-DXd conditions largely track my own. Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg walks into two stated vetoes at once: TITAN-TCC put 11% of patients into grade 3-4 immune enterocolitis with both treatment-related deaths (2/83, pmid:36868252), in a man whose 2025 immune-mediated pancreatitis peaked at lipase 384 U/L. Veto on the ipilimumab-3 schedule specifically, lifted only for a lower-ipilimumab schedule with protocolized amylase/lipase surveillance and written stopping rules; eyes-open consent informs the risk, it does not mitigate it. conservativecriticdissenttoxicityRanking the ipilimumab boost above pertuzumab-trastuzumab gets the safety ordering backwards: a registered prespecified endpoint (pmid:36868252) does not shrink 2 treatment-related enterocolitis deaths in 83 patients for a man with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis, while the payload-free doublet carries 13+ years of post-marketing data and touches none of the four vetoes (pmid:37793085). I have vetoed the ipilimumab-3 boost schedule on the risktaker's row, and this pick survives my reading only converted to the lower-ipilimumab schedule (grade 3-4 TRAEs already 39.1% at nivo1/ipi3 in CheckMate 032, pmid:31100038) and moved below the doublet. Trial rigor is an evidence argument; the toxicity denominator stays where it is. criticconservativedissentevidence_qualityTheir rank 1 mirrors my own position, so the objection worth writing targets rank 3: the 'gentler schedule' has no efficacy evidence behind it. Every response signal in this class came from ipilimumab 3 mg/kg (TITAN-TCC ITT ORR 33%, 90% CI 24-42, pmid:36868252; 38% at nivo1/ipi3 in CheckMate 032), while the low-ipilimumab cohort of the same study responded at 26.9% versus 25.6% for nivolumab alone (pmid:31100038). Cutting the ipilimumab dose for safety deletes the only arm that ever beat monotherapy and keeps the added irAE exposure in a patient with prior immune-mediated pancreatitis. concensusiterisktakerdissentguideline_fitThe quarrel is with the rank-4 pick, not the T-DXd we both rank first. "Both drugs are prescribable off-label today" is the weakness, not the selling point: nivolumab plus ipilimumab has no listing in NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 in any line, and both supporting trials (pmid:36868252, pmid:31100038) enrolled post-platinum patients, a line this patient skipped. Once consensus runs out the endorsed route is a protocol slot, and prescribing the nivo1/ipi3 boost outside one buys TITAN-TCC's two enterocolitis deaths per 83 patients without its monitoring scaffold. concensusiteconservativequalifiedguideline_fitThe rank-1 T-DXd conditions match mine, so this lands on rank 3, where the safety case rests on borrowed authority: ASCO and NCCN irAE algorithms manage toxicity from listed regimens, and this doublet is listed nowhere in NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026. TITAN-TCC (pmid:36868252) also required prior platinum, which this patient never received, so the population mismatch the conservative names in their own third concern should have pushed the pick down rather than into rank 3 with conditions. The lower-ipilimumab schedule softens the irAE curve but does nothing about the missing listing. advocaterisktakervetopreference_fitI am passing over the T-DXd row to flag rank 4, because nivo1/ipi3 is the one pick that trips two stated vetoes at once: the TITAN-TCC boost schedule produced 11% grade 3-4 immune enterocolitis with both treatment-related deaths (pmid:36868252), squarely on the severe-GI veto, in a man whose 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis sits on the pancreatitis-risk veto. "Eyes-open consent rather than avoidance" is the right instinct about aggressiveness, and the preference file's experimental posture agrees, but that file separates aggressiveness from four specific agent-class vetoes and this schedule fails two of them. If a CTLA-4 option goes forward at all, it should be the lower-ipilimumab schedule with lipase stopping rules written into the plan, not the ipi3 boost. advocatecriticdissentpreference_fitI chose the rank-2 row because the rank-1 T-DXd conditions track the preference file's own decision gates and I have no quarrel there. The TITAN-TCC appraisal is careful about bias and silent about the patient: 11% grade 3-4 enterocolitis with both trial deaths (pmid:36868252) lands on the severe-GI veto, the 2025 checkpoint pancreatitis lands on the pancreatitis-risk veto, and neither veto appears anywhere in the rationale. Ranking a two-veto regimen above LY4052031 (nct:NCT06465069), the trial written for his exact post-EV history with a payload that clears the neuropathy veto, gets the order backwards for this patient.

docs.title: CLSP-1025 (TP53 R175H x HLA-A*02:01 T-cell engager), NCT06778863 (clsp-1025)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker5lowBoth eligibility gates are already answered in his record: HLA-A*02:01 on 2025-01 typing and TP53 R175H in plasma. An off-the-shelf engager needs no manufacturing runway, four sites sit inside his care orbit, and the preclinical package behind the format, structure-resolved specificity in Science 2021 plus the affinity work showing the engager beats CAR formats at this antigen density, is unusually deep for a first-in-human program. The only human precedent on this axis is a single TCR-T patient with a 55% regression lasting 6 months, so the shot is thin, but it aims at a truncal driver mutation the tumor cannot shed the way it can shed a surface antigen. Request tissue confirmation of R175H in parallel with screening, not as a precondition for it.The R175H call rests on one plasma read at 0.09% VAF; the sponsor's central test could simply fail to confirm it, or the variant could be subclonal.; No clinical data exist for CLSP-1025 or any agent in its class; CRS and off-tumor behavior in humans are unknown.; Dose escalation means possible enrollment at a dose nobody expects to work.; Peptide-HLA copy number per cell is very low, which the preclinical lineage itself flags as the shared obstacle. conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate3lowBoth eligibility gates are already answered in this record without cutting tissue: HLA-A*02:01 on the 2025-01 typing and TP53 R175H on the 2025-06 plasma draw. An off-the-shelf engager needs no apheresis slot and no manufacturing wait, histology is open, and four sites sit inside the patient's usual care orbit. The 0.09% VAF plasma read is thin evidence that the current clone carries R175H, and the sponsor's central confirmation is where this holds or fails, so checking whether the 2023 tissue panel specified R175H comes first. No clinical readout exists for this class yet, only its preclinical lineage, which is the risk an efficacy-leaning posture is buying here.A single 0.09% VAF plasma call is a weak basis for a whole eligibility case; tissue-level confirmation of R175H should be pulled from the existing NGS report before a screening visit.; Peptide-HLA copy number on the tumor surface is low for every agent in this class, which is the shared obstacle the preclinical work keeps running into.; Cytokine release syndrome is the expected toxicity; it does not trip any stated veto, but it does mean inpatient step-up dosing.; Tumor HLA-A*02 loss of heterozygosity is unmeasured and computable from existing exome data; if the allele is lost, this pick and the PRAME axis both weaken at once.

docs.title: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (TAPUR arm or off-label, pending ERBB2 report) (trastuzumab-pertuzumab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative2moderateBoth antibodies carry well over a decade of post-marketing safety data (trastuzumab since 1998, pertuzumab since 2012), biosimilar supply, and a payload-free toxicity profile: in MyPathway the leading events were diarrhoea 36.1%, fatigue 29.4% and nausea 22.4%, no single serious term exceeded 1.7%, and cardiac monitoring follows a standard LVEF algorithm. This is the only HER2 option in the dossier that touches none of the four stated vetoes. The tradeoff is efficacy: ORR 41.0% at IHC 3+ amplified but 25.9% overall, activity after T-DXd exposure is untested, and the TAPUR arm turns on ERBB2 amplification or overexpression documented in the still-unretrieved full NGS report. I am ranking the safer HER2 route above the more active ones and saying so plainly.Off-label and off-guideline in urothelial carcinoma; the protocolized route (TAPUR) is gated on a qualifying ERBB2 genomic report nobody has retrieved yet; MyPathway's IHC-tier gradient (41% at 3+, 8.3% at 1+, 0% at IHC 0) means the pending re-stain decides whether this option has a floor at all; No data on activity in T-DXd-exposed tumors; the basket predates that sequencing question critic4lowMyPathway is a non-randomized basket and I grade it ROBINS-I serious, but it is also the study that quantifies the HER2 tier gradient this whole case turns on: 41% ORR at amplified IHC 3+, falling to 8.3% at 1+ and zero at IHC 0, with two of the five complete responses in urothelial tumors. No cytotoxic payload means neither the neuropathy veto nor the deruxtecan ILD class problem applies, which matters when nearly every other HER2 row collides with one or both. The arm is conditional twice over: ERBB2 amplification sits unread in the 2023 NGS report, and activity of naked HER2 antibodies after progression on a HER2 ADC is undocumented in this tumor type. It earns rank 4 because the drugs are approved, access is protocolized, and the evidence base, while single-arm, is internally consistent and fully disclosed.ROBINS-I serious: open-label basket, no comparator, ORR surrogate, and KRAS status confounds the pooled estimate (28.1% wild-type versus 7.1% mutant); The urothelial signal is two complete responses inside a 263-patient pooled cohort; no urothelial-specific confidence interval exists; Conditional on an unretrieved NGS report; the same retrieval could surface an FGFR3 alteration and an approved oral option that outranks this row; No data on naked-antibody activity after T-DXd exposure; ADC-resistant tumors may have already selected against the target concensusite——did not pick— advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconservativedissentpreference_fitOur rank-1 rows agree, so I am aiming at rank 2, where the real disagreement lives. MyPathway's pooled ORR was 25.9%, the 41% belongs only to amplified IHC 3+ tumors, and nobody has tested naked HER2 antibodies after a HER2 ADC (pmid:37793085), yet this sits at rank 2 while the whole Nectin-4 axis, the one target this patient held a 25-month complete response against, goes unranked as phase-1 material. With efficacy_toxicity_weight at 0.7 and prefers_trials true in preferences.json, that is the counterweight pressed past what the preference file will bear. advocateconservativequalifiedpreference_fitThe pick itself earns a slot as the one HER2 route that touches none of the four vetoes, and MyPathway's toxicity table (pmid:37793085) backs that up. The placement is what I dispute: this file reads efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7 with "surface trials prominently and rank novel-mechanism options seriously rather than as fallbacks", yet a 25.9% overall ORR with no post-T-DXd activity data sits at rank 2, above every novel-mechanism trial in the dossier. Being the board's counterweight is a legitimate job, but even inferred preferences are the ones on file, and they point the other way.

docs.title: zanidatamab (payload-free HER2 bispecific), fallback if 3+ holds but T-DXd stops (zanidatamab)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative4lowIncluded reluctantly, as the payload-free fallback if the re-stain stays 3+ but T-DXd is stopped for tolerability: with no cytotoxic payload the neuropathy, ILD, emesis and pancreatitis vetoes do not bite, and the phase 1 safety file was benign, six grade 3 treatment-related events in 4 of 132 patients and no treatment-related deaths. Everything else fails my usual tests: first-in-human single-arm evidence, ORR 37.0% (95% CI 27.0-48.7) driven largely by biliary tract disease, and an accelerated approval dating only to 2024-11. The pan-tumor trial cohort bars prior HER2-directed therapy, so the realistic route is off-label prescription, which stands or falls with the IHC tier.Phase-1 single-arm evidence outside biliary tract cancer; response durability in urothelial carcinoma is unknown; Post-approval safety follow-up is under two years, far short of the long-tail window in which antibody-class toxicities declare themselves; Prior T-DXd closes the registered trial cohort, and the off-label payer case collapses if the repeat IHC comes back below 3+ critic——did not pick— concensusite4lowIf the re-stain confirms 3+ but GI intolerance forces a switch, the HER2 axis should not be abandoned, and zanidatamab is the payload-free way to stay on it: 37% ORR across HER2-expressing tumors in the phase 1 (NCT02892123) with almost no grade 3 toxicity, now enrolling in phase 2 (NCT06695845). No guideline lists it in urothelial carcinoma, so this is a trial-only fallback and it is ranked like one.Registered pan-tumor cohorts have barred prior HER2-directed therapy, which the current T-DXd course triggers; screening has to settle that before this option is real.; Durability outside biliary tract cancer is thin, and the 37% ORR is a phase 1 estimate across mixed histologies. advocate——did not pick—

docs.title: FGFR3 axis, conditional: retrieve NGS report; erdafitinib if altered, vepugratinib trial (NCT05614739) as the investigational arm (vepugratinib)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite2lowThe only other biomarker route both major bodies endorse in urothelial carcinoma is FGFR: the ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline interim update on first-line therapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma (Ann Oncol 2024) names erdafitinib for FGFR-altered tumours after enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, and NCCN Bladder Cancer v1.2026 lists erdafitinib for susceptible FGFR3 alterations (category 2A). docs.title: sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) phase 3 trial, NCT07419295, TROP2 axis via randomized enrollment (sacituzumab-tirumotecan)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite3lowNo guideline endorses a TROP2 agent in urothelial carcinoma today, and the class precedent is a withdrawal: Gilead pulled the sacituzumab govitecan accelerated approval on 2024-10-18 after TROPiCS-04 missed overall survival (pmid:39934055). Where consensus is absent, the guideline-aligned move is a randomized trial, and NCT07419295 is a phase 3 of sacituzumab tirumotecan against chemotherapy in exactly this post-EV, post-checkpoint space. Enrolling is the way to reach a TROP2 agent without stepping outside the evidence framework NCCN and ESMO actually operate on.The comparator arm is a taxane or vinflunine, and a taxane assignment would run straight into his established CIPN; that risk is inherent to randomization.; His TROP2 read is low-positive on a research assay; SG benefit was seen across expression levels (pmid:39086310), but weak expression stays a weaker predictor.; Back-to-back topoisomerase I payloads after T-DXd and the washout window need sponsor input before screening. advocate——did not pick—

Cross-critiques

CriticTargetAgreementDimensionComment risktakerconcensusitevetotoxicityI went after rank 3 because rank 1 matches my own position and rank 2 is a records request, not a therapy. The comparator arm of NCT07419295 is paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine, so two of the three control drugs are taxanes and preferences.json vetoes taxane backbones outright on established CIPN; consenting means accepting a coin flip he cannot afford to lose. Calling that risk 'inherent to randomization' concedes my point rather than answering it, and I take risks on upside, not on a control-arm assignment the veto already forbids. conservativeconcensusitedissentpreference_fitRandomized entry is usually the move I applaud, but the comparator arm of NCT07419295 is a taxane or vinflunine, and a coin flip that can assign a taxane to a man with established CIPN cannot honor the stated neuropathy veto; calling that risk inherent to randomization names the problem without solving it. The class this trial reaches for also sits behind a withdrawn urothelial approval, with TROPiCS-04 missing OS (HR 0.86, p=0.087) and 7% grade 5 TEAEs (pmid:39934055). If the TROP2 axis is worth a slot at all, a nonrandomized route that cannot land him on a taxane fits this preference file better than rank 3 here. advocateconcensusitedissentpreference_fitI part ways at rank 3 rather than rank 1, so this row targets the sac-TMT trial. Randomization in NCT07419295 can put him on taxane or vinflunine, both neuropathy-causing agents against his established CIPN, and the pick's own concern list calls that risk "inherent to randomization" as if that settles it. A veto the patient cannot opt out of once assigned is a reason to skip this trial for him, not a caveat to enrolling; a guideline-clean process does not make the comparator arm preference-clean.

docs.title: FT825 / ONO-8250 (off-the-shelf iPSC-derived HER2 CAR-T) (ft825)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate4lowIf the HER2 branch continues at all, this is the version that survives the file's constraints: an allogeneic product needs no apheresis, prior HER2-directed therapy is not an exclusion, and there is no deruxtecan payload to argue with the 2026-03 chest CT read. Yale, MSK and Jefferson are enrolling. It still waits on the 2026-08 validated HER2 tier, because HER2 benefit tracks the stain rather than running independent of it: 61.3% response at central IHC 3+ in DESTINY-PanTumor02, and 41% falling to 8.3% at IHC 1+ in MyPathway. Conditioning chemotherapy and CRS are real, and the ongoing mRNA vaccine series has to be cleared against the prior-gene-therapy exclusion before anyone books a screening slot.Gated entirely on the pending validated HER2 tier; if the current tumor is HER2-low, the whole branch drops to cross-tumor extrapolation.; The prior cell or gene therapy exclusion is a live question given two vaccine programs, and it should be asked before rather than during screening.; Lymphodepleting conditioning in a patient with chronic CIPN and a pancreatitis history needs the toxicity conversation up front.; Phase 1 dose escalation in HER2-expressing solid tumors, with no urothelial efficacy signal to quote.

docs.title: ASP2998 (TROP2-directed STING agonist conjugate), monotherapy or pembrolizumab arm (asp2998)
docs.text:
Persona stances

PersonaRankConfidenceRationaleConcerns risktaker——did not pick— conservative——did not pick— critic——did not pick— concensusite——did not pick— advocate5lowUrothelial carcinoma is a named escalation and expansion histology with no cap on prior regimens, and prior TROP2 or topoisomerase-I exposure is permitted, so the T-DXd course does not close this door the way it closes the zanidatamab and NEOK002 rows. A STING-agonist payload is a different bet from a cytotoxic ADC and should depend less on antigen density, which suits a weak TROP2 stain; the TROPHY-U-01 biomarker analysis found benefit across expression levels, though almost everyone studied sat well above this patient's low signal. The enfortumab vedotin combination arms should be declined at first contact, and that preference stated in writing, because an MMAE arm would walk straight into the neuropathy veto. Phase 1 with no efficacy data, and an immune-agonist payload in a man with checkpoint-associated pancreatitis in 2025 means lipase surveillance belongs in the plan rather than in the follow-up.Randomization or assignment to an enfortumab vedotin combination arm would violate the neuropathy veto; the arm preference has to be settled with the site before consent.; This patient's TROP2 signal sits below almost the entire TROPHY-U-01 distribution, so expression-agnostic entry is not the same as expression-agnostic benefit.; STING agonism is an inflammatory mechanism in a patient whose 2025 pancreatitis arose on immunotherapy; q3-4wk lipase monitoring should continue on study.; The validated 2026-08 TROP2 tier is still unretrieved, and it calibrates how much weight this axis deserves.

docs.text:

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Palmieri/Santin (2026)Gynecol Oncolprimary FISH-negative endometrial carcinoma cell lines (HER2 IHC 0, 1+, 2+) and HER2 IHC 1+ and 2+ xenografts—non-binding control ADC—HER2 binding at low receptor density still delivers enough DXd to trigger double-strand breaks, supplemented by bystander transfer and ADCC.T-DXd was cytotoxic against IHC 1+ and 2+ FISH-negative lines but not against the IHC 0 line, where killing matched the control ADC. Both IHC 2+ and IHC 1+ xenografts showed growth suppression and longer survival.strongmedcross tumor only41690203DOIEndometrial models, not urothelial, and the IHC 0 result marks the floor: activity tracked expression tier rather than being independent of it. If repeat validated IHC returns HER2-low rather than 3+, this is the evidence base — weaker and less predictive of benefit than the IHC 3+ data behind the tumor-agnostic approval. Yazdi/Barok (2025)Cancer LettHER2-amplified breast (JIMT-1) and gastric (MKN7, SNU-216) lines; SCID mouse xenografts—untreated cells and cross-comparison among four HER2 ADCstrastuzumab emtansine, trastuzumab deruxtecan, XMT-1522 and disitamab vedotin, as publishedADC exposure selects drug-tolerant polyploid giant cells that downregulate HER2 protein and upregulate nectin-4, moving the vulnerable antigen from one target to another.All four HER2 ADCs induced polyploid giant cancer cells whose daughter cells carried reduced HER2 protein; JIMT-1 lost the HER2 amplicon after XMT-1522. HER2-negative tumors implanted on the contralateral flank were unaffected, placing the effect at the range of a few cell diameters.strongmedcross tumor only27166974DOIBreast and gastric lines only, no urothelial model. ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Abrahimi/Merghoub (2026)J Exp Medmultiple bladder cancer cell lines, patient-derived bladder tumor organoids, and xenograft bladder cancer models—untransduced T cells; intravenous versus intravesical deliveryintravesical instillation compared with intravenous adoptive transferA second-generation CAR built on the mesothelin scaffold engages MUC16, the physiologic mesothelin ligand, on bladder tumor cells.MSLN-28z CAR T cells were active across bladder cancer lines and patient-derived organoids, and MUC16 was enriched in tumors refractory to existing therapy. Intravesical delivery gave better tumor control than intravenous transfer while limiting systemic T-cell engraftment.strongmedpartial42360231DOIThe target engaged is MUC16, not mesothelin itself, and the delivery route was intravesical — designed for organ-confined disease, not a para-aortic node. It is the strongest bladder-specific mesothelin-scaffold data available and it does not transfer directly to systemic mesothelin CAR T dosing. Scholler/Siegel (2026)Front Immunolovarian and pancreatic tumor lines, plus a human mesothelin knock-in mouse model—conventional membrane-distal anti-mesothelin CARs (SS1, M5 lineage)—Most surface mesothelin is proteolytically shed, leaving a juxtamembrane stump; a binder against the stump neither loses its epitope to shedding nor gets decoyed by soluble mesothelin in serum.CAR 422 T cells matched conventional anti-mesothelin CARs for cytotoxicity and in-vivo activity, and retained activity against tumor cells resistant to the conventional CARs. On-target off-tumor toxicity was lower in the human mesothelin knock-in mouse.moderatemedweak42459653DOIOvarian and pancreatic models, no urothelial data, and CAR 422 is not in a trial this patient could enter. It does explain why serum soluble mesothelin is worth measuring before any mesothelin-directed product, and why binder epitope should be read off each protocol.

docs.title: M7A-DC / M7GA-DC (mesothelin-directed DARPin-MMAE conjugates)
docs.text:
intervention_id: msln-drug-conjugate · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Wang/Liu (2025)Nat Commun3D tumor spheroids and pancreatic cancer mouse models with limited mesothelin expression—conventional full-size mesothelin ADCs; PD-1 blockade alone—A DARPin against the protease-sensitive C-terminal region of mesothelin is internalized and releases MMAE, which then kills adjacent mesothelin-negative cells; the small format penetrates spheroids better than an IgG-based ADC.Both conjugates were internalized by mesothelin-positive cells and produced bystander killing of mesothelin-negative cells. M7GA-DC improved tumor control and survival in pancreatic models with limited mesothelin, and adding PD-1 blockade generated durable immunologic memory.moderatelowweak40849430DOIPancreatic models and a preclinical-only agent. Worth flagging against this patient's constraints rather than for them: the payload is MMAE, the same class that drove his chronic neuropathy on enfortumab vedotin.

docs.title: mesothelin x CD3 T-cell engager (LABC-13F08 BiTE and BiTE-secreting T cells)
docs.text:
intervention_id: ct-95 · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Kosti/Dunn (2025)J Immunother CancerMSLN-positive ovarian, mesothelioma and pancreatic cell lines; NSG mice xenografted with the same, using transduced primary human T cells—untransduced primary T cells; monovalent BiTE versus BiTE-secreting T cells—A bispecific engager crosslinks CD3 on T cells to surface mesothelin; T cells engineered to secrete it locally sustain the engager concentration inside the tumor.The monovalent BiTE was potent in vitro, and BiTE-secreting T cells controlled ovarian and mesothelioma xenografts with some monotherapy control in a pancreatic model. The secreted engager recruited non-engineered bystander T cells and drove activation-dependent killing of cells lacking mesothelin, and an inducible off-switch cleared the engineered cells.moderatemedweak40081946DOINo urothelial model, and the specific construct differs from CT-95. The antigen-independent bystander killing reported here cuts both ways — it may cover heterogeneous expression, and it is also a plausible source of off-tumor toxicity.

docs.title: DS-3939a (TA-MUC1-directed ADC, DXd payload)
docs.text:
intervention_id: ta-muc1-adc · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Takano/Agatsuma (2026)Mol Cancer Therclinical tumor tissue microarrays across cancer types, TA-MUC1-positive cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts—isotype control ADC; xenografts pretreated with other cytotoxic ADCs—The antibody reads the aberrantly glycosylated tumor-associated MUC1 glycoform rather than MUC1 protein per se, which is what separates tumor from the ubiquitous normal-tissue expression; the DXd payload then induces DNA damage and apoptosis.Tissue microarray staining put bladder among the highest TA-MUC1-positive rates, alongside lung and breast. DS-3939a inhibited growth of TA-MUC1-positive cells in vitro and caused regression in cell-line and patient-derived xenografts, including models previously exposed to other cytotoxic ADCs.strongmedpartial40635151DOIBladder appears in the expression survey but the efficacy models are not urothelial, and DS-3939a is in phase I/II (NCT05875168) rather than on this patient's trial list. The glycoform point is the actionable one: the 2026-08 MXIF read MUC1, and a TA-MUC1 clone would answer a different question.

docs.title: PRAME peptide/HLA-A*02:01-directed TCR-mimic antibody (Pr20)
docs.text:
intervention_id: brenetafusp · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Jensen/Vincent (2026)J Immunother CancerNUT carcinoma cell line panel, patient-derived xenograft, tissue microarray, and targeted immunopeptidomics with labeled peptide standardsn=5 cell lines; n=77 tissue microarray samples; n=165 sequenced patient samplesPRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative targets; BRD4::NUTM1 knockout versus parental—A TCR-based bispecific modeled on brenetafusp engages the HLA-A*02:01/SLLQHLIGL (PRAME425) complex and redirects CD3 to lyse the presenting cell.Targeted mass spectrometry detected the PRAME425 epitope in all four HLA-A*02-positive, PRAME-positive samples tested, at higher levels than the PRAME312 or PRAME462 epitopes. Both the brenetafusp-modeled bispecific and PRAME425 TCR T cells produced T-cell-mediated killing of PRAME-positive cells.strongmedpartial41644270DOINUT carcinoma, a fusion-driven tumor whose PRAME expression is oncogene-driven; nothing here says urothelial carcinoma presents PRAME425 at comparable density. It does show the epitope is directly measurable by mass spectrometry, which is a sharper readout than IHC if PRAME imaging comes back equivocal. Chang/Scheinberg (2017)J Clin InvestPRAME-positive/HLA-A2-positive human cancer and leukemia lines; mouse xenograft models of human leukemia—PRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative lines; unmodified IgG1 versus afucosylated Fc—An antibody shaped like a TCR binds the PRAME300-309 (ALYVDSLFFL) peptide presented on HLA-A*02:01, converting an intracellular antigen into a surface target.Pr20 bound PRAME-positive HLA-A2-positive cancers, and the afucosylated form drove ADCC and was effective in leukemia xenografts. Binding rose sharply after IFN-γ exposure through induction of the immunoproteasome subunit β5i, which spares the ALY epitope from destructive internal cleavage.moderatemedpartial28628042DOILeukemia xenografts, not solid tumor, and Pr20 is not brenetafusp. Two transferable points: the epitope is presented at very low copy number, and its density is IFN-γ-dependent — so a PRAME-directed agent's target may vary with the inflammatory state of the lesion, not only with PRAME transcript level.

docs.title: PRAME-specific TCR T cells with a PD1-41BB chimeric costimulatory receptor
docs.text:
intervention_id: ima203-prame-tcr-t · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Sailer/Sommermeyer (2022)Cancers (Basel)PRAME-positive tumor lines with repetitive rechallenge in vitro; PD-L1-positive melanoma xenograft in mice—PRAME TCR T cells without the PD1-41BB receptorsingle infusion of TCR T cellsA high-sensitivity PRAME TCR isolated from non-tolerized repertoires drives killing, while a PD1-41BB switch receptor converts PD-L1 engagement from inhibition into costimulation.Adding PD1-41BB increased IFN-γ secretion and cytotoxicity and prevented exhaustion under repetitive tumor rechallenge, without changing the in-vitro safety profile. A single dose cleared a PD-L1-positive melanoma xenograft that TCR T cells alone could not.strongmedweak35454906DOIMelanoma xenografts in immunodeficient mice, so the switch-receptor benefit is measured against tumor PD-L1 only, with no host immune contribution. IMA203 as trialed does not carry this receptor.

docs.title: H2-scDb (TP53 R175H/HLA-A*02:01-directed bispecific single-chain diabody)
docs.text:
intervention_id: clsp-1025 · 3 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats DiNapoli/Vogelstein (2026)J Clin Investhigher-affinity H2 scFv variants from phage biopanning, tested as bispecific antibodies and as CD28z CAR, CD3γ and TCR formats; mouse xenograft models—parental H2 scFv affinity variant across each format—Raising scFv affinity for the p53 R175H peptide-HLA complex changes engager potency and receptor function in opposite directions, because a CAR's serial engagement depends on release from a low-density antigen.Bispecific antibody killing and xenograft tumor control improved as affinity moved into the low nanomolar range, with specificity preserved. The same higher-affinity binders reduced function in every CAR format tested, through weaker T-cell activation on contact.moderatemedpartial41542775DOIXenografts only. Read alongside the disclosure that the senior group founded Clasp Therapeutics, this is the direct preclinical lineage of the CLSP-1025 engager, and it argues that the engager format — not a CAR — is the right one at this antigen density. Mog/Zhou (2024)Sci Transl Medcancer cells titrated for peptide-HLA density in vitro; mouse tumor models—conventional CARs and patient-derived TCRs against the same p53 neoantigen—A receptor combining a TCR-mimic antibody fragment for recognition with MyD88 and CD40 modules for NF-κB costimulation, sitting between a CAR's affinity and a TCR's sensitivity.Co-STAR T cells killed cells bearing low antigen densities better than conventional CARs or patient-derived TCRs. In mice, Co-STARs gave greater T-cell expansion and more durable regressions than TCRs carrying the same MyD88/CD40 costimulation.strongmedpartial38985855DOIPreclinical only, and no Co-STAR product is in a trial this patient could enter. It quantifies the shared obstacle for every p53-neoantigen agent — copy number on the cell surface — which is the reason the CLSP-1025 and NT-175 packages should be read as one problem rather than two. Hsiue/Zhou (2021)Sciencehuman cancer cell lines presenting p53 R175H on HLA-A*02:01, with T cells, and mouse xenograft models—wild-type TP53 and HLA-A2-negative cell lines—An antibody selected against the HMTEVVRHC peptide bound to HLA-A*02:01 is built into a bispecific diabody that also engages CD3, redirecting T cells against a mutant-p53-derived neoantigen.The antibody bound the mutant peptide-HLA complex with specificity resolved structurally, discriminating R175H from wild-type sequence. Despite very low peptide-HLA copy number on the cancer cell surface, the bispecific activated T cells to lyse antigen-presenting cancer cells in vitro and in mice.strongmedpartial33649166DOICell lines and xenografts, no urothelial model, and no clinical publication exists for CLSP-1025 — this paper and its successors are the entire evidence base for that trial. This patient's R175H was seen in plasma ctDNA at 0.09% VAF, so whether the current tumor clone even carries it is unestablished.

docs.title: TP53 R175H-directed TCR T cells and p53-reactive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes
docs.text:
intervention_id: tp53-r175h-tcr-t · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Kim/Rosenberg (2022)Cancer Immunol Reswhole-exome screening of metastatic solid tumors with immunologic identification of reactive T cells; TCR-transduced cells tested in vitro and in vivon=163 patients sequenced; n=78 with TP53 missense mutation; 21 unique T-cell reactivities; 39 TCRsautologous TIL without p53 reactivity; HLA-mismatched and wild-type TP53 targets—TCRs isolated against shared TP53 hotspot neoantigens recognize the mutant peptide only in the context of the matching HLA allele, making the pair — not the mutation alone — the eligibility gate.A library of 39 TCRs covered TP53 mutations shared by 7.3% of patients with solid tumors, recognizing tumor in a mutation- and HLA-specific way. Autologous TIL infused into 12 patients gave only 2 partial responses, with low-frequency, exhausted, poorly persisting p53-reactive cells; one patient given peripheral blood lymphocytes transduced with an HLA-A*02-restricted p53 R175H TCR had a 55% regression lasting 6 months.moderatehighpartial35749374DOIPubMed types this record as an editorial/comment, which is a metadata error — the text is a primary report. The single R175H/HLA-A*02 TCR-transduced patient is the closest human precedent for NT-175 and the transient response is the honest ceiling to quote; it also shows why an engineered TCR product beat unselected TIL. Malekzadeh/Deniger (2020)Clin Cancer Ressorted antigen-experienced peripheral blood lymphocytes from patients with TP53-mutant tumors, stimulated in vitro against p53 neoantigens; tumor cell line recognition assays—patients without TIL reactivity to mutated TP53; wild-type p53 and HLA-mismatched targets—Antigen-experienced circulating T cells mirror the intratumoral p53-neoantigen repertoire, so blood can substitute for tumor as the starting material for identifying reactive TCRs.All five patients with p53-reactive TIL had matching reactivity in blood, and the four without TIL reactivity had none in blood either. One culture was 78% reactive against p53 R175H on HLA-A*02:01, and TP53-mutation-specific T cells recognized tumor lines carrying the right HLA and mutation, confirming natural processing and presentation.moderatehighpartial31996390DOISmall patient numbers and no clinical outcome. Directly useful given this case's tissue scarcity: banked PBMCs and apheresis could be screened for R175H/HLA-A*02:01 reactivity without spending the one fresh-frozen tumor vial.

docs.title: lymph-node-targeted amphiphile peptide vaccine boosting of TCR T cells
docs.text:
intervention_id: personalized-neoantigen-vaccine · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Sodhi/Hartman (2026)J Immunother Cancersyngeneic mouse tumors engineered to express membrane-localized or cytoplasmic neoantigens; pan-cancer TCGA analysis of intratumoral IgG—cytoplasmic versus membrane-localized version of the same neoantigen; CD8-depleted and Fc-receptor-deficient arms—Membrane-exposed neoantigens elicit class-switched IgG that engages Fc receptors and myeloid cells, a CD4-dependent arm of vaccine efficacy that runs alongside the CD8 response.Membrane-localized but not cytoplasmic neoantigens drove class-switched IgG, myeloid activation and tumor restriction independent of CD8 T cells, requiring CD4 help, antigen-specific IgG and Fc engagement. A Trop2 T256R mutant with impaired membrane localization failed to elicit comparable vaccine-induced control, and CXCL13 or IL-21 co-expression amplified the antibody arm.moderatelowweak42097835DOIEngineered syngeneic models with defined antigens, far from a 24-peptide personalized program. Relevant because this patient's EliSpot response is CD4-skewed (2 of 14 pools) and currently read as a weak signal — this model gives CD4-dominant responses a plausible effector route, and predicts that where the epitope sits on the protein matters. Drakes/DeMuth (2024)Cancer Immunol Resestablished murine solid tumors refractory to TCR T-cell monotherapy; human TCR T cells against NY-ESO-1, mutant KRAS and HPV16 E7 in vitro—TCR T cells alone; vaccine aloneamphiphile-conjugated cognate peptide plus adjuvant given after TCR T-cell transfer, without lymphodepletionAmphiphile conjugation traffics peptide and adjuvant to draining lymph nodes, where transferred T cells are re-stimulated in situ and the endogenous repertoire is recruited alongside them.Vaccine plus TCR T cells eradicated tumors that TCR T cells alone could not, with expansion of both the transferred cells and the endogenous antitumor repertoire and no lymphodepletion. Durable protection tracked with antigen spreading to tumor antigens the vaccine did not encode.strongmedpartial38270373DOIMurine tumors plus in-vitro human confirmation; no cancer-patient data. It is the mechanistic argument for sequencing this patient's ongoing neoantigen vaccine with a TIL or TCR T product rather than running them as separate programs.

docs.title: CTLA-4 plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade — intratumoral mechanism of the doublet
docs.text:
intervention_id: nivolumab-ipilimumab · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Spranger/Gajewski (2014)J Immunother CancerB16.SIY murine melanoma—single-agent anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-L1 or IDO inhibition; FTY720-treated mice to block lymphocyte egresspermutations of anti-CTLA-4 mAb, anti-PD-L1 mAb and the IDO inhibitor INCB23843The doublet acts on T cells already inside the tumor, restoring IL-2 production and proliferation, rather than by priming new T cells in draining lymph nodes.All three doublets improved tumor control over single agents, with complete rejection in many mice and no vaccine or adoptive transfer. Priming in draining nodes rose only minimally, while tumor-infiltrating CD8 T cells regained IL-2 production and proliferation by day 3; blocking new T-cell trafficking with FTY720 preserved most of the effect.strongmedweak24829760DOIA single immunogenic murine melanoma line, and the mice were checkpoint-naive. This patient progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance, so the relevant question is whether an exhausted intratumoral pool still responds to CTLA-4 addition — which this model does not test.

docs.title: [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46-I (albumin-binder FAP radioligand)
docs.text:
intervention_id: fap-radioligand-therapy · 2 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Saito/Ono (2026)Ann Nucl MedU87MG (high FAP) and HT-1080 (low FAP) tumor-bearing mice; SPECT/CT and radioligand therapy studies—[177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46 without the albumin binder; vehiclesingle administration of [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46-I compared with [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46An albumin-binding moiety prolongs blood residence, raising tumor accumulation and dose delivered per administration; killing is by beta emission across the FAP-positive compartment rather than by receptor signaling.Binding affinity was preserved (IC50 1.5 ± 0.3 nM) while tumor accumulation and retention rose over the parent ligand. The albumin-binder version suppressed and shrank tumors where the parent [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46 did not.moderatelowweak41653396DOIGlioblastoma and fibrosarcoma xenografts where FAP is on the tumor cells themselves, not the stromal-FAP configuration seen on this patient's MXIF. The gating problem is upstream anyway: the only FAPi PET on record showed uptake in BCG-granulomatous prostate tissue and no FAP-avid urothelial carcinoma. Chen/Chen (2025)J Immunother CancerCT26-FAP syngeneic mouse tumors; immunohistochemistry and single-cell RNA sequencing of the treated microenvironment—radioligand alone, anti-PD-L1 alone, and untreated mice; 68Ga versus 177Lu label—FAP-targeted beta emission causes double-strand breaks and raises tumor PD-L1, converting the stromal compartment into an adjuvant for checkpoint blockade.177Lu-DOTA-2P(FAPI)2 induced double-strand breaks and upregulated PD-L1 more effectively than the 68Ga label. Combined with anti-PD-L1 it eliminated tumors, and rechallenged mice showed complete rejection; single-cell analysis showed more infiltrating CD8 T cells, fewer regulatory T cells, and a contribution from mature neutrophils.stronglowweak39800373DOICT26 colorectal cells engineered to express FAP, so the model bypasses the question of whether native stromal FAP delivers enough dose. It offers a mechanistic reason to pair FAP radioligand with checkpoint blockade if imaging ever confirms FAP-avid urothelial disease, and nothing more.

docs.title: ATR inhibition as synthetic lethality in ARID1A-deficient tumors
docs.text:
intervention_id: berzosertib · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Williamson/Lord (2016)Nat Communisogenic and naturally ARID1A-mutant tumor cell lines in vitro, with in-vivo confirmation—ARID1A-proficient isogenic cellsclinical-stage ATR inhibitors, in vitro and in vivoARID1A loss produces topoisomerase 2A and cell-cycle defects that leave the cell dependent on ATR checkpoint activity; removing ATR forces premature mitotic entry.ARID1A defects sensitized tumor cells to ATR inhibitors in vitro and in vivo. In ARID1A-mutant cells, ATR inhibition triggered premature mitotic entry, genomic instability and apoptosis.strongmedpartial27958275DOINo urothelial model, and the case's ARID1A alteration is reported without zygosity or protein-loss confirmation — the biomarker in these experiments is ARID1A deficiency, not the presence of a mutation call. This is the original rationale behind the ATR-inhibitor trials on the list (ART0380, tuvusertib) and remains hypothesis-grade for this patient.

docs.title: ATR inhibition in ARID1A-deficient cells — KLF5 as a modifier
docs.text:
intervention_id: ceralasertib · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Awwad/Jackson (2025)Nat Commungenome-scale CRISPR screens in ARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-proficient cells under ATR inhibition—ARID1A-proficient isogenic cells; untreated screen arm—KLF5 protects against replication stress partly by regulating BRD4 recruitment to chromatin, so KLF5 loss compounds the replication stress that ARID1A deficiency already imposes.KLF5 loss severely reduced fitness of ARID1A-deficient cells and sensitized ARID1A-proficient cells to ATR inhibition. The mechanism ran through replication stress, DNA damage, DNA-RNA hybrid accumulation and genomic instability on ATR inhibition.moderatelowweak39779698DOIScreen-based and in-vitro only. Its practical use in this case is as a caution rather than a lead: ATR-inhibitor response in an ARID1A-mutant tumor is modified by other genes, so a single ARID1A call is a thin basis for predicting benefit.

docs.title: PARP inhibition with temozolomide in ARID1A-mutated cancers
docs.text:
intervention_id: parp-inhibitor-arid1a · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Yu/Wang (2023)Cancer ResARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-proficient cancer cells; ovarian tumor xenografts carrying ARID1A mutations—temozolomide alone, PARP inhibitor alone, ARID1A-proficient cellstemozolomide combined with PARP inhibitor, in vitro and in xenograftsARID1A deficiency leaves accumulated DNA base lesions and abasic sites with delayed long-patch base excision repair, so adding a methylating agent to PARP trapping converts unrepaired lesions into double-strand breaks.ARID1A-deficient cells accumulated base lesions and abasic sites and recruited long-patch BER effectors slowly. Temozolomide alone was inactive, but combined with a PARP inhibitor it produced double-strand breaks, replication stress and fork instability, and significantly delayed growth of ARID1A-mutant ovarian xenografts.moderatelowweak37306706DOIOvarian models and a combination with no urothelial trial behind it. The negative half is the useful half: PARP inhibitor monotherapy was not the active arm, which argues against reading ARID1A loss as a PARP-inhibitor indication on its own.

docs.title: EZH2 inhibition in ARID1A-deficient cancer
docs.text:
intervention_id: ezh2-inhibitor-arid1a · 1 row(s)

ReportModelnControlDoseMechanismKey findingEffect (qual)TranslatabilityCase fitPMIDDOICaveats Yamada/Kono (2021)Gastric CancerARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-wild-type gastric cancer cell lines, including ARID1A knockdown; cell viability and colony formation—ARID1A-wild-type parental linesEZH2 inhibitors across a dose rangeLoss of the SWI/SNF subunit ARID1A leaves the tumor dependent on PRC2/EZH2-driven repression, with PI3K/AKT signaling as the downstream survival axis.EZH2 inhibitors reduced viability of ARID1A-deficient cells dose-dependently and selectively relative to ARID1A-wild-type cells. ARID1A knockdown raised phosphorylated AKT, and EZH2 downregulation normalized PI3K/AKT signaling in the deficient cells.moderatelowweak32506298DOIIn vitro only, no xenograft arm, gastric rather than urothelial. No EZH2-inhibitor trial appears on this case's list, so it stays as background for the synthetic-lethality axis rather than a route to an option.

docs.title: Manuscripts considered — urothelial-mets-her2-discordant-kndl
docs.text:
Master inventory: 48 clinical (38 included, 10 considered & excluded) + 41 pre-clinical (34 included, 7 considered & excluded) + 39 additional trial publications/registrations. One row per paper, sorted by year (newest first). Excluded rows are papers a Libby agent reviewed and chose NOT to feed to the board, with the exclusion reason captured. Toxicities use CTCAE-style term · grade · n/N · rate. Pre-clinical rows leave the toxicity cell blank by design. A printable PDF version is linked from the case Downloads section.

ReportReferenceTypeInclusionInterventionIndication / modelDesignnEffect sizeVarianceToxicities (type · n/N · rate)Case fitNotes Rosenberg/Milowsky (2026)ESMO OpenPMID 42155320clinicalincludedenfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab — 5-year follow-upCisplatin-ineligible, previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (1L)84.4% visceral disease; 55.6% with creatinine clearance <60 mL/min. Median follow-up 62.1 months.Phase 1b/2 dose escalation and cohort A (EV-103/KEYNOTE-869, NCT03288545)45ORR: 73.30 % confirmedmDoR: 22.10 monthsmPFS: 12.70 monthsmOS: 26.10 monthsOS rate: 41.50 % 5-year survival estimateconfirmed ORR—95% CI 8.4 to not estimable95% CI 6.1 to not estimable95% CI 15.5 to not estimable95% CI 26.50–56.00peripheral sensory neuropathy — 25/45 · 55.6%fatigue — 23/45 · 51.1%fatigue G>=3 — 5/45 · 11.1%alopecia — 22/45 · 48.9%lipase increased G>=3 — 8/45 · 17.8%rash maculo-papular G>=3 — 5/45 · 11.1%treatment-related skin reaction — 30/45 · 66.7%serious treatment-related AE — 7/45 · 15.6%TRAE leading to dose reduction — 15/45 · 33.3%TRAE leading to discontinuation — 20/45 · 44.4%treatment-related death G5 — 1/45 · 2.2%partialThe longest published follow-up on EV plus pembrolizumab, with 41.5% alive at five years, which is the reference class for a patient who reached complete response and then stopped for neuropathy. Per-term AE rates come from PMC full text (PMC13213747) because the abstract gives none and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT03288545. Grade >=3 lipase increase at 17.8% is worth weighing against this patient's 2025 pancreatitis. Kawahara/Nishiyama (2026)Cancer Rep (Hoboken)PMID 41578675clinicalincludedenfortumab vedotin rechallenge after toxicity interruptionMetastatic urothelial carcinoma treated at a single institution, January 2022 to December 2024 (any)48 patients treated with enfortumab vedotin; 36 developed dermatologic adverse events and 20 resumed the drug after interrupting for them.Retrospective single-institution observational cohort48AE rate: 75.00 % dermatologic AEs on initial exposure (36/48), median onset 11 daysAE rate: 65.00 % recurrence after rechallenge (13/20), generally lower grade than the first episoderecurrence of dermatologic adverse events after rechallenge——dermatologic adverse event — 36/48 · 75%dermatologic adverse event on rechallenge — 13/20 · 65%weakThe only published cohort addressing enfortumab vedotin rechallenge, and it addresses skin toxicity rather than efficacy or neuropathy. Nothing here speaks to whether re-exposure works after a 25-month response, and neuropathy, the toxicity that stopped this patient, is not the toxicity studied. Barber-Rotenberg/Tanyi (2026)Mol TherPMID 41566776clinicalincludedhuCART-meso (fully human anti-mesothelin CAR T cells)Mesothelin-expressing lung adenocarcinoma, ovarian cancer and mesothelioma (2L+)14 ovarian, 5 mesothelioma, 1 lung adenocarcinoma. No urothelial patients.Phase 1 single-arm20DCR: 60.00 % stable disease in 12 of 20; no objective responsesORR: 0.00 % maximum target-lesion reduction 41%mPFS: 12.30 weeksmOS: 26.10 weeksbest overall response————CRS — 7/20 · 35%cross tumor onlyNo objective responses in 20 patients, which is the realistic prior for conventional mesothelin CAR-T in solid tumors regardless of how strong the stain is. Sets the expectation for the mesothelin branch: a validated stain would open trial access, not predict benefit. Khattak/KEYNOTE-942 Investigators (2026)J Clin OncolPMID 42223134clinicalincludedintismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940) plus pembrolizumabResected stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma (adj)157 randomized 2:1 to combination versus pembrolizumab alone; median planned follow-up 60.3 months at the December 2025 cutoff.Randomized phase 2b (KEYNOTE-942, NCT03897881)157RFS HR: 0.51 combination vs pembrolizumab aloneEFS HR: 0.41 distant metastasis-free survivalOS HR: 0.47 favourable trend, confidence interval crosses 1Biomarker: increased TCR clonality and novel clonotypes versus pembrolizumab alone greater novel-clone expansion in patients without recurrencerecurrence-free survival hazard ratio at 5 years95% CI 0.29–0.8995% CI 0.20–0.8495% CI 0.17–1.34—No new safety signals at five years; per-term rates are not reported in this descriptive update.cross tumor onlyThe most durable randomized signal that adding an individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine to PD-1 blockade changes outcome, in resected melanoma rather than metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
