docs.title: What this page is
docs.text:
Libby searched published studies and open clinical trials for treatments aimed at the specific features of your cancer, the ones in your records. This page walks through what came back: one first step that everything else depends on, ten treatment options worth discussing with your care team, four options you may hear about that are on the page as not recommended, and a longer tail of possibilities that were looked at and set aside, with the reasons why. Where the research has real numbers, we give them in plain terms. Where it does not, we say so instead of dressing anything up.

One honest note before anything else. Almost every option on this page hinges on test results that already exist but have not been pulled out of their reports. That is unusual, and it is actually good news: the most important next move in your case costs a records request, not a treatment decision.

docs.title: What we know about your cancer
docs.text:
You have urothelial (bladder) cancer, high grade, that had spread to the liver when it was found in late 2023. First-line treatment with an antibody-drug combination plus immunotherapy worked remarkably well: the liver disease resolved completely, and that response held for about two years. The antibody-drug part was stopped after roughly 25 months because of nerve damage in your hands and feet, and this year the cancer came back in two lymph nodes in your abdomen while you were on maintenance immunotherapy. Those nodes were treated with focused radiation in June. You started a new drug, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), in July; it targets a protein called HER2 and you have had two doses, with severe nausea and bloating after the second. You also have a separate, earlier prostate cancer that was treated in 2020 and shows no sign of activity.

The single most important fact on this page is a disagreement between test results. Three separate high-quality tests, on tumor tissue from 2023 through spring of last year, all found HER2 at the strongest level (called 3+). But a research-grade imaging test run this month on the newest biopsy found only a weak HER2 signal. The research test is not an approved way to measure HER2, so it cannot overrule the three strong results, but it raises a real question: does the cancer as it exists today still carry high HER2? A proper repeat HER2 test was already done on that new tissue this month. The answer is sitting in a report that has not been retrieved yet.

Two more things sit unread in existing reports. Your 2023 tumor sequencing counted exactly one genetic change with a matching treatment, and the report in hand never says which one it is. And your records never state whether the tumor carries a change in a gene called FGFR3, which about 15 to 20 percent of cancers like yours have and which has its own approved pill.

Other features of your tumor matter for the options below. It carries very high levels of a surface protein called Nectin-4, at least it did before treatment; the drug that produced your two-year response targets exactly that protein, and long exposure can teach a tumor to dial it down, so today's level is unknown. A research test found low levels of a protein called TROP2 and strong signals for two others (mesothelin and MUC1), all needing confirmation with standard tests. The tumor has a higher-than-average number of mutations, which can favor immunotherapy. Blood tests found a trace of a mutation called TP53 R175H, and you carry the immune-system type (HLA-A*02:01) that some newer trials require. A blood test that tracks tumor DNA has been positive for a long time, rose this spring, and then read zero on two draws after the radiation, which may mean the radiation did real work; the next draws will tell.

Two health flags shape the choices below: one chest scan last year suggested possible early lung scarring while a more recent scan showed none (an unresolved discrepancy that matters because some drugs, including your current one, can inflame the lungs), and you had a mild, symptom-free bout of pancreas inflammation in 2025 that your team still monitors with blood tests.

docs.title: What you told us matters most
docs.text:
Here we have to be straightforward: you did not fill out a preferences form. Everything in this section was inferred from your records, so treat it as a set of defaults to confirm or correct, not as your words.

The record reads as strongly experimental-leaning. You are already pursuing personalized cancer vaccines, cell-therapy programs, and other investigational routes at the same time, and you have traveled internationally for testing and consults. So this page takes trials seriously as first choices, not fallbacks, and it weights effectiveness somewhat more heavily than side effects.

Four side-effect limits were inferred, and they do real work in the ranking below. First, drugs that cause nerve damage: you already have lasting numbness and hand spasms from prior treatment, so options built on that drug class were pushed down or off the list. Second, drugs that cause severe nausea and gut trouble, because that is an active problem on your current drug. Third, drugs with high lung-inflammation risk, because of the unresolved chest-scan question. Fourth, drugs that stress the pancreas, because of the 2025 episode. One practical constraint also matters throughout: your remaining tumor tissue is scarce, and the newest biopsy is only 5 to 10 percent tumor cells, so options that can be screened with blood tests, scans, or existing records were favored over ones that demand a fresh biopsy.

docs.title: The first step everyone agreed on
docs.text:
Before any treatment decision, two sets of existing results need to be retrieved and read. This was the one step with unanimous support, it involves no drug and no procedure, and everything below it hangs on the answers.

The first is the HER2 answer. The repeat, properly validated HER2 test on your newest tissue was already performed this month; only the result tier has not been pulled into your record. Retrieving it is a records request that should take days. If the tissue has to be recut and restained instead, that is about three to seven days plus paperwork. One caution to carry into the reading: the newest biopsy contains only 5 to 10 percent tumor cells, which can make a surface-protein stain read weaker than it really is. Ask that the report state the tumor content, and a second read on the tissue from last spring's recurrence is a sensible hedge against that sampling problem.

The second is the sequencing retrieval. Your existing tumor-sequencing reports, from 2023 through 2025, hold three unread answers: whether the tumor has an FGFR3 gene change (roughly a 15 to 20 percent chance, and if yes it opens a treatment door with formal guideline backing, Option 6 below), the identity of the one genetic change your 2023 report says has a matching treatment, and the tumor's HER2 gene copy number, which one of the HER2 options below turns on. All of this comes from reports that already exist. No new tissue is spent.

Why this gates everything: the HER2 result decides three of the options below, and it feeds the separate decision about whether to continue your current drug, whose approval for your situation is written for the strongest HER2 level. Study after study shows the benefit of HER2 drugs tracks the HER2 level closely; in the key trial behind your current drug, about 6 in 10 people at the strongest level saw their tumors shrink, versus fewer than 4 in 10 across all levels. And the sequencing answer could surface an option that outranks most of this page.

What if the HER2 test comes back negative or low? Then the three HER2 options below (Options 1, 5, and 7) come off the table, and your current drug loses its formal approval footing for you; it would then rest on weaker evidence borrowed from other cancer types, which is a different and less certain conversation. The rest of the options on this page do not depend on HER2 and stand or fall on their own tests. If those other doors were also to close, no retained Nectin-4, no confirmed TP53 mutation in tissue, no FGFR3 change, and negative confirmatory stains on the research leads, then this page would have nothing further to rank, because Libby's list only covers treatments aimed at your cancer's specific targetable features. Standard treatment for bladder cancer would still exist and would still be worth pursuing, but that is a separate conversation that belongs with your oncologist, not on this page.

docs.title: The options
docs.text: Every option here is investigational for your situation: a trial drug, an off-label use, or an early-stage program. The decision about continuing your current drug, T-DXd, is deliberately not ranked here, because it is an approved treatment and belongs to the standard-care conversation with your team. What this list answers is: if T-DXd stops, or when you and your team look beyond it, what targets your cancer's specific features?

docs.title: Option 1 — Zanidatamab (a HER2 antibody with no chemotherapy payload)
docs.text:
This option is only on the table if the HER2 test comes back positive at the strongest level. If it comes back negative or low, this option is off the table, along with Options 5 and 7. The rest of the page does not depend on that test.

This option carries caveats. Zanidatamab is an antibody that grabs the HER2 protein at two points at once. Unlike your current drug, it carries no chemotherapy payload, and that is the whole point of its position here: in its first human study, severe drug-related side effects occurred in only 4 of 132 people and nobody died from treatment. It touches none of the four side-effect limits above. If the strong HER2 result holds but the current drug has to stop because of the nausea, this is the gentlest way to keep treating the target.

The tradeoffs are real. In that same study, about 1 in 3 people saw their tumors shrink, but most of those people had bile-duct cancer, not bladder cancer, and nobody has measured how the drug performs after a drug like your current one. There is also a biological worry: if the cancer survived a HER2-targeted drug by reducing its HER2, an antibody with no payload could be hit even harder by that change. And the practical route is awkward, because the trial designed for this situation excludes people who have already had HER2-directed treatment, which your current drug counts as. The realistic path is off-label prescription, and insurance approval would lean heavily on that HER2 result.

docs.title: Option 2 — AKY-1189 (a radioactive particle aimed at Nectin-4)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats: it is a first-in-human study with no results of any kind yet. This treatment attaches a powerful, short-range radioactive particle to a molecule that seeks out Nectin-4, the protein your most effective treatment so far was aimed at. The radiation kills the cell it lands on and its close neighbors, so it matters less if some tumor cells have reduced the protein. That is the appeal in your exact situation: after 25 months of a Nectin-4 drug, some loss of the target is plausible, and this mechanism is the one that best survives it. The study also starts with an imaging scan that shows whether your tumor still carries Nectin-4 today, answering that open question with a scan instead of spending scarce tissue. Prior treatment with your previous drug is explicitly allowed, which almost no other Nectin-4 study permits.

Be clear about what is not known: everything. No person has published results on this drug, for benefit or for harm. The known concerns of this drug class are bone-marrow suppression (you had anemia in 2025, since corrected) and stress on the kidneys, and your current kidney-function number is missing from the record, a gap that needs closing before this conversation goes anywhere. Early joiners in a dose-finding study may also receive doses too low to work, because finding the dose is the study's purpose. Two screening hurdles apply: the study needs a measurable tumor on scans, and the radiation you had in June treated the only known sites. Sites are within reach in the Northeast. A sensible first move that costs nothing: retrieve the result of the Nectin-4 imaging you already had in June, which may answer the expression question before any screening visit.

docs.title: Option 3 — CLSP-1025 (a drug that points your immune cells at a TP53 mutation)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats: the drug class has no human results yet, and the mutation it targets has only been seen in your blood, at a very low level. This is an off-the-shelf drug (no cell collection, no manufacturing wait) that acts like a matchmaker: one end recognizes a fragment of the mutated TP53 protein displayed on tumor cells, the other end grabs your immune cells and forces the two together. It requires two things you already have on paper: the specific mutation (TP53 R175H) and the immune-system type HLA-A*02:01. A mutation like this sits deep in the cancer's machinery, so the tumor cannot easily shed it the way it can shed a surface protein. The one human precedent for attacking this exact target, with a different technology, was a single patient whose tumors shrank by half for six months.

Now the hedges, and they are load-bearing. No drug of this class has published results in people, so benefit and safety are both unmeasured; the expected side effect is an immune overreaction called cytokine release syndrome, with the first doses given in the hospital. And the mutation call itself is the weak link: it comes from a single blood test that found it in 0.09 percent of the DNA fragments examined. A trace that small is a much less sure sign than finding the mutation in the tumor itself; it could be a minor subpopulation, or it might not confirm at all when the trial's lab checks. Before any screening visit, ask your team to look for this mutation in your existing 2023 sequencing report. That is free, fast, and could firm up or quietly close this option.

docs.title: Option 4 — LY4052031 (a next-generation Nectin-4 drug, built for people in your exact situation)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats. This is an antibody-drug conjugate like the one that gave you your two-year response, aimed at the same Nectin-4 protein, but carrying a different chemotherapy payload, one that does not cause the nerve damage that forced your previous drug to stop. The study group in question was written specifically for people who already had that previous drug; prior exposure is required, not excluded. The biology also leans favorable: studies of how tumors escape your previous drug suggest they more often break the delivery machinery than discard the Nectin-4 target itself.

The headline number needs honest handling. Early results reported at a conference this year showed tumors shrinking in about half of previously treated patients at the chosen dose. That figure is unpublished, comes from a small ongoing dose-finding study run by the company, and has no error bars; numbers like this usually shrink as more patients are added. Treat it as a reason to screen, not a promise. There is also no published side-effect table yet; the payload class typically causes diarrhea, nausea, and low blood counts, which lands on your active nausea problem and needs a plan rather than a shrug. Whether a payload of this type works well right after your current drug, whose payload is a chemical cousin, is an unstudied question worth putting to the trial doctor directly. Several sites are within reach in the Northeast, screening runs on records rather than fresh tissue, and the same two hurdles as Option 2 apply: measurable disease after the June radiation, and a washout period after your current drug.

docs.title: Option 5 — Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (two well-known HER2 antibodies, no payload)
docs.text:
This option is only on the table if the HER2 test comes back positive, at the strongest level or with extra HER2 gene copies on the retrieved report. If the test reads low without extra copies, this option closes.

This option carries caveats. These are the two oldest, best-understood HER2 antibodies, used together without any chemotherapy attached, available through a structured access study or off-label. The supporting study is the clearest illustration of why the HER2 test matters so much: tumors shrank in about 4 in 10 people at the strongest HER2 level with extra gene copies, about 1 in 4 overall, fewer than 1 in 10 at the weak level, and nobody at zero. Two of the five complete responses in that study were bladder cancers. The side-effect profile is the mildest of any drug option on this page: diarrhea in about a third of people, mostly mild, with more than a decade of safety experience behind both drugs and routine heart monitoring the only standing requirement. It is the one HER2 option that touches none of your four side-effect limits.

The open questions: that study was not randomized, benefit was measured by tumor shrinkage rather than survival, and nobody has tested these antibodies after a drug like your current one, so a tumor that dodged your current drug by reducing HER2 would likely dodge this too. What is contested about its placement is a values question worth settling yourself: it trades the higher, shakier upside of the newer trial options for a modest, better-documented benefit with gentler side effects. Where it sits in your personal order depends on how you weigh that trade, and on two results from the first step: the HER2 tier and the gene copy number.

docs.title: Option 6 — The FGFR3 route: a records request away from real
docs.text:
This option carries caveats: it only exists if the sequencing retrieval finds an FGFR3 gene change, which is roughly a 15 to 20 percent chance. If the change is there, this becomes one of the strongest doors in the case, and the only non-HER2 route with formal guideline backing for exactly your situation. There is an approved daily pill for FGFR-altered bladder cancer (that belongs to the standard-care conversation with your team), and there is a trial of a next-generation FGFR3-selective drug for the investigational route; one of its study groups is written for people who have both an FGFR3 change and HER2 expression, the single spot in the trial registry where your two main features meet.

Nothing about your tumor is known to argue for or against the change being present; the answer is simply unread. The typical side effects of this drug class are high blood phosphate, mouth sores, and nail and eye problems, none of which touch your four limits. The honest arithmetic: an 80 to 85 percent chance the retrieval closes this door, a 15 to 20 percent chance it opens something with more consensus behind it than most of this page. The records request that answers it is the same one described in the first step.

docs.title: Option 7 — FT825 (an off-the-shelf HER2 cell therapy)
docs.text:
This option is only on the table if the HER2 test comes back positive at the trial's required level. If not, it closes along with Options 1 and 5.

This option carries caveats: nothing has been measured for it in bladder cancer. This is a cell therapy grown from donor-derived stem cells and engineered to hunt HER2, given after a short course of chemotherapy that clears space for the cells. Because it is off-the-shelf, there is no cell collection and no manufacturing wait, and unusually, prior HER2 treatment does not exclude you, which makes it one of very few HER2 trial doors your current drug has not already shut. It avoids the payloads behind your nausea and the lung-inflammation worry.

The costs are structural. The clearing chemotherapy brings a window of low blood counts, the therapy can trigger the same immune overreaction described under Option 3, and this is an early dose-finding study with no results yet in your cancer type. One quieter concern deserves a direct question: the clearing chemotherapy suppresses immune cells broadly, and you have spent a year building up vaccine-trained immune cells; whether one would undo the other should be asked before anything is scheduled. Also ask whether the ongoing vaccine series trips the trial's exclusion for prior cell or gene therapy. Sites are within your usual care orbit.

docs.title: Option 8 — ASP2998 (a TROP2-aimed drug that carries an immune alarm instead of chemotherapy)
docs.text:
This option carries caveats, and the biggest one is your own test result. This early trial drug delivers an immune-alarm signal (a "STING agonist") to cells carrying the TROP2 protein, waking the immune system inside the tumor rather than poisoning cells directly. Bladder cancer is a named study group, there is no cap on prior treatments, and prior TROP2- or similar-payload therapy is explicitly allowed, so your current drug does not close this door the way it closes most TROP2 doors.

The hedge that has to travel with this option: the research-grade test this month found your TROP2 level to be low. A low or weak result is a real positive, but it is a much less sure sign that a TROP2-aimed drug will help than a strong result would be, and that makes this option more uncertain than its neighbors. A validated TROP2 test was already run this month; its tier is in the same unretrieved stack as the HER2 result, and it should be read before this option gets real weight. Beyond that, the drug has no published results on benefit or safety. An immune-stimulating payload in someone with a 2025 bout of pancreas inflammation means the existing blood-test monitoring belongs in the plan. And one arm of this trial combines the drug with the agent that caused your nerve damage; the acceptable arms (drug alone, or with pembrolizumab) should be settled with the site in writing before consent. Sites are within reach.

docs.title: Option 9 — Adding ipilimumab to restart immunotherapy, at a reduced dose only
docs.text:
This option carries caveats, and it is the most contested item on this page. The idea: your tumor has an above-average mutation count and once responded deeply to immunotherapy, so adding a second immune drug (ipilimumab, which releases a different brake than the one your previous immunotherapy released) might reignite that response. Your care team is already exploring this, and it is the only option here that could start now, with no screening test, no trial slot, and no washout debate.

Here is the tension, plainly. In the trial that tested this exact maneuver after progression on a drug like yours, about 1 in 3 people responded, but that result came with serious costs: about 1 in 9 developed severe immune inflammation of the gut, and 2 of 83 died from treatment. That full-dose schedule collides with two of your four side-effect limits at once (severe gut toxicity, and pancreas risk given your 2025 inflammation), and it is off the table on this page. What is ranked instead is a reduced-ipilimumab schedule with mandatory pancreas blood-test monitoring and written stopping rules. The honest catch, and the reason this option is contested rather than settled: every good response number in this drug class came from the full dose. The gentler schedule has never beaten immunotherapy alone in any trial, so you would be accepting added immune-side-effect risk for a benefit that is plausible but unproven. It also has no formal guideline listing for bladder cancer, which makes both the safety scaffolding and the insurance case things your team would have to build themselves. A registered trial exists that includes this combination, but its entry rules require a tumor type composition yours probably does not meet. If this option appeals, the questions section below has the specific things to pin down first.

docs.title: Option 10 — Sacituzumab tirumotecan trial (a randomized TROP2 study)
docs.text: This option was considered but not recommended. It's on the page because Libby surfaces what was weighed and rejected, not just what was kept. This is a large randomized trial of a new TROP2 drug, and randomized entry is normally the cleanest, most rigorous way into a new drug class. It fails here for two independent reasons. First, the comparison arm is chemotherapy, and two of the three allowed chemotherapy drugs are from the class that caused your lasting nerve damage; joining means accepting a coin flip that could assign you a drug your situation forbids, with no opt-out. Second, you are likely not eligible anyway: the trial requires prior platinum chemotherapy, a treatment you never had. That platinum requirement recurs across several trials in this space and is worth flagging to your team as a strategic question in its own right. The class history adds a further reason for caution, described under Option 13.

docs.title: Option 11 — Continuing your personalized vaccine programs
docs.text:
This option carries caveats, and the honest label for it is: hypothesis stage. You are already receiving personalized vaccines built from your own tumor's mutations, across two programs, with blood-based monitoring that fits the tissue-scarcity constraint. This entry is about continuing, not starting, and about being straight regarding what the evidence shows so far. In your own monitoring, immune responses appeared against 2 of 14 evaluable vaccine targets at four months, of a helper type rather than the killer type that most directly attacks tumors, and your tumor-DNA blood test rose through most of the vaccine period. No tumor shrinkage in your record is attributable to vaccination. The encouraging randomized evidence for this vaccine class comes from a different cancer (melanoma) in a different setting.

Why it stays on the page: side effects are the mildest here (sore arms, feeling run down), it is fully aligned with the path you have chosen, and the banked immune cells it generates feed the future cell-therapy programs you are pursuing. The immune-response test after the current mRNA series finishes is a named branch point: it will tell you whether this axis is building something or not. One interaction to manage deliberately: ongoing vaccine dosing may count as "prior gene therapy" under some cell-therapy trial rules, including Option 7's, so ask before it quietly closes a door.

docs.title: Option 12 — Trastuzumab plus paclitaxel
docs.text: This option was considered but not recommended. This off-label HER2 combination pairs an antibody with a taxane chemotherapy. In the supporting study, nearly 9 in 10 people developed some degree of nerve damage from the taxane. You already have lasting nerve damage from prior treatment, and gentler ways to target HER2 exist on this page (Options 1 and 5). The rejection stands regardless of how the HER2 test comes back.

docs.title: Option 13 — Sacituzumab govitecan
docs.text: This option was considered but not recommended. This TROP2 drug once had a conditional approval in bladder cancer. In its earlier study, tumors shrank in about 1 in 4 people, but the larger confirmatory trial found that people did not live meaningfully longer than with standard chemotherapy, about 7 in 100 died of treatment-related complications (mostly infections during low blood counts), and the approval was withdrawn in 2024. Tumor shrinkage that does not translate into longer life is exactly the trap careful reading exists to catch. Your low TROP2 result further weakens the case. A trial-only route technically exists, but spending a treatment slot here competes with better-fitted doors.

docs.title: Option 14 — Datopotamab deruxtecan
docs.text: This option was considered but not recommended. This TROP2 drug carries the same payload family as your current drug, which means it re-runs the exact problems already limiting you: the severe nausea, and the lung-inflammation risk that the unresolved chest-scan question makes hard to price. It has no published results in bladder cancer, your TROP2 is low, and back-to-back use of sibling payloads invites the tumor to resist both. The TROP2 door kept open on this page is Option 8, whose payload works differently.

docs.title: The longer tail: options looked at and set aside
docs.text:
Beyond the fourteen options above, thirty-nine more feature-targeting possibilities were examined and set aside. None was ignored; each carries a recorded reason, and a few are worth knowing about because circumstances could revive them.

Some are blocked by entry rules rather than by science. The most notable is a drug aimed at Nectin-4 and TROP2 at once, blocked solely because its trial excludes anyone with possible drug-induced lung disease, which the unresolved chest-scan discrepancy triggers; a formal lung-specialist review that cleared your scans would convert it into a live candidate, which is one more reason to resolve that discrepancy. Another carries the best HER2 response number in bladder cancer (tumors shrinking in about half of patients) but is built on the payload class that caused your nerve damage, and its US trials exclude prior HER2 treatment besides. A cell-therapy route using tumor-harvested immune cells needs a surgically removable tumor, which you currently do not have, and several others have closed their doors to bladder cancer or have no site a US patient can reach.

Others were folded into options already listed: an alternative attack on the same TP53 mutation as Option 3 that requires manufacturing your own cells and a longer runway, and two backup Nectin-4 drugs kept in reserve if Option 4's screening fails.

A third group rests on targets that only a research-grade test has seen so far: the mesothelin, MUC1, PRAME, and stromal-FAP leads. Each has trials in principle, but each waits on a validated stain or scan that has not confirmed the target, and the record already contains a cautionary tale here: you were immune-type-matched for a MAGE-A4 trial until expression testing came back negative. Expression first, screening second. The related sequencing-dependent ideas (drugs aimed at the ARID1A mutation's repair weaknesses) are hypothesis-grade, and the same rank-one records retrieval doubles as the cheap test of whether any of them apply. Finally, about a dozen concepts fit your tumor on paper but have no open program anywhere a patient can currently reach them.

docs.title: Questions to ask your oncologist
docs.text:
1. Can we submit the records requests this week for the repeat HER2 result from this month and the full sequencing reports (FGFR3 status, the unnamed actionable alteration, and the HER2 gene copy number), and can the HER2 report state the tumor content of the sample it was read on?
  2. What is the concrete plan and timeline for the T-DXd stop-or-continue decision, given the severe nausea after dose 2 and the tumor-DNA blood draws ahead? And if the new HER2 result comes back negative or low, which of the options on this page would we pivot toward?
  3. Can we get a pulmonology review to formally resolve the disagreement between last year's chest scan and June's? It affects the safety pricing of my current drug and would unlock at least one blocked trial.
  4. Can we retrieve the June Nectin-4 imaging result before spending any trial-screening visit on a Nectin-4 option, and does any measurable tumor remain on scans after the June radiation, since most of these trials require one?
  5. Can we check my existing 2023 sequencing report for the TP53 R175H mutation in tumor tissue, since the trial aimed at it currently rests on one very low-level blood result?
  6. Before I continue the vaccine series, can we confirm with the cell-therapy trials we care about that ongoing vaccine dosing will not count against their prior-therapy exclusions?
  7. If we pursue the reduced-dose ipilimumab route, what written stopping rules and pancreas monitoring would we put in place, and how do we weigh doing that off-label against saving the slot for a trial?
  8. Several trials in this space require prior platinum chemotherapy, which I never had. Does that change how we sequence things from here?

docs.text: The treatment strategies that are standard for this patient's situation, meaning a regulator approved them for a population that includes this patient or a major academic or clinical-society guideline carries them. This report runs alongside the targetable-feature ranking rather than in place of it, and it does not narrow what that ranking surfaces.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
• Standard of care options (offline HTML) — the same standard-of-care assessment, self-contained HTML that opens offline
  • Standard of care options (PDF) — print-friendly, grouped by next step

12 standard options assessed: 3 to consider now, 3 behind an open gate, 3 already received.

Twelve standard options were assessed. Three are open now, three sit behind a gate a records request or a pending stain can close, three have already been used, and three were screened and set aside. The one that matters most is platinum: both NCCN and ESMO carry platinum-based chemotherapy as the standard next systemic line after progression on enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, and this patient has never received it. No platinum appears anywhere in the treatment history, which makes a full guideline-preferred line still unspent. Whether that means cisplatin or carboplatin turns on an eGFR the record does not contain and on how much added neuropathy the team will accept on top of established CIPN.

Already spent: the preferred first line itself (EV plus pembrolizumab, a 25-month complete response), pembrolizumab as a single agent (progression happened on maintenance, so the TMB-H label does not reopen it), and SBRT to both known nodal sites in June 2026.

Gated: continuation of T-DXd, the current therapy, waits on the validated 2026-08 HER2 re-stain, already drawn, tier unretrieved. Erdafitinib waits on FGFR3 status sitting in the same unretrieved sequencing reports. EV rechallenge waits on contemporary Nectin-4 expression and on the neuropathy that ended the first course.

This report adds the standard-of-care options alongside the experimental ranking; it does not remove, reorder, or argue against anything that ranking surfaces, and the one bridge between the two tables is the sequencing section below, which names where the tracks compete or foreclose one another without choosing between them.

docs.title: Assessed and set aside
docs.text:
3 option(s) screened against this patient and set aside

Screened against this patient and found not to apply. Listed for the audit trail.

  • Avelumab switch maintenance after platinum: Set aside so the platinum row is not misread as importing the whole first-line sequence: if platinum is given here it comes after PD-1 progression, a setting where the avelumab maintenance evidence does not apply and the ESMO interim update explicitly recommends platinum without it.
  • Sacituzumab govitecan (mUC approval withdrawn): Listed because a TROP2-low-positive readout makes this the drug a reader would go looking for: it is no longer standard of care in urothelial carcinoma after the 2024 withdrawal. TROP2-directed options for this case are investigational and already ranked in the experimental table.
  • Single-agent taxane (paclitaxel or docetaxel): Guideline-carried for this line but set aside on the profile: single-agent taxanes offer modest response rates and their defining toxicity lands directly on this patient's chronic CIPN, while a platinum doublet remains unused ahead of them in the same guideline.

docs.title: How these sit alongside the targeted options
docs.text:
The ranked recommendations stay scoped to this case's targetable features, and nothing on this page changes that ranking. What this section adds is the sequencing: where a standard option and a targeted option compete for the same line, and where taking one would close the door on the other.

Competes for the same line of therapy

  • Platinum-based chemotherapy (gemcitabine plus cisplatin, or gemcitabine plus carboplatin): Occupies the same next-line slot as the ranked investigational options, with washout implications for their enrollment windows. Sequencing also runs the other way: at least one ranked protocol (sacituzumab tirumotecan) requires prior platinum, so this regimen is currently the only route to that eligibility. (interacts with: zanidatamab, clsp-1025, sacituzumab-tirumotecan)
  • Erdafitinib (conditional on FGFR3 alteration): Shares its FGFR3 gate with the ranked investigational FGFR3 option (vepugratinib, rank 7) and with the rank-1 records-retrieval workup that closes the gate for both; if FGFR3 confirms, the approved drug and the trial option compete for the same slot. (interacts with: her2-reconciliation-ngs-retrieval-workup, vepugratinib)
  • Enfortumab vedotin rechallenge (monotherapy): Sits in the same Nectin-4 axis as the ranked next-generation options (LY4052031 novel-payload ADC, 225Ac-AKY-1189 radioligand), which share the contemporary-expression gate but avoid the MMAE payload; prior EV exposure is an exclusion in some Nectin-4 protocols, so rechallenge and trial entry interact both ways. (interacts with: ly4052031, ac225-aky-1189)
  • Structured surveillance after consolidative SBRT (imaging plus serial ctDNA): A monitored break occupies the same decision slot as every systemic option on either table, and it interacts with trial screening in a specific way: SBRT has already consolidated the only known measurable sites, so the RECIST-measurability question the ranked trials share is live regardless of whether therapy continues.

May foreclose a targeted option

  • Trastuzumab deruxtecan continuation (current therapy): Continuing consumes the washout window the ranked HER2 trial options need, and accumulating T-DXd exposure can itself exclude enrollment in some HER2-directed protocols; stopping opens those doors. The stop/continue call is this row's pending HER2 gate plus ctDNA kinetics. (interacts with: zanidatamab, trastuzumab-pertuzumab, ft825)
  • SBRT to oligometastatic nodal disease: By consolidating the only known measurable sites, the June SBRT is what created the RECIST-measurability question that recurs across the ranked trials' screening gates; any future repeat SBRT at oligoprogression would re-open the same trade-off between local control and trial-evaluable disease.

Independent of the targeted options

  • Intravesical BCG maintenance (bladder-directed): Bladder-directed therapy does not consume a systemic line or interact with trial washouts; its one case-specific interaction is diagnostic, since BCG granulomas are a known false-positive source on FAP-directed imaging. (interacts with: fap-radioligand-therapy)

Reading this report

An option earns a row here only if a regulator approved it for a population that includes this patient, or a major society's guideline carries it. What makes it standard names the endorsing body and, next to it, whether that endorsement was written for this patient's situation or for a different population. Fit to this patient is judged against the case profile alone, so an option the patient has already had and progressed on is marked rather than re-offered. This page is additive: it runs alongside the ranked recommendations and does not narrow, rerank, or filter the targeted options that ranking surfaces.

Libby is experimental. Standard of care is set by a treating team using the full clinical record, not by this page. Guideline versions and approvals move, eligibility here is inferred from a scrubbed profile rather than an examination, and nothing on this page is a recommendation to start, stop, or sequence a treatment. docs.title: TMB 12.4 mut/Mb + ongoing immune sensitivity — checkpoint re-intensification (ipilimumab addition)
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences highTMB recomputed from the whole-exome data already generated, using a validated caller, or read from a companion-diagnostic-grade panel reportorthogonal validationWESNo specimen if recomputed from existing exome data; archival FFPE if a companion-diagnostic panel is ordered insteadDays if the existing reports are retrieved; 2-3 weeks for a new companion-diagnostic panelTMB-H eligibility for trials that name an assay, and the strength of the neoantigen argument behind checkpoint re-intensification.The 12.4 mut/Mb value sits above the TMB-H bar but comes from an institutional 468-gene laboratory-developed panel, while the tumor-agnostic indication reads TMB-H by an FDA-approved test, and FoundationOne CDx remains the only approved TMB companion diagnostic. Recomputing from the existing exome data comes first and costs no tissue; this is the fallback if a trial insists on an approved assay.Caris Life Sciences · MI Cancer Seek UStest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 (specimen receiving) · 888-979-8669 · CustomerSupport@CarisLS.comTempus AI · Tempus xT UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654NCT02628067 mediumPD-L1 IHC by the companion clone a candidate protocol names (22C3 pharmDx or equivalent), on contemporary tissueheterogeneityIHCArchival FFPE acceptable; one slide on the shared block cut when a protocol requires it3-7 daysEntry to trials that specify a PD-L1 clone and cutoff; not a gate on checkpoint use itself.The two results on file are CPS 5 on the primary and CPS 0 in the liver metastasis, which is discordance rather than a number, and both date from 2023 on a laboratory clone validated as comparable to 22C3 rather than the companion assay itself. docs.title: ARID1A / TERT promoter / TP53 mutations — hypothesis-grade synthetic-lethality axis
docs.text: PriorityTestTypeModalityTissueTurnaroundDecision gatedRationaleProvidersReferences essentialRetrieval of the full existing sequencing reports (institutional 468-gene tumor/normal panel 2023-11, two commercial WES/WTS platforms, WGS 2025-03), read for FGFR3 and FGFR2 status and for the identity of the single OncoKB-actionable alterationconfirmatoryNGS_panelNo specimen; records retrieval onlyDays, once release forms are signedErdafitinib eligibility via FGFR3/FGFR2 status (THOR, NCT03390504), plus the identity of the one OncoKB-actionable alteration in the tissue reports.The record counts exactly one alteration with an OncoKB treatment interpretation and never names it, and FGFR3 status, which gates erdafitinib in roughly 15-20% of metastatic urothelial carcinoma, appears nowhere in the derived profile. Leaving it unretrieved risks missing the strongest genomic option in the case while scarce tissue is spent on stains for weaker ones.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne CDx preferredtest info · 400 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210 · 888-988-3639 · client.services@foundationmedicine.comListed as the fallback if a report cannot be released and sequencing has to be repeated; FoundationOne CDx is also the report format most sponsors accept without re-testing. The actual first action is a records request to the laboratories that already ran the institutional panel, the two exome and transcriptome platforms, and the 2025 genome.Caris Life Sciences · MI Cancer Seek (whole exome plus whole transcriptome) UStest info · 4610 South 44th Place, Phoenix, AZ 85040 (specimen receiving) · 888-979-8669 · CustomerSupport@CarisLS.comTempus AI · Tempus xT / xR UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654No client-services phone or email is published on a currently reachable page; order through the contact form.NCT03390504 highComprehensive plasma ctDNA panel covering FGFR3 and FGFR2 alterations, ERBB2 copy number, and variants acquired under prior therapyorthogonal validationctDNATwo Streck tubes of whole blood (about 20 mL)1-2 weeksErdafitinib eligibility when the archival reports cannot be retrieved; the same draw returns ERBB2 copy number.If the archived reports cannot be released or turn out not to cover FGFR3, a plasma panel answers the erdafitinib question without touching tissue, and detectable ctDNA on two MRD platforms says shed is adequate for it. A negative plasma result therefore cannot exclude an FGFR3 fusion and routes back to tissue.Foundation Medicine · FoundationOne Liquid CDx UStest info · 400 Summer Street, Boston, MA 02210 · 888-988-3639 · client.services@foundationmedicine.comTempus AI · Tempus xF UStest info · 600 West Chicago Avenue, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654The published xF panel includes FGFR3 and ERBB2; confirm fusion coverage with client services.NCT03390504 mediumBRAF codon 600 status read off the retrieved full tissue NGS reportconfirmatoryNGS_panelNo specimen; readout from the existing reportDaysDabrafenib plus trametinib under the tumor-agnostic BRAF V600E indication, if present.BRAF V600E is uncommon in urothelial carcinoma and the honest expectation is that it is absent. Reading it off the existing report costs a records request.—NCT02034110 mediumNTRK1/2/3 fusion status read off the retrieved whole-transcriptome and NGS reports; an RNA fusion panel only if none of them covered NTRKconfirmatoryRNA_seqNo specimen for the readout; archival FFPE if an RNA fusion panel is orderedDays for the readout; 2-3 weeks if an RNA fusion panel is neededTumor-agnostic TRK inhibition (larotrectinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib) if a fusion is present.This is a records problem and not a testing problem: whole-transcriptome sequencing that would show an NTRK fusion has already been run on two platforms and the reports are not in hand. It costs nothing beyond the retrieval already needed, and leaving it unread means an approved oral agent stays formally unassessed rather than excluded. A DNA panel without RET intronic coverage would not settle it on its own.—NCT03157128 mediumSomatic homologous-recombination gene status (BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, PALB2, RAD51 paralogs) read off the retrieved tissue NGS report; an HRD score only if a protocol asks for oneco-mutationNGS_panelNo specimen for the readout; archival FFPE if an HRD score is later requiredDays for the readout; 3-4 weeks if a genomic-scar HRD assay is addedDNA-damage-response trial eligibility (ATR and PARP inhibitor protocols) alongside the ARID1A hypothesis.Germline testing was negative in 2023-12, which leaves somatic homologous-recombination status as the unanswered half, and it sits in a panel report that covers those genes and has never been retrieved. Urothelial carcinoma is not a PARP-inhibitor indication, so the realistic payoff is trial eligibility next to the ARID1A synthetic-lethality hypothesis rather than an approved drug. No new specimen is involved.Myriad Genetics · myChoice CDx (BRCA1/2 plus genomic instability score) preferredtest info · 322 North 2200 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116 · 800-469-7423 · helpmed@myriad.comOnly relevant if a protocol demands a genomic-scar score; the published cutoff is a genomic instability score of 42 or above. docs.title: Measured, but not to decision resolution
docs.text:
15 biomarkers from the Selected general biomarker report have a result on file that cannot carry a treatment decision as it stands. These are distinct from the per-feature workup below: the target call is not in question, the resolution of the existing result is.

BiomarkerWhat is on fileWhy it is not decision-gradeHardening stepStatus HER2 protein overexpression (IHC 3+)essentialprofile.json:biomarkers[0] HER2, confirmation_status 'ihc_pending'; profile.json:biomarkers[0] three concordant IHC 3+ results (primary 2023-11, liver met 2023-11, recurrence 2025-03), clone 4B5 and a national reference lab; profile.json:biomarkers[0] discordant weak HER2 on research-grade MXIF of 2026-08 nodal tissue; repeat validated IHC performed 2026-08, tier not in the record; profile.json:targetable_features[0] names HER2 reconciliation as the near-term decision gateThe 3+ calls describe 2023 and 2025 tumor. The current (2026-08) nodal tumor has been read only by research-grade multiplex immunofluorescence, which is not a validated HER2 assay and scored weak. Closing the gap needs the tier from the validated HER2 IHC drawn 2026-08 (4B5 or equivalent, reflex ISH if 2+), reported with tumor content stated, since the nodal cores carry only 5-10% tumor.Validated HER2 IHC (clone 4B5 or equivalent) with reflex ISH if 2+, on contemporary tumor tissue, reported as an expression tier (3+ / 2+ / 1+ / 0) with tumor content statedaddressed above Mesothelin (MSLN) protein expressionhighprofile.json:biomarkers[4] mesothelin strong on research-grade MXIF 2026-08, confirmation_status 'ihc_pending'; profile.json:biomarkers[4] decision_resolution asks for validated mesothelin IHC before trial screening; profile.json:targetable_features[3] treats this as a confirmation-first leadThe only evidence is research-grade multiplex immunofluorescence, not a validated clinical mesothelin IHC, and mesothelin is atypical in urothelial carcinoma, which raises the bar on assay specificity. A validated stain on tumor tissue is what mesothelin-directed trials will ask for, and the 5-10% tumor content of the nodal cores has to be stated on the report.Validated clinical mesothelin IHC (clone 5B2 or the candidate protocol's own assay), scored with tumor content statedaddressed above Nectin-4 (NECTIN4) protein expressionhighprofile.json:biomarkers[2] Nectin-4 95% membranous (primary 2023-11), 100% in the in-situ component (2025-03), confirmation_status 'confirmed'; profile.json:biomarkers[2] Nectin-4-directed imaging performed 2026-06, result not in the available record; profile.json:targetable_features[1] flags acquired Nectin-4 downregulation after enfortumab vedotin as plausible and unverifiedBoth stains predate 25 months of enfortumab vedotin. Antigen downregulation is a recognised route to EV resistance, so the historical 95-100% result cannot carry a re-targeting decision. Closing the gap means the 2026-06 Nectin-4 imaging read, or a contemporary IHC on post-EV tissue.Contemporary Nectin-4 IHC on post-enfortumab-vedotin tissue, or retrieval of the 2026-06 Nectin-4-directed imaging readaddressed above PRAME expression (HLA-A*02:01-restricted)highprofile.json:biomarkers[7] PRAME-directed imaging completed 2026-08, result not in the available record, confirmation_status 'unknown'; profile.json:biomarkers[12] HLA-A*02:01 positive by high-resolution typing 2025-01, confirmation_status 'confirmed'; profile.json:targetable_features[5] describes this axis as conditional on expressionThe 2026-08 PRAME imaging read is not in the record, and imaging is not what a PRAME trial screens on. Trials require expression by validated IHC or RT-PCR at a stated threshold, which has not been done. Retrieve the imaging read, then run the expression assay the candidate protocol names.PRAME expression by validated IHC (clone EPR20330) or RT-PCR, scored at the threshold the candidate protocol namesaddressed above TROP2 (TACSTD2) protein expressionhighprofile.json:biomarkers[3] TROP2 low positive (weak) on research-grade MXIF 2026-08, confirmation_status 'ihc_pending'; profile.json:biomarkers[3] validated TROP2 IHC performed 2026-08 at a tertiary academic center, tier not in the available recordA weak MXIF signal is recorded as low expression and not as a negative, and multiplex immunofluorescence is not a validated TROP2 assay. The validated IHC drawn 2026-08 needs to be retrieved and reported as a tier, percent times intensity or H-score, so that trials gating on expression can be screened against a real number.Validated TROP2 IHC reported as a tier (percent membranous staining times intensity, or H-score) rather than as positive or negativeaddressed above Tumor mutational burden, high (TMB-H)highprofile.json:biomarkers[9] TMB 12.4 mut/Mb in primary and liver metastasis, confirmation_status 'confirmed'; profile.json:biomarkers[9] method 'institutional hybrid-capture tumor/normal NGS panel (468-gene class), 2023-11'; profile.json:biomarkers[9] decision_resolution already flags the cross-assay calibration hedgeThe value comes from an institutional 468-gene hybrid-capture panel. The tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab indication reads TMB-H by an FDA-approved test, and FoundationOne CDx is still the only approved TMB companion diagnostic as of 2026-08, so 12.4 mut/Mb on a laboratory-developed panel does not satisfy the label as written. TMB recomputed from the whole-exome sequencing already performed, or a companion-diagnostic-grade panel report, would settle it.TMB recomputed from the whole-exome data already generated, using a validated caller, or read from a companion-diagnostic-grade panel reportaddressed above B7-H3 (CD276) protein expressionmediumabsent from profile.json:biomarkers[]; no B7-H3 or CD276 result on file; the 2026-08 research MXIF panel recorded in profile.json covered HER2, TROP2, mesothelin, MUC1 and FAP, and returned no B7-H3 read—B7-H3 (CD276) IHC on tumor tissueaddressed above BRAF V600E mutationmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[11] names only ARID1A, TERT promoter and TP53 among 16 tissue mutations; profile.json:biomarkers[11] states exactly one alteration carries an OncoKB treatment interpretation and does not identify it; no BRAF call appears in profile.json:biomarkers[]—BRAF codon 600 status read off the retrieved full tissue NGS reportaddressed above Homologous recombination deficiency / BRCA1 / BRCA2 pathogenic variantmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[11] germline panel negative 2023-12; profile.json:biomarkers[11] tissue NGS performed on a 468-gene class panel that would cover BRCA1/2, ATM and PALB2, report not in the available record; no somatic HR gene result and no HRD score appear in profile.json:biomarkers[]—Somatic homologous-recombination gene status (BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, PALB2, RAD51 paralogs) read off the retrieved tissue NGS report; an HRD score only if a protocol asks for oneaddressed above MUC1 protein expressionmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[5] MUC1 strong on research-grade MXIF 2026-08, confirmation_status 'ihc_pending'; profile.json:biomarkers[5] decision_resolution asks for validated MUC1 IHC with clone and threshold per candidate trialResearch-grade multiplex immunofluorescence with no validated tier. MUC1 is expressed at low level on normal epithelia, so a strong signal only becomes meaningful when the assay distinguishes the tumor-associated glycoform the candidate agent targets. The stain has to be the clone that protocol names.Validated MUC1 IHC using the clone and threshold the candidate protocol names, glycoform-specific (Tn-MUC1) where the agent targets that epitopeaddressed above NTRK1 / NTRK2 / NTRK3 gene fusionmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[11] institutional tumor/normal NGS 2023-11 reports 'no structural variants', without naming NTRK; profile.json:biomarkers[11] WES/WTS on two commercial platforms and WGS 2025-03 performed, reports not in the available record; no NTRK call, positive or negative, appears anywhere in profile.json:biomarkers[]—NTRK1/2/3 fusion status read off the retrieved whole-transcriptome and NGS reports; an RNA fusion panel only if none of them covered NTRKaddressed above NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) expression, HLA-A*02:01-restrictedmediumabsent from profile.json:biomarkers[]; no NY-ESO-1 or CTAG1B result on file; profile.json:biomarkers[8] shows MAGE-A4 expression was tested for a TCR trial in 2024 and NY-ESO-1 was not; profile.json:biomarkers[12] HLA-A*02:01 positive, so the restriction requirement is met—NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) expression by IHC or RT-PCR, run on the same block as PRAMEaddressed above PD-L1 protein expressionmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[1] CPS 5 and 5% tumor cells on the primary (2023-11), CPS 0 on the liver metastasis (2023-11), confirmation_status 'confirmed'; profile.json:biomarkers[1] method 'IHC E1L3N clone, validated comparable to 22C3 pharmDx'; profile.json:biomarkers[1] decision_resolution notes heterogeneity weakens PD-L1 as a predictor hereTwo sites gave CPS 5 and CPS 0, which is discordance and not a number, and the stain used a laboratory clone validated as comparable to 22C3 pharmDx rather than the companion assay itself. No PD-L1 result exists on tissue from 2025 or later. A trial specifying CPS at or above 10 by 22C3 would need a fresh companion-assay read on contemporary tissue.PD-L1 IHC by the companion clone a candidate protocol names (22C3 pharmDx or equivalent), on contemporary tissueaddressed above RET gene fusionmediumprofile.json:biomarkers[11] tissue NGS 2023-11 reports 'no structural variants', without naming RET; profile.json:biomarkers[11] WES/WTS and WGS performed, reports not in the available record; no RET call appears in profile.json:biomarkers[]—RET fusion status read off the retrieved whole-transcriptome or NGS report; an RNA fusion panel only if RET was not coveredaddressed above Fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP), stromallowprofile.json:biomarkers[6] FAP-positive stroma on research-grade MXIF 2026-08, confirmation_status 'unknown'; profile.json:biomarkers[6] FAPI PET 2025-09 showed intense uptake in prostate and seminal vesicle only, attributed to biopsy-proven BCG granulomatous inflammation, with no FAP-avid urothelial disease; profile.json:biomarkers[6] repeat FAP imaging 2026-06, result not in the available recordStromal positivity on an unvalidated multiplex assay conflicts with a FAPI PET that showed no avid urothelial lesion, and the uptake it did show sits in granulomatous tissue, a classic false positive. What would settle it is quantitative FAPI PET uptake in the known nodal disease, read with the post-SBRT inflammatory caveat stated.Retrieval of the 2026-06 FAP-directed imaging read, with quantitative FAPI PET uptake in the known nodal disease only if that read is uninformativeaddressed above

First authorLast authorYearJournalNCTPhaseIndicationLineBiomarkernDesignInterventionComparatorEndpointEffectLower CIUpper CIpQualityPMIDDOIFitTumor-type relationModalityDev statusSponsorToxicity flagsInclusion notes ——2026—NCT072879951/2Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors; urothelial carcinoma in dose escalation and expansion2L+TROP2-directed; prior TROP2 or topoisomerase I-directed therapy explicitly allowed428Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion, monotherapy and combinationASP2998 (TROP2-directed STING agonist conjugate), alone or with pembrolizumab, enfortumab vedotin or carboplatin—DLT; treatment-emergent adverse events————low——partialindicationADCphase 1 activeAstellas Pharma—Urothelial carcinoma is a named escalation and expansion histology with no cap on prior regimens, and prior TROP2 or topoisomerase-payload exposure is permitted, which keeps the door open after trastuzumab deruxtecan. A STING-agonist payload is a different bet from a cytotoxic ADC and may matter less on TROP2 expression level, which is the hedge on a weak stain. New York and New Jersey sites; the enfortumab vedotin combination arms should be declined given the neuropathy. ——2026—NCT074192953Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer after anti-PD-(L)1, platinum and enfortumab vedotin2L+TROP2-directed; no expression cutoff for entry590Randomized open-label phase 3 (TroFuse-031)Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT, MK-2870) versus paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunineInvestigator's choice paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunineOverall survival————low——weaksame-drugADCphase 3 activeMerck Sharp & Dohmesevere peripheral neuropathyEntry requires prior anti-PD-(L)1, prior platinum-based chemotherapy and prior enfortumab vedotin, and this patient never received platinum, so the trial is closed to him on a line-of-therapy technicality rather than on biology. That gap recurs across the registered post-EV urothelial trials and is worth flagging to the treating team as a strategic question about whether platinum is ever given. The control arm is taxane or vinflunine, both of which run against the established neuropathy. ——2026—NCT076703121/2MUC1-expressing advanced, relapsed or refractory solid tumors2L+MUC1 expression190Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansionXYA02 (MUC1-directed agent)—Safety, tolerability and preliminary efficacy————low——weakbasketotherphase 1 activeXYone Therapeutics—Selection is MUC1 expression across relapsed or refractory solid tumors, which fits the multiplex finding, but the study has not opened, runs in Australia only, and the registry record does not name the construct or the MUC1 epitope. Since normal epithelium carries wild-type MUC1, whether the assay resolves a tumor-associated glycoform is the question that decides whether this is a real option. Track rather than pursue. ——2026—NCT076863672Metastatic or unresectable synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round cell liposarcoma in HLA-A*02:01-positive patients2L+HLA-A*02:01 positive; PRAME expression expected by histology42Phase 2 single-arm in rare PRAME-expressing sarcomasBrenetafusp (IMC-F106C)—Objective response rate————low——weakcross-tumorbispecific otherphase 2 activeNational Cancer Institute—Restricted to synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round cell liposarcoma, so it is informational only, but it shows the PRAME ImmTAC class moving out of melanoma into tumors selected for high PRAME expression plus the same HLA restriction this patient carries. That is the precedent an off-melanoma request would lean on if PRAME comes back positive here. Central HLA typing is offered through the protocol. ——2025—NCT070201171Nectin-4-expressing advanced solid tumors, urothelial carcinoma among the named cohorts2L+Nectin-4 expression; [64Cu]Cu-AKY-1189 uptake gates the therapeutic dose150Phase 1 dose escalation and expansion, theranostic pair (64Cu imaging, 225Ac therapy)[225Ac]Ac-AKY-1189 (Nectin-4-directed actinium-225 radioligand) with [64Cu]Cu-AKY-1189 imaging—DLT and adverse events (Part 1); ORR (Part 2)————low——strongindicationradioligandphase 1 activeAktis Oncology—Prior enfortumab vedotin is explicitly permitted, which almost no other Nectin-4 protocol allows, and an alpha-emitting radioligand kills by crossfire rather than by antigen engagement on every cell, so it is the Nectin-4 re-targeting route that does not depend on retained uniform expression or on an MMAE payload. Sites include New York, Pennsylvania and Maryland. Two gates to check: a measurable RECIST lesion after SBRT to the only known nodal disease, and the 3-week washout from trastuzumab deruxtecan. ——2025—NCT071935111/2Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer and other solid tumors2L+Nectin-4 and TROP2 co-targeting; molecular test report required at screening355First-in-human phase 1/2, monotherapy (Part A) and combination (Part B)AVZO-103 (Nectin-4 x TROP2 bispecific ADC, exatecan payload), alone or with a combination agent—DLT and MTD/RP2D (phase 1); ORR (phase 2)————low——strongindicationADCphase 1 activeAvenzo Therapeuticsinterstitial lung disease / pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoringOne agent covers two of this patient's features at once, and the bispecific design is built for heterogeneous or partly lost antigen, which is the specific worry after 25 months of EV and with TROP2 only weakly positive. FDA Fast Track covers post-EV urothelial cancer, and Connecticut, Massachusetts and New York sites are within the patient's usual care geography. The exclusion that matters is a history of drug-induced ILD, which the unresolved 2026-03 chest CT read and the current deruxtecan exposure could make an issue at screening. ——2025—NCT067788631Advanced solid tumors harboring TP53 R175H in HLA-A*02:01-positive patients; bladder cancer named among conditions2L+TP53 R175H by accredited laboratory test AND HLA-A*02:01 by central assay90Phase 1 monotherapy dose escalation (Part A) and HLA-selected expansion (Part B)CLSP-1025 (TP53 R175H peptide-HLA-A*02:01-directed T-cell engager)—MTD/RDE (Part A); ORR (Part B)————low——partialbasketbispecific otherphase 1 activeClasp Therapeutics—Both eligibility gates are already answered in this record: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed on 2025-01 typing, and TP53 R175H reported on Guardant360 plasma in 2025-06. The catch is that the R175H call rests on a single 0.09% VAF plasma read, so the sponsor's central confirmation is the real gate and a tissue-level confirmation would be worth having first. Sites in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Maryland; the prostate primary is covered by the exclusion's remission carve-out. ——2025—NCT067560351Advanced cancers associated with mesothelin expression2L+Mesothelin expression (tumor types associated with mesothelin expression)70Phase 1a dose escalation and 1b expansionCT-95 (mesothelin x CD3 bispecific antibody)—MTD/recommended dose; treatment-emergent adverse events————low——partialbasketbispecific otherphase 1 activeContext Therapeutics—Entry is written around mesothelin expression rather than a fixed histology list, which is the only way an unusual mesothelin-positive urothelial carcinoma gets a hearing. The strong 2026-08 signal came from research-grade multiplex immunofluorescence, so a validated mesothelin IHC has to come first, and soluble mesothelin as an antigen sink is worth measuring on the same visit. New Jersey and Pennsylvania sites; prior mesothelin CD3 or CAR-T therapy is excluded, which does not apply here. ——2025—NCT068856971Mesothelin-expressing advanced solid tumors including mesothelioma2L+Mesothelin expression by on-study screening assay100Phase 1 dose escalation in mesothelin-expressing solid tumors, expansion in mesotheliomaTNhYP218 (anti-mesothelin TNaive/SCM CAR T cells) after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide—RP2D by DLT; preliminary ORR in mesothelioma————low——partialbasketCAR-Tphase 1 activeNational Cancer Institute (CCR)—Dose escalation takes mesothelin-expressing solid tumors generally, with no limit on prior regimens, so urothelial carcinoma is not excluded by histology. The trial runs its own mesothelin assay at screening, which makes a local validated stain the qualifying step rather than the deciding one. Measurable disease and one prior FDA-approved standard therapy are required; Bethesda is the only site. ——2025—NCT075243481Advanced refractory solid tumors2L+Nectin-4-directed149Phase 1 first-in-human, all-comer advanced solid tumorsE303 (SBE303, Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate)—Safety and tolerability; efficacy————low——partialbasketADCphase 1 activeSamsung Bioepis—Entry asks only for an advanced solid tumor that progressed on or is intolerant of standard therapy, with no stated Nectin-4 cutoff and no prior-ADC exclusion in the posted criteria, which makes it one of the few Nectin-4 protocols a post-EV patient can approach without a waiver. The payload is not named in the registry record and should be asked for directly, since an MMAE payload would put it behind the neuropathy veto. US sites are Arizona and Virginia only. ——2025—NCT066958452HER2-overexpressing (IHC 3+) advanced solid tumors, urothelial carcinoma among the listed conditions2L+HER2 IHC 3+ by sponsor-designated central laboratory200Phase 2 single-arm, cohort 1 pan-tumor (HER2-therapy-naive), cohorts 2 and 3 breast and gastroesophagealZanidatamab (HER2-targeted biparatopic bispecific antibody)—Confirmed objective response rate by independent central review————low——weakbasketbispecific otherphase 2 activeJazz Pharmaceuticals—Cohort 1 is a genuine HER2 IHC 3+ pan-tumor basket that names urothelial carcinoma, but it bars prior HER2-targeted therapy, and only the breast and gastroesophageal cohorts admit (indeed require) prior trastuzumab deruxtecan. Current T-DXd therefore forecloses the one cohort this histology fits. Central IHC 3+ confirmation would also be required, which is the same pending re-stain that governs the rest of the HER2 branch. ——2025—NCT076121891Select advanced or metastatic solid tumors with no available standard therapy2L+EGFR and MUC1 co-expression (select tumor types)155Phase 1 dose escalation with backfill (part A) and expansion (part B)NEOK002 (EGFR x MUC1 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate)—Dose-limiting toxicity and recommended dose————low——weakbasketADCphase 1 activeNEOK Biointerstitial lung disease / pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoringThe exclusion that decides this row is procedural rather than biological: the most recent systemic therapy cannot have been an ADC with a topoisomerase I payload, which is exactly what trastuzumab deruxtecan is, so an intervening regimen would be needed. A known history of interstitial lung disease is also excluded. MUC1 here is a strong multiplex-immunofluorescence signal with no validated stain and no glycoform resolution, so the target call is not yet at the standard a protocol would screen on. New York site. ——2025—NCT075451221Nectin-4-positive triple-negative breast cancer, colorectal cancer or urothelial cancer2L+Nectin-4 positivity162Phase 1a/1b first-in-human dose escalation and expansionCT-202 (Nectin-4-directed bispecific antibody)—Safety, tolerability and dose finding————low——weakindicationbispecific otherphase 1 activeContext Therapeutics—A Nectin-4-directed bispecific carries no cytotoxic payload at all, which is the cleanest way around the MMAE neuropathy problem, and urothelial cancer is one of three enrolling histologies with ECOG up to 2. It runs only in Australia, and the posted criteria give no Nectin-4 cutoff or prior-ADC rule, both of which would need asking. Prior severe skin toxicity is the one stated exclusion of note. ——2025—NCT074926281Advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with Nectin-4 positivity and assessed HER2 status2L+Nectin-4 IHC >=1+ in >=10% of tumor cells with HER2 by IHC/ISH, central review42Phase 1 dose escalation of dual-target allogeneic CAR-NK cells with an inducible caspase-9 safety switchEB-DT-NK-UC101 (allogeneic cord-blood-derived Nectin-4/HER2 dual-target CAR-NK cells) after lymphodepletion—Safety and tolerability————low——weakindicationCAR-NKphase 1 activeBeijing Biotech—Prior enfortumab vedotin and prior HER2-directed therapy are both explicitly allowed, which no US protocol on this list manages, and the Nectin-4 bar of IHC >=1+ in >=10% of cells is low enough to survive partial antigen loss. The trial runs only in China and strongly prefers a fresh biopsy after the most recent regimen, which collides with the tissue scarcity here. Logged so the board can see that a dual-target, post-EV, post-HER2 design exists and is enrolling somewhere. ——2025—NCT072137911FAP-positive pancreatic, breast, ovarian, gastric, colorectal, esophageal and biliary tract cancers2L+Clinical or imaging evidence of FAP expression by local assessment241Phase 1 dose escalation and expansion (FiREBOLT)LY4337713 (FAP-directed agent)—Safety and dose finding————low——weakcross-tumorotherphase 1 activeEli Lilly and Company—Entry accepts imaging evidence of FAP expression rather than requiring a stain, which would suit this case, but the histology list stops at pancreatic, breast, ovarian, gastric, colorectal, esophageal and biliary tumors and does not include urothelial carcinoma. It stays in the file as the current benchmark for FAP-directed therapy outside the radioligand class. If the 2026-06 FAP imaging is convincing, a sponsor conversation about histology expansion is the only route. ——2024—NCT064650691Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma and other solid tumors2L+Nectin-4-directed; no expression cutoff stated for entry420Phase 1 dose escalation, dose optimization and expansion; cohort B2 restricted to prior-EV patientsLY4052031 (Nectin-4 ADC, camptothecin-98 topoisomerase I payload)—RP2D (phase 1a); ORR (phase 1b)ORR 47% in post-enfortumab-vedotin participants at 3.6 mg/kg (ASCO 2026 initial NEXUS-01 results)———low——strongindicationADCphase 1 activeEli Lilly and Company—Cohort B2 is written for exactly this patient: urothelial carcinoma, at least one prior regimen, and prior enfortumab vedotin required rather than excluded. The topoisomerase payload sidesteps the MMAE neuropathy that drove EV discontinuation, and initial phase 1 data put the post-EV response rate at 47%. Measurable disease is required for B2, corneal keratopathy is an exclusion, and the nearest sites are New York and Massachusetts. ——2024—NCT062414561Advanced HER2-expressing solid tumors2L+HER2 expression (protocol-defined per tumor type)351Phase 1 dose escalation, Regimen A (FT825) and Regimen B (FT825 + cetuximab)FT825 / ONO-8250 (off-the-shelf iPSC-derived HER2 CAR-T), with or without monoclonal antibodies—DLT; treatment-emergent adverse events————low——partialbasketCAR-Tphase 1 activeFate Therapeutics—An allogeneic HER2 CAR-T needs no apheresis and no manufacturing slot, which matters in a case where tissue and time are both short. Eligibility runs on HER2 expression across solid tumors rather than on a histology list, and unlike the HER2 antibody and ADC trials here it does not exclude prior HER2-directed therapy. The contemporary HER2 tier from the 2026-08 stain is still the gate, and prior CAR-T or other cell therapy is excluded. Connecticut, New York and Pennsylvania sites. ——2024—NCT062657271/2Advanced or metastatic Nectin-4-expressing solid tumors2L+Nectin-4 expression348Phase 1/2 dose escalation, optimization and expansion cohortsCRB-701 (SYS6002, site-specific Nectin-4 ADC with MMAE payload), alone or with anti-PD-1—MTD and payload-adjusted dose (Part A); ORR (Parts B and C)————low——weakbasketADCphase 1 activeCorbus Pharmaceuticalssevere peripheral neuropathy interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoringEligibility is Nectin-4 expression across solid tumors rather than a histology list, and Connecticut and Massachusetts sites are convenient, but three exclusions bite here: pre-existing grade 2 or worse neuropathy, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis within 6 months, and a history of solid tumors other than the one under study, which the prostate primary may trigger. The lower free-MMAE design is meant to spare neuropathy, but it is still an MMAE payload in a patient with established CIPN. Reachable only if the neuropathy grades below 2 on formal assessment. ——2024—NCT060516951/2Mesothelin-expressing solid tumors with tumor loss of heterozygosity of HLA-A*022L+Germline HLA-A*02 heterozygosity, tumor HLA-A*02 LOH by NGS, and mesothelin expression474Phase 1/2 of logic-gated CAR T cells, entry through the BASECAMP-1 screening study (NCT04981119)A2B694 (autologous logic-gated Tmod mesothelin CAR T cells) after lymphodepletion—DLT and RP2D (phase 1); overall response rate (phase 2)————low——weakbasketCAR-Tphase 1 activeA2 Biotherapeuticsinterstitial lung disease / pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoringInclusion reads "or other solid tumors with MSLN expression", so urothelial carcinoma is not excluded by histology, but entry runs only through BASECAMP-1, whose own tumor-type list does not name it, and the whole approach depends on tumor HLA-A*02 loss of heterozygosity, which is unmeasured here and is already queued as a computation on the existing exome data. A history of interstitial lung disease requiring prolonged steroids within a year is an exclusion. Low probability, but the LOH analysis costs nothing extra and would settle it. ——2024—NCT071561361Advanced PRAME-positive cancers in HLA-A*02:01-positive patients2L+HLA-A*02:01 positive and PRAME-positive per protocol testing140Phase 1 monotherapy dose escalationIMC-P115C (half-life-extended PRAME-directed ImmTAC)—Dose-limiting toxicity and adverse events————low——weakbasketbispecific otherphase 1 activeImmunocore—Eligibility is the patient's own pair of gates, HLA-A*02:01 plus PRAME positivity, with no histology restriction, so this is on-axis by construction. It runs only in Australia, France, Italy and Spain, which is the reason for the weak rating rather than anything about the biology. Worth keeping visible in case a US site opens or the sponsor's other PRAME programs read out. ——2024—NCT065185642Recurrent ARID1A-mutated endometrial cancer2L+ARID1A loss-of-function mutation by any CLIA-certified NGS assay25Phase 2 investigator-initiated, single-armTuvusertib (M1774, ATR inhibitor) with avelumab—Objective response rate————low——weakcross-tumorsmall moleculephase 2 activeDana-Farber Cancer Institute—The one trial found that selects patients on ARID1A loss of function rather than merely tolerating it, which makes it the reference point for how strong that hypothesis currently is; it enrolls endometrial cancer only, so this patient cannot join. Pairing an ATR inhibitor with a checkpoint antibody is also the closest analogue to what the immune-intensification branch here is reaching for. Massachusetts. Meric-Bernstam FLee JY2024Journal of Clinical OncologyNCT044823092HER2-expressing advanced solid tumors excluding breast, gastric and colorectal; bladder cohort in part 12L+HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+ by local or central testing267Open-label phase 2, seven tumor cohorts (part 1) plus HER2-tier cohorts (part 2)Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks—Investigator-assessed confirmed objective response rateORR 61.3% in the central HER2 IHC 3+ population; 37.1% across all patients49.4072.40—med3787053610.1200/JCO.23.02005weakbasketADCapprovedAstraZeneca / Daiichi Sankyointerstitial lung disease / pneumonitis-high-risk agents without tight monitoring severe GI toxicity / highly emetogenic regimensThis is the evidence the current therapy rests on: a bladder cohort inside the pan-tumor study whose IHC 3+ population responded at 61.3%, against 37.1% overall, which is why the pending re-stain tier and not the 2023 result decides whether to continue.
